TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.summary: A supplied smooth mean equation gives the hierarchy mean output

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.text: Smooth phase-independent strain and covector coefficients, nonzero initial covectors, their covector evolution, and a smooth periodic zero-mean source give a concrete transverse output. The velocity starts at zero, and both velocity and pressure are periodic in phase. The theorem invokes the smooth transverse ODE solver, then identifies its momentum equation with the hierarchy operators.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.summary: The smooth zero-initial transverse solve supplies hierarchy data

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.text: Given smooth velocity and pressure on the slab, zero velocity phase mean, pointwise transversality, and the prescribed momentum equation, this theorem packages them as a `HierarchyTransverseOutput`. The conclusion preserves both supplied functions on every slab slice. It assumes the analytic solution and does not prove its existence or impose an initial condition.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.summary: A supplied transverse solution realizes the hierarchy equation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ext.text: Two smooth slab profiles agreeing on the slab are equal as stored functions, because both use the specified zero extension outside it. No global continuation argument is involved.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ext.summary: Equality on the slab determines the stored profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.fderiv.text: For a positive slab and closed envelope `S`, proves that a profile vanishing before activation or outside `S` has zero full within-slab derivative there. Closedness makes the inactive condition relatively open. Local equality to zero and uniqueness of within derivatives justify the result; pointwise vanishing at an isolated point would not suffice.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.fderiv.summary: A derivative vanishes on the relatively open inactive region

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.graphR.text:
Read the actual smooth profile on the transported graph.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.graphR.summary: Reading a profile on the transported graph

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.text: The phase direction ranges over the entire real line at each fixed time and label.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.summary: The phase derivative along a profile slice

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.text: Restriction to a time line extracts the actual time derivative, including at the boundary of the closed slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.summary: The time derivative along a profile slice

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.text:
The actual profile operators in (5.20) and (5.25) on a closed time slab.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.summary: Concrete differential operators on the time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.text: Evaluation of the material operator is the within-slab time derivative of the profile plus multiplication by M. The operator has been expressed in parent labels, so no separate label transport term appears here.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.summary: The material operator is time derivative plus strain

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelA.text: If the coframe and both input profiles are phase independent, their label advection is phase independent as well. The derivative acts only on the label slice, whose values do not change with phase. This verifies the mean-product condition used to cancel the source’s inactive-region average.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelA.summary: Slow advection of means remains independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.text: The operator profile `G` acts pointwise on a velocity profile, and its result is inserted into the label component of the joint direction. The resulting map is linear in the velocity. The definition uses the given coframe values but does not assert that they come from an inverse flow.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.summary: The coframe turns velocity into a label direction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.text: At an on-slab point, the direction selected from `G` and `u` is exactly `(0, G.val x (u.val x), 0)`. Thus only the label coordinates vary. The theorem exposes the pointwise meaning of the composed profile maps without imposing extra geometry on `G`.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.summary: Read the coframe direction in coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text:
The three scalar coframe derivatives form the Eulerian label gradient.

Default-value audit (b5): Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability. Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: The three slow derivatives of a scalar profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text: The bundled slow gradient is the sum of within-slab directional derivatives in the three coframe directions, multiplied by their Eulerian basis vectors. This is an evaluation identity at a point of the slab, rather than an estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: The slow gradient written in coordinate directions

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text: The coframe label gradient of a scalar profile is the coframe transpose applied to its ordinary label gradient.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: Label pressure gradients use the transposed coframe

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.linear.text: For a smooth periodic parent flow and coefficient profiles equal to its actual inverse coframe, strain and transported covector, the physical graph of the material and pressure operators equals the linearized momentum expression. The time derivative is taken within the closed slab. The proof polarizes the nonlinear graph identity to remove quadratic self-advection of the perturbation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.linear.summary: The profile mean equation becomes physical linearized momentum

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map.text: A bounded linear map `Fmap : E →L[ℝ] F` acts on each value of a smooth slab profile, producing another smooth profile. The result is linear in the input profile. Boundedness gives continuous linear postcomposition and therefore preservation of the supplied smoothness on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map.summary: Apply a bounded linear map to profile values

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map_ap.text: At a point of the time slab, the profile obtained by `map Fmap f` has value `Fmap (f.val x)`. This is the pointwise interpretation of bounded linear postcomposition. The on-slab hypothesis removes the constructor’s zero-extension branch before applying the map.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.text: At a slab point, the residual of the parent plus a graph-read perturbation equals the graph-read concrete profile momentum plus the parent residual. The assumptions identify `G`, `M`, and `κ` with the actual inverse-label derivative, parent gradient, and transported covector. The inverse-label transport equation and differentiability hypotheses are supplied explicitly.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.summary: Profile momentum evaluates to the physical residual identity

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.text: The Eulerian momentum residual equals the graph of the profile momentum terms plus the parent residual. The theorem uses the actual parent flow `hX`, smoothness `hU`, periodicity `hper` and inverse-label regularity `hAreg`. The hypotheses `hG`, `hM` and `hκ` identify the profile coefficients with the inverse coframe, velocity gradient and transported covector. The statement combines the material, nonlinear and pressure chain rules used at the start of Lemma 5.8’s proof.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.summary: Momentum under evaluation on the parent graph

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.text: Given `hf : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (hierarchyProfileSlab T)`, this returns the same function on the closed slab and zero everywhere else. The construction creates a representative suitable for pointwise linear algebra. It requires smoothness only within the slab and does not make the zero extension globally smooth.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.summary: Represent a smooth slab function by its zero extension

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.text: At a point satisfying `hx : x ∈ hierarchyProfileSlab T`, the representative constructed by `ofSmooth` evaluates to the original function `f x`. The membership condition is essential because the constructor replaces values outside the slab with zero. This lemma removes the representation wrapper in pointwise equations.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.text: If the fixed-time, fixed-label phase slice of a smooth profile is constant, its joint within-slab derivative in any pure phase direction `(0,0,c)` vanishes. The time must belong to the slab. This establishes the vanishing phase-advection and phase-gradient conditions required when a mean field is packaged into the hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.summary: Phase-independent profiles have zero phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.text: The transported covector profile `κ` is converted to its inner-product functional and applied to an advecting velocity. The scalar result is inserted into the phase coordinate. This gives a linear map from velocity profiles to pure phase directions, including zero when the velocity is transverse.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.summary: Contract velocity with the transported covector

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.text: At a point of the slab, `phaseDirections κ u` is `(0, 0, ⟪κ,u⟫)`, with both fields evaluated at that point. Only the phase component changes. This identity makes the transversality condition visible as the vanishing of the entire fast direction.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.text:
The fast scalar derivative of the pressure multiplies the transported covector.

Default-value audit (b5): Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.summary: The fast pressure gradient follows the transported covector

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.text: At a slab point, the fast gradient is the directional derivative in the phase variable multiplied by the covector. The derivative is taken with time and label fixed.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.summary: The fast gradient is covector times phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The divergence correction is the slow curl of `profileWavePotential`. The binder `G` supplies the inverse-label differential, `κ` supplies the covector, and `V` is a smooth profile on the closed slab. The hypothesis `hκ` requires its phase-zero covector to be nonzero at every time and label, while `hT` gives positive slab length. This definition alone does not identify `G` and `κ` with a common flow; the geometric compatibility is supplied in the divergence and longitudinal theorems.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: The slow curl correction vanishes on the inactive region whenever the input profile does. The binder `hS` requires a closed label set, `hV` gives vanishing outside it or before activation, and `hκ` supplies nonzero covectors. The proof first establishes vanishing of the potential at each inactive label, then uses locality of differentiation on the relatively open complement. This controls a common support set through the slab; it does not state an arbitrary pointwise-in-time support theorem without a common set.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Curl completion preserves the common inactive region

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At any slab time, including an endpoint, assume the entire label-phase slice of `V` vanishes. Its concrete divergence completion vanishes on that slice as well. The proof uses only label and phase operations, so no time neighborhood of zero values is needed. A nonzero covector on the slab is required by the completion construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Completion preserves an identically zero time slice

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: The phase derivative of $\langle\kappa,C[V]\rangle$ equals minus the pulled-back slow divergence of $V$. The hypotheses `hG` and `hκflow` identify the coframe and covector with one $C^2$ inverse-label map `A`; `htrans` imposes transversality at every label and phase. The binder `hκ` excludes zero covectors throughout the slab. This supplies the geometric input needed before the normalized primitive recovers the second slaving identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Phase derivative of the longitudinal correction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: The completion is odd under simultaneous reflection of label and phase. The coframe and covector are even by `hGeven` and `hκeven`, and the input profile is odd by `hVodd`. The named hypotheses `hper` and `hmean` require period one and zero phase mean, while `hκ` excludes zero covectors. The argument first obtains an even normalized potential, whose slow curl is odd. Eulerian oddness then uses an odd inverse-label map.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Curl completion preserves joint odd reflection

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For a nonzero covector and transverse input, the profile plus its curl completion has zero slow-plus-fast divergence. The hypotheses identify `G` with the derivative of a twice differentiable inverse chart `A` and `κ` with its adjoint applied to the launch covector. This proves the geometric claim at every phase, rather than merely along one evaluated graph.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The completed transverse profile is divergence free in the chart

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a time in the closed slab, applying the profile’s within-slab derivative to `(0,d,0)` equals the ordinary Fréchet derivative of its fixed-time, fixed-phase label slice applied to `d`. The label line remains entirely within the slab. This identifies the coordinate calculus used by the concrete hierarchy with familiar spatial derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The label component of the joint derivative is spatial differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For a positive slab length, this linear operator takes the joint within-slab derivative of a smooth vector profile and restricts it to label directions. Its output is a smooth profile of continuous linear maps. The following evaluation theorem identifies it with the ordinary label derivative on the slab, including endpoint times.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The profile derivative with time and phase fixed

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At any time in $[0,T]$, evaluating the profile label differential gives the ordinary Fréchet derivative of the label slice with time and phase fixed. Positive slab length ensures the joint derivative operator is valid. The spatial inclusion stays inside the slab, so no time-boundary extension is needed.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The encoded label differential is the ordinary spatial derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The slow divergence contracts the label derivative with the inverse-flow differential in the Eulerian directions.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Slow divergence is a coframe trace contraction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a point of the slab, evaluation of the averaged profile is the unit-period phase mean at the same time and label. The result explains the average operator used by the hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The bundled phase average equals the unit-period integral

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: The correction obtained by slow curl has zero phase average. In addition to positive slab length `hT` and nonzero covectors `hκ`, the named hypothesis `hG` requires the coframe to be independent of phase. The proof commutes phase averaging with the slow curl and uses the normalized potential's zero mean. This condition is natural for a coframe obtained from the parent flow, but it is essential to the abstract profile statement.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Slow curl completion has zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If `h` says that every on-slab phase slice is constant, its phase average equals the original profile. The proof identifies the integrand with a constant and uses the normalized average of a constant. Equality outside the slab follows from the common zero-extension representation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Averaging leaves a phase-independent profile unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If the coframe is independent of phase and the potential has zero phase average, its slow curl also has zero phase average. The proof commutes the label derivative through the phase integral and then applies the fixed linear curl map. The phase-independence hypothesis on `G` is essential to moving that coefficient outside the average.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl preserves zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: The smooth-profile potential has zero phase average. The named arguments `hT` and `hκ` provide a positive time slab and a nonzero phase-zero covector at every time and label. No mean-zero assumption on `V` is required for this normalization statement, because `phasePrimitive` subtracts the mean of its primitive by definition. Periodicity of the potential is a separate property, requiring periodic and mean-zero input.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Normalized wave potentials have zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Fast divergence pairs the covector with the phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: The evaluation formula for the slow curl differentiates $Q(t,a,s)$ only in the label variable, composes that derivative with the coframe `G`, and applies `curlOfDerivative`. The hypotheses are `hT : 0 < T` and the time membership `ht`; both profiles are already smooth by their types. This precisely identifies the one label derivative spent in forming the divergence correction, without asserting any quantitative norm bound by itself.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Slow curl differentiates labels at fixed phase

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: The slow divergence of a slow curl vanishes when its coframe comes from an actual inverse-label map. The time belongs to the closed slab by `ht`, with `hT` giving positive length. The coordinate sum in the conclusion is the paper's pulled-back divergence at fixed phase.

If the coframe and potential are each one-periodic in phase at a fixed time, their slow curl is one-periodic as well. Equality of phase-shifted potential slices gives equality of their label derivatives. The theorem does not need phase independence of the coframe, only the stated periodicity.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl preserves phase periodicity

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If the coframe and potential are even under joint reflection of labels and phase, taking the slow curl makes the result odd. A label derivative reverses the potential’s reflection sign, while the coframe does not change it. The statement holds for smooth profile representatives on a positive-length slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl of an even potential is odd

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The sum of slow and fast profile divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: On the slab, evaluating the total profile-divergence operator gives the sum of the coframe-weighted label trace and the covector paired with the phase derivative. This theorem unfolds both encoded operators into ordinary derivatives. It holds for any smooth input profile and does not require transversality or zero divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Total profile divergence is the slow trace plus phase contraction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If each inverse chart is surjective and twice differentiable, and the coframe and covector agree with its derivative, the completed transverse profile has total divergence zero as a profile-space equality. Surjectivity matters: it extends the cancellation from labels reached by the chart to every label and every phase on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Surjective inverse charts give divergence cancellation at every label

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For a phase-independent mean profile, zero physical divergence of its graph evaluation implies zero total profile divergence, provided the differentiable inverse charts are surjective and the geometric coefficients match them. Phase independence transfers the physical graph’s conclusion to arbitrary phase values. The solenoidal physical mean is an explicit hypothesis.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: A solenoidal physical mean has zero profile divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The actual phase primitive defining `Q[V]`. The covector is read at phase zero because the geometric covector is phase independent.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The phase primitive defining the vector potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: On the slab, the profile potential evaluates to the normalized phase primitive of the cross product with the covector at phase zero. The construction requires a nonzero covector; reading it at phase zero matches its later phase-independent use.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The bundled potential has the pointwise integral formula

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a fixed time and label, a one-periodic velocity profile with zero phase mean gives a one-periodic normalized wave potential. The covector is nonzero throughout the slab so the profile constructor is defined with its regularity proof. The statement does not require transversality because periodicity depends on the primitive’s mean, not on fast-curl inversion.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: A periodic zero-mean input has a periodic potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: With an even nonvanishing covector and an odd velocity under joint label-and-phase reflection, the normalized potential is even. The velocity must also have periodic zero-mean phase slices. Reversing phase changes the sign of integration, cancelling the input’s odd sign; the zero-mean normalization prevents an extra constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: An odd velocity has an even normalized potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.text: This linear operator takes the derivative of a smooth slab profile in the direction $(1,0,0)$. Time changes while label and phase remain fixed. Its input `hT : 0 < T` makes the closed slab a domain with unique derivatives. After graph evaluation the same operation corresponds to a material derivative, so it must not be read as a fixed-position Eulerian derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.summary: Differentiate a profile at fixed label and phase

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.text: At a point `z` belonging to the profile slab, `slabTimePartial` evaluates to the within-Fréchet derivative of the profile applied to $(1,0,0)$. The domain-membership hypothesis is essential because profile representatives are set to zero outside the slab. This gives the concrete meaning of the linear operator before its chain rule along the inverse flow.

For a smooth periodic parent flow, one time derivative of a profile at fixed label and phase becomes the material derivative of its evaluated physical field. The identity adds the ordinary Eulerian time derivative to the spatial derivative applied to the parent velocity. It holds on the closed time slab. This theorem states the first-order formula; repeated use supplies the higher-order identity in the auxiliary argument.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.summary: Material differentiation of an evaluated profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.smooth.text: A smooth profile carries smoothness within the closed time–label–phase slab. This projection of its membership condition is the regularity input for the concrete differential operators.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.smooth.summary: A bundled profile is smooth within its slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySourceTermBounds.text: This proposition bundles the exact mean decomposition, the zero-mean relay, three mean-product estimates, the parent residual estimate, and the relay, slow and fast transverse estimates. Derivative hypotheses are requested only when `n + 1 ≤ H`, and level hypotheses only from two through `P`. It is an input contract for assembly, not an existence theorem for those estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchySourceTermBounds.summary: The individual source estimates needed by the recurrence

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.text:
Local operations preserve vanishing on the inactive region. Slow advection of two means is again fixed by the phase average.

Default-value audit (b5): These are preservation properties supplied for an operator family. The record does not prove locality or support preservation for arbitrary linear maps.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.summary: Support properties of the hierarchy operations

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.construc.text: For depth at least one, propagates inactive-region membership through every oscillation, completion and oscillatory pressure, and through all retained transverse sources. It assumes support preservation of the selected transverse solver and completion. Means need only be fixed by averaging; neither their velocity nor their pressure is asserted to vanish on this region.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.construc.summary: The selected recursion keeps oscillations in the inactive submodule

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.remainde.text: Subtracts the retained tail sum of mean-mean label advections from the finite remainder and proves that the difference lies in the inactive submodule. All oscillations, completions and oscillatory pressures must be inactive. This identifies what remains; it does not assert that the full remainder vanishes outside the envelope.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.remainde.summary: Only slow products of means survive outside the oscillations

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.transver.text: At level at least two, assumes older oscillations, completions and pressures vanish on the inactive region, while every mean is fixed by averaging. The preliminary source differs there from a sum of mean-mean products; subtracting its average removes that sum. The supplementary source also vanishes because its differentiated oscillatory factor is inactive.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.transver.summary: Centering removes the surviving mean products outside the envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTransverseOutput.text:
Package an oscillatory velocity and pressure with zero phase mean and vanishing fast advection in every test direction. These are the algebraic constraints expected of a transverse hierarchy solve; the evolution equation is supplied by the solver separately.

Default-value audit (b5): The structure records velocity, pressure, zero phase mean, and zero fast self-advection constraints. It does not assert an ODE solve or nonzero amplitude, so the all-zero output is allowed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTransverseOutput.summary: A transverse oscillation with its pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.text:
This subtype imposes both period-one phase dependence and simultaneous label–phase lattice invariance on a smooth slab profile. These are exact function identities, not properties of a chosen Fourier approximation.

Default-value audit (b5): The underlying representative is zero outside the slab, with smoothness and twisted periodicity on its stored domain. The abbreviation adds no existence assertion for nonzero waves.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.summary: The space of twisted periodic slab profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Label.text: This predicate asks that the phase-zero label slice be spatially periodic at every time of the slab. It does not by itself assert phase independence or periodicity at other phase values. Those additional facts are supplied when phase-independent coefficients or phase averages are sent to the torus mean solver.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Stores the deformation, inverse, material strain and time derivative on the label torus, with their evolution equations and exact profile values. Both inverse identities, finite coefficient bounds and the one-sided endpoint Hessian inequality are required. These are hypotheses for a real endpoint problem, not merely names for arbitrary bounded matrices.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The deformation data required by the endpoint mean solver

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Requires the deformation, inverse and strain lifts to be even at every time in the closed slab. This property is used only when selecting the odd mean and even pressure from an endpoint solution. It does not assert oddness of the forcing or automatically establish parity of the solved fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The mean coefficients are even in their spatial labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Uses the record’s `inverse_value` identity to show that the coframe profile has the same value at every phase. It is a lift of a torus coefficient depending only on time and label. This independence is needed for averaging and for slow advection of mean fields to remain a mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The inverse coframe profile is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: When the transverse covector agrees with the adjoint inverse deformation applied to the carrier, the mean geometry supplies smooth lift and pullback maps. They satisfy the time-evolution law, a left-inverse identity, and the transverse-projection identity. The theorem also proves the covector is nonzero on the active interval, using the geometric data rather than assuming an arbitrary projection.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The mean geometry supplies transverse coordinates and projection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Assume the central wave, coframe and strain bounds, compatibility of the covector, and the displayed small label-variation condition. Every fixed-plane homogeneous solution at a label within $2\ell$ of a lattice point has weighted growth at most $eD^3$. The theorem also supplies the positive central norm and its continuous within-interval derivative. The interval length is bounded by `T ≤ 1`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The central wave controls forward growth on the envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: At any time in the closed slab, the generator formed from the transverse strain, lift and pullback is spatially periodic in the label. This lets the forward stability estimate near the origin be transferred to every periodic copy of the envelope. The theorem states an exact periodicity property, not a bound on the generator.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The fixed-plane generator is periodic in the label

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text:
The parent deformation lifts the fixed launch plane into the moving transverse plane.

Default-value audit (b5): The map is defined on the orthogonal complement of the launch covector. For k=0 that domain is the whole space; the actual launch assumptions exclude zero before treating it as a two-dimensional plane.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: Lifting the launch plane into the transported plane

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text:
The inverse parent deformation reads the coordinates of the transverse projection in the fixed launch plane.

Default-value audit (b5): The projected pullback is defined for arbitrary coefficient values. Its inverse relationship with the lift requires the coframe identities and a nonzero transported covector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: Reading fixed coordinates after transverse projection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanR.text: Packages a mean output together with divergence-free label velocity, displacement vanishing at both endpoints, and the physical-component relation `B = F v`. It keeps the raw endpoint solution and states whether the output is unchanged or its odd part. Recovery and nonincreasing label-norm fields preserve quantitative information through that optional symmetry selection.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanR.summary: One endpoint mean with its normalization and recovery data

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paper.text: Packages the qualitative approximation properties, oscillation and mean Hölder bounds, residual estimate, signed pressure-Hessian cap, central-gradient error and perturbed-flow deformation for one fixed `PhysicalApproximationData`. Every field concerns that same hierarchy and parent graph. The cutoff, `switchSize` and cost parameters are supplied freely; their identification with the paper quantities belongs to constructors. This proposition requires the listed facts rather than establishing them by its definition.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paper.summary: The physical estimates for one common approximation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text:
Exact coefficients with their physical values on the parent label slab.

Default-value audit (b5): The coefficient profiles are tied by value equalities to the specified U, X and k. The record also contains analytic mean and transverse data. These obligations must be constructed; they are not inferred from arbitrary profile fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The physical coefficients carried by the parent geometry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Builds the physical leading input from the explicit stationary-shear velocity and pressure profiles. The hypotheses require a nonzero carrier, a positive envelope fitting inside the centered cell, and phase width in $(0,1]$, as well as the exact parent and flow identifications. Both switch sources are zero because this first wave is already present at activation. Momentum, parity and transverse equations are included as proof fields.

For any set `S` containing the support of the periodized radial envelope, the constructed leading input satisfies `Inactive 0 S`. The proof uses vanishing of that envelope for both velocity and phase pressure; the two switch sources are identically zero. The conclusion is restricted to the hierarchy slab through the definition of `Inactive`, rather than an assertion about every real time.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The first profiles vanish outside the envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Under `hU` and `hX`, the parent velocity and two-time flow are exactly the stationary shear and its flow. The theorem identifies the general twisted hierarchy operators with the explicit first-wave operators by comparing the inverse deformation, material gradient and transported covector. It licenses reuse of the explicit wave equations for the actual parent geometry; it does not select that geometry.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The stationary shear gives the same operators

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Proves surjectivity of the inverse parent chart and evaluates the coframe and covector on that chart. They become its Jacobian and the adjoint Jacobian applied to the carrier. The identities use the actual flow inverse relation, providing the chain-rule data needed when profiles are read as physical fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The profile coframe becomes the actual inverse-chart derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Converts the parent-geometry reflection theorem into the `MeanCoefficients.Even` predicate for the exact selected coefficient record. The value identities tie the profile inverse and strain to their torus lifts. This lets the mean solver’s conditional symmetry clause apply to an odd forcing without selecting a new coefficient system.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The selected mean coefficients have the required even symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: For a divergence-free smooth periodic parent and a certified mean result, proves zero total profile divergence of the physical-component mean. Phase independence removes the fast derivative. The slow part follows from the volume-preserving parent deformation and divergence-free label velocity through the Piola identity, rather than from phase averaging alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The physical mean is divergence free in profile coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text:
The completion loses one spatial derivative and gains a factor $\lambda^{-1}$; its material derivative plus the label pressure gradient obeys the same gain. The inputs include `d : ParentGeometry ...`, the standing parent bounds, a width exponent `a ≥ 16`, and any continuous positive weight `γ`. Zero phase mean and transversality are required for `V`. The second estimate also requires zero means for `F` and `q` and the active-slab momentum equation. The parent power is explicitly $2(15+a)$, independent of derivative order.

Scope comparison: the library hypotheses `A.average V = 0` and `A.average F = 0` hold on the whole closed slab, while the paper passage is read in the active-slab setting. This helper also permits an arbitrary positive continuous time weight and receives explicit parent jet bounds. These changes are mixed in direction; a general active-slab extension adapter preserving all constraints is not provided or checked in this return.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: Completion and linear relay gain one frequency power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: The actual unswitched leading profiles admit representatives on the full profile slab whose active values, pressure, and completion are the raw leading fields. The hypotheses include the parent bounds and `w.HierarchyRegularity r h`, with a continuous positive weight. The theorem identifies those representatives on $[t_0,T]$ and proves the completion and relay bounds there with no forcing norm. This supplies the homogeneous case without assuming that an unswitched leading field was already zero before activation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The unswitched leading correction satisfies the homogeneous relay estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Specializes the mean-result divergence theorem to the exact output chosen by `physicalSolvers`. It requires the actual parent flow, smooth periodic divergence-free velocity, and `T ≤ 1` for the endpoint solver. This supplies a concrete zero-divergence certificate for the physical graph construction without changing the selected mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The selected mean solve satisfies the graph divergence requirement

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: For an actual odd smooth periodic parent flow, proves evenness of the inverse coframe, material strain, transported covector and deformation at labels. Oddness of the flow and evenness of the derivative of an odd map supply the sign relations. Profile parity outside the slab uses their zero representative convention.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: An odd parent gives even deformation, strain and covector

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: The transverse covector of `ParentGeometry` equals the adjoint mean inverse applied to the fixed carrier at every slab point. This is the compatibility relation needed by the fixed transverse coordinate system. It identifies two representations of the same wave vector without introducing a new quantitative bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The carrier is pulled back by the inverse coframe

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: At a slab time and label, `ParentGeometry` identifies its mean inverse with the derivative of the inverse flow evaluated along the forward flow, its strain with the physical velocity gradient there, and its covector with `labelWaveVector`. These are exact value identities connecting the stored coefficient profiles to the parent field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: Read the transverse coefficients from the parent flow

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.text: Records that the integral over one phase period vanishes for every time on $[0,T]$ and every label. The field is already a smooth twisted profile; this predicate adds its normalization. It is used when taking periodic phase primitives and when multiplying by coefficients independent of phase. It contains no estimate on the profile's size.

If `f` has zero phase mean and the operator-valued profile `c` is phase-independent on the slab, their pointwise application has zero phase mean. Completeness of the input and output spaces supports the phase integrals. At each time and label the fixed bounded linear map passes through the integral, so its application to the mean is zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.summary: A phase independent coefficient preserves the zero mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.text: If `hf` gives zero phase mean for a smooth profile, every time jet has zero phase mean on the same nondegenerate slab. The proof applies the earlier derivative-of-average theorem. This preserves the normalization needed to apply the phase primitive repeatedly while differentiating the auxiliary oscillatory hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.summary: Time differentiation preserves the zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Combines $T \le  1$, a physical leading input, and a phase-independent odd profile whose value on the slab equals the parent momentum residual pulled back by `X 0 t`. The pressure `p` and parent geometry are fixed parameters. The depth `P` indexes later constructions but is not constrained by the structure; existence does not establish the quantitative approximation estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Parent residual and data for the finite expansion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This predicate requires a graph-evaluated profile time derivative of order $j$ to have spatial derivative bound $CB^m$ whenever $j\le q$ and $j+m\le N$. Time derivatives are taken on the profile before graph evaluation, so they are material derivatives after a flow readout. The total-order restriction is part of the predicate; it does not assert all pairs with $j\le q,m\le N$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Geometric spatial bounds for material profile time derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This proposition records zero phase mean for the leading pressure and activation force, transversality of that force, and equality of `completionSwitch` with its selected completion. It does not store a new solution or numerical estimate. Together with the leading momentum equation already in the physical data, these fields justify the level-two relay cancellation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The leading wave normalization needed by the first correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: From `LeadingRelayData`, the stored completion switch has zero phase average. The proof rewrites it as completion of the activation force and uses the finite solver’s centering property with the supplied zero-force-mean field. This makes the switch suitable for both the averaged-source cancellation and the recurrence assembly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The leading normalization centers the completion switch

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Defines the profile multiplying the activation derivative as the centered wrapped unswitched leading velocity plus its wrapped slow curl completion. It is a raw function of time, label, and phase. The definition itself does not claim time smoothness across activation; subsequent residual formulas only require its regularity on slices where the switch derivative is nonzero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Unswitched leading velocity together with its completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a time on the parent slab, assumes two jets of the wrapped unswitched leading velocity, three jets of its actual wave potential, and two radius-weighted inverse-coframe jets. It bounds the activation primary by $\mathrm{BV} + \lVert \mathrm{curlOfDerivativeCLM}\rVert \cdot \ell^{-1}\cdot 4\cdot \mathrm{BP}\cdot \mathrm{BG}$. The identity uses the actual inverse deformation from parent geometry; the jet estimates are hypotheses, not consequences of the seed interface alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Two primary jets follow from the exact wrapped potential

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a hierarchy-regular active seed, assumes three scaled jets of the raw unswitched leading velocity, three scaled potential-coefficient jets, and two radius-weighted inverse-coframe jets. Centered wrapping and the normalized potential estimate then give two jets of the actual activation primary. The explicit budget is $\mathrm{BV} + \lVert \mathrm{curlOfDerivativeCLM}\rVert \cdot \ell^{-1}\cdot 4\cdot (16\cdot \mathrm{BK}\cdot \mathrm{BV})\cdot \mathrm{BG}$, exposing every finite derivative cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Three leading jets control two completed activation jets

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a slab time where the switch derivative is nonzero, the unswitched primary profile is smooth in label and phase. Its product with the switch derivative is already a smooth profile; division by this nonzero time-only scalar recovers the primary. The theorem intentionally makes no such inference on slices where that derivative vanishes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Recover primary smoothness on an active switch slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: When `b.leading` is exactly the later-wave input built from the stated seed and parent, the sum of its two switch profiles at every slab slice equals the derivative of the time switch times `activationPrimary`. The identity uses the same coframe and transported covector as the hierarchy and applies to all labels and phases.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Both activation sources share one time factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At depth $P\ge2$, the last retained velocity is a selected transverse correction with no activation switch. Its material completion plus label pressure gradient is bounded by the normalized relay estimate applied to its actual source. The right side uses measured oscillation and source sizes at order $n+1$, multiplied by one inverse frequency.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The last retained wave controls the linear tail

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming $2 \le  P$, a smooth periodic odd divergence-free parent, smooth periodic even pressure, and the parent label flow, derives `PhysicalApproximationProperties b`. It discharges the previous theorem’s mean-divergence premise using the physical solver’s Piola identity. The conclusion remains qualitative: numerical size and pressure estimates are proved separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected hierarchy satisfies the qualitative approximation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The selected finite hierarchy has smooth velocity and pressure, the required parities, zero divergence and its exact residual. The assumptions `hP : 2 ≤ P`, `hX`, `hU`, `hp`, `hper`, `hpper`, `hodd` and `hdiv` describe the smooth odd solenoidal parent and its flow. The datum `b` already identifies the parent residual with the physical one and records its oddness. The proof derives pressure parity from these facts, so a separate even-pressure assumption is unnecessary.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The constructed approximation satisfies the physical equations

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At an index in levels two through `P`, the actual mean forcing is fixed by the hierarchy average. The averaged source is already phase independent, and the parent residual has the same property. This supplies the correct input condition for the selected mean solve and later label-only norm comparisons.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Every retained mean source is phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a level between two and `P`, the relay’s phase average vanishes if the leading pressure and completion switch are centered. The proof identifies the previous completion with the selected curl construction, obtains its zero mean, and combines this with the retained pressure normalization. This isolates the linear contribution from the mean source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected linear relay has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a retained level, the phase average of the actual source before the mean solve is a sum of oscillation advection, divergence–oscillation products, and mean–mean advection. The theorem uses the genuine inverse label flow, zero pressure mean, and centered switch. Its proof imports the geometric cancellation that replaces the fast averaged product by a slow derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected mean source contains exactly three slow products

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For every correction field `v`, the velocity passed to `ChildFlow.childVelocity` equals the already defined physical approximate velocity plus `v`. The identity is definitional and ensures that the flow estimate and cutoff estimate refer to the same field. Smoothness, smallness, and divergence conditions on `v` are imposed only when applying those estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The child flow uses the same approximate velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This definition is six times the product of the numbers of admissible mixed words through orders $n$ and $n+1$, multiplied by $2^n2^{n+1}$. It collects the combinatorial factors in the completion estimate. Parent geometry, frequency, and input norms are deliberately kept outside this order-only quantity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The explicit derivative-count factor in the curl estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The uncut leading velocity together with its curl completion has a scaled two-jet bound $C\mathsf D^{a+27}\lambda^{-5/4}\gamma(t)$. The theorem first fixes constants from the parent velocity table `W` and `hW`, then assumes the parent flow bounds, carrier normalization and `CenterWaveOn`. The selected `w : SeedOn ...` and its `HierarchyRegularity` determine the actual primary field. This estimate supplies `hPrimary` in the residual theorem for a general cutoff.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Two-derivative bound for the uncut leading wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume a profile vanishes off a closed subset of the active interval, and its positive weight is bounded by $C_\gamma$ on that support. Weighted profile-derivative bounds, the stated readout-map coefficient controls, and `hWave` then give a graph bound with amplitude $C_\gamma\mathrm{freq}^{\alpha}$ and spatial rate $\mathrm{freq}^2$. Outside the support all time derivatives vanish. This retains the smaller amplitude available only on the switching interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Closed support preserves the small activation amplitude

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For positive depth, this converts the actual factorial norms of the mean, oscillation, remainder, and switch profiles into their four `GeometricGraphJet` bounds. It assumes inverse-flow coefficient bounds, the carrier-rate absorption `hWave`, inactivity before activation, and closed switch support. The mean retains rate $D^{a+1}$; the other terms use $\mathrm{freq}^2$. The switch amplitude keeps the support bound $\Gamma$, and every amplitude pays the extraction factor $q!T^{-q}$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected hierarchy supplies four distinct graph bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a smooth periodic parent with its label flow, the inverse label map and the coframe $B(a)=D(X(t,0))(X(0,t,a))$ are smooth at every slab time. Evaluating `B` at the inverse label of an Eulerian point returns the inverse flow derivative at that point. The proof uses the actual flow inverse identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The graph coframe is the inverse flow derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This real expression collects the graph differentiation cost, retained higher-level count, coefficient jet bounds and level-loss factors in the higher-pressure estimate. It contains no carrier-frequency decay itself; the theorem multiplies it by $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/12}$. Its purpose is to expose how constants depend on depth and parent coefficients.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The explicit coefficient in the higher-pressure Hessian estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This scalar field is the physical graph of the sum of selected transverse pressures at levels two through `P`. The leading pressure is excluded. This separation is needed because the higher terms are bounded in operator norm using the transverse equation, while the leading term is controlled by a one-sided Hessian estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Read the higher selected oscillatory pressures together

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The actual oscillatory correction vanishes before activation or outside the transported common label envelope. The parent hierarchy has depth at least one and a closed label support, and its leading data satisfy the common inactivity conditions. On the same region the residual is exactly the slow mean-product tail. This result localizes the oscillations and their divergence completions; it does not assert that the mean correction or the Fourier truncation difference is supported there.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Oscillations vanish outside the transported envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The leading-pressure field is the inverse-label graph of the pressure component of the selected leading output. It refers to the same leading input used to construct the hierarchy. To apply the signed seed estimate, a later theorem explicitly identifies this output pressure with the regular seed’s twisted pressure.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume the leading output pressure is exactly the twisted pressure of the supplied regular seed, and that seed has a primary budget at every slab time. For a smooth periodic parent flow, the actual `leadingPressure` then satisfies the explicit signed Hessian upper bound. The equality hypothesis `hSeed` prevents applying a seed estimate to an unrelated selected pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Transfer the signed seed estimate to the selected leading pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Reads `b.leading.output.V` on the same inverse-flow phase graph used for the complete approximation. It isolates the leading wave from the rest of the retained oscillation. This definition does not require $P \ge  1$; identifying it as the first term of the retained sum is a separate theorem with that depth hypothesis.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Eulerian readout of the prescribed leading wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If `hL` identifies the approximation's leading input with the explicit first-wave input, evaluating its velocity on the physical phase graph recovers the localized transported profile. The equality holds for `t` in the closed slab. The inverse flow is the stationary shear at negative time, so the phase and label substitutions are the ones used in the explicit first-wave construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Reading the first profile gives its physical wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Reads the phase average of the retained profile velocity along the inverse parent flow. This produces the Eulerian mean correction, whose profile is independent of phase. It is separated from the oscillatory correction because its estimates and support differ: the mean may extend throughout the torus and before the wave activates.

For at least one retained level and a smooth periodic divergence-free parent flow, the actual physical mean correction has zero spatial divergence at all slab times. The proof uses the selected mean divergence equations and the physical graph identity. This supplies a necessary hypothesis when taking divergence of the summed physical momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical mean correction is divergence free

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For `1 ≤ P`, the physical mean correction equals the graph of the sum of selected mean profiles from level two through `P`. The first mean profile is zero by construction. This identity links the velocity field already used by the approximation to exactly the mean sum appearing in the pressure calculation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The mean velocity begins at the second level

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The phase average of the retained velocity equals the sum of the selected mean profiles on the Eulerian graph. The displayed Lean sum starts at level one, whereas the paper starts at two; the construction has $B_1=0$. The datum `b` fixes all levels and their solvers, so this is an identity for the actual expansion, rather than a choice of an unrelated mean field.

The mean correction has $C^{m,1/2}$ size bounded by a parent power times $\lambda^{-5/2}$. The hypothesis `hlevels` controls the actual hierarchy through the requested orders, and `hProperties` supplies smoothness. The bounds `hLabel`, `hCoeff` and `hLossScale` control composition with the inverse labels. The statement treats `m ≤ q` with one coefficient chosen for that finite range; varying `q` yields every order in the paper. No fast phase factor is spent on the mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Higher derivatives of the mean correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The sum of the selected mean corrections solves the physical linearized Euler equation over $U$, with its own summed mean pressure and force. The assumptions `hP : 1 ≤ P`, `hX`, `hU` and `hper` give the actual hierarchy and smooth periodic parent flow. Lean uses `derivWithin` on the closed interval for the time derivative. The force is built from the same selected mean equations, so no independent source is introduced.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The summed means satisfy linearized Euler momentum

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The physical mean forcing is the inverse-label graph of the sum of `meanForceAt i` over levels two through `P`. This sums the actual forcing records, including the single parent-residual contribution at level two. It is a concrete velocity-valued function whose momentum identity and estimates are established subsequently.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the selected mean sources on the physical graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This definition takes the negative phase average of the hierarchy source at index `i` and subtracts the parent residual exactly when `i = 2`. It is the actual mean forcing used by the selected construction. The function is defined at every natural index, but its equation and estimates are invoked on retained levels two through `P`.

The mean-pressure field is the graph of the finite sum of selected scalar pressures `q i` at levels two through `P`. This retains the actual pressure supplied by each mean solve. It does not replace those pressures with an independently chosen Poisson solution; the Poisson equation is derived from their summed linearized momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the selected mean pressures on the physical graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The mean pressure satisfies $\Delta\bar q=\operatorname{div}\bar f-2\operatorname{tr}(\nabla U\,\nabla\bar W)$. The hypotheses `hX`, `hU`, `hper` and `hdiv` give a smooth periodic solenoidal parent, and `hP : 1 ≤ P` identifies the retained mean sum. The proof differentiates its linearized momentum equation and uses solenoidality of the selected mean correction. The operator composition inside `LinearMap.trace` is the matrix product in the paper.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Poisson equation for the summed mean pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume the measured levels of the chosen physical approximation satisfy the order-two bounds. Then the unweighted seminorms of its summed means and actual mean sources are bounded by the same level-count factor times $C\,\mathrm{loss}^6\mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. This specializes the abstract finite-sum estimate to the exact sources stored in the physical construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The actual mean velocity and force share one finite bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The sum of the central derivatives of the higher oscillation and the mean correction is $O(\lambda^{-5/12})$. The hypotheses `hOsc` and `hMean` supply their order-one profile bounds at rates $\lambda^{-23/12}$ and $\lambda^{-5/2}$, while `hcoeff` controls the inverse coframe. The weight satisfies `hγle : γ ≤ 1` on the activation interval. The paper’s $\lambda^{-1/3}$ error follows after the separate small-step inequality absorbs another factor $\lambda^{-1/12}$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The central remainder has decay lambda to minus five twelfths

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume inactive leading data on a closed support, positive envelope length, prescribed phase width, a positive weight bounded by one, controlled coefficient jets and actual level bounds at orders one and two. Then the higher oscillatory pressure Hessian is bounded on the entire slab by its explicit prefactor times $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/12}$. Support propagation supplies zero pressure before activation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The actual higher pressures obey the full-slab Hessian bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the actual physical approximation, parent flow and incompressibility hypotheses establish the summed linearized equation and divergence constraint. Together with second-order bounds on the selected mean and forcing sums, controlled inverse coframe jets, and a parent-gradient Hölder bound, this gives the displayed Hessian norm estimate with frequency decay $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. The bound is for the actual selected mean pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected mean pressure has the expected small Hessian

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Abbreviates `twistedHierarchyOperators` built from the inverse deformation, strain, and transported covector of `d`. The `_data` argument makes the operators accessible from approximation data, but its contents do not change the operator choice. These are the same parent operators used for the transverse, mean, and curl completion equations.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Operators determined by the parent geometry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Subtracts the phase average from the full retained velocity and reads the result on the graph determined by the inverse parent flow `X t 0`. The result is the Eulerian oscillatory correction. Removing the average here is algebraic; the later graph-sum identity identifies it with the completed transverse levels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Eulerian readout of the zero mean oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The nonleading oscillation is evaluated on the inverse-label graph for the selected physical approximation. The stored sum is the completion of level one plus the velocities and their completions from levels two through $P$. Translating the source-indexed completion storage into the revised manuscript gives $\sum_{p=2}^P V_p+\sum_{p=2}^{P+1}C_p$. This declaration defines the Eulerian graph of that profile, rather than the unevaluated profile itself.

For `PhysicalApproximationData b` and `hP : 1 ≤ P`, the physical oscillation remainder equals the inverse-label graph of the total profile minus its phase average and first transverse profile. This is equality of velocity fields, with no estimate. The depth hypothesis identifies the selected first profile with the leading input. Later bounds differentiate this exact remainder at the origin.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Remove the leading wave from the centered expansion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming at least one retained level, the physical oscillation remainder is the graph of the full retained profile minus its phase average and its first transverse velocity. The construction identifies that first velocity with the given leading output. This equality connects the named physical remainder to the measured profile sum used in the central estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical remainder is the leading-subtracted oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: From order-one actual level bounds, a controlled inverse-flow coframe, admissible label and phase scales, and a loss bound $\mathrm{loss} \le  K \cdot  D^c$, bounds the physical remainder’s derivative on the active slab. Its frequency decay is $-5/12$, obtained from $-23/12$ after one carrier derivative costs $3/2$. The displayed constant retains depth cardinality, coframe, and loss dependence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One physical derivative leaves a decaying oscillatory remainder

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Under `IsLabelFlowOn`, smoothness of the parent on the closed slab, and spatial periodicity, the Eulerian higher oscillation remainder is jointly smooth on that slab. The argument combines smooth retained profiles with smooth inverse labels. This is qualitative regularity; it does not establish the small derivative bound used for the central error.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Smoothness of the higher oscillation on the graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Identifies the zero-mean part of the constructed velocity with the graph of the sum of $V_i+C_i$ over $1\le i\le P$. The Lean completion `C i` belongs to velocity `V i`; the paper denotes that completion by $C_{i+1}$. The equality comes from the solver construction and includes the empty-depth case.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The oscillation is the sum of completed levels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming `hP : 1 ≤ P`, splits the oscillation into the prescribed leading velocity and `oscillationRemainder`. The proof separates the first summand and uses that the constructed `V 1` is the given leading output. The remainder includes the leading curl completion as well as all transverse and completion terms from levels two onward.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Separate the leading wave from the oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming the leading transverse profile is zero on the initial slice, the physical oscillatory velocity is identically zero at time zero. The proof includes all retained transverse profiles and their completions, using completion’s preservation of a zero slice. No lower bound on retained depth is needed for this statement; an empty sum also vanishes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical oscillation vanishes initially

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: With $P \ge  1$, a closed support set, $0 < \tau$, and inactive leading data, the Eulerian oscillation vanishes whenever $t \le  \tau$ or the inverse label lies outside that set. The non-strict time inequality includes the activation slice. The theorem concerns the oscillation only; mean corrections need not vanish there.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The oscillation vanishes through a positive activation time

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For positive retained depth, closed label support and nonnegative activation time, inactive leading data imply that the physical oscillation vanishes through activation and outside the transported support. When activation equals zero, `hLead` explicitly supplies the leading zero initial slice. This extra endpoint premise avoids inferring a boundary value from an empty interval of earlier slab times.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Include the activation endpoint in the vanishing statement

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The physical oscillation is bounded by $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-5/4}$ uniformly in time and space. The assumptions `hlevels` give the actual hierarchy bounds at order zero, `hinactive` makes the oscillation vanish before $t_0$, and `hγmax` states $\gamma\le1$. The coefficient inequality `hBudget` absorbs the finite sum of levels. The proof evaluates the weighted profile estimate on the graph without paying a spatial derivative cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The oscillatory velocity has size lambda to minus five quarters

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The flow of $V+v$ and its inverse have derivative bound $\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b\lambda^{1/4}$. The arbitrary perturbation is smooth and periodic by `hv` and `hvPer`, solenoidal by `hvDiv`, and satisfies the order-two bound `hvSize`. The actual hierarchy bounds `hLevels` through order two and `hsmall` control the lifted particle flow. The conclusion `DeformationOn` includes the flow equation, lattice compatibility and inverse maps as well as both derivative bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The perturbed flow has polynomial deformation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The approximate velocity satisfies Euler momentum with the retained tail and activation residual. The binder `props : PhysicalApproximationProperties b` supplies smoothness, parity, solenoidality and the exact momentum identity; this declaration extracts them and splits the residual into two graph terms. It is therefore a statement readout, not the construction of those properties. `assemble_of_parent` establishes the required `props` from the standing parent assumptions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The approximate Euler equation and its two residuals

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The oscillatory velocity has $C^{m,1/2}$ size $C_{m,P}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{3(m+1)/2-5/4}$. The input `hlevels` provides the measured hierarchy estimates at order $m+1$, while `hcoeff` controls the coframe to that order. The hypotheses `hExp` and `hr` ensure that the chosen step exponent absorbs the parent losses. The estimate is valid on the whole interval because `hinactive` handles times before activation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Higher derivatives of the oscillatory velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a fixed approximation of positive depth, assumes its qualitative properties, all-order actual level estimates, a positive amplitude weight bounded by one, inactivity before launch and coframe jet bounds. It derives the oscillatory and mean Hölder estimates with the explicit prefactors above. Scale assumptions and the `hGraph` and `hLoss` exponent inequalities remain inputs; the theorem does not establish the level recurrence itself.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Physical Hölder estimates from the measured levels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The higher oscillatory pressure Hessian has size $O(\lambda^{-5/12})$, and the mean pressure Hessian has size $O(\lambda^{-5/2})$, with parent-dependent powers written explicitly. The common inputs `hLevels` are the actual hierarchy bounds through order two. The coframe, adjoint, strain and projection bounds support the oscillatory estimate. The mean estimate uses the parent-gradient bound `hParent` and the summed mean equation. Both conclusions concern the pressures of the same datum `b`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Higher and mean pressure Hessians decay at different rates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Identifies the approximation’s leading velocity and pressure with a supplied regular seed, then combines its `PrimaryPressureBudget` with a smooth periodic odd parent flow. It proves a signed upper Hessian bound on the entire slab and the exact rank-one central gradient with the selected `waveSwitch`. The full approximation’s higher corrections and central error are outside this declaration.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Reading the seed pressure and central gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The leading, higher and mean pressure bounds combine into a one-sided Hessian bound, and the velocity gradient at the origin is the leading rank-one tensor plus an error of size $\lambda^{-1/3}$. This assembly theorem takes `hLead`, `hHigher`, `hMean` and `hLeading` as inputs. It also uses measured order-one levels, coframe bounds and `hsmall`. The same hierarchy supplies all these quantities; the general physical-step construction establishes the inputs before calling this theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Pressure upper bound and the central gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The forcing of the level-$i$ mean equation is the negative phase average of its preliminary source, with the transported parent residual subtracted only at $i=2$. The input `b : PhysicalApproximationData d p P` fixes the actual physical expansion and parent residual. Thus this definition follows the special first mean equation and the uniform rule at higher levels. It is the source whose unweighted norm enters the mean estimates and their finite sum.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The mean source includes the parent residual at level two

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For supplied physical approximation data, the constructed profiles satisfy the finite-sum formulas, zero divergence, exact momentum residual, support and total-field smoothness. The assumptions specify a smooth periodic incompressible parent and the leading inactive region. The library stores the correction of $V_p$ as `u.C p`, which is the revised manuscript\'s $C_{p+1}$. This theorem concerns that constructed family; the new Paper statement separately asserts seed existence and uniqueness among all families satisfying the recursion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The finite hierarchy satisfies the exact residual identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Bounds at all retained levels control the weighted oscillatory part and the unweighted sums of means and mean sources. The hypotheses `hLevels` concern `actualMeasuredLevels`, so they measure the constructed profiles rather than arbitrary scalar proxies. The theorem sums them using the seminorm triangle inequality and $\lambda\ge1$. Its conclusion uses `paperMeanSource`, retaining the parent residual in the first mean equation, and subtracts the phase average to identify the oscillatory part.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Retained bounds control the oscillatory and mean sums

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The strain profile stored in the physical approximation data is phase independent. This is read from its physical value as a pulled-back parent gradient and is used in averaging and cancellation identities.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The parent strain has no phase dependence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume a smooth periodic parent flow, parent mixed derivative bounds, and `GeometricGraphJet` bounds for the actual mean, oscillation, tail, and switch profiles. Then Eulerian time derivatives of the mean and full velocity have spatial half Hölder bounds when $i+m+1\le N$; the residual has order-one half Hölder bounds when $i+2\le N$. The mean keeps its smaller spatial rate, while the oscillatory terms use the larger carrier rate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Four graph bounds give the physical time estimates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Turns the approximate pressure at time `t` into an `EndpointSmoothPotential` using smoothness and periodicity from `PhysicalApproximationProperties`. On the slab its lift is the actual approximate pressure. Off the slab the definition deliberately chooses the zero potential, making a total family available to the Fourier-cutoff interface.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: A periodic pressure potential on each slab slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a time $t \in  [0,T]$, the lift of `b.potential h t` is exactly `b.pressure t`. The proof selects the in-slab branch of the definition. This identity is used to rewrite the cutoff interface’s pressure gradient back to the pressure in the physical momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The slice potential equals the approximate pressure
