TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: The amplitude-weighted norm of $(Z\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY$ is controlled by the unweighted norm of `Z`, the next-order weighted norm of `Y`, and the norm of `scaledPhaseCoefficientProfile h κ`. The hypotheses `hh`, `hγ`, and `hpos` require a nonzero phase scale and a positive continuous amplitude on the active interval. The factor $\lambda^{3/2}$ in the paper comes from bounding the scaled covector $h^{-1}\kappa$ when $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Phase advection has one additional phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For the product $(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y$, this version assigns the reciprocal amplitude to `V`, which is measured at order $n+1$. The second factor uses the full-slab unweighted order-$n$ norm. The theorem allows the declared Hölder flag and obtains the same $3Q_n^2L$ coframe cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Weighting the factor inside the divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: Here the amplitude weight is assigned to `Y`, while the differentiated factor `V` is measured in the unweighted order-$(n+1)$ norm. The estimate applies on the active interval with positive continuous `γ`, nonzero label width, and the supplied scaled-row bound. This placement is needed for mixed mean–oscillation interactions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Weighting the factor outside the divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: An operator-valued twisted profile acts pointwise on a vector-valued profile with the same carrier. Each factor repeats under the same joint shift, so the result does too. This bilinear operation retains smoothness and phase periodicity and supports the concrete hierarchy’s coefficient multiplications.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: Apply compatible operator and vector profiles pointwise

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: At a point `x` of the profile slab, `applyField A f` evaluates to the continuous linear map `A x` applied to `f x`. This exposes the ordinary pointwise meaning of the bundled bilinear operation. The lemma is used to turn equalities of profile values into the Leibniz identities needed for the time norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: Evaluate an operator profile on a vector profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: The underlying periodic output of pointwise application in the twisted space is the corresponding periodic application of the two underlying inputs. This definitional equality exposes the original operation. It lets the proof of a concrete equation ignore the additional lattice-symmetry wrapper without losing that certified property.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: The twisted product retains ordinary operator application

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The coefficient-independent twisted phase average is the actual unit-period integral.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The twisted average is the unit-period integral

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The lattice-compatible correction has zero phase average. This supplies the completion law of the finite solver.

For the constructed hierarchy, the phase average of the source equals the three slow-product sums. The hypotheses identify the selected completion with the concrete curl completion, impose phase-independent geometric coefficients and zero-mean selected pressures, and require a surjective label map with the correct coframe. The result establishes the cancellations that the abstract assembly lemma previously assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The selected twisted hierarchy has the exact averaged source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: If `C` has zero operator average and `D` agrees on the slab with a scalar time multiple of `C`, then `D` also has zero average. The theorem uses pointwise equality `hD` and does not demand differentiability of the scalar function. This handles the activation multiplier in the leading completion relay.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: A time multiplier preserves zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The abstract averaging operator evaluates to the ordinary one-period phase mean of the profile at fixed time and label. It identifies the algebraic hierarchy source split with the paper's averaging convention.
The concrete phase-average operator is idempotent. Taking a second full-period average therefore leaves the first average unchanged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Averaging a mean profile leaves it unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: A hierarchy average is a phase-independent, label-periodic mean profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Averaging produces a periodic mean profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The phase average of label advection by a zero-mean oscillation on a phase-independent mean is zero. The hypotheses `hG`, `hY`, and `hB` provide phase independence of the coframe, zero phase average of the oscillation, and phase independence of the mean. The result explains one of the mixed products removed from the averaged hierarchy source. It is an identity of the actual twisted-profile operators, rather than a numerical estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: An oscillation advecting a mean has zero average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The phase average of label advection by a phase-independent mean on a zero-mean oscillation vanishes. The assumptions `hG`, `hB`, and `hY` express phase independence of the coframe and mean and zero phase mean of the oscillation. Differentiation in the label commutes with phase averaging for these smooth profiles. Together with the reverse mixed-product identity, this leaves only two-oscillation and two-mean interactions in the averaged source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: A mean advecting an oscillation has zero average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The product of two phase-independent means under slow advection is phase independent.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Slow advection of means is phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: Assume `G` is independent of phase and the scalar pressure profile has zero phase mean at every time and label. Then its label-gradient profile has zero average under the twisted operators. The derivative-of-average identity and coefficient independence are both needed; zero mean of pressure alone would not remove a phase-dependent coefficient.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: A phase-independent coframe preserves the pressure cancellation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The phase average of a twisted vector profile is genuinely periodic in the labels at phase zero. A label translation changes the phase by the carrier pairing, but averaging over a full period removes that shift. This supplies an ordinary torus field for the mean solver, rather than merely a twisted field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Averaging removes the phase twist from the labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The label-coordinate material relay preserves the unit-period phase mean zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Material evolution preserves zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: A phase-independent mean acting in the phase direction produces a source with zero phase average. The hypothesis `hκ` says that the covector is phase independent, and `hB` says the averaging operator fixes `B`. The differentiated profile `Y` belongs to the smooth periodic twisted profile space; it need not itself have zero phase mean. Periodicity makes its phase derivative integrate to zero. Applying this identity term by term gives the supplementary source its required centering.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Mean phase advection has zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The phase average of $(C[V]\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY$ equals that of $(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y$. The hypotheses `hVmean` and `htrans` give the zero phase mean and transversality of `V`; `hGPhase`, `hκPhase`, `hA`, `hsurj`, `hG`, and `hκflow` identify the actual transported coframe and covector. Periodic integration by parts moves the phase derivative, and the completion identity replaces it with a label divergence. No fast derivative remains in the averaged source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Phase averaging turns fast completion advection into label divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The full-period phase average preserves reflection parity.

The phase average of the preceding linear correction vanishes, including the special subtraction at level two. The hypotheses require phase-independent coefficients, zero phase mean of the preceding correction and pressure, and zero average of `completionSwitch`. Consequently the relay contributes no mean forcing. The mean equation is driven by the quadratic interactions and, at level two, the transported parent residual, rather than by this linear term.

Averaging $H_p$ leaves precisely the oscillation-label, divergence-label, and mean-label products of total level $p$. The hypotheses specify the actual transported geometry, zero phase means of oscillations and pressure, phase-independent means, and physical divergence completions. The conclusion replaces every fast completion interaction by its integrated-by-parts label counterpart. It is stated for `p ≤ P`; the separate mean-source definition adds the parent residual at $p=2$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The mean forcing contains only slow interactions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text:
On a twisted profile every mixed jet is bounded on the slab, so any bounded time multiplier gives a genuine real-valued finite seminorm.

Default-value audit (b5): The interval is nondegenerate by hT and the chosen time set lies within it. The proof hτ bounds the weight, while profile smoothness and periodicity bound the sampled jets. An empty time set is allowed and gives a harmless zero seminorm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The finite seminorm with a bounded time weight

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The bundled seminorm evaluates to the exact finite mixed-word norm of the weighted slices. Its construction includes a bound on the time weight and requires the indexing times to lie inside the closed slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The weighted seminorm equals the finite derivative norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Phase averaging is contractive for the supremum-based finite mixed seminorm with any bounded time-only weight on `A`. Each constant derivative word commutes with averaging, and the norm of its phase integral is bounded by the corresponding supremum. The flag `False` specifies this theorem’s supremum norm; no Hölder contraction is claimed here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Phase averaging decreases each weighted finite norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: A pointwise bilinear product is bounded by the product of the factor seminorms when `τfg = τf * τg` on the time set and all three multipliers are bounded. The explicit constant is the admissible-word count times $2^n$ times twice the bilinear-map norm. The result covers both supremum and optional half-Hölder measurements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Place a product’s time weight on its two factors

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: For a centered profile, phase-independent coframe and covector, and nonzero covector, the weighted completion norm costs one extra mixed derivative and one inverse positive frequency. The theorem assumes the geometric curl-row and normalized-potential coefficient budgets. Its explicit constant contains admissible-word counts, powers of two, and $K^2$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The completion gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The label-advection norm is bounded by the norm of the advector times one additional label or phase derivative of the advected field. The hypothesis `hG` bounds each scaled coframe row by `L`, and `hℓ` requires a nonzero label scale. The weights `r` and `q` are bounded on the chosen time set `S`; the output uses their product. Thus the amplitude weight can be placed on either factor, with the remaining parent cost supplied by the coframe estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Label advection obeys the weighted product estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The actual fixed-weight seminorm is monotone in derivative order.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Weighted seminorms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: If `A ⊆ B ⊆ Icc 0 T`, the seminorm on `A` is at most the seminorm on `B` with the same multiplier and derivative order. Boundedness of the multiplier is assumed on the larger set. The comparison restricts available samples and does not compare different weights.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: A smaller time set has no larger weighted norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Assuming `hh : h ≠ 0`, the order-$n$ norm of fast advection is bounded by two product constants, the unweighted scaled-covector norm, the order-$n$ advector norm, and the weighted order-$(n+1)$ norm of $Y$. The bounded time weight `τ` lives on `A`; only the differentiated profile carries it.

For a centered smooth profile, bounds the weighted finite-word seminorm of its phase primitive by twice that of the profile, at the same spatial and phase order. The time set `A` is any subset of the slab, and `τ` is any weight with the supplied bound `hτ`. The theorem uses the non-Hölder seminorm (`False`); it does not differentiate the weight.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The normalized primitive costs at most a factor of two

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The order-$n$ seminorm of one scaled label derivative is bounded by the order-$(n+1)$ seminorm of the original profile, with the same bounded time weight. The statement allows either value of `holder`. Constant directions commute, so the extra derivative belongs to the enlarged finite family without differentiating the time weight.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: A scaled label derivative consumes one order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The weighted seminorm through order `n` of one scaled profile derivative is bounded by the original profile's seminorm through order `n+1`. The assertion permits either value of the Hölder flag `holder`, any subset of the time slab, and any bounded time weight. The derivative acts only on label and phase variables, leaving that weight untouched.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: A scaled derivative spends one spatial order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The product $(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y$ is bounded using one extra derivative of `V`, the current-order norm of `Y`, and a bound `hG` for the scaled coframe rows. The weights satisfy `hweight : τP t = τV t * τY t`, so the estimate permits distributing the amplitude weight between the two factors. The theorem allows the optional Hölder seminorm as well; the paper's spatial and phase norm is its `holder = False` instance.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The divergence product obeys the same weighted estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: If every full-slab scaled coframe-row norm is at most `L` and $\ell\ne0$, the weighted order-$n$ divergence norm is bounded by $3Q_nL$ times the weighted order-$(n+1)$ norm of `V`. Here $Q_n$ is the finite product constant. The factor three counts spatial coordinates; the weight stays entirely on `V`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The three coframe rows bound slow divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: If `R` evaluates to the raw relay of centered profiles `V` and `F`, a common normalized coefficient budget bounds its weighted order-$n$ norm by the explicit order constant times $K^2\,\mathrm{freq}^{-1}$ and their order-$(n+1)$ norms. The weight is only bounded in time; `freq > 0` and $\ell\ne0$ are explicit.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The linear relay gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text:
The same periodic curl completion, restricted to the lattice-compatible profiles of the finite hierarchy.

Default-value audit (b5): The constructor requires T>0, phase independence of the covector and its nonvanishing on the slab. The returned twisted profile is built from a proved completion, not a default branch on failed hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The curl correction within the twisted profile space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: For a zero-phase-mean velocity and phase-independent `G` and `κ`, the bundled completion evaluates to the pulled-back curl of its relay potential. Covector nonvanishing is required to form the smooth potential. The result identifies the actual completion profile with the concrete curl expression used in finite-order estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The centered completion is the pulled-back curl

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: For a twisted zero-mean odd input and even coframe and covector, the twisted completion remains odd under joint label-and-phase reflection. The covector is phase independent and nonzero on the slab. The result is inherited from the periodic completion; lattice compatibility and parity are separate properties retained by the wrapper.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The lattice-compatible correction retains joint oddness

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: For a positive slab, phase-independent nonzero covector profile and zero-mean velocity profile, computes curl completion at a closed-cell point from the supplied raw field. The result factors out the time scalar. Smoothness of the multiplied raw field and its equality to the profile on the cell are explicit hypotheses; unique differentiation justifies the spatial derivative at cell faces.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The completion of a scalar multiple on the closed cell

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: The wrapped curl completion preserves a time-only scalar factor on the whole label space. It uses only the profile identity at the given time.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: A time factor passes through the wrapped correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: The periodic profile underlying the twisted completion is exactly the periodic completion of the underlying input. This is a definitional equality: the twisted constructor only adds the proof of lattice compatibility. Its assumptions include positive slab length, phase independence of the covector, and nonvanishing covector values on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: Forgetting the twist reveals the same periodic completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: For a profile of zero phase mean, the twisted completion has the same underlying smooth profile as the original slow-curl completion. The comparison assumes a phase-independent, nonzero covector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The twisted correction agrees with the smooth correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: With phase-independent inverse coframe and covector and a nonvanishing covector on the slab, completing the zero profile gives zero. The proof exposes the relay potential, whose zero input has zero potential and label derivative. This identifies the inactive or absent forcing case without choosing a nonzero correction.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.concr.text: For a positive time slab and even coframe, material matrix and covector profiles, proves that the concrete hierarchy operators preserve odd velocity and even pressure submodules. The sign changes of label and phase derivatives are accounted for explicitly. This supplies only operator closure; parity of the selected analytic solves remains a separate requirement.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.concr.summary: Even coefficients preserve odd velocities and even pressures

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: For a selected finite construction with $P\ge1$, the velocity and mean beyond the retained depth vanish by the construction’s index rule. Consequently the measured last-index `Y` and `Z` equal the final completion size and the mean is zero. The residual must be phase independent, as required by the finite hierarchy constructor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: The selected expansion has the required last-index values

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: For $2\le p\le P$, the selected relay has an inverse-frequency bound in terms of the measured oscillation and source at level $p-1$. At $p=2$, the transverse activation force is canceled exactly by `completionSwitch`; later levels use the selected transverse source. The coefficient budget, normalized pressures, coefficient evolution, and switch identity are all explicit premises.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: Each selected relay is controlled by the preceding level

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: Odd leading velocity and sources, even coefficients and leading pressure, and parity-preserving solvers give odd $V_p,C_p,B_p$ and even pressures at every level. The hypotheses `hMean`, `hTransverse`, and `hCompletion` describe the solvers' parity laws; the remaining named hypotheses supply the initial and coefficient parities. The conclusion also gives odd total profile velocity and remainder. This is the propagation theorem; the physical solvers discharge its solver hypotheses when applied to the actual construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: Reflection parity persists through the finite hierarchy

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: For relay levels `2,…,P+1`, the exact constructed relay equals the analytic wave-relay formula using the preceding velocity and adjusted force. The theorem also proves both relevant phase averages vanish. Its assumptions include phase-independent nonzero carrier geometry, the coframe and covector evolution laws, exact completion, activation compatibility, and zero pressure means. The final level is included although it lies beyond the solved transverse corrections.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: Identify every selected relay including the final remainder term

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: Adds `0 < τ` to the strict-inactivity construction theorem and extends all its vanishing and remainder identities through the activation slice. The conclusion still leaves the slow mean-product tail, rather than forcing the entire residual to zero. All support and completion hypotheses remain tied to the selected finite recursion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: The support conclusion extends through positive activation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: For any activation parameter, propagates vanishing of oscillations, completions, oscillatory pressures and transverse sources on the strict inactive region. The tail equals the slow mean-product sum there. Closed envelope, positive slab, depth at least one, and preservation by the actual chosen transverse solve and completion are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: The twisted expansion has its exact inactive-region remainder

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.contD.text: For the supplied strain and evolving nonzero covector, `hfreq : freq ≠ 0` gives joint smoothness of all four transverse coefficient formulas. The proof propagates covector nonvanishing from the underlying coefficient data and excludes zero squared norms before differentiating reciprocals. The result concerns coefficient regularity on the slab and does not supply any uniform derivative bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.contD.summary: The actual transverse coefficients are jointly smooth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.contD.text: A twisted profile, evaluated at any time in the closed slab, is smooth in label and phase. The lattice condition is additional structure; it does not change this slice regularity statement.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.deriv.text: For positive slab length, the actual periodic slab derivative restricts to twisted profiles. The translation law for the derivative proves its output lies in the same carrier space. The result is a profile of continuous linear maps on joint coordinates, preserving access to all time, label, and phase directions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.deriv.summary: Differentiate while retaining the carrier twist

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.deriv.text: Taking the underlying periodic profile after differentiating in the twisted space yields the periodic derivative of the underlying input. This definitional identity shows that the carrier constraint adds proof structure only. It allows concrete formulas for the derivative within the slab to be reused directly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.deriv.summary: The twisted derivative is the same periodic derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.text: For `hT : 0 < T`, this linear operator takes the derivative of a smooth twisted profile within its closed time slab and evaluates that derivative on a fixed vector `v`. The vector can point in time, label, or phase directions. Its output remains a smooth twisted profile; values outside the slab follow the profile representation rather than describing an extension of the physical field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.summary: Differentiate a profile along one fixed direction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.text: At a point `x` satisfying `hx : x ∈ hierarchyProfileSlab T`, the bundled directional derivative evaluates to `fderivWithin` of the underlying function applied to `v`. The assumption `hT : 0 < T` belongs to the operator. This is an evaluation identity, so it supplies no estimate or claim about derivatives outside the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.summary: Read a directional derivative on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.text: The derivative of the pointwise application `A f` in a fixed direction is the derivative of `A` applied to `f` plus `A` applied to the derivative of `f`. The slab duration is positive and the bundled profiles are smooth. The proof works with within-Fréchet derivatives, so the identity remains valid at the time endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.summary: Directional derivatives obey the operator application rule

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.text: For a smooth twisted profile on a positive-duration slab, differentiating along `w` and then `v` gives the same profile as the reverse order. The proof uses symmetry of the second within derivative on the convex slab, whose interior is nonempty. This handles boundary times as well as interior times without assuming a particular smooth extension.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.summary: Two fixed directional derivatives commute on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.text: For a positive slab duration, any constant direction `v`, and a fixed continuous linear map `L`, differentiating the mapped profile equals mapping the differentiated profile. Smoothness is carried by the profile type. The proof uses the within-Fréchet chain rule and uniqueness of derivatives on the closed slab; it is not a statement about a time-dependent map `L`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.summary: Directional differentiation commutes with a fixed linear map

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.diver.text: The graph evaluation of the finite hierarchy’s velocity is divergence free when every completed transverse solver output and every mean output has zero profile divergence. The theorem assumes those solver properties, the graph derivative, and the coframe and covector identities. It transports the abstract finite construction’s divergence result and does not itself establish the solver hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.diver.summary: The finite constructed perturbation is divergence free on its graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.euler.text: For a jointly smooth periodic parent with label flow on a positive closed slab, take `B ≥ 1`, `C,D ≥ 0`, and the stated parent and material graph jet bounds. When `i ≤ q` and `i + m + 1 ≤ N`, the $i$th fixed-position graph jet belongs to spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ at every slab time. Its norm is bounded by $3(m+1)(1+2^{N+q}D)^iCB^{m+1+i}$. The additional spatial order supplies the half-Hölder seminorm, including at the time endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.euler.summary: One extra spatial order gives the Hölder graph bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.euler.text: For a smooth periodic parent with label flow `X`, this recurrence expresses the next fixed-position time derivative of the inverse-flow graph of `f`. It is the previous derivative of the graph of `timeDerivative f` minus a binomial sum of spatial derivatives of lower graph jets applied to parent velocity jets. `hT` and `ht` include the closed-slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.euler.summary: Convert one further profile time derivative to Eulerian form

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.eval_.text: At any slab point, the joint derivative within the slab applied to `(0,0,1)` equals the ordinary one-variable derivative of the phase slice. The entire phase line remains in the slab at its fixed time. Unlike the time-direction lemma, this statement does not need positive slab length.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.eval_.summary: The joint phase direction equals the ordinary phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.eval_.text: For positive slab length and a point in the slab, applying the joint derivative to `(1,0,0)` equals the one-variable derivative within `Icc 0 T` with label and phase fixed. The conclusion includes endpoint times. It is a within-interval derivative, not a global derivative across the zero extension.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.eval_.summary: The joint time direction equals the slab time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given smooth label fields `B` and `q`, spatial periodicity of both, and the mean momentum equation, packages them as a twisted mean output. Their exact values are preserved on the slab. Phase independence supplies the required twist automatically. The theorem assumes the analytic mean solution and does not enforce endpoint conditions itself.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: A periodic physical mean enters the twisted hierarchy

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: On `0 < T ≤ 1`, constructs a mean result for a source fixed by the concrete average. The endpoint inverse supplies the raw fields. If coefficients are even and the forcing odd, reflection averaging selects compatible parity without increasing the label norm; otherwise the raw solution is retained and the conditional parity clause remains valid.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Solve and optionally symmetrize the actual mean equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: The transverse solve obeys the weighted estimates of Lemma 5.3 with the fixed parent power $\mathsf D^{20}$. A sufficiently small envelope is chosen before the derivative order, through `∃ A ... ∃ C : ℕ → ℝ`. The hypotheses give the parent flow and spatial derivative bounds, a central wave `hc`, and closed supported data. One conclusion allows nonzero launch data; the other bounds the selected zero-start velocity and its frequency-weighted pressure when the source vanishes before activation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Transverse velocity and pressure estimates at every order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Drops the two equalities identifying numerical bounds from `exists_parentGeometry_withBounds` and returns an inhabited parent-geometry record. All smoothness, periodicity, carrier nonvanishing, pressure differentiability and coercivity assumptions remain. This is an existence wrapper for the same construction, not a weaker analytic input requirement.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The parent geometry exists under the stated flow bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: From a smooth periodic parent and its flow, constructs coframe, strain and transported-covector profiles with exact physical values. A nonzero carrier, inverse-flow bound, strain bound and pressure-Hessian-minus-residual-gradient inequality are explicit inputs. The resulting mean coefficient bounds equal the supplied `D` and `L`, preserving their quantitative provenance.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The actual parent flow supplies both solver coefficient systems

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: This consequence of the unit-duration construction retains the bounds needed on the actual active interval. The constants `Krec n` are selected before the parent data and do not depend on carrier frequency or retained hierarchy depth. The parent, flow, radius and derivative hypotheses remain required; the theorem supplies coefficient budgets rather than selecting a wave.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Choose the coefficient bounds for the actual transverse solve

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: From the given nonnegative parent derivative table, choose one nonnegative constant at every order. For every compatible parent with sufficiently small positive envelope and normalized launch carrier, explicit lift, pullback, pressure and generator bounds exist. Both the actual-duration and unit-duration solve coefficients are bounded by the same $K_nD^{20}$. This extra unit-duration estimate supports later uniform choices.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Choose coefficient budgets valid up to unit duration

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a nonnegative table of parent derivative constants, the theorem chooses one exponent `A ≥ 30`. For every parent satisfying the displayed smoothness, flow, derivative and central-wave hypotheses with $\ell\le D^{-A}$, the weighted forward estimate holds near each lattice copy of the envelope. The exponent is chosen before the parent, so it is uniform over this specified class.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Choose an envelope exponent for uniform forward stability

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a positive slab with $T \le  1$, a label flow, smooth periodic parent velocity and pressure, and oddness of both velocity and its momentum residual, constructs `PhysicalApproximationData` with the prescribed leading input `L`. The residual profile is the pullback of the actual parent residual. The theorem allows every natural depth `P` and adds no independently selected forcing.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Use the actual parent residual in the hierarchy

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a nonnegative parent derivative table, choose natural exponents `p`, `s₀` and order constants before the parent data. For every permitted envelope exponent `s ≥ s₀`, the actual selected mean satisfies a bound with loss $D^{p+2+2s}$ and one additional source derivative. The phase scale is arbitrary because the source and mean are phase independent. The parent and mean coefficient compatibility hypotheses remain essential.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The selected mean loses one source derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: The theorem chooses an envelope exponent and order constants so every compatible physical hierarchy satisfies the transverse-solve recurrence with loss $D^{20}$. The leading input must be inactive off the periodic envelope and before activation. The bound `T ≤ 1` is carried by `cfg.time_le_one` inside `PhysicalApproximationData`, although it is not a separate visible parameter in the theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The actual parent yields a uniform transverse level bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: The actual residual pulled back along the forward parent flow is an admissible mean source, with its value independent of phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The pulled-back parent residual is an admissible mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Chooses fixed exponents and order-dependent constants before the parent and source. For a genuine periodic flow with the stated velocity jets, deformation bounds and coefficient identities, bounds the selected mean’s order-`n` label norm by an order-`n + 1` source norm times a power of `D`. The optional odd selection costs no additional constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The selected mean satisfies the finite label estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: This combines the transported raw-jet theorem with coefficient assembly. The output sequence `L` depends on the parent derivative sequence `R`, while the parent flow, normalized frequency, time subset, and order are quantified afterward. Under the stated smoothness, deformation, normalization, and width assumptions it bounds every concrete relay coefficient by $L_n(1+|\ell^{-1}|)D^{15}$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: A genuine parent flow supplies the normalized relay budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: For a fixed nonnegative parent derivative sequence `R`, the theorem chooses `C` before the parent, frequency, and time subset. Smooth periodic velocity, a genuine label flow, forward and inverse deformation bounds, and central frequency normalization then give the raw relay-jet package. Nonvanishing of the normalized covector is derived from the transported geometric bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Transported parent fields supply the raw relay derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a fixed nonnegative parent derivative sequence, this theorem chooses an order-constant sequence controlling the scaled transported covector. A smooth periodic parent flow with bounded deformation and central frequency normalization supplies the label jets. The resulting bound is $K_nD^2\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$ under the prescribed phase width and label-width condition.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The transported covector has the required fast coefficient bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: A smooth source with zero phase mean has a selected transverse velocity and normalized pressure on $[0,T]$. The inputs are `hT : 0 < T`, `d : TransverseCoefficients M κ`, and `hFMean`, which says the phase average of `F` vanishes. The output is `Nonempty (TransverseResult hT G M κ F)`, carrying zero initial velocity, the equation, transverse constraint, pressure normalization, and support laws. The conclusion is existence of this structured result; it does not itself state uniqueness among all competing solutions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Existence of the normalized transverse solve

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given time order `q` and nonnegative input cost arrays, this chooses an output array before the slab, scalar frequency, and fields. Assuming `hfreq : freq ≠ 0`, $0<T\le1$, `D ≥ 1`, nonnegative label width, and $\ell D^p\le1$, the three mixed bounds for strain, normalized covector, and reciprocal squared norm yield common amplitude $D^{e_M+2e_\kappa+e_Q}$, with natural exponents. It bounds all four selected coefficient time seminorms and two explicit coefficient mixed bounds. Covector nonvanishing comes separately from `d`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Choose one old-parent bound for all transverse coefficients

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a seed and its hierarchy regularity certificate, constructs velocity and pressure representatives on the whole parent slab with zero phase means. Their values equal the actual unswitched leading wave and pressure throughout the active interval only. The proof smoothly extends the amplitude and scalar pressure coefficient before multiplying by their fixed periodic phase profiles, preserving the zero means without asserting the wave equation outside the active interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Unswitched waves have smooth representatives with exact active values

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: From a nonnegative all-order sequence `C`, the theorem selects a sequence `L` so that any raw parent-jet package satisfying $D\ge1$ and $\ell D^{16}\le1$ gives a common relay budget. The allowance is $L_n(1+|\ell^{-1}|)D^{15}$. The chosen sequence precedes the coefficient functions and the time index.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: All relay coefficients share one finite allowance

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ext.text: Twisted profiles are equal once their values agree on the slab. The proof reduces to extensionality of their underlying smooth representatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ext.summary: Equality on the slab determines a twisted profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.fderi.text: For any lattice vector, the derivative within the slab of a twisted profile satisfies the same joint translation identity. Both its representative and the slab domain are invariant under that translation. The theorem concerns the actual within-domain derivative, including at boundary times, without assuming global smoothness of the zero extension.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.fderi.summary: The slab derivative keeps the carrier-dependent lattice period

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.freq_.text: Multiplying the output by the carrier before measuring its words bounds the carrier-weighted seminorm of the original output.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.freq_.summary: Frequency-weighted output bounds the pressure seminorm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text:
The Eulerian field $g^\natural(t,x)$ obtained by evaluating a twisted profile at the inverse label and its phase. The argument `f : HierarchyTwistedProfile T k E` carries smoothness, phase periodicity and the combined label–phase lattice rule. The argument `A : Velocity` is used as a label map; taking `A t = X t 0` gives the actual inverse parent flow.

Default-value audit (b5): This delegates to the underlying smooth profile. Twisted periodicity is available from the bundle, but periodic physical graph values also require the lattice behavior of the supplied label map.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: Evaluation of a profile on the transported graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: Reading a finite sum of twisted profiles on the physical graph equals the pointwise sum of their individual graph readings. The statement works for any normed target and any chosen inverse-label map. It is the linearity identity needed to split the constructed total pressure into separately estimated components.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: Physical graph evaluation commutes with finite sums

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: For a phase-independent twisted profile, a bound on the actual unweighted seminorm gives graph jets retaining the input frequency exponent `α`. The theorem requires the inverse-label scale and coframe estimates, positive frequency, and smooth chart, but no phase-width or carrier bound. The graph field is identified with the phase-zero mean composed with the inverse labels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: The measured mean avoids the phase-frequency derivative cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: A whole-slab unweighted seminorm bound gives graph jets with frequency exponent $3n/2+α$, under the same positive-scale, carrier, chart, and coframe assumptions as the weighted estimate. The proof uses unit amplitude weight on $[0,T]$. Thus no inverse amplitude weight is introduced for the depth remainder.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: The unweighted remainder has the full physical derivative cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: A bound on the actual amplitude seminorm gives physical graph jets with restored factor `γ t` and frequency exponent $3n/2+α$. The theorem assumes positive coordinate scales, $D,\lambda,L\ge1$, continuous positive weight, and the precise chart and coframe estimates. It assembles the seminorm-to-jet conversion with the physical chain rule, retaining explicit order and parent constants.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: A measured weighted profile gives explicit physical jet bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: A twisted profile with reflection multiplier `sign` retains that same multiplier after evaluation on an odd inverse-label map. The assertion is pointwise in time and space. The profile’s joint reflection reverses both label and phase, matching the two changes caused by a spatial reflection of the inverse labels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: The profile reflection sign survives graph evaluation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.text: The phase curve of a twisted profile has a `HasDerivAt` witness whose value is the evaluated phase-derivative profile. Time lies in the slab, with `0 < T`; labels and phase are arbitrary. The proof extracts smoothness of the fixed-time label-phase slice, so this statement rules out reliance on the default value of `deriv`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.summary: The phase operator supplies a genuine derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.text: Under the same inactive-prefix hypothesis and positive activation time, every mixed spatial jet has time derivative zero within the full slab at activation. Smoothness provides a derivative, and uniqueness on the nondegenerate closed inactive prefix identifies its value with zero. This conclusion concerns one time derivative, not all time orders.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.summary: The time derivative of each spatial jet also vanishes there

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.text: For a twisted profile with complete target, the normalized phase mean has a within-time derivative equal to the phase mean of the profile’s time derivative. The assertion holds at every time of a positive-length closed slab. Joint continuity and genuine derivatives on the compact unit phase interval justify differentiation under the integral, including at temporal endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.summary: Averaging in phase commutes with one time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hiera.text:
The Appendix D norm of the launch slice, with no amplitude weight.

Default-value audit (b5): The singleton launch time lies in the positive closed slab by its explicit membership argument. Smooth periodic profile slices ensure the actual finite derivative values are bounded.
A label coefficient controlled in the scaled coordinates controls all of its mixed words at the physical labels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hiera.summary: Scaled label derivatives control mixed coefficient words

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inact.text: The differential operators for the actual twisted hierarchy satisfy the inactive-region laws used by the ordered recursion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inact.summary: Concrete operators preserve the inactive region

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inact.text:
Twisted profiles vanishing at each inactive point form a submodule.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a subspace of profiles whose values vanish on the specified inactive region. It asserts value support, not by itself support of arbitrary derivatives across a nonsmooth boundary.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inact.summary: Twisted profiles supported in the active region

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.text: Assume $D\ge1$, $\ell\ge0$, $\ell D^7\le1$, smooth inverse-flow derivatives, and raw order-`j` bounds $C(j)D^{7j+1}$ with nonnegative costs. The actual inverse coframe then has unweighted order-`m` norm at most the finite coefficient-order constant times $D$. The phase width is arbitrary because this coefficient is independent of phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.summary: A small label radius absorbs inverse-coframe derivative growth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.text: Reflection of both label and phase gives the same parity after evaluation on the inverse parent graph. The parent is odd by `hodd`, and `hf : HierarchyProfileReflectionParity sign f.val.val.val` fixes the profile parity. The assumptions `hX`, `hU` and `hper` make the inverse labels odd. Taking `sign = -1` gives the odd velocity correction used in Lemma 5.8; taking `sign = 1` gives even fields.
The reciprocal of a positive continuous amplitude is bounded on every nonempty compact subset of the active interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.summary: The reciprocal amplitude stays bounded on compact intervals

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.text: At $t\in[0,T]$, iterating the within-slab time derivative of a fixed mixed spatial word agrees with applying that word to the bundled time jet. The label and phase point x stays fixed. The positivity binder hT and smooth profile structure justify the derivative interpretation, including one-sided values at the endpoints; the theorem asserts equality, not a seminorm bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.summary: Time jets are the fixed-coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.text: For a smooth profile valued in a complete normed space and `T > 0`, moves any iterated within-time derivative through integration over the fixed phase interval `c..d`. The endpoints may occur in either order; the integral uses the oriented interval convention. The label is fixed, and the time may be an endpoint of the closed slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.summary: Time derivatives pass through a fixed phase integral

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.text: Commutates any closed-slab time jet with `phasePrimitive` at a fixed label and phase, for a smooth profile in a complete normed space and `T > 0`. Both the phase integral and its normalizing subtraction are differentiated. A zero phase mean is not assumed for this identity; that condition enters later when the primitive is bundled as a periodic profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.summary: Time derivatives pass through the normalized phase primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.text: The slow advection uses the actual label derivative and the coframe.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.summary: Slow advection uses the coframe label derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.text: Writes the actual slow label advection of `g` by `z` as three scalar-vector products. Each scalar is a scaled row of the inverse deformation applied to `z`; each vector is a scaled label derivative of `g`. The assumption `ℓ ≠ 0` cancels the inverse row scaling against the derivative scaling. The identity concerns the whole operator, before any time-norm estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.summary: Slow advection is the sum of three scaled products

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.text: Label advection has sign minus the product of the two profile signs.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.summary: Slow advection multiplies signs and reverses parity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.text: The label pressure gradient reverses the reflection sign with an even coframe.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.summary: The slow pressure gradient reverses parity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map.text: A bounded linear map on the value space acts pointwise on twisted profiles and preserves their lattice translation identities. It also preserves the existing unit phase period and smoothness. The resulting linear operator changes values only by the specified bounded linear map, without altering the carrier or domain.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map.summary: Linear images preserve the carrier-compatible translation law

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map_e.text: At a point in `hierarchyProfileSlab T`, applying the bundled profile map equals applying the continuous linear map to the original profile value. The `.val.val.val` projections pass through the twisted, periodic, and smooth wrappers. Membership in the slab is retained explicitly because the lowest-level representatives are zero-extended outside it.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map_v.text: The underlying periodic profile of a linear image in the twisted space is the periodic linear image of the underlying profile. The equality is definitional. It confirms that preserving the carrier-dependent lattice condition introduces no additional transformation beyond the supplied bounded linear map.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map_v.summary: The carrier-compatible linear image retains its formula

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: Defines the explicit scalar $((3\,2^N L)^N)4^N$ used to dominate graph differentiation costs through spatial order $N$. It depends only on the coefficient cap and the chosen finite order. The definition itself has no positivity assumption on $L$; the norm estimates and monotonicity theorem use `1 ≤ L`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: A common factor for spatial graph differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: Taking the active interval to be $[0,T]$ gives the equality between material completion plus pressure gradient and the four raw relay terms. The theorem retains the actual coefficient evolution and normalized-pressure premises. It proves equality for the supplied profiles; it does not select a solution of the transverse equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The material completion identity on the full slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: This version derives both the velocity time equation and the normalized phase-pressure formula from the bundled momentum equation, transversality, and zero means. Together with coframe and covector evolution, they identify material completion plus pressure gradient with `waveRelayAt` on the full slab. The theorem therefore removes the separate pressure-formula premise of the earlier representation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The momentum equation supplies the full relay representation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: The actual relay evaluation is determined by the selected momentum equation and its normalized phase pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The momentum equation determines the relay identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: With phase-independent coframe, strain, and covector, the material derivative of the centered completion plus the label pressure gradient equals the raw relay on $[t₀,T]$. Hypotheses supply coefficient evolution, zero velocity mean, nonvanishing covector, the velocity equation, and the chosen pressure formula. The strict inequality `hstart : t₀ < T` provides unique differentiation on the active interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The active material derivative equals the four relay terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: Assume both velocity and switch force are transverse and centered, and their momentum equation holds on the slab. Then subtracting the completion of the force from material completion plus pressure gradient leaves the homogeneous relay of `V`. The proof first derives the forced relay identity and then cancels the force’s own potential contribution.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: Subtracting the switch completion removes the activation force

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: Evaluate the abstract hierarchy material operator as the within-time derivative of the profile plus the parent gradient applied to it. The identity holds on the time slab with positive duration.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The material operator on a twisted profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: The material derivative preserves the reflection sign with an even material matrix.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanG.text: Defines $[3\,2^mL]^m4^m$, the explicit graph-derivative factor for a phase-independent profile. There is no oscillatory phase contribution, so this coefficient omits the extra factor two from the oscillatory version. It helps express the paper’s distinction between a frequency-dependent graph loss and the parent-only loss for means.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanG.summary: The derivative cost of a phase independent graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanO.text: If nonnegative `loss` is at most `K * D^r`, the sixth power of that loss in the finite mean budget can be replaced by $K^6D^{6r}$. The frequency is nonnegative and the profile constant is nonnegative. This numerical comparison exposes the fixed parent exponent while leaving depth in the finite level count.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanO.summary: Replace the mean loss by a fixed parent power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanP.text: If every actual retained level from two through `P` satisfies the order-two hierarchy bound, the sums of mean velocities and mean sources are each bounded by the number of levels times $C\,\mathrm{loss}^6\mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. The source includes the parent residual only at level two. Frequency and loss are at least one.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanP.summary: Sum the order-two mean and source estimates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanS.text: If the concrete phase-average operator fixes `F`, evaluating at phase zero gives a smooth label field periodic on the lattice. Every other phase has the same value. This turns the algebraic mean-source hypothesis into an actual phase-independent forcing for the endpoint solver; it uses the concrete average, not an arbitrary projection.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanS.summary: An averaged source is a smooth periodic label field

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanS.text: For a phase-independent source profile, every time derivative of order $i\le q$ has label norm at most $q!T^{-q}$ times its order-$q$ factorial time norm, assuming `0 < T ≤ 1`. Phase independence follows from the supplied averaging identity `hS`. The proof first extracts order $i$, then enlarges its factorial and inverse-time factors to the common order $q$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanS.summary: Extract a source derivative from the factorial norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mem_i.text: Unfolds the submodule membership condition into equality with zero on the strict inactive region. It applies to the underlying representative of a twisted profile. The equality is definitional and gives no derivative or support propagation by itself; those results use the closed envelope and profile smoothness separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mem_i.summary: Inactive membership means vanishing at every inactive point

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mem_r.text: Unfolds membership in the reflection submodule into the profile’s sign equation under simultaneous reflection. The equivalence is definitional and holds for every real sign. It provides the notation bridge between abstract submodule propagation and concrete parity statements for the nested twisted-profile representative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mem_r.summary: Submodule membership is exactly the reflection equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mixed.text: If a smooth profile vanishes throughout the earlier part of the slab and `0 < t₀ ≤ T`, every mixed spatial derivative word vanishes at activation. Earlier slices and all their spatial derivatives are zero, and continuity of the derivative profile gives the endpoint value. The strict positivity of `t₀` is essential to the left-limit argument.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mixed.summary: Every spatial derivative vanishes at a positive activation time

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.momen.text: The constructed hierarchy cancels the physical parent residual, leaving exactly the retained remainder and two activation sources. The hypothesis `hRphys` identifies the phase-independent residual profile with the parent momentum residual pulled back by $X$; `hL` is the leading-wave equation. With `hP : 2 ≤ P` and the parent coefficient identities, the finite hierarchy momentum identity becomes an Eulerian identity. No small-error estimate replaces this cancellation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.momen.summary: The hierarchy cancels the parent residual exactly

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: Assume phase-independent mean velocity and forcing have second-order profile bounds of size $C_{\rm mean}D^b\mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$, with controlled inverse-label coefficients and parent gradient Hölder norm. If their physical graphs satisfy divergence-free linearized momentum, the graph pressure Hessian has the displayed norm bound with the same frequency decay. The equation and divergence condition are premises, not consequences of the norms.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Mean profile estimates imply a physical Hessian estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: Assume each retained higher pressure vanishes on the hierarchy inactive region and the summed Hessian is bounded at every active time. A nonnegative bound then holds on the whole closed slab. Before activation the pressure sum is identically zero as a spatial function, so its Hessian vanishes without requiring a weighted estimate there.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: Assume the solver selects genuine transverse results, the physical coefficient identities and first-order coefficient bounds hold, and the actual levels satisfy the order-one and order-two bounds. Then the Hessian norm of the sum of pressures at levels two through `P` is bounded by the explicit prefactor times $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/12}$. The active time also needs `γ t ≤ 1`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: The higher oscillatory Hessian gains five twelfths

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: For `T > 0`, a jointly smooth periodic parent with label flow `X`, and `B ≥ 1`, `C,D ≥ 0`, assume `hparent` for parent time orders below `q` and spatial orders through `N`. Assume `hmaterial` for graph evaluations of profile jets with total time and spatial order at most `N`. The fixed-position graph jets have bound $(1+2^{N+q}D)^iCB^{m+i}$ when `i ≤ q` and `i + m ≤ N`, throughout the closed slab. Each converted time derivative consumes at most one spatial order.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Eulerian time derivatives spend additional spatial orders

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: For a phase-independent profile, bounds on its time derivatives in unweighted label norms yield spatial bounds for their graph evaluations. The hypotheses supply a smooth readout map `A`, its derivative field `B`, label scale, coefficient bounds through $N$, and a common profile amplitude. For $j\le q$ and $m\le N$, the spatial rate is $D^{a+1}$ per derivative, without a new-frequency factor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Mean graph derivatives cost only the label scale

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: For a positive continuous weight $\gamma$, a profile bound in weighted time-derivative seminorms gives graph derivatives with amplitude $\gamma(t)\,\mathrm{freq}^{\alpha}$. Assuming phase width $h=\mathrm{freq}^{-1/2}$, carrier bound $\|k\|\le D\,\mathrm{freq}$, and the supplied readout-coefficient bounds, each spatial derivative costs $D^{\max(a,1)+1}\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. Orders satisfy $j\le q$ and $m\le N$; the estimate holds on the active interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Oscillatory graph derivatives retain the amplitude weight

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: At an active time and for an admissible derivative word, the norm of the unweighted mixed derivative is at most `γ t` times the amplitude seminorm. Strict positivity of `γ` allows its inverse to be canceled. This restores the actual size of a field from its normalized spatial measurements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Recover a pointwise derivative with its amplitude factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: For `hi : i ≤ q`, one time derivative is bounded by the factorial time seminorm with cost $i!T^{-i}$. The spatial seminorm `N` and profile `f` are arbitrary, and `hT : 0 < T` ensures that the $i$th weight can be inverted. The proof keeps the $i$th nonnegative summand and divides by $T^i/i!$. In the auxiliary argument the inverse slab-length estimate converts this extraction cost to a fixed parent-frequency power.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Extracting one time derivative from the weighted sum

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofTwi.text: A phase-periodic profile whose on-slab slices satisfy the joint label-phase translation law is placed in the twisted submodule. The underlying profile remains unchanged. The supplied proof `h` covers all lattice vectors, labels, phases, and slab times, so no additional periodic wrapping is performed.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofWra.text: A smooth profile with unit-periodic phase is multiplied by a radial envelope and extended through the centered lattice cell with the carrier-dependent phase shift.
