The assumptions `hLip`, `hodd`, `hs` and `ht` provide uniqueness on the flow interval. The proof combines oddness of the forward flow with evenness of the derivatives of odd maps. This is a parity statement, not an estimate of their size.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.even_materialGr.summary: Even material gradient and transported wave vector

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_bound_it.text: Assume a positive-order flow derivative is jointly continuous through the closed slab, as recorded by `hJet`. Spatial periodicity reduces its size to a compact label cell, producing one real bound for every time and label. The theorem uses `hn` to exclude the unbounded zeroth-order lifted transition map.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_bound_it.summary: A continuous periodic derivative has a uniform bound

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_lattice_.text: Under the same smooth odd periodic flow hypotheses, assume `2 ≤ μ ≤ D` and $\ell\le D^{-3}$. A point whose inverse label lies in the periodic-envelope support is then within distance $\mu^{-1}$ of a lattice point. The conclusion follows from the previous $2D\ell$ estimate and a numerical scale comparison.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_lattice_.summary: A small envelope gives inverse-frequency spatial confinement

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_lattice_.text: For a smooth odd periodic velocity and its label flow, assume the forward flow derivative is bounded by nonnegative `D`. If the inverse label of `x` belongs to the closed periodic-envelope support, some lattice point is within distance $2D\ell$ of `x`. Oddness fixes the origin, periodicity fixes its lattice translates, and the derivative bound controls their displacement.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_lattice_.summary: The transported envelope stays close to a lattice point

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_variatio.text: Under spatial Lipschitz control `hLip`, differentiability `hU`, a uniformly Lipschitz spatial derivative `hDlip`, and continuity along the reference trajectory `hDcont`, there is a matrix curve initially equal to the identity. It solves $F'=DU(X)F$ within the closed interval and is the Fréchet derivative of each label transition at `a`. Both properties are conclusions, not assumptions about a formal matrix curve.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_variatio.summary: The Jacobian solves the variational equation

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_variatio.text: For a jointly $C^2$ spatially periodic velocity on a nondegenerate closed slab, `hU` and `hperiodic` provide the uniform bounds required by the variational construction. The resulting matrix curve starts at the identity, solves the Jacobian ODE within the slab, and differentiates the actual transition map at the chosen label.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_variatio.summary: Periodic smoothness supplies the variational solution

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasDerivWithinA.text: At fixed Eulerian position `x`, the time derivative of the inverse label `X t s x` is its spatial derivative applied to the negative velocity. Joint $C^2$ periodic regularity and membership of both times supply the differentiability needed for this chain rule. The statement holds within the slab, including its endpoints.

For a label flow of a spatially periodic velocity that is jointly $C^2$ on a nondegenerate closed slab, the inverse label derivative along a trajectory satisfies the reverse matrix equation. Both the starting time `s` and evaluation time `t` must belong to the slab. The conclusion is a within-slab derivative, including endpoints.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasDerivWithinA.summary: The actual inverse label derivative evolves along the flow

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasDerivWithinA.text: The actual flow covector satisfies $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ on the closed time interval. The hypotheses are `hX` for the flow, `hlr` for positive interval length, `hU` for joint $C^2$ regularity, and `hper` for periodicity of the velocity. Both times are constrained by `hs` and `ht`. The matrix $M$ is evaluated along the particle path in the conclusion; oddness and divergence freeness are unnecessary for this identity.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasDerivWithinA.summary: Transported covector solves the adjoint equation

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasFDerivWithin.text: For a smooth periodic parent flow on a positive-length slab, assume also joint smoothness of its inverse label map. The theorem identifies the joint within-slab derivative as time component $-A_xU$ and spatial component $A_x$. It applies at every slab time and label; regularity of the inverse is a hypothesis here, not its conclusion.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasFDerivWithin.summary: The inverse flow has its exact joint transport derivative

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasFDerivWithin.text: Assume a continuous velocity, a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound, and the spatial derivative `hspace` of the flow at the chosen point. The joint derivative within the slab sends a time increment to the velocity along the trajectory and a label increment through `F`. This proves a joint derivative from the existing separate ingredients.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasFDerivWithin.summary: The joint flow derivative separates time and labels

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasFDerivWithin.text: For a jointly $C^2$ periodic parent on a nondegenerate slab, the joint time-label derivative uses the actual spatial derivative of the transition and the velocity along that trajectory. Both `hs` and `ht` restrict the times. The result is a derivative within the product slab, so its endpoint meaning is explicit.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasFDerivWithin.summary: Periodic smoothness supplies the joint flow derivative

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasGradientAt_l.text: The phase obtained by composing the initial linear phase with the reverse transition has gradient `labelWaveVector` at the transported particle. The assumptions are those of a $C^2$ periodic flow on the closed slab. The wave vector `k` is arbitrary in this identity; nonvanishing is not required to compute the gradient.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.hasGradientAt_l.summary: The transported phase has the inverse-transpose gradient

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.inverse.text: If both times lie in the interval and the velocity has the uniform spatial Lipschitz bound, the reverse transition map is both a left and a right inverse of the forward transition map. The result is a statement about functions. It does not yet assert differentiability of the inverse maps.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.inverse.summary: Swapping start and end times gives both flow inverses

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.iteratedFDeriv_.text: For a periodic velocity with a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound, positive-order derivatives of a flow transition agree after every lattice translation. The order assumption `hn : 1 ≤ n` matters because the lifted flow itself changes by the lattice vector. The theorem states equality of the derivative functions without supplying their smoothness separately.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.iteratedFDeriv_.summary: Positive flow derivatives are spatially periodic

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.labelDerivative.text: The spatial derivative of a flow starts at the identity and satisfies $F_t=MF$ along each trajectory. The binder `hX` gives the flow, while `hU` and `hper` require a jointly $C^2$ periodic parent. No divergence condition or Euler equation is needed. The theorem identifies the actual Fréchet derivative of the transition map, so this is not merely an ODE for an unrelated matrix field.

The derivatives of a forward transition and its reverse compose to the identity in both orders. The hypotheses `hX`, `hU` and `hper` give an actual flow of a jointly $C^2$ periodic parent, with both times in the slab. The inverse derivative is evaluated at the transported point. Consequently the deformation is injective, which is the algebraic reason that vanishing physical and label displacements are equivalent at an endpoint.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.labelDerivative.summary: Forward and reverse flow derivatives are inverses

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.labelJets_evolv.text: For every order $n$, the label derivatives of the flow satisfy the differentiated trajectory equation. The hypotheses `hX`, `hU` and `hper` supply a genuine flow of a jointly smooth periodic velocity on $[0,T]$. The conclusion includes spatial smoothness and continuity of both sides. Subtracting the linear term with the chain-rule identity gives the higher variational equation used in Proposition 5.1.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.labelJets_evolv.summary: Differentiating the parent flow in its labels

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.labelSecondDeri.text: For a $C^2$ periodic velocity and its label flow on a nondegenerate closed slab, the actual second label derivative exists, starts at zero and obeys the Hessian-forced equation. The forcing applies the velocity Hessian to two first flow derivatives. This is a theorem about `fderiv` of the supplied flow, not merely existence of an unrelated solution to the formal variation equation.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.labelSecondDeri.summary: The actual second flow derivative satisfies its variational equation

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.lipschitzWith_l.text: Assume the velocity is spatially Lipschitz with the same nonnegative constant `K` throughout the slab. Every transition `X s t` with `hs` and `ht` is Lipschitz in its starting label with constant $\exp(K(r-l))$. `Real.toNNReal` packages that positive real bound; the conclusion concerns labels, not time derivatives.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.lipschitzWith_l.summary: One Lipschitz bound for all transition maps

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.mono.text: Restricts the initial-value and trajectory certificates of an existing two-time flow from a time set `I` to a subset `J`. The same flow function is retained. This is a restriction result, not existence of a new flow or a guarantee of interval nondegeneracy on an arbitrary subset.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.mono.summary: Restrict an actual two-time flow to a smaller time set

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_forcedVari.text: For a zero-initial-data solution `z` of the forced variational equation, bounds `hF` and `hG` by `D` on the forward and inverse Jacobians yield $\|z(t)\|\le\int_0^t D^2\|N(s)\|\,ds$. Continuity of the coefficient and forcing is explicit. The result bounds a supplied solution; it does not create the higher variation itself.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_forcedVari.summary: A bounded propagator controls forced variations

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_iteratedFD.text: With actual inverse-Jacobian bound `hInv` and forward derivatives bounded by $CD^{5i+1}$ through the required order, the inverse-Jacobian derivative of order `n` is bounded by $(n!)^2C^nD^{7n+1}$. The theorem requires `D,C≥1`, sufficient forward smoothness, and the periodic flow assumptions that establish invertibility.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Forward flow bounds control all inverse-Jacobian derivatives

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_iteratedFD.text: Under the same forward and inverse flow bounds, the label derivatives of the transported wave vector are bounded by the inverse-Jacobian estimate multiplied once by $\|k\|$. The original vector `k` is fixed during differentiation. No lower bound on its size is required for this estimate, which does not involve division by its norm.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Transported wave-vector derivatives inherit the coframe bound

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_iteratedFD.text: The order-$n$ flow derivative is bounded by the partition sum with prefactor $C\mathsf D^2$. The assumptions `hn`, `hUjet`, `hXjet` and `hODE` give $n\ge2$, velocity derivatives, lower flow derivatives and their evolution. The forcing consists of partitions with at least two positive blocks, so every flow derivative on the right has lower order. This is the induction mechanism in Proposition 5.1.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_iteratedFD.summary: The recurrence for higher parent flow derivatives

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_labelWaveV.text: Two deformation bounds control the transported covector by $|k_*|/\mathsf D\le|\kappa|\le\mathsf D|k_*|$. The assumptions `hF` and `hG` bound the derivative and inverse derivative of a genuine label flow; `hU` and `hper` supply smooth periodic velocity. At the central activation time, substituting $|\kappa|=\lambda$ supplies both bounds on the carrier $k_*$.

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_multilinea.text: A higher variation starting at zero has norm at most $\mathsf D^2C$ when its forcing has norm at most $C$. The assumptions `hz₀`, `hz` and `hNbound` give the initial value, differential equation and forcing bound. Both deformation bounds enter through `hF` and `hG`; `hT₁ : T ≤ 1` removes the interval length from the integral estimate.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_multilinea.summary: The deformation controls a forced higher variation

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_normalized.text: Normalization at the origin, `hcenter`, and bounds on the forward and inverse deformation give $|k_*|/\lambda\le\mathsf D$ and $\mathsf D^{-2}\le|\kappa|/\lambda\le\mathsf D^2$. The assumptions `hF₀`, `hG₀`, `hF` and `hG` are the required bounds at activation and at the measured label. The complementary lower bound on $|k_*|$ follows from the unnormalized transport estimate at activation.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_normalized.summary: Wave vector bounds after frequency normalization

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_secondVari.text: Assume the supplied second variation solves the differentiated ODE `hz` with zero initial value, both Jacobians are bounded by `D`, and the velocity Hessian is bounded by $CD^2$. With $0<T\le1$, its size is at most $CD^6\|u\|\|v\|$. Two factors come from propagation and two from the first variations in the Hessian forcing.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_secondVari.summary: The second variation costs six deformation factors

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_sub_le.text: The distance between two trajectories obeys the usual Grönwall bound in either time direction.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_sub_le.summary: The parent flow obeys a two-sided Grönwall bound

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.odd.text: The transition map of an odd velocity is odd in its initial label. The hypotheses `hLip` and `hodd` give a common Lipschitz bound and oddness throughout the interval, while `hs` and `ht` place both flow times there. Uniqueness compares the trajectory from $-a$ with the negative trajectory from $a$. Taking $a=0$ shows that the flow fixes the origin.

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.primaryPressure.text: For a smooth periodic parent flow, bounds on the inverse coframe and its first label derivative give the exact gradient of the transported phase, a Hessian bound, and first- and second-order bounds for the rescaled inverse-label map. The theorem assumes positive envelope length and `L ≥ 1`. These are the geometric inputs to `PrimaryPressureBudget`.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.primaryPressure.summary: The parent flow supplies phase derivatives and inverse-label jets

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.restart.text: For a label flow with uniform spatial Lipschitz bound, evolving from `s` to `t` and then restarting from that position to `u` equals direct evolution from `s` to `u`. All three times must lie in the interval. The proof applies uniqueness at the common intermediate position.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.restart.summary: Restarting a trajectory at an intermediate time changes nothing

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.terminal_hasDer.text: For an actual label flow of a jointly smooth periodic velocity on $[0,T]$, with `T > 0`, proves the within-time derivative of $G(t,x)=D(X(t,0))(X(0,t,x))$ equals $-G(t,x)\circ M(t,x)$. Here $M$ is the velocity gradient along the forward trajectory. The proof differentiates the inverse identity and uses both inverse relations; it includes the two temporal endpoints.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.terminal_hasDer.summary: The inverse deformation satisfies its variational equation

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.terminal_hasDer.text: Given `hX : IsLabelFlowOn U X (Icc a b)`, `hab : a < b`, and joint smoothness of $f$, the curve $r\mapsto f(r,X(s,r,x))$ has within-interval derivative $D_tf(t,X(s,t,x))$. Both reference time $s$ and evaluation time $t$ must lie in the interval. This is an actual derivative statement, including its endpoints.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.terminal_hasDer.summary: A trajectory differentiates by the material derivative

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.terminal_iterat.text: Under `IsLabelFlowOn`, `a < b`, and joint smoothness of both the velocity and the field, the $q$th within-time derivative of $f(r,X(s,r,x))$ equals the $q$th material iterate evaluated along that trajectory. The reference time and evaluation time belong to the slab. The proof iterates the genuine derivative identity while preserving smoothness.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.terminal_iterat.summary: Label time derivatives are material derivatives along the flow

TorusEuler.IsMaximalEulerSolution.text:
A smooth periodic Euler solution that cannot be extended to any longer interval. Besides `IsEulerSolution T u p`, the predicate requires that every real $S>T$ admit no smooth periodic Euler velocity agreeing with $u$ throughout $[0,T)$. Agreement is required for velocity; pressure is allowed its own normalized representative. The predicate expresses nonextendibility, while the separate common-interval uniqueness theorem explains why this is the maximal solution from the chosen initial data.

Default-value audit (b4): The conjunction includes IsEulerSolution, so T>0 and smoothness cannot be discarded while reading nonextendibility. The universal quantifier runs over every real S>T; such S exist. Agreement is on the nonempty interval [0,T). No integral, division or supremum is introduced here. This is a predicate of no continuation, not itself an existence or uniqueness theorem.
TorusEuler.IsMaximalEulerSolution.summary: No smooth continuation beyond the terminal time

TorusEuler.IsScheduledPhysicalCrossing.text: This proposition asks for an actual physical amplification and growing crossing whose initial first coupling, old ratio, and new crossing coupling equal the supplied scalars. It therefore records compatibility of abstract stage numbers with physical wave data. It does not by itself assert that such a crossing exists for arbitrary scalar inputs.
TorusEuler.IsScheduledPhysicalCrossing.summary: A physical crossing with the prescribed successive couplings

TorusEuler.IsScheduledPhysicalCrossing.c.text: A witness of the scheduled physical crossing implies positivity of both old and new first couplings and the logarithmic increment bound $|\log(\nu_{new}/\nu_{old})|\le2\varepsilon_{old}$. The theorem extracts these facts from the concrete growing crossing and then rewrites with the compatibility equalities. It does not require crossings at any other stage.
TorusEuler.IsScheduledPhysicalCrossing.c.summary: A scheduled physical crossing controls the coupling increment

TorusEuler.LaterPrimaryCosts.text: Records a radius floor and fixed scalar costs for the later leading-pressure upper Hessian and activation-primary two-jet bounds. Both estimates quantify over every selected later input above that floor. The pressure loss may depend on the radius exponent, while the activation parent power is fixed as `a + 27`. These are explicit analytic obligations, not unproved free constants.
TorusEuler.LaterPrimaryCosts.summary: Two later-wave estimates remain before uniform stage closure

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.CenterWave.text:
CenterWaveOn records the covector equation and a nonzero transverse central amplitude solving the homogeneous seed equation. Its stability field quantifies over every transverse solution and compares its amplitude to the central one at any ordered pair of active times. Its coupling field writes $D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|\le\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a$, avoiding division by norms. Nonzero central data make this equivalent to the paper’s normalized coupling inequality. Frequency normalization is supplied by a separate predicate.

Default-value audit (b5): The nonzero and growth conditions are restricted to Icc t₀ T. They would be vacuous on an empty interval; uses in the paper enforce 0≤t₀<T. The stability inequality also relies on the recorded positive center norm.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.CenterWave.summary: Central affine-wave data on the active slab

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.CenterWave.text: Transport center data across an exact equality with the parent's central gradient on the physical slab.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.CenterWave.summary: Transporting central data across equal gradients

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.CenterWave.text: For a selected `CenterWaveOn` solution and positive `freq`, define $\gamma(t)=\mathrm{freq}^{3/4}\lVert\mathrm{center}(t)\rVert$. Continuity of `M` and the assumed peak cap imply that this weight is continuous, positive and at most one on the closed activation interval. The theorem also supplies a continuous within-interval derivative. The peak cap is an input, not a conclusion of wave selection.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.CenterWave.summary: The central amplitude gives a positive normalized weight

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.text:
A localized seed with its projected initial data and quantitative control near the origin. The field `activation` is $\mathbf a(t_0,a)=(I-P_{\kappa(t_0,a)})\mathbf a(t_0,0)$, and `equation` records its linear differential equation. The fields `near` and `transverse` contain comparison, positivity and orthogonality conditions. This structure records those properties; a localization theorem constructs a seed satisfying them.

Default-value audit (b5): The record includes estimates and a strictly positive coupling, in addition to the seed equation. It is stronger than the bare public seed predicate; the proof constructs these extra properties instead of assuming them of every seed.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.summary: The localized seed and its activation data

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.Hie.text: Records $0 \le  t_0 < T$, a nonnegative switch rate, $0 < \ell$ with $2 \cdot  \ell < 1/2$, and $0 < h \le  1$. It also requires smooth strain, covector, and amplitude on the active slab, with nonzero covector there. These hypotheses justify wrapping and smooth activation; they do not include quantitative seed normalization or a lower bound on amplitude.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.Hie.summary: Regularity and scale assumptions for the switched seed

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.Hie.text: The regularity assumptions $0 \le  t_0$ and `t₀ < T` imply $T > 0$. This short order argument supplies the positive-slab witness demanded by concrete profile operators and by unique differentiability of $[0,T]$. It says nothing about the duration being bounded above or about quantitative activation rates.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.Hie.summary: The active interval has a positive terminal time

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.Pri.text: This proposition records positive frequency and coframe scales, the prescribed phase width, the central amplitude cap, strain and covector bounds, phase-gradient and Hessian identities, and coefficient bounds through two derivatives. The center and coefficient caps are required only after activation. It is a package of assumptions used by the signed pressure estimate, not a proof of those assumptions.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.Pri.summary: The quantitative inputs for the signed leading Hessian

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.bou.text: With the same concrete coefficient and transport hypotheses and a supplied normalized relay budget, the weighted leading relay costs one derivative and gains one inverse frequency. The right side contains only the switched velocity norm, because subtracting the completion switch has removed the activation force. Any bounded time-only weight on a subset of the slab is allowed.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.bou.summary: The leading relay bound needs only the switched velocity

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.text: The selected projected seed is jointly smooth whenever its actual coefficient fields are jointly smooth on the closed activation slab.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.summary: The chosen projected seed is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.text: For positive envelope radius and phase width $0<h\le1$, a seed jointly smooth on $[t_0,T]$ gives a jointly smooth leading profile in time, label and independent phase. The radial envelope is smooth despite its norm-based expression because it is constant near the origin. This statement concerns the active slab before time switching or periodic cell extension.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.summary: The envelope and phase preserve active seed smoothness

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.text: With positive envelope radius and $0<h\le1$, assume the gradient, covector and selected amplitude are jointly smooth on the active slab and the covector never vanishes there. The leading pressure is then jointly smooth in time, label and phase. The explicit nonvanishing condition licenses division by $\|\kappa\|^2$, while the normalized phase primitive contributes a smooth scalar factor.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.summary: The leading pressure is smooth for nonvanishing transported phase

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.text: If $t_0<T$, the selected seed is jointly smooth on the active slab, the envelope radius is positive, $0<h\le1$ and the switch rate is nonnegative, then the switched leading profile is jointly smooth for all $t\le T$. The flat smooth cutoff makes the preactivation part zero. No regularity of the unswitched seed before $t_0$ is required.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.summary: The switched leading profile is smooth through activation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.text: The smooth leading pressure extends to a jointly smooth switched pressure for every $t\le T$ when $t_0<T$ and the switch rate is nonnegative. The assumptions retain positive envelope radius, $0<h\le1$, smooth actual coefficients and a nonzero covector on the active slab. Flatness of the same switch used for velocity handles the time seam.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.summary: The pressure also extends smoothly through activation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.text: Under the active-seed smoothness, flat-switch, valid phase width and strict-envelope-collar assumptions, any jointly smooth label map `A` produces a jointly smooth localized transported leading wave on $[0,T]$. The proof evaluates the smooth twisted profile on the graph $(A(t,x),\langle k,A(t,x)\rangle)$. Flow identities and parity are unnecessary for this composition theorem.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.summary: Smooth graph evaluation gives the physical leading wave

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.text: Given a smooth selected amplitude on $[t_0,T]$, $t_0<T$, nonnegative switch rate, positive envelope radius with $2\ell<1/2$, and $0<h\le1$, the phase-twisted extension of the switched leading profile is jointly smooth for all $t\le T$. The launch covector `k` is arbitrary. Flatness handles time activation, and the strict spatial collar handles all lattice-cell walls.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.con.summary: The actual switched wave glues smoothly through every cell

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.env.text: For a seed on an interval of length at most one, combines fixed-plane center stability, a positive center norm, small generator variation on the scaled radius-two ball, and supplied scaled coframe, coefficient, and envelope jets. It obtains a global scaled jet bound for envelope times amplitude through order `N`. The explicit constant contains the order recurrence, both coframes, and the factor $\exp(1)$ from perturbing center stability.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.env.summary: Local weighted stability bounds the enveloped seed jets

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.eve.text: The localized amplitude remains even in the label when the coefficient fields $M$ and $\kappa$ are even. The assumptions `hM`, `hκ` and `hκne` give continuity in time and a nonzero covector; `hMeven` and `hκeven` give parity. The activation values agree at opposite labels, and uniqueness of the same linear equation preserves that equality on the active interval.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.eve.summary: The projected seed remains even in the label

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.exi.text: For each parameter order $n$, this chooses a phase constant before the seed, frequency, and time order. Given `freq ≥ 1`, seed regularity, a smooth time multiplier, and the stated amplitude, generator, pressure-coefficient, and multiplier derivative caps through $q$, both the multiplied leading velocity and frequency-times-pressure have scaled derivative bounds proportional to $\gamma(t)\mathrm{freq}^{-5/4}$. Their explicit coefficients contain the finite homogeneous-growth and product costs.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.exi.summary: The leading velocity and normalized pressure have weighted time bounds

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.fix.text: For a seed on $[l,r]$, a nonvanishing transported covector, continuous inverse coframes, and the coframe evolution equation, the readout $R(\mathrm{amplitude})$ solves the fixed-plane homogeneous equation with generator $-2RMJ$. Its initial value is the readout of the central amplitude, and lifting by `J` recovers the seed. The proof compares the lifted ODE solution using uniqueness.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.fix.summary: Read the seed in its fixed transverse plane

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: Uses the value of `PaperWaveCutoff` as the multiplier of the regular leading seed and wraps the result into the parent’s twisted profile space. This permits the constant first-wave cutoff as well as later activations. The definition provides a field with bundled regularity; its momentum equation and symmetry are separate theorems.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The leading wave with an arbitrary time cutoff

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: Combines the generic leading velocity and pressure into `HierarchyTransverseOutput` for the given coframe, strain and covector profiles. The constructor proves zero velocity average and the vanishing phase-advection condition from transversality. The covector must agree with the seed field; the momentum identity is established by a later theorem.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: Packaging the leading transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: For coefficient profiles agreeing with the seed’s strain and covector, the generic transverse output satisfies its material-plus-phase-gradient equation with `genericLeadingSwitch` as source. The proof transfers the raw identity through the profile representation and centered-cell uniqueness. This is a genuine equation for the constructed pair, conditional on the coefficient identifications.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The wrapped leading pair has the stated activation source

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: Applies the within-slab cutoff derivative to the same regular leading seed. Smoothness and vanishing before activation of that derivative are proved from the positive slab duration in `reg`. This field is the leading activation source; it excludes the curl-completion contribution, which is constructed separately.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The leading source created by the activation derivative

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: The generic leading switch has zero profile phase average. It is a time-only multiple of the same zero-mean seed as the leading velocity, so the velocity-average theorem applies to the cutoff derivative. This property is needed before completing the source by the normalized phase-potential construction.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The leading activation source has zero phase average

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: At a slab time and a label in the closed centered cell, the leading switch profile is exactly the cutoff derivative times the raw leading seed. The envelope fit removes the periodization from the evaluation identity. Including cell boundary points matters for the subsequent derivative and curl-completion identifications.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The activation source on the closed centered cell

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: The generic leading switch profile at a slab time equals the within-time cutoff derivative times the centered periodized leading wave. It gives the concrete source generated by differentiating the time cutoff. The completion source remains a separate term, so this evaluation alone is not the entire physical residual.

The generic leading switch has odd reflection parity under the same active-label evenness hypothesis on the amplitude. Its scalar multiplier is the cutoff derivative, which depends only on time and vanishes before activation. This supplies the parity needed to complete the source without breaking the approximate velocity’s symmetry.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The leading activation source is odd under reflection

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: The generic leading switch is orthogonal to a covector profile agreeing with the seed’s transported covector on the slab. This specializes transversality of time multiples to the cutoff derivative. The conclusion is pointwise orthogonality, which is used to show the corresponding phase-advection contribution vanishes.

On the centered label cell, the wrapped leading profile equals $\widetilde\chi(t)A_1(t,a,s)$. The amplitude and radial envelope belong to the selected SeedOn family, with quantitative regularity ensuring the envelope fits strictly inside the cell. The vanishing collar makes periodization agree with the original profile there. The theorem accepts any admissible time cutoff and any real initial wave vector. It does not state this identity for arbitrary envelope and phase-profile choices.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The switched leading wave on the centered cell

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: The generic leading profile at a slab time is the cutoff value times the centered twisted periodization of the seed’s leading wave. This exposes the concrete meaning of the bundled profile for arbitrary labels and phases. The formula retains periodization and therefore does not assume the label lies in the centered cell.

The leading-wave derivative at the origin is exactly $\widetilde\chi(t)\mathbf a(t,0)\otimes\kappa(t,0)$. The cutoff `χ : PaperWaveCutoff t₀ T` is arbitrary. The hypotheses `hX`, `hU`, `hper` and `hodd` describe the parent and ensure its flow fixes the origin; `reg` gives the localized seed regularity. The profile identities $g(0)=F_h'(0)=1$ and $F_h(0)=0$ remove all slow-derivative contributions at that point.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The leading wave gives the central rank-one gradient

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: The generic leading velocity has reflection sign minus one when the seed amplitude is even in labels on its active slab. The time cutoff affects neither label nor phase parity. This is the symmetry property later transferred through an odd parent flow to obtain the odd physical approximate velocity.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The chosen leading wave is odd under reflection

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: Applies the cutoff value to the regular seed’s leading pressure, preserving the same carrier and phase normalization as the leading velocity. The result is a scalar twisted profile. Its zero phase mean and even reflection parity are proved separately, and the signed Hessian bound requires the analytic parent estimates.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The leading pressure with an arbitrary time cutoff

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: On the centered label cell, the wrapped pressure is the time cutoff multiplied by the selected unswitched pressure. The regularity data fix the radial envelope and the normalized pressure primitive $P_h$, and ensure the envelope vanishes near the cell boundary. Hence wrapping does not alter its values on that cell. The result is an exact evaluation formula; it is not a pressure estimate or a theorem for arbitrary smooth primitives.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The switched leading pressure on the label cell

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: The generic pressure profile evaluates, at a time in $[0,T]$, to the cutoff value times the centered periodized leading pressure. It is the scalar counterpart of the velocity evaluation formula. This identity is later used to transfer pressure parity, phase mean and pointwise Hessian estimates to the chosen cutoff.

Assumes one nonnegative quadratic-form bound `Q` holds for the seed pressure for every admissible selected switch rate. It transfers that bound to any `PaperWaveCutoff`. At each active interior time the proof chooses a rate that has already saturated, then multiplies by $0\le\chi\le1$; continuity reaches activation. The conclusion is one-sided, and the uniform `hFamily` hypothesis is essential.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: Every admissible cutoff preserves the signed pressure cap

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: For every slab time and label, the generic pressure’s phase mean is zero. The normalized pressure primitive has zero phase average, and the time cutoff and centered phase translation preserve it. This fixes the phase-pressure representative used in the transverse output; it is distinct from fixing the spatial mean of the Eulerian pressure.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The switched leading pressure retains its normalization

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.text: Assuming amplitude, strain and covector are even in labels on the active interval, the generic pressure has reflection sign plus one. The pressure primitive is even, while the radial envelope and time cutoff preserve that symmetry. The proof treats the off-slab and pre-activation zero regions separately from the active formula.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen.summary: The chosen leading pressure is even under reflection

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.has.text: At a time in the active interval $[t_0,T]$, the leading seed has within-time derivative equal to minus its strain action and phase-pressure gradient. The width satisfies $0<h\le1$. This is a homogeneous equation for the unswitched seed; multiplying by a time cutoff later produces the separate activation source.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.has.summary: The unswitched seed solves the homogeneous equation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.has.text: For $r \ge  0$ and $0 < h \le  1$, the switched seed obeys its forced linear momentum equation as a derivative within the full slab. Before activation all terms vanish; at the seam the left and right within derivatives are joined. This establishes the equation at the activation time as well as away from it.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.has.summary: Join the switched seed equation across activation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.has.text: Assume the inverse-label map fixes the origin, has derivative `Ax` there and satisfies `Ax.adjoint k = κ t 0`. Then the selected leading graph has derivative equal to the activation factor times the rank-one map formed from the central amplitude and covector. The theorem uses the seed’s profile normalization and regularity, including the localized envelope near the origin.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.has.summary: The leading wave contributes the expected rank-one gradient

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.has.text: For a smooth odd periodic parent flow, the derivative of the selected leading graph at the origin is the switch times the rank-one map formed from the central seed amplitude and the actual label wave vector. The flow hypotheses establish the inverse-label derivative and the fact that the origin is fixed. No remainder estimate is included.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.has.summary: The actual parent gives the central rank-one wave term

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.hie.text: From a smooth periodic odd parent and its label flow, a nonzero carrier, $0 \le  t_0 < T$, and admissible envelope, phase, and switch parameters, obtains `HierarchyRegularity` for the seed. It also proves label evenness of amplitude, material gradient, and transported covector. The amplitude parity and regularity come from the seed construction, not additional assumptions here.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.hie.summary: An odd smooth parent supplies the seed regularity

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.lea.text:
The unswitched leading profile is the selected amplitude multiplied by `radialEnvelope ell a` and `waveProfile h s`. Its argument `w` is a `SeedOn`, whose activation data are the projection of the prescribed central amplitude, rather than an arbitrary transverse field. The definition therefore implements the paper with its later chosen radial envelope and profile family. It has exactly the product form $g\mathbf aF_h$ but is narrower than the earlier notation with arbitrary $g$ and $F_0$.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula is defined for every width and radius. Smoothness and the uniform profile estimates use ℓ>0 and 0<h≤1; the seed record supplies its equation and near-center properties on the active interval.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.lea.summary: Unswitched localized oscillation from the selected seed

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.lea.text:
The unswitched pressure multiplies `wavePressurePrimitive h` by the negative `wavePressureCoefficient`. That coefficient includes the radial envelope and the coupling $2\langle\kappa,M\mathbf a\rangle/\|\kappa\|^2$. The binder `w` again fixes the `SeedOn` amplitude with projected activation data. Thus this is the chosen-family version of $-p_{\rm w}gP_0$, not a definition parameterized by an arbitrary odd periodic profile and arbitrary envelope.

Default-value audit (b5): The raw pressure formula contains the inverse squared covector norm and the normalized profile primitive. The nonzero-covector, width and smoothness conditions are established by the seed and profile theorems.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.lea.summary: Leading pressure for the selected localized wave

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.lea.text: The explicit pressure, minus the wave-pressure coefficient times the normalized phase primitive, agrees as a phase function with `oscillatoryPhasePressure` for the leading oscillation and zero forcing. This is an algebraic identification for arbitrary real width and time. It does not add nonvanishing or smoothness hypotheses; those are imposed when interpreting the reciprocal coefficient analytically.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.lea.summary: The explicit leading pressure equals the phase solver pressure

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.lea.text: Defines the raw leading activation source as the derivative of the switch multiplied by the unswitched leading velocity. The label and phase remain independent here. A separate wrapping step will put the expression into the twisted profile space, while the completion part of the activation residual is constructed separately.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.lea.summary: The velocity term from differentiating the time cutoff

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.nor.text: The operator norm of the derivative of the Euclidean gradient equals the norm of the second iterated Fréchet derivative. The statement has no smoothness premise because both derivative constructions are total and their definitions agree under the Euclidean dual identification. Actual estimates invoke it only for pressures already proved smooth.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.nor.summary: The Hessian norm agrees with the second derivative norm

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pap.text: The raw leading velocity and its pressure satisfy the homogeneous transverse momentum equation throughout $[t_0,T]$. The hypotheses `hI : t₀ < T`, `hh : 0 < h`, and `hh₁ : h ≤ 1` accompany `w : SeedOn ...`. The same conclusion includes transversality and zero phase mean of both velocity and pressure. This statement applies to $A_1$, before activation is multiplied in; the switched profile has an additional derivative-of-cutoff source.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pap.summary: The unswitched leading wave has zero forcing

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pre.text: Let the label map and its inverse be continuous, and let both pressures be smooth. If the pressures agree on the preimage of the closed centered cell, their Hessians agree at every point of that set, including its boundary. The argument differentiates on the interior and extends by continuity; equality on an arbitrary thin closed set would not suffice.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pre.summary: Pressure agreement on the closed cell includes its boundary Hessian

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.text: The displayed carrier, strain, coframe, phase-width and center caps, together with the scaled label coefficient jets, produce a `PrimaryPressureBudget` for the actual parent inverse flow. The resulting coframe constant is `L * B`, and the coefficient constant includes the squared inverse-label derivative cost. The theorem packages quantitative hypotheses; it does not establish the supplied label jet estimate.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.summary: Construct the leading pressure budget from label coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.text: This version starts with bounds on the envelope-weighted seed amplitude and normalized pressure-amplitude coefficient instead of an already bounded label coefficient. Their product supplies the missing label jets, after which the parent geometry builds `PrimaryPressureBudget`. All regularity, carrier, coframe and central caps remain explicit assumptions, so this is a conditional assembly theorem.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.summary: Construct the pressure budget from the actual seed jets

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.text: At the inverse label `a = A t x`, this coefficient is twice the activation-envelope factor times the inner product of the covector with strain applied to the seed amplitude, divided by the covector’s squared norm. It is the scalar $c_{\mathbf a}$ in the leading pressure $-c_{\mathbf a}P_h$. Its sign is proved later from the selected seed.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.summary: The scalar multiplying the leading pressure primitive

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.text: At an active time, a second-order bound for the carrier-scaled label coefficient and derivative bounds for the rescaled inverse-label map imply common bounds for the physical coefficient, its gradient and Hessian. The bound is $2C_0J^2\mathrm{freq}^{-7/4}$. Positive frequency and `J ≥ 1` are explicit, and seed regularity supplies positive envelope length.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.summary: Convert coefficient jets from labels to physical space

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.text: Assume the central amplitude cap, second-order bounds for the envelope-weighted seed, and smooth second-order bounds for the normalized pressure-amplitude coefficient. Their product gives a second-order bound for the carrier-scaled leading pressure coefficient. The constant is $4P_0B_0\mathrm{freq}^{-3/4}$; all input coefficient bounds are nonnegative.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pri.summary: Build coefficient jets from amplitude and pressure factors

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.reg.text: For a smooth periodic odd parent, a nonzero launch covector and $0\le t_0<T$, every already selected `SeedOn` for the actual material gradient and transported covector is jointly smooth on its closed active slab and even in the label. Smooth parameter dependence proves regularity; ODE uniqueness proves parity from the projected initial data. The theorem preserves the same seed rather than selecting a replacement.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.reg.summary: The selected seed is smooth and even under an odd parent

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.sca.text: Defines the slow amplitude $\chi_{\ell}(\ell x)\,a(t,\ell x)$ from a supplied seed, using the fixed radial envelope and radius-scaled labels. The envelope does not depend on time, so the same homogeneous amplitude generator governs this field. Positivity of the radius and smoothness enter through `HierarchyRegularity` in the later estimates, rather than through this definition.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.sca.summary: The envelope amplitude in radius-scaled labels

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.text: Defines the switched leading oscillation by multiplying the envelope-supported profile `w.leading h` by `waveSwitch t₀ r t`. It retains the same selected seed amplitude, phase width `h` and activation time. For nonnegative `r` it is zero through activation; subsequent theorems require a positive envelope radius and $0<h\le1$ to obtain the intended smooth profile properties.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.summary: The localized seed with its actual activation switch

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.text: For a nonnegative switch rate and any time $t\le t_0$, the switched leading profile is exactly zero at every label and phase. This requires no smoothness, phase-width restriction or envelope-radius sign, because the zero switch alone annihilates the profile. The equality includes the activation instant and underpins the flat extension argument.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.summary: The leading profile vanishes through the activation time

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.text: For positive envelope radius, the switched leading profile is zero wherever the label norm is at least twice that radius. The result holds at every time and phase, without a sign restriction on the switch rate or a condition on the phase width. It is the spatial support equality used to remove the label-cell boundary seams.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.summary: The leading profile vanishes beyond the envelope radius

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.text: Assuming $T > 0$, $r \ge  0$, and $0 < h \le  1$, the actual `derivWithin` on $[0,T]$ plus strain and phase-pressure terms equals the switch forcing at every slab time. Positivity of `T` supplies unique differentiability, converting the derivative witness into the derivative value used by the hierarchy operators.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.summary: The leading momentum balance on the closed slab

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.text: If $r \ge  0$ and $t \le  t_0$, the switch forcing, switched leading velocity, and phase derivative of the switched pressure all vanish. The statement includes the seam itself. The pressure conclusion follows because at such a time the entire phase function is zero, rather than from a bound on its primitive.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.summary: All leading momentum terms vanish before activation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.text: Assume the selected seed is even in the label on its active slab, the phase width lies in $(0,1]$ and the switch rate is nonnegative. For every $t\le T$, simultaneous negation of label and phase negates the switched leading profile. Before activation this follows from zero switching; during activation it combines the even envelope and seed with the odd scalar phase profile.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.summary: The switched profile is odd under combined reflection

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.text: At every fixed time and label, the switched leading profile is one-periodic in its independent phase when $0<h\le1$. Its amplitude, radial envelope and switch are independent of the phase, so they preserve the scalar profile’s period. This does not assert ordinary label periodicity before the supported cell-extension construction.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.summary: The switched leading profile retains unit phase periodicity

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.text: Defines the switched pressure by multiplying `w.leadingPressure h` by the same `waveSwitch t₀ r t` used for the leading velocity. This keeps the velocity-pressure pair synchronized through activation. Its formula still contains the reciprocal squared transported-covector norm; smoothness is established later using nonvanishing and joint regularity of the actual coefficients.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.summary: The leading pressure with the same activation switch

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.text: For the actual smooth periodic odd parent, nonzero launch covector and $0\le t_0<T$, the selected seed yields jointly smooth switched velocity and pressure for all $t\le T$. Positive envelope radius, $0<h\le1$ and nonnegative switch rate are required. The theorem also proves simultaneous label-phase oddness of the leading velocity; periodic spatial gluing is a separate result.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.swi.summary: The actual parent gives smooth symmetric switched profiles

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.tra.text: For a smooth periodic odd parent, nonzero launch covector, $0\le t_0<T$, nonnegative switch rate, $0<h\le1$ and a positive envelope strictly inside the cell, the selected seed’s physical leading wave is jointly smooth on $[0,T]$, spatially periodic and odd. It uses the actual inverse parent flow. The conclusion concerns the leading wave; the divergence correction is required separately for a solenoidal completed velocity.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.tra.summary: The actual physical leading wave is smooth periodic and odd

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.tra.text: The transported switched seed pressure is exactly the negative product of `primaryPressureCoefficient` with the periodic pressure primitive evaluated at the transported phase. This equality is purely definitional and holds for arbitrary displayed parameters. It exposes the product whose second derivative has a signed leading tensor and smaller geometric terms.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.tra.summary: Write the transported pressure as coefficient times primitive

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.tra.text: For a regular seed and `PrimaryPressureBudget`, the raw transported pressure Hessian is bounded above as a quadratic form by the explicit constant times $\mathrm{freq}^{-1/4}$. The proof uses the sign of the leading rank-one term and bounds the remaining tensors in norm. It does not bound the absolute Hessian norm or its negative eigenvalues.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.tra.summary: The leading pressure has a small upper quadratic bound

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: Defines the completion part of the activation residual by applying the concrete curl completion to `twistedLeadingSwitch`. The supplied covector profile must be phase independent and nonzero on every slab slice. Completing the already switched source preserves smooth activation without requiring the unswitched seed to extend smoothly across `t₀`.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Apply curl completion to the activation source

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: Assuming the covector compatibility used in the completion evaluation theorem, the completion switch vanishes whenever a slab time satisfies $t \le  t_0$. Its factorization contains the derivative of the switch, which is zero on that half-line. This gives the inactive-time property for the second part of the activation residual.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The completion source vanishes through activation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: At a label in the interior of the centered cell and a slab time, the completion switch equals the switch derivative times the slow curl of the unwrapped seed potential. Interior membership provides a neighborhood where wrapping and raw values agree, so their Fréchet derivatives agree. The statement explicitly requires covector compatibility and nondegeneracy.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The completion source agrees with the interior curl formula

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: Extends the completion-switch formula from the interior to every label in the closed centered cell. Smooth wrapped and raw potential profiles agree on the cell, and unique differentiability identifies their derivatives there. The proof keeps the switch derivative inside the smooth source until after differentiation, so the activation seam remains covered.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The completion formula remains valid on cell faces

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: On the slab, and when the hierarchy covector equals the seed covector, the completion switch equals the switch derivative times `wrappedUnswitchedCompletion`. The proof moves a time-only scalar through the phase potential, label derivative, and curl. It does not differentiate the unswitched seed in time, so no time extension is needed here.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The completion source factors out the switch derivative

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: With even coframe and covector profiles and an even seed amplitude, the completion switch has odd joint reflection parity. The proof applies the concrete completion parity theorem to the already odd, zero-phase-mean leading switch. Nonzero phase-independent covector assumptions are retained because this is the actual curl completion operator.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Curl completion preserves the activation source parity

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: Wraps the actual switched leading velocity into `HierarchyTwistedProfile T k Vec3`, using the proved smoothness of its centered periodization and its phase periodicity. The regularity bundle is required at construction. The carrier `k` can be arbitrary here; its compatibility with the parent covector is imposed when building the transverse hierarchy output.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The switched seed as a twisted velocity profile

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: Builds `HierarchyTransverseOutput` from the wrapped velocity and pressure. The velocity has zero phase average, and its fast advection against every test profile vanishes because the seed is perpendicular to the actual covector. The hypothesis `hκ` identifies the hierarchy covector with the seed covector throughout the slab; no corresponding strain identity is required until the momentum theorem.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Package the switched seed as a transverse output

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: With `hM` and `hκ` identifying hierarchy strain and covector with the seed coefficients, the material operator on the wrapped velocity plus phase gradient of its pressure equals the wrapped leading switch. The proof checks the closed centered cell using the actual within-time derivative, then extends by skew periodicity to the entire profile space.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The wrapped leading equation has exactly the switch source

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: The actual later-wave completion and pressure, after subtracting the completion switch, equal the zero-forcing relay of the switched velocity. The theorem assumes the parent coefficients’ phase independence, transport equations, and agreement with the seed geometry. Centering and transversality are derived for the selected leading profile and switch before applying the general cancellation identity.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The leading relay is homogeneous after subtracting the switch

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: Wraps the raw product of the switch derivative and the unswitched leading velocity into the twisted profile space. Its regularity proof includes smooth gluing at activation and at cell faces. This is only the velocity part of the switch residual; curl completion supplies a second contribution.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The wrapped velocity part of the activation residual

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: The wrapped leading switch has zero phase average as a twisted profile. Its switch derivative and envelope are phase-independent scalar factors multiplying the zero-mean wave profile. The proof therefore uses the same period-translation and integral-linearity argument as the leading velocity, rather than any time equation.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The activation source has zero phase average

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: At any slab time up to and including `t₀`, the twisted leading switch is zero at every label and phase. The proof uses that the smooth switch has derivative zero on the inactive half-line. Thus the activation source itself glues to zero at the seam, not only the switched velocity.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The wrapped switch source vanishes through activation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: On the slab and closed centered cell, the twisted leading switch agrees with the raw derivative-cutoff source. Its radial envelope vanishes before reaching the cell faces, which makes the wrapping irrelevant there. The theorem does not claim the raw formula is ordinarily periodic in labels outside this cell.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Recover the activation source throughout the centered cell

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: At a time in $[0,T]$, the twisted leading switch evaluates to the centered phase periodization of `leadingSwitchProfile`. This equality connects the abstract profile operator calculation with the raw derivative-cutoff source. Outside the slab the profile uses its zero representation, so the theorem is deliberately restricted to slab times.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Evaluate the wrapped activation source on the slab

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: An even seed amplitude makes the twisted leading switch odd under simultaneous label and phase reflection. The switch derivative depends only on time, while the envelope is even and the wave profile is odd. Before activation the source vanishes, so the parity proof also covers times outside the seed’s active interval.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The velocity activation source has odd reflection parity

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: For a regular localized seed and a twisted covector agreeing with its transported wave vector, the switched leading force is transverse at every slab point. Before activation it vanishes; afterward transversality comes from the seed. Twisted periodicity transports the centered-cell calculation to every label, so the claim is not limited to the envelope’s preferred cell.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The activation force is perpendicular to the wave vector

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: The phase-average operator applied to the twisted leading velocity is the zero profile. On each slab slice, the velocity is a scalar multiple of the zero-mean wave profile, and centered phase translation preserves that mean. Profile extensionality then promotes the slice identities to equality in the twisted profile space.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The leading velocity has zero phase average

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: For a slab time satisfying $t \le  t_0$, the twisted leading velocity is zero at every label and phase. This follows from the nonnegative-rate switch vanishing on the entire earlier interval, and survives centered wrapping. The statement includes the activation slice and imposes no support restriction on the label.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The wrapped leading velocity vanishes through activation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: At a slab time and a label in the closed centered cell, the twisted leading profile equals the raw switched seed. The envelope support and strict cell-fitting condition remove the effect of periodization, including on cell faces. This permits the raw seed ODE to be used in profile identities.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Recover the leading seed throughout the centered cell

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: For a slab time, unwraps the twisted leading velocity to the centered phase periodization of `switchedLeading`. This is the whole-label-space evaluation formula. Recovering the raw, unperiodized seed additionally requires that the label lie in the centered cell, as handled by a later theorem.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Evaluate the wrapped leading velocity on the slab

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: For a seed with `HierarchyRegularity`, reading the twisted leading profile on the inverse-label phase graph gives the original localized transported leading wave at every slab time. This is equality on the entire spatial lift, not only the central label cell. It connects the periodic profile construction to the explicit seed formula.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The selected leading profile has the localized physical value

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: For any closed set `S` containing the support of the periodized envelope, the leading velocity, pressure, velocity switch, and completion switch vanish on the inactive region. The first three vanish directly from the time cutoff or envelope. Locality of the phase primitive and slow curl propagates the same property to completion.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Both leading profiles and both sources vanish together

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: For a regular later seed, converts order-`n` scaled jet bounds for switched velocity and frequency-weighted pressure into amplitude-seminorm bounds for the wrapped profiles. The only added factor is the number of admissible mixed words through order `n`. The weight is continuous and strictly positive on the active interval; `freq`, `BV`, and `BP` are assumed nonnegative.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Raw seed jets bound the wrapped leading seminorms

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: If the seed amplitude is even in labels throughout the active interval, the twisted leading velocity is odd under $(a,s) \mapsto  (-a,-s)$. The radial envelope is even and the wave profile is odd in phase. The proof includes the inactive interval and the zero representation off the slab.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Joint label and phase reflection changes velocity sign

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: If the centered representative of a label has norm at least $2 \cdot  \ell$, then the wrapped leading velocity, pressure, and velocity switch all vanish at that label and every phase. The time must lie in the slab. This directly proves support localization for the three multiplicative envelope formulas; completion is handled separately.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Velocity pressure and switch share the envelope support

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: Given raw scaled derivative bounds for the switched leading velocity, frequency-times-pressure, and leading switch profile, this bounds the factorial time seminorms of the corresponding wrapped profiles. Each uses the same sum of time weights and admissible-word count. The pressure conclusion is `freq * P ≤ C * BP`, with only `freq ≥ 0`; it is not an unweighted pressure bound when that factor vanishes.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Wrapped leading profiles inherit their raw time bounds

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: Wraps the actual switched leading pressure into the scalar twisted profile space. Smoothness and phase periodicity come from the regularity bundle and the pressure-primitive construction. The selected pressure has zero phase mean, proved below, which fixes its phase gauge but is distinct from a zero spatial mean for the final Eulerian pressure.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The switched pressure as a twisted scalar profile

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: For $t \in  [0,T]$ with $t \le  t_0$, the twisted pressure vanishes for every label and phase. The time cutoff is zero, so the entire pressure profile is zero before any periodization is considered. This is a value identity and not merely a vanishing phase derivative.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The wrapped leading pressure vanishes through activation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: At a slab time and a label in the centered cell, the twisted pressure is the raw switched leading pressure. Factoring out the envelope proves the radial vanishing needed for the wrapping identity. This equality is used before taking phase derivatives in the leading momentum calculation.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Recover the leading pressure throughout the centered cell

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: At a time in $[0,T]$, evaluating the twisted pressure equals the centered phase periodization of the switched pressure formula. The statement holds for all labels and phases. It exposes the constructed value for later phase-average and momentum calculations, without removing the periodization at arbitrary labels.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Evaluate the wrapped leading pressure on the slab

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: The graph of the twisted pressure associated with a regular seed equals the localized transported switched pressure for every time in the closed slab. This identifies the actual selected scalar field with the explicit pressure profile. It is a value identity, so derivative estimates still require smoothness and compatibility of the inverse-label map.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The selected pressure equals its localized physical formula

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: For a smooth lattice-equivariant inverse-label map with continuous inverse, every physical point has a lattice translate whose inverse label lies in the centered cell. The actual twisted-pressure Hessian at the original point equals the raw transported-pressure Hessian at that translate. This gives a precise transfer of local pressure estimates to the whole periodic lift.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Translate the physical Hessian to a central label cell

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: The same upper quadratic-form bound holds for the actual twisted-pressure graph when the smooth inverse-label map is lattice equivariant and has a continuous inverse. The proof translates to the closed centered cell and uses Hessian agreement there. The conclusion remains one-sided; periodic extension does not turn it into an operator-norm estimate.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The signed bound holds across periodic cell faces

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: For the inverse map of a smooth periodic parent flow, a regular seed and the stated primary budget give the global signed Hessian upper bound for the twisted pressure graph. The flow supplies the inverse and lattice identities required by the cell-translation theorem. The conclusion controls the quadratic form above and makes no absolute smallness claim.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The actual parent transports the signed pressure bound

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: At every slab time and label, the phase mean of the twisted leading pressure is zero. The coefficient and switch are independent of phase, while the chosen pressure primitive has zero mean. Centered wrapping changes phase only by translation, so it preserves this gauge condition.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The leading pressure uses the zero phase mean gauge

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: Assuming label-even amplitude, strain, and covector on the active interval, the twisted leading pressure is even under simultaneous label and phase reflection. The scalar pressure coefficient is even and its phase primitive is even. Envelope vanishing at cell faces ensures that centered wrapping respects the same reflection identity.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: Joint reflection preserves the leading pressure

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.text: With a positive envelope radius strictly inside the cell and the stated phase and switch restrictions, the twisted switched profile agrees with the original profile throughout the closed centered cell at every time. If the selected amplitude is even on the active slab, the extension is odd under simultaneous label-phase reflection for all $t\le T$. Boundary agreement uses envelope vanishing rather than a false reflection rule for centered representatives.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.twi.summary: The extension agrees locally and reflects globally

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.wei.text: The leading velocity divided by $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ is at most $\lambda^{-5/4}$; the phase pressure satisfies the companion bound with $4\mathsf D^3$. The assumptions include `hc`, nonvanishing at the center, `hκ`, a lower covector bound, and `hM`, the strain bound. The scalar cutoff lies in $[0,1]$. The velocity estimate uses the near-center comparison contained in the seed.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.wei.summary: The leading velocity and pressure at amplitude scale

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.wra.text: At a fixed time, label, and phase, takes the slow curl of the potential of the centered wrapped unswitched leading velocity using the supplied coframe. Only label differentiation is involved. The definition remains meaningful without a time-smooth extension of the unswitched seed across activation; the switched completion is proved equal to a scalar multiple later.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.wra.summary: Spatial curl completion of the unswitched seed

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.amplitudeL.text:
The physical label error includes both Duhamel terms and the frame change.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression is a finite explicit estimate, not a norm by definition. Nonnegative geometric data and the Duhamel argument justify the bound used by the seed construction.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.amplitudeL.summary: The variation of the physical amplitude across labels

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframeLif.text:
The forward frame $A_\perp$ as a linear map from the fixed plane $k_*^\perp$ to physical vectors. It is `F.comp (transversePlane k).subtypeL`, so `F` is applied to a vector already in that plane. Lean uses the plane itself, with its inherited Euclidean norm, rather than choosing an orthonormal coordinate matrix from $\mathbb R^2$. With `F` equal to the flow derivative, this is the coordinate-free version of the paper's transported columns.

Default-value audit (b5): For k=0 the transverse-plane subtype is the whole space. Identifying this as a two-dimensional transported frame requires nonzero k and inverse-deformation identities.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframeLif.summary: The transported frame on the fixed transverse plane

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframeLif.text: The transported transverse frame satisfies $\partial_tA_\perp=MA_\perp$. The hypothesis `hF : HasDerivWithinAt F ((M t).comp (F t)) I t` gives the corresponding evolution of the full deformation. Composing with the fixed inclusion of $k_*^\perp$ commutes with this time derivative. The within-interval derivative includes boundary times when the supplied deformation derivative is available there.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframeLif.summary: Evolution of the transported transverse frame

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframePul.text:
The backward map from physical vectors to the fixed plane $k_*^\perp$. The definition first projects onto the plane perpendicular to `G.adjoint k`, then applies the inverse deformation `G`. A final orthogonal projection makes the codomain the fixed plane; the next source lemma shows the intermediate vector already belongs there. With mutually inverse forward and backward deformations, `coframe_identities` gives the two inverse and projection identities used in the paper.

Default-value audit (b5): Projection and pullback are total operations. At a zero transported covector the transverse projection becomes the identity; the physical coframe results supply nonzero data and the inverse identities.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframePul.summary: Coordinates after projection onto the moving plane

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframePul.text: A continuous inverse-coframe curve gives a continuous coordinate reader provided its adjoint image of the launch covector never vanishes on the time set. Nonvanishing is essential for the continuity result for the normalized transverse projection. No differentiability of the inverse coframe is required, which is useful when the seed proof differentiates only the forward lift.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframePul.summary: A nondegenerate inverse coframe has a continuous reader

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframe_co.text: If $GF=I$, the launch covector is nonzero and $\|F\|\le D$, then $G^*k$ is nonzero and $\|k\|\le D\|G^*k\|$. The adjoint of the inverse identity recovers `k` from its transport. This both licenses the normalized transverse projection and converts absolute inverse-coframe changes into errors relative to the transported covector.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframe_co.summary: An inverse pair keeps the transported covector nonzero

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframe_id.text: The backward map followed by the forward frame is the identity on the fixed transverse plane, while the reverse composition is the physical transverse projection. The hypotheses `hGF` and `hFG` say that `G` and `F` are mutual inverses. Thus the coordinate-free maps satisfy $A_\perp^\dagger A_\perp=I$ and $A_\perp A_\perp^\dagger=I-P_\kappa$. The covector in the projection is `G.adjoint k`, the transported launch covector.

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.contDiffOn.text: Restriction of the forward coframe to the fixed launch plane is smooth.
The projected inverse coframe is smooth wherever the transported covector is nonzero.

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.contDiff_t.text: The fixed transverse coframe and its evolution operator are jointly smooth whenever the input coefficients are smooth and the covector stays nonzero.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.contDiff_t.summary: Smooth coframe fields for a nonvanishing covector

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_com.text: One absolute envelope exponent enforces both the fixed-coordinate Duhamel perturbation budget and the physical coupling budget.
