TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_com.summary: One envelope exponent controls both perturbation budgets

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_lat.text: Chooses a universal natural threshold at least $240$. Any supplied growing crossing satisfying the stated ratio and error smallness conditions, with nonzero scale and rescaled time at least two, then gives `CenterWaveOn` on its physical time interval. The chosen `D` must dominate both the shear growth constant and the reciprocal first-coupling budget. The crossing itself is an input, not constructed by this theorem.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_lat.summary: Growing crossings supply the later center data

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_pap.text: The unswitched leading velocity and its normalized pressure have weighted size at most $C_n\mathsf D^{20}\lambda^{-5/4}$ on $[t_0,T]$. The parent flow bounds, the carrier normalization, and `CenterWaveOn` are explicit hypotheses. The seed `w` also supplies `w.HierarchyRegularity 0 h`, with $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. Both norms differentiate the independent label and phase variables before the amplitude weight is applied. This is the raw leading profile, before multiplying it by an activation cutoff.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_pap.summary: The unswitched leading wave and pressure are small

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.text: For a fixed parent jet table `W`, chooses one radius threshold $A\ge30$ before derivative order, then an order constant before the parent and seed. Under the physical scale, flow and central-wave hypotheses, any profiles whose active-cell values are a common multiplier `c`, with $|c|\le1$, times the seed satisfy the weighted velocity-plus-frequency-pressure bound $CD^{20}\lambda^{-5/4}$. Time derivatives of `c` are not estimated.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.summary: Uniform amplitude bounds for arbitrary bounded time multipliers

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.text: For a fixed parent jet-control sequence, chooses one exponent $A \ge  30$ before the derivative order; each order then receives constants `C`, `Bseed`, and `Pcoef`. Under the stated smooth-flow, deformation, center-wave, frequency, and radius assumptions, these bound leading velocity and frequency-weighted pressure by $\gamma\cdot C\cdot D^{20}\cdot \mathrm{freq}^{-5/4}$, enveloped amplitude by $\mathrm{Bseed}\cdot D^{13}\cdot \lVert \mathrm{center}\rVert$, and normalized pressure coefficient by $\mathrm{Pcoef}\cdot D^7$.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.summary: One radius choice supports every order of seed jets

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.text: Projects the leading velocity and frequency-weighted pressure estimates from the combined parent seed theorem. For a fixed nonnegative parent jet sequence, one radius exponent works at all orders; the multiplicative constant is selected separately for each order. The theorem applies to every seed with the required center-wave, flow, deformation, frequency, and small-radius hypotheses, and to any fixed-time switch of magnitude at most one.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.summary: Actual parent data give the two leading jet budgets

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.text: For a fixed parent jet-control sequence, chooses a radius exponent and then an order-dependent constant bounding the wrapped leading velocity seminorm plus frequency times the wrapped pressure seminorm by $C\cdot D^{20}\cdot \mathrm{freq}^{-5/4}$. The actual seed must satisfy hierarchy regularity and the parent and center-wave hypotheses. Finite word counting converts scaled jets, while positive center amplitude permits normalization by `gamma`.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.summary: Wrapped leading waves satisfy the amplitude seminorm estimate

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.text: For a fixed nonnegative parent jet-control sequence, chooses nonnegative constants for every order before choosing the parent flow, deformation bound, carrier, or frequency. Smooth periodic parents on a slab of length at most one with bounded forward and inverse deformation then give smooth lift, readout, and generator fields. Their jets have powers $D^{16\cdot i+1}$, $D^{16\cdot i+9}$, and $D^{16\cdot i+11}$ through the prescribed order.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_par.summary: Parent jets give uniform transverse coframe budgets

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_see.text: For each fixed order and coframe constant at least one, chooses a constant $B \ge  1$ before the seed and parent parameters. Assuming center stability $D^3$, prescribed coframe jets, and $2\cdot \mathrm{C1}\cdot \ell\cdot D^{30} \le  1$, the enveloped amplitude has scaled jets bounded by $B\cdot D^{13}\cdot \lVert \mathrm{center}(t)\rVert$. The first generator derivative controls radius smallness, while higher-order constants enter only the prefactor.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_see.summary: The scaled enveloped seed costs thirteen parent powers

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_see.text: The central seed extends to nearby labels with projected activation data and quantitative comparison. The hypothesis `hStable` bounds every transverse solution relative to the central seed, and `hCoupling` supplies the positive central coupling. Deformation, coefficient and variation bounds are also required. The radius conditions `hSmall` and `hNear` make the label perturbation small enough. The conclusion constructs a `SeedOn` record rather than assuming its comparison estimates.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_see.summary: Localizing a seed with controlled transverse growth

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_see.text: A nonnegative parent derivative budget fixes a constant `C` and radius exponent $A\ge3$ before the parent is chosen. A smooth periodic odd flow, inverse deformation bounds, gradient bounds and `CenterWaveOn` then produce a seed on every positive radius $\ell\le D^{-A}$. Its covector is the actual transported launch covector; the seed retains the prescribed center, projected activation data, amplitude equation, transversality and quantitative near-center coupling.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_see.summary: A sufficiently small envelope localizes the actual parent wave

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.firstWave_.text: Packages the first-wave covector ODE, amplitude ODE, nonvanishing, transversality, weighted forward stability and positive raw coupling into `CenterWaveOn`. The hypotheses are positive frequency, $|s|\le1$, $T\|B_s\|\le1/8$ and $D\ge2$. It supplies the complete center data expected by the general localization theorem, with the stationary shear gradient as coefficient.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.firstWave_.summary: The first wave satisfies every center hypothesis

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.firstWave_.text: Recasts the first-wave center package using the derivative of the stationary parent velocity at the origin. The exact identity between this derivative and `stationaryShearGradient s` transports all ODE, stability and coupling fields unchanged. The same short-time, shear and positive-frequency hypotheses remain, so this wrapper connects the explicit first wave to the geometric parent theorem.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.firstWave_.summary: The first center data use the actual parent gradient

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.generatorL.text:
Label Lipschitz bound for the fixed-coordinate generator.

Default-value audit (b5): This polynomial is defined for arbitrary real inputs. Its interpretation as a nonnegative Lipschitz bound uses the nonnegative geometric bounds in the stability lemmas.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.generatorL.summary: The variation of the fixed-coordinate generator

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.nearLabelS.text:
The common sensitivity of the amplitude, covector and material gradient.

Default-value audit (b5): This maximum is defined for all real inputs. The two constituent estimates and nonnegative data are required before it controls the physical differences.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.nearLabelS.summary: A common bound for the near-center differences

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.text: The norm of the transported frame is at most the norm of the full deformation `F`. Restricting a linear map to the transverse plane cannot increase its operator norm, because the plane has the inherited Euclidean norm. There is no invertibility hypothesis in this inequality. The paper's $|A_\perp|\le\mathsf D$ follows when the standing flow bound gives $\|F\|\le\mathsf D$.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.summary: The frame norm is bounded by the deformation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.text: The difference of the two forward lifts from the fixed transverse plane has operator norm at most the difference of the ambient coframes. Both lifts are obtained by composition with the same norm-one subtype inclusion. This estimate transfers the parent deformation’s label Lipschitz bound directly into the coordinate generator comparison.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.summary: Restricting the coframe does not enlarge its difference

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.text: The norm of the coordinate-reading map is at most the norm of the inverse deformation `G`. Its preceding orthogonal projection has norm at most one, and the final codomain restriction preserves vector norms. The result holds for every `k` and `G`; the paper applies it when `G` is the inverse flow derivative with norm at most $\mathsf D$. It supplies the bound on $A_\perp^\dagger$ without a Gram-matrix estimate.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.summary: The inverse frame norm is bounded by inverse deformation

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.text: The coordinate-reader gap is bounded by $\|G-G_0\|+\|G_0\|\|P_{G^*k}-P_{G_0^*k}\|$. This is an algebraic norm estimate valid even for degenerate transported covectors; it uses the projection norm bound rather than continuity. The two terms distinguish changing inverse deformation from changing transverse direction in the nearby-label argument.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.summary: The reader difference splits into coframe and projection errors

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.text: Combines the forward coframe, inverse coframe, material gradient and transverse-projection differences into `generatorLabelSlope D LF LG LM LP` times the label distance `d`. The common norm bounds and nonnegative `D` control the composition factors. This is the generator estimate needed to apply weighted perturbation theory to the actual parent coordinates, rather than to abstract chosen lifts.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra.summary: Actual coframe bounds control the seed generator

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_fixed.text: Under a common nonnegative bound `D` for the specified gradient, lift and reader factors, the generator difference is at most $2D^2$ times the sum of the lift, reader and gradient differences. The assumptions are deliberately asymmetric: the estimate uses `J` and `R₀`, together with both gradients. This explicit bound determines the allowable label radius for Duhamel propagation.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_fixed.summary: Three coefficient differences control the generator difference

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_hasCo.text: The positive center weight has a continuous derivative on the closed slab.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_hasCo.summary: The positive center weight has a continuous derivative

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_itera.text: From smooth forward and inverse coframes, strain, and a nonzero covector, assumes raw jet budgets with slopes five, seven, six, and sixteen for the longitudinal projection. It bounds the transverse lift, readout, and fixed-plane generator through a common order using slope sixteen and offsets one, nine, and eleven. Explicit finite Leibniz constants account for each operator composition.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_itera.summary: One derivative slope controls lift readout and generator

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_relat.text: Suppose two inverse coframes differ by at most `L d`, and the launch covector is bounded by `D` times its reference transported norm. Their adjoint transports then differ by at most $LDd$ times that reference norm. The adjoint preserves operator norm. This converts an absolute coframe estimate into the relative covector estimate required by the coupling comparison.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_relat.summary: Inverse coframe differences give relative covector errors

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.paper_hier.text: On the active interval and within radius $2\ell_*$, the selected seed has amplitude at most twice its central amplitude and positive coupling $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a$. The inputs `w : SeedOn ...`, `ht : t ∈ Icc t₀ T`, and `hx : ‖x‖ ≤ 2 * ℓ` specify the seed and region. The result reads the established near-origin properties of `w`, using `w.at_center` to identify the center with the same seed's value at the origin.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.paper_hier.summary: Seed size and positive coupling near the origin

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.physical_e.text: If the nearby lift has norm at most `D`, the lift difference is at most `L d`, the reference coordinate has size at most `D g`, and the coordinate error is at most `B d g`, the physical error is at most $(DB+LD)dg$. The split $Jx-J_0y=J(x-y)+(J-J_0)y$ separates propagation error from the changing coordinates.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.physical_e.summary: Coordinate errors transfer to the physical amplitude

TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.transporte.text: The actual coframe has no zero transported covector for a nonzero launch.
TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.transporte.summary: A nonzero launch gives a nonzero transported covector

TorusEuler.MomentumTensor.text:
The columns of a real momentum tensor in the Euclidean coordinates of the lift.

Default-value audit (b5): This is the space of three vector-valued columns, with the function-space norm. Tensor contractions and their norm estimates are separately established.
TorusEuler.MomentumTensor.summary: A momentum tensor represented by its three columns

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.Entries.text: Abbreviates a doubly indexed family `Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ`, the type used for the older and full strain entries in the reduced amplitude formulas. It imposes no symmetry, trace, or size condition. The frame and operator definitions later provide geometric entries; individual theorems supply the analytic assumptions required for their comparisons.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.Entries.summary: Real matrix entries in the preceding frame

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.ScaledAmplitu.text: This finite index type separates the nine entries of the older strain, the nine entries of the full strain, and six scalar inputs. The nested sum type records which group a coordinate belongs to. It lets one apply a single multivariate polynomial estimate to all four entries of the reduced amplitude matrix.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.ScaledAmplitu.summary: Coordinates for the two strains and six scalars

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.U.text:
The coordinate $U=-S\,E_1\cdot\mathbf a$ of a transverse amplitude. The negative sign and factor $S$ match the growing direction, whose first and second frame components have opposite signs and different sizes. This definition does not require transversality. With nonzero $S$ and $Z$, transversality determines the third component from $U$ and $V$. Thus the arXiv coordinate is $\alpha_1=-U$.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.V.text:
The coordinate $V=E_2\cdot\mathbf a$, without the rescaling used for $U$. It records the component in the velocity direction of the preceding wave. The definition assumes neither a wave equation nor transversality. In the growing initial polarization $\mathbf a=-S^{-1}E_1+E_2$, the separate lemma `growing_components` gives $U=V=1$. This is the arXiv coordinate $\alpha_2$.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.V.summary: Second amplitude coordinate in the preceding frame

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_dec.text: A transverse amplitude equals $-(U/S)E_1+VE_2+((XU-QV)/(SZ))E_3$. The assumptions `he`, `hscale`, `hS`, `hZ` and `hperp` supply orthonormality, nonzero denominators and perpendicularity to $k$. The first two coordinates are defined projections; perpendicularity determines the third. This declaration reconstructs the given amplitude. It does not separately state an existence-and-uniqueness quantifier for arbitrary coordinate pairs.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_dec.summary: Transverse amplitude reconstructed from two coordinates

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_den.text: Assume $M,S\ge1$, the wave coordinates and reference coordinate are bounded by $M$, and `hclose` bounds $|X-x|+|Z-1|$ by $d\le1/2$. Then $Z\ge1/2$ and $m\ge1/4$, with reciprocal bounds and explicit errors. The final error includes $M^2/S$; it does not assume that the second wave coordinate already equals its reference value.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_den.summary: The amplitude denominators stay away from zero

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_den.text: On $[0,T]$, the coordinate comparison and $S^{-1}\le2\delta$ imply $Z\ge1/2$, $m\ge1/4$, and bounded reciprocals. The reciprocal wave norm differs from $s(\varepsilon,\tau)^2$ by at most $4(3T^2d+2T^4\delta)$. Here `s` is $\cos\varphi$. The hypotheses explicitly retain the coordinate error $d\le1/2$ and $S\ge1$.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_den.summary: Reciprocal bounds on the normalized interval

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_pai.text: For an orthonormal frame, nonzero wave scale, nonzero shear, and nonzero third wave-vector coordinate, perpendicularity determines all three amplitude components. The first two are $-U/S$ and $V$; the third is $(XU-QV)/(SZ)$. The current paper writes $U=-\alpha_1$, $V=\alpha_2$, and $(X,Q,Z)=\zeta$. This is an algebraic coordinate identity, independent of the amplitude evolution equation.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_pai.summary: Transversality determines the remaining amplitude component

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_wav.text: The six inputs are $X,Q,Z,S^{-1},Z^{-1},m^{-1}$. Their reference values are $x,-\varepsilon\tau,1,0,1,s^2$. Under the stated normalized window conditions, `hsmall` and `hclose` use $120\delta T^6\le1/2$. Both vectors lie in the box of radius $4T^2$, and each difference is at most $1448T^8\delta$. The theorem also returns $Z\ge1/2$.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.amplitude_wav.summary: Six scalar inputs have uniform comparison bounds

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.continuousOn_.text: The coefficient error is continuous on each interval where the moving coordinates are defined. Its entries depend on the strain and wave vector alone.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.continuousOn_.summary: Continuity of the amplitude coefficient error

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.errorOperator.text:
The raw error operator, in the same pair norm as the reference comparison.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.errorOperator.summary: The amplitude coefficient error in the pair norm

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.errorOperator.text: The amplitude coefficient error is at most $CM^n d$ when every actual and reference scaled input has size at most $M$ and their differences are at most $d$. Absolute `C`, `n` are chosen first. Nonzero $S,Z$, $M\ge1$ and $d\ge0$ are explicit assumptions. The input list includes reciprocal denominators; bounds for them must be supplied before this algebraic estimate yields the manuscript’s polynomial error.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.errorOperator.summary: Polynomial sensitivity of the amplitude coefficient error

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.errorOperator.text: Wave-coordinate closeness, normalized strain and coupling errors, positive shear, and the stated smallness give a uniform polynomial bound for the full amplitude error matrix. The proof bounds the rational inputs away from singular denominators, estimates the zero-correction matrix, and adds the correction-strain contribution at most six delta.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.errorOperator.summary: A polynomial bound for the amplitude matrix error

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.growing_compo.text: The chosen growing initial polarization has both raw amplitude coordinates equal to one. This algebraic initial-data calculation is used when comparing the perturbed system with the growing reference solution.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.growing_compo.summary: The growing polarization starts with two unit components

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.moving_amplit.text: From the preceding affine wave and a transverse new amplitude, derives the exact equations $U\prime=-\mathrm{damping}\,U+\mathrm{driving}\,V+(R(U,V))_1$ and $V\prime=U+(R(U,V))_2$. It assumes trace-free older strain, nonzero preceding vectors and coordinate scales, and `hZ`. Here $U=-\alpha_1$, $V=\alpha_2$; $R$ depends on the frame, strain and wave vector. No smallness bound on $R$ is proved by this identity.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.moving_amplit.summary: The amplitude follows the reference system plus one error operator

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.normFactor.text:
The factor $m=X^2+Q^2/S^2+Z^2$ in the squared wave-vector length. It is defined as a scalar expression with no hypotheses. The identity $|k|^2=\lambda^2m$ requires the orthonormal coordinate representation, and is stated separately by `wave_norm_sq_eq`. The bound $m\ge1/4$ later prevents the wave-pressure denominator from approaching zero on the comparison interval.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula contains an inverse or quotient. Its nondegenerate mathematical use requires the denominator conditions in the argument or the calling lemma; totalized inversion alone does not provide them.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.normFactor.summary: Squared length factor of the scaled wave vector

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.norm_errorOpe.text: Adding the strain $E$ changes the amplitude error operator by at most $6S\|E\|$. Here `E` is already divided by the physical growth rate $r$. The assumptions `he`, `hS`, `hx`, `hq`, `hz` give an orthonormal frame, $S\ge1$, $|X|,|Q|\le S$ and $Z\ge1/2$. The proof uses that the pressure-adjusted strain is a reflection, which preserves its vector norm.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.norm_errorOpe.summary: Additional strain contributes a controlled amplitude error

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.norm_pairOper.text: If every entry of a two-by-two matrix is at most $d$ in absolute value and `hd : 0 ≤ d`, bounds the norm of its action on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ by $2d$. Lean’s product norm is the maximum of the two coordinate magnitudes. This is not an assertion that the same operator was measured using the Euclidean pair norm.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.norm_pairOper.summary: Entry bounds control the two-component operator norm

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.normalized_am.text: The projected amplitude derivatives equal the action of the exact two-row matrix on $(U,V)$. The hypotheses require an orthonormal frame, nonzero frequency and shear, `hZ`, transversality `hperp`, the first two frame derivative identities, and the amplitude equation `ha` for the full strain `M`. This pointwise statement includes arbitrary additional strain. It does not assume a small perturbation or a particular growing solution.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.normalized_am.summary: Amplitude equations projected onto the moving frame

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.normalized_am.text: The growing-model coefficient and the raw error add to the exact physical rows.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.normalized_am.summary: The reference matrix and error give the exact equation

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.pairOperator.text:
This continuous linear map realizes a real two-by-two matrix on ℝ × ℝ. The pair carries the product maximum norm, which is the norm used by the reference comparison estimates.

Default-value audit (b5): The two-dimensional product uses the maximum norm. The matrix formula is total and linear; relating it to the Euclidean physical amplitude uses separate norm comparisons.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.pairOperator.summary: A two-by-two matrix acting on coordinate pairs

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.pairOperator_.text: Applying the pair operator gives the usual two matrix-row products. This connects the scalar amplitude equations to the bounded linear operator used in the perturbation argument.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.pairOperator_.summary: The matrix action written as two scalar rows

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.polynomial_ev.text: For any real multivariate polynomial `p`, there are $C\ge0$ and a natural exponent $n$ depending only on `p`. On every coordinate box of radius $M\ge1$, its value is bounded by $CM^n$ and its change by $CM^nd$ when all coordinate changes are at most $d\ge0$. Induction on polynomials supplies these constants without assuming a finite ambient index type.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.polynomial_ev.summary: Polynomial values vary polynomially on bounded boxes

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.pressureU.text:
The coefficient $F_U$ multiplying the library amplitude coordinate $U$ in the normalized pressure numerator. For the paper coordinates, $U=-\alpha_1$, so $F_1=-F_U$. The entries supplied to the definition are those of the full normalized strain, including the preceding shear. Nonzero denominator and actual pressure identities are separate results; substituting $E_c=0$ alone does not remove the sign change.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula contains an inverse or quotient. Its nondegenerate mathematical use requires the denominator conditions in the argument or the calling lemma; totalized inversion alone does not provide them.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.pressureU.summary: Coefficient of the first amplitude in the pressure

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.pressureV.text:
The coefficient $F_V$ in the pressure numerator multiplying the second amplitude coordinate. It is computed from the full normalized strain `A`, the three wave-vector coordinates and $S$. When the extra strain is zero, its entries reduce to the manuscript’s expression in $b_{ij}$. Divisions by $Z$ are total in the definition; the amplitude calculation separately assumes $Z\ne0$.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula contains an inverse or quotient. Its nondegenerate mathematical use requires the denominator conditions in the argument or the calling lemma; totalized inversion alone does not provide them.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.pressureV.summary: Coefficient of the second amplitude in the pressure

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.rawMatrix.text:
The two-row coefficient matrix acts on the library pair $(U,V)=(-\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$. The entries `A` describe the full normalized strain driving the amplitude, while `b` describes the older gradient driving the frame; the formula also uses the pressure coefficients and the scaled squared-length factor. To obtain the current paper's amplitude matrix, one must conjugate by $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)$, which changes both off-diagonal signs. Setting the additional strain to zero is only the model substitution and does not remove this coordinate conversion. The definition alone asserts neither the amplitude equation nor nonzero denominators.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula contains an inverse or quotient. Its nondegenerate mathematical use requires the denominator conditions in the argument or the calling lemma; totalized inversion alone does not provide them.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.rawMatrix.summary: Exact coefficient matrix for the two amplitude coordinates

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.referenceMatr.text: The matrix with rows $(-2\varepsilon\tau xs^2,s^2(1-\varepsilon x))$ and $(1,0)$ acts on $(U,V)$. In the arXiv notation, $x=\tan\varphi$, $s=\cos\varphi$ and $(U,V)=(-\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$. Thus the displayed reference system requires a sign change in the first coordinate. This declaration defines coefficients; it does not prove convergence to them.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.referenceMatr.summary: Reference coefficients in the library amplitude coordinates

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.referenceScal.text: When $0\le\varepsilon\le1$, every entry of both the older and full reference strain matrices has absolute value at most one. The proof inspects their explicit entries $0,1/2,\varepsilon/2,1$. This supplies the reference-side box bound needed before comparing polynomial amplitude rows.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.referenceScal.summary: Both reference strains lie in the unit box

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.referenceScal.text: This matrix has only two nonzero entries: $(0,1)=1/2$ and $(2,1)=\varepsilon/2$. These are the rescaled older couplings at the reference values. All other entries are zero. It represents the coefficient limit used in the comparison, with Lean’s zero-based indices corresponding to the paper’s first and third rows.

The reference full strain adds entry $(1,0)=1$ to the older reference matrix. The other nonzero entries remain $1/2$ and $\varepsilon/2$. The added unit entry records $\sigma_p/\sigma=1$ after shear rescaling, and is responsible for the leading transfer between the raw amplitude components.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.referenceScal.summary: Reference strain includes the preceding shear

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledAmplitu.text: The finite list of variables in which the raw amplitude coefficients are polynomial. It includes scaled entries of both the older gradient and the full strain, the three wave-vector coordinates, and inverse shear and denominator variables. The paper gives a reduced list after setting the additional strain to zero. This definition supplies algebraic inputs; bounds and closeness to reference values are separate assumptions.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledAmplitu.summary: Scaled inputs for the amplitude coefficients

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledEntries.text: The array preserves six entries, multiplies entries $(0,1)$ and $(2,1)$ by $S$, and divides entry $(1,0)$ by $S$. Lean indices start at zero. This places the large shear and the two selected couplings at comparable sizes before the coefficient rows are treated as polynomials.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledEntries.summary: Rescale the three exceptional strain entries

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledEntries.text: Under the normalized coupling and older-norm hypotheses, $0\le\varepsilon\le1$, $T,S\ge1$, and $3T\delta\le1$, both actual scaled strain matrices have entries of absolute value at most two. The full strain here omits the additional error. Its proof adds the unit reference bound to the previously established entry errors.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledEntries.summary: Both actual scaled strains lie in a fixed box

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledMatrix.text: The two-by-two matrix combines scaled strain entries, wave coordinates, and three independent reciprocal inputs. It is polynomial over any commutative ring, so its reference value can be evaluated by setting inverse shear to zero. To recover the physical raw rows, `scaledMatrix_eq` substitutes genuine inverses and requires nonzero $S$ and $Z$.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledMatrix.summary: Amplitude rows as polynomials in reciprocal coordinates

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledMatrix_.text: For nonzero shear `hS` and third wave coordinate `hZ`, substituting the scaled strain arrays and actual reciprocals into `scaledMatrix` gives `rawMatrix`. The proof derives nonvanishing of `normFactor` from $Z\ne0$, then clears denominators in all four entries. This is the bridge from formal polynomial sensitivity to the actual amplitude operator.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledMatrix_.summary: Polynomial rows recover the physical amplitude equations

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledMatrix_.text: Substituting the reference coordinates, strain entries, inverse shear zero, and reciprocal norm $s^2$ into the scaled coefficient matrix gives `referenceMatrix`. The identity is valid for every real $\varepsilon,\tau$. Its proof uses the three reference pressure values and $s^2(1+x^2)=1$. It identifies the limiting algebraic coefficient matrix; it is not a convergence theorem for families of actual waves.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledMatrix_.summary: Scaled reference entries give the reference amplitude matrix

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledNormFac.text: This polynomial is $X^2+Q^2\,\mathrm{invS}^2+Z^2$. At `invS = S⁻¹` it equals the normalized squared wave-vector norm `normFactor`. Treating the reciprocal shear as an independent input allows evaluation at its reference value zero, representing the infinite-shear coefficient limit rather than a physical finite shear.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledNormFac.summary: Squared wave norm with an independent inverse shear

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledNormFac.text: Substituting $S^{-1}$ into the polynomial norm gives `normFactor X Q Z S`. The equality holds for every real $S$, including zero under Lean’s convention for inverse. It only identifies two total expressions; using either as a nonzero wave norm still requires the geometric hypotheses supplied later.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledNormFac.summary: The polynomial norm agrees with the wave norm

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledOlderEn.text: If all older entries have size at most $\delta\ge0$, $S\ge1$, and the two selected coupling errors are bounded by $\delta$, every scaled entry differs from its reference by at most $\delta$. The hypotheses `h12` and `h32` control $2Sb_{01}-1$ and $2Sb_{21}-\varepsilon$; the remaining entries use `hb`.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledOlderEn.summary: The older scaled strain is close to its reference

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledOlderSt.text: This version obtains the entrywise bound from an orthonormal frame and $\|B\|\le\delta$. With $S\ge1$ and the two selected coupling estimates, each scaled older entry lies within $\delta$ of its reference value. The operator norm is used only to bound its matrix coefficients; no trace or time-derivative hypothesis is needed.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledOlderSt.summary: The older operator norm controls all reference errors

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.text: This polynomial gives the contribution of the first raw amplitude coordinate $U=-\alpha_1$ to the pressure pairing. It uses a scaled strain array and independent inverse-shear and inverse-third-coordinate inputs. Because the sign of $U$ is reversed from the paper’s $\alpha_1$, its physical specialization corresponds to $-F_1$.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.summary: Pressure contribution from the first amplitude coordinate

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.text: At the scaled strain entries and reciprocal inputs $S^{-1},Z^{-1}$, `scaledPressureU` equals `pressureU`. The equality is algebraic and requires no nonzero hypotheses because the corresponding totalized expressions use the same inverse factors. This bridge does not assert that the associated wave or pressure denominator is nonzero.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.summary: The first pressure polynomial matches its rational form

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.text: This polynomial gives the contribution of $V=\alpha_2$ to the pressure pairing, using the rescaled strain entries. Its independent inputs `invS` and `invZ` stand for $S^{-1}$ and $Z^{-1}$ at a physical state. With the full no-error strain substituted, it reproduces the paper’s $F_2$.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.summary: Pressure contribution from the second amplitude coordinate

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.text: Specializing `scaledPressureV` to `scaledEntries A S`, $S^{-1}$ and $Z^{-1}$ returns `pressureV`. The proof unfolds the coordinate definitions and rewrites division as multiplication by inverse. It works for arbitrary real inputs, while interpretation as a physical amplitude coefficient belongs to later nondegenerate statements.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.summary: The second pressure polynomial matches its rational form

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.text: At the reference inputs, the library coefficients are $F_U=\varepsilon\tau$, $F_V=(x+\varepsilon)/2$ and $m=1+x^2$. The paper instead writes $F_1=-F_U$ because its first amplitude coordinate is $-U$. The inverse-shear input is set to zero in polynomial variables. These algebraic equalities identify the limiting expressions; they do not themselves establish a limit of actual waves.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledPressur.summary: Pressure coefficients at the reference inputs

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledStrainE.text: For an orthonormal frame, $T,S\ge1$, and nonnegative $\delta$, combine the older norm and coupling bounds with `hσ`, the estimate $|\sigma_{\mathrm{ratio}}-1|\le2T\delta$. Every entry of the full strain with error omitted then differs from reference by at most $3T\delta$. Only the shear entry needs the additional strength-ratio error.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.scaledStrainE.summary: The full scaled strain has a controlled reference error

TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.wave_norm_sq_.text: The scaled coordinate representation gives $|k|^2=\lambda^2(X^2+Q^2/S^2+Z^2)$. `he` is orthonormality and `hscale`, `hS` rule out zero scaling factors. The statement is purely algebraic and does not assume the wave equation. The proof uses preservation of the norm under orthonormal coordinates, which explains why no cross terms appear.
TorusEuler.MovingAmplitude.wave_norm_sq_.summary: Wave-vector norm in the scaled coordinates

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Packages the preceding wave, older strain and error path on $[0,T]$, with $T\ge2$, $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$, $S\ge1$, and explicit error bounds. The structure requires nonzero perpendicular preceding data, their affine ODEs, trace-free continuous older strain, continuous error, coupling controls and $240\delta T^6\le1$. It contains no new wave yet. Stronger polynomial smallness is supplied separately for amplitude and coupling comparison.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: Data for amplification on a normalized time interval

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Reuses the normalized preceding wave vector, normalized preceding amplitude, and their oriented cross product as the three frame axes. The data in `w` make this an orthonormal frame on $[0,T]$, as proved separately. This abbreviation itself defines axes at every real time, including times outside the interval where nonvanishing and orthogonality are not guaranteed.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: The preceding wave supplies the three frame axes

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Proves continuity of each of the three frame axes throughout $[0,T]$ by deriving their within-interval derivatives from the preceding affine-wave equations. The trace-free and nonvanishing data are supplied by `w`. This establishes the operator-continuity inputs for new-wave existence, including one-sided behavior at the endpoints, without assuming smoothness of the frame as an independent field.

Combines continuity of the older strain and matrix error with continuity of the preceding frame and relative strength to prove continuity of the full normalized gradient. The preceding ODEs supply continuity of its vectors. This is the hypothesis needed for affine-wave existence on the closed window; it establishes neither differentiability of the error nor an equation for the gradient.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: The assembled normalized gradient is continuous

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Given a new wave-vector path satisfying its ODE and initial direction with nonzero carrier, proves continuity of `w.matrixError k scale` on the window. Its proof first obtains $Z\ge1/2$, which keeps coordinate denominators nonzero, then assembles continuous frame entries and coordinates. This is continuity of the exact error operator; its polynomial size bound is a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: The common amplitude error operator is continuous

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: For nonzero carrier `scale`, constructs $k,a$ on the entire normalized window with $k(0)=\lambda E_3(0)$ and $a(0)=-E_1(0)/S+E_2(0)$. Both satisfy the affine-wave equations for `w.gradient` and remain nonzero and perpendicular. It asserts existence and these geometric properties, without an amplitude comparison. The carrier may be negative here; the oriented coupling estimates later require it to be positive.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: Construct the new wave with growing initial polarization

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Adds $0<\mathrm{next}\le\varepsilon/32$ and a window containing the crossing horizon to the amplitude-and-coupling construction. It returns a zero of the reference logarithmic derivative, the actual amplitude maximum, and a crossing strictly between that zero and the horizon. Every crossing in the closed bracket has explicit peak-normalized strength bounds, and the first unit of normalized time satisfies the early-gain estimate. All these conclusions concern the same constructed wave.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: A growing wave reaches the prescribed successor ratio

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: For a sufficiently large universal $C_0$, positive carrier, valid window and both smallness conditions, constructs one pair of wave paths and one reference Riccati solution carrying all estimates together. The first normalized coupling is at least $\varepsilon/2$ on the full window. In the late range it stays within $\varepsilon$ of one, and the coupling ratio divided by $\cos\varphi$ stays within $1/2$ of one. The same paths satisfy the logarithmic amplitude bound.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: One growing wave satisfies amplitude and coupling bounds

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Chooses an absolute natural threshold $N\ge240$. For every $C_0\ge N$, valid window and nonzero carrier satisfying $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$, constructs the growing wave together with a reference Riccati solution on all nonnegative times. On the window, the wave remains nonzero and transverse and satisfies $|\log(\|a\|/a_{\rm ref})|\le\varepsilon$. It does not yet assert the new coupling bounds or a return crossing.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: One growing wave remains close to the reference amplitude

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: There is a universal natural threshold such that, under the normalized polynomial smallness, every transverse amplitude `b` satisfies $\|b(v)\|/\|a(v)\|\le252eS\,\|b(u)\|/\|a(u)\|$ for $0\le u\le v\le T$. The growing amplitude `a` has the growing seed scaled by a positive `c`, stays nonzero and transverse, and shares the wave vector and strain with `b`. The global Riccati solution is also an input.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: One threshold bounds every transverse solution relative to the growing one

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Defines the normalized gradient $B+S(\sigma_p/\sigma)E_2\otimes E_1+E$ using the preceding frame and relative strength stored in `w`. The operators $B$ and $E$ are already expressed in normalized time. It combines the three contributions used in the new affine-wave equation; this definition makes no claim that the resulting operator is trace free or an Euler background.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: The new wave sees older strain plus shear and error

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Defines the second new-wave coupling as $2S\langle\widehat k\times\widehat a,(M/r)\widehat a\rangle$. It uses the oriented third axis of the new frame and represents $\eta_+/\nu$ in the physical normalization. It is not the coupling ratio by itself: the successor ratio is obtained by dividing this quantity by `growingNu`.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: Second coupling of the new wave in normalized units

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text:
Defines the first new-wave coupling as $2S\langle\widehat k,(M/r)\widehat aangle$, with the normalized gradient supplied by `w.gradient`. In a physical realization this equals $
u_+/
u$ because $2S/r=1/
u$. The formula itself accepts arbitrary paths and does not assert positivity; the comparison theorem proves that property for the constructed growing wave.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: First coupling of the new wave in normalized units

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Defines the difference between the exact two-component amplitude operator and its reference operator for a given path $k$ and carrier `scale`. It uses the preceding frame, older and full gradients, and the scaled wave-vector coordinates. There is no amplitude argument, making the same error operator available to every transverse amplitude evolving along that wave vector.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: One amplitude error operator for a fixed wave vector

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Produces absolute constants $C\ge0$ and a natural exponent $p$, chosen before any window or wave data, such that $\|R(t)\|\le CT^p\delta$ on each valid window. The new wave vector must solve its affine ODE and start in the prescribed direction with nonzero carrier. This quantifier order is what makes the constants uniform over the later construction; no particular numerical values are extracted here.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: The common amplitude error has a uniform polynomial bound

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: At a time `t` in $[0,T]$, applies the window’s nonzero and perpendicular preceding-data fields to prove orthonormality of its three frame axes. This statement does not require the new wave vector or amplitude. The interval membership is essential: the structure controls the preceding vectors only on its specified time window.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: The preceding axes are orthonormal throughout the window

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: For a fixed new wave vector with its ODE and activation direction, any amplitude satisfying the associated affine ODE and pointwise transversality has the two reference-plus-error equations for $U,V$. The operator is exactly `w.matrixError k scale t`, so it is independent of the chosen amplitude. The variables satisfy $U=-\alpha_1$, $V=\alpha_2$; the statement does not impose growing initial amplitude data.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: Every transverse amplitude uses the same reduced equations

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Reuses the ratio $\|k_p(t)\|\|a_p(t)\|/(\|k_p(0)\|\|a_p(0)\|)$, comparing the current preceding-wave strength to its initial value. The window places zero in its interval and makes both initial vectors nonzero, so the denominator is positive. Bounds on this ratio still require the preceding-frame logarithmic strength law and the older-strain estimate.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: Preceding strength relative to its activation value

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: For any new wave-vector path satisfying the activation direction and the affine ODE for `w.gradient`, obtains the coordinate error bound $120\delta T^6\le1/2$. Nonzero `scale` is required, while no new amplitude is involved. The window supplies all preceding-wave, trace and error assumptions to the general moving-wave-vector comparison.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: The constructed wave vector follows its polynomial reference

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.text: Under the new-wave ODE and activation direction, proves $1/2\le Z\le3/2$, $|X|\le T^2$, $|Q|\le T$, and a normalized squared length at least $1/4$. It combines the coordinate comparison with the window’s small ratio. These bounds justify divisions by $Z$ and the pressure denominator in the amplitude reduction, and hold only within the normalized window.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.Amplificatio.summary: The wave-vector coordinates stay away from singular denominators

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.LaterPhysica.text: This record identifies a physical amplification model with the given preceding pair, older velocity gradient, and correction `E`. Its last field identifies the model’s total gradient with the actual parent gradient on the comparison slab. These equalities prevent the subsequent wave selection from using an unrelated model trajectory.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.LaterPhysica.summary: The comparison data refer to the actual parent gradient

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.LaterWaveSel.text: This record packages a normalized window, comparison smallness, a growing crossing at the prescribed frequency and peak amplitude, and the fact that the crossing occurs after activation but within the first half. Its `center` field proves transverse stability and positive coupling over the actual parent gradient for that same wave.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.LaterWaveSel.summary: One selected path carries the crossing and center estimates

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text:
The physical data consist of an older gradient $B$, a continuous correction $E$, and a nonzero transverse preceding wave on a compact time set $I$ containing activation. The record assumes both preceding-wave equations, zero trace of $B$, continuity of $B,E$, and positive first and third couplings at activation. It does not assume that $I$ is an interval or that $B$ is smooth. A separate clock-inclusion hypothesis places the active normalized slab inside $I$. These are assumptions packaged as data, not an existence theorem or the later comparison estimates.

Default-value audit (b5): The interval contains the activation time, the preceding data are nonzero and the initial couplings are positive. These fields exclude the empty-window and zero-normalization cases in the subsequent rate and ratio definitions.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: Physical data on a compact amplification window

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: The data of a growing physical wave with prescribed peak `Ustar` and target coupling ratio `next`. The structure records its initial direction, affine equations, transversality, peak attainment, coupling lower bound, and the least crossing within the stated bracket. It also records strength, logarithmic coupling, and early-gain estimates. A value `d` supplies these fields; the existence theorem constructs such a value from comparison smallness.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: A normalized wave with its first crossing

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: For an existing `GrowingCrossing` record, the delay from activation is strictly greater than $1/r$ and at most the crossing horizon divided by $r$. These inequalities come from the record’s `crossing_after_switch` and upper bracket endpoint. They do not assert that the selected time is the first crossing before the reference-turn bracket.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The selected crossing occurs after switching and before the horizon

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: At a selected growing crossing, the actual first coupling is positive, the ratio of third to first coupling equals the requested `next`, and the logarithmic change in first coupling is at most twice the old ratio. These are properties of the same selected wave and physical gradient, extracted from its crossing record.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: A selected crossing supplies the next frozen couplings

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: If the supplied gradient agrees with the physical gradient at the crossing and the requested next ratio is positive, both frozen couplings are positive there. Their ratio and logarithmic first-coupling bound are unchanged. Unlike the equation transport lemma, this needs equality only at the single crossing time.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The actual gradient retains the positive crossing couplings

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: For positive frequency, gains, and strength constants, an actual crossing with gain gap at least 640, strength between $c\mu^{1/4}$ and $C\mu^{1/4}L^2$, and first coupling between $\pi$ and $4\pi$ has explicit rate and delay bounds. A further lower bound on the next gain ensures delay at most $\mu^{-1/8}LNext^3$. The conclusion also gives strict time advancement, normalized delay at least $2L^2$, and weighted duration.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: Physical strength and coupling give the next activation clock

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: At activation, the selected covector is `scale` times the preceding third frame vector and has norm `scale` when the scale is positive. Its amplitude is a positive multiple of $-E_1/S+E_2$. The positive normalization preserves the growing direction and refers to the same crossing witness used later.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The selected wave has the prescribed launch directions

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: On an interval starting at a selected crossing, the switched rank-one gradient formula becomes the unswitched formula because the wave cutoff is already one. The finish must remain before the model endpoint. The correction `E` is unchanged, so the next physical comparison uses the same actual gradient splitting.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: After crossing the preceding rank-one term is fully active

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: Restricting a selected wave to an interval beginning at its crossing preserves nonzero perpendicular data and the actual covector and amplitude equations. The supplied finish must not exceed the previous active endpoint. The previous switch equals one on the whole restricted interval because the crossing occurs after switch completion.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The crossed wave remains valid on the successor interval

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: The selected wave’s affine equations on a successor interval can be rewritten with any gradient `B` that agrees there with the physical model gradient. The only additional premise is the endpoint bound for the restriction. This transports equations along an exact equality and does not estimate a discrepancy between two gradients.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The successor equations use the identified physical gradient

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: For the same growing crossing whose peak is `scale` to the power $-3/4$, positive scale and coupling ratio $(4\log\mathrm{freq})^{-2}$ imply the normalized amplitude is at most $\exp(3-4\log\mathrm{freq})$ throughout the first physical switching unit. The proof cancels the peak normalization and substitutes the chosen ratio into the crossing’s early-gain estimate.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The normalized amplitude is small during the initial switch

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: For a physical growing crossing with old ratio given by `L` and target ratio given by `LNext`, the hypotheses $L>0$ and $640L\le LNext$ put its normalized delay between $2L^2$ and $2L\,LNext$. This combines the lower crossing bound with the explicit horizon identity. Existence of the growing crossing is assumed through the supplied object.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: Successive gains bracket the normalized crossing delay

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: For an actual physical growing crossing, identifying the initial ratio with the inverse square of `L` gives $2L^2\le rate\,(crossing-t_0)$. The crossing object supplies the comparison and positivity properties used by the proof. No separate positivity hypothesis on `L` appears in this theorem; the prescribed ratio is the relevant compatibility assumption.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: An actual growing crossing lasts at least the inverse ratio

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: When the prescribed peak is $\lambda^{-3/4}$ and $\lambda>0$, the strength estimate at the recorded crossing has denominator $\lambda^{1/4}$. The theorem rewrites $\lambda\lambda^{-3/4}=\lambda^{1/4}$ and applies the stored crossing-strength bounds. It retains the constants $e^{-1}/4$ and $18e^3$ and does not supply a new crossing.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The induction peak gives a quarter-power strength denominator

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: With positive wave scale, preceding gain at least one, and gain separation `640 * Lprev ≤ L`, a wave normalized to peak amplitude $\mathrm{scale}^{-3/4}$ has crossing strength between $(e^{-1}/4)\mathrm{scale}^{1/4}$ and $18e^3\mathrm{scale}^{1/4}L^2$. The hypothesis identifies the old coupling ratio with the preceding gain. These are loose bounds suited to iteration.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: Crossing strength has uniform induction bounds

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: Using the actual smooth periodic odd parent flow, this theorem proves the prescribed label covector is nonzero and its transported value agrees with the selected Eulerian wave vector throughout the activation slab. The model gradient must agree with the parent’s actual central gradient. Oddness fixes the origin, connecting the label trajectory to the central physical comparison.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The chosen label covector transports to the selected physical wave

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: A `GrowingCrossing` occurs after the switching delay. Therefore, for any `t` at or after `d.crossing`, the activation cutoff `waveSwitch t₀ w.rate t` equals one. The theorem uses the crossing record’s delay bound and the positive rate carried by the physical amplification data.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The switch is fully active by the crossing

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: Transfers normalized comparison bounds back to a physical crossing: the scaled components satisfy $|X|\le T^2$, $|Q|\le T$, and $|Z-1|\le1/2$. Here `T ≥ 2` is the normalized window length and the evaluated time belongs to `w.activeSlab T`. Further hypotheses require a nonzero scale, clock containment, a sufficiently large comparison constant, and ratio and error smallness.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The selected wave retains its physical geometry

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: The active slab is $[t_0,\mathrm{clock}(T)]$, namely $[t_0,t_0+T/r]$ for the positive rate stored in `w`. The definition only specifies endpoints. Inclusion in the original physical set `I` is supplied later, and positivity of the normalized length is not part of this set definition.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The physical interval for a normalized time window

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: The frame is built from the preceding wave vector and amplitude stored in `w`: their normalized directions and their cross product. On the recorded physical set `I`, `preceding_data` guarantees both vectors are nonzero and perpendicular. The abbreviation is defined for all times, so the record’s geometric guarantees should only be used on `I`.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The preceding wave supplies the moving frame

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text:
The inverse change of time $t=t_0+\tau/r$ from normalized to physical time. The parameter `w` supplies the positive rate $r$ frozen at activation. The comparison theorem separately assumes `MapsTo w.clock (Icc 0 T) I`, ensuring that the whole normalized interval lies inside the physical interval. Differentiating a physical-time path after this substitution divides its derivative by $r$.

Default-value audit (b5): The rate is positive for the amplification record. Hence this affine clock is invertible with its elapsed-time map; that would not follow for a raw zero rate.

For a window with endpoint `t₀ + 2 * half`, normalized time $2r\,\mathrm{half}$ maps exactly to that endpoint, and the normalized interval maps into the physical interval. Positivity of the rate is inherited from the physical amplification structure. This is a clock identity and containment statement, not a crossing existence result.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The normalized clock reaches the physical endpoint

TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.text: Applying the physical clock to elapsed normalized time returns the original real time. The equality uses only the positive, hence nonzero, rate from `w`. It is valid for all real times, while derivative and geometric properties of the wave remain restricted to the physical window.
TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl.summary: The inverse clock recovers the original physical time
