TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.basis_orthonorm.text: Normalize the nonzero perpendicular preceding wave and amplitude vectors and complete them by the cross product to obtain an orthonormal basis.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.basis_orthonorm.summary: Orthonormality of the preceding wave frame

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.clock_continuou.text: The affine map from normalized time to physical time is continuous. Its range lies in the required time window only under the separate interval hypothesis.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.clock_mem_slab.text: A normalized time in the allowed interval maps into the physical slab between activation and the terminal clock value. Positive rate gives the order preservation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.clock_mem_slab.summary: The normalized clock stays in its physical slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.conjError.text:
Define the error matrix by conjugating the library error through the first-coordinate reflection. This changes coordinate convention and does not introduce a new error source.

Default-value audit (b5): This is ordinary composition with a fixed reflection for every time and operator, including a zero error operator. No inverse or off-domain default is introduced; continuity and size estimates remain separate hypotheses or conclusions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.conjError.summary: The error matrix in the paper coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_co.text: Compose a continuous physical-time function with the normalized clock, assuming the clock maps the normalized interval into its domain.
A continuous error-operator curve remains continuous after composition with the fixed reflection on either side.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_co.summary: Continuity of the conjugated error matrix

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_cr.text: Two continuous three-vector fields have a continuous cross product. This supplies continuity of the third moving-frame vector.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.text: A continuous reference slope gives a continuous deviation after the algebraic change of variables, because the reference cosine factor never vanishes. No deviation ODE is assumed here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.summary: Continuous deviation from a continuous reference slope

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.text: Recover the deviation as a quotient of the continuous slope plus damping by the positive cosine factor. Thus the deviation envelope is continuous on nonnegative times without appealing to an additional existence theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.summary: Continuity of the bounded reference deviation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_fr.text: For continuous nonzero wave and amplitude vectors, all three normalized-frame vectors are continuous on the interval. This is a continuity fact; perpendicularity and orthonormality are handled separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_fr.summary: Continuity of the moving orthonormal frame

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_no.text: A continuous vector field that never vanishes on a set has a continuous normalized direction there. The nonvanishing assumption is necessary because normalization is totalized at zero in Lean.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_ph.text: Continuous, nonzero wave-vector and amplitude paths give continuous new-frame couplings on the normalized time interval. The physical background and error are continuous by the amplification data. The nonvanishing hypotheses permit normalization of both paths. This theorem supplies continuity of the two couplings separately; positivity of the first coupling, obtained from Lemma 2.7, then permits their quotient in the crossing argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_ph.summary: The new physical couplings are continuous

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuous_damp.text: The quarter-damping term in the reference-slope representation is continuous. This supplies a continuous envelope when reconstructing the deviation from the paper's formula.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coordinates_clo.text: Convert the vector comparison with the reference wave into three scalar error bounds for the moving-frame coordinates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coordinates_clo.summary: Coordinate errors from wave vector comparison

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.cos_referenceAn.text: Translate the paper's reference-angle cosine into the algebraic factor used in the scalar ODE library. The identity is unrestricted in epsilon and time.
Rewrite the squared reference cosine as the reciprocal of one plus the squared tangent parameter. This identifies the denominator in the relative wave-length estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_budget.text: Choose a common polynomial error budget that dominates the wave-coordinate and slope errors and is at most one half. This puts the rational coupling comparison in a single admissible parameter range.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_budget.summary: One small error for all coupling estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_conclu.text: Absorb the concrete error 256 times the eighth power of the horizon times the common budget, plus twice delta, and apply the coupling comparison. This packages the final numerical step of Lemma 2.7 without recreating any numbered input.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_conclu.summary: Coupling conclusions from a common error budget

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.crossing_streng.text: Given the turning time, reference maximum and gain, bounded deviation, amplitude formula, logarithmic comparison, wave-number bound, and continuous coupling ratio, this theorem produces a crossing in the open bracket. It also identifies the actual amplitude maximum and gives constants $e^{-1}/4$ and $18e^3$ at every crossing in the closed bracket. The final clause is the early-gain estimate. The hypotheses expose precisely which facts Proposition 2.8 consumes.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.crossing_streng.summary: Crossings with strength and early gain bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.damping_eq.text: Identify epsilon times time times sine of twice the angle with the library damping coefficient. This allows the same derivative equation to be read in both notations.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.deviation_eq_of.text: Given the paper's ansatz for the reference slope, solve algebraically for the library deviation. Strict positivity of the cosine factor justifies the division.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.deviation_eq_of.summary: Recovering the deviation from the slope formula

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.driving_eq.text: Identify the cosine-squared driving term of the paper's scalar equation with the algebraic coefficient used by the Riccati library.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.elapsed_mem_Icc.text: A physical time in the active slab has elapsed normalized time in the prescribed interval. This is the inverse interval calculation used to restrict arbitrary propagated amplitudes.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.elapsed_mem_Icc.summary: The physical slab maps to normalized time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.errorSize_restr.text: The error size of the active-slab restriction is bounded by the original error size. The scalar inverse-shear contribution is unchanged and the physical supremum can only decrease.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.errorSize_restr.summary: The restricted amplification error is no larger

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.finiteSmallness.text: Transfer the finite-smallness hypothesis to the active slab using the preceding error monotonicity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.flipCLM.text:
Define the bounded linear map sending a two-coordinate state to the negative of its first coordinate and the unchanged second coordinate. It reconciles the U,V convention with the paper's alpha coordinates.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a globally defined bounded linear reflection on a two-dimensional real space. It involves no division, choice of representative, interval restriction, or exceptional default.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.flipCLM.summary: Reflection of the first amplitude coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.flipCLM_apply.text: Compute the reflection map as the pair consisting of minus the first coordinate and the second coordinate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.geometry_of_clo.text: Coordinate closeness to the reference vector gives bounds on the first two scaled coordinates used in amplitude estimates. The hypotheses include the interval and epsilon bounds needed to absorb the reference polynomial terms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.geometry_of_clo.summary: Geometry from nearby scaled wave coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.gradient_contin.text: Combine the older gradient, preceding shear, and correction to obtain continuity of the full gradient on the physical time window. This is used for amplitude ODE solvability.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.gradient_contin.summary: Continuity of the full background gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.growingFactor_r.text: A uniform logarithmic amplitude comparison, positivity, and twice epsilon at most one bound the reference-amplitude ratio by exp one times the actual amplitude ratio. This closes the physical propagator estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.growingFactor_r.summary: Replacing the reference ratio by the actual amplitude ratio

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.text: Apply the first coordinate projection to a within-interval derivative of a two-coordinate curve. This is ordinary bounded-linear-map differentiation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.summary: The derivative of the first state coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.text: Apply the second coordinate projection to a within-interval derivative of a two-coordinate curve.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.summary: The derivative of the second state coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.mapsTo_restrict.text: The normalized clock lands in the active slab by construction. This supplies the domain hypothesis for the copied amplification data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.mapsTo_restrict.summary: The clock maps into the restricted interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.nbasis.text:
Abbreviate the preceding moving frame composed with the normalized clock. The expression is defined at every time, while orthonormality and ODE conclusions are asserted only on the admissible interval.

Default-value audit (b5): The original frame is evaluated at every real clock value, including outside its hypothesis window. Its constituent normalizations use total real inverses, so a zero vector has a formal value; orthonormality is used only where the amplification data give nonzero perpendicular vectors.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ne_zero_of_zeta.text: If the third scaled wave coordinate is nonzero, then the underlying wave vector is nonzero. This supports later normalization of the new wave direction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ne_zero_of_zeta.summary: A nonzero third coordinate excludes a zero wave

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.newWaveVector_r.text: Restrict the new wave-vector data and its initial condition to the active slab. No new wave-vector solution is constructed.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normFactor_cos_.text: The estimate bounds $|m/(1+x^2)-1|$ by $2T^2e_0+2T^2\delta$ from errors at most $e_0\le1/2$ in $X$ and $Z$, a bound on $Q$, and inverse-shear control. It allows $S^{-2}\le2\delta$. Setting $x=\tan\varphi$ converts the denominator to $\cos^2\varphi$ and supplies the relative norm estimate in Lemma 2.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normFactor_cos_.summary: Relative error in the squared wave vector norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_bounds_of_.text: If the normalized state is within one half of $(1,0)$ and the stated transverse geometry holds, then $V\le|\mathbf a|\le(1+40T^4S^{-2})V$. Here $V=\alpha_2$. The hypotheses include an orthonormal frame, nonzero scales, perpendicularity, and bounds on the wave-vector coordinates and $Y$. The proof bounds the two small physical components and applies the Euclidean norm identity. It does not itself prove proximity of the normalized state.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_bounds_of_.summary: The amplitude norm from its second component

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_conjError_.text: The norm of the conjugated error is at most the original error norm, using the norm-one bounds for the reflection on both sides.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_flipCLM_le.text: Bound the operator norm of the diagonal reflection by one. The inequality is enough to transfer the error-operator estimate through conjugation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_flipCLM_le.summary: The amplitude reflection does not increase norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_movingAmpl.text: An arbitrary transverse amplitude obeys $|\mathbf b(t)|\le126S\exp(2D)(a_{\rm ref}(t)/a_{\rm ref}(a))|\mathbf b(a)|$ under the stated wave-vector geometry and raw amplitude equations. The proof passes from physical vectors to normalized coordinates, uses their propagator estimate, and returns to physical vectors. Nonnegative deviation is an input taken from Lemma 2.5. The estimate permits any starting time in the prescribed interval.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_le.text: The separate bounds $|X|\le T^2$, $|Q|\le T$ and $1/2\le Z\le3/2$ imply $|\zeta|\le3T^2$ when $T\ge2$. The proof squares the Euclidean norm and compares the sum of the three coordinate squares with $(3T^2)^2$. This elementary step explains the change from the library's coordinate estimates to the arXiv vector estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_le.summary: A polynomial bound for the scaled wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_sub_l.text: Bound the norm of the wave-vector difference by the sum of its three scalar coordinate errors. This converts the quantitative nilpotent estimate to the statement of Lemma 2.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_sub_l.summary: A vector error from scalar coordinate errors

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedCoupl.text: Under the moving-frame and nonvanishing assumptions, identify the algebraic normalized first and second couplings with the physical couplings divided by the preceding first coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedCoupl.summary: Converting normalized couplings to physical rates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedState.text: Between any ordered times in the interval, the normalized state obeys $\|z(t)\|\le2\|z(a)\|\exp(2D)$. The integral $D$ contains $(1+|Y|)^2/s$ times the raw matrix-error bound. The assumptions supply both amplitude equations, continuous errors, the Riccati equation, and nonnegative deviation. This estimates arbitrary initial states, rather than only the growing state. Smallness of the polynomial budget later makes the exponential factor bounded.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedState.summary: Normalized growth is controlled by the integrated error

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedStrai.text: Identify the normalized strain, including preceding shear and correction, with the full physical gradient divided by the amplification rate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_clos.text: For growing initial data, the normalized error is at most $4\exp(2D)D$, where $D$ integrates the conjugated raw-error bound. This version assumes nonnegativity of the reference deviation instead of proving it again, allowing Lemma 2.5 to supply that fact. Continuous coefficient bounds and both perturbed amplitude equations are explicit inputs. The conclusion is pointwise in the maximum norm on $(h,l)$; the polynomial bound is supplied later.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_clos.summary: The normalized growing state remains close

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_fact.text: The physical error and finite-smallness assumptions give the coefficient estimates used throughout the comparison. The theorem requires $C_0\ge240$ and includes $S^{-1}\le2\delta$, $S^{-2}\le2\delta$, $T^2\le S$, and pointwise normalized gradient and coupling bounds. Its inverse-shear-squared conclusion has factor two; it does not state every sharper intermediate inequality in the paper's displayed chain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_fact.summary: Small physical errors give normalized coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.nstrain.text:
Abbreviate the older gradient divided by rate, the normalized preceding rank-one shear, and the correction divided by rate. Equality with the full rescaled gradient is proved separately.

Default-value audit (b5): Scalar division by the amplification rate is formally total, but physical amplification data make that rate strictly positive. The expression exists outside the active time interval without asserting the wave or frame equations there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.nstrain.summary: The normalized strain including the preceding shear

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ratio_error_bou.text: Control the error of a quotient after the denominator is bounded away from zero. The explicit numerical bound is used to transfer separate first and second coupling errors to their ratio.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ratio_error_bou.summary: Converting additive errors to a relative ratio

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.raw_matrix_comp.text: Package the raw matrix comparison hypotheses from a continuous nonnegative deviation and the common amplitude error. This exposes the needed part of Lemma 2.5 at the proof boundary.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.raw_matrix_comp.summary: The normalized matrix comparison with explicit deviation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.raw_system_of_a.text: Translate the paper's alpha system into the library U,V system, conjugating the error matrix by the first-coordinate reflection. The scalar angle identities identify the reference coefficients exactly.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.raw_system_of_a.summary: The perturbed amplitude system after changing signs

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceNu_low.text: When $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $\tau\ge0$, and $Y(\tau)>0$, the first normalized reference coupling is at least $\varepsilon$. This version takes the positive reference rate as an explicit hypothesis. The coupling proof obtains that sign from Lemma 2.5 in the early range. The algebra combines $\sin\varphi+\varepsilon\cos\varphi\ge\varepsilon$ with the nonnegative remaining term in the reference coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceNu_low.summary: A positive lower bound for the reference coupling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceSlope_.text: Translate the reference-slope predicate into the initial condition and the library Riccati derivative equation. The equivalence imports no separate existence or uniqueness conclusion.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceSystem.text: The four entries of the paper reference matrix are expressed using the library damping and driving functions. They are minus the damping, minus the driving, minus one and zero. This identity records the sign change needed to compare with the library's $(U,V)$ system. It is purely algebraic and contains no existence or convergence assertion for a differential equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceV_late.text: From the supplied amplitude ratio and bounded nonnegative deviation, bound the late-time reference-amplitude ratio by absolute multiples of the peak time divided by the current time. The remaining exponential integral is bounded independently of the terminal horizon.

Combine the reference-amplitude ratio with the late quadratic wave-vector scale to obtain two-sided linear-in-time strength bounds. This remains a statement about the reference profile until physical comparison is supplied.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceV_late.summary: Reference strength on the late time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceV_rati.text: The ratio $a_{\rm ref}(\tau)/a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)$ equals $\sqrt{s(\tau)/s(\tau_m)}$ times the exponential integral of $s(1+e)$ between those times. The complete amplitude formula is an input for every nonnegative time, along with continuity of its integrand and ordered times. Thus this proof explicitly consumes the formula in Lemma 2.5, rather than deriving the ratio again solely from the rate ansatz.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceV_rati.summary: Ratios from the reference amplitude formula

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.rescale_amplitu.text: Apply the time chain rule to the amplitude equation under the normalized clock, including the rescaled pressure coefficient.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.rescale_waveVec.text: Compose the physical wave vector with the affine normalized clock and divide its derivative by the positive amplification rate to obtain the normalized wave equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residualQ.text:
Define the residual in the shear-scaled second wave coordinate after subtracting the limiting coupling to the third coordinate.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression is total for arbitrary input coordinates and coefficients. Any divisions inherited from normalized data use Lean total inverses; the ODE interpretation and estimates are made only for positive admissible shear and rate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residualX.text:
Define the first coordinate of the perturbation to the limiting nilpotent wave-vector system, including frame entries, varying strength, and the physical correction.

Default-value audit (b5): The polynomial/rational expression is defined at all real inputs, with divisions by the shear totalized at zero. Its interpretation as a residual and the estimates require shear at least one and the stated frame/coefficient assumptions.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residualZ.text:
Define the residual third wave-coordinate derivative, whose reference value is zero.

Default-value audit (b5): The explicit division by shear has a formal value even at shear zero. The residual estimate assumes shear at least one, so that value is never used in the comparison argument.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residual_bounds.text: Under normalized coefficient bounds and a scale at least one, each residual is at most five times horizon times delta times the sum of the wave-coordinate magnitudes. The estimates keep every perturbation in the nilpotent comparison budget.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residual_bounds.summary: Bounds for the three wave equation residuals

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.restrictSlab.text:
Build physical amplification data on the smaller interval between activation and the terminal clock value, retaining the same parameters and functions while restricting their hypotheses.

Default-value audit (b5): The declaration takes a nonnegative normalized horizon and a mapping hypothesis for the original window; those supply the restricted structure fields. It keeps all original functions unchanged, including their values outside the new slab, but restricts all analytic assertions to the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.restrictSlab.summary: Restricting amplification data to the active slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.riccati_perturb.text: Assuming a nonnegative deviation, continuity, and a bound on the raw error matrix, control the coefficients of the normalized triangular perturbation. The nonnegative deviation is an explicit hypothesis from Lemma 2.5.

Bound propagation of the normalized state from an arbitrary earlier time by an exponential of the integrated perturbation budget. The nonnegative deviation supplies stability of the unperturbed triangular part.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.riccati_perturb.summary: A perturbed triangular propagator between two times

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.s_ratio_bounds.text: In the late range, compare the ratio of cosine factors with the squared ratio of the two times. The scalar estimates convert the amplitude formula into explicit late decay bounds.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.seven_sq_le_eps.text: Under the stated smallness of epsilon, seven times epsilon squared is at most epsilon. This numerical absorption is used only in the late coupling estimates.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.sin_referenceAn.text: Rewrite the sine of the reference angle as its tangent parameter times its cosine factor. This is a direct algebraic bridge between the two notations.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.slab_subset.text: If the normalized clock maps the interval into the original physical window, then the whole active physical slab is a subset of that window.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.slab_subset.summary: The active slab lies in the original window

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.sqrt_clock_boun.text: If $1/(4\varepsilon_+)\le x\le3/(2\varepsilon_+)$ and both ratios are positive, then $\sqrt{x/\varepsilon}$ lies between one half and twice $(\varepsilon\varepsilon_+)^{-1/2}$. These are algebraic hypotheses; the lemma does not construct a crossing or assume a differential equation. It converts the tangent bounds at a crossing into the scale used by the strength estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.sqrt_clock_boun.summary: The crossing fixes the square-root strength scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.strengthRatio_b.text: The preceding strength ratio differs from one by at most $2T\delta$ when its logarithmic derivative equals the frame entry $b_{33}$, the older gradient has norm at most $\delta$, and $T\delta\le1$. Nonzero transverse data and frame orthonormality are explicit hypotheses. Taking the derivative identity as an input preserves the numbered dependence on Lemma 2.2 in the proof of Lemma 2.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.strengthRatio_b.summary: Bound preceding strength from its logarithmic derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.strengthRatio_c.text: The strength ratio in normalized time is the physical preceding strength evaluated at the clock divided by its initial strength.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.strengthRatio_c.summary: The preceding strength ratio along the clock

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.tan_referenceAn.text: Identify the tangent parameter of the reference angle with epsilon times time squared divided by two. Later geometric estimates supply the positivity hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.waveVector_poly.text:
Given the preceding frame identities, normalized gradient bounds and the activated wave-vector equation, the sum of coordinate errors is at most $120\delta T^6\le1/2$. The assumptions include $240\delta T^6\le1$, $S\ge1$ and $0\le\varepsilon\le1$. This theorem takes the frame equations explicitly rather than proving them again, so its use in Lemma 2.4 retains the stated dependence on Lemma 2.2.

The proof uses the nilpotent reference propagator to retain polynomial dependence on the horizon, rather than a direct exponential Gronwall bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.waveVector_poly.summary: Polynomial wave vector error from the frame equations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.wave_norm_compa.text: For $\tau\ge2/\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$, the estimate $|K^2s^2/\lambda^2-1|\le1/2$ implies $x/2\le K/\lambda\le3x$. The wave scale is positive and $K$ is nonnegative. Applied with $K=|k|$, this reads the norm estimate from Lemma 2.4 directly. Since $x\le1/s\le2x$ in this range, it also gives the manuscript's comparison with $\lambda/\cos\varphi$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.wave_norm_compa.summary: Late wave number bounds from the squared norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.zetaRef_apply.text: Evaluate the three coordinates of the reference wave vector in terms of the algebraic tangent parameter, epsilon times time, and one.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.zeta_one.text: Identify the second coordinate of the scaled wave vector with the library coordinate containing the shear factor.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.zeta_two.text: Identify the third coordinate of the scaled wave vector with the corresponding moving-frame coordinate divided by the initial wave length.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.zeta_zero.text: Identify the first coordinate of the scaled wave vector with the normalized moving-frame coordinate used by the library.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.A1Body.text:
Package the quantified conclusion of Theorem A.1 with its universal constant and exponent fixed. This proposition is an explicit hypothesis passed to the rescaled solver, not an assumption that a solution exists by definition.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a proposition recording the full unit-interval conclusion with fixed C and p. It has no computational fallback; coefficients, sources, positive ellipticity/coercivity parameters, and all regularity assumptions remain quantified inside the proposition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.A1Body.summary: The unit interval inverse after choosing constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.EndpointSystem.text: An endpoint solution remains a solution when coefficient and source functions are replaced by functions equal on the interval. Behavior outside the interval is irrelevant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.EndpointSystem.summary: Transferring a solution across equal interval data

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.ae_spatialSlic.text: Almost every time slice of a joint square-integrable sum or difference agrees with the corresponding sum or difference of spatial slices. This supplies representative compatibility in the weak instantaneous equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.ae_spatialSlic.summary: Spatial slices respect sums and differences

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.budget_le_powe.text: Bound the explicit recovery expression involving the mixed inverse and instantaneous inverse by a universal constant times a power of the combined coefficient budget. The chosen exponent is twice the freezing exponent plus one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.budget_le_powe.summary: A single polynomial bound for the two inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.coefficientMul.text: A scalar multiple of a coefficient acts as the same scalar multiple of its action on a field. This is the pointwise linearity used in rescaling the vorticity term.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.coefficientMul.summary: Moving a scalar through coefficient multiplication

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_cur.text: A jointly smooth periodic spatial lift on the time slab determines a smooth curve in the half-Holder space, using the supplied finite spatial jets of the lift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_cur.summary: Smooth Holder curves from smooth periodic lifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_lif.text: If the displacement lift is smooth and its within-time derivative is the velocity, identify the velocity lift with the time derivative and obtain joint smoothness.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_lif.summary: Smooth velocity from a smooth displacement

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_sol.text: A solenoidal curve whose Euclidean lift is jointly smooth is smooth as a curve in the divergence-free Holder subspace.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_sol.summary: Smooth curves in the divergence-free subspace

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_tim.text: A jointly smooth function on the time-space slab has a jointly smooth derivative in the time direction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_tim.summary: Smoothness of the time derivative on a slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.continuousOn_i.text: Continuous coefficient, source, and velocity curves give a continuous integrated residual, since the vorticity-velocity product has a continuous primitive.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.continuousOn_i.summary: Continuity of the integrated momentum residual

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.endpointClosed.text: Composing a continuous curve with a clock mapping the new closed interval into the old one cannot increase its closed-time norm.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.endpointSystem.text: A solution on $[0,T_1]$ gives a solution on $[0,T_2]$ whenever $\sigma>0$ and $\sigma T_2=T_1$. The new displacement is $\sigma^{-1}z(\sigma\tau)$, its derivative is $v(\sigma\tau)$, and the vorticity coefficient gains a factor $\sigma$. The source and pressure gradient are composed with the same time change. Both zero traces and the integrated equation are preserved. Taking $\sigma=T$, $T_1=T$, $T_2=1$ gives the paper’s normalization.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.endpointSystem.summary: Time rescaling preserves the full endpoint system

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.eval_sourceDer.text: Evaluation at a label commutes with the time primitive, so the source derivative is the negative forcing integrand. Continuity supplies the fundamental theorem of calculus on the closed interval.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_instant.text: Choose the pointwise compressed inverses on the time interval and use smooth inversion of operator curves to obtain the asserted time regularity and uniform bound. The selected family is assigned the identity outside the interval, where no regularity is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_instant.summary: Continuous instantaneous inverses from pointwise inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_isometr.text: Conjugate a continuous linear equivalence through a linear isometry equivalence while preserving its stated inverse bound. This changes the representation of the solenoidal space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_isometr.summary: Transporting an inverse through an isometry

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixedSo.text: Assuming the mixed solution already has the required spatial derivative words, differentiate the projected equation and use the product rule and commuting projection to obtain every differentiated equation with its lower-order Leibniz correction. Regularity itself comes from the supplied higher-order freezing conclusion, not this differentiation lemma.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixedSo.summary: Differentiated mixed equations for spatial derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixedTi.text: Given a mixed projected solution, ellipticity, and a continuous bounded instantaneous inverse family, construct a continuous solenoidal representative with both primitive endpoints zero. Recover the constant by time averaging and identify almost-everywhere representatives by testing the difference against the positive coefficient.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixedTi.summary: Recovering a continuous velocity from the mixed solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixed_r.text: Represent the continuous endpoint solution in the mixed Holder-in-label and square-integrable-in-time space, preserving both constraints and its projected residual equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixed_r.summary: A mixed representation of an endpoint solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_smoothS.text: Apply the mixed higher-order clause of Lemma A.2 to obtain every finite spatial derivative hierarchy, differentiate the mixed equation to expose its commutators, and recover time-smooth representatives through base-space instantaneous inverses. Joint smoothness follows from matched finite spatial jets; this differs from the paper's use of instantaneous inverses on each higher Holder class.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_smoothS.summary: A smooth solution from mixed spatial regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_solenoi.text:
Transfers the spatial conclusion of Lemma A.2 from the fixed space of the strong Leray projection to the concrete solenoidal half-Hölder subspace. The supplied freezing conclusion identifies the compressed coefficient and its polynomial bound. The theorem returns an equivalence whose action is the projected coefficient multiplication, together with the corresponding inverse norm estimate. It is used separately at each time for $K(t)$; continuity of the resulting family is supplied later.

Only the base-space clause of the supplied freezing conclusion is used in this transfer; its higher-order clause is not consumed here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_solenoi.summary: Transferring the freezing inverse to solenoidal fields

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_spatial.text: For a finite spatial derivative hierarchy satisfying the differentiated mixed equations, recover time-smooth representatives using the supplied instantaneous inverse family and induction on word length. All permitted time derivatives retain the spatial derivative relations and the endpoint primitive conditions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_spatial.summary: Time regularity of the spatial derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_unitSol.text: Given the mixed inverse and the continuous bounded family of instantaneous inverses, construct the unique continuous solenoidal velocity with zero time mean and constant projected residual. The explicit norm estimate combines the two inverse bounds; coercivity is used to identify its almost-everywhere mixed representative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_unitSol.summary: The unit interval solution from two inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.fixedTime42.text: The spatial case of Lemma A.2 is applied to $K(t)$ with ellipticity $D_-^{-2}$ and Lipschitz bound $2K_1$. The resulting isomorphism is transported to the divergence-free half-Hölder subspace. The norm bound is $C_2(2+D^2+K_0+2K_1)^{p_2}\|\mathbb P\|$ for the inverse composed with the Leray projection. This factor is later absorbed into the common $A$. The helper assumes the stated freezing conclusion instead of invoking an unrelated inverse theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.fixedTime42.summary: The fixed time inverse from spatial freezing

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.freezingConclu.text: Assembles the higher-order conclusion once the compressed map preserves the Hölder class, has unique preimages in that class, and both forward and inverse norm bounds are supplied. It identifies the inverse image with the one already given by the base equivalence. A single enlarged constant then serves both directions of the higher-norm comparison. This is the final assembly used for each Hilbert-space case of Lemma A.2; it does not derive the input regularity or bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.freezingConclu.summary: Combining the higher Hölder inverse estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasDerivWithin.text: The scalar map taking a new time to T times that time has within-set derivative T on every set. This supplies the clock derivative for the later chain rule and needs no interval-mapping hypothesis.
Evaluate a joint derivative on the pure time direction to obtain the derivative of a time slice at a fixed spatial point, with the time-interval boundary treated by within derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasDerivWithin.summary: Time derivatives of jointly smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialDeri.text: Directional differentiation on torus lines distributes over the sum of two Holder fields.
Differentiate pointwise application of an operator-valued Holder coefficient to a field, obtaining the derivative of the coefficient times the field plus the coefficient times the field derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialDeri.summary: The spatial product rule for a coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialDeri.text: Negating a Holder field negates its directional derivative along every torus line.
Two Holder fields representing the same directional derivative on every torus line agree pointwise. This identifies derivatives after differentiating a projected equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialDeri.summary: Uniqueness of a spatial directional derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialHold.text: A hierarchy of coordinate derivative words through order N plus one restricts to a hierarchy through order N.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialHold.summary: Discarding the highest spatial derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.integral_norm_.text: The inequality $\|v\|_{L^2}^2\le D^2(1+L)^2\|M Fz+Fv\|_{L^2}^2$ holds for every mean-zero $L^2$ velocity, with $z=\int_0^t v$. The hypotheses give $F_t=MF$, a left inverse bounded by $D$, and a gradient bound $L$ on $0<T\le1$. The proof extends the continuous-velocity estimate by density, because both quadratic expressions are continuous on $L^2$. This fills the Sobolev scope missing from the older pointwise derivative lemma.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.integral_norm_.summary: Controlling label velocity by displacement velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.integratedMome.text: If coefficients and sources agree throughout the time interval, their integrated momentum residuals agree at every time of that interval.
An interval-integral substitution identifies the momentum residual for rescaled coefficients and velocity with the original residual at the scaled time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.integratedMome.summary: The integrated residual under time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.lifts42.text: Construct the smooth kinetic and vorticity coefficient lifts from the smooth deformation and velocity gradient of the parent flow.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mapsTo_scale.text: A positive scale taking the new terminal time to the old one maps the entire new closed interval into the old closed interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mapsTo_scale.summary: Scalar time rescaling maps the required intervals

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanDeformatio.text: The inverse deformation of the rescaled flow is the original inverse deformation evaluated at the rescaled time.
The deformation matrix of the rescaled flow is the original deformation evaluated at the rescaled time.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanGradientRa.text: The time derivative of the rescaled gradient acquires two factors of T, one from velocity scaling and one from the clock.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanGradientRa.summary: The gradient derivative after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanGradient_s.text: The gradient of the rescaled parent velocity is T times the original gradient at the rescaled time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanGradient_s.summary: The velocity gradient after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanHsharp_sca.text: The rescaled H-sharp is T squared times the original H-sharp at the rescaled time, because both the gradient derivative and its square have that factor.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanHsharp_sca.summary: The quadratic-form coefficient after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanHsharp_sca.text: For positive T at most one, the upper bound H-sharp at most the identity passes to the scaled parent. The proof treats negative quadratic values separately; multiplication by T squared need not decrease a negative value in the order needed for a naive argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanHsharp_sca.summary: The quadratic upper bound survives rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanKinetic_sc.text: The kinetic coefficient of the rescaled flow is K evaluated at the rescaled time, without an additional power of T.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanKinetic_sc.summary: The kinetic coefficient after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanParentFlow.text: For positive T at most one, the rescaled velocity and flow satisfy the mean-parent assumptions on the unit interval, including derivatives, periodicity, divergence freedom, and inverse flow identities.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanParentFlow.summary: The rescaled parent satisfies the flow hypotheses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanVorticity_.text: The pulled-back skew vorticity coefficient acquires one factor of T under the unit-interval rescaling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanVorticity_.summary: The vorticity coefficient after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixedPathCoeff.text: Spatial derivatives of K and Omega give the corresponding derivative of the path operator K minus J Omega. The time primitive is a fixed bounded operator and commutes with this spatial differentiation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixedPathCoeff.summary: Spatial differentiation of the mixed path coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_fixed.text: A continuous solenoidal velocity with zero terminal primitive has a mixed representative fixed by the combined spatial and temporal projection. The zero time mean encodes the second endpoint condition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_fixed.summary: The mixed representative satisfies both constraints

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_projecti.text: If the spatial projection of a continuous residual is a time-independent field, then its mixed representative has zero combined spatial and time-mean projection. This links the integrated equation to the mixed equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_projecti.summary: The mixed projection removes the constant field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_solution.text: Two mixed fields fixed by the projection and solving the same compressed equation agree because the supplied mixed operator is an isomorphism. This is uniqueness conditional on that inverse, not a new freezing theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_solution.summary: Uniqueness from the supplied mixed inverse

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.norm_symm_le_o.text: For a continuous linear equivalence, a lower bound controlling the input norm by the output norm gives the corresponding operator norm bound for its inverse.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.parent42.text: Convert the paper's smooth mean-parent flow into the older inverse library's parent structure, transporting gradient bounds from labels to Eulerian points through the inverse flow.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.pow_le_of_le_s.text: If $0\le x\le cS^4$, $c\ge0$, $S\ge1$ and $n\le m$, then $x^n\le c^nS^{4m}$. This elementary inequality is the step used to replace different inverse exponents by one common power of the parent controls. Its hypotheses make raising to a power and enlarging the exponent legitimate. It asserts no estimate for the analytic operators until their bounds have supplied the values of $x,c,S$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.pow_le_of_le_s.summary: Absorbing powers into a common polynomial bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledFlow.text:
Define the two-time parent flow with both time arguments multiplied by T. Spatial variables are unchanged.

Default-value audit (b5): Defined by composition for every real T, without division. At T = 0 both time arguments are zero; the theorem giving the required rescaled parent flow assumes positive T at most one.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledFlow_bac.text: Setting the terminal time of the rescaled two-time flow to zero gives the original backward map from T times the new time. This is an evaluation identity, not a separate proof of the inverse-flow relation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledFlow_zer.text: Setting the initial time of the rescaled two-time flow to zero gives the original forward flow evaluated at T times the new time. This is an evaluation identity and uses no flow equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledVelocity.text:
Define the parent velocity after time rescaling by multiplying its value at T times time by T. This is the velocity whose flow follows the original trajectories at the rescaled clock.

Default-value audit (b5): Defined for every real scaling factor T, including zero or negative T. The factor-zero velocity is zero; the parent-flow theorem is only used for positive T at most one, which maps the desired interval correctly.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledVelocity.summary: The parent velocity on the unit time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.smooth42.text: For a smooth periodic physical force, every solution of the integrated endpoint equation has a smooth displacement and yields smooth Eulerian corrections with $b(0)=c$. The helper assumes the previously constructed inverse and transfers its displacement regularity to the chosen solution. It differentiates the projected momentum residual and constructs a normalized pressure from the resulting gradient. The label and Eulerian equations follow. The original integrated potential is used only through its equation; the proof does not establish that the reconstructed pressure equals $-\phi_t$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.smooth42.summary: Recovering the smooth physical correction and pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.smoothData_con.text: Once the velocity is jointly smooth and the coefficients and source are smooth, obtain joint smoothness of its primitive, the spatial constant field, and the pressure gradient. The constant is recovered by projecting a fixed-time residual, while the gradient is the residual minus that constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.smoothData_con.summary: Smooth displacement constant and pressure gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.sobolevEnergy_.text: Lemma 4.1 and the full Sobolev comparison of label and displacement derivatives give coercivity $[2D^2(1+L)^2]^{-1}$ for the unit-time coefficients $K(T\tau)$ and $T\Omega(T\tau)$. The helper rescales the parent itself, so the upper bound on the new endpoint Hessian follows from $T\le1$. It accepts arbitrary mean-zero $L^2$ velocities. This is the hypothesis supplied to Theorem A.1, and the named Lemma 4.1 is an explicit argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.sobolevEnergy_.summary: Sobolev coercivity after rescaling the parent flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.solve42.text: Given Lemma 4.1 and the body of Theorem A.1 with fixed constants, the helper solves the endpoint problem on $[0,T]$. It uses $K(T\tau)$, $T\Omega(T\tau)$ and the rescaled source on $[0,1]$, then transfers the solution and uniqueness back. The norm bound retains the ellipticity and coercivity parameters before polynomial absorption. For a smooth rescaled source it retains smoothness of $z$; it does not retain the other smoothness conclusions about $c$ and the integrated pressure gradient.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.solve42.summary: The endpoint solution from the unit interval inverse

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.text:
Define a linear isometry between the fixed space of the strong Leray projection and the divergence-free Holder subspace. Both descriptions contain the same underlying field; this is a type-level identification without an analytic inversion.

Default-value audit (b5): Both directions preserve the same underlying Holder field and merely exchange equivalent subspace membership proofs. The zero field is handled ordinarily; there is no coefficient inverse, arbitrary representative, or exceptional value.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.summary: Identifying the two solenoidal Holder spaces

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.text: The forward isometry leaves the underlying Holder vector field unchanged.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.summary: The fixed space identification preserves the field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.text: The inverse isometry likewise leaves the underlying Holder field unchanged, so estimates transfer without changing norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.summary: The inverse identification preserves the field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatiallyPerio.text: Evaluating a torus-valued Holder field on the Euclidean covering map gives a spatially periodic field.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.srcDeriv42.text: For the prescribed integrated force source, differentiate its Holder-space primitive to obtain minus the deformation transpose applied to the pulled-back force. Pointwise evaluation agrees with this derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.srcDeriv42.summary: The derivative of the pulled back force source

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.strongMixedLer.text: Translation invariance and the Haar-space norm bound imply that the combined Leray and time-mean projection preserves the given spatial directional derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.strongMixedLer.summary: The mixed projection commutes with spatial differentiation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Asub.text:
The linear space of bounded coefficient derivatives. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): Each word of the symmetric coefficient family has its own finite uniform bound on the slab. No common bound over all words, continuity in time, or realization as actual derivatives is built into this space. These additional facts are supplied where the smooth ODE is inserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Asub.summary: The linear space of bounded coefficient derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DA.text:
Shift the derivative family of a coefficient. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): The maps are restrictions of word-index shifts, with closure in the relevant subspaces proved in the definition. They encode already-weighted directions supplied elsewhere, rather than inserting an extra scalar weight here. Symmetry gives commutation; no new spatial differentiability is inferred merely from the shift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DA.summary: Shift the derivative family of a coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DA_apply.text: Evaluate a shifted coefficient derivative. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DA_comm.text: The weighted derivative maps commute (`DA_comm`), as required by Lemma D.3. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DE.text:
The weighted derivative in the direction `i` on solution jets. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): The maps are restrictions of word-index shifts, with closure in the relevant subspaces proved in the definition. They encode already-weighted directions supplied elsewhere, rather than inserting an extra scalar weight here. Symmetry gives commutation; no new spatial differentiability is inferred merely from the shift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DE.summary: Shift the derivative family of a solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DE_apply.text: Evaluate a shifted solution derivative. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DE_comm.text: The weighted derivative maps commute (`DE_comm`), as required by Lemma D.3. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF.text:
Shift both forcing and initial derivative families. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): The maps are restrictions of word-index shifts, with closure in the relevant subspaces proved in the definition. They encode already-weighted directions supplied elsewhere, rather than inserting an extra scalar weight here. Symmetry gives commutation; no new spatial differentiability is inferred merely from the shift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF.summary: Shift both forcing and initial derivative families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF_apply_fst.text: The forcing component of the shift prepends the selected direction to its word index. The same shift acts simultaneously on the initial-value component.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF_apply_snd.text: The initial-value component of the shift prepends the selected direction to its word index. This ensures that spatial differentiation commutes with prescribed initial data.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF_comm.text: The weighted derivative maps commute (`DF_comm`), as required by Lemma D.3. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF_comm.summary: Forcing and initial derivative shifts commute

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.EP.text:
Admissible time regularity of a solution derivative family. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): An element is a symmetric family of functions differentiable within the slab with continuous within-derivatives. This is weaker than being the derivative family of a single spatial function. Values outside the slab are unconstrained; later OdeData constructions supply the actual finite derivative family.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.EP.summary: Admissible time regularity of a solution derivative family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Esub.text:
The linear space of solution derivative families. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): An element is a symmetric family of functions differentiable within the slab with continuous within-derivatives. This is weaker than being the derivative family of a single spatial function. Values outside the slab are unconstrained; later OdeData constructions supply the actual finite derivative family.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Esub.summary: The linear space of solution derivative families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Fsub.text:
The linear space of forcing and initial derivatives. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): Only the forcing part has a weighted boundedness condition; the second component is an arbitrary symmetric family of initial values. No continuity of the forcing is included here. The combined seminorm separately measures the initial component and the forcing component.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Fsub.summary: The linear space of forcing and initial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: The actual selected velocity and pressure satisfy the quantitative inverse estimate in the measured active-slab seminorm. The positive coefficient-word bound enters only through its dimensionless budget. The selected solution has zero initial data, zero phase mean and support inherited from the forcing. Positive weight and covector hypotheses make the measured velocity and frequency-weighted pressure estimates meaningful.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Bound the selected transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: Smooth strain and a smooth everywhere nonzero covector give smooth pressure coefficients for the amplitude and source terms. Nonvanishing is essential for the factors involving the inverse squared covector norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Nonvanishing covectors give smooth pressure coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: Lemma 5.3(i)–(ii) (cc:uf:tower:lem:inverse) for arbitrary smooth supported launch data and for the selected zero-start transverse solve. The frequency-weighted active seminorms are the actual Appendix D norms. This passes pointwise word estimates to the finite weighted norms used in Section 5. Constants may depend on the derivative order but the final power of the parent bound does not.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The supported transverse inverse preserves every derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: Derivative-order constants control the actual coframe, generator and pressure coefficient words. The measured oscillatory inverse budget retains a single power `D ^ 20` at every order. The supported labels lie within twice the envelope radius of a lattice point. The parent bounds and central weighted stability supply the near-origin propagator estimate; smallness of the label radius absorbs differentiated coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Coframe and pressure constants have uniform parent cost

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: The parent deformation and velocity bounds determine a radius exponent for the selected fixed-plane forward propagator. The supported labels lie within twice the envelope radius of a lattice point. The parent bounds and central weighted stability supply the near-origin propagator estimate; smallness of the label radius absorbs differentiated coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The transverse propagator is controlled near the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: The finite launch seminorm controls each admissible derivative word of the initial profile. This supplies the individual initial-data bound required by the ODE recurrence from the paper's summed launch norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The launch norm bounds each derivative word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: A bound `C ℓ D^27` on the rescaled jets of positive order of a phase-independent coefficient gives the bound `C D^{-3}` on its weighted derivative words of positive length, since `ℓ ≤ D^{-30}`. The supported labels lie within twice the envelope radius of a lattice point. The parent bounds and central weighted stability supply the near-origin propagator estimate; smallness of the label radius absorbs differentiated coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: A small envelope absorbs differentiated coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: For a smooth function of labels alone and nonnegative label scale, any mixed label-phase word is bounded by the label scale to the word length times the corresponding Fréchet derivative norm. A phase derivative annihilates such a coefficient; the bound is sufficient without separating that zero case in later estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Label derivatives control phase independent derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: For a smooth label field and a nonnegative scale, the jth derivative norm of a↦f(ℓa) equals ℓ^j times the jth derivative norm of f at ℓa. This turns a rescaled-label estimate into the weighted derivatives of Appendix D, including j=0.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Rescaling labels inserts the derivative weights

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: Positive frequency, nonvanishing smooth covector, and finite derivative bounds for κ/λ and λ²/|κ|² give a finite derivative bound for the normalized pressure-source coefficient. The result isolates the coefficient multiplying the forcing in the zero-mean pressure primitive.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The normalized pressure source has bounded derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text:
The selected oscillatory inverse constant in the sum of velocity and carrier-weighted pressure seminorms. The constants collect the fixed-plane inverse, the two coframes and the pressure primitive. Their use requires the displayed nonnegative bounds; the eventual estimate has a single power of the parent scale at every derivative order.

Default-value audit (b5): These are total real-valued expressions for arbitrary scalar arguments. A negative duration or a negative coefficient bound does not have the intended estimate interpretation. The application theorems impose nonnegative budgets and a positive time slab. No division occurs here; the selected amplification factor is controlled only at its nonnegative argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The constant for transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: The velocity part has degree thirteen in `D`. Its pressure contribution has degree twenty, while the direct forcing contribution has degree six. The constants collect the fixed-plane inverse, the two coframes and the pressure primitive. Their use requires the displayed nonnegative bounds; the eventual estimate has a single power of the parent scale at every derivative order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: One parent exponent bounds velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text:
The per-word velocity constant from the fixed-plane solve and the two coframes. The constants collect the fixed-plane inverse, the two coframes and the pressure primitive. Their use requires the displayed nonnegative bounds; the eventual estimate has a single power of the parent scale at every derivative order.

Default-value audit (b5): These are total real-valued expressions for arbitrary scalar arguments. A negative duration or a negative coefficient bound does not have the intended estimate interpretation. The application theorems impose nonnegative budgets and a positive time slab. No division occurs here; the selected amplification factor is controlled only at its nonnegative argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The constant for transverse velocity derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: A solve on an interval of length at most one has a common coefficient for its initial-data and source bounds. The constants collect the fixed-plane inverse, the two coframes and the pressure primitive. Their use requires the displayed nonnegative bounds; the eventual estimate has a single power of the parent scale at every derivative order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: A unit time interval gives a common constant

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.IsSymm.text:
Derivative families invariant under permutations. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): This is only invariance of a family under permutations of its list index. It does not assert existence of an underlying smooth field or derivative relations. The empty word is allowed and its symmetry condition is automatic.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.text:
Pointwise power bound `‖∂^m f x‖ ≤ C_m D^{a(m+1)}` (the pointwise form of (D.6)). The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate includes smoothness and an inequality at every order, including zero. It does not itself assert D≥1 or nonnegative constants. Monotonicity and product/rescaling theorems supply their own sign hypotheses, so the formula at a nonpositive scale is not silently interpreted as a parent estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.summary: Pointwise derivatives bounded by powers of the parent scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.comp_l.text: A fixed contraction applied on the left preserves the power bound. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.comp_l.summary: A contraction preserves polynomial derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.const_.text: Multiplying the coefficient field by a constant scalar multiplies its derivative constants by the absolute value of that scalar. The power of the parent scale is unchanged.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.const_.summary: Scale a coefficient and its derivative constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.mono_c.text: Pointwise enlargement of the nonnegative derivative constants preserves the same smooth coefficient power bound. The field, parent scale and exponent stay fixed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.mono_c.summary: Increase the constants in a derivative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.mono_e.text: When the parent scale is at least one, increasing the absolute exponent weakens every derivative bound. This permits several coefficient estimates to share one exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.mono_e.summary: Increase the parent exponent in a derivative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0.text:
Time differentiation together with the initial value. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): The forcing component is the within-interval derivative multiplied by the interval indicator, hence zero outside the slab. The data component evaluates at the actual left endpoint. The admitted solution-family regularity makes the derivative legitimate on the slab; no differentiability of the zero extension across its boundary is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0.summary: Time differentiation together with the initial value

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_comm.text: The weighted derivative maps commute (`L0_comm`), as required by Lemma D.3. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_comm.summary: Spatial shifts commute with time differentiation and initial evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_fst.text: On the closed interval the forcing component of L₀ is the within-interval time derivative of the solution family. Outside the interval this component is explicitly zero by the indicator in the definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_fst.summary: Recover the time derivative in the forcing component

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_snd.text: The data component of L₀ evaluates every word of the solution family at the left endpoint. It is the initial datum that accompanies the forcing in the inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_snd.summary: Recover the initial value in the data component

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaf2.text:
The leaf jets at a base scale `D₀` with `D₀ ^ d2Scale ≤ D`; `D` is the scale of the chain. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.

Default-value audit (b5): The witness D₀ is explicitly at least one and satisfies D₀^64≤D, so the comparison cannot use a zero or negative base scale. The predicate stores coefficient bounds at D₀, not at an unspecified smaller positive number. It does not construct new parent data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaf2.summary: Coefficient estimates at a smaller parent scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaf2.toLeaf.text: The two-scale leaf jets give the leaf jets at the chain scale. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaf2.toLeaf.summary: Transfer coefficient bounds to the larger parent scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaves.text:
The facts of Lemmas 3.1, D.1, D.2, D.3 that the library chain consumes. This module passes supplied proofs of Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2, and a derivative recurrence obtained from D.3, into the copied transverse argument. The local class is a bundle of hypotheses, not an additional axiom.

Default-value audit (b5): The class stores proofs of the cited statements and a weighted ODE estimate; declaring the class does not assert that an instance exists. The entry theorem explicitly constructs an instance from its hypotheses. The factor Φ is constrained only on nonnegative arguments, which is the domain used by the estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaves.summary: The cited estimates needed for the transverse inverse

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: Localized homogeneous seed estimates in normalized spatial coordinates. The ODE estimate is used only on the support of the envelope. Initial data are the projected center amplitude, including every derivative of the envelope. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Bound the enveloped seed in rescaled labels

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: Smooth deformation and covector data give a smooth longitudinal coframe in the stated parameter domain. The construction uses the supplied nonvanishing hypotheses wherever inverse covector lengths occur.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: The longitudinal coframe depends smoothly on its coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: A single natural exponent is chosen large enough to enforce the finite list of smallness requirements for the transverse coframe. It is independent of the derivative order; the constants at each order remain separate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Choose one envelope exponent for the coframe bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: Lemma 5.3(iii) for the unswitched leading velocity and its normalized primitive pressure on the active slab. The norm is taken in the independent label and phase, before taking the physical graph. This passes pointwise word estimates to the finite weighted norms used in Section 5. Constants may depend on the derivative order but the final power of the parent bound does not.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Bound the leading oscillation and its pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: On the actual closed parent slab, the same radius exponent serves all orders of the initial leading velocity and pressure estimates. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: One envelope exponent controls every leading derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: The scaled leading velocity and pressure estimates obtained from the same seed and parent coefficients. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Retain the leading profile derivative estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: The coframe coefficients of the actual parent flow satisfy the power bound (D.6), by Lemma D.2(a) (`transverseCoframe_jetPower`), as used in the proof of Lemma 5.3 (06c_finite_hierarchy.tex:92-95). The leaf jets hold at the base scale `D₀`; the geometric bounds on the flow hold at the scale `D`. The fields are `F = D_a X`, `G Q` with `Q` the projection orthogonal to `G^T k`, and `-2 (G Q)(M F)`; the lift `J`, the pullback `R` and the generator `A` are fixed contractions of them (`J = F ι`, `R = π (G Q)`, `A = π (-2 (G Q)(M F)) ι` with the inclusion `ι` and the orthogonal projection `π` of the transverse plane). The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: The transverse coframe has polynomial derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: The physical enveloped seed has polynomial cost (D^{13}) at every fixed order. The restriction on the label radius uses only the first derivative of the generator. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: The enveloped seed has one fixed parent exponent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: A bound for each derivative of the rescaled leading field gives a bound for the finite weighted raw norm. The number of admissible words and the inverse positive amplitude weight are accounted for explicitly.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Rescaled derivatives control the weighted finite norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.text:
The data of the linear ODE `x' = A x + f` on `[l, r]` at a fixed point `p`. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

Default-value audit (b5): The record requires l<r, smooth coefficient/source/solution and a strictly positive differentiable weight on the slab. The homogeneous stability estimate is only at the stored parameter point p; it is not an unstated uniform estimate at every parameter. Sign assumptions on K are provided by downstream estimates, not by this record alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.summary: A smooth linear equation with a positive weight

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.Rw.text:
The differentiated right side of the equation. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

Default-value audit (b5): The word derivative of Ax+f is a total Lean expression, but the smooth ODE interpretation is used only on the stored slab where OdeData supplies regularity. Unlike xj and aj, this expression is not padded by a time or order cutoff.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.Rw.summary: The differentiated right side of the equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aE.text:
The coefficient jets as an element of the space of coefficients. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

Default-value audit (b5): The bundled family uses the deliberately zero-padded finite jets. Membership proves only symmetry and the required within-slab regularity or boundedness. It does not identify the padded family with all higher derivatives of the original field. For aE the positive-order bound is an explicit input, and compactness bounds the zero-order coefficient.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aE.summary: Place coefficient derivatives in the bounded linear space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aj.text:
The jets `∂^w A(t, p)` of order `≤ n` (zero otherwise and outside the slab). Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

Default-value audit (b5): The definition sets entries to zero both above the retained derivative order and outside the closed time slab.
