Symmetric derivative towers of a smooth periodic field. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The record includes symmetry, smooth time dependence, actual spatial-derivative relations and equality of lifted entries with the derivatives of the given field. Those assertions are restricted to the time slab. It is stronger than an arbitrary symmetric continuous family; its existence is separately proved from smooth periodic input.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.SymTower.summary: A smooth periodic field with its symmetric derivative family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk.text:
Project the kinetic product and subtract its initial value. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression subtracts its projected product at time zero, retaining the constant term of the integrated equation. It is total for arbitrary word families and does not require their being derivatives. The relevant continuity and norm bounds are separate hypotheses and results.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk.summary: Project the kinetic product and subtract its initial value

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TkB.text:
The `K`-action as a bilinear map on the spaces of towers. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): These bilinear maps are bundled only after proving that the explicit kinetic and integrated vorticity actions preserve the required family spaces. The time interval is positive in their setup. They are algebraic maps with later seminorm bounds, not a claim that every input solves the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TkB.summary: The kinetic action on admissible derivative families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TkB_val.text: Forgetting the subspace proofs in the bilinear kinetic action gives the explicit expression P(au)(t)−P(au)(0) at every word. The term at time zero is retained because the integrated equation has an unknown constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TkB_val.summary: Read the kinetic action on the underlying families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_add_le.text: The projected kinetic product with its initial value subtracted respects addition in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_add_le.summary: The kinetic action is additive in the coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_add_ri.text: The projected kinetic product with its initial value subtracted respects addition in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_add_ri.summary: The kinetic action is additive in the velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_contin.text: Continuous entries of the coefficient and solution families make each projected kinetic-product difference continuous in time. This validates its membership in the forcing-family space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_contin.summary: The kinetic action preserves continuity in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_der.text: `Tk a v` of a derivative tower is a derivative tower (Leibniz rule; TeX 46-48). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_der.summary: The kinetic action preserves spatial derivative relations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_leibni.text: A coordinate shift of the projected kinetic product and its initial value is the sum of the terms with the shift assigned to the coefficient and to the solution. This is the unweighted word-family Leibniz rule; the weighted version is used in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_leibni.summary: The kinetic action obeys the derivative product rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_mem.text: Permutation symmetry and continuity of the two inputs imply that the kinetic action belongs to the symmetric continuous forcing-family space. This is a well-definedness result for the operator, not the mean equation itself.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_mem.summary: The kinetic action gives an admissible forcing family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_perm.text: Symmetric coefficient and solution families give a symmetric kinetic action after projection and subtraction of the time-zero value. No differentiation in time is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_perm.summary: The kinetic action preserves permutation invariance

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_smul_l.text: The projected kinetic product with its initial value subtracted respects constant scalar multiplication in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_smul_l.summary: The kinetic action respects coefficient scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_smul_r.text: The projected kinetic product with its initial value subtracted respects constant scalar multiplication in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_smul_r.summary: The kinetic action respects velocity scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom.text:
Integrate and project the negative vorticity product. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): This expression is the negative projected clamped primitive of the finite Leibniz product. Its analytic interpretation uses T>0 and continuous inputs; arbitrary totalized integral values outside that setting are not used for estimates. The sign agrees with the integrated mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom.summary: Integrate and project the negative vorticity product

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TomB.text:
The `Ω`-action as a bilinear map on the spaces of towers. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): These bilinear maps are bundled only after proving that the explicit kinetic and integrated vorticity actions preserve the required family spaces. The time interval is positive in their setup. They are algebraic maps with later seminorm bounds, not a claim that every input solves the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TomB.summary: The integrated vorticity action on admissible derivative families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TomB_val.text: Forgetting the subspace proofs in the bilinear vorticity action gives minus the projected time primitive of the Leibniz product. This is the coefficient term whose operator norm carries a factor T.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TomB_val.summary: Read the vorticity action on the underlying families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_add_l.text: The negative projected time primitive of the product respects addition in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. Continuity on a nonnegative time interval supplies integrability for the additive identity. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_add_l.summary: The integrated vorticity action is additive in the coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_add_r.text: The negative projected time primitive of the product respects addition in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. Continuity on a nonnegative time interval supplies integrability for the additive identity. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_add_r.summary: The integrated vorticity action is additive in the velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_conti.text: On a positive interval, continuity of both families makes each projected time-primitive product continuous. This validates the integrated term in the forcing-family space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_conti.summary: The integrated vorticity action preserves continuity in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_leibn.text: A coordinate shift of the projected time integral of the product is the sum of the terms with the shift assigned to the coefficient and to the solution. This is the unweighted word-family Leibniz rule; the weighted version is used in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_leibn.summary: The integrated vorticity action obeys the derivative product rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_mem.text: On a positive interval, the integrated vorticity action of two continuous symmetric families is again such a family. The proof combines symmetry with continuity of the primitive.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_mem.summary: The integrated vorticity action gives an admissible forcing family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_perm.text: Symmetric coefficient and solution families give a symmetric integrated vorticity action. The word permutation affects neither the fixed time integral nor the projection.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_perm.summary: The vorticity action preserves permutation invariance

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_smul_.text: The negative projected time primitive of the product respects constant scalar multiplication in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_smul_.summary: The integrated vorticity action respects coefficient scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_smul_.text: The negative projected time primitive of the product respects constant scalar multiplication in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_smul_.summary: The integrated vorticity action respects velocity scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw.text:
Expand every derivative of coefficient times velocity. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The finite recursion distributes each derivative letter between coefficient and solution. At the empty word it is the pointwise half-Hölder product. It is defined for arbitrary families; only IsDer and symmetry hypotheses make it the derivative family of an actual product.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw.summary: Expand every derivative of coefficient times velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw0_bound.text: The zero-order coefficient product at an allowed time is bounded by twice the product of the two closed-time norms. The factor two is the half-Hölder multiplication bound used in this implementation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_add_le.text: The finite Leibniz product respects addition in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_add_le.summary: The Leibniz expansion is additive in the coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_add_ri.text: The finite Leibniz product respects addition in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_add_ri.summary: The Leibniz expansion is additive in the velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_bound.text: The empty-word product has half-Hölder norm at most twice the product of the two input norms at the same time. This local multiplication bound becomes the operator bounds for the kinetic and integrated actions.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_contin.text: Continuous coefficient and solution entries make every finite Leibniz product entry continuous in time on the closed interval. This gives integrability for the vorticity action.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_contin.summary: Continuous coefficient and velocity families give continuous products

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_der.text: The Leibniz expansion of two symmetric derivative towers is a derivative tower (product rule). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_der.summary: The Leibniz product of derivative families is differentiated correctly

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_perm.text: The Leibniz product family is permutation invariant when both input families are. The induction accounts for every distribution of derivative letters between the two factors.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_perm.summary: The Leibniz expansion is invariant under coordinate permutations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_smul_l.text: The finite Leibniz product respects constant scalar multiplication in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_smul_l.summary: The Leibniz expansion respects coefficient scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_smul_r.text: The finite Leibniz product respects constant scalar multiplication in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_smul_r.summary: The Leibniz expansion respects velocity scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Wd.text:
Words of the three label directions. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): This is the list type on the three coordinate directions. The empty word represents order zero. No ordering, smoothness, derivative relation or commutation property is built into the abbreviation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl.text:
Time clamped to `[0,T]`, so that primitives only see the values on `[0,T]`. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula max(0,min(t,T)) is total for all real T,t. Its interval-membership lemma requires T≥0; for T<0 the formula is zero rather than a point of the empty interval. On [0,T] it is the identity. No smoothness of this clamp across the endpoints is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl.summary: Clamp the time to the closed parent interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl_eq.text: At a time already in [0,T], clamping returns the same time. This permits the totalized primitive to be replaced by the ordinary time primitive on the physical interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl_eq.summary: Clamping leaves times inside the interval unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl_mem.text: If T is nonnegative, the clamped time max(0,min(t,T)) lies in [0,T] for every real t. The sign hypothesis matters; the definition alone is total for all T.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cm_add.text: Coefficient multiplication is additive in the matrix coefficient. This supplies the left linearity of the product used in the integrated mean equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cm_smul.text: A scalar multiplying the matrix coefficient can be pulled out of coefficient multiplication. This supplies scalar linearity of the coefficient action.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dA.text:
The weighted derivations `ℓ ∂_i` on the three spaces of towers. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The weighted derivations are ℓ times restricted word shifts and are total even for negative or zero ℓ. The norm-identification and lifting results require ℓ≥0; the actual envelope radius is positive. They preserve the explicit subspace constraints by construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dA.summary: The radius weighted derivative on coefficient families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dA_val.text: On underlying families, the coefficient derivation is exactly ℓ times the coordinate shift. This is the evaluation identity used in the weighted Leibniz rules.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dA_val.summary: Read the radius weighted coefficient shift

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dE.text:
The solution derivation is the coordinate shift multiplied by the label radius ℓ, restricted to solenoidal families with zero total time integral. It therefore encodes the derivative weight without losing the endpoint constraints.

Default-value audit (b5): The weighted derivations are ℓ times restricted word shifts and are total even for negative or zero ℓ. The norm-identification and lifting results require ℓ≥0; the actual envelope radius is positive. They preserve the explicit subspace constraints by construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dE.summary: The radius weighted derivative on endpoint solution families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dE_val.text: On underlying constrained families, the solution derivation is exactly ℓ times the coordinate shift. The subtype carries the already-proved endpoint and solenoidal constraints.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dF.text:
The forcing derivation is the coordinate shift multiplied by the label radius ℓ. It acts on the symmetric continuous families used for the projected forcing equation.

Default-value audit (b5): The weighted derivations are ℓ times restricted word shifts and are total even for negative or zero ℓ. The norm-identification and lifting results require ℓ≥0; the actual envelope radius is positive. They preserve the explicit subspace constraints by construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dF.summary: The radius weighted derivative on forcing families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dF_val.text: On underlying forcing families, the forcing derivation is exactly ℓ times the coordinate shift. This relates the abstract derivation to the weighted word norm.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.endpointC.text: Time families equal on the closed interval have equal closed-time norms. The equality does not require their arbitrary values outside that interval to coincide.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.endpointC.summary: Agreement on the interval gives equal time suprema

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.eq_of_der.text: Two derivative towers with the same base and derivative relations coincide. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.eq_of_der.summary: The base field and derivative relations determine the family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exactNorm.text: For nonnegative label radius, the abstract exact-order coefficient norm equals the sum of the corresponding wordwise closed-time norms with factor ℓ^m. This identifies the commutator hypothesis in D.3 with (5.13).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exactNorm.summary: Read the weighted exact order coefficient norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exactNorm.text: The exact-order norm of Lemma D.3 is the weighted word norm (D.1). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exactNorm.summary: The abstract exact order norm is the weighted derivative sum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exists_sy.text: A jointly smooth periodic field on the slab has a symmetric derivative tower (jets of the sorted word, `sections/06d_mean_estimates.tex:46-48`: "label derivatives preserve the constraints"). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exists_sy.summary: Construct all periodic spatial derivatives in the Hölder space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exists_ve.text: The symmetric tower of a smooth divergence-free velocity `v = z_t` with `z(0) = z(T) = 0` is an element of `Esp T` (the endpoint and divergence constraints are preserved by label derivatives, `sections/06d_mean_estimates.tex:46-47`). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exists_ve.summary: The velocity derivative family satisfies both endpoint constraints

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.finiteNor.text: For nonnegative label radius, the abstract solution norm through order n equals the sum of the solution-family word norms weighted by ℓ to their lengths. The family remains in the solenoidal endpoint-constrained space.

For nonnegative label radius, the abstract forcing norm through order n equals the weighted sum of its wordwise closed-time norms. This is the forcing-side identification used in the lifted mean estimate.

The finite norm of Lemma D.3 is the weighted word norm (D.1) (scaling of derivations; TeX 52-58). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.finiteNor.summary: The abstract finite norm is the weighted derivative sum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSA.text: The coefficient-family space is stable under every coordinate shift. This supplies the invariant domain for the coefficient derivations in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSA.summary: Coefficient families are closed under label shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSE.text: The constrained solenoidal solution-family space is stable under every coordinate shift. Zero total time integral is imposed at every word, so the endpoint condition survives the shift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSE.summary: Endpoint solution families are closed under label shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSF.text: The forcing-family space is stable under every coordinate shift. This supplies the target-space derivations that commute with the integrated operators.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSF.summary: Forcing families are closed under label shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_coe.text: The spatial derivative of coefficient multiplication is the derivative of the coefficient times the field plus the coefficient times the derivative of the field. The hypotheses are actual spatial-derivative relations in the torus Hölder spaces.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_coe.summary: Spatial differentiation obeys the coefficient product rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_neg.text: Negating a field negates its specified torus spatial derivative. This handles the sign convention for the integrated source and vorticity primitive.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_pjL.text: The fixed Leray projection commutes with a specified spatial derivative. This preserves the projected equation when label derivatives are taken.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_pjL.summary: Spatial differentiation commutes with the Leray projection

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_uni.text: Two proposed half-Hölder spatial derivatives of the same field in the same direction agree. This lets an abstract derivative family be identified with the family constructed from the smooth field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_uni.summary: A spatial derivative in the Hölder space is unique

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.leibnizK.text: Applying a weighted coordinate shift to the kinetic action differentiates its coefficient or its solution factor. The subtraction at time zero commutes with that shift, giving the D.3 Leibniz identity on the constrained spaces.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.leibnizK.summary: The weighted kinetic action obeys the Leibniz rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.leibnizOm.text: Applying a weighted coordinate shift to the integrated vorticity action differentiates its coefficient or solution factor. Time integration and projection are fixed linear operations, so they preserve the Leibniz identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.leibnizOm.summary: The weighted vorticity action obeys the Leibniz rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.main_towe.text:
The lifting estimate (Lemma D.3 on the towers of the integrated mean system (4.9), `sections/06d_mean_estimates.tex:44-58`): `‖v‖_{[n],1/2} ≤ C_n C_low ‖P ∫ g‖_{[n],1/2}` as sums of closed-time norms of the words; `H1` is the first item of Theorem 4.2, `hmom` the projected equation (4.9) at the base level. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

The commutator smallness distinguishes multiplication by $K$ from time integration of $\Omega$: the latter contribution carries an additional factor $T$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.main_towe.summary: Lift the mean inverse bound to every spatial order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.mem_solen.text: If the base entry of a genuine derivative family is solenoidal, every higher entry is solenoidal as well. The result uses the derivative relations, not permutation symmetry alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.mem_solen.summary: Spatial derivatives preserve the solenoidal constraint

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.norm_S_eq.text: Inclusion of a solenoidal half-Hölder field into the ambient half-Hölder space preserves its norm. The constrained space has the inherited norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.norm_S_eq.summary: The solenoidal subspace inherits the Hölder norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.norm_prim.text: On a positive closed interval the primitive norm is at most T times the closed-time norm of its continuous integrand. This is the source of the factor T in the vorticity-action bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.norm_prim.summary: Interval length controls the time primitive norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.phaseOper.text: All coordinate derivative words of the zero vector field vanish. In the endpoint argument this carries the zero initial and terminal displacement identities to every derivative order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.phaseOper.summary: Every spatial derivative of the zero field vanishes

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.pjL.text:
The Leray projection `P` of Theorem 4.2 as an endomorphism of `C^{0,1/2}`. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): This is the fixed continuous Leray projection followed by inclusion of its solenoidal image into the ambient Hölder space. Its operator norm is carried explicitly in the estimates; no norm-one assertion is smuggled into the definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.pjL.summary: Leray projection in the spatial Hölder space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC.text:
The time primitive restricted to the parent interval. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The integral ends at the clamped time and therefore only uses the physical interval when T≥0. Integral notation remains total outside integrability hypotheses, but continuity supplies integrability in all analytic uses. The operation is used as a continuous primitive on the slab, not as a globally smooth function across the clamp endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC.summary: The time primitive restricted to the parent interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_add.text: For continuous functions on a nonnegative closed interval, the clamped time primitive distributes over addition. Continuity supplies the integrability needed for linearity of the integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_add.summary: The time primitive distributes over addition

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_con.text: On a positive time interval, the primitive of a continuous family is continuous. Only continuity on the closed physical interval is required for the tower construction.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_eq.text: At an allowed time, the clamped primitive equals the ordinary integral from zero to that time. Thus clamping changes only the auxiliary values outside the interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_eq.summary: The clamped primitive agrees with ordinary integration inside

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_smu.text: Constant scalar multiplication commutes with the clamped time primitive. This is the scalar linearity needed to construct the bilinear vorticity action.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_smu.summary: The time primitive respects constant scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift.text:
Add one label derivative to a family. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total linear reindexing by prepending a coordinate letter. It is meaningful for arbitrary families and is not by itself a differentiation theorem. Preservation of constraints and commutation are established separately from symmetry and the derivative-family hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shiftOn.text:
The derivation `∂_i` on a submodule of towers that is closed under it. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): A proof that every coordinate shift preserves the submodule is an explicit argument. The definition restricts that already-defined shift and does not infer closure or actual differentiability from the submodule alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shiftOn.summary: Restrict a derivative shift to an invariant subspace

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shiftOn_c.text: Weighted shifts commute on any shift-stable subspace of symmetric families. The proof uses permutation symmetry and multiplication of the common scalar weight, so it does not require the entries to be realized as derivatives first.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift_mem.text: Prepending one coordinate direction preserves permutation symmetry and continuity in time. Thus the shift remains inside the space of symmetric families, without yet asserting that its entries are derivatives of a field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift_mem.summary: A label shift preserves the continuous derivative family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift_mem.text: A shift of a solenoidal family whose every word has zero total time integral still has both properties. This expresses preservation of the mean endpoint and divergence constraints under differentiation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift_mem.summary: A label shift preserves the terminal displacement constraint

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt.text:
Put coordinate derivative letters in increasing order. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): Merge sort returns a canonical ordering of the finite coordinate list. It preserves multiplicities, including repeated directions and the empty word. The sorting operation is combinatorial; equality of mixed derivatives uses the separate smoothness results.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt.summary: Put coordinate derivative letters in increasing order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt_eq_of.text: Two permutation-equivalent coordinate words have identical sorted representatives. This is the combinatorial equality used when constructing a symmetric derivative family.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt_eq_of.summary: Permuted derivative words have the same sorted form

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt_perm.text: Sorting a coordinate word preserves its letters with multiplicity. This supplies a canonical representative of the derivative multi-index.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt_perm.summary: Sorting preserves the multiset of derivative directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.tower.text:
Permutation-invariant towers, continuous in time on `[0,T]`. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The submodule records permutation symmetry and continuity in time for every word. It does not require actual spatial-derivative relations. When T<0 the continuity domain is empty; applications explicitly use T≥0 or T>0 and IsDer or SymTower supplies the missing derivative interpretation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.tower.summary: Symmetric derivative families continuous in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.tower_lif.text: Apply the cited derivative estimate to endpoint families. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.tower_lif.summary: Apply the cited derivative estimate to endpoint families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.word_appl.text: A word of shift maps evaluates the family at the reversed shift word followed by the original word. Permutation symmetry later removes the reversal when passing to the derivative norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.word_appl.summary: A sequence of shifts reads the corresponding derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.word_norm.text: For a symmetric continuous family and nonnegative terminal time, the empty-word seminorm after a word of shifts equals the closed-time norm of that word's entry. This is the identification between D.3's operator notation and the concrete derivative family.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.word_norm.summary: Read the supremum after a sequence of derivative shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zeroSemi.text:
The zero-order seminorm `sup_{t ∈ [0,T]} ‖u [] t‖` on a submodule of towers. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The supplied inclusion in the continuous-family space and T≥0 make the closed-time supremum well behaved. It measures only the empty word and can vanish for a nonzero whole family. Higher-order estimates arise by shifting the family before this seminorm is applied.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zeroSemi.summary: The undifferentiated supremum seminorm of a family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zeroSemi_.text: The zero-order seminorm of a family is exactly the supremum-in-time norm of its empty-word entry. Higher words are invisible until the shifts are applied.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zero_orde.text: The first clause of the supplied Theorem 4.2 gives existence, uniqueness and a bound for the integrated endpoint problem. Applying it to the residual of any constrained family and using uniqueness yields the zero-order inverse estimate for that family, which is the hypothesis required by D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zero_orde.summary: The endpoint theorem bounds the undifferentiated velocity family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.adjL.text:
Matrix transpose as a fixed linear operator. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.

Default-value audit (b5): These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are total on the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.adjL.summary: Matrix transpose as a fixed linear operator

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.adjL_apply.text: Evaluation of the fixed continuous linear adjoint map gives the transpose of the matrix coefficient. Its operator norm is then an order-independent factor in the relay budget.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.adjL_apply.summary: Recover matrix transpose from its operator form

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.appL.text:
The application `(A, v) ↦ A v` of a field of linear maps to a field. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.

Default-value audit (b5): These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are total on the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.appL.summary: Apply a continuous linear operator to a vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.average_transve.text: The transverse source `f_p + f_p^S` of (5.27), (5.28) has zero phase mean when the means `B_i`, `2 ≤ i ≤ p`, are phase independent. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.average_transve.summary: The transverse source has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.boundedWeightSe.text: For phase-independent inverse deformation and nonvanishing covector, the actual curl completion of a zero-mean profile has the stated weighted estimate. The scalar time multiplier is only required to be bounded on the measured set; positive frequency and label/phase scales are separate assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.boundedWeightSe.summary: Transfer the divergence correction estimate to profile seminorms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.boundedWeightSe.text: If a twisted residual profile agrees on the measured time set with the explicit relay formula, D.1 and the coefficient budget bound its weighted seminorm by inverse frequency times the order n+1 seminorms of velocity and forcing. A bounded scalar time multiplier is permitted; the application uses the inverse central amplitude weight.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.boundedWeightSe.summary: Transfer the linear residual estimate to profile seminorms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.centerWaveOn_mo.text: The conditions `(5.5)` on the centre wave only weaken when the scale `D` is increased. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.centerWaveOn_mo.summary: Increasing the parent scale weakens the central wave assumptions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.text: Converse of `CoefficientNormFinite.fieldNormFinite`: if the lift `(t, a, s) ↦ c(t, a)` has finite norm (D.1) for some `ℓ > 0` and `h`, the coefficient `c` has a finite norm. The mean is measured in unweighted label norms over the entire time interval. The comparison with half-Hölder norms is where one derivative of the source is lost.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.summary: Finite lifted norms imply finite coefficient norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.text: (D.6) bounds every coefficient norm: all jet suprema of all orders are finite. Positive-order coefficient derivatives retain a factor of the envelope radius. The supremum-to-Hölder comparison uses half of that gain, leaving its square root to absorb the zero-order endpoint constant A.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.summary: Polynomial derivative estimates make coefficient norms finite

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.text: The finite norm (D.1) of a coefficient is bounded by the (5.8)-type sums of spatial suprema: if `∑_{j ≤ n} ℓ^j ‖∂^j c(t)‖_∞ ≤ S` for every `t` (and `S ≥ 0`), then `‖c‖_{[n]} ≤ (∑_{m ≤ n} #words(m)) · S`. Positive-order coefficient derivatives retain a factor of the envelope radius. The supremum-to-Hölder comparison uses half of that gain, leaving its square root to absorb the zero-order endpoint constant A.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.summary: Spatial suprema bound the sum of coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.text: The finite coefficient norm is nonnegative. The mean is measured in unweighted label norms over the entire time interval. The comparison with half-Hölder norms is where one derivative of the source is lost.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.summary: The finite coefficient norm is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientPowe.text: Operator-norm jet bounds `‖D^m c(t,x)‖ ≤ K_m 𝖣^{a(m+1)}` of a field smooth in the label give the power bound (D.6) in the form of Appendix D, with constants `#{words of order m} · K_m`. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientPowe.summary: Full derivative bounds give coordinate coefficient estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientPowe.text: (D.6) from operator-norm jet bounds with arbitrary (possibly negative) constants. The two coefficients are K=FᵀF and Ω=Fᵀ(Mᵀ−M)F, with F the deformation. Their derivative bounds are obtained by finite products of the parent coefficients before choosing the small label radius.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientPowe.summary: Replace derivative constants by nonnegative upper bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiffOn_seed.text: Smooth strain and covector with no covector zero make both the seed operator −(Id−2Pκ)M and the projection Id−Pκ jointly smooth on the given set. This supplies regularity for the parameter-dependent linear seed ODE.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiffOn_seed.summary: Nonzero transported covectors give smooth seed coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_phaseP.text: The zero-mean phase primitive of a jointly smooth family is jointly smooth. This gives the regularity needed to commute parameter derivative words with the primitive in the relay calculation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_slice.text: A velocity slice of a field smooth on the slab is smooth. Bernstein bounds the truncated parent derivatives, and the differentiated flow equation controls the deformation. Lemma D.2 supplies coefficient products, inverses and the small-radius absorption; the final absolute exponent need not be sharp.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_slice.summary: Smooth parent velocities have smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_slice'.text: A slice of a field that is jointly smooth on the slab is smooth. The completion and relay gain one inverse carrier frequency and cost one spatial derivative. The pressure and vector-potential formulas eliminate the dangerous fast derivative without differentiating the mean or the forcing in time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_slice'.summary: Joint smoothness gives smooth coefficient slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.continuousOn_in.text: Continuity of the pointwise inverse of a coframe family given by a left inverse. The first label derivatives of the parent coefficients make the fixed-plane ODE a small perturbation of its value at the origin. A common envelope exponent controls both amplitude comparison and positivity of the physical coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.continuousOn_in.summary: A given left inverse gives continuous coframe inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.crossL.text:
The cross product `κ ↦ κ × ·` as a continuous linear map of `κ`. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.

Default-value audit (b5): These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are total on the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.crossL_apply.text: Evaluation of the packaged continuous linear map gives the ordinary cross product κ×v. This identifies the fixed bilinear operation whose norm is included in the relay coefficient bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.crossL_apply.summary: Recover the cross product from its operator form

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.curlCorrection_.text: The divergence correction `C[V] = 𝐝 × Q[V]` of a profile vanishing on the inactive region vanishes there (it centres its input and acts pointwise in time and label). The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.curlCorrection_.summary: Taking the divergence correction preserves the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.deriv_leadingPr.text: The phase derivative of `𝗉[A₁]` (copy of the private `deriv_leadingPressure`, `PaperHierarchyLeadingEquation.lean:13`, for a seed in predicate form). The unswitched seed is initially available only on the active slab. A smooth extension supplies global representatives, and only their equality with the unswitched leading profiles on that slab enters Lemma 5.5.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.deriv_leadingPr.summary: Differentiate the explicit leading pressure in the phase

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeSupport.text: The support `supp g` of the periodized envelope is invariant under lattice translations. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeSupport.summary: Envelope support is invariant under lattice translations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text:
This packages the twisted extension of g(a)z(s)u(t,a) as a smooth profile of phase period one. Smoothness of both factors, phase periodicity and the fitting-radius hypothesis are supplied explicitly.

Default-value audit (b5): Positive radius and strict fitting inside the centered cell are explicit, as are global smoothness of the extension and periodicity of the phase function. The choice of extension before activation is auxiliary; only its stated active-slab agreement is later used. The constructor does not identify every off-cell value with the raw compact profile.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: Extend an amplitude times its phase profile periodically

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text: The preceding pointwise zero phase-mean identity gives zero for the bundled phase-average operator on the wrapped vector profile. This makes it admissible for the transverse solve and primitive estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: The wrapped velocity has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text: Evaluation of the packaged profile equals the chosen twisted periodization on the slab. This is an equality of representatives there, with no additional estimate or global equality outside the recorded time slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: Read the localized twisted profile at a point

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text: A zero-mean periodic phase factor makes the phase mean of the localized twisted product vanish. Translation of the phase caused by the lattice extension does not change that mean.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: The wrapped profile preserves zero phase mean

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text: If the slow field and the periodic phase function are smooth and the positive envelope fits strictly inside the centered cell, their localized twisted periodization is smooth on the profile slab. The compact label support removes boundary discrepancies between neighboring cells.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: The localized twisted extension is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.eq_of_gradient_.text: Two smooth periodic functions with the same gradient and the same mean over the label cell coincide. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.eq_of_gradient_.summary: Equal gradients and means determine the scalar function

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_A_bound.text: The arithmetic lemma bounds the expression defining the endpoint inverse constant using polynomial controls on the zeroth and first derivatives of $K$ and $\Omega$. For $D\ge2$, it absorbs the fixed leading constant and all data powers into a single exponent $C_A$, obtaining $A\le D^{C_A}$. The theorem treats the four coefficient norms as arbitrary nonnegative numbers with explicit upper bounds. The surrounding proof supplies their analytic meanings before applying this estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_A_bound.summary: Bounding the endpoint inverse constant by one power

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_KOmega_p.text: This helper derives the coefficient-power bounds for $K=(D_aX)^TD_aX$ and $\Omega=(D_aX)^T(M^T-M)D_aX$. It consumes the exact statements of Proposition 5.1 and Lemma D.2, using the latter’s product rule. The derivative constants and exponents are chosen uniformly before the parent data. These estimates serve two distinct purposes in the mean proof: bounding the endpoint inverse constant from low orders and making higher derivative coefficients small after the radius weights are inserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_KOmega_p.summary: The kinetic and vorticity coefficients have polynomial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_common_e.text: One absolute envelope exponent enforces both the fixed-coordinate Duhamel perturbation budget and the physical coupling budget. The first label derivatives of the parent coefficients make the fixed-plane ODE a small perturbation of its value at the origin. A common envelope exponent controls both amplitude comparison and positivity of the physical coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_common_e.summary: Choose an envelope satisfying both comparison requirements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_halfHold.text: A smooth periodic field on the slab is realized, at each time of `[0,T]`, by an element of `C^{0,1/2}(𝕋³; E)` (the empty word of the generic slab jets). The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_halfHold.summary: Realize each periodic slice in the Hölder space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_isSeed.text: Existence of the seed of §5.1: over a parent with launch data and a central seed (5.5), the solution `𝐚` of the seed equation (3.2) on `[t₀,T]` with the initial value (5.4) `𝐚(t₀,a) = (Id - P_{κ(t₀,a)}) 𝐚(t₀,0)` exists, is jointly smooth, transverse to `κ`, and equals the central seed at the origin. Existence and smoothness here come from the linear seed ODE with projected initial data. No small-envelope estimate or conclusion of Lemma 5.3 is assumed for this existence step.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_isSeed.summary: Solve the seed equation from its projected initial amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_launch.text: Every parent with `λ ≥ 1` admits a launch (`t₀ = 0`, `k_* ≠ 0` with `|κ(0,0)| = λ`). The mean equation itself is independent of the carrier. This auxiliary launch allows the statement of Proposition 5.1, which is packaged with launch data, to be used for the mean coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_launch.summary: Supply auxiliary launch data for any parent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_leading_.text: A smooth extension of the active seed gives smooth twisted velocity and pressure profiles on the entire slab. On the active interval they agree with A₁ and its prescribed pressure, and their phase means are zero. Their values before activation are auxiliary representatives and are not claimed to be the physical switched wave.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_leading_.summary: Represent the unswitched wave by smooth full interval profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_meanCoef.text: Finite bounds for `K`, `Ω` of (4.1) and their first label derivatives on `[0,T] × ℝ³` (continuity on the compact `[0,T] × [-1/2,1/2]³` and periodicity). Their values do not enter: Theorem 4.2 is used here only for existence. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_meanCoef.summary: Compactness bounds the mean coefficients and first derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_monotone.text: A nondecreasing coordinate word of length `m` is the word of a monotone map `Fin m → Fin 3`. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_monotone.summary: A sorted word determines a monotone coordinate sequence

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_seedOn_o.text: With the Section 5 parent, launch, central stability and first coefficient jets, one absolute radius exponent gives a library seed carrying quantitative near-origin bounds. The seed is built by the fixed-coordinate Duhamel argument, and the radius threshold controls both the ODE perturbation and the physical coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_seedOn_o.summary: Construct a seed with the required near origin bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_smoothMe.text: A solution `(B, q̄)` of (5.11) is a smooth mean solution in label coordinates (the phase-0 slices; `B = D_aX v`, `v = z_t`, `div_a v = 0`, `B_t + MB + (D_aX)^{-T}∇_a q̄ = f̄`), for the parent `par` of Theorem 4.2 with the coefficients of the flow. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_smoothMe.summary: Translate a profile solution into a smooth endpoint solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_smooth_h.text: A smooth periodic field on the slab is realized by a curve in `C^{0,1/2}` that is smooth in time (the empty word of the generic slab jets; the smooth variant of `exists_halfHolder_curve`). Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_smooth_h.summary: Realize a smooth periodic field as a smooth Hölder curve

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_sortedWo.text: Symmetry of the derivatives of a smooth function: every coordinate component `D^m f(x)(e_{β 0}, …, e_{β (m-1)})` is the value of one nondecreasing coordinate word of length `m` (the sorted word of the letters of `β`). This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_sortedWo.summary: Smoothness allows coordinate derivatives to be sorted

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_velocity.text: Given the cited Bernstein statement, this helper produces constants $V_n$ controlling the parent velocity derivatives by $V_nD^n$ for every positive order. It uses the gradient bound as the amplitude input, which avoids requiring control of the undifferentiated velocity by the same argument. Its hypotheses allow the Fourier band $4D$ and $D\ge1$, whereas the displayed parent proof uses band $2D$ and $D\ge2$. Those relaxed hypotheses explain its stronger classification.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_velocity.summary: Bernstein bounds for all positive velocity derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.expansionPressu.text: The expansion pressure to order `P` is unchanged by truncating at `P`. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion C_{P+1} is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.expansionPressu.summary: Removing unused levels leaves the pressure unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.expansion_trunc.text: The expansion to order `P` is unchanged by truncating at `P`. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion C_{P+1} is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.expansion_trunc.summary: Removing unused levels leaves the velocity unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.halfHolder_lift.text: The lift of an element of a space of torus fields is periodic. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.halfHolder_lift.summary: Lifting a torus field gives a periodic function

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.hasDerivWithinA.text: The time derivative of the leading oscillation `A₁` of a seed on `[t₀,T]`: by the seed equation (3.2), `∂_tA₁ = -MA₁ - ∂_s𝗉[A₁] κ` (the step of `leading_homogeneous`, kept as a derivative statement). The seed equation cancels the homogeneous part of the time derivative. The remaining derivative of the time cutoff is the activation error retained in the exact finite-expansion identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.hasDerivWithinA.summary: Differentiate the leading oscillation using the seed equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.holderFieldNorm.text: The finite Hölder norm is nonnegative. The mean is measured in unweighted label norms over the entire time interval. The comparison with half-Hölder norms is where one derivative of the source is lost.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.inactiveVP.text:
The inactive region `{t < t₀} ∪ {a ∉ supp g}` of the slab, as a submodule of profiles. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.

Default-value audit (b5): This is the submodule of profiles vanishing on the indicated open inactive region. Its definition does not assert that a given profile belongs to it. In particular, the means are not automatically members; the support induction proves membership only for the relevant oscillatory profiles.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.inactiveVP.summary: Profiles vanishing before activation and outside the envelope

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.innerL.text:
The inner product `(u, v) ↦ ⟪u, v⟫` as a bilinear map (the map `innerSL ℝ`). The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.

Default-value audit (b5): These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are total on the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.innerL.summary: Inner product as a fixed bilinear operator

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.innerL_apply.text: Evaluation of the fixed bilinear map gives the Euclidean inner product. It is used for the contractions in the normalized pressure and vector-potential coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.innerL_apply.summary: Recover the inner product from its bilinear form

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.integratedSolut.text: A smooth mean solution solves the integrated endpoint problem (the glue passage "(4.9) is (4.11) integrated once in time", `sections/06b_mean_inverse.tex:136-139`): for the curves `K`, `Ω` of (4.1) in `C^{0,1/2}` (smooth in time, with lifts `p.kinetic`, `p.vorticity`) and the integrated source `src` of a smooth force, the label velocity of a smooth solution of the mean equation is the velocity of a `PaperMeanIntegratedSolution`. Copy of `PaperSmoothMeanSolution.exists_integratedSolution` with `k` replaced by its four used fields. Multiplying the smooth mean equation by the transpose deformation and integrating in time gives the equation used by Theorem 4.2. The Leray projection removes the label pressure gradient; endpoint displacement supplies the zero total velocity integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.integratedSolut.summary: Integrating a smooth mean solution gives the endpoint system

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.inv_sqrt_mul_se.text: Half a radius factor remains after Hölder conversion. Positive-order coefficient derivatives retain a factor of the envelope radius. The supremum-to-Hölder comparison uses half of that gain, leaving its square root to absorb the zero-order endpoint constant A.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.inv_sqrt_mul_se.summary: Half a radius factor remains after Hölder conversion

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.isClosed_envelo.text: The periodic envelope has closed support. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.isExpansion_ide.text: The identities of Proposition 5.4 for every expansion of depth `P ≥ 2`, given the leading switch `(∂_t+M)V₁ + κ∂_s𝗉₁ = χ̃'A₁` (from (3.4) and (3.7), `06c_finite_hierarchy.tex:355-358`). Each conclusion is a clause of the identities conjunct of `Statement.proposition_5_4`, in the same order; see the module docstring for the TeX steps. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion C_{P+1} is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.isExpansion_ide.summary: The finite expansion satisfies its exact residual identity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.jetValues_nonne.text: Every derivative size in the supremum is nonnegative. The mean is measured in unweighted label norms over the entire time interval. The comparison with half-Hölder norms is where one derivative of the source is lost.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.jetValues_nonne.summary: Every derivative size in the supremum is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.kinetic_derivat.text: Along a smooth mean solution, the time derivative of Kv is expressed using the smooth momentum equation and the deformation identities. This is the differential identity subsequently integrated and projected to obtain the endpoint equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.kinetic_derivat.summary: Differentiate kinetic momentum along a mean solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelDirection_.text: The unit label directions of Appendix D are the coordinate directions. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelDirection_.summary: Unit label derivatives use the coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelLipschitz_.text: First-order power bounds for deformation, inverse deformation, strain, normalized covector and projection give uniform label differences for the coframe and generator coefficients. These bounds are supplied by the power clause of Proposition 5.1, not obtained by calling the old library's global coefficient estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelLipschitz_.summary: The parent derivative estimate gives local coefficient comparison

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelWord_eq_it.text: The value of a coordinate word is the iterated derivative on the coordinate directions of its letters. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelWord_eq_it.summary: A coordinate word evaluates the iterated Fréchet derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leadingSwitch.text: The leading velocity and pressure of any admissible expansion satisfy $(\partial_t+M)V_1+\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_1=S$. The expansion predicate fixes $S=\widetilde\chi^{\prime} A_1$ on the label cell. The proof uses the homogeneous equation for the seed and differentiates the cutoff product, including the inactive interval. The conclusion is the leading equation only; the corresponding curl-correction activation term enters the full momentum identity through the completion operator.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leadingSwitch.summary: Switching on the wave produces the cutoff forcing

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leading_homogen.text: The leading equation (3.4) for a seed in predicate form: copy of `SeedOn.paper_hierarchy_leading_homogeneous` and of `hasDerivWithinAt_leading_homogeneous_momentum` (:27), reading only the seed equation (3.2) and the transversality of `S5.IsSeed`: on `[t₀,T]`, `∂_tA₁ + MA₁ + ∂_s𝗉[A₁] κ = 0`, `κ·A₁ = 0`, and `A₁`, `𝗉[A₁]` have zero phase mean. The unswitched seed is initially available only on the active slab. A smooth extension supplies global representatives, and only their equality with the unswitched leading profiles on that slab enters Lemma 5.5.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leading_homogen.summary: The leading oscillation solves the homogeneous transverse equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leafBounds_of_h.text: The jets (D.6) of the coefficients of Proposition 5.1 (`h5_1`, with the absolute exponent `C0`) give the library form `LeafBounds` at the scale `D^{C0}`, with constants independent of the data: `K_n D^{C0 (n+1)} ≤ max(K_n,0) (D^{C0})^e` for every `e ≥ n+1` since `D ≥ 1`. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leafBounds_of_h.summary: The parent proposition supplies the seed coefficient estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.lemma55_main.text: Proposition 5.1 controls the transported coefficients, and Lemma D.1 supplies product, derivative and phase primitive bounds. Together they give the two estimates of Lemma 5.5 for arbitrary smooth twisted profiles satisfying the mean-zero, transverse and momentum hypotheses. The exponent of $\mathsf D$ is chosen independently of derivative order. This result supplies the general estimates; the separate proof of Lemma 5.5 constructs representatives of the leading oscillation and then applies its homogeneous case.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.lemma55_main.summary: Prove both inverse frequency estimates for the divergence correction

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.levelSource_tru.text: The level source of order `p ≥ 2` is unchanged by truncation. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion C_{P+1} is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.levelSource_tru.summary: Removing unused levels leaves the preliminary source unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.mFourierCoeff_c.text: Fourier coefficients commute with complex-linear maps. Copy of the private `mFourierCoeff_comp_complexCLM`, for a map into `ℂ` from the complex Euclidean space; same proof. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.mFourierCoeff_c.summary: Fourier coefficients commute with complex linear evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanHsharp_le_o.text: The coercivity (5.2) of the parent of §5.1 gives the hypothesis `H^# ≤ Id` of Theorem 4.2, by (4.3) along each trajectory `t ↦ X(t,a)`. The coercivity assumption on the parent pressure and residual is transported along the flow to the quadratic-form hypothesis of Theorem 4.2. This is the bridge that permits the endpoint inverse over the Section 5 parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanHsharp_le_o.summary: Parent pressure coercivity gives the endpoint curvature bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanInt_slice_s.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth in the label at each time of `[0,T]` (copy of the private `paperMean_slice_spatial`). Multiplying the smooth mean equation by the transpose deformation and integrating in time gives the equation used by Theorem 4.2. The Leray projection removes the label pressure gradient; endpoint displacement supplies the zero total velocity integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanInt_slice_s.summary: A smooth mean field has smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanInt_slice_t.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth in time at each label (copy of the private `paperMean_slice_time`). Multiplying the smooth mean equation by the transpose deformation and integrating in time gives the equation used by Theorem 4.2. The Leray projection removes the label pressure gradient; endpoint displacement supplies the zero total velocity integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanInt_slice_t.summary: A smooth mean field has smooth time slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanKinetic_smo.text: Joint smoothness of the kinetic coefficient `K = (D_aX)^T D_aX` of (4.1). The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanKinetic_smo.summary: The kinetic coefficient is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanParentFlow_.text: The selected parent satisfies the endpoint flow assumptions. The coercivity assumption on the parent pressure and residual is transported along the flow to the quadratic-form hypothesis of Theorem 4.2. This is the bridge that permits the endpoint inverse over the Section 5 parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanParentFlow_.summary: The selected parent satisfies the endpoint flow assumptions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanProfile_per.text: A phase-independent twisted profile is periodic in the label at fixed phase. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanProfile_per.summary: A phase independent twisted profile is spatially periodic

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSlice_contD.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth in the label at each time of `[0,T]`. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSlice_contD.summary: A smooth slab field has smooth label slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSolvable_of.text: Theorem 4.2 gives a mean solution for every phase-independent smooth forcing under the standing parent hypotheses. The proof constructs the integrated source from the transported forcing, applies the endpoint theorem to the parent deformation and vorticity coefficients, and recovers the physical mean and its normalized pressure. The result is the mean-solvability predicate used by the finite recursion. Smoothness is included in the solution profiles; uniqueness is supplied by a separate use of Theorem 4.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSolvable_of.summary: The endpoint theorem supplies the normalized mean solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanTimeSlice_c.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth in time on `[0,T]` at each label. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanTimeSlice_c.summary: A smooth slab field has smooth time slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanUnique_of_t.text: The normalized solution of the mean equation (5.11) is unique (`06d_mean_estimates.tex:3-14`), for the parent of §5.1. `h4_2` enters through the uniqueness clause of its first item: a normalized solution `(B, q̄)` of (5.11) gives (by `integratedSolution_of_smooth`, "(4.11) integrated once in time") a solution of the integrated system (4.9) with source `L = -∫_0^t (D_aX)^T f̄`, whose velocity is unique; this fixes `B = D_aX v`, then `∇_a q̄` by (5.11), and `q̄` by its normalization. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanUnique_of_t.summary: Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity and normalized pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanVorticity_s.text: Joint smoothness of the vorticity coefficient `Ω = (D_aX)^T (M^T - M) D_aX` of (4.1). The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanVorticity_s.summary: The vorticity coefficient is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.mem_inactive_of.text: A twisted profile vanishes on the inactive region as soon as it vanishes at its inactive points over the label cell (the lattice twist and the periodicity of `supp g`). The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.mem_inactive_of.summary: Vanishing on the cell extends by twisted periodicity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.momentum_eval.text: (5.11) at a point of the slab, with `B`, `q̄` replaced by their phase-0 values: `f = ∂_tB + MB + (D_aX)^{-T}∇_a q̄`. Consequently the source is independent of the phase. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.momentum_eval.summary: Evaluate the mean equation on its phase zero slice
