The declaration names an assumed proposition; it proves none of those conclusions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body54.summary: Expansion identities at a chosen radius exponent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body58.text: Names the body of Lemma 5.8 with `a`, `b`, `Γ` and the order-dependent constants `K` fixed. The expansion, parent and smallness hypotheses remain explicit. Its conclusions cover smoothness, the exact momentum residual, oscillation and mean bounds, and the residual bound containing the derivative of the time cutoff.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body58.summary: Approximate solution estimates at fixed constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body59.text: Records Lemma 5.9 at specified constants while retaining the parent, seed, expansion and smallness assumptions. It bounds the quadratic form of the natural pressure Hessian and the error in the central rank-one gradient contribution. The latter assertion is restricted to the active interval from `t₀` through `T`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body59.summary: Pressure and central gradient at fixed constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.text: Stores a torus representative of an approximate velocity, its actual Fourier cutoff, and a smooth mean-zero pressure satisfying the Poisson and projected-momentum equations. Velocity regularity, oddness, zero divergence and Fourier support are fields. Unlike `TruncatedChildStage`, this record omits the approximate-residual representation and its cutoff identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.summary: The Fourier cutoff and its Poisson pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.p.text: The cutoff child’s Euclidean velocity is spatially periodic for every real time. The proof uses equality in the unit torus after translation by an integer lattice vector. It needs no slab-membership premise because periodicity comes from the global torus representation, independently of the slab regularity fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.r.text: Defines the residual from the cutoff child’s velocity and selected pressure using `momentumResidual` on the closed slab. The time derivative is therefore taken within that slab. No residual estimate is asserted here; those estimates must be supplied when the child becomes an inductive stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.r.summary: Compute the momentum residual of the cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.v.text: Defines the velocity by composing the stored continuous torus field with `toUnitTorus`. Thus the Euclidean field is periodic at every time by construction. Its smoothness and equation properties on the closed slab come from the record; this definition does not extend those properties to other times.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.v.summary: Lift the cutoff velocity to Euclidean space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.v.text: Expresses the child velocity as the real vector Fourier cutoff of its stored approximate torus field, lifted back to Euclidean space. This equality holds at every time by the record’s `cutoff` field. Agreement of that representative with the original approximate velocity is separately restricted to the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.v.summary: Identify the lifted velocity with the Fourier cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: Constructs an `InductiveEulerStage` from a cutoff child and explicit velocity, flow, residual and pressure bounds. Equalities `hSlab` and `hRadius` identify its time interval and Fourier radius with the schedule. The stored velocity and pressure are preserved; the residual bound is rewritten into the stage’s inverse-cube notation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: Turn the cutoff child into an inductive stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: The stage assembled from a cutoff child has the same pressure function as that child. All bounds needed to construct the stage remain hypotheses; this theorem adds no pressure estimate. Its purpose is to transport the actual Poisson pressure and its Hessian bounds through the record constructor.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: The assembled stage preserves its pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: Under exactly the hypotheses of `InductiveEulerStage.ofCutoffChild`, its velocity equals the cutoff child’s lifted velocity. Substituting the slab and Fourier-radius equalities makes the result reflexive. This identity allows estimates proved for the child field to be used for the new indexed stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: The assembled stage preserves its velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: Builds a complete later step from a certified prefix, an actual later-wave selection and its cutoff child. The prefix supplies the accumulated first-coupling estimate; the crossing supplies strength and ratio information. The step uses the same child and wave throughout, preserving their quantitative and geometric identities.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: Extend the certified prefix with the constructed child

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: For a growing crossing and a child decomposed as approximate velocity plus tail, adds the tail’s first spatial derivative to the central error. The assumed second-order tail bound and scheduled frequency relations improve the combined estimate to the inverse quarter power of the child frequency. The cutoff-weighted rank-one contribution is preserved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: Add the Fourier tail to the central gradient error

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: Constructs an `InductiveEulerWave` using the supplied crossing, cutoff child and quantitative hypotheses. It stores the actual amplitude, wave vector, smooth switch and corrected central error, then proves the crossing ratio and completed-cutoff clauses. The hypotheses tie the child velocity to the same cutoff field used in every error estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: Attach the actual crossing to the cutoff child

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.LocalStep.text: Asserts existence of the parent geometry, seed, cutoff and finite expansion that connect a specified parent stage, child stage and wave. The clauses include actual graph-read oscillation, truncation and approximate-residual identities. This is local data for already supplied stages; it does not by itself choose an infinite construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.LocalStep.summary: Record the parent and expansion for one step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.StepApproxBou.text: Collects four properties of the supplied approximate fields: full-depth velocity size, residual size, oscillation size and low-order mean bounds. It is a proposition about existing velocities, not their construction. In particular, it contains no pressure-Hessian field; the child pressure is controlled later using Proposition 5.11.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.StepApproxBou.summary: The approximation estimates needed by one step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.StepNumbers.text: Records the numerical conditions needed to apply the Section 5 statements at parent index `i`: flow smallness, residual decay, tail constants, parent jets, oscillation constants and mean bounds. The full-depth order is determined by `P.order (i + 2)`. This proposition concerns constants and frequencies, not existence of any velocity field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.StepNumbers.summary: The numerical inequalities consumed by one step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.TailBounds.text: Defines a uniform family of tail estimates for every `CutoffChild`: if the approximate velocity has Hölder regularity at order `M`, then its difference from the cutoff child has each lower order `m ≤ M`, with the usual factor $\Lambda^{m-M}$. The constants `Ct` are supplied, not constructed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.TailBounds.summary: All lower order errors of a Fourier cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.abs_le_orderM.text: For an order satisfying `hP : P ≤ 7 * frequencyExponent b s`, bounds its absolute constant by the finite majorant. The proof uses nonnegativity of every summand. It supplies the elementary domination needed when the construction chooses one threshold for many expansion orders.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.abs_log_le_of.text: If $|u-1|\le\varepsilon\le1/2$, then $|\log u|\le2\varepsilon$. The assumptions imply `u ≥ 1/2`, so the logarithm is controlled away from zero. This turns a relative estimate for the new first coupling into the logarithmic increment that is summed over successive crossings.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.abs_log_le_of.summary: Convert a small relative change to a logarithmic bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.activation_lt.text: Assuming `Theorem71Conclusions`, proves that every activation time is strictly below the limit `T`. Monotonicity and convergence first give a weak upper bound; comparison with a later strictly larger activation makes it strict. The low indices require a separate comparison with the third activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.activation_lt.summary: Every activation precedes the accumulation time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.activation_mo.text: Extracts monotonicity of the whole activation sequence from `h71 : Theorem71Conclusions c C T`. The first two physical activation times coincide at zero, and the unused index zero is also zero. Strict growth is only supplied from index two onward, so the global conclusion is monotonicity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.affineWave_ex.text: Given a continuous matrix field and nonzero perpendicular initial wave vector and amplitude, constructs solutions of the wave ODEs on the closed interval and preserves both nonvanishing and orthogonality. No Euler condition on the matrix field is assumed. This permits an approximate parent gradient, for which the affine Euler hypotheses need not hold.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.affineWave_ex.summary: Solve the wave equations over a continuous gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.average_expan.text: For an expansion satisfying `S5.IsExpansion`, and assuming its first velocity level has zero phase average, proves that the whole expansion averages to the sum of mean terms from level two through `P`. Higher transverse profiles and curl corrections have zero mean, while the mean profiles are phase independent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.average_expan.summary: The phase average is exactly the mean correction

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.average_first.text: Proves zero phase average of the first velocity level from the actual expansion and seed data. The launch hypothesis, positive radius and phase width, and fit of the envelope inside the fundamental cell are retained. The proof identifies this level with the leading velocity profile, whose phase factor has mean zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.average_first.summary: The leading oscillation has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.band_mono.text: A continuous torus field supported at frequencies at most `D` also satisfies the support predicate for any larger cutoff `D′`. The proof simply restricts the vanishing requirement to fewer Fourier modes. No smoothness or positivity hypothesis is needed for this monotonicity statement.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.base_gradient.text: Adds the first spatial derivative of the actual cutoff tail to the approximate central error when the first cutoff is identically one. Differentiability, second-order tail control and the approximate gradient estimate are explicit premises. Large current frequency and a nondecreasing next frequency bound the new error by the inverse quarter power.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.base_gradient.summary: The first child has the required central gradient splitting

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.bernstein_all.text: From the assumed Lemma B.1, obtains nonnegative constants `K m` bounding the full $m$th derivative of a smooth periodic lift with frequencies at most $4D$. The conclusion is $K_m A D^m$ when the torus sup norm is at most `A`. The factor $3^m$ converts coordinate estimates to operator norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.bernstein_all.summary: Bernstein bounds for the full spatial derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.centerWaveOn_.text: From the assumed Lemma 2.6 and a growing crossing, proves `CenterWaveOn` whenever `D` dominates the transverse transfer constant and inverse coupling lower bound. The proof uses the transfer operator on every transverse solution and cancels the positive seed scaling. The crossing record supplies nonvanishing, orthogonality and the coupling estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.centerWaveOn_.summary: Transfer comparison bounds to the central seed hypotheses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.centerWaveOn_.text: Converts `Lemma61Conclusions` for an existing first wave into `CenterWaveOn` for the stationary shear gradient, for positive frequency and any `D ≥ 2`. The propagation estimate’s normalization factor is canceled using nonvanishing amplitude, and the normalized coupling estimate becomes the required unnormalized inner-product lower bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.centerWaveOn_.summary: The first wave satisfies the central seed requirements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.clock_mem_act.text: For any normalized time in `[0,T]`, its physical clock value belongs to the active slab. Strict monotonicity of the clock supplies both endpoints. This is the converse domain conversion needed when applying the comparison results and when transferring peak-amplitude statements to physical time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.clock_mem_act.summary: Return normalized time to the active interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.complete_eq_z.text: If a twisted vector profile vanishes on an entire time slice, its divergence-correcting completion also vanishes on that slice. The covector is phase independent and nonzero, and the time lies in a positive slab. The proof first removes the zero phase average, then applies the completion’s slice identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.complete_eq_z.summary: A vanishing profile has a vanishing completion

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.conclusions_o.text: From an actual construction, the prescribed stationary base and cutoff formulas, and the initial-frequency floor, obtains the full `Theorem71Conclusions` bundle for some accumulation time. Most clauses come from stage and wave fields. The additional eventual-comparison clause uses the supplied Lemmas 1.3, 2.2 and B.1; it is not merely a projection.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.conclusions_o.summary: Export the quantitative conclusions and common lifetime

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.contDiff_slic.text: A function jointly smooth on a closed time slab is smooth in space at each time belonging to the slab. The target can be any real normed space. The proof composes with the smooth map sending a spatial point to the fixed-time pair, so no time-interior assumption is needed.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.continuousOn_.text: The cross product of two continuous three-dimensional vector functions is continuous on the same time set. The proof expands its three coordinates into products and differences. Combined with normalized wave directions, this proves continuity of the third coupling used to locate the next activation.

For a physical amplification window on a closed interval, its gradient is continuous there. The proof combines continuity of the older gradient and error with the rank-one term formed by the preceding wave pair. Their derivative equations supply continuity of that pair; no differentiability of the error is required.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.continuousOn_.summary: The later-wave background gradient is continuous

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.continuousOn_.text: Normalizing a vector-valued function preserves continuity on a set if the function is continuous there and never vanishes there. Nonvanishing is required explicitly because normalization divides by the norm. The result helps prove continuity of the physical coupling ratio before selecting its least crossing.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.continuousOn_.summary: A nonzero continuous vector has a continuous direction

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.deformationOn.text: A deformation estimate with constant `C` remains valid with any `C′ ≥ C`. The underlying flow equations and lattice compatibility are preserved; only the two derivative-norm bounds are weakened. This permits the construction to replace an analytic estimate by the larger scheduled frequency bound.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.deformation_o.text: Applies the supplied flow-existence clause `h510` to the correction `s.velocity - V`. Smoothness, periodicity and zero divergence follow from the cutoff child and approximate field; the two-derivative size bound is an explicit premise. Since adding this correction recovers the child exactly, the resulting deformation estimate concerns the actual child velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.deformation_o.summary: Apply the flow estimate to the actual cutoff correction

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.derivativeSiz.text: Assuming a nonempty active interval and nonnegative weight `γ` there, transfers a global pointwise bound on $|\widetilde\chi'|\,|\gamma|$ to `PaperWaveCutoff.derivativeSize γ`. The proof identifies the within-slab derivative and applies the conditional supremum bound. It does not derive the smallness of the switch.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.derivativeSiz.summary: A pointwise switch bound controls its weighted supremum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.divergence_su.text: At a point where both vector fields are differentiable, the divergence of their difference equals the difference of their divergences. The assumptions matter because `fderiv` is a total operation in Lean. This identity shows that the cutoff correction is divergence free when both the child and approximate velocity are.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.divergence_su.summary: Divergence distributes over a differentiable difference

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.elapsed_mem_I.text: If physical time lies between `w.clock a` and `w.clock b`, its normalized elapsed time lies between `a` and `b`. The physical amplification record supplies a strictly increasing clock with an inverse. This elementary conversion is used to carry comparison and crossing estimates between the two time coordinates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.elapsed_mem_I.summary: Convert a clock interval to normalized time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.elapsed_mem_a.text: A time in the physical active slab maps under `elapsed` into the normalized interval from zero to `T`. This specializes the general clock-interval conversion and uses that the clock at zero is activation time. It carries physical amplitudes into the domain of the comparison lemmas.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.eventually_lo.text: States that $(\log x)^6\le x^{1/16}$ for all sufficiently large real `x`. The conclusion is eventual, with no explicit numerical threshold. It follows from the logarithm’s little-o estimate and is used to turn the schedule’s logarithmic gain into a decaying time-length bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.eventually_lo.summary: A power eventually dominates the sixth logarithmic power

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_admiss.text: For arbitrary `b` and real-valued majorant `F`, constructs an admissible threshold by summing $|F(t)|$ plus the exponential floor through index `s`. Every summand is positive. The partial sums are nondecreasing, dominate `F`, and satisfy the logarithmic floor, showing that the universal threshold clause used in Section 8 has witnesses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_admiss.summary: Construct an admissible threshold above any majorant

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_base_o.text: Constructs the base stage, first child and first wave from the assumed Lemma 6.1 and fixed Section 5 statements, together with the parent, jet, tail and numerical hypotheses. The base velocity is the prescribed stationary shear, and its first cutoff is identically one. No preactivation-vanishing requirement is imposed on this first oscillation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_base_o.summary: Start the induction with the stationary shear and first wave

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_child_.text: Applies the fixed-constant forms of Lemmas 5.8–5.10 and Proposition 5.11 to a specified parent, seed and expansion. With the numerical and tail hypotheses, constructs a cutoff child and next stage, preserving velocity and pressure identities and exporting approximation, truncation, increment and central-error data. Expansion existence itself is an input here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_child_.summary: Build the child from the fixed Section five statements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_constr.text: Given a base with local Section 5 data and an extension for every certified finite prefix, constructs one infinite sequence using classical choice. It preserves the supplied base, the local data of every chosen step, and the actual smooth-switch formula for later cutoffs. Extension availability is a premise, not hidden in the choice.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_constr.summary: Choose one infinite sequence from the local extensions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_cutoff.text: Builds a `CutoffChild` from a smooth periodic approximate velocity, existence of a truncation, and the first regularity and Fourier-support conclusions of Proposition 5.11 supplied as `hT1`. It constructs a smooth mean-zero Poisson pressure and the projected-momentum identity. Residual bounds are not among the inputs or outputs of this constructor.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_cutoff.summary: Construct the cutoff child from truncation conclusions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_freque.text: Chooses an initial-frequency threshold ensuring finite smallness for every later physical window with the stated strength, coupling, older-gradient and error bounds. Its output also places the entire crossing search in the first half of the interval. The schedule’s logarithmic control is explicit; no crossing or wave is constructed by this numerical lemma.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_freque.summary: The scheduled window satisfies comparison and crossing requirements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_freque.text: Assuming the listed Section 2 statements, constructs a `LaterWaveSelection` from an actual `LaterPhysicalWindow` and scheduled older-gradient, error, coupling and strength bounds. It combines the comparison window, least crossing, peak normalization and central seed estimates. The selected crossing occurs strictly after activation and no later than one half length afterward.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_freque.summary: Select a later wave over the actual parent gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_growin.text: Assuming Lemmas 2.5 and 2.7 and Proposition 2.8, builds a peak-normalized growing wave with a least coupling-ratio crossing in the prescribed bracket. Positive scale and peak, finite smallness, the next-ratio bound and a long enough window remain premises. The reference turning time is identified through its zero characterization, not assumed equal to a second chosen time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_growin.summary: Construct the growing wave and its least crossing

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_induct.text: Constructs an inductive child with exactly the cutoff velocity and pressure, assuming the actual residual and pressure-increment estimates, approximation bounds, tail bounds and flow clause. It derives the smaller correction and oscillation estimates at the scheduled scale. The residual bound concerns `s.residual`, so a small unrelated error field cannot replace it.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_induct.summary: The quantitative cutoff becomes the next inductive stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_induct.text: From Lemma B.1, Lemma 1.3 and the cited Section 2 results, chooses comparison and initial-frequency thresholds uniformly for all tips. A tip with lifetime bounds and matching constants then admits an actual later physical window and wave selection. The older-gradient estimates, current coupling ratio and strength bounds are extracted from the existing stages and wave.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_induct.summary: Every sufficiently large tip admits the next wave

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_induct.text: Assuming Lemma B.1, finds a large-frequency threshold so every tip with lifetime bounds supplies its older stage’s central gradient estimates on the next wave’s comparison interval. The proof verifies that this interval fits inside the older slab, and uses the actual residual and smoothness of that older stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_induct.summary: An inductive tip supplies the older gradient estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_induct.text: Assuming Lemma 1.3 and a fixed strength constant at least two, chooses a frequency threshold giving the weighted derivative bound for any later-wave selection at a tip. The estimate holds for every real time. It combines early amplitude gain, the physical rate bound and compact support of the switch derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_induct.summary: The weighted switching derivative is small at every tip

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_lifeti.text: Assuming Lemma 1.3, chooses one initial-frequency threshold such that every parameter record above it satisfies `LifetimeBounds`. Besides the geometric half-length estimates, it ensures the first half length is at most one quarter. The logarithmic inequality is obtained by applying the supplied `h1_3` to the record.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_lifeti.summary: Large initial frequency gives all lifetime bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_monoto.text: An element of `appendixCoefficientOrderWords m` has exactly length `m` and nondecreasing letters. This theorem represents it by a monotone map from `Fin m` to the three coordinates. It supplies the form expected by the coordinate version of Bernstein’s inequality, without any analytic hypothesis.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_parame.text: Assuming Lemma 1.3 and positive threshold values satisfying the logarithmic floor, constructs parameter records for every sufficiently large initial frequency. The prescribed exponents, comparison constant, strength constant and threshold are retained exactly. The output also exceeds an arbitrary extra floor `N₀` and carries the lifetime bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_parame.summary: Choose a schedule with the specified threshold

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_sorted.text: For any ordered tuple of coordinate directions, finds a nondecreasing word giving the same iterated derivative of the smooth function at every point. The witness is the sorted list of directions. Symmetry of constant-direction derivatives makes sorting legitimate, so the restricted word family still controls all components.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_sorted.summary: Derivative symmetry allows sorted coordinate words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_step_o.text: Given a certified prefix and selected later wave, uses Proposition 5.4 to obtain its seed and expansion and the fixed Section 5 bounds to construct the child. The carrier is transported through the actual parent flow. Support and vanishing are proved for the graph-read oscillation, and the output retains the exact smooth-switch cutoff formula.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_step_o.summary: Complete one later step with its local expansion data

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_veloci.text: Assuming Lemma B.1, produces constants depending only on the requested order `N`. For any stage with frequency at least one, all spatial derivatives through order `N + 1` are bounded by $C_N\mu^{5(N+1)+1}$ on its slab. The stage’s Fourier support and velocity bound supply the Bernstein inputs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.exists_veloci.summary: Uniform derivative bounds for every parent stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.graphRead_sub.text: Evaluating the difference of two twisted profiles along the same physical graph equals the difference of their evaluations. The equality is pointwise in time and space and holds by definition. It lets the mean and oscillatory decomposition of a profile become a decomposition of the physical velocity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.halfLength_bo.text: For sufficiently large initial frequency, proves positivity of every half length, its bound by the parent frequency to power $-1/16$, and a factor-four decrease at the next step. The recurrence and logarithmic bound are explicit hypotheses. The latter is not recovered by calling a separate proof of Lemma 1.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.halfLength_bo.summary: Half lengths shrink geometrically along the schedule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.hessian_split.text: For smooth scalar functions `p` and `q`, writes the Hessian of `p` as the Hessian of `p - q` plus that of `q`. Both smoothness assumptions are explicit. This turns the pressure-increment bound from Proposition 5.11 into the accumulated pressure inequality for the next stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.hessian_split.summary: Split the child pressure Hessian into two terms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.holderNorm_no.text: For any function into a real normed space, proves nonnegativity of `spatialHolderHalfNorm m f`. The assertion follows from nonnegative norm values and Hölder quotients, and does not require a regularity hypothesis. It is only a sign statement about the total encoding, not evidence that the analytic Hölder norm is finite.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.holderNorm_no.summary: The encoded Hölder norm is always nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.isTruncation_.text: Shows that a `CutoffChild` is an `S5.IsTruncation` of its approximate velocity. The proof uses uniqueness of a torus field with the given Euclidean lift, then projects the pressure smoothness, periodicity, zero mean and Poisson equation. This is what permits Proposition 5.11 to be applied to the constructed child.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.isTruncation_.summary: The cutoff record satisfies the paper truncation predicate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.labelDirectio.text: Identifies `hierarchyLabelDirection 1` with the constant coordinate-direction fields. The equality concerns the vector fields themselves, at every label point. It allows the hierarchy word notation at unit scale to be read as ordinary repeated coordinate differentiation in the Bernstein argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.labelDirectio.summary: Unit label directions are ordinary coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.labelWord_eq_.text: For a smooth function `f`, identifies a word of unit label derivatives with its iterated Fréchet derivative evaluated on the coordinate directions listed by that word. The list length supplies the derivative order. This is a change of notation, with smoothness needed for the derivative identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.labelWord_eq_.summary: A coordinate word evaluates the full derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.laterPhysical.text: If the physical interval ends two half lengths after activation, then normalized length `2 * rate * halfTime` maps exactly to that endpoint. The positive rate stored in the amplification record makes division valid. Monotonicity then shows that the whole normalized interval maps into the physical interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.laterPhysical.summary: The normalized window ends at the physical final time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.laterWindow_g.text: For the given frequency recurrence and maximal order rule, proves that the two gains used by a later wave satisfy a factor-640 separation and a logarithmic upper bound. The logarithmic inequality is supplied as `hLog`. The indices are relative to the older velocity, so the gains lie three and four frequency indices ahead.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.laterWindow_g.summary: The scheduled gains are separated and logarithmically bounded

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.later_cutoff_.text: Assuming that each later cutoff equals its stored `waveSwitch`, rewrites it using the preceding wave’s strength and first coupling. The rate becomes the square root of twice their product. The result includes the separate zero branch before activation and the envelope-cutoff formula afterward, with the paper’s shifted indices.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.later_cutoff_.summary: Recover the paper formula for every later cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.lemma13_sched.text: Applies the assumed statement `h13` of Lemma 1.3 to the schedule stored in `P`. It returns divergence of the derivative orders and the logarithmic frequency inequality, with the paper index shifted by one. This declaration does not call the library proof of Lemma 1.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.lemma13_sched.summary: Slow orders and the logarithmic schedule estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.norm_linearMa.text: If a continuous linear map sends each coordinate direction to a vector of norm at most a nonnegative `M`, its operator norm is at most $3M$. The explicit factor three is the number of spatial coordinates. This supplies a concrete constant when derivative estimates are expressed coordinatewise.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.norm_linearMa.summary: Three coordinate bounds control a linear map

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.ofFnWord_eq_i.text: Converts a tuple `β : Fin m → Fin 3` into the list `List.ofFn β` and identifies the resulting coordinate word with the $m$th derivative evaluated on that tuple. Smoothness of `f` is a premise. The remaining work reconciles the list length with the prescribed natural number `m`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.ofFnWord_eq_i.summary: Indexed directions and words give the same derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.older_central.text: From Lemma B.1 and the projected-momentum hypotheses, obtains a uniform threshold for the central gradient and its time derivative. On any contained interval, the derivative within the original slab is also a derivative within the smaller interval. The bounds are powers nine and eighteen of the older frequency.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.older_central.summary: Restrict the older gradient estimates to a comparison interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.opNorm_le_coo.text: Bounds the operator norm of an $m$-linear map by the sum of its values on all coordinate-direction tuples. The target `X` is any real normed space. Expanding each input vector and using multilinearity gives the estimate needed to convert coordinate Bernstein bounds into full derivative bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.opNorm_le_coo.summary: Control a multilinear norm by coordinate values

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.orderMajorant.text: Defines the finite sum of $|\Gamma_0(P)|$ for $0\le P\le7K(s)$. The order bound is inclusive because the range ends at $7K(s)+1$. This scalar helper lets an admissible threshold control every constant used at a step, without assuming that the original constants are positive.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.orderMajorant.summary: A majorant for all required expansion orders

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.osc_profile_v.text: For an expansion whose cutoff is zero at activation, proves that its oscillatory profile vanishes on the whole closed interval before activation. Earlier-time vanishing and the sum identity are explicit inputs. At positive activation it uses continuity; at zero it uses the leading cutoff and the transverse profiles’ initial data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.osc_profile_v.summary: The oscillation vanishes through the activation endpoint

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.osc_support.text: A profile vanishing outside the periodic label envelope has graph-read support within inverse parent frequency of some lattice point, on the child slab. The parent flow fixes the origin and has controlled deformation; the radius satisfies the stated cubic inverse-scale bound. On the torus, this is support near the origin.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.osc_support.summary: The physical oscillation stays near a lattice point

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.paperCutoffOf.text: Packages `waveSwitch t₀ r` as a `PaperWaveCutoff`, proving smoothness, values between zero and one, and vanishing before activation. Only nonnegativity of the rate is required, so a zero rate is allowed. This declaration does not assert that the switch eventually reaches one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.paperCutoffOf.summary: Use the smooth switch as the paper cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.paperCutoffOf.text: On a nondegenerate closed slab, the derivative stored by `PaperWaveCutoff` agrees with the ordinary derivative of the smooth switch. The premise `hT : 0 < T` gives uniqueness of derivatives within the interval, including its endpoints. This identity permits pointwise switch estimates to control the paper’s derivative norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.paperCutoffOf.summary: The slab derivative equals the ordinary switch derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalEta_s.text: The third physical coupling is unchanged when the amplitude is multiplied by a positive scalar. Both normalized directions occurring in its cross-product formula remain the same. Together with the corresponding first-coupling identity, this preserves the coupling ratio and the selected crossing after peak normalization.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalEta_s.summary: Positive amplitude rescaling preserves the third coupling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalNu_sm.text: Multiplying the new wave amplitude by a positive constant leaves its normalized direction and therefore its first physical coupling unchanged. The wave vector is held fixed. This is why normalizing the amplitude to the required peak does not alter the first-coupling estimates established for the unscaled seed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalNu_sm.summary: Positive amplitude rescaling preserves the first coupling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalWaveA.text: Builds `StepApproxBounds` from the parent’s Bernstein jets, the actual velocity split, and the oscillation and mean estimates of Lemma 5.8. Its name does not mean that it derives every field from that lemma alone: the required residual estimate is supplied separately as `hRes`, and pressure estimates are absent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalWaveA.summary: Collect the approximation estimates from the supplied bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalWave_.text: Rewrites the next frequency as the parent frequency raised first to the current exponent and then to the next exponent. The equality follows by applying `P.frequency_step` twice. It aligns the local formulas for cutoff and residual decay with the frequencies stored in the inductive parameter record.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalWave_.summary: Expand the next frequency through two recurrence steps

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalWave_.text: Assuming the initial frequency is at least two, obtains the corresponding parent-frequency lower bound, monotonicity of the two adjacent derivative orders, and a depth at least `max 2 order`. The depth is six times the next frequency exponent. These are the index inequalities needed to apply the expansion and cutoff estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.physicalWave_.summary: The scheduled depth covers every required lower order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.profile_zero_.text: A smooth profile vanishing at all earlier nonnegative times also vanishes at its activation time, provided that time is strictly positive and belongs to the slab. The proof takes the left-hand limit. The strict positivity premise is essential; activation at zero is handled separately using initial data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.profile_zero_.summary: Continuity closes vanishing at positive activation time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.projectedMome.text: Assuming Lemma B.1, constructs torus representatives for the advection and residual of a smooth periodic velocity satisfying the projected-momentum identity. The Fourier support and size hypotheses yield gradient and time-gradient bounds with powers nine and eighteen, plus a derivative estimate for the residual. All conclusions concern the closed slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.projectedMome.summary: Derive the parent gradient and residual bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.residual_size.text: Combines the depth identity `nxt = lam^K`, a weighted cutoff derivative bound, and two numerical rate inequalities. It converts the expansion term at depth `6K` to `nxt^(-4)` and concludes that the full residual-bound expression is at most `nxt^(-7/2)`. The analytic residual identity is not part of this arithmetic lemma.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.residual_size.summary: Both residual terms reach the next frequency scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.scheduled_T2_.text: Combines bounds for the parent, oscillation, remaining increment, child flow, true residual and pressure increment to prove the next stage’s velocity, deformation, residual and cumulative pressure bounds. The pressure estimate is supplied directly as `hPress57`; it is not inferred from an omitted approximate-pressure bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.scheduled_T2_.summary: Close the velocity residual and pressure inequalities

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.scheduled_bou.text: Starting with the actual cutoff child and the slab-norm clauses of Proposition 5.11 supplied as `hE`, `hC3` and `h57`, produces pointwise-in-time residual, pressure-error, second-order velocity-tail and pressure-increment estimates. It controls the slab suprema using the assumed full-depth velocity and residual bounds; it does not substitute a slice norm for a slab norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.scheduled_bou.summary: Convert slab estimates into scheduled child bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.scheduled_inc.text: For a cutoff child, combines the assumed tail estimates, the split `V = parent + osc + mean`, and the scheduled mean and tail-size bounds. The result is Hölder control through order `q` of the child increment after removing the oscillation, at size equal to the inverse child frequency.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.scheduled_res.text: Under `f ≥ 1`, `K ≥ 0`, `2K ≤ f` and `f² ≤ g`, bounds $Kf^5g^{-3}$ by one half. The proof compares the inverse cube of `g` with the inverse sixth power of `f`. This is the numerical part of controlling the residual derivative in the endpoint coercivity condition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.scheduled_res.summary: The residual derivative fits the coercivity allowance

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.spatialHolder.text: If `f` has spatial Hölder regularity at order `m`, its negative has the same regularity and exactly the same encoded norm. The proof checks the derivative suprema and Hölder quotients. This reverses the sign of the Fourier-tail difference without changing its estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split510.text: Separates the assumed Lemma 5.10 into thresholds for `a` and `b` and a lower coefficient family `Γ₀`. It preserves the statement’s freedom to enlarge the coefficients. The equality of types is definitional, so this theorem reorganizes the input hypothesis for later application to a truncation error.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split510.summary: Expose the constants in the flow estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split511.text: Given Proposition 5.11 and a symbol satisfying `S5.CutoffSymbol`, extracts the exponent thresholds and constant families required by `Body511`. The scalar `C` and family `K` stay fixed while `b` and `Γ` may be enlarged. This is a definitional view of the assumed statement.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split511.summary: Expose the constants for the chosen Fourier cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split54.text: Rewrites the assumed statement of Proposition 5.4 as existence of a lower bound `a₀` such that `Body54 a` holds for every larger radius exponent. The proof is the input `h` itself because the types are definitionally equal. It supplies a common exponent without proving Proposition 5.4 anew.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split54.summary: Separate the radius exponent from expansion identities

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split58.text: Unpacks the assumed Lemma 5.8 into a radius threshold, then a frequency exponent threshold and constant families. The resulting estimates hold for every larger exponent and every coefficient family dominating `Γ₀`. The original `K` remains fixed. This is definitional reshaping for the common cost table.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split58.summary: Expose the constants in the approximate estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split59.text: Reads the assumed Lemma 5.9 as a family `Body59 a b Γ` after its existential constants have been separated. Increasing `b` and replacing `Γ₀` by a dominating family are part of the statement. The proof is the original hypothesis, so no pressure estimate is derived independently here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.split59.summary: Expose the constants in the pressure estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stage_frequen.text: For a parameter record whose initial frequency is at least four, every frequency exceeds the initial one, every next frequency is at least twice the current one, and every next frequency is at least its square. These elementary growth estimates support the parent coercivity and summability arguments.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stage_frequen.summary: The scheduled frequencies grow at least quadratically

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stage_parent.text: Assuming Lemma B.1, finds a uniform initial-frequency threshold making every inductive stage a valid Section 5 parent on any positive shorter slab with `T ≤ 1`. The parent scale is the ninth power of its frequency. The proof checks actual residual restriction, Fourier support, deformation and the pressure-minus-residual coercivity inequality.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stage_parent.summary: Every large stage supplies the next parent hypotheses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stepNumbers_o.text: Turns a scheduled numerical budget into `StepNumbers`, provided the cost table dominates the analytic, cutoff and mean constants. The coefficient identity `hΓc` identifies the step constant family; positivity assumptions are retained where needed. The resulting mean constant is the parent frequency, while the step constant is $\Gamma D^b$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stepNumbers_o.summary: Extract step inequalities from the common cost table

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stepNumerical.text: For a parameter record whose threshold dominates the fixed-order cost table, builds the numerical budget at every index. The exponent floor, initial-frequency floor and lower bound on the step coefficient are explicit premises. Domination is sufficient: the record’s threshold need not equal the fixed-order majorant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stepNumerical.summary: One dominating threshold pays every step estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stepSmall_of_.text: If the frequency is at least one and `C ≤ freq^(1/32)`, then `C * freq^(-1/12) ≤ 1`. Multiplication by the positive inverse power and addition of exponents give the claim. A nonnegativity assumption on `C` is unnecessary for this upper-bound implication.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.stepSmall_of_.summary: The scheduled constant satisfies the expansion smallness condition

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.steps_of_loca.text: Given a construction `c`, local data for its base step and local data for every selected later step, proves `Theorem71Steps c a ψ`. Index one reads the base; indices `n + 2` read the selected step. The proof only rearranges existing witnesses and preserves their fields.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.steps_of_loca.summary: Assemble every local step into the sequence

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.sum_coordinat.text: Writes a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ as the finite sum of its coordinates multiplied by the three coordinate directions. This is ordinary coordinate algebra. It is used to convert bounds on coordinate derivatives into bounds on continuous linear and multilinear derivative operators.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.tailTwo_of_ta.text: For expansion depth at least two, specializes the assumed tail estimates to order two and bounds the norm factor by its shifted square. The result uses `Ct * truncErr`. The cutoff scale and constant sign are explicit hypotheses; the analytic tail estimate itself is assumed in `hTails`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.tailTwo_of_ta.summary: Express the second derivative tail with the common error parameter

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.tails_of_lemm.text: For a fixed admissible Fourier symbol, the supplied Lemma B.1 gives nonnegative constants controlling every lower-order cutoff error. The approximate field must have Hölder regularity at the higher order, and the cutoff scale must be positive. The proof changes the sign of the paper’s tail and identifies the actual child velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.tails_of_lemm.summary: Obtain all cutoff tails from the assumed lemma

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.threeHundredT.text: If `b ≥ 1`, then $K(q)=320b(q+1)$ is at least 320 for every natural order `q`. The proof is multiplication of natural-number inequalities. This elementary floor ensures the large separation between successive frequencies used in the lifetime and parent estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.threeHundredT.summary: Every frequency exponent exceeds the fixed floor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.truncErr.text: Defines the scalar $\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V(t)\|_{P,1/2})^2$ used for one time slice of the cutoff error. The exponent on the cutoff scale is an integer exponent, so orders above two give inverse powers. This definition itself contains no regularity, positivity or error estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.truncErr.summary: The Fourier tail parameter on one time slice

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.truncErr_le_n.text: Assuming the scheduled relation between parent, child and next frequencies, a full-depth Hölder bound on `V`, and `K ≤ μ`, bounds `K * truncErr` by the next frequency to the power $-5$. The premise `hV` gives genuine Hölder regularity, which is used to justify nonnegativity of the norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.truncErr_le_n.summary: The Fourier tail reaches the next frequency scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.twisted_sum_a.text: Evaluating a finite sum of twisted profiles at a time-label-phase point gives the sum of their evaluations. The proof inducts over the finite index set. It is algebraic and holds without slab-membership assumptions, making the expansion’s pointwise vanishing reducible to vanishing of each term.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.twisted_sum_a.summary: Evaluate a finite sum of twisted profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.two_le_freque.text: Every `InductiveEulerParameters` record has initial frequency at least two. The argument combines the stored exponential floor for the threshold at index one with `initial_threshold`. No separate largeness premise is needed here because those numerical requirements are already fields of the parameter record.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.unit_amplitud.text: Dividing a crossing amplitude by its positive stored seed factor recovers an amplitude vector with the unscaled growing initial direction. The wave vector still has the required initial scale and ODE. This identity supplies the exact input form expected by Lemma 2.6 before its transfer estimate is rescaled back.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.unit_amplitud.summary: Remove peak scaling from the growing amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.velocityDepth.text: Given a decomposition `V = U + O + M`, Hölder regularity of its three terms, and the scheduled parent, oscillation and mean bounds, proves $1+\|V\|_{P,1/2}\le3\lambda^{2(P+1)}$. The constants must each be at most the parent frequency `μ`; the proof is norm addition and exponent arithmetic.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.velocityDepth.summary: Control the approximate velocity at full expansion depth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: For central wave index `j`, its increasing physical clock sends the normalized interval $[0,\mathrm{window}_j]$ into $[t_{j+2},S_{j+2}]$. Positivity of the rate gives monotonicity, and `w.physical_window` identifies the right endpoint. The shift by two reflects that this record describes the next wave relative to its preceding wave.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: Normalized time stays inside the physical wave interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: For a proposed normalized-window constant `K`, this defines the coefficient $e^{-1}C^{-1}/(6(2K)^2)$ used in the limit curl lower bound. Here `C` is `w.strengthConstant`; the factor two reflects the relaxed window used to extract component bounds from Lemma 2.4. Positivity is asserted separately under `0 < K`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: A positive coefficient for the principal curl term

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: The coefficient used in the limit curl lower bound is positive if `hK : 0 < K`. The strength constant is at least two by the central-wave record, so its reciprocal is positive, and the squared window denominator is nonzero. This prevents the principal growing term from disappearing in Proposition 8.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: The principal curl coefficient is strictly positive

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: Assume `h2_2`, `h2_4`, a positive window constant, the logarithmic gain bound `hlog`, eventual older-gradient control `hOld`, comparison smallness for every constant, and uniform prefix convergence of gradients `hprefix`. For all large `j`, the curl of `u` on $[t_{j+2},t_{j+3})$ exceeds a positive multiple of $\lambda_{j+1}^{1/8}$ minus controlled $1/32$-power and constant errors. The lower-bound argument uses the stored central-wave splitting and crossing strength.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: The central curl lower bound survives the limit

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: The first coupling of `w.physical j` is the $(0,1)$ entry of the older gradient $DU_j(t_{j+2},0)$ in the frame of wave `j + 1`. The stored preceding-pair and older-gradient identities establish this equality. The statement identifies the physical parameter with the paper’s coupling; positivity and numerical bounds come from other fields.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: The first coupling uses the older central gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: The initial strength of `w.physical j` is the product of the preceding wave’s covector and amplitude norms at time $t_{j+2}$. The theorem rewrites the physical record’s stored pair as `waveVector (j + 1)` and `amplitude (j + 1)`. It introduces no estimate; the lower and upper bounds come from the crossing data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: The physical strength is the preceding wave strength

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: For a physical amplification record `P`, assume twice its first coupling is at most its initial strength. Then its shear parameter $S=\sigma/\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}$ is at least one. Positivity of strength, coupling and rate comes from `P`. This supplies the normalization inequality directly, without invoking a separate moving-frame construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: Sufficient strength makes the normalized shear at least one

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: The active slab of `w.physical j` at normalized length `w.window j` is exactly $[t_{j+2},S_{j+2}]$. This follows by unfolding the slab and using the stored physical-window endpoint. It permits hypotheses on the construction’s interval to be supplied to amplification lemmas written in normalized time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: The active slab is the prescribed stage interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: Assuming an initial frequency at least two, every normalized wave interval satisfies `w.window j ≤ windowConstant w * (4 * log (s.frequency (j + 4)))^4`. The proof combines the frozen strength and coupling bounds with the slab identity. The index `j` here describes wave `j + 2`; the declaration supplies the upper length bound used in the curl projection.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: The normalized interval grows at most as the fourth gain power

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: This defines the positive candidate $2\sqrt{8C\pi}$, where `C` is the central-wave strength constant. It is independent of the stage index. The rate bound obtained from the frozen strength and coupling makes this constant control the normalized length by the fourth power of the later logarithmic gain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: A constant controlling the normalized wave interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..text: The selected normalized-window constant is positive because `w.strengthConstant ≥ 2` and $\pi>0$. Positivity matters when it is later used in the denominator of the curl coefficient. The theorem needs no extra frequency assumption; its inputs are already constrained by the central-wave record.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.CentralWaves..summary: The normalized-window constant is strictly positive

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.Stages.activa.text: The activation sequence of `s` is monotone without an extra Theorem 7.1 hypothesis. Its zeroth and first entries coincide, and each later increment is nonnegative by the record’s `activation_step` field. This is the weaker ordering needed when placing several adjacent waves on a common time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.Stages.activa.summary: The stage record orders its activation times

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.Stages.correc.text: The correction bound already stored in `s` implies a pointwise estimate for the $m$th spatial derivative of $U_{n+1}-U_n-O_{n+1}$. It requires `m ≤ s.order (n + 1)` and a time in the new stage’s closed slab. This version reads the stage record directly rather than taking `Theorem71Conclusions` as an argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.Stages.correc.summary: The stage record controls each correction derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.Stages.freque.text: Assuming `hinit : 2 ≤ s.frequency 0`, every step satisfies $\lambda_n^{288}\le\lambda_{n+1}$. The exponent in the prescribed recursion is at least 320, so the weaker exponent 288 is available uniformly. Since $288=9\cdot32$, this is the numerical separation used to compare the older ninth-power gradient with the new scale to power $1/32$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.Stages.freque.summary: Successive frequencies absorb the older gradient scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.Stages.freque.text: If the initial frequency is at least two, every later frequency is at least two as well. This combines the initial bound with monotonicity from index zero. It supplies positive bases for inverses, logarithms and real powers in the central vorticity estimates, without introducing a separate condition at each stage.

For an inductive stage record `s`, the assumption `hinit : 2 ≤ s.frequency 0` makes the frequency sequence monotone. The proof uses the power recursion and the positive exponent parameter stored in `s`. No order-growth conclusion or large-stage threshold is needed for this elementary consequence of the schedule.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.Stages.order_.text: For each natural number `n`, the derivative order of wave `n + 1` is at least one. The first order is fixed by `s.initial_order`; subsequent orders belong to the admissible set in `s.order_maximum`. This is enough to use the correction estimate at order one when transferring central vorticity to the limit.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.Stages.order_.summary: Every wave controls at least one derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.abs_apply_le_.text: Every coordinate of `v : Vec3` has absolute value at most its Euclidean norm. The proof pairs `v` with a unit coordinate vector and applies Cauchy–Schwarz. It is used both in operator-norm estimates and in extracting coordinate bounds from the normalized wave-vector estimate of Lemma 2.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.abs_apply_le_.summary: A coordinate is bounded by the vector length

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.activation_lt.text: The lifetime and strict-increase clauses in `h71` put every activation strictly below `T`. Monotonicity and convergence first give a non-strict upper bound by `T`; a later strictly larger activation upgrades it. For indices zero and one, the argument compares with the third activation instead of assuming those initial times are distinct.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.activation_lt.summary: Every activation precedes the accumulation time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.activation_mo.text: Assuming `h71 : Theorem71Conclusions c C T`, the full natural-number sequence of activation times is monotone. The proof handles the unused zeroth time and the two initial zero times separately, then uses `h71.times_increase` from index two onward. Monotonicity includes the initial equalities; it does not assert strict increase at every index.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.bernstein_coo.text: Assuming `hB_1`, there are nonnegative constants `Cb m` controlling each coordinate derivative of a torus field with frequencies at most $4D$. The coordinate word `β` must be monotone, avoiding repeated permutations of mixed derivatives. The estimate is extracted from one term in Lemma B.1’s sum and holds for every positive `D` admitted by that Lean statement.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.bernstein_coo.summary: One coordinate derivative inherits the Bernstein bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.bernstein_jet.text: From `hB_1`, choose constants `K₁` and `K₂`. A $C^2$ periodic lift with band $4D$, positive `D` and sup norm at most `A` satisfies $\|Df\|\le K_1AD$ and $\|D^2f\|\le K_2AD^2$. Coordinate estimates bound the operator norms; symmetry of the second derivative supplies both coordinate orders.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.bernstein_jet.summary: Bernstein controls the first two full derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.boundedPeriod.text: Using `h59`, this builds a continuous bilinear map from two tuples in the range of smooth jets through order `m + 2` to compatible jets through order `m`. The range equivalence recovers the unique smooth velocities, applies their actual projected momentum and takes its jets. The preceding estimate proves boundedness before any extension to the closure.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.boundedPeriod.summary: The momentum operation is bounded on smooth jet tuples

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.closedSlab_ve.text: From Theorem71Conclusions and a Proposition81Conclusions Euler pair, the authors construct a continuous velocity limit on the full closed slab and prove uniform stage convergence there. The proof obtains the bound $\|U_{n+1}-U_n\|\le2\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$ by adding the order-zero corrected increment and oscillation bounds, then uses summability and stage continuity. The Proposition 8.1 premise serves the additional agreement $u=w$ before the terminal time. The reader supplement supplies that premise for every admitted Theorem 7.1 construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.closedSlab_ve.summary: The velocities converge uniformly on the closed terminal slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.contDiffOn_pe.text: Assume `h59`, a positive prefix length, and a time-indexed family of smooth periodic fields. If every finite jet tuple is continuous in time and the family satisfies the actual integrated projected momentum equation, then the velocity is jointly smooth on the closed prefix. The proof lifts the equation to all jet orders, bootstraps time regularity, and recovers joint regularity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.contDiffOn_pe.summary: The integrated Euler equation gives joint smoothness

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.contDiffOn_pe.text: For a velocity `u` on a positive closed prefix, assume smooth periodic spatial slices, jointly continuous spatial derivatives of every order and the integrated projected equation. With `h59`, the conclusion is joint smoothness on that same prefix, including time zero. The proof temporarily packages valid slices as smooth periodic fields and agrees with the original velocity throughout the asserted domain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.contDiffOn_pe.summary: Continuous spatial jets promote the integrated equation to smoothness

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.errorSize_le.text: Assume `h2_2`, a physical window $[t_0,\mathrm{finish}]$, a coupling ratio at most one, and uniform bounds `Bmax`, `Btmax`, `Emax` for the older gradient, its derivative and the central error. Then `errorSize` is bounded by eight times the sum in (6.6). The derivative hypothesis `hBd` is explicitly within the same closed window.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.errorSize_le.summary: Older-gradient variation bounds the comparison error

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.errorSize_non.text: For any physical amplification record, `errorSize` is nonnegative. It is a sum of supremum expressions built from norms and absolute values, divided by positive rate or coupling parameters. This lower bound is needed when scalar absorption estimates are applied to the comparison error in the Section 7 construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.errorSize_non.summary: The normalized comparison error cannot be negative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_ce.text: Assume Lemma B.1 through `hB_1` and a construction with `h71`. For all sufficiently large stages, the central gradient is bounded by $\lambda_n^9$ throughout that stage’s closed slab. Bernstein at order one, the band $2\lambda_n^5$ and the velocity bound give the estimate after absorbing a fixed constant into the growing frequency.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_ce.summary: Older central gradients satisfy the ninth-power bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_fi.text: Assume Lemmas 1.3, 2.2 and B.1 through `h1_3`, `h2_2` and `hB_1`. For a fixed construction and any natural constant `C₀`, all sufficiently late physical waves satisfy `FiniteSmallness` with that constant. The threshold may depend on `C₀`; there is no single stage asserted to work for every constant simultaneously. This exports comparison hypotheses needed by Proposition 8.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_fi.summary: Every fixed comparison constant works for sufficiently late waves

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_st.text: From `hB_1` and a construction `c`, the central gradient and its time derivative satisfy $\lambda_n^9$ and $\lambda_n^{18}$ bounds for all sufficiently large `n`. The proof applies `stage_derived_low_bounds` after the frequency passes its threshold, reading smoothness, frequency support, divergence and residual identity from `c.stages`. No separate `h71` argument is required.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_st.summary: Large stages satisfy both central gradient bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.exists_induct.text: Given positive `T`, all stage slabs covering it, square-separated frequencies, orders tending to infinity, and activation times converging to `T`, the stated increment and residual hypotheses produce a velocity limit. It is continuous on the closed slab and smooth with the actual projected Euler equation on $[0,T)$. Spatial derivatives converge uniformly only on strict prefixes. Periodicity, oddness and zero divergence pass from the stages.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.exists_induct.summary: The tower yields a continuous terminal velocity and preterminal Euler flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.exists_induct.text: Under the tower, oscillation, residual and schedule hypotheses, and `h59`, there exist velocity and pressure satisfying `IsEulerSolution T u p`. The velocity is odd before `T`, extends continuously to the closed slab, and is the uniform stage limit there. Every finite spatial derivative and every Hölder norm converges on positive strict prefixes. The proof recovers pressure from the projected equation; it does not claim smoothness at `T`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.exists_induct.summary: The limit has an Euler pressure and Hölder convergence

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.text: The explicit covector is $\kappa(t)=\lambda(e_1-2\pi t e_2)$. The definition allows any real `freq`, including zero; it does not itself assert a nonzero wave vector. The following nonvanishing and ODE lemmas supply the conditions needed when this formula is installed in `FirstWaveOrigin`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.summary: The first covector along the stationary shear

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.text: This expands the explicit covector at an axis `i : Fin 3` into scalar coordinates. The first coordinate is `freq`, the second is $-2\pi t\,\mathrm{freq}$ and the third is zero. The formula imposes no positivity condition; such conditions enter only when nonvanishing is required.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.summary: Coordinates of the initial shear covector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.text: The inner product of the explicit covector and seed is zero for every frequency, tilt and time. The first two coordinate products cancel and the covector’s third coordinate vanishes. This calculation establishes perpendicularity directly; it does not invoke the propagation result of Lemma 2.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.summary: The explicit first pair stays perpendicular

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.text: With `hf : 0 < freq`, the explicit covector is nonzero at every time. Its first coordinate remains equal to the positive frequency, so a zero-vector equality would contradict `hf`. This hypothesis is required here even though the underlying formula is defined for zero frequency.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.summary: Positive frequency prevents a zero covector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveGaug.text: The scalar factor is $g(t)=(1+(2\pi t)^2)^{-1}$. It controls the first two coordinates of the explicit unnormalized seed and is defined for every real time. Positivity of its denominator will establish that the seed’s second coordinate never vanishes, which avoids a degenerate moving frame.

The scalar gauge is strictly positive at every real time, because its denominator is one plus a square. In the explicit seed this gauge is exactly the second coordinate. The theorem therefore supplies the nonvanishing argument without a restriction to the construction’s time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveGaug.summary: The first seed keeps a positive second coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveOrig.text: For a nonnegative final time and positive frequency, explicit formulas produce a first wave at the origin over the stationary shear. The covector is $\lambda(e_1-2\pi t e_2)$; the seed is checked directly against its equation and rescaled to attain the peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$. This is the existence route used by the current Lemma 6.1 proof. The paper describes solving the linear seed equation instead.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.text: For tilt `s`, the seed is $g(t)(2\pi t e_1+e_2)-s\arctan(2\pi t)e_3$. Its value at time zero is $e_2$. It is not yet normalized to the peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$: a later existence proof multiplies it by a positive constant obtained from its maximum on the chosen interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.summary: An explicit seed before peak normalization

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.text: The seed’s three coordinates are $2\pi t g(t)$, $g(t)$ and $-s\arctan(2\pi t)$. The indicator tests on `i : Fin 3` select the coordinate. This scalar form is used to verify orthogonality, nonvanishing and the differential equation directly for the first wave.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.summary: Coordinates of the unnormalized first seed

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.text: The explicit seed is nonzero for every real tilt and time. Its second coordinate is the gauge $g(t)>0$, so equality to the zero vector is impossible. This holds before normalization and supplies the positive maximum used when rescaling to the prescribed peak amplitude.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.first_couplin.text: Assuming the frame identities of Lemma 2.2, a positive frequency, $|\rho|\le1$ and $T|B_\rho|\le1/8$, the first coupling of the normalized initial wave is at least $\pi$ throughout $[0,T]$. The proof starts at $2\pi$ and controls the variation of the first two frame vectors. The intermediate estimate $2\pi-2t|B_\rho|^2$ occurs in the proof, while the public conclusion states the lower bound $\pi$.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.frame_axis_de.text: Under `h2_2`, a transverse wave pair over a trace-free gradient has a derivative for each frame axis on `J`. At any `t ∈ J`, one may choose its derivative vector with norm at most $2\|B(t)\|$. The proof uses the frame equations and orthonormality supplied by the lemma, retaining a uniform bound for all three axes.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.frame_axis_de.summary: Each moving axis turns at a controlled speed

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.hasDerivAt_fi.text: The formula for the first covector satisfies $\kappa_t=-B_s^T\kappa$ at every real time. The proof differentiates the affine formula and substitutes the explicit adjoint shear. No frequency positivity is needed for this equality, though a nonzero covector is required when constructing the moving frame.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.hasDerivAt_fi.summary: The explicit covector solves its transport equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.hasDerivAt_fi.text: Assuming `hf : 0 < freq`, the unnormalized seed has derivative given by `affineWaveAmplitudeOperator` for the stationary shear and explicit covector. The calculation differentiates the gauge and arctangent, then clears the nonzero denominators. This verifies the seed equation directly and supplies the derivative identity used in the existence conjunct of Lemma 6.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.hasDerivAt_fi.summary: The explicit seed solves the amplitude equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.increment_jet.text: From the increment clause of `h71`, this extracts a pointwise bound for the $m$th derivative of $U_{n+1}-U_n-O_{n+1}$. The assumptions include `m ≤ P.order (n + 1)` and time membership in the new stage’s closed slab. Its bound is $\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$, obtained by dropping the other terms of the Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.increment_jet.summary: Each corrected increment has small spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.inner_vec3.text: For vectors `x` and `y` in `Vec3`, the real inner product is the sum of the three coordinate products. The finite-coordinate identity introduces no wave assumptions. It is the elementary calculation used to verify that the explicit first covector and seed remain perpendicular.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.inner_vec3.summary: The Euclidean inner product in three coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.lemma13_sched.text: Given the statement of Lemma 1.3 as `h13`, every parameter record has orders tending to infinity and satisfies $4\log\lambda_{i+3}\le(\log\lambda_i)^2$. The proof supplies the record fields to `h13` and converts the paper index $j\ge1$ to $i+1$. It uses the lemma as a hypothesis rather than calling its library proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.lemma13_sched.summary: Slow orders control the later logarithmic gain

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.limit_agreeme.text: Assume `h71`, the Proposition 8.1 conclusions `h81`, and uniform convergence of the stage velocities to a field `w` on the closed slab. Then `u t = w t` for $0\le t<T$. The argument compares two pointwise limits, using order-zero Hölder convergence from `h81`; it does not identify the values of `u` at or after `T`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.limit_agreeme.summary: The continuous terminal limit agrees before the endpoint

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.mFourierCoeff.text: For a continuous complex-linear map `L` between complete normed complex spaces, the Fourier coefficient of $L\circ g$ equals `L` applied to the coefficient of `g`. Compactness gives integrability and permits the map to pass through the integral. This allows vector Fourier-band information to be tested by scalar measurements.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.mFourierCoeff.summary: Fourier coefficients commute with linear measurements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.nonneg_period.text: For every order `m` and product-estimate hypothesis `h59`, the combined momentum bound is nonnegative. The selected Hölder-product constant has a nonnegativity proof and the other factors are norms, a square root or a square. The theorem does not assert strict positivity or a sharp operator norm.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_advectio.text: Let `A` represent $Du\,u$ on the torus, with `hA` identifying its values. If the velocity, gradient and second derivative are bounded by nonnegative `M`, `B` and `H`, then $\|A\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le2(BM+B^2+HM)$. The proof combines a Lipschitz estimate at short distances with a sup-norm estimate at long distances.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_advectio.summary: Velocity jets control the Hölder norm of self-advection

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_fderiv_s.text: For a $C^2$ vector field, the derivative of $Du\,u$ is bounded by $\|Du\|^2+\|D^2u\|\,\|u\|$. The proof applies the product rule to evaluating the derivative map on the velocity. No periodicity or Euler equation is assumed; this is the local estimate used to control the parent’s projected momentum.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_fderiv_s.summary: Differentiating self-advection costs two spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_periodic.text: For smooth periodic `u` and `v`, the order-`m` jet norm of their signed projected momentum is bounded by `periodicMomentumJetBound h59 m` times their two order-`m + 2` jet norms. The proof explicitly obtains the product estimate from `h59`, then applies tensor divergence and Leray bounds. It is conditional on the cited estimate (5.59).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_periodic.summary: Two extra spatial derivatives control the projected momentum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_realHalf.text: The continuous field underlying `f : HalfHolder Labels Vec3` has sup norm at most the HalfHolder norm of `f`. The Hölder norm already controls pointwise values, so the proof passes that bound through the continuous-map norm characterization. This is used for the Leray-projected advection in the parent time-derivative estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_realHalf.summary: The supremum norm is bounded by the Hölder norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_signed_t.text: Unit orthogonal axes `x` and `y` and coefficients `a`, `b` are given. If their squared magnitudes match the corresponding squared components of `z`, then $\|a x+b y\|\le\|z\|$. The signs may differ from the actual components. This estimate bounds the moving-frame derivative in the first-coupling proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_signed_t.summary: Two orthogonal components cannot exceed the full length

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_sq_vec3.text: For every vector `x`, its squared Euclidean norm equals the sum of its three squared coordinates. The proof reduces this identity to the preceding inner-product formula. The seed-equation calculation uses it to turn the pressure correction denominator into an explicit positive scalar expression.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.opNorm_le_sum.text: The operator norm of a continuous real-linear map from $\mathbb R^3$ is at most the sum of its values on the three unit axes. The codomain is any real normed space. Expanding an input vector in coordinates and bounding each coordinate by its length supplies the conversion used after Bernstein’s coordinate estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.opNorm_le_sum.summary: Coordinate directions bound the full operator norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.parent_derive.text: Given `hB_1`, choose a frequency threshold `N`.
