Smooth periodic parent data with velocity bound `freq`, band $2\mathrm{freq}^5$, a small residual and the represented projected evolution satisfy gradient bounds $\mathrm{freq}^9$ and $\mathrm{freq}^{18}$ in space and time. The hypotheses include `0 < T`, `N ≤ freq`, `1 ≤ freqnext`, and `hEq` on the closed slab. The time derivative uses `derivWithin` there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.parent_derive.summary: The projected equation bounds the parent gradient in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicMomen.text: Given `h59 : Statement.Text.eq_5_59`, this chooses its product-estimate constant at order `m + 1` and combines it with the Leray, tensor-divergence and jet-to-Hölder bounds. The result is a scalar bound for projected momentum from order `m + 2` jets to order `m` jets. Its value depends on the witness selected from `h59`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicMomen.summary: The product estimate supplies a momentum bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.text: On a positive closed prefix, assume smooth periodic stages, smooth limiting spatial slices, uniform convergence of every spatial derivative, uniformly vanishing residuals and the stage projected equation. The theorem returns the integrated limit equation, its time derivative and joint smoothness. The product estimate `h59` is used in the momentum map; no symbolic residual replacement is used to assert the equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.summary: Vanishing residuals give an actual smooth projected Euler limit

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.text: With `h59`, the signed projected momentum becomes a continuous bilinear map from two completed compatible jet spaces of order `m + 2` into the order-`m` space. It is obtained by extending the bounded map on smooth jet tuples along their dense isometric inclusion. Later evaluation lemmas identify its values on smooth inputs with the actual spatial derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.summary: Projected momentum extends to compatible limiting jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.text: For smooth periodic inputs, the `i`th component of the completed momentum map at `x` is $D^i[-\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes v)](x)$. Here `i : Fin (m + 1)` restricts the output order. The equality identifies component values, rather than only matching norms or giving an abstract existence result.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.summary: Each output jet is the actual momentum derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.text: Apply the completed momentum map to the compatible jets of smooth periodic fields `u` and `v`. The result is exactly the order-`m` jet tuple of their bundled signed projected momentum. Density-based extension therefore preserves the original operator, which is essential before using the jet-space evolution to infer regularity of the physical velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.summary: The extended momentum agrees with smooth Euler momentum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.preceding_str.text: Assume Lemma 2.2, a transverse nonzero wave solving the covector and amplitude equations over a trace-free gradient, and `hB : ‖B t‖ ≤ μ^(1/32)`. If $\mu\ge1$ and the interval length is at most $\mu^{-1/16}$, the strength stays above $e^{-1}$ times its left-endpoint strength. The log-strength equation from `h2_2` controls the loss.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.preceding_str.summary: The preceding wave loses at most one exponential factor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.proposition82.text: For a construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, the bounded-velocity and central-vorticity conclusions follow from Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.4 and B.1. The proof combines covector geometry, retained preceding strength and convergence of later increments. It also exports the quantitative lower bound on each late activation interval needed to prove divergence of the vorticity integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.proposition82.summary: Vorticity growth across all late crossing intervals

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.realHalfHolde.text: This definition regards a torus `HalfHolder` field as a continuous torus field. It preserves every pointwise value while dropping the extra Hölder information from the type. The conversion allows the projected advection term to be combined with a continuous residual when estimating the parent’s time derivative in the proof of (7.6).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.realHalfHolde.summary: Forget Hölder control while retaining the same field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.realNormedBan.text: If the complexified vector Fourier coefficients of `g` vanish above radius `R`, then every real continuous linear measurement has the same frequency bound. The proof builds the corresponding complex-linear coordinate map and commutes it with Fourier coefficients. This converts the stage’s band predicate into the normed-space band predicate required by Lemma B.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.realNormedBan.summary: The vector frequency bound controls scalar measurements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.slab_pos.text: Each slab endpoint in a construction is strictly positive. The zeroth slab is one; a later slab is its nonnegative activation time plus twice a positive half length from `c.lifetime`. This prevents the closed-slab derivative arguments from being applied on an interval with zero or negative length.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.slab_succ_le.text: For every `i`, the endpoint $S_{i+2}$ is at most $S_{i+1}$. The activation increment is at most the old half length, while four times the next half length is at most the old one. The statement starts with the first positive-index slab and does not assert a separate comparison between $S_1$ and $S_0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.slab_succ_le.summary: Later stage endpoints are nested from the first stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stage_derived.text: Assuming `hB_1`, a smooth periodic stage with bounded velocity, frequency support, zero divergence and `closedSlabLerayMomentum = R` has central gradient and time-gradient bounds $\mathrm{old}^9$ and $\mathrm{old}^{18}$. The old frequency exceeds a chosen threshold and the next scale `μ` is at least one. The proof constructs the Hölder advection representative and torus residual needed by `parent_derived_low_bounds`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stage_derived.summary: The stage residual identity yields the central derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stationaryShe.text: For every real tilt `s`, the adjoint shear maps $y$ to $2\pi\langle e_1+s e_3,y\rangle e_2$. The proof identifies it through inner products rather than matrix entries. This is the operator that drives the covector equation $\kappa_t=-B_\rho^T\kappa$ in the explicit first-wave construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stationaryShe.summary: The transposed shear points along the second axis

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stationaryShe.text: The stationary shear gradient sends a vector $x$ to $2\pi x_2(e_1+s e_3)$. Here `s` is an arbitrary real tilt, and `x 1` is the second coordinate. The identity expands the rank-one map used in (6.1), making the first-wave ODE calculation an explicit coordinate calculation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stationaryShe.summary: The shear acts through the second coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.tendstoUnifor.text: Assume `h59`, uniform convergence of compatible velocity jets through order two, and continuity of the limiting tuple on $[0,S]$. The projected quadratic momenta then converge uniformly in time at each fixed spatial point `x`. The proof applies the bounded bilinear momentum map and evaluates the zeroth output jet.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.tendstoUnifor.summary: Second-order jet convergence passes through the projected momentum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.trace_station.text: The rank-one shear gradient has trace zero for every real tilt `s`. Its action is along the first and third axes and depends only on the second coordinate, so all diagonal entries vanish. The first-coupling proof supplies this identity to the trace-free hypothesis of Lemma 2.2.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.two_le_freque.text: For a parameter record `P`, the initial frequency satisfies $2\le\lambda_0$. The logarithmic floor at order one and `P.initial_threshold` supply the lower bound; the exponent parameter is already positive in the record. This is a consequence of the chosen schedule, not an additional assumption about a stage.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.unitAxis.text: This abbreviation gives the coordinate vector $e_{i+1}$ in $\mathbb R^3$. Lean indexes the axes by `Fin 3`, so indices zero, one and two correspond to the paper’s first, second and third coordinates. It supplies the concrete vectors used to verify the first wave at the origin.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.wave_geometry.text: From `h2_4`, choose the lemma’s threshold `N`. A growing crossing with `N ≤ C₀`, `1 ≤ C₀`, normalized length `T ≥ 2`, positive scale and `FiniteSmallness` has $|X|\le(2T)^2$, $|Q|\le2T$ and $|Z-1|\le1/2$ on its active slab. The equality `I = w.activeSlab T` is required to match the two domains.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.wave_geometry.summary: The new wave keeps a substantial third component

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.admissible_jet_.text: The hypothesis hb bounds the value sets of every admissible word through order n. For a word w in that set, its pointwise norm is bounded by the finite word norm; when holder holds, its spatial difference is bounded by the same norm times the square root of the distance. The case of equal points is separated before division by that square root.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.admissible_jet_.summary: Bound one derivative word by the finite norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'.text: The definition appends the index i to a derivative word and sorts the resulting list. It supplies a canonical representative of the enlarged multi-index for display (D.2). The input word may be arbitrary; preservation of admissibility and injectivity are separate results with the required sorted-word hypotheses. Sorting itself is a finite combinatorial operation and asserts no commutation of derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'.summary: Insert one derivative direction into a sorted word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_i.text: For a fixed letter i, adjoining and sorting is injective on the admissible words through order n. The domain restriction matters: arbitrary differently ordered lists could have the same sorted output. Cancellation of the added letter gives a permutation of the old words, and their nondecreasing order upgrades that permutation to equality. The result controls multiplicities when summing the interpolation estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_i.summary: Adding a fixed derivative direction preserves distinct words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_m.text: If w is an admissible nondecreasing word of length at most n, appending a letter and sorting yields an admissible word of length at most n + 1. The proof checks the new length and its sorted order separately. This lets the Hölder interpolation argument use one additional label derivative without leaving the supplied finite set of derivative bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_m.summary: The enlarged word remains admissible one order higher

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_p.text: The sorted word obtained by adjoining i is a permutation of the original word followed by i. This is a combinatorial statement about lists, valid without a sortedness hypothesis on the input. It is later combined with commutation of constant-direction derivatives to identify the new word with a derivative of the old one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_p.summary: Sorting preserves the enlarged derivative multi-index

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.coefficientPowe.text: Assume hs gives spatial smoothness, each K m is nonnegative, D is nonnegative, and h bounds every derivative operator norm. The theorem obtains CoefficientPower with constants multiplied by the number of sorted coordinate words of length m. It proves boundedness of the sets whose suprema define the coefficient sizes before applying the supremum estimates, so those real-valued suprema carry their intended meaning.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.coefficientPowe.summary: Recover coefficient bounds from derivative operator bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.coefficientPowe.text: The hypothesis hc includes smoothness, bounded coordinate jets, and the coefficient estimate (D.6). It yields a pointwise operator bound for the mth derivative with an additional factor $3^m$. Sorting an ordered coordinate word preserves its derivative because the directions commute; the sum over all ordered tuples then accounts for that factor. The conclusion is a conversion of hc, not an independent construction of coefficient bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.coefficientPowe.summary: Turn coefficient bounds into derivative operator bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.hierarchyJetVal.text: For a continuous bilinear map B, the smooth fields f and g have bounded derivatives for every admissible word up to n. The result proves boundedness for the product word, including half-Hölder quotients when holder is true. Leibniz bounds use all subwords of w, and admissibility of those subwords follows from their sorted order. This establishes finiteness separately from the product norm inequality.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.hierarchyJetVal.summary: Bound the derivative values of a bilinear product

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.hierarchyLabelD.text: Setting the label weight to one makes each hierarchy direction the corresponding constant coordinate vector. This function equality removes the weighting convention before ordinary coordinate calculus is applied. It does not assert a derivative bound or any property of a field; it identifies the two direction families used in the coefficient norms of Appendix D.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.hierarchyLabelD.summary: Unit weights give the coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.holderWord_le.text: For $0<\ell\le1$, the supremum values of one word and its three enlarged coordinate words control every half-Hölder quantity of that word by their sum divided by $\sqrt\ell$. The assumptions hbw and hbi provide the bounded suprema explicitly. The proof combines a uniform-value bound with a gradient bound and treats coincident points separately. Summing this per-word estimate gives display (D.2).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.holderWord_le.summary: One extra derivative gives a half Hölder word bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_a.text: For one fixed word w, smoothness of f, g, and the directions combines with hbf and hbg to show that the derivative values of f + g are bounded above. The bound is the sum of the two existing suprema. The holder flag is fixed to False, so this lemma supplies supremum control only; the Hölder difference quotients are not part of its conclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_a.summary: Preserve bounded derivative values under addition

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_d.text: Bounded weighted derivatives through order n + 1 give smoothness and bounded weighted derivatives through order n of the unweighted derivative in direction d i. The hypothesis hr requires the weight r i to be strictly positive. The proof first differentiates in the weighted direction, then multiplies by its reciprocal; this explicit hypothesis prevents the inverse at zero from being used as a derivative rescaling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_d.summary: Remove a direction weight from derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_s.text: Multiplying a smooth family by the real scalar c preserves boundedness of the quantities measured for a fixed derivative word. The proposition holder can include half-Hölder quotients as well as supremum values. The proof identifies the new set with the old set scaled by $|c|$, which is nonnegative. No positivity or nonzero condition on c is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_s.summary: Preserve bounded derivative values under scalar multiplication

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.list_eq_castSuc.text: A list of Fin 4 letters that contains no last letter can be written as a list of Fin 3 letters mapped by Fin.castSucc. Thus every mixed derivative word without the phase letter is a label word. This is a finite combinatorial helper; it asserts no differentiation, regularity, or norm bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.list_eq_castSuc.summary: Words without a phase letter use only label directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_labelLinea.text: For a continuous linear map A from three-dimensional Euclidean space to a real normed space, its operator norm is bounded by the sum of the three coordinate-direction values. The coordinate expansion and triangle inequality supply the bound. It turns the three extra word bounds in holderWord_le into control of the full gradient required by Hölder interpolation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_labelLinea.summary: Control a linear norm by coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_sub_sqrt_o.text: If $\|v\|_\infty\le A$ and $\|Dv\|_\infty\le B$, then $\|v(x)-v(y)\|\le\sqrt{2AB}\sqrt{|x-y|}$. The function is differentiable and the two bounds are nonnegative. The proof combines the uniform bound $2A$ and the Lipschitz bound $B|x-y|$, then takes a square root. This is the interpolation step used for each spatial derivative in the proof of (D.2).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_sub_sqrt_o.summary: Uniform and derivative bounds give half-Hölder control

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.opNorm_le_coord.text: For a continuous multilinear map with m arguments in three-dimensional space, the operator norm is at most the sum of its norms on all ordered coordinate tuples. The target X is any real normed space, not necessarily an algebra. Expanding each argument in coordinates gives the estimate used by coefficientPower_pointwise; all ordered tuples appear here, before any sorting.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.opNorm_le_coord.summary: Control a multilinear norm by coordinate values

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseAverage_je.text: Assume each field is smooth, each phase slice is one-periodic, and the supremum value sets for every admissible word through n are bounded. The phase average is then smooth with bounded value sets for the same words. The proof commutes each word with averaging and bounds the integral by the original supremum. The flag is False, so no half-Hölder estimate is asserted here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseAverage_je.summary: Preserve smoothness and bounded jets under phase averaging

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.text: At a point x in label–phase space, this definition integrates f at x + (0,r) over one phase period. It retains the starting phase in x until periodicity is supplied by a later theorem. Smoothness permits differentiation under the integral, and periodicity then identifies this translated mean with the phase-independent average used in Lemma D.1.

For a smooth f and any fixed direction d in label–phase space, the directional derivative of the translated phase average equals the translated average of the directional derivative. The proof first differentiates the parameter integral, then moves evaluation at d through the integral. Both arguments use continuity on the integration interval, while phase periodicity is unnecessary for this identity.

If each phase slice of f is one-periodic, averaging f after an arbitrary phase translation gives its ordinary phase mean at the same label. The result identifies the two integral representations used in Lemma D.1. It makes no smoothness claim and does not establish the derivative or norm estimates; those follow from the separate smoothness and boundedness lemmas.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.summary: Remove the starting phase from a periodic average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.text: A smooth field f on label–phase space has a smooth translated phase average. The target is a complete real normed space, so integration of its values is available with the usual smooth-parameter integral theorem. This statement does not require phase periodicity: smoothness follows from integrating translations over the fixed compact interval alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.summary: Smoothness passes through the translated phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.text: For a family of constant directions d and a finite word w, applying that word to the translated phase average equals averaging the corresponding derivative word of f. Smoothness hf lets the one-derivative commutation theorem be reapplied at each stage. The index type J is arbitrary, and the statement does not impose an order on the word.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.summary: Commute every derivative word with phase averaging

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseOperatorWo.text: A word of directional derivatives applied to the sum of two smooth fields is the sum of their words. The direction fields themselves must be smooth, through hD; they need not be constant or commuting for this additive identity. Induction on the word uses the derivative of a sum at each step. The result supplies finiteness estimates in Lemma D.1.

For a smooth spatial field f and an ordered tuple β of m coordinate indices, the unweighted derivative word equals the mth Fréchet derivative evaluated on those coordinate vectors. The hypothesis hf supplies smoothness, and List.ofFn turns the tuple into the word expected by phaseOperatorWord. This identifies the library word notation with the coordinate derivatives used in Lemma D.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseOperatorWo.summary: Read coordinate words as iterated derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.spatialHolderHa.text: A continuous linear map L satisfying hL, the pointwise contraction bound, preserves SpatialHolderHalf m and does not increase its norm. The proof moves L through each derivative and each spatial increment. In Lemma B.1 this transfers cutoff estimates through complexification and the real-part map. No Fourier-support or cutoff assumption belongs to this general composition lemma.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.sumCoordinateDi.text: Every vector in the Euclidean model of the torus is the sum of its three coordinates times the coordinate directions. The proof evaluates each coordinate after moving the projection through the finite sum. This supplies the elementary expansion used to compare derivative operator norms with coordinate partial derivatives in Lemma D.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.sumCoordinateDi.summary: Resolve a vector into coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_eq_zero_of.text: If a word contains a letter whose entire direction field is zero, its iterated directional derivative is the zero function. The statement needs no smoothness: any continuous-linear derivative applied to the zero vector is zero, including a totalized derivative value. In the phase-independent reduction the phase direction becomes the zero label direction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_eq_zero_of.summary: A zero direction annihilates the derivative word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_fst_of_con.text: For a smooth label field f, a family of constant directions d_i in label×phase space and any word w, differentiating f∘fst along d_i equals differentiating f along their label components and then composing with fst. Time and norms do not enter this identity. It supplies the chain rule used to remove the phase variable from a phase-independent field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_fst_of_con.summary: Constant mixed derivatives restrict to the label directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_map_letter.text: For any direction family D, letter map e, word w and function f, applying the word w after replacing every direction by D(e i) equals applying the mapped word to D. No smoothness is assumed because this is a definitional rearrangement of the same total derivative operators. It is bookkeeping for derivative words, not a separate analytical estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_map_letter.summary: Renaming derivative directions leaves their composition unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.MeanParentFlow.text:
This proposition bundles the standing assumptions of Section 4: 0 < T ≤ 1, joint smoothness of U on [0,T]×ℝ³, spatial ℤ³-periodicity, pointwise divergence freeness, and IsLabelFlowOn U X [0,T]. The flow has two time arguments: X s t a starts at label a at time s and is evaluated at time t. The paper’s X(t,a) is X 0 t a; its inverse is X t 0. Volume preservation and invertibility of the spatial deformation are consequences of these assumptions, not additional fields written into the structure. No Euler equation or pressure assumption is made for U.

Default-value audit (b4): The strict positivity of T excludes an empty or one-point time interval. Divergence uses fderiv of U t, but joint smoothness on the slab gives genuine differentiable spatial slices, including at the temporal endpoints. IsLabelFlowOn uses derivative witnesses, not selected derivatives. Together with smooth periodic U it determines the smooth invertible particle flow used downstream. The structure contains no integral, supremum, ENNReal.toReal, division, or square root; such operations appear only in derived coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.MeanParentFlow.summary: A smooth incompressible parent and its particle flow

TorusEuler.Paper.ModelCase.text:
For every normalized time τ in [0,T], every entry of B in the preceding frame equals modelEntries(ν,η), and the error matrix E_c is zero at physical time w.clock τ. The frozen ν and η are the activation values stored by w. The predicate constrains a supplied physical configuration; it neither constructs one nor asserts the wave equations for k. The model conclusions of Lemma 2.3 additionally require NewWaveVector and the clock inclusion.

Default-value audit (b4): The universal quantifier over [0,T] is vacuous if T < 0; ModelCase itself imposes no lower bound on T. Lemma 2.3 supplies T ≥ 2 and clock inclusion, so the relevant interval is nonempty and all frame evaluations lie in I. Inherited frame normalizations and the clock are guarded by PhysicalAmplification on I. No new integral, derivative, supremum, or square root occurs in this predicate.
TorusEuler.Paper.ModelCase.summary: Model background with two entries and zero error

TorusEuler.Paper.NewWaveVector.text:
Given a PhysicalAmplification w on I, this says λ > 0, k(t₀) = λE₃(t₀), and k′ = −Mᵀk at every time of I, where M = B + a_p ⊗ k_p + E_c. The number 2 in w.basis t₀ 2 is the paper’s third frame vector because Fin 3 is indexed by 0, 1, 2. There is no amplitude in this predicate. The parameters t₀ and I come from w; k is a supplied function, not an object chosen by the definition.

Default-value audit (b4): The explicit λ > 0 excludes the zero launch. PhysicalAmplification assumes nonzero perpendicular preceding vectors, so its frame at t₀ is orthonormal and E₃ is nonzero. The ODE is asserted with HasDerivWithinAt, avoiding a default-zero derivative equality. The definition alone does not say that I is an interval or that k stays nonzero at every point of a disconnected I. In Lemmas 2.3–2.8, MapsTo w.clock [0,T] I and T ≥ 2 provide the connected active slab on which linear-ODE nonvanishing is used. No new division, integral, supremum, or square root is evaluated here.
TorusEuler.Paper.NewWaveVector.summary: Wave vector launched in the third frame direction

TorusEuler.Paper.ProfileFamily.text:
One positive C works simultaneously for every 0 < h ≤ 1: F_h and P_h are smooth and 1-periodic, F_h is odd, P_h has phase average zero and derivative F_h, F_h′(0)=1, −Ch ≤ F_h′ ≤ 1, and |F_h| ≤ Ch at every phase. For each integer j ≥ 2 there is another positive constant C_j, chosen before h, controlling |∂^jF_h| by C_j h^{1−j}. The exponent is an integer, so h ^ (1−(j:ℤ)) is a negative integral power for j ≥ 2. This is a property of any supplied pair of families; it does not choose the profiles.

Default-value audit (b4): h > 0 excludes the zero base of every negative power. The ContDiff hypotheses guard deriv and iteratedDeriv, so the derivative estimates cannot be satisfied merely by default-zero derivatives of a nonsmooth profile. Smooth P_h is integrable over [0,1], legitimizing phaseMean(P_h)=0. Bounds are pointwise, not real sSup values; no empty/unbounded supremum or ENNReal.toReal is involved. There is no square root. The family is unconstrained outside 0 < h ≤ 1, as in the paper.
TorusEuler.Paper.ProfileFamily.summary: Profile conditions for localization and controlled negative slope

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_13_of.text: The proof first obtains polynomial derivative bounds for $K$ and $\Omega$, then converts them into the half-Hölder coefficient norms using the supplied comparison estimate. Positive derivative order leaves a factor $\sqrt{\ell}$ after the weighted coefficient rule is applied. The final arithmetic chooses the radius small enough that $D^C\sqrt{\ell}\le1/A$. Its explicit inputs are Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.2 and display (D.2); the polynomial bound on $A$ remains a hypothesis of the resulting statement.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_13_of.summary: Absorbing mean coefficient derivatives into the radius

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_14_of.text: This proof reconstructs the smooth endpoint system from an arbitrary MeanSolution, bounds the inverse constant by a fixed power of $D$, and invokes the coefficient thresholds of (5.13). It builds derivative towers preserving the endpoint and divergence constraints, applies the lifting theorem derived from Lemma D.3, and translates the result into the finite half-Hölder norm. The final use of $T\le1$ controls time integration. Its explicit inputs preserve the actual chain of cited results rather than hiding the endpoint argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_14_of.summary: Lifting the endpoint inverse to every Hölder order

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_59.text: The product estimate follows from the bilinear half-Hölder inequality with the explicit choice $C_m=3(m+1)2^m$. The proof checks that this constant is nonnegative and applies the library theorem to the two fields and their continuous bilinear product. The resulting estimate includes the factor $\|B\|$ and supplies regularity of the product as well as the norm inequality, so it covers all tensor products needed by the cutoff argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_59.summary: The product estimate in physical Hölder norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_D_2.text: The proof applies the uniform-and-gradient interpolation inequality to each derivative word, then sums first at an exact order and then through order $n$. Appending a fixed coordinate is injective on sorted words, which controls the next-order sum. It proves the needed half-Hölder boundedness instead of assuming it. The older comparison wrapper is deliberately not called because its dependencies would pass through Lemma D.1, which the paper does not cite here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_D_2.summary: Interpolation and summation prove display D.2

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.section8_set.text: Theorem 7.1 implies the existence of a common construction for Section 8. The proof selects a smooth admissible Fourier cutoff, chooses an envelope floor, and constructs an admissible threshold above the resulting majorant. It then takes the initial frequency at the allowed lower bound. The step identities are discarded because this setting proposition retains only the quantitative conclusions of Theorem 7.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.section8_set.summary: Choosing the construction used in Section eight

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.corollary_8_3.text: This is a direct proof of the corollary statement; there is no additional list of cited numbered results in its type. The construction and the conclusions of Propositions 8.1 and 8.2 are hypotheses inside that statement. Central vorticity divergence excludes continuation. The quantitative lower bound is integrated over crossing intervals, then a curl-versus-gradient estimate proves divergence of the other integral. Periodic Beale--Kato--Majda is not formalized here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.corollary_8_3.summary: Maximality and integral divergence from crossing bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_1_3.text: The proof of Lemma 1.3 derives the adjacent-order bound, divergence of the retained orders, and the logarithmic gain estimate from the schedule. It applies the library result and changes from its index $i$ to the manuscript index $j=i+1$. The threshold needs a positive cubic logarithmic floor; monotonicity of $\mathcal B$ and bounds on other construction constants are not used by this argument. This is a leaf proof with no numbered-result premise.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_1_3.summary: Slow order growth from the threshold schedule

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_1.text: The proof combines phase transport, cancellation of self-advection, the background and wave pressure gradients, and zero divergence. It also packages differentiability and uses linear propagation to preserve nonzero perpendicular vectors. The result has no earlier numbered theorem as a hypothesis because the paper cites none here. The highlighted source steps use the actual affine-wave lemmas, not merely the older statement wrapper.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_1.summary: Pressure cancels the affine wave acceleration

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_2.text:
The proof obtains orthonormality from nonzero perpendicular wave data, then applies the derivative formula for the moving frame. That formula differentiates normalized vectors, takes the cross product for the third axis and uses zero trace for the logarithmic strength. No previous numbered result is assumed. The two wave equations and the trace condition are unpacked from the statement's hypotheses.

No symmetry of the background acceleration $B'+B^2$ is required for these frame identities.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_2.summary: Normalize the wave and differentiate its frame

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_3_of.text:
The conditional proof takes exactly Lemma 2.2 as its numbered input. One content theorem derives constant preceding strength and the scaled model equations from the frame identities. A second proves uniform convergence by a quantitative wave-vector estimate and continuity of the coefficient functions. Combining these two conclusions yields the full statement of Lemma 2.3, including nonvanishing of the limiting denominator.

This is a strong-shear limit theorem, not the finite-window polynomial error estimate of Lemma 2.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_3_of.summary: Model equations and the strong shear limit

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_4_of.text: The conditional proof takes Lemma 2.2, rescales its frame identities and obtains polynomial wave-vector bounds. It controls the raw amplitude error in the library variables $(U,V)$, then sets $\mathcal E=PRP$ with $P=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)$ to return to $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$. The error depends on the wave vector and background, so one operator works for all amplitudes. Continuity and the strength-ratio estimate are exported explicitly.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_4_of.summary: Compare the wave vector and conjugate the amplitude error

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_5.text: The proof constructs a global Riccati solution and uses uniqueness to transfer its properties to every reference solution. It translates $x=\tan\varphi$ and $s=\cos\varphi$, bounds the deviation, integrates the ansatz, and obtains the unique turning time. The sign conditions give the amplitude maximum; the gain integral becomes $\log a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)$. No numbered result is an input to this proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_5.summary: Global reference slope, peak and amplitude gain

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_6_of.text: Assuming Lemmas 2.4 and 2.5, this proof derives all conclusions of Lemma 2.6. It controls the normalized state using the integrated matrix error, then recovers the physical norm and transverse transport. It differentiates the normalized coordinates directly, whereas the manuscript uses Liouville's formula for one equation. A library theorem supplies the onto transport for a continuous background. The bound uses the explicit coefficient $252eS$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_6_of.summary: Amplitude comparison and the transverse propagator

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_7_of.text: The proof assumes Lemmas 2.4, 2.5, and 2.6 and derives Lemma 2.7. It uses the rational coupling formulas in the preceding frame, the cancellation in their reference values, and a polynomial perturbation bound. Positivity of the reference rate in the early range is taken from Lemma 2.5. The late comparison is then combined with the physical error budget to obtain the stated coupling bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_7_of.summary: Positivity and late ratios of new couplings

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_3_1.text: The proof of Lemma 3.1 collects the properties already proved for the explicit bump construction. It obtains a common positive constant and the higher-order constants from the family theorem, then returns that property list as the numbered statement. The construction gives $C=1/2$, although the statement quantifies over an unspecified positive $C$. There are no numbered-result premises here; the declaration is named without an additional conditional-proof suffix.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_3_1.summary: Periodic profiles with controlled negative slope

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_4_1.text:
The proof supplies the actual flow derivative $F$, gradient $M$ and derivative $M_t$ to the general Sobolev Hardy theorem. Smoothness of the material gradient gives the required time derivative and its continuity. The flow variation equation supplies $F_t=MF$, and the stated quadratic upper bound supplies $H^\#\le I$. The resulting inequalities apply to the given mean-zero $L^2$ velocity. No numbered theorem is assumed by this proof leaf.

The upper bound on $H^\#$ is a quadratic-form bound; symmetry of $H^\#$ is not assumed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_4_1.summary: Applying the Hardy inequalities to the parent flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_10_of.text: Pulls the perturbation back by the parent flow and splits the label velocity into an oscillatory part and a phase independent mean. Theorem 5.6 supplies profile norms; Proposition 5.1 gives inverse-deformation coefficients; Proposition 5.4 supplies the divergence identity and preactivation vanishing. The code establishes PhaseJetBound 2 for the oscillatory label velocity and PhaseJetBound 1 for the mean, then invokes ChildFlow.exists_childFlow_of_profile_jet_bounds for the extended label/phase flow and its deformation control. Finally uniform spatial Lipschitzness identifies every label flow with the constructed flow. The mean jet hypothesis used by the helper is weaker than the order-two norm displayed for both components in the TeX proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_10_of.summary: Controlling the child flow through label and phase variables

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_3_of.text: This short proof consumes exactly the statements of Lemma 3.1, Proposition 5.1 and Lemmas D.1–D.3. It derives the weighted ODE recurrence from Lemma D.3 and passes the result to the assembly theorem. The larger implementation uses the projected inverse coframe and an independently derived homogeneous leading-wave estimate, so it should not be read as a literal transcription of every displayed internal dependency in the prose. Its output remains the separately documented Statement.lemma_5_3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_3_of.summary: The seed and transverse inverse estimates from cited results

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_5_of.text: Proposition 5.1 and Lemma D.1 are the two numbered inputs. The proof first obtains the general completion and material derivative estimates from `lemma55_main`. It then represents the unswitched leading velocity and pressure by smooth twisted profiles on the full slab, proves their homogeneous transverse equation on $[t_0,T]$, and applies the general estimate with zero forcing. The final zero-norm calculation removes the forcing term. No time derivative of the forcing or the parent strain enters the asserted bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_5_of.summary: The divergence correction and its linear residual gain frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_7_of.text: The coefficient bounds of Proposition 5.1 and the product estimates of Lemma D.1 give Lemma 5.7. The proof derives $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$, bounds the inverse coframe, and applies the derivative-word estimate on the weighted and unweighted time intervals. A phase-independent profile removes every fast derivative. Global smoothness and periodic extension are already carried by the lattice-twisted profile type, so the support assumption is not used to construct an extension here.

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_8_of.text: This conditional proof supplies oddExpansions_of to lemma_5_8_of_odd. The assembled conclusion is the smooth periodic odd divergence free approximate velocity, its pressure and residual equation, the amplitude and Hölder bounds, and the separated hierarchy-tail and activation contributions to the residual. The cited inputs are Lemma 5.3, Proposition 5.4, Lemma 5.5, Theorem 5.6 and Lemma 5.7; their consumption is in the two builders rather than the three-line wrapper.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_8_of.summary: The approximate Euler solution and its bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_9_of.text: The proof assembles four claims: the leading pressure has an upper Hessian bound, the higher and mean pressure Hessians have absolute bounds, and the central derivative remainder is small. Each claim is proved from the supplied Paper statements and then passed to the assembly theorem. For the leading pressure remainder, the proof obtains its profile norm from Theorem 5.6 at level one, whereas the paper cites Lemma 5.3 for that estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_9_of.summary: Pressure Hessian bounds and the central gradient return

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_6_1_of.text: Assuming Lemma 2.2, this theorem proves the full Lemma 6.1 statement. Explicit first-wave formulas supply existence. The reflection estimate gives propagation relative to the seed, the initial normalization gives the strength bounds, and the cited frame identities keep the coupling above $\pi$. The general ODE existence route described in the paper is replaced by a direct check of formulas.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_6_1_of.summary: The first wave estimates from the frame identities

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_A_2.text: Combines the two base inverses with exponent $145$, taking the larger of their constants so that one pair serves both Hilbert spaces. For each higher order it uses preservation of the Hölder class, unique preimages, and bounded forward and inverse maps. The two supplied base equivalences agree because both represent the same compression. This is a leaf of the numbered proof spine; its source calls the library results that carry the freezing and continuation arguments.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_A_2.summary: Spatial freezing for both projection spaces

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1.text: Builds the complete cutoff lemma from the inverse Fourier kernel. Its operator constant is the kernel mass, its Bernstein constants are sums of derivative masses, and its tail constants come from absolute moments. All are fixed before the scale and field. The proof separately handles complex fields and real velocities, then proves Bernstein in any real normed target. There are no numbered theorem hypotheses; the kernel and differentiation lemmas are its library inputs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1.summary: The convolution proof of the cutoff estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_1.text: The proof first writes each weighted estimate as an unweighted estimate for $f/\gamma(t)$. Positive amplitude recovers smoothness of the original field when needed. It applies the derivative count, bilinear Leibniz estimate and phase-integral bounds, and supplies boundedness of every output jet. The half-Hölder product estimate comes directly from its algebra inequality. Display (D.2) is not used by this leaf proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_1.summary: Differentiation and phase integration prove Lemma D.1

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2.text: The proof handles products by bilinear Leibniz bounds and inverses by the iterated derivative estimate for inversion. It converts between coordinate derivative sums and operator norms with explicit order constants. The final part factors $\ell_*^mD^{a(m+1)}$ and retains one radius factor at positive order. Constants are selected before the parameter and fields, and each calculation uses the natural exponents of the formal statement.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2.summary: Leibniz inverse derivatives and coefficient weights

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_3.text: The proof replaces each coefficient bound by its nonnegative part, sets the unused order-zero bound to zero, and chooses an explicit constant before the spaces and operators. Exact-order bounds are converted to bounds for individual derivative words. It then applies the library lifting argument, which differentiates the equation and inducts on word length. The proof is a leaf and takes no other numbered theorem as a premise.

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_2_8_o.text: The proof assumes Lemmas 2.4 through 2.7. The reference lemma supplies the turning time, amplitude formula, maximum, and gain. The amplitude comparison gives nonvanishing and logarithmic closeness, while the coupling lemma gives a continuous positive denominator and the late ratio bounds. Wave-number control comes from Lemma 2.4. These inputs yield the crossing, strength constants, and early-gain conclusion without assuming a crossing in advance.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_2_8_o.summary: Crossing strength and the initial amplitude gain

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_.text: Applies Lemma B.1 clause by clause to the cutoff: parity, divergence, frequency support, spatial and time derivative commutation, and the real and complex tail bounds. Lemma 5.8 supplies the approximate stage; Lemma 5.9 supplies its signed pressure comparison; the explicit hypothesis for (5.59) supplies the quadratic Hölder estimate in exists_cutoffBounds. A constructed zero-mean Poisson pressure is identified with the pressure of any given truncation by periodicPoissonPressure_unique. Slab suprema give the combined error estimate, and adding the approximate-pressure Hessian bound gives (5.57). The source docstring calls pressure uniqueness the content of this row, while ledger decision D20 classifies that uniqueness result as glue; the source-level proof supports the latter classification.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_.summary: Fourier truncation gives the child Euler stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_1_o.text: This proof takes the statements of Lemmas B.1 and D.2 as explicit inputs. Bernstein estimates control the parent derivatives; higher flow variations yield $D^{5n-4}$, hence deformation derivatives with power $D^{5m+1}$. Product, inverse and composition arguments bound the remaining coefficients. The final weighted sums absorb derivative growth through $\ell\le D^{-C}$. The implementation chooses a sufficient absolute exponent, not an optimized one, and the highlighted proof ranges distinguish these steps from the proposition’s formal statement.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_1_o.summary: Deriving parent coefficients from Bernstein and coefficient rules

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_2_o.text: The proof takes Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.1, the Hölder comparison and display (5.14) as inputs. It extracts $v$ from MeanSolution, sets $g=(D_aX)^T\bar f$, and controls the final product $B=D_aXv$. One implementation detail differs from the prose: it first estimates $g$ in the order-$n+1$ supremum norm and then applies the Hölder comparison to $g$. The resulting estimate still loses exactly one source derivative and retains an exponent independent of $n$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_2_o.summary: The mean inverse loses one supremum derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_4_o.text: Theorem 4.2 is the only numbered hypothesis of this proof. It gives solvability and uniqueness for the normalized mean equation. A separate transverse ordinary differential equation and the localized seed then give the profiles, while the final call proves their divergence, momentum and support identities. The envelope exponent starts at $a_0=3$, ensuring that the support fits inside the label cell. The conclusion is the complete predicate of Proposition 5.4, including existence and uniqueness.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_4_o.summary: Construct the finite expansion and prove its residual identity

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o.text: Lemma 1.3 and the product estimate (5.59) suffice for the conditional proof of Proposition 8.1. Vanishing oscillations before activation and the remaining increment bounds give convergence on each earlier interval. The projected Euler equation passes to the limit using the product bound. Periodic uniqueness identifies the resulting solution with every maximal solution having the same initial data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o.summary: The Euler limit from order growth and products

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_2_o.text: This proof uses Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.4 and B.1 to establish Proposition 8.2 for a construction and Euler limit supplied by its hypotheses. The helper theorem proves bounded velocity, the divergence of central curl and its quantitative interval lower bound. The four inputs control the schedule, frame evolution, wave geometry and Bernstein estimates, respectively.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_2_o.summary: Bounded velocity and vorticity growth from four lemmas

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_4_o.text: Assuming Lemma 1.3, the proof obtains growth of the derivative orders. It constructs the continuous limit on the closed time interval and uses shrinking oscillation supports to obtain every local spatial trace away from the origin. Agreement with the Euler solution transfers those traces to the velocity. The final step controls the time derivative through local velocity jets and the near and far pressure operators.

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2.text:
This proof establishes the main paper’s existential smooth-extension remark from the specialized auxiliary library theorem. It extracts one scheduled construction and one Euler singularity witness. Periodic Euler uniqueness and maximality add equality of lifetimes and agreement for any second maximal solution from the same initial data. The global periodic extension supplies the required terminal neighborhood. Decision D28 identifies this as a library proof, exempt from the one-to-one auxiliary spine route.

This proves the existential remark without discharging the generalized auxiliary reference theorem for arbitrary admitted cutoffs, thresholds and constructions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2.summary: The library witness gives the terminal extension

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2_of.text: Assuming hAux_1_1 proves the generalized auxiliary theorem, this wrapper chooses a cutoff symbol, takes the envelope floor to be zero, obtains an admissible threshold and a sufficiently large frequency, and projects a singularity witness with its smooth extension. This route is retained but unused after decision D28. The active spine proves the remark from auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness instead; hAux_1_1 is not discharged here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2_of.summary: Obtain the remark from the generalized auxiliary theorem

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_1_1_of.text: Assumes exactly the four cited Section 8 results and the existence of the construction fixed there. Proposition 8.1 provides the solution and initial data; Proposition 8.2 provides the terminal velocity and curl properties; Corollary 8.3 provides maximality and both divergent integrals; Proposition 8.4 provides both off-origin limits. The final two lines combine maximal-time equality with common-interval agreement. This is a conditional assembly theorem; the spine supplies its assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_1_1_of.summary: Main singularity theorem from the Section 8 construction

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_4_2_of.text: Assuming Lemma 4.1, Theorem A.1 and Lemma A.2, this proof establishes Theorem 4.2. It rescales the endpoint equation to unit time, obtains coercivity from the displacement inequalities, and applies Theorem A.1. It then recovers the smooth forced equation and applies Lemma A.2 at each time. A common polynomial absorbs both bounds. The smooth branch differentiates the projected residual and reconstructs a zero-mean pressure; it does not prove the paper’s identification $\mathsf q=-\phi_t$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_4_2_of.summary: Deriving the endpoint inverse from three results

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of.text: Obtains the uniform numerical recurrence from master_recurrence and the structural support facts from Proposition 5.4. It chooses the final parent exponent as 6c and applies the abstract induction with derivative budget H = n + 3p + 1. The first level is handled separately, and levelConstant_indep removes artificial dependence on the surrounding depth. The resulting level estimates have the stated λ exponents; finite sums give the three global bounds and the direct remainder estimate gives the tail. Uniformity concerns the exponent of D, not constants C_(n,p) or C_(m,P).
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of.summary: All order hierarchy bounds from the finite recurrence

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of.text: This conditional proof takes exactly the thirteen numbered results cited by Theorem 7.1. It chooses the cutoff and expansion constants before the admissible threshold, constructs the stationary base and every later wave, and assembles one sequence with all the quantitative conclusions and step identities. Highlighted ranges identify a particular part of this construction. The unconditional theorem supplies the thirteen inputs through the paper spine.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of.summary: The inductive sequence from the cited estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of.text:
Assuming Lemma A.2, solve the mixed projected equation, recover a continuous velocity by fixed-time inverses, and construct the displacement, constant field, and pressure gradient with uniqueness and a polynomial bound. For smooth data, mixed spatial derivative words and base-space instantaneous inverses recover time derivatives and joint smoothness; the proof does not use the higher-order spatial inverse clause in the way the TeX does.

If the freezing estimate has exponent $p_A$, the resulting velocity estimate uses exponent $2p_A+1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of.summary: Recovering the endpoint solution from the two freezing inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion.text:
This bundles convergence of the initial data in every spatial C^{m,1/2} norm, their oddness, incompressibility and smoothness, a smooth Euler solution u with normalized pressure p on [0,T), uniform convergence on each [0,S] with S < T, and oddness at all preterminal times. maximal_agreement quantifies over every maximal solution from u(0), placing its time at least T and identifying its velocity with u on [0,T). It does not by itself assert the existence of a separate longer maximal solution. Here the candidate Euler solution exists as one of the supplied fields.

The compared maximal lifespans are real-valued and hence finite. This conditional comparison does not by itself construct a maximal solution on a possibly infinite lifespan; Corollary 8.3 later establishes maximality at the accumulation time.

Default-value audit (b4): IsEulerSolution provides T > 0, spatial and temporal smoothness, periodicity and integrability of the normalized pressure. Smooth periodic slices make the real Hölder norms finite on the relevant times; the parent theorem also supplies Theorem71Conclusions, hence 0 < T < S_j. The convergence clause is vacuous for S < 0, which is harmless because it also quantifies over every positive S < T. Universal maximal_agreement alone can be vacuous if no maximal solution is supplied; later Corollary83Conclusions and the headline witness provide an actual maximal solution.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion.summary: A smooth Euler limit before the accumulation time

TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition82Conclusion.text:
The first two fields are Proposition 8.2: a uniform finite essential-supremum bound for u and |curl u(t,0)| → ∞ as t approaches T from within [0,T). The third is a quantitative lower bound exported from its proof: for all sufficiently large j and t in [t_j,t_{j+1}), |curl u(t,0)| is at least c₁ λ_{j−1}^{1/8} − C₁ λ_{j−1}^{1/32} − C₁ with c₁ > 0. The paper first bounds curl U_j with an older-frequency term; the export has passed to u and absorbed that term using the schedule. Corollary 8.3 uses this export in the Lean route.

Pointwise central blow-up alone does not imply divergence of its time integral; the quantitative crossing-interval lower bound is the additional information used by Corollary 8.3.

Default-value audit (b4): torusLInf remains in ℝ≥0∞: comparison with ENNReal.ofReal M rules out infinite velocity norm and does not convert infinity to zero. This bundle alone does not assert T > 0 or smoothness; without them a terminal filter can be empty and curl uses total fderiv. In Statement.proposition_8_2, Theorem71Conclusions and Proposition81Conclusions supply positive time, smoothness and a nontrivial terminal approach. The lower bound also relies on the parameter frequency schedule for positive real-power bases.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition82Conclusion.summary: Bounded velocity and divergent central vorticity

TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition84Conclusion.text:
This pairs HasOffOriginLimits for u and its Eulerian time derivative. Each predicate quantifies over every compact set K in the complement of the integer lattice and every finite spatial order m, then supplies a smooth-enough local limit field whose ambient spatial jets converge uniformly on K. The time derivative is derivWithin on [0,T), so time zero is read from the right. This is finite-order convergence on each compact set; SmoothTerminalExtension is the separate statement of joint smooth extension through T.

Default-value audit (b4): The bare bundle does not impose positive T or differentiability of u. For T ≤ 0 the terminal filter can be trivial, and derivatives of arbitrary fields can default to zero. Statement.proposition_8_4 supplies Theorem71Conclusions and Proposition81Conclusions, hence T > 0 and a smooth Euler solution. On that domain timeDerivative is the actual within derivative. Empty compact K is an allowed harmless subcase; the quantifier also covers every nonempty compact set avoiding the lattice.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition84Conclusion.summary: Off-origin limits for velocity and its time derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.ReferenceSlope.text:
Y is a supplied real function with Y(0) = 1 and, for every τ ≥ 0, within-[0,∞) derivative cos²φ(1−ε tan φ) − ετ sin(2φ)Y − Y². The half-line derivative makes the initial-time requirement one-sided. This predicate is a solution condition, not an existence or uniqueness theorem; those assertions are in Statement.lemma_2_5. It places no restriction on ε and no condition on values of Y at negative times.

Default-value audit (b4): The ODE is expressed with HasDerivWithinAt, so an arbitrary nondifferentiable function cannot satisfy it merely because deriv defaults to 0. The half-line has a unique derivative direction at every point including 0. The tangent uses an arctangent argument and never reaches a pole. The right-hand side has no reciprocal of Y, so the zero at the amplitude peak is admissible. No integral, supremum, ENNReal conversion, or square root is evaluated here.
TorusEuler.Paper.ReferenceSlope.summary: The reference Riccati initial value problem

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd.text:
The manuscript correction $C_q$ is the library field `u.C (q - 1)`. Thus the library stores a correction at the level of its source oscillation, while the paper writes $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$. This definition changes the index only. It does not make $C_1$ zero for an arbitrary family: the expansion predicate separately requires `u.C 0 = 0`. The distinction matters when comparing the revised formulas with library statements that retain the earlier indexing.

Default-value audit (b4): The only degenerate convention is natural subtraction q−1=0 at q=0. This aliases an out-of-range paper index to C₁; all paper uses restrict to q≥1. The raw definition does not force C₁=0. No derivative, integral, division, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd.summary: Correction indexed by its receiving level

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.CutoffSymbol.text:
This is the fixed symbol ψ from Appendix B. It is smooth on ℝ³, depends only on ‖ξ‖, lies between zero and one, equals one on the unit ball, and vanishes when ‖ξ‖>2. Smoothness makes the support inclusion agree with the compact-support formulation in the paper. The zero symbol cannot satisfy the unit-ball condition.

Default-value audit (b4): This predicate contains no numerical derivative, integral, quotient, supremum, ENNReal.toReal conversion or square root. ContDiff is a regularity assertion, not the value of a derivative. The condition ψ=1 on a nonempty ball excludes a trivial zero cutoff. The boundary ‖ξ‖=2 is handled by smoothness/continuity together with vanishing outside the closed ball.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.CutoffSymbol.summary: Smooth radial Fourier cutoff equal to one near zero

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion.text:
This predicate says the supplied R,S and family u follow the construction of §5.5 at depth P. It identifies R=R_U∘X and S=χ̃′A₁, fixes the switched leading velocity/pressure, C₁=B₁=q̄₁=0, all curl corrections, the mean and transverse solves for 2≤p≤P, and V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0. The mean pressure has zero integral over the centered label cell; the transverse pressure has zero phase mean. Identities involving the unperiodized leading fields are imposed only on the centered cell and extend through the lattice twist. This record specifies candidate data; Proposition 5.4 separately asserts existence and uniqueness of the slots actually used.

Default-value audit (b4): hT>0 and smooth profile types protect derivatives and phase integrals. The mean-pressure integral is real valued and smooth on a compact cell, so its zero value is a genuine gauge. The leading factors retain the positive-radius, positive-width and nonzero-covector requirements supplied by Parent, Launch and Origin in every theorem. The raw predicate does not assert P≥2: at small P some finite recurrences are vacuous, and arbitrary unused slots of u are unconstrained. No unbounded supremum or ENNReal.toReal occurs directly in this predicate.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion.summary: The equations defining the finite expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsSeed.text:
IsSeed describes an arbitrary amplitude on the active interval, rather than selecting one by choice. It records agreement with the prescribed center at the origin, the initial projection $(\mathrm{Id}-P_{\kappa(t_0,a)})\mathrm{center}(t_0)$, the homogeneous seed ODE, transversality and joint smoothness. The near-origin amplitude and coupling bounds are deliberately absent. They must be proved from the parent and central assumptions, which is why the bridge through seedNear_of_h51 adds substantive information.

Default-value audit (b4): The transverse projection and amplitude operator divide by ‖κ‖²; if κ=0 they take totalized algebraic values that need not model the seed equation. Parent with 0<T and Launch gives a genuine nonzero transported κ at every label. IsSeed.smooth and the HasDerivWithinAt field prevent a default derivative from satisfying the ODE merely as a numerical equality. Launch ensures t₀<T, so derivatives within the interval are unique, including its endpoints. Without that context the interval can be empty or a singleton. No integral, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root is used by the predicate.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsSeed.summary: A smooth seed with projected activation data

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation.text:
For given T,ψ,Λ,V,u,p, this identifies u with the real Fourier cutoff S_ΛV whenever a continuous torus field c lifts to V(t). It also requires every p(t) to be smooth, periodic, have zero mean on the centered cell, and solve Δp=−tr((∇u)²) on [0,T]. The cutoff equation is universal over representations c, not existential. Proposition 5.11 supplies a smooth periodic V, so a representation exists and the implication determines u. The predicate by itself does not assert Λ≥1, T>0, or regularity/periodicity of V.

Default-value audit (b4): If V has no continuous periodic lift, the cutoff implication is vacuous; the raw predicate then need not identify u at all. Proposition 5.11’s constructed V is smooth and periodic, which supplies the missing representation. It also assumes Λ≥1, excluding division by zero in ψ(ξ/Λ), and 0<T, excluding an empty slab. p’s smoothness protects the pressure Laplacian and its zero-mean integral; u’s spatial derivative is genuine once the cutoff identity is instantiated with a lift. Without that instantiation fderiv u could take its default zero. No ENNReal.toReal conversion occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation.summary: Fourier truncation with normalized Poisson pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Launch.text:
Launch records $0\le t_0<T$, a nonzero constant carrier $k_*$, and the exact equality $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$. It separates the frequency used to scale the wave profile from the norm of the carrier, which can differ because of deformation. The parent predicate supplies $\lambda\ge1$. Together these conditions support the two-sided bounds $D^{-1}\lambda\le|k_*|\le D\lambda$ and $D^{-2}\lambda\le|\kappa|\le D^2\lambda$ used later.

The fixed carrier is an arbitrary nonzero real vector, not necessarily a lattice vector; the twisted-profile representation later supplies physical periodicity.

Default-value audit (b4): The inequalities force T>0 and exclude an empty activation interval. On its own Launch does not assert that X is a flow or that its derivative is genuine, and can allow lam=0 if a bad X makes κ=0. Parent supplies lam≥1 and the smooth inverse-flow interpretation. There is no division, integral, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root in the record itself.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Launch.summary: Activation time and frequency at the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution.text:
For fixed d and profiles f,B,q, this is the mean equation B_t+MB+𝐝q=f, together with phase independence and an endpoint representation B=D_aX v. It supplies smooth periodic v,z with z_t=v, z(0)=z(T)=0 and div_a v=0. By the volume-preserving Piola identity this is the paper’s 𝐝·B=0 condition. The endpoint condition selects the initial mean velocity; it does not require B(0)=0. This predicate does not normalize the spatial mean of q; IsExpansion.mean adds that gauge.

The mean correction may be nonzero before activation; the two endpoint displacement conditions do not impose preactivation vanishing.

Default-value audit (b4): hT>0 excludes an empty or singleton endpoint interval. Profile and v,z smoothness protect the derivatives, and z_t=v is asserted with HasDerivWithinAt rather than an unguarded derivative equality. The scalar/vector phase averages are over smooth finite-dimensional-valued functions and hence integrable. The pressure-phase condition is κ∂s q=0; ParentGeometry’s nonzero κ makes it actual phase independence. A spatially constant q is an allowed gauge freedom here. There is no numerical supremum or ENNReal.toReal conversion in the predicate.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution.summary: Mean equation with zero endpoint displacement

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Origin.text:
For fixed parent data and center(t)=𝐚(t,0), this combines CenterWaveOn with lam^(3/4)‖center(t)‖≤1 on [t₀,T]. CenterWaveOn requires the covector and seed differential equations, nonvanishing and transversality, comparison of every transverse seed solution with center, and D⁻¹‖κ‖‖center‖≤κ·M center. This last inequality is the coupling condition ν≥D⁻¹ without dividing by the two norms. The normalization is only γ≤1; the paper’s equality max γ=1 is not asserted. The extra covector equation and its nonvanishing are consequences of the parent flow carried here for the library interface.

Default-value audit (b4): Inside CenterWaveOn, stability divides by ‖center(t)‖; nonzero explicitly rules out its zero-denominator fallback at every sampled time. Parent adds D≥2 and lam≥1, while Launch gives 0≤t₀<T. Consequently γ>0 on a nonempty compact interval, and its reciprocal is bounded because center has a derivative there. The raw structure can be vacuous on an empty [t₀,T] without Launch; its γ≤1 clause alone permits a zero weight without Parent and nonzero data. No integral, ENNReal.toReal or square root is used.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Origin.summary: Central seed conditions and upper normalization

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Parent.text:
For the fixed data T,U,X,pU,D,lam, this proposition records T≤1, D≥2 and lam≥1; a label flow of U; joint smoothness, periodicity, oddness and incompressibility of U; its Fourier support below 2D; the gradient and forward/reverse deformation bounds (5.1); and the pressure/residual conditions (5.2),(5.6). Fourier support and the residual supremum are expressed through continuous fields on the unit torus whose lifts equal the Euclidean fields. Unlike the paper’s convention, the structure does not require pU to be the zero-mean solution of its Poisson equation, nor separately require the residual to be divergence free. It admits any smooth periodic pressure with the listed residual properties. This is an input predicate, not an existence theorem.

Default-value audit (b4): Standalone Parent only assumes T≤1, so T<0 makes all slab-quantified clauses vacuous; the numbered statements add 0<T, and Launch also implies it. With 0<T, joint smoothness prevents default spatial and within-time derivatives; flow regularity follows from the smooth periodic parent, and the reverse transition is an actual inverse. D≥2 and lam≥1 prevent zero denominators and degenerate real powers. The residual bound is a norm of a continuous torus field, hence finite, rather than an unchecked real supremum. The pressure gauge is absent by design, not supplied by a zero-valued integral. No ENNReal.toReal occurs in the predicate.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Parent.summary: The parent assumptions for the finite expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.TransverseSolution.text:
This predicate records the transverse momentum equation, perpendicularity to the transported covector, zero phase mean of the velocity, zero initial velocity, and zero phase mean of the pressure. The last condition removes the pressure’s phase-constant ambiguity. It does not itself assume a zero-mean source; the statements using it supply that condition where needed. Existence and uniqueness are separate theorems, enabling Lemma 5.3 to estimate any normalized solution rather than only a chosen construction.

The profile types already carry full-slab smoothness, phase periodicity and the lattice twist.

Default-value audit (b4): Profile smoothness and hT>0 make the derivative operators genuine on the closed slab. q is real valued and smooth in phase, so pressure_mean_zero is an ordinary finite integral, not the default integral of a nonintegrable function. The transported covector is nonzero through d, which is needed for its physical pressure interpretation even though this record contains no explicit division. No unbounded supremum, ENNReal.toReal conversion or square root occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.TransverseSolution.summary: Transverse equation with zero start and normalized pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd.text:
The level-$p$ field $Y_p$ is $V_p+C_p$, with the correction read through the manuscript index convention. In the library this is `u.V p + u.C (p - 1)`. The correction is produced by the preceding oscillation, so this sum has the size of a level-$p$ oscillation in the induction. This definition contains no estimate and imposes no equation on its input family; those properties belong to the expansion predicate and the hierarchy theorem.

Default-value audit (b4): The inherited natural subtraction in Cd maps p=0 to storage slot zero. No regularity or transversality follows from this raw sum; those belong to IsExpansion. There are no analytic default values, integrals, divisions, suprema, ENNReal.toReal conversions or square roots in the sum.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd.summary: The oscillation and the preceding correction

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd.text:
The level field $Z_p$ adds the mean $B_p$ to $Y_p=V_p+C_p$. Its definition uses the manuscript correction index through `Yd`. It is the field entering the quadratic label-advection sums; its phase-dependent part is $Y_p$. The definition is algebraic for any profile family. Phase independence of the mean and the norm estimates are properties supplied by the mean equation and the expansion estimates, not by this sum alone.

Default-value audit (b4): The raw definition inherits Cd’s truncated predecessor at p=0, outside the positive paper indices. Addition itself has no junk-value convention. No derivative, integral, division, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root is evaluated by this definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd.summary: Oscillation, preceding correction and mean at one level

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.curlCorrection.text:
This is C[V]=𝐝×Q[V], with Q[V]=−∂s⁻¹((κ×V)/‖κ‖²). The argument d supplies the inverse deformation and nonzero phase-independent κ. The library completion is defined for every twisted profile by first handling its oscillatory part; the paper’s identity V+C[V]=𝐝̃×Q[V] requires V to have zero phase mean and be transverse. Those hypotheses are imposed where the completion is used in the expansion and its estimates.

Default-value audit (b4): The denominator ‖κ‖² is protected by d.oscillation.covector_ne_zero, explicitly passed to complete. Phase independence is also passed. Smooth real/vector profiles on a period give genuine integrable primitives, and hT>0 protects within-slab derivatives. For inputs without zero phase mean, completion uses the oscillatory part rather than asserting that the displayed C[V] identity holds for arbitrary V. This is a domain convention, not a hidden proof of transversality. No unbounded real supremum or ENNReal.toReal occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.curlCorrection.summary: Divergence correction obtained from the wave potential

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.envelopeSupport.text:
This takes the topological support of the envelope after periodic extension from the centered cell. The raw envelope is g(a)=χ(‖a‖/ℓ), using the fixed smooth cutoff in ActivationProfiles. periodizeCentered selects a representative in the half-open centered label cell, so this support is repeated across all lattice translates. Outside this set the oscillatory profiles and their sources vanish. It is not just one Euclidean ball when viewed on ℝ³.

Default-value audit (b4): radialEnvelope divides by ℓ. At ℓ=0 the quotient is zero everywhere, so the envelope is identically one and its support is all space, not a localized ball. radius with D≥2 gives ℓ>0. A sufficiently large exponent additionally keeps the support away from the cell boundary, making periodic extension smooth. tsupport is a topological closure, not a numerical supremum; no unbounded-sSup fallback is involved. No integral or ENNReal.toReal occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.envelopeSupport.summary: Spatial support repeated over the label lattice

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion.text:
The retained velocity is $W=\sum_{p=1}^{P}(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$. The finite index range begins at one and ends at $P$; the last divergence correction is consequently $C_{P+1}$. Proposition 5.4 proves that this equals $\sum_{p=1}^{P}Z_p+C_{P+1}$ for an admissible expansion. This definition is only the finite sum. Its divergence, momentum residual and support properties are conclusions of the proposition, using the equations of the individual profiles.

This is the profile perturbation; the corresponding physical velocity is $U+W^\natural$.

Default-value audit (b4): At P=0 the finite interval is empty and W is zero. The section’s substantive statements assume P≥2. No regularity, divergence cancellation or size estimate follows from the bare sum. Cd(p+1) uses ordinary positive predecessors, so no natural-subtraction boundary is reached here. Analytic defaults occur only inside already supplied profiles, not in this algebraic definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion.summary: Finite velocity expansion including the final correction

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansionPressure.text:
The profile pressure is the finite sum $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^{P}(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$. Here the oscillatory pressures have zero phase mean and the mean pressures are independent of the phase in an admissible expansion. The condition $\bar q_1=0$ is supplied separately by the expansion predicate. This definition only adds the two pressure components at each retained level; it does not solve the pressure equations or choose their normalization.

In an admissible expansion each mean pressure also has zero spatial integral, a gauge imposed by `IsExpansion.mean`, not by this finite sum.

Default-value audit (b4): The sum is zero for P=0 and the statements use P≥2. The definition by itself does not impose either pressure gauge; those are predicates on the input family. No derivative, integral, division, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs in the finite sum.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.fieldNorm.text:
For any real normed space E, time set A, scalar multiplier τ and natural order n, this sums the suprema of the spatial and phase derivatives of τ(t)f(t,a,s) through total order n. The derivative directions already include the factors ℓ and h. The library enumerates canonical sorted words, so each label multi-index and phase order is counted once. There are no time derivatives: τ is constant during each differentiated slice. The argument False selects supremum norms, not half-Hölder quotients. On smooth bounded fields with positive scales this is the finite norm (D.1), with the time domain and multiplier made explicit.

Because the multiplier depends only on time, applying it before or after label and phase differentiation gives the same weighted derivative; it is never differentiated in these norms.

Default-value audit (b4): This raw definition assumes neither differentiability nor boundedness. A derivative of a nonsmooth input can take Mathlib’s default zero. Each hierarchyJetValues set contains 0, but an unbounded set has real supremum 0; a small result alone therefore proves no bound. Empty A gives the set {0} at every word and hence zero. A zero ℓ or h kills derivatives in that direction; τ=0 kills the entire field. S5 applications use positive scales, a nonempty closed time interval, smooth twisted profiles and a bounded multiplier. The relevant boundedness lemma is hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_bddAbove_weighted (HierarchyActualNorms.lean:330). No integral, ENNReal.toReal or square root is evaluated because holder=False.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.fieldNorm.summary: Finite norms from scaled derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.launchNorm.text:
