This is the finite norm of f(t₀,a,s) with time restricted to the singleton {t₀}. It supplies the initial-data term in (5.20). The singleton restricts only which slice is sampled; the differentiated variables remain a and s, so this is not a derivative within a singleton time set.

Default-value audit (b4): A time outside [0,T] reads the smooth profile’s stipulated zero extension, giving a zero slice irrespective of the interior data. Launch puts t₀ inside [0,T]; smoothness and the compact periodic quotient then bound all sampled jets. Real sSup must still be read with these guards, and zero ℓ or h suppresses the corresponding derivatives. There is no reciprocal weight, integration, ENNReal.toReal conversion or square root here.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leading.text:
The raw leading field is $(g(a)F_h(s))\mathbf a(t,a)$, with the selected radialEnvelope and waveProfile definitions. It is defined directly on the active time interval’s ambient variables, so its norm in Lemma 5.3 does not first require a smooth extension to the entire time slab. The time switch is applied elsewhere. The paper permits an arbitrary fixed smooth cutoff with the stated plateau and support; this implementation commits to one such cutoff.

Default-value audit (b4): The envelope contains division by ℓ. waveProfile is an interval integral of waveSlope, whose construction divides by h and by 1−the bump’s phase mean. For arbitrary scales these total operations can lose their intended meaning. Parent and radius/width give ℓ>0 and 0<h≤1; the latter ensures a positive slope denominator and smooth periodic integrands, so the integral is genuine. IsSeed supplies smooth amp on the activation interval. The raw definition alone has none of these guards. No supremum or ENNReal.toReal is used.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leadingPressure.text:
This is −2g(a)(κ·M𝐚)/‖κ‖² times P_h(s), where P_h is the zero-mean periodic primitive of F_h. The minus sign is part of the pressure formula. U and X provide the actual strain and transported covector; amp is the proposed seed. It is the unswitched pressure paired with A₁, not the parent pressure pU and not the sum of all hierarchy pressures.

Default-value audit (b4): The coefficient divides by ‖κ‖², so κ=0 would silently force that coefficient to zero. Parent, positive slab length and Launch exclude this. The envelope and phase primitives inherit the ℓ>0, 0<h≤1 requirements described for leading; with these guards the phase integrals are over smooth real functions and cannot vanish merely because they are undefined. The raw definition accepts bad data and gives no nonzero or regularity certificate itself. There is no real supremum or ENNReal.toReal conversion here.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource.text:
The preliminary source $H_p$ contains the material derivative of $C_p$, the label gradient of $\mathsf p_{p-1}$, and the two quadratic sums of total levels $p$ and $p+1$. At level two it subtracts the completion of the activation term. For $p\ge3$ that subtraction is zero, giving the displayed formula directly. The correction is indexed as in the revised manuscript, so $C_p$ comes from $V_{p-1}$ and does not require the new oscillation $V_p$.

Default-value audit (b4): At p=0 or p=1, natural predecessor indices and empty finite sums produce total algebraic values that are not the H_p of the paper. IsExpansion only uses this source for 2≤p≤P. There is no analytic operation intrinsic to this definition beyond the supplied operators A; their derivative and average guards must come from ops d when interpreted physically. No ENNReal.toReal or square root is introduced.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource.summary: The source formed from preceding profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource.text:
The mean forcing is $\bar f_p=-\langle H_p\rangle$, except that the transported parent residual is also subtracted at $p=2$. The argument `R` represents $R_U\circ X$ and the argument `cS` represents the activation correction already removed from $H_2$. This definition follows the revised correction index through `levelSource`. It supplies the right side of the mean equation; its solution and its norm bound require the separate endpoint result.

Default-value audit (b4): The conditional p=2 branch and finite algebra are total. An arbitrary R or abstract average need not produce a genuine mean field; the concrete geometry and IsExpansion.residual supply those properties. Phase integrals in ops d are over smooth real/vector profiles. No new division, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs. Levels below two are outside the paper’s intended source range.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource.summary: Mean forcing including the parent residual

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.ops.text:
This abbreviation packages the actions ∂t+M, the label gradient 𝐝, the phase gradient κ∂s, label advection, phase advection and phase averaging. Its argument d is a ParentGeometry for the actual parent U,X,k; d carries smooth coefficient profiles and identifications with the inverse deformation, strain and covector. It acts on smooth lattice-twisted profiles. An equation using (ops d).material is therefore an equation in the profile space, including the inherited zero extension outside [0,T].

Default-value audit (b4): The operators contain derivatives within the positive-length slab and phase integrals. hT:0<T and smooth profile types ensure genuine derivatives on the slab; finite-dimensional vector/scalar values and smooth phase-periodic slices make the phase means integrable. Outside the slab the representative is intentionally zero and carries no physical claim. No inverse of a possibly singular matrix is selected here: d supplies the actual coefficient identities. No ENNReal.toReal is used in this alias.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource.text:
The oscillatory forcing is $f_p=-(H_p-\langle H_p\rangle)$. The definition uses the preliminary source with the special activation subtraction at level two. Its negative sign is part of the definition; adding $H_p$ to this forcing leaves its phase average. The supplementary forcing caused by transport under the means is a separate term. The transverse equation uses the sum of those two forcings, after the new mean has been determined.

For an arbitrary abstract operator package, zero phase average is not automatic; it uses idempotence of the actual phase-average operator.

Default-value audit (b4): There is no new division or analytic choice here; any integral is hidden in the supplied A.average. In the concrete profile operators it averages smooth finite-dimensional-valued periodic functions and is genuine. The paper uses p≥2, which avoids the artificial predecessor indices in levelSource. Arbitrary abstract averaging maps need not make this expression mean zero. No supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource.summary: Negative centered part of the preliminary source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.radius.text:
The radius is defined by $\ell_*=(D^a)^{-1}$ for a natural-number exponent $a$. Paper statements first choose a threshold $a_0$, then quantify over every $a\ge a_0$, and only afterward choose the order-independent exponent in their estimates. This order of quantifiers permits one radius to absorb all derivative costs without making its exponent depend on the differentiation order. Positivity follows from $D\ge2$.

Default-value audit (b4): At D=0 and a>0 the inverse is Lean’s zero, so ℓ_* would fail to be a positive radius. Parent enforces D≥2, hence D^a>0 and ℓ_*>0. At a=0 the radius is 1 and support localization inside the cell fails; sufficiently large a₀, rather than the raw definition, supplies the small-radius condition. No derivative, integral, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder.text:
The remainder contains $(\partial_t+M)C_{P+1}+\mathbf d\mathsf p_P$, label interactions with $i+j\ge P+1$, and phase interactions with $i+j\ge P+2$. Both indices range from one to $P+1$. This is the literal finite-sum expression in the revised manuscript. The expansion predicate sets the top oscillation and mean to zero, so the top field is only $C_{P+1}$. Bounds and phase independence outside the envelope are later theorems about this expression.

The activation contribution $S+C[S]$ is separate from this retained tail.

Default-value audit (b4): The formula is defined even at P=0, but its residual interpretation requires P≥2 and all IsExpansion recurrences and top conventions. Without those constraints it is simply an expression in arbitrary profiles and operators. Positive shifted indices avoid predecessor underflow. No new derivative, integral, division, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root is chosen here; concrete operator guards are inherited from ops d.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder.summary: The linear and quadratic terms beyond the depth

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.strainField.text:
This is M(t,a)=(D_xU)(t,X(t,a)). Its value is a continuous linear map on Euclidean three-space, so subsequent norms are operator norms. X 0 t is the transition from time zero to t; the direction of these two time arguments matters.

Default-value audit (b4): fderiv ℝ (U t) can equal its default zero on a nonsmooth slice. Parent.velocity_smooth gives genuine spatial derivatives for every t∈[0,T], which is where the estimates use M. No regularity is claimed for values outside that slab. There is no division, integration, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root in this definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.strainField.summary: Parent velocity gradient along a trajectory

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource.text:
The supplementary forcing is the negative sum $-\sum_{i=2}^{p}(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_{p+1-i}$. Its last term involves the newly found mean $B_p$ and the leading oscillation $Y_1=V_1$ of an admissible expansion. The other factors belong to earlier levels. This is why the mean equation is solved first. Phase independence of the means and the covector makes each summand have zero phase average; that fact is proved separately.

Default-value audit (b4): If p<2 the finite sum is empty and equals zero. For the actual summation range 2≤i≤p, p+1−i≥1, so natural subtraction never folds a valid term into an unintended zero-level slot. Generic A.phaseAdv carries no analytic certificate by itself; ops d provides smooth differentiation. No integral, division, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root is introduced in this definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource.summary: The mean transport of the oscillatory profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.totalDivergence.text:
This is 𝐝̃·W=(𝐝+κ∂s)·W, expressed as the sum of the label divergence determined by d.inverse and the phase derivative contracted with d.covector. The output is a smooth scalar profile. A zero output in Proposition 5.4 is the divergence cancellation needed before graph evaluation produces an Eulerian incompressible velocity.

Default-value audit (b4): The underlying derivatives are applied to smooth profile slices and along a slab with hT>0, so they do not use the zero derivative of a nonsmooth field on that domain. The type’s zero extension outside the slab is intentional and carries no assertion about Eulerian regularity there. The definition has no division, integration, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.totalDivergence.summary: Divergence with label and phase derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.uNorm.text:
This measures all label and phase derivatives through order n on [0,T], with scales ℓ and h and multiplier one. It is the norm used for the mean corrections, which need not vanish before activation. Smoothness and both periodicity conditions are carried by the profile type. The norm contains no time derivatives.

Default-value audit (b4): For an arbitrary T<0 the time set is empty and the value is zero. At positive T, smooth lattice-twisted profiles have bounded spatial and phase jets on the compact quotient; hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_bddAbove_weighted supplies the requisite BddAbove statements. Thus the unbounded-supremum fallback is excluded in the stated theorems. The definition by itself does not require ℓ,h>0, so zero scales can suppress higher derivatives. Parent with radius/width supplies positive scales. No division, integral, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs in this specialization.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.wNorm.text:
wNorm specializes fieldNorm to the active interval $[t_0,T]$ and the reciprocal weight $\gamma(t)^{-1}$. Derivative words use the scaled label and phase directions before the time weight multiplies the resulting field. Thus the estimate measures oscillatory corrections relative to the central amplitude without differentiating that amplitude in label or phase. The underlying profiles are smooth on the entire slab, even though only their active restrictions are measured; the active-profile library theorem has the broader time-domain interface.

Default-value audit (b4): If γ(t)=0, Lean sets γ(t)⁻¹=0 and erases that time slice rather than assigning infinite size. An unbounded reciprocal can also make a real sSup collapse to zero. Parent gives lam≥1; Origin.wave.nonzero gives center(t)≠0, and its derivative assertion gives continuity on [t₀,T]. Compactness then bounds the positive reciprocal. Launch gives 0≤t₀<T, so the sampled times lie in the smooth slab. Without those contextual guards, the bare definition is not a norm with the advertised interpretation. If t₀>T the sampled interval is empty and the value is zero. No ENNReal.toReal conversion occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.wNorm.summary: The active norm relative to the central amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.waveVector.text:
The Paper vocabulary defines $\kappa(t,a)$ by the library labelWaveVector, with reference time zero and fixed carrier $k_*$. The library formula transports a covector by the transpose of the inverse flow derivative. Consequently this is the same geometric field as $(D_aX)^{-T}k_*$ in the parent setup. Nonvanishing and quantitative frequency bounds are proved separately from invertibility of the flow and the launch-frequency equality; they are not built into this definition.

Default-value audit (b4): An arbitrary reverse map can be nondifferentiable, in which case its fderiv is zero and κ can collapse to zero even for k≠0. Parent plus 0<T gives differentiable inverse transitions; Launch supplies k≠0, so κ is nonzero on the whole slab. These facts are needed by downstream divisions by ‖κ‖². No division, integral, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs in this definition itself.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.waveVector.summary: The wave vector transported by inverse deformation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.weight.text:
The weight is $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathrm{center}(t)|$. It measures transverse corrections relative to the central seed and removes its changing amplitude from the forward estimates. Origin supplies both nonvanishing of the center and an upper normalization, so the active norm can divide by $\gamma$ safely in the subsequent argument. Label and phase derivatives act on the field before this time-dependent factor is applied; derivatives of $\gamma$ are not part of those spatial norms.

Default-value audit (b4): The raw function can be zero when center(t)=0 or the frequency is zero. Those cases would erase the slice in wNorm because 0⁻¹=0. Parent gives lam≥1 and Origin.wave.nonzero gives center(t)≠0, so γ>0 on [t₀,T]. A positive continuous function on this compact interval is bounded away from zero, excluding an unbounded reciprocal in the real supremum. No integral, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs in weight.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.width.text:
This definition fixes $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ using the real power function. It is the width of the phase profile $F_h$ and the weight attached to each phase derivative in the finite-order norm. Combining its size with the central seed scale $\lambda^{-3/4}$ gives the leading velocity scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$. Positivity and the bound $h\le1$ follow from the parent assumption $\lambda\ge1$ rather than from the definition alone.

Default-value audit (b4): Real.rpow is a total operation even at zero or a negative base; those cases need not represent a positive profile width. Parent.frequency_ge_one excludes them. In particular 0<h≤1 also keeps the denominator 1−phaseMean(periodicWaveBump h) in waveSlope strictly positive. This definition itself has no derivative, integral, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root call.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Cd_reflFamily.text: Unfolding the completed-family component gives the divergence correction as the negated reflection of the original correction. This is a definitional identity, not a new estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.CoefBounds.text:
Bounds `NG n`, `Nk n` for the norms (D.1) of the coefficients `(D_aX)⁻¹` and `κ` on every time set in `[0,T]`.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate includes finite coefficient norms on every allowed time subset and their stated upper bounds. An empty subset is allowed but is not used to infer a nontrivial slab bound; the application supplies the actual slab and positive scales.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.CoefBounds.summary: Uniform bounds for the coframe and wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.EvenGeometry.text:
The parities of the coefficient profiles of an odd parent: `(D_aX)⁻¹`, `M`, `κ` are even.

Default-value audit (b5): A structure containing three parity equalities. It is not a new geometric construction and does not imply existence of an odd parent; evenGeometry proves it from the parent data.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.EvenGeometry.summary: Even coefficients for the reflected hierarchy

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.text:
The standing data of the norms: `T, ℓ, h > 0`, `0 ≤ t₀ ≤ T`, and the weight `γ` continuous, positive and at most one on `[t₀,T]`.

Default-value audit (b5): The structure explicitly excludes zero or negative scales and time length, requires 0 ≤ t₀ ≤ T, and imposes continuous positive weights at most one on the active interval. These conditions rule out degenerate reciprocal weights in subsequent norm comparisons.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.summary: Positive scales and weights on the time slab

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.active.text: The active interval lies in `[0, T]`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.active.summary: The active interval lies in the full slab

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finP.summary: Finiteness of the active unweighted profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finU.summary: Finiteness of the full unweighted profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.invBoun.text: The inverse bound of a norm setting.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.invBoun.summary: The reciprocal weight is bounded on the active interval

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.weight_.text: The weight of a norm setting is positive.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.OddExpansions.text:
This proposition asks for a threshold in a above which the physical perturbation of every permitted expansion is odd. It isolates the symmetry input needed by the quantitative approximation argument. oddExpansions_of establishes it from the parity of the construction and the uniqueness clause of Proposition 5.4.

Default-value audit (b5): A proposition over permitted expansions, not a choice of an expansion. It can be vacuous if there are no admissible expansions; later uses combine it with the existence clause of Proposition 5.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.OddExpansions.summary: Oddness of every sufficiently separated expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_U.text: The plain seminorm is at most the `U` seminorm.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_U.summary: The full slab norm controls the active unweighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_W.text: The plain seminorm is at most the `W` seminorm.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_W.summary: The weighted norm controls the active unweighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.text:
A field is independent of the phase.

Default-value audit (b5): A universal equality predicate, meaningful for every field. It does not supply differentiability; the derivative consequences add smoothness hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.eq_comp.text: A phase-independent field is its own composition with `(a, s) ↦ (a, 0)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.eq_comp.summary: A phase independent field ignores the phase coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.fderiv_e.text: The derivative of a phase-independent smooth field only sees the label component of the increment.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.fderiv_e.summary: Only label increments affect phase independent fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.labelPar.text: Label derivatives of a phase-independent smooth field are phase independent.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.phasePar.text: The phase derivative of a phase-independent smooth field vanishes.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.phasePar.summary: Phase derivatives vanish for phase independent fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.S_eq_smul.text: `S = χ̃' V` (the activation term, the same for `χ̃'`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.S_eq_smul.summary: Activation is the derivative of the switch

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_le_W.text: The `U` seminorm is at most the `W` seminorm for profiles vanishing before `t0`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_le_W.summary: The weighted norm controls an initially vanishing profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_mono.text: For derivative orders n ≤ m, the unweighted seminorm of order n is at most that of order m. The statement compares derivative orders of one profile and makes no monotonicity assertion in the hierarchy index.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_mono.summary: Unweighted norms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Un.text:
The unweighted norm on `[0,T]` as a seminorm.

Default-value audit (b5): NormSetting supplies a positive time slab and smooth twisted profiles, which make the unweighted seminorm finite. It includes the whole slab; controlling it by an active weighted norm additionally requires vanishing before activation.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_eq_smul.text: `V₁ = χ̃ V`: for a twisted profile `V` equal to `A₁` on `[t₀,T] × cell`, the first velocity `V₁ = χ̃A₁` (on the cell) is `χ̃ V` on the whole slab (lattice twist; before `t₀` both vanish).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_eq_smul.summary: The first velocity is the switched leading wave

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_transverse.text: `V₁ = χ̃A₁` is transverse: `κ·V₁ = 0` on the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_transverse.summary: The leading velocity is transverse to the wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.VanishBefore.text:
A profile vanishing for `t < t₀`.

Default-value audit (b5): A universal vanishing predicate restricted to [0,T] and t < t₀. At t₀ = 0 it is vacuous; equality at the activation time is obtained from the relevant smoothness or cutoff data when needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.VanishBefore.summary: A profile vanishes before the activation time

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.W_mono.text: For derivative orders n ≤ m, the weighted seminorm of order n is at most that of order m. The variables being compared are derivative orders, not hierarchy levels; this corrects the loose use of “level” in the source docstring.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.W_mono.summary: Weighted norms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Wn.text:
The weighted norm as a seminorm.

Default-value audit (b5): NormSetting supplies continuous positive weights and a compact nonempty active interval, so the amplitude seminorm is finite. The weighted norm is meaningful at every permitted derivative order; controlling the whole slab additionally requires preactivation vanishing.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Wn.summary: Weighted active profile norms as seminorms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Yd_reflFamily.text: `Yd` commutes with the reflection of a family.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Yd_reflFamily.summary: Reflection of the completed oscillatory velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Zd_reflFamily.text: `Zd` commutes with the reflection of a family.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_average.text: The activation term has zero phase mean.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_average.summary: The activation source has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_eval.text: The activation term on the slab: `S = χ̃' · (twisted extension of A₁)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_eval.summary: Activation is the differentiated time cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_holder.text: Assumes an active-interval C^(1,1/2) bound Bγ(t) for the extended leading profile together with its divergence correction. At a fixed time, the activation source and its correction are χ̃′ times this pair, so homogeneity gives the bound B times χ.derivativeSize γ. Before activation both terms vanish. The estimates for B are supplied by the caller from Lemmas 5.3 and 5.5 and Lemma 5.7; this helper does not itself take those numbered hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_holder.summary: Bounding the activation error in physical space

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_divergence.text: The physical velocity $U+W^\natural$ is divergence free when the parent is divergence free and the profile has zero total label-phase divergence. The chain rule identifies the physical divergence of the evaluated profile with that total divergence. The result uses the parent flow and inverse coframe; it does not replace the total divergence condition by a statement about label derivatives alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_divergence.summary: Solenoidality after evaluation on the graph

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual.text: The physical velocity and pressure satisfy the Euler momentum identity with the evaluated profile residual. The input profile identity contains the negative pullback of the parent residual. Material differentiation along the parent flow and the spatial chain rules convert all remaining terms to Eulerian coordinates. Evaluation of the pulled-back parent residual at inverse labels cancels it exactly, leaving the specified profile remainder and activation terms.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual.summary: The parent residual cancels in physical space

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_smooth.text: Adding the graph of a smooth lattice-twisted velocity profile to the parent gives a jointly smooth spatially periodic velocity; the analogous pressure is smooth and periodic as well. The parent supplies regularity of its inverse flow. This result establishes these regularity properties for arbitrary profiles before any hierarchy equations are used. Oddness, zero divergence and the residual identity are proved separately for the actual expansion.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_first.text: `⟨V₁⟩ = 0`: `V₁` agrees on the cell with the bridge profile of `χ̃A₁` (`Bridge.leadingVelocityProfile`), whose phase average vanishes.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_first.summary: The first oscillatory velocity has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_le.text: (D.5) of Lemma D.1 (the phase average and the centered part).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_le.summary: Phase averaging and centering preserve derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_material_ze.summary: Material evolution preserves a vanishing phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_phaseGrad_z.text: `⟨κ∂_s q⟩ = 0` for every pressure profile (the phase derivative of a periodic function has mean zero, and `κ` does not depend on the phase).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_phaseGrad_z.summary: A periodic phase gradient has zero average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_reflection.text: The phase average commutes with the reflection.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_sourceBefor.text: Averages the pre-mean source and rewrites the fast phase products by periodic integration by parts, using transversality and the divergence correction identity. The resulting formula contains averaged label products, a label divergence product and the mean–mean label product. This is the mechanism by which the mean source avoids paying a fast phase derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_sourceBefor.summary: Integration by parts rewrites the mean source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_vrefl.summary: Velocity reflection commutes with phase averaging

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.band_jets.text: Bernstein's inequality in operator norm (B.1): a real vector field on the torus with frequencies at most `4Λ` satisfies `‖∇^m g(x)‖ ≤ C_m Λ^m ‖g‖` (the coordinate sums of (B.1) are converted to operator norms by `exists_sortedWord` and `opNorm_le_coordinateSum`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.band_jets.summary: Bernstein bounds for the parent residual jets

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_abstract.text: The splitting argument for a bilinear map, over an abstract module with an involution `r`: if `r(B f g) = -σ(f)σ(g) B f g` whenever `r f = σ(f) f`, `r g = σ(g) g` with `σ = ±1`, then `r(B f g) = -B(r f)(r g)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_abstract.summary: Extending parity identities to all profile pairs

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_neg_neg.text: A bilinear map is even under `(f,g) ↦ (-f,-g)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_neg_neg.summary: Two sign changes cancel in bilinear terms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefBounds_of_h5_1.text: The coefficient norms `‖(D_aX)⁻¹‖_{[n]} ≤ N_G(n)`, `‖κ‖_{[n]} ≤ N_κ(n)` on every time set in `[0,T]`, from (D.6) and (5.8) of Proposition 5.1 (`h5_1`), when `ℓ_* ≤ 𝖣^{-C}`; `N_G(n) = K_n 𝖣^C`, `N_κ(n) = K_n 𝖣^C λ`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefBounds_of_h5_1.summary: Parent geometry controls the advection coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField.text:
The coefficient field `(t,a,s) ↦ c(t,a)`.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField.summary: A label coefficient extended independently of phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField_bounds.text: Norms of a phase-independent coefficient from bounds on its Fréchet jets (`ℓ^m |∇^m c(t,a)| ≤ B` for `m ≤ n`, uniformly bounded jets): the field `(t,a,s) ↦ c(t,a)` has a finite norm (D.1) of order `n`, at most `#W_n B` (the argument of `coef_bounds` without a functional).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField_bounds.summary: Label jet bounds control coefficient profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coef_bounds.text: Norms of a phase-independent coefficient. For a smooth coframe `G` with uniformly bounded jets and `ℓ^m |∇^m G(t,a)| ≤ B` for `m ≤ n`, and a continuous linear functional `L`, the field `(t,a,s) ↦ L(G(t,a))` has a finite norm (D.1) of order `n`, at most `#W_n ‖L‖ B`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coef_bounds.summary: Profile norms of phase independent coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coframeC.text:
The coframe `(D_aX)⁻¹(t,a) = D(X(t,·)⁻¹)(X(t,a))` on a time set.

Default-value audit (b5): Uses the total Fréchet derivative of a supplied flow map. For arbitrary nonsmooth maps that derivative can take its default zero value; ParentGeometry and the parent estimates ensure it is the actual derivative in every analytic application.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coframeC.summary: The inverse deformation as a coefficient field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.compl_exp_split.text: Exponent splitting for the completion terms of (5.37), (5.38).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.compl_exp_split.summary: Separating the divergence correction decay powers

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.complete_smul_time_.text: `C[·]` acts at fixed time: if `W(t,·,·) = c V(t,·,·)` at one time `t` (for a constant `c`), then `C[W](t,·,·) = c C[V](t,·,·)` (the curl completion is linear and uses only the profile at the time `t`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.complete_smul_time_.summary: Time multiplication commutes with divergence completion

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.continuous_phase_sl.text: The phase slices of a twisted profile are continuous.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_acti.text: `C[·]` acts at fixed time: at `t ∈ [t₀,T]`, `C[S](t,·) = χ̃'(t) C[V₀](t,·)` for the extended leading profile `V₀` (library `complete_smul_wrapped_eval`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_acti.summary: Time factors pass through the divergence correction

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_extL.text: `C[V₀]` vanishes at labels outside `supp g` (it is a label derivative of the wave potential of `V₀`, which vanishes on the open complement of `supp g`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_extL.summary: The correction preserves the envelope support

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_vref.text: `C[ϱV] = ϱC[V]` for `⟨V⟩ = 0` (even coframe and wave vector): the phase primitive of `-V(t,-a,-s)` is `Q[V](t,-a,-s)` (`wavePotential_neg_reflected`), and the slow curl of a reflected potential is minus the reflected slow curl.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.deriv_le.text: (D.3) of Lemma D.1 (label and phase derivatives).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.deriv_le.summary: The costs of label and phase differentiation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.divProd.text:
`(𝐝·V) Y`.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.divProd.summary: The label divergence times a vector field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.divergence_add'.text: The divergence is additive on differentiable fields (copy of the private `divergence_add`, `TorusEuler/HierarchyPhysicalApproximation.lean:241`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.divergence_add'.summary: Adding divergences of smooth vector fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.domain_bounds.text: For a time domain contained in [0,T], a positive time weight, and a smooth profile with finite weighted derivative norms, the graph readout satisfies the integer and half Hölder estimates with Λ = D^(C₁+a+1) λ^(3/2). If the field is independent of the phase, the same argument uses Λ = D^(C₁+a+1). The proof iterates the coefficient estimate for one physical derivative and then bounds the full Fréchet derivatives by coordinate words.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.evalLM.text:
Evaluation of a twisted profile at a point as a linear map.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.eval_add.text: Evaluation of a sum of profiles.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.eval_add.summary: Evaluation distributes over sums of profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.eval_sub.text: Evaluation of a difference of profiles.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.eval_sub.summary: Evaluation distributes over differences of profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.evenGeometry.text: The coefficient profiles of an odd parent are even (library `ParentGeometry.reflection`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.evenGeometry.summary: Parent symmetry supplies even hierarchy coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.exists_seed_extensi.text: The seed extends to a jointly smooth field on `ℝ × ℝ³` that agrees with it on `[t₀,T] × ℝ³` (library Seeley extension in time).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.expansion_average_C.text: `⟨u.C i⟩ = 0` for the corrections of an expansion (`C_{p+1} = C[V_p]`; `C₁ = 0`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.expansion_average_C.summary: Every divergence correction has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading.text:
The twisted profile on `[0,T]` of the leading field of an extended seed `ampE`.

Default-value audit (b5): The constructor takes positive scales, a support-fit inequality, and smoothness of the extended seed. Its extension can differ from the original seed before the active interval; no analytic bound on an arbitrary extension there is inferred from the active estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_active_e.text: On `[t₀,T]` the extended leading profile is the twisted extension of `A₁`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_active_e.summary: Recovering the leading field after activation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_average.text: The extended leading profile has zero phase mean (`F_h` has zero mean).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_eq_zero_.text: The extended leading profile vanishes at labels outside `supp g`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_eq_zero_.summary: The extended seed stays inside the envelope

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_eval.text: Evaluation of the extended leading term.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_jets.text: Jets of the twisted extension versus jets of `A₁` at a time `t ∈ [t₀,T]`, for the fields scaled by a constant `c` (the weight `γ(t)⁻¹`): every jet of one is a jet of the other or zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_jets.summary: Twisted extension preserves the leading jets

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_transver.text: On `[t₀,T]` the extended leading profile is transverse to `κ` (the seed is).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_transver.summary: The extended leading velocity is transverse

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_wNorm_le.text: The norm comparison: on `[t₀,T]`, `‖V₀‖_{[n],γ} ≤ ‖A₁‖_{[n],γ}` (the latter the norm (D.1) of the raw field `S5.leading` on `[t₀,T] × ℝ³ × ℝ`), and the raw field has bounded jets (so its norm is a genuine finite norm).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_wNorm_le.summary: The extended profile retains the weighted bound

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv.text:
`(f·κ)∂_s g`.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv.summary: Advection through the fast phase derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_eq.text: The fast advection term as a product of the given factors.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_eq.summary: Phase advection expressed as bilinear products

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_eq_flip.text: The fast advection term with the factors flipped.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_eq_flip.summary: Reordering the factors in phase advection

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_left.text: Phase advection, weight on the advecting field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_left.summary: Putting the weight on the advecting phase field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_right.text: Phase advection, weight on the advected field ((5.39), second line): `‖(f·κ)∂_s g‖_{[n],γ} ≤ c_n (c_n N_κ ‖f‖_{[n]}) (h⁻¹ ‖g‖_{[n+1],γ})`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_right.summary: Putting the weight on the advected phase field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fderiv_comp_neg'.text: The derivative of `b ↦ f(-b)` (no differentiability needed).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fderiv_comp_neg'.summary: Differentiating spatial reflection with total derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_add.text: Finite norms (D.1) are closed under addition.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_add.summary: Finite derivative norms persist under addition

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_sum.text: Finite norms (D.1) are closed under finite sums.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_sum.summary: Finite sums retain finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_zer.text: The zero field has finite norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_zer.summary: The zero profile has finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_add_le.text: The norm (D.1) is subadditive on fields with finite norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_add_le.summary: The triangle inequality for profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_congr_on.text: The norm (D.1) of a field on a time set only depends on the field on that set.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_congr_on.summary: Identical time slices have identical derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_nonneg'.text: Every norm (D.1) is nonnegative (a supremum of norms, with `0` among the values).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_nonneg'.summary: Nonnegative sums of scaled derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_smul_time.text: A time multiplier of modulus at most one does not increase the norm (D.1) of a field whose jets are bounded.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_smul_time.summary: Time multiplication preserves spatial derivative estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_sum_le.text: The norm (D.1) of a finite sum of fields with finite norms is at most the sum of the norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_sum_le.summary: Bounding the derivative norm of a finite sum

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_zero.text: The zero field has norm zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_zero.summary: The zero profile has zero derivative norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.final_bounds.text: Conversion of the bounds of `graph_from_words` into the form of the statement, `C_m Λ^m γ(t) N_m` and `C_m Λ^{m+1} γ(t) N_{m+1}`, when the word constants are at most `(∏_{l<j} κ₀_l) Λ^j` with `Λ ≥ 1`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.final_bounds.summary: Converting derivative words to physical bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graphPoint.text:
The graph point `x ↦ (A(x), k·A(x))` at a fixed time, with `A = X(t,·)⁻¹`.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_from_words.text: (5.44), (5.45) at a fixed time from the word estimate. Let `A = X(t,·)⁻¹` be smooth with `G(A(x)) = D A(x)` for the coframe `G` at time `t`, and suppose the `d̃`-words of `f` satisfy `∑_{|w|=m} ‖d̃_w f‖_{[0],γ} ≤ P_m ‖f‖_{[m],γ}` with finite norms. Then the graph `F = f(t) ∘ (A, k·A)` satisfies `∑_{|w|=m} sup |∂_w F| ≤ γ(t) P_m ‖f‖_{[m],γ}` and `‖F‖_{C^{m,1/2}} ≤ 3(m+1) γ(t) (∑_{j≤m+1} P_j) ‖f‖_{[m+1],γ}` (the chain rule (3.1), `sup |g(t)| ≤ γ(t)‖g‖_{[0],γ}`, and the Hölder bound by one more derivative).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_norm_le_wNorm.text: The value of an inactive profile on the physical graph is bounded by its weighted order-zero norm. On the activation interval the proof uses the positive weight and the bound $\gamma\le1$; before activation it uses vanishing of the profile. This produces a bound on the whole time slab without an Eulerian derivative loss. Applied to the oscillatory expansion, it supplies the supremum estimate in Lemma 5.8.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd.text: Given the five cited results and the proposition that all permitted expansions are odd, assembles Lemma 5.8. Proposition 5.4 gives the hierarchy identity and divergence constraint; Theorem 5.6 gives the oscillatory, mean and tail bounds; Lemma 5.7 converts them to physical Hölder norms. For the activation term, Lemma 5.3 bounds the raw leading wave at order three and Lemma 5.5 bounds its divergence correction at order two. The estimate distinguishes the tail, which improves with depth P, from the χ̃′ contribution, which is governed by the derivative size of the time cutoff.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd.summary: Assembling the approximate solution from odd expansions

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelConstant_indep.text: For $P\ge P^{\prime}$ and $q\le P^{\prime}$, the recursively defined level constant at depth $P$ equals the one at depth $P^{\prime}$. The proof observes that the interaction pairs at these levels are identical, then inducts on $q$. This lets Theorem 5.6 use a constant depending only on derivative order and the current level, even when the expansion is built to a larger depth. No uniform bound in the level itself is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelConstant_indep.summary: A level constant is independent of larger depths

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence.text: Consumes the bounds from Propositions 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 and Lemmas 5.3 and 5.5, Lemma B.1 and Lemma D.1 and constructs a single exponent c with L = D^c. It bounds the parent residual, the unswitched leading pair, the mean and centered oscillatory products, the two solves and the completion, then obtains HierarchyNormRecurrence. The averaging identity moves the fast mean product to a label divergence. The final block estimates the finite remainder directly. The exponent c is independent of derivative order and hierarchy depth; the constants K(H) and K_P(m,P) retain their allowed dependence.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence.summary: The expansion norms satisfy every finite recurrence

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredLevels'.text:
Keeps every component of an existing numerical hierarchy except its oscillatory measurement at p = 1, which is replaced by the prescribed nonnegative function osc₁. In the proof of Theorem 5.6 this is the bound for the unswitched leading pair. It permits the cancellation of χ̃′ in the level-two relay without changing any profile or any higher-level measurement.

Default-value audit (b5): Only the oscillatory numerical component at index 1 is overwritten. The supplied h₁ proves its nonnegativity. No physical field is changed, and comparison with the original measurements requires the separate domination hypothesis.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredOf.text:
Builds the nonnegative numerical measurements of an actual finite expansion: weighted norms for oscillatory sources, velocities, pressures and completions, and unweighted norms for mean fields and their sources. The pressure contribution is scaled by λ. NormSetting supplies the positivity and finiteness facts needed to use these quantities as seminorm measurements.

Default-value audit (b5): The measured data are built from norms of actual profiles, with NormSetting certifying positive parameters and finite seminorms. The pressure factor λ is used in the theorem only for λ ≥ 1. Exterior velocity indices come from the separate truncation convention.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredOf.summary: Measuring each source and velocity in its natural norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily.text:
The reflected family: `ϱV_p`, `ϱC_p`, `ϱB_p`, `𝗉_p ∘ reflection`, `q̄_p ∘ reflection`.

Default-value audit (b5): Every component is transformed algebraically at every natural index, including zero. Velocity, mean and completion components are negated after reflection; pressure components are only reflected. Validity as an expansion is a separate theorem.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily_B.text: Unfolding the reflected family gives its mean velocity B_p as the negated reflection of the original mean velocity. This is a definitional identity used in checking the reflected mean equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily_V.text: The `V` component of the reflected family.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily_p.text: Unfolding the reflected family gives its oscillatory pressure as the ordinary reflection of the original pressure, with no velocity sign. This sign convention makes its gradient transform as a velocity.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily_q.text: Unfolding the reflected family gives its mean pressure as the ordinary reflection of the original mean pressure. The mean velocity receives the minus sign separately.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflection_of_parit.text: The reflection of a profile of parity `σ` is `σ` times the profile.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflection_split.text: Splitting. An additive map `M` that agrees with `L` on reflection-even profiles and with `-L` on reflection-odd profiles is `L ∘ reflection`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflection_split.summary: Recovering reflection from the even and odd parts

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.relay_two_eq.text: At level two the differentiated switch in the material derivative of C[V₁] cancels the correction of the activation source S. What remains is χ̃ times the completion/pressure relay for the unswitched leading pair. This identity is why the numerical recurrence uses an unswitched level-one bound instead of estimating χ̃′ separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.relay_two_eq.summary: The activation derivative cancels in the second relay

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.relay_vanish_before.text: The linear term vanishes before `t₀`: if `C` and `p` vanish at all times `< t₀`, so does `(∂_t+M)C + 𝐝p`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.relay_vanish_before.summary: The linear relay vanishes before activation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.residual_uNorm.text: The pulled-back residual `‖R_U∘X‖_{[n]} ≤ K_n λ^{-5/2}` when `ℓ_* ≤ 𝖣^{-C}` ), from (B.1) (`hB_1`) and (5.7) (`h5_1`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.residual_uNorm.summary: The pulled back parent residual in profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.rowCLM.text:
`(M, v) ↦ (M v)_j`.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.rowCLM_apply.text: Action of the row functional on a vector.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.seed_even.text: The seed is even in the label: `𝐚(t,-a) = 𝐚(t,a)` on `[t₀,T]`, since `𝐚(t,-a)` solves (3.2) with (5.4) (the coefficients `M`, `κ` are even) and the seed is unique.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.seed_even.summary: Uniqueness makes the seed even in the label

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.seminorm_finset_le.text: A seminorm of a finite sum (copy of the private library lemma `hierarchy_seminorm_finset_le`, `TorusEuler/HierarchySourceAssembly.lean:309`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.seminorm_finset_le.summary: A seminorm bounds a finite sum by its terms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slab_fderiv_slice.text: The derivative within the slab in a direction without time component is the derivative of the time slice.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slab_fderiv_slice.summary: Spatial directions ignore the boundary of the time slab

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slice_contDiff.text: A function jointly smooth on `[0,T] × ℝ³` is smooth in space at each time of `[0,T]`.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slice_fderiv_label.text: The derivative of a slice in a label direction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slice_fderiv_label.summary: Label derivatives agree with derivatives of slices

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_average.text: The phase average as a field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_average.summary: Phase averaging commutes with taking time slices

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_divProduct.text: The divergence product as a field: `(𝐝·V)Y`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_divProduct.summary: The divergence product written on profile slices

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_labelAdv.text: The label advection as a field: `(f·𝐝)g = ∑_j ((D_aX)⁻¹ f)_j ∂_{a_j} g`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_labelAdv.summary: Label advection written as a field product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_mono.text: The unweighted norm on a smaller time set is smaller.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_mono.summary: Restricting the time interval reduces the norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_phaseAdv.text: The phase advection as a field: `(f·κ)∂_s g`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_phaseAdv.summary: Phase advection written as a field product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_phasePeriodi.text: The slices of a profile are `1`-periodic in the phase.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv.text:
`(f·𝐝)g = ∑_j (G f)_j ∂_{a_j} g` for the coframe `G`.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_eq.text: The slow advection term as a product of the given factors.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_eq.summary: Label advection expressed as bilinear products

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_eq_flip.text: The slow advection term with the factors flipped.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_eq_flip.summary: Reordering the factors in label advection

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_left.text: Label advection, weight on the advecting field ((5.39), first line, weight on `Z`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_left.summary: Putting the weight on the advecting label field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_right.text: Label advection, weight on the advected field ((5.39), first line): `‖(f·𝐝)g‖_{[n],γ} ≤ c_n (c_n N_G ‖f‖_{[n]}) (3ℓ⁻¹ ‖g‖_{[n+1],γ})`, by (D.4) for the coefficient `(G f)_j` and for its product with `∂_{a_j} g`, and (D.3) for `∑_j ‖∂_{a_j} g‖`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_right.summary: Putting the weight on the advected label field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowDiv.text:
`𝐝·V = ∑_i (G ∂_{a_i} V)_i`.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowDiv_eq.text: The slow divergence term as a product of the given factors.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowDiv_eq.summary: Label divergence expressed through coframe rows

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowDiv_le_one.summary: Unweighted control of the label divergence

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.smooth_of_weighted.text: A field whose weighted field is smooth is smooth (the weight is a nonzero constant at each time).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.smooth_of_weighted.summary: A positive time weight preserves spatial smoothness

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.smulCLM.text:
`(r, v) ↦ r v`.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.smulCLM.summary: Scalar multiplication as a continuous bilinear map

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.spatialDerivativeWo.text: The spatial chain rule (3.1), iterated: with `A = X(t,·)⁻¹` and the coframe `G` with `G(A(x)) = D A(x)`, every Eulerian derivative word of the graph `g ∘ (A, k·A)` is the graph of the `d̃`-word of `g`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.spatialDerivativeWo.summary: Repeated chain rule along the physical graph

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.spatialHolderHalfNo.summary: Nonnegative norms for physical Hölder estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.sum_coordinate.text: A vector is the sum of its coordinates times the coordinate directions.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.sum_coordinate.summary: Expanding a vector in coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.suppSource_vrefl.text: `f_p^S` of the reflected family is the reflection of `f_p^S`, (5.28).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.suppSource_vrefl.summary: Reflection preserves the supplementary mean source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_BB.summary: Bounding the product of two mean velocities

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_YY.summary: Bounding the averaged oscillatory label product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_fastB.summary: Bounding the mean against an oscillatory phase derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_fastC.summary: Bounding the centered completion phase product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_slow.text: The centered label product of `Z = Y + B`, `Z' = Y' + B'` (`Y`, `Y'` vanishing before `t₀`, `B`, `B'` phase independent): `‖(Z·𝐝)Z' - ⟨…⟩‖_{[n],γ} ≤ 2Λ_n (‖Y‖_γ + ‖B‖)(‖Y'‖_γ + ‖B'‖)` at order `n+1`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_slow.summary: Centering removes the product of two means

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeDirection.text:
The direction field of `d̃_i = ∑_j G_{ji}(∂_{a_j} + k_j ∂_s)` at a fixed time: `(a, s) ↦ (G(a) e_i, k · G(a) e_i)`. For `G = (D_aX)⁻¹` this is `d̃ = (D_aX)^{-T}(∇_a + k_*∂_s)` of.

Default-value audit (b5): A total algebraic direction built from a supplied coframe G and carrier k, without taking an inverse or derivative. If G is not the inverse flow deformation, the direction remains defined but need not represent an Eulerian derivative; the graph chain rule requires that geometric identification.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeDirection.summary: The physical derivative in label and phase variables

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeDirection_smoo.text: The direction fields of `d̃` are smooth for a smooth coframe.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeDirection_smoo.summary: Smooth coefficients give smooth physical derivative directions

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord.text:
The `d̃`-word `d̃_{w₁} ⋯ d̃_{w_m} f` of a field, time by time (the first letter is the outermost derivative).

Default-value audit (b5): The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord.summary: Ordered physical derivatives of a profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_cons.text: One letter of a `d̃`-word applied to a word is the word with one more letter.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_cons_eq.text: `d̃_i g = ∑_j G_{ji} ∂_{a_j} g + (k·G e_i) ∂_s g`: one letter of a `d̃`-word is a sum of products of phase-independent coefficients with the label and phase derivatives of Lemma D.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_cons_eq.summary: One physical derivative splits into label and phase terms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_eq_opWord.text: The `d̃`-words are the operator words of the one-letter `d̃`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_eq_opWord.summary: Physical derivative words as operator compositions

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step.text: One letter of `d̃`, by Lemma D.1. For a coframe `G` and a carrier `k`, whose coefficients `G_{ji}` and `k·G e_i` (fields independent of the phase) have finite norms (D.1) bounded by `Nc` and `Nk`, and a field `f` with `‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}` finite: `d̃_i f` has a finite weighted norm and `∑_i ‖d̃_i f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ c_n (3 Nc (3ℓ⁻¹ ‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}) + 3 Nk ‖∂_s f‖_{[n],γ})`. Uses `hD_1` (Lemma D.1): (D.4) for each of the four products of `d̃_i f` (`tildeWord_cons_eq`) and (D.3) for `∑_j ‖∂_{a_j} f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ 3ℓ⁻¹‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step.summary: Bounding one physical derivative of a profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_general.text: The one-step estimate for a general field : `∑_i ‖d̃_i f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ c_n (9 Nc ℓ⁻¹ + 3 Nk h⁻¹) ‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}`. Uses `hD_1` through `tilde_step` and the phase bound `‖∂_s f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ h⁻¹‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}` of (D.3).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_general.summary: The full phase cost of one physical derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_phaseInd.text: The one-step estimate for a phase-independent field: `d̃_i f` is again phase independent, and `∑_i ‖d̃_i f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ 9 c_n Nc ℓ⁻¹ ‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}`, since `∂_s f = 0`. Uses `hD_1` through `tilde_step`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_phaseInd.summary: Phase independent fields avoid the fast derivative cost

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverseSolution_.text: (5.15) is preserved: if `(V, 𝗉)` solves the transverse equation from zero with source `f`, then `(ϱV, 𝗉 ∘ reflection)` solves it with source `ϱf`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverseSolution_.summary: Reflection preserves the transverse evolution equation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverse_average_.text: A solution of the transverse equation (5.15) has a source of zero phase mean: `f = (∂_t+M)V + κ∂_s𝗉` with `⟨V⟩ = 0`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverse_average_.summary: The transverse equation forces zero source average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.truncate.text:
The levels of `u` restricted to `1..P` (`C_i` for `i ≤ P`), zero elsewhere.

Default-value audit (b5): The natural-index condition sets V and B to zero outside 1 ≤ p ≤ P, and C to zero outside p ≤ P. It leaves both pressure families untouched. No estimate for these exterior pressures follows from the definition; later tail arguments use only the truncated velocity components.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.truncate.summary: Extending the finite velocity hierarchy by zero

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_jets.text: Jets of a twisted profile versus jets of a raw field at one time: every jet of one is a jet of the other or zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_jets.summary: Twisted extension preserves local derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_wNorm_le.text: Norm of a twisted profile versus the raw field: on `[t₀,T]`, `‖V₀‖_{[n],γ} ≤ ‖F‖_{[n],γ}` (the latter the norm (D.1) of the raw field on `[t₀,T] × ℝ³ × ℝ`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_wNorm_le.summary: Twisted extension preserves weighted leading norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_average.summary: Phase averaging does not increase the unweighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_divProduct.summary: An unweighted bound for the divergence product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_labelAdv.text: (5.39) for the label advection without weight, on `[0,T]`.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_plain.text: For a field vanishing before `t₀`, the unweighted norm on `[0,T]` is the one on `[t₀,T]`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_plain.summary: Vanishing before activation reduces the full slab norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_wNorm.text: If a smooth profile vanishes for $t<t_0$, its unweighted norm on $[0,T]$ is bounded by its weighted norm on $[t_0,T]$ when $0<\gamma\le1$. Continuity of the weight is also assumed. The vanishing hypothesis is essential because the two norms use different time intervals. In the remainder estimate, terms containing an oscillation or correction inherit this vanishing; products of two means are estimated directly in the full-slab unweighted norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_wNorm.summary: The weighted active norm controls the full slab norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_phaseAdv.text: (5.39), second line, in the unweighted norm on `[0,T]`: `‖(f·κ)∂_s g‖_{[n]} ≤ c_n (c_n N_κ ‖f‖_{[n]}) (h⁻¹ ‖g‖_{[n+1]})`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_phaseAdv.summary: Unweighted control of the phase advection term

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl.text:
The symmetry of the construction on velocity profiles: `ϱf(t,a,s) = -f(t,-a,-s)`.

Default-value audit (b5): Reflection and negation are algebraic operations on already smooth twisted profiles. No reciprocal, partial inverse or arbitrary choice is introduced; pressures use ordinary reflection in reflFamily.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl.summary: Reflection of velocity profiles with a minus sign

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_apply.text: Unfolding of the vector reflection `vrefl` (negated reflection).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_eval.summary: Evaluating velocity reflection at a label and phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_vrefl.summary: Reflecting the velocity twice changes nothing

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_left.text: (5.39) for the label advection with the weight on the advecting field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_left.summary: Weighted label advection of the first factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_righ.text: `‖(f·𝐝)g‖_{[n],γ} ≤ c_n (c_n N_G ‖f‖_{[n]}) (3ℓ⁻¹ ‖g‖_{[n+1],γ})`, (5.39) with the weight on the advected field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_righ.summary: Weighted label advection of the second factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_left.text: (5.39), second line, with the weight on the advecting field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_left.summary: Weighted phase advection of the first factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_righ.summary: Weighted phase advection of the second factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_smul_time_le.text: A time multiplier of modulus at most one does not increase the weighted norm: if `F = c G` on `[t₀,T]` and `|c| ≤ 1` there, then `‖F‖_{[n],γ} ≤ ‖G‖_{[n],γ}`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_smul_time_le.summary: A bounded time factor preserves the weighted estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.waveC.text:
The wave vector `κ(t,a)` on a time set.

Default-value audit (b5): The wave vector is defined from the supplied flow derivative for every input. The parent-flow hypotheses are what identify it with the transported nonzero covector; the definition alone does not establish those geometric facts.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.waveC.summary: The transported wave vector as a coefficient field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wavePotential_smul_.text: For any fixed wave vector K, scalar c and phase profile V, the wave potential of cV equals c times the wave potential of V. Linearity of the cross product and phase primitive proves the identity, even at K = 0 under the total reciprocal convention. The consuming completion estimate works at each fixed time.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wavePotential_smul_.summary: Time multiplication commutes with the wave potential

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wavePotential_zero.text: The wave potential of the zero profile vanishes.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.weighted_add.text: The time weight distributes over sums of fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.weighted_sum.text: The time weight distributes over finite sums of fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.weighted_zero.text: The time weight of the zero field is zero.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordConst.text:
The one-step constant `κ₀_n = 12 c_n #W_n max(K_n, 0)` of the proof of Lemma 5.7, for the constants `K_n` of (5.8) in Proposition 5.1.

Default-value audit (b5): Finite sums, products and max are total. The max clips any supplied negative coefficient constant to zero; analytic use still requires that it bounds the coefficient jets. The order-zero word set is nonempty.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordConst_nonneg.text: The word constant of Lemma 5.7 is nonnegative.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordNorm_le_of_valu.text: A word norm is at most another one when every value of the first is dominated by a value of the second.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordNorm_le_of_valu.summary: Dominating every derivative value bounds the word norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_add.text: Derivative words are additive on smooth functions.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_comp_add.text: Words in constant directions commute with translations.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_comp_add.summary: Translations commute with constant directional derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_eventuallyEq.text: Words of functions that agree near a point agree near that point.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_smul_const.text: A derivative word of a constant multiple.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_smul_const.summary: Constants pass through ordered derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_zero.text: Derivative words vanish on the zero function.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_zero.summary: Derivative words annihilate the zero field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_general.text: Iteration of the physical derivative operator is bounded in the weighted finite-order profile norm. Each step spends the coefficient bound for the inverse coframe and the sum of the slow cost $\ell^{-1}$ and fast cost $|k_*|h^{-1}$. The product constants depend on the derivative order. Finite norms and positive scales and weights are explicit hypotheses; applying the coefficient estimates converts this bound into the power of $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2}$ in Lemma 5.7.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_general.summary: Iterating physical derivatives with the phase cost

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_phaseIndep.text: For a phase-independent profile, iterating the physical derivative operator uses only the inverse coframe and slow label derivatives. The bound has no contribution $|k_*|h^{-1}$, because the phase derivative vanishes at every step. Positive scales, a positive weight, finite coefficient bounds and a finite profile norm are assumed. This is the derivative estimate underlying the improved phase-independent clause of Lemma 5.7.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_phaseIndep.summary: Iterating physical derivatives without a phase cost

TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.L.text:
Defines $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$ from the entire frequency sequence. The integer argument is the paper’s index $j$, and the frequency sequence already uses the paper’s indexing. This definition does not impose positivity or a recurrence; those come from the schedule data. The shift by one is needed when reading Lemma 1.3, where $L_{j+1}$ therefore involves $\lambda_{j+2}$.

Default-value audit (b4): The standalone definition accepts arbitrary real frequencies. Real.log is total and does not itself certify positivity; a zero or unit frequency can collapse the gain, and negative inputs are outside the paper convention. In the construction, InductiveEulerParameters records b ≥ 1, a positive threshold, its logarithmic floor, the initial lower bound and the frequency recurrence (InductiveStageConstruction.lean:24–41). Those schedule conditions force the frequencies above one. Do not infer positive gain from the definition alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.L.summary: The logarithmic gain prescribed by the next frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.ε.text:
Defines $\varepsilon_j=L_{j+1}^{-2}$ by applying the library ratio function to the next prescribed logarithmic gain. The paper writes the same identity as $\varepsilon_{j-1}=L_j^{-2}$ for $j\ge2$. This index shift is part of the definition, not an estimate. Positivity and smallness of the gain and ratio are supplied by the schedule hypotheses and the later amplification bounds.

Default-value audit (b4): The standalone definition accepts arbitrary real frequencies. Real.log is total and does not itself certify positivity; a zero or unit frequency can collapse the gain, and negative inputs are outside the paper convention. In the construction, InductiveEulerParameters records b ≥ 1, a positive threshold, its logarithmic floor, the initial lower bound and the frequency recurrence (InductiveStageConstruction.lean:24–41). Those schedule conditions force the frequencies above one. Do not infer positive gain from the definition alone. In addition, Lean sets the reciprocal of zero to zero: ε_j is zero when the chosen gain is zero. Positive gains in the parameter schedule exclude this case in the application.
TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.ε.summary: The coupling ratio prescribed by the next gain

TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.τ.text:
The half length $\tau_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^3$ for the prescribed frequency sequence. Here $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$, so the logarithm in this expression involves $\lambda_{j+2}$. The definition applies to every natural index, but the paper uses it for $j\ge1$. The activation times and the final-time identity $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$ are specified separately.

Natural subtraction gives a syntactic value at $j=0$, but it is not an additional paper clause defining $\tau_0$.

Real.log is total and does not itself certify positivity; a zero or unit frequency can collapse the gain, and negative inputs are outside the paper convention. In the construction, InductiveEulerParameters records b ≥ 1, a positive threshold, its logarithmic floor, the initial lower bound and the frequency recurrence (InductiveStageConstruction.lean:24–41). Those schedule conditions force the frequencies above one. Do not infer positive gain from the definition alone. TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_1.text:

For every order-connected time set J with UniqueDiffOn, every differentiable F and primitive P, every trace-free D with a specified within-J derivative D′ and self-adjoint D′ + D², and every WaveOn k a, it asserts two conclusions. If k·a vanishes on J, the affine velocity and stated pressure are differentiable in the needed variables and satisfy momentum and incompressibility. From nonzero perpendicular data at any t₀ in J, both vectors remain nonzero and perpendicular throughout J. Smoothness, oddness, periodicity, and mean normalization of F,P are not required here. TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_2.text:

For an arbitrary J these are relative derivative statements, not a claim of an ODE on an open interval.

Their product is positive, so Real.log is never applied to 0 or a negative strength. The pressure denominator in WaveOn is likewise nonzero. TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_3.text:
The configuration is a PhysicalAmplification on a compact I containing the image of [0,T] under t = t₀ + τ/r, with T ≥ 2. It also asserts ζ₃ ≠ 0 on the entire slab for those sufficiently large S. The universal quantifier over ε is harmless outside the physical ε > 0 range because no w with that ratio exists.

There is a natural threshold N, independent of all physical data, after which every C₀ ≥ N gives the following result under FiniteSmallness, the two wave predicates, T ≥ 2, clock inclusion and the growing initial amplitude. With ν₊ and η₊ evaluated in the new wave’s normalized frame, ν₊ ≥ εν/2 on the whole slab. At times τ ≥ √2/ε it also gives |ν₊/ν−1| ≤ ε and |η₊/(ν₊cos φ)−1| ≤ 1/2. For every MeanParentFlow and quadratic-form bound H^#≤Id, every label a and every L² path v on (0,T] with zero time integral obey the two inequalities of Lemma 4.1.
