TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8.text:
After a is fixed, choose b₀, a depth-dependent floor Γ₀ and constants K(m,P). The claim holds for every b≥b₀ and every Γ≥Γ₀, every admissible expansion of depth P≥2, and Γ(P)D^bλ^(−1/12)≤1. The physical velocity V=U+W^♮ is jointly smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free; Π=pU+𝖯^♮ is jointly smooth and periodic. Its exact residual is the graph evaluation of R_P+S+C[S]. The oscillatory velocity has uniform size λ^(−5/4); all Hölder orders are controlled separately for oscillatory and mean parts. The residual’s C^(1,1/2) bound contains the depth tail and χ.derivativeSize γ, the supremum of the weighted activation derivative. This lemma quantifies over already supplied expansions rather than selecting one. This declaration defines a proposition; the corresponding theorem in Paper.Spine supplies its proof.

Default-value audit (b4): 0<T, D≥2, λ≥1, Launch and Origin protect interval derivatives, inverses and real powers. Smooth typed profiles, the valid flow and the seed/cutoff give the asserted genuine physical derivatives. Every displayed spatial Hölder bound is paired with SpatialHolderHalf, excluding unbounded spatial suprema. The activation-size supremum is over the nonempty compact interval [t₀,T] of the continuous χ′γ, so it is finite. The phase and mean-pressure integrals are of smooth finite-dimensional data. No ENNReal.toReal conversion occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8.summary: Approximate Euler solution with controlled physical residual

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_9.text:
Under the common expansion and step-smallness assumptions, the Hessian of the pressure correction 𝖯^♮ is at most Γ(P)D^bλ^(−1/4) times the identity as a quadratic form at every point and time. This is an upper quadratic-form estimate, not a bound on the absolute Hessian or its operator norm. On [t₀,T], the central velocity gradient differs from ∇U+χ̃ center⊗κ by at most λ^(−1/3) in operator norm. InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℝ center κ sends v to (κ·v)center; reversing the arguments would describe a different matrix. The error E_c is encoded as the displayed difference, so no separate error field is chosen. This declaration defines a proposition; the corresponding theorem in Paper.Spine supplies its proof.

Default-value audit (b4): The parent and constructed profiles are smooth on a positive-length slab, so the gradients and Hessians in the conclusion are genuine. Their availability follows from the common hypotheses rather than from interpreting a zero-valued fderiv as evidence of smoothness. Parent, Launch and Origin exclude zero λ and κ and degenerate profile widths. The inequalities are pointwise or operator-norm inequalities, not unchecked real suprema. There is no new integral, ENNReal.toReal conversion or square root.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_9.summary: Pressure Hessian upper bound and central gradient return

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1.text:
For 0 < ρ ≤ 1, λ ≥ 1 and T > 0 with T‖Bρ‖ ≤ 1/8, this asserts that a FirstWaveOrigin exists and that every such wave has the conclusions of Lemma 6.1. The existence conjunct prevents a universal claim about an empty wave type. FirstWaveOrigin includes the initial covector λe₁, an amplitude in the positive e₂ direction, the ODEs, transversality, and attainment of the normalization max|a| = λ^{−3/4}. The conclusion is at the origin; it does not by itself build the full spatial hierarchy.

Default-value audit (b4): T > 0 excludes an empty or singleton time interval, λ ≥ 1 guards real powers, and ρ > 0 preserves the intended shear parameter. FirstWaveOrigin.transverse makes the amplitude and covector nonzero; HasDerivWithinAt certifies genuine derivatives. Nonempty FirstWaveOrigin is asserted in addition to the universal conclusion, blocking vacuity from an uninhabited witness type.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1.summary: The first wave exists and satisfies the seed bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2.text:
One nonnegative real C and natural p serve two cases: H=ℝ³ with the spatial Leray projection, and H=L²((0,1];ℝ³) with the commuting spatial and zero-time-mean projections. In each case B is a HalfHolder operator field, μ>0, Lip≥0, B is Lipschitz with that constant, and its quadratic form is at least μ‖w‖². The second coercivity assertion is only for paths with endpointIntegral 1 w=0. The conclusion is FreezingConclusion, including a genuine continuous linear isomorphism and the higher-order regularity equivalence. Replacing C^{1,1/2} by a Lipschitz bound strengthens the printed base statement; when higher regularity is requested the separate C^{k,1/2} hypothesis is retained.

Default-value audit (b4): μ>0 excludes the reciprocal-zero degeneration and Lip≥0 prevents a negative Lipschitz cap. The coercive fields live in bundled HalfHolder spaces with finite norms, so no unbounded real supremum is hidden in the base norm. In the path case Lp membership ensures a finite L² norm and a genuine finite-interval mean, excluding ENNReal.toReal ⊤=0 and non-integrable mean defaults. FreezingConclusion uses a continuous linear equivalence rather than a totalized singular inverse. Higher-order derivative and Hölder-supremum norms are invoked only with SpatialHolderHalf, which explicitly supplies differentiability and boundedness. A zero increment contributes 0 to the Hölder seminorm intentionally.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2.summary: The two Hölder inverses and their higher regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1.text:
For each smooth even cutoff ψ, this chooses one operator constant and two sequences of nonnegative order constants before quantifying over Λ>0, value spaces and fields. It packages the multiplier identity; derivative commutation; parity, divergence and frequency preservation; uniform and C^{0,1/2} bounds; the Hölder tail estimate; and Bernstein’s estimate. Complex Banach-valued fields form the first block, real velocity fields the second; Bernstein allows any real normed target and detects frequency support through scalar linear measurements. The real time-derivative clause uses a nondegenerate closed slab and HasDerivWithinAt. Sorted coordinate words represent multi-indices. This generalizes the paper’s radial ψ and Λ≥1 assumptions to even ψ and Λ>0; the norm convention is the spatial Fréchet-jet norm. It is the proposition proved by the spine lemma.

Default-value audit (b4): Λ>0 guards Λ⁻¹ and negative integer powers. MemLp is required for the complex L∞ bound, continuous fields are used for uniform/real blocks, and SpatialHolderHalf provides derivative and bounded-supremum guards for Hölder estimates. The unrestricted multiplier formula may involve default Fourier coefficients of a nonintegrable g, but it is only an algebraic formula for the total cutoff; the analytic norm clauses carry stronger hypotheses. Real time commutation assumes a<b and joint smoothness, and asserts HasDerivWithinAt. Bernstein explicitly concludes BddAbove for each derivative supremum. There is no ENNReal.toReal collapse.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1.summary: The frequency cutoff preserves structure and controls derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1.text:
For every positive radius ℓ, positive phase width h, positive time weight γ and order n, this packages four estimates: label/phase differentiation, bilinear products, phase averaging and the zero-mean primitive, and the unweighted half-Hölder product rule for phase-independent fields. Finiteness is required on the inputs and asserted on the outputs. The product is any continuous bilinear map, with its norm included in the explicit constant. The phase-integral block additionally assumes a complete target and period one in s; zero mean is required only for the primitive. Constants are three for the summed label derivative, two for the primitive, and an explicit word-count factor for products. This defines the proposition; the spine supplies the proof.

Default-value audit (b4): ℓ,h,γ are strictly positive, guarding all reciprocals and preventing the weighted field from collapsing to zero. FieldNormFinite and HolderFieldNormFinite give actual derivatives and bounded nonempty supremum sets. CompleteSpace plus smooth phase slices makes the Bochner averages and primitives genuine; periodicity and zero mean make the primitive an inverse in the intended class. For Hölder quotients dist≥0 rules out negative square roots, and coincident points contribute zero. None of the infinite quantities is passed through ENNReal.toReal.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1.summary: Derivative product and phase estimates for finite norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2.text:
The three conjuncts close CoefficientPower under bilinear products of norm at most one, under inverse in a complete real normed algebra, and under summation with a small positive label radius. Output constant sequences are chosen before the time type, D, the fields and, in the product block, the bilinear map. The product exponent is 2 max(a,b); the inverse exponent is 3 max(a,e), where ‖c⁻¹‖≤D^e. The last block assumes 0<ℓ≤(D^a)⁻¹ and retains one factor ℓ when at least one derivative hits c. Natural exponents encode the paper’s absolute real powers after upward rounding; the resulting small-scale hypothesis can be stricter than the literal real-exponent one.

Default-value audit (b4): All three blocks assume D≥1. CoefficientPower includes smoothness and boundedness of every supremum, so a default norm value cannot replace a finite coefficient estimate. Part (b) requires IsUnit(c t x) at every point before using Ring.inverse, excluding its default value on nonunits; CompleteSpace supports inverse calculus. The inverse norm bound alone would not suffice without IsUnit. Part (c) assumes ℓ>0 and D^a>0, guarding the reciprocal and positive scale. No ENNReal conversion occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2.summary: Uniform product inverse and weighted coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3.text:
Fix a finite ordered set of derivative directions, a target order n and numerical bounds C_m; then choose C_n before all vector spaces, operators, coefficients and solutions. The statement assumes commutation of L₀ with derivatives, the Leibniz relation for each coefficient action, commutation of forcing and coefficient derivatives, nonnegative operator bounds bν, a uniform zero-order estimate for every admissible u, and (D.7) only for 1≤m≤n. It concludes the finite-derivative-norm estimate for any v,f satisfying Lv=f. The unknown derivatives DE need no separate commutation hypothesis in the written Lean statement; it uses canonical ordered words. Quotient forcing spaces can encode equations modulo gradients, while the space E encodes preserved constraints. This is an abstract seminorm theorem, not a claim of existence of a solution.

Default-value audit (b4): The derivative operators are supplied linear maps, so there is no fderiv default in this proposition. The finite norms are finite sums of seminorm values, not unbounded real suprema or Bochner integrals. Zero seminorms or Clow=0 are allowed and can make the abstract estimate trivial; this is legitimate for seminorm/quotient settings, and the uniform zero-order hypothesis then constrains all admissible u. Identifying these abstract seminorms and maps with actual smooth field norms is an application obligation. No inverse, square root or ENNReal.toReal is evaluated.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3.summary: A zero order inverse estimate lifts to higher derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_2.text:
After one absolute threshold for C₀, assume the growing wave hypotheses, 0 < ε₊ ≤ ε/32, and T ≥ H = 2/√(εε₊). The proposition chooses τ_m, characterized as the zero of every reference solution on [0,∞), with τ_m ≥ 2/ε; it asserts at least one ratio crossing η₊/ν₊ = ε₊ in [τ_m,H]. It chooses a real peak that is an actual greatest value of ‖a‖ over [0,T]. Every crossing in that interval then has normalized strength σ₊/(λ peak) between exp(−1)/(4√(εε₊)) and 18 exp(3)/√(εε₊). Finally all amplitudes at τ∈[0,1] are at most exp(3−1/√ε) peak. The universal reference-solution characterization is used with Lemma 2.5’s existence and uniqueness.

Default-value audit (b4): ε and ε₊ are positive, so √ε, √(εε₊), and their reciprocals are legitimate. λ > 0, and the nonzero growing initial value gives peak > 0 because peak is an IsGreatest value of the actual image of the nonempty interval [0,T]. Thus λ peak cannot vanish. The coupling denominator ν₊ is positive on the slab by the preceding coupling result. IsGreatest entails membership and boundedness, avoiding empty or unbounded real-supremum defaults. The existential crossing prevents the interval from being merely empty. References to a_ref occur only through ReferenceSlope; no uncontrolled integral is added here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_2.summary: Successor crossing with strength bounds and early gain

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.text:
First choose one natural exponent C and coefficient constants K(m). For every proposed sequence C′(m), choose composition constants Kf(m); only then quantify over every parent and launch. This order makes C and K independent of the parent and allows Kf to depend on the derivative constants of f. The six coefficient families are D_aX, its inverse, M, κ/λ, λ²/‖κ‖² and P_κ. Their m-th Fréchet derivatives have bound K(m)D^(C(m+1)); smooth normed-space-valued f with amplitude Af≥0 has the composition bound Kf(m)Af D^(Cm). For 0<ℓ≤D^(−C), the final clause gives the finite weighted sums in (5.8). The real sequences K,Kf are not separately declared positive. Operator norms of Fréchet derivatives replace the paper’s sums of coordinate derivative suprema; the absolute constants absorb the dimension factors. This declaration defines a proposition; the corresponding theorem in Paper.Spine supplies its proof.

Default-value audit (b4): The explicit 0<T, Parent and Launch assumptions give a nonempty slab, D≥2, λ≥1, a genuine smooth invertible flow and κ≠0. Hence λ⁻¹, λ²/‖κ‖² and P_κ cannot use division-by-zero values. Smoothness protects the iterated derivatives. The pointwise coefficient estimates and the assumed derivative bounds on f provide BddAbove for the real spatial suprema in the final clause; those suprema are not independent evidence of boundedness. Af=0 is allowed and its order-zero hypothesis forces f=0 on the slab, a valid degenerate case. ℓ is explicitly positive. No ENNReal.toReal conversion is used.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.summary: Parent coefficients and composition at every order

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.text:
For each admissible smooth cutoff symbol ψ, choose all absolute and order constants before the parent. Under the common expansion and step-smallness hypotheses, every Λ≥1 has a pair u,p satisfying IsTruncation; every such pair has the claimed velocity and residual parity, incompressibility and Fourier support at 2Λ and 4Λ. The tail parameter is ε=Λ^(2−P)(1+‖V‖_(C_t C^(P,1/2)))². Lean uses an integer exponent 2−P, so it can be negative. The residual-plus-pressure estimate is quantified over two independent times t,t′, correctly bounding the sum of the two time suprema rather than only a simultaneous-time sum. The final Hessian bound is one sided. This proposition states existence and estimates for every truncation, not an explicit ∃! pair. This declaration defines a proposition; the corresponding theorem in Paper.Spine supplies its proof.

Default-value audit (b4): Λ≥1 excludes zero division in the Fourier symbol and makes negative integer powers genuine. The constructed V is smooth and periodic, so the universal cutoff implication has an actual continuous torus lift to which it can be applied. The p-slice smoothness and zero-mean condition make its integral a genuine normalization. Smooth periodic V and R_V on the compact time slab bound the real slab suprema on the right; the left-side Hölder norms carry explicit SpatialHolderHalf certificates. The two-time quantifier must be retained to recover the sum of suprema. 0<T excludes an empty time domain. No ENNReal.toReal conversion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.summary: Truncated next parent and its normalized pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.text:
After choosing a sufficiently large absolute envelope exponent a, this chooses C and K(n) uniformly over all positive slabs, admissible parents and ParentGeometry data. Every proposed MeanSolution(f,B,q) satisfies ‖B‖_[n]≤K(n)D^C‖f‖_[n+1] for every natural n. There is no Launch or Origin hypothesis: the mean inverse needs the parent and its geometry, not a particular growing seed. The norms are unweighted on all [0,T], consistent with the mean’s nonzero initial velocity selected by its terminal displacement. The only derivative loss stated here is one label/phase order in the source norm. This declaration defines a proposition; the corresponding theorem in Paper.Spine supplies its proof.

Default-value audit (b4): 0<T, D≥2 and λ≥1 are explicit through the hypotheses, making radius and width positive and the slab nonempty. The profile types supply smoothness and periodicity; with multiplier one their jets are bounded on the compact quotient, as recorded by hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_bddAbove_weighted. MeanSolution carries genuine within-time derivatives and endpoint constraints. Its phase averages are integrable because their values are real or Euclidean vectors. An unchecked real sSup is therefore not the reason for the inequality. There is no γ denominator, ENNReal.toReal conversion or unguarded square root here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.summary: Mean correction bounded with one extra source derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.text:
For every admissible parent, launch, central seed and time cutoff, this first asserts existence of a seed satisfying IsSeed. For every such seed and every P≥2 it asserts existence of R,S,u satisfying IsExpansion. It then gives uniqueness of R,S, the V,B,𝗉,q̄ slots from 1 through P and the C slots from 1 through P+1. Unused slots of the infinite indexed family u are not declared unique. Finally every such family has the sum identity, total divergence zero, the residual identity (5.29), the formula and envelope support of W_osc, pre-activation vanishing, the top-level conventions and phase independence of R_P outside the envelope. Smoothness is encoded in the profile types. The seed existence clause makes explicit an object fixed earlier in the text. This declaration defines a proposition; the corresponding theorem in Paper.Spine supplies its proof.

Default-value audit (b4): P≥2 prevents empty-recursion artifacts. The whole family is not defined by arbitrary choice here: existence is a genuine conjunct, and subsequent universal implications address families satisfying the full recurrences. Parent/Launch/Origin protect all leading-field denominators and the positive slab. Mean and oscillatory pressure gauges integrate smooth real functions on compact domains. Profile derivative operators use their smooth types and hT>0. No real supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs in the conclusion; the statement cannot gain its divergence or residual identity merely from an unbounded norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.summary: The finite expansion and its exact remainder

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.text:
For every construction c and C,T satisfying Theorem71Conclusions, there are velocity and pressure fields u,p with Proposition81Conclusions. This asserts existence on [0,T), convergence in every spatial Hölder order on each shorter closed slab, and agreement with every maximal solution from the limiting data. The statement is universal in the admissible construction, not tied to one particular choice function. It is the proposition of Proposition 8.1, proved in the spine.

The maximal-solution comparison is conditional and quantifies over finite real lifespans. It does not assert existence of a general maximal continuation beyond the constructed preterminal solution; Corollary 8.3 supplies maximality at the accumulation time.

Default-value audit (b4): The construction hypotheses and the conclusion IsEulerSolution give positive time, smooth periodic fields and finite spatial norms. Real supremum defaults cannot justify convergence on the actual relevant slices because the smooth periodic fields are bounded. The universal maximal-agreement clause is read together with the existential Euler fields; maximality at T is only concluded later.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.summary: The approximate velocities converge to a smooth Euler flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.text:
For every construction satisfying Theorem71Conclusions and every u,p satisfying Proposition81Conclusions, this asserts Proposition82Conclusions. Besides bounded velocity and central curl blow-up it exports the quantitative curl lower bound from the proof, already passed to the limit. The pressure is an input only through the Euler-solution conclusions. The lower bound is available to the Lean proof of Corollary 8.3 without assuming a formalized Beale–Kato–Majda criterion.

Default-value audit (b4): Theorem71Conclusions gives T > 0, and Proposition81Conclusions gives genuine smooth periodic Euler fields, preventing a bottom-filter limit or zero-default curl. The velocity bound compares an extended-real essential supremum with a finite ENNReal.ofReal bound. No ENNReal.toReal or nonintegrable Bochner integral appears.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.summary: Velocity stays bounded while central vorticity diverges

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.text:
For every Section 7 construction and every Euler limit furnished by Proposition 8.1, the velocity and its fixed-spatial-point time derivative have limits in C^m(K) for every finite m and compact K avoiding the torus origin. In the lifted representation K avoids every integer lattice point. HasOffOriginLimits permits the local limiting extension to depend on K and m. Joint smooth extension across T is a stronger, separate auxiliary conclusion.

Default-value audit (b4): The hypotheses give T > 0 and smooth Euler fields on [0,T), so the terminal filter is nontrivial and the derivatives represent actual derivatives on that domain. The definition demands convergence of ambient jets to a genuinely C^m local limit, not just pointwise convergence. Empty K is harmless because all compact K are quantified. There is no claim about u or the Euler equation at t=T.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.summary: Velocity and its time derivative converge off the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.remark_1_2.text:
This asks for a singular Euler flow with all of Theorem 1.1’s witness and uniqueness conclusions, and additionally a single smooth periodic extension through the terminal time away from the origin. It is stronger than the headline off-origin finite-order limit statement. The spine proves this remark from auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness for the library’s chosen construction, as decision D28 records; it does not prove or use the generalized Aux.Statement.theorem_1_1. No Euler equation is asserted for the extension after the singular time.

Default-value audit (b4): EulerSingularityWitness supplies an actual positive-time maximal solution and genuine smooth preterminal fields, excluding empty-interval and derivative-default shortcuts. Lower-integral divergence keeps infinity as ⊤. SmoothTerminalExtension is an existence statement about an open neighborhood and matching field, so no numerical junk operation certifies the extension. The uniqueness clause is accompanied by the actual maximal witness.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.remark_1_2.summary: The singular flow can extend smoothly off the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_1_1.text:
This defines the full headline proposition. It asks for smooth odd divergence-free periodic initial data, a finite positive maximal time, a smooth Euler velocity with normalized pressure, bounded velocity, divergent gradient and vorticity integrals, diverging central vorticity, and off-origin limits of velocity and its time derivative. The extra universal conjunct states uniqueness of the maximal velocity and its lifespan for those initial data. Compared with TorusEuler.Theorem11, this includes the uniqueness clause. It is a definition of a proposition; TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_1_1 is the spine proof.

Default-value audit (b4): EulerSingularityWitness contains IsMaximalEulerSolution and therefore a positive time and actual smooth Euler fields. Lower integrals retain infinity in ℝ≥0∞, and the terminal filter is nontrivial because T > 0. Pressure smoothness on the compact cell ensures its mean is an integrable Bochner integral. The source-level smoothness guards the spatial and within-time derivative values. The uniqueness conjunct accompanies an actual maximal witness and cannot replace it with a vacuous universal statement.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_1_1.summary: A smooth Euler flow with finite time singularity

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_4_2.text:
One pair C≥0,p∈ℕ works for every smooth periodic MeanParentFlow with H^#≤Id and every set of caps D≥1, L, K₀,K₁,Ω₀,Ω₁ bounding the inverse deformation, M, and the coefficients and first label derivatives. K and Ω are HalfHolder curves whose lifts equal the geometric formulas on the slab. With A=C(D+L+K₀+K₁+Ω₀+Ω₁)^p, every continuous source has an EndpointSystemSolution, the velocity estimate, and uniqueness of z,v,c,G on the interval. For every smooth periodic force and corresponding source primitive, every such solution yields smooth displacement, b(0)=c, and a smooth periodic zero-mean label pressure solving (4.11); the pushed-forward fields solve (4.12). Finally, at each time it gives a true linear equivalence for the compressed kinetic operator and bounds its inverse followed by Leray projection. The Lean L is a gradient cap; the paper’s source L is called src.

The recovered smooth pressure is obtained from the projected residual; the result does not assert that it equals $-\phi_t$ for the original integrated potential.

Default-value audit (b4): Parent smoothness and T>0 guard every fderiv, derivWithin and material fderivWithin, including endpoint times. The kinetic inverse is a continuous linear equivalence with inverse e.symm, not a total inverse at a singular operator. The source and solution curves are continuous; endpointClosedTimeNorm is therefore a real supremum of a bounded nonempty image. The smooth-force source primitive and Ωv integral are genuinely integrable. The zero spatial mean of qLabel is an integral of a smooth periodic function over a compact cell, not an undefined integral set to 0. Coefficient caps are forced nonnegative by their actual norm bounds; D≥1 makes the scale base positive. The arbitrary potential φ has only gradient uniqueness, while the separately recovered qLabel carries the mean gauge. No unguarded ENNReal.toReal or square-root normalization occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_4_2.summary: The endpoint problem selects a unique mean correction

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6.text:
For a sufficiently large fixed envelope exponent, choose one exponent C, level constants K(n,p) and sum constants KP(m,P), all before the parent and depth. Under D^C λ^(−1/12)≤1, every expansion of depth P≥2 has the level estimates (5.34)–(5.36), including the separately written p=1 cases. K(n,p) does not depend on P. The same expansion has the bounds for W_osc and the summed means/sources in (5.37). Its remainder satisfies KP(m,P)λ^(−5/4)λ^(−2P/3), with no residual factor D^C on that right-hand side. The exponent C is independent of derivative order, level and depth. All orders are quantified, not just a depth-dependent finite range. This declaration defines a proposition; the corresponding theorem in Paper.Spine supplies its proof.

Default-value audit (b4): Parent and Launch give D≥2, λ≥1 and a nonempty positive slab; real powers therefore use positive bases. P≥2 and the explicit Finset.Icc ranges prevent the zero-level and empty-sum conventions from standing in for the induction. Origin makes γ positive with bounded inverse, and typed smooth profiles yield bounded jets before using the real suprema. The assumed expansion fixes the mean and transverse pressure gauges and all correction indices. The smallness condition is an actual numerical hypothesis, not a consequence of division by zero. No ENNReal.toReal occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6.summary: All order frequency decay through every finite expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1.text:
Read the quantifiers in this order: choose any admissible radial cutoff ψ and any desired floor a₀; then choose b ≥ 1, an envelope exponent a ≥ a₀ and a majorant F; for every threshold B satisfying AdmissibleThreshold b F B there is N₁; for every N ≥ N₁ there are parameters P, a construction c and a time T. P is identified with b, B and λ₀=N, and its strength constant is exactly 18 exp 3. Both Theorem71Conclusions and Theorem71Steps are required. Thus B is chosen after the universal constants and before N. The quantifier ∀a₀,∃a≥a₀ allows arbitrarily large choices of a; it does not say every sufficiently large a works. The step record identifies actual velocities, pressure, oscillations and central amplitudes, but leaves the covector/first-wave identifications described in its annotation unstated.

The increment fields give spatial estimates at each time without a separate conjunct spelling out time continuity in the displayed norm. Theorem71Steps nevertheless represents the oscillation through jointly smooth twisted profiles and identifies its physical graph readout, so the absence of that extra conjunct is not evidence that time regularity is unavailable.

Default-value audit (b4): The parameter record supplies positive frequencies and threshold floors; Theorem71Conclusions supplies positive lifetime and norm guards; Theorem71Steps supplies a positive slab, smooth profiles and actual step identities. Universal implication over admissible B does not include a separate existential witness B, although AdmissibleThreshold is an ordinary numerical majorization condition; no inconsistency or emptiness is established by this reading. The existence of c is substantive. This declaration only defines the proposition; its compiled standard-axiom inventory is not by itself proof that the proposition holds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1.summary: One approximate sequence for every derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1.text:
The constants C≥0 and p∈ℕ are chosen before all coefficient data. On [0,1], K is pointwise self-adjoint, Ω is skew-adjoint, both satisfy EndpointCoefficientC1Bound, K≥κId with κ>0, and the zero-mean L² path energy is bounded below by μ‖v‖² with μ>0. For every continuous HalfHolder source L, the proposition supplies an EndpointSystemSolution, uniqueness of z,v,c,G on [0,1], and ‖v‖₀≤CQ^p‖L‖₀ with Q=2+κ⁻¹+μ⁻¹+K₀+K₁+Ω₀+Ω₁. If the lifts of K,Ω,L are jointly smooth on the closed slab, it also asserts smoothness of z,c,G. The coefficient hypothesis asks for time continuity in C^{0,1/2} and bounded first spatial derivatives; it does not require time continuity in C^{1,1/2}.

Default-value audit (b4): κ>0 and μ>0 guard both reciprocals in Q. EndpointCoefficientC1Bound includes nonnegative caps, actual differentiability of each lifted coefficient and time continuity in the HalfHolder norm. Thus its derivative caps cannot be default-zero bounds, and the integrated momentum is integrable. v is continuous in the conclusion and L is continuous by hypothesis, making their closed-time real suprema bounded on a nonempty interval. L² test paths have finite norm and integrable energies; their internal ENNReal conversion is finite by the Lp type. Only G=∇φ is unique; no unintended uniqueness of an ungauged φ is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1.summary: The endpoint inverse with uniqueness and a polynomial estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_13.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13. For every proposed natural exponent CA, choose the floor a₀; then for each a≥a₀ choose C and Cm. These choices precede the parent and every positive A≤D^CA. With ℓ=D^(−a), Kin=(D_aX)ᵀD_aX and Om=(D_aX)ᵀ(Mᵀ−M)D_aX, the statement asserts boundedness of the order-m half-Hölder jet samples and the two inequalities ℓ^m(|Kin|_(m,1/2)+|Om|_(m,1/2))≤Cm(m)D^C√ℓ≤Cm(m)/A for m≥1. It does not prove that the endpoint inverse constant A has the assumed polynomial bound; the citing result supplies that hypothesis. Norms use the Appendix D maximum convention for each half-Hölder block. At the source level its spine arguments are 5.1, D.2, Text eq_D_2. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_13.summary: Small weighted derivatives of the mean coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_14.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_14. After choosing an absolute envelope exponent, the estimate is uniform over all parents, MeanSolution(f,B,q), and smooth periodic velocities v representing B=D_aX v. For every n, if the source g=(D_aX)ᵀf at phase zero has finite weighted half-Hölder norm, then v does too and ‖v‖_[n],1/2≤Cn(n)D^C‖g‖_[n],1/2. The same v is the displacement derivative selected by the endpoint mean problem. The input and output use the same derivative order n; the extra derivative in Proposition 5.2 appears only when comparing Hölder and supremum norms. HolderFieldNormFinite is a substantive boundedness hypothesis, not decorative metadata. At the source level its spine arguments are 4.2, 5.1, D.2, D.3, Text eq_5_13. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_59.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59. For each natural order m, choose one nonnegative real Cm. It then works in every triple of real normed spaces for every continuous bilinear map B and fields f,g satisfying SpatialHolderHalf m. The output x↦B(f(x),g(x)) is again C^(m,1/2), with norm at most Cm‖B‖ times the product of the input norms. Scalar multiplication, tensor formation and vector contractions are instances of this generalization of the displayed product estimate. The norm of B is written explicitly, so the constant is independent of the chosen bilinear operation. At the source level its spine arguments are none. TorusEuler.Paper.Text.section8_setting.text:
This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.section8_setting. The opening of Section 8 fixes one construction supplied by Theorem 7.1. This proposition makes that choice explicit by existentially quantifying P, c, C and T with Theorem71Conclusions. It does not include Theorem71Steps or the equalities connecting P with a separately supplied threshold. Those stronger data are unnecessary for the statements of Propositions 8.1–8.4. At the source level its spine arguments are 7.1. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

Neither this theorem nor its proposition includes a limit velocity or closed-slab convergence. The separate `ReviewF7.closedSlabSetting` supplies the terminal limit clause used for the rest of the opening paragraph.
TorusEuler.Paper.Text.section8_setting.summary: Existence of the construction fixed in Section eight

TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions.text:
For a fixed construction c, constant C and time T, this records the shear, activation and slab times, (T1)–(T4), localized small oscillations, convergence t_j → T > 0, and two estimates exported from the proof. All stage indices start at zero; positive-wave clauses explicitly require j ≥ 1, and later-wave clauses j ≥ 2. The pressure and residual are already tied to actual velocity and pressure by the construction type. This bundle alone does not identify O_j with the oscillation built in Section 5. Theorem71Steps adds that identification and the central amplitude identity, but does not identify the central covector with the step covector or record the first-wave data (6.3). The statement of Theorem 7.1 fixes C = 18 exp 3, whereas this bundle only requires C ≥ 2.

The spatial increment estimates are pointwise in time and do not separately state continuity in the displayed time norms.

Default-value audit (b4): The imported construction has a positive frequency schedule, genuine smooth stage velocities and pressures, actual flow data, and momentum residuals (InductiveStageConstruction.lean:24–41,78–115). Thus spatial derivative defaults do not supply the (T1)–(T4) estimates. lifetime gives 0 < T < S_j, excluding empty slabs and an empty terminal filter. In T4_late_values, ν ≥ π > 0 guards η/ν, while C ≥ 2 guards C⁻¹ and the strength lower bound makes σ positive. At the next activation this same data makes 2σν > 0 in later_cutoff, guarding sqrt. increment pairs every real Hölder norm with SpatialHolderHalf, which carries smoothness and BddAbove. Nat subtraction is used only under j ≥ 1 or j ≥ 2. No ENNReal.toReal conversion occurs. Time regularity of O_j is not asserted by this bundle alone; it should be read through the exported step identities when needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions.summary: The common sequence and its quantitative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData.text:
At a fixed step j this record ties a Section 5 parent, launch, central seed, full seed, cutoff and finite expansion to the construction c. The parent scale is D=λ_{j−1}⁹, wave frequency λ_j, radius D^{−a}, width λ_j^{−1/2}, and depth 6K(q_{j+1}). It records the approximate Euler equation for V=U_{j−1}+W♮, the Fourier truncation U_j=S_{λ_j⁵}V with zero-mean pressure, and O_j=(W−〈W〉)♮. The explicit positive-slab parameter hT and the smooth twisted-profile types matter. This record can be formed at j=0 syntactically; Theorem71Steps invokes it only for j≥1. The central amplitude is identified, but the central wave vector is not identified with the covector built from k and the parent flow. The initial data and normalization of the first wave are also not recorded.

Default-value audit (b4): A positive slab is an explicit parameter; parent and launch hypotheses give positive scales and a nonzero carrier, and the step-level fields retain S5 finiteness, smoothness and nondegeneracy conditions. HierarchyTwistedProfile is built over a smooth slab profile (HierarchySmoothProfiles.lean:29–45), so it is not merely an arbitrary phase function. The approximate clause requires joint smoothness of V and Π before imposing momentumResidual; the truncation fixes the actual pressure/residual. A direct identification of the central covector is absent, so any argument relying on that equality must establish it elsewhere. This is a source boundary, not a constructed degenerate counterexample.

TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Steps.text:
For every natural j≥1, this asks for a positive slab and witnesses k, a central amplitude, a full seed, parent geometry, a cutoff, source profiles and hierarchy profiles satisfying Theorem71StepData. The envelope exponent a and the Fourier symbol ψ are shared across all j; the other witnesses may vary with the step. It is the extra construction export used by the auxiliary statements. It supplies Section 5 identities rather than just size estimates for U_j and O_j.

Default-value audit (b4): The explicit hT prevents an empty or singleton [0,S_j], and j≥1 prevents a spurious Nat-subtraction interpretation. Existence of a full record, rather than implication from one, is required at every positive step. Smooth-profile and scale guards are inherited from Theorem71StepData. This export still omits the covector/first-wave identifications described there; it is not a proof of all construction details merely by its name.
TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Steps.summary: Every positive step has the prescribed construction data

TorusEuler.Paper.WaveOn.text:
For every time t in J, k has within-J derivative −Dᵀk and a has within-J derivative −Da + p_w k, with p_w = 2⟨k,Da⟩/‖k‖². This packages only the two differential equations of (2.1). It does not assert k·a = 0, nonvanishing, trace freeness, symmetry of D′ + D², or existence of a wave. The predicate HasDerivWithinAt supplies a derivative witness; it is stronger than merely writing an equality using the total function derivWithin. Orthogonality must be supplied separately in Lemmas 2.1 and 2.2.

Default-value audit (b4): Bare predicate: the pressure coefficient divides by ‖k t‖², so k t = 0 gives the totalized value 0; nonvanishing is not a field. The uses in Lemma 2.2 assume k ≠ 0, and the persistence part of Lemma 2.1 starts from nonzero data. The Euler part of Lemma 2.1 deliberately allows k = 0. HasDerivWithinAt is not a default-zero derivative function, but on an empty or isolated time set its information can be vacuous or nonunique. Lemma 2.1 adds OrdConnected and UniqueDiffOn; the amplification statements restrict to a nondegenerate slab. No integrals, real suprema, ENNReal.toReal, or square roots occur in this predicate itself.

TorusEuler.Paper.alpha.text:
At t = w.clock τ, return (S⟨E₁,a⟩, ⟨E₂,a⟩, S⟨E₃,a⟩). These coordinates rewrite a as (α₁/S)E₁ + α₂E₂ + (α₃/S)E₃ on the active slab. The second coordinate is not multiplied by S. The definition accepts any amplitude function and does not impose the amplitude ODE or orthogonality; those are separate assumptions. Coordinate numbers in Lean are one lower than the subscripts in the paper.

The library's reduced coordinates are $(U,V)=(-\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$. Passing between the two systems conjugates the error matrix by $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)$, changing both off-diagonal signs.

Default-value audit (b4): There is no division by an amplitude component here. The inherited clock and shear involve division by r, but PhysicalAmplification proves r > 0 and σ > 0. The reconstruction in the paper uses S⁻¹ and requires an orthonormal frame, both legitimate on I. Evaluation at an arbitrary τ outside the assumed active slab need not retain the frame’s geometric interpretation. Zero amplitude maps to zero coordinates intentionally; later ratios α₁/α₂ require the separate positivity conclusion of Lemma 2.6.
TorusEuler.Paper.alpha.summary: Scaled coordinates of the amplitude vector

TorusEuler.Paper.corollary_8_3.text: This spine theorem proves `Statement.corollary_8_3`: for the same Section 7 construction and limit satisfying Propositions 8.1 and 8.2, the accumulation time is the actual finite maximal lifespan and both gradient and vorticity time integrals diverge. Its explicit numbered proof-argument list is empty, but the construction and solution hypotheses remain inside the statement; the empty list does not make those hypotheses disappear. The Lean proof integrates the quantitative curl lower bound exported by Proposition 8.2 over crossing intervals. It neither invokes nor formalizes the periodic Beale–Kato–Majda criterion used by the paper. Equality of the stated conclusion and fidelity of the proof route are therefore separate questions. This return inspects source and supplied dependency facts; it does not rerun Lean or a Comparator.
TorusEuler.Paper.corollary_8_3.summary: The accumulation time is the maximal existence time

TorusEuler.Paper.exists_appendixB_cutoff.text: This glue theorem constructs an admissible S5 cutoff symbol from Mathlib’s smooth radial bump. Its radius is two, it equals one on the unit ball, and it vanishes outside the radius-two ball. The proof supplies radiality, smoothness, the range [0,1] and the two cutoff values. This is useful because Theorem 7.1 is quantified over every such symbol; it is not the proof of a numbered manuscript result.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_1_3. For every b ≥ 1, threshold B, initial frequency N, order sequence q and frequency sequence satisfying the floor and schedule, this gives q_j ≤ q_{j+1} ≤ q_j+1 for j ≥ 1, q_j → ∞, and L_{j+1} ≤ (log λ_{j−1})². B(s)>0 is explicit. The maximum defining q_{j+1} is IsGreatest, which includes membership as well as maximality. Monotonicity of B and domination of fixed-order constants are omitted because this arithmetic result does not need them; q_0 and B(0) are unconstrained. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3.summary: Slow order growth, divergence and logarithmic gain bound

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_1.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_1. For every order-connected time set J with UniqueDiffOn, every differentiable F and primitive P, every trace-free D with a specified within-J derivative D′ and self-adjoint D′ + D², and every WaveOn k a, it asserts two conclusions. If k·a vanishes on J, the affine velocity and stated pressure are differentiable in the needed variables and satisfy momentum and incompressibility. From nonzero perpendicular data at any t₀ in J, both vectors remain nonzero and perpendicular throughout J. Smoothness, oddness, periodicity, and mean normalization of F,P are not required here. The Euler clause also allows k = 0, and persistence includes earlier times in J as well as later ones. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_1.summary: An affine wave solves Euler and remains transverse

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_2.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_2. For every time set J, trace-free B, and WaveOn k a with both vectors nonzero and perpendicular at every t in J. It states orthonormality of E₁ = k/‖k‖, E₂ = a/‖a‖, E₃ = E₁×E₂, the three within-J frame equations, and the within-J identity (log(‖k‖‖a‖))′ = B₃₃. Entries (0,1), (2,1), and (0,2) mean B₁₂, B₃₂, and B₁₃. No smoothness or time derivative of B is assumed, and no symmetry of B′ + B² is needed. For an arbitrary J these are relative derivative statements, not a claim of an ODE on an open interval. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_2.summary: Moving frame evolution and preceding strength identity

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_3.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_3. The configuration is a PhysicalAmplification on a compact I containing the image of [0,T] under t = t₀ + τ/r, with T ≥ 2. The paper is recovered by taking I to be exactly that slab; a larger I measures δ on a larger window. The first conjunct assumes ModelCase and NewWaveVector. It makes the preceding strength constant, gives all three ζ equations, and gives the two α equations for every amplitude vector at points with ζ₃ ≠ 0. The second conjunct fixes ε and T, then for every positive tolerance chooses S₀ before any model configuration; every such configuration with ratio ε and S ≥ S₀ has uniform ζ and coefficient errors at most that tolerance. It also asserts ζ₃ ≠ 0 on the entire slab for those sufficiently large S. The universal quantifier over ε is harmless outside the physical ε > 0 range because no w with that ratio exists. At the source level its spine arguments are 2.2. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_3.summary: Model equations and the strong shear limit

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_4.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_4. The absolute constants are selected before the physical data: ∃ C∈ℝ, p,N∈ℕ, then every C₀ ≥ N. The factor C and exponent p split the paper’s CT^C; the statement does not separately require C ≥ 0. The configuration is a PhysicalAmplification on a compact I containing the image of [0,T] under t = t₀ + τ/r, with T ≥ 2. The paper is recovered by taking I to be exactly that slab; a larger I measures δ on a larger window. Assuming FiniteSmallness and NewWaveVector, the proposition bounds ζ−ζ₀ and the normalized squared wave length by CT^pδ ≤ 1/2, gives 1/2 ≤ ζ₃ ≤ 3/2 and ‖ζ‖ ≤ 3T², and chooses one continuous error operator ℰ valid for every amplitude vector. ℰ acts on ℝ×ℝ with its max norm; ζ uses the Euclidean norm. The final conjunct also bounds the relative variation of the preceding strength by 2Tδ. That bound and continuity of ℰ are exported from the proof, so the Lean proposition contains more than the printed lemma statement. At the source level its spine arguments are 2.2. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_4.summary: Uniform wave comparison with a common amplitude error

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_5.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_5. For every 0 < ε ≤ 1, this proposition first asserts existence of a ReferenceSlope solution on [0,∞). For every such Y it then asserts uniqueness on that half-line, |Y| ≤ 1, one function e with 0 ≤ e ≤ ε/8 satisfying both (2.13) and the amplitude identity (2.14), and one zero τ_m with 2 ≤ ετ_m ≤ 3. It gives positivity before and negativity after that zero, a global maximum of a_ref at τ_m, and log a_ref(τ_m) ≥ (√ε)⁻¹−1. Values of Y or e at negative times are not specified. The same e appears in the pointwise formula and the integral formula; it is not reselected for each τ. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_5.summary: Global reference solution, unique peak and amplitude gain

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_6.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_6. The absolute constants are selected before the physical data: ∃ C∈ℝ, p,N∈ℕ, then every C₀ ≥ N. The factor C and exponent p split the paper’s CT^C; the statement does not separately require C ≥ 0. The configuration is a PhysicalAmplification on a compact I containing the image of [0,T] under t = t₀ + τ/r, with T ≥ 2. The paper is recovered by taking I to be exactly that slab; a larger I measures δ on a larger window. Assume the two wave predicates, FiniteSmallness, and the initial amplitude −S⁻¹E₁ + E₂. Then α₂ remains positive, every reference solution Y controls α₁/α₂+Y, and α₂ ≤ ‖a‖ ≤ (1+CT^pδ)α₂. Every reference solution also gives |log(‖a‖/a_ref)| ≤ ε. For each 0 ≤ τ₁ ≤ τ₂ ≤ T, the proposition supplies a continuous linear equivalence Φ between the two transverse planes, characterized by transporting every amplitude solution. Its norm is bounded by 252 exp(1) S ‖a(τ₂)‖/‖a(τ₁)‖. The equivalence asserts surjectivity as well as linearity; it is not merely a matrix with a forward bound. At the source level its spine arguments are 2.4, 2.5. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_6.summary: Growing amplitude comparison and transverse transport

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_7.text:
This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_7. There is a natural threshold N, independent of all physical data, after which every C₀ ≥ N gives the following result under FiniteSmallness, the two wave predicates, T ≥ 2, clock inclusion and the growing initial amplitude. With ν₊ and η₊ evaluated in the new wave’s normalized frame, ν₊ ≥ εν/2 on the whole slab. At times τ ≥ √2/ε it also gives |ν₊/ν−1| ≤ ε and |η₊/(ν₊cos φ)−1| ≤ 1/2. The late-time clause is conditional and may have no eligible τ if T is short. The paper’s subscripts + denote the new wave, not the older wave stored by w. At the source level its spine arguments are 2.4, 2.5, 2.6. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

The displayed cosine uses the reference angle, not the exact angle of the perturbed wave vector.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_7.summary: Positive first coupling and late successor ratio bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_3_1.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_3_1. The proposition asserts ProfileFamily for the concrete waveProfile and wavePressurePrimitive constructed in the library. It therefore supplies the odd smooth 1-periodic profiles, their zero-mean periodic primitives, the slope normalization and all stated derivative bounds uniformly in 0<h≤1. It is stronger than the paper’s bare existential claim because it identifies particular witnesses. At the source level its spine arguments are none. TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_4_1.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_4_1. For every MeanParentFlow and quadratic-form bound H^#≤Id, every label a and every L² path v on (0,T] with zero time integral obey the two inequalities of Lemma 4.1. Set z(t)=∫₀^t v, ξ=D_aX z, and ξ_t=Mξ+D_aX v. The first inequality bounds ∫⟨H^#ξ,ξ⟩ by half the integral of ‖ξ_t‖²; the second gives that half-integral as a lower bound for ∫(⟨Kv,v⟩+⟨Ωv,z⟩). Representing H¹₀ by the primitive of a zero-mean L² derivative encodes both endpoint conditions. v t is a chosen representative of an L² class, but all expressions involving it are inside integrals and are unchanged almost everywhere. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_4_1.summary: The two endpoint displacement energy inequalities

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_10.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_10. For every small added velocity v that is jointly smooth, periodic and divergence free, with each spatial derivative of order j≤2 bounded by λ^(−5/2), the field V+v has a flow with deformation bound Γ(P)D^bλ^(1/4). The proposition then gives the same forward and reverse derivative bound for every label flow of V+v on [0,T]. The inverse deformation is represented by the derivative of the reverse transition Yf t 0, not by an algebraic inverse at a possibly singular matrix. The per-order derivative hypothesis is implied by the paper’s bound on the full C² norm. Constants are chosen before b,Γ,parent,v, under the common step-smallness assumption. At the source level its spine arguments are 5.1, 5.6, 5.4. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_10.summary: Controlled deformation after a small velocity perturbation

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3.text:
This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3. For a sufficiently small absolute envelope radius, one C and sequence K(n) work for every parent, launch, central seed and geometry. The first clause bounds any compatible seed by twice its central size on ‖a‖≤2ℓ and makes κ·M𝐚 strictly positive there. Clause (i) bounds a transverse forced seed on [t₀,T] by its weighted initial norm and weighted source, with initial data and source supported in the envelope. Clause (ii) bounds any TransverseSolution with a zero-mean source vanishing before activation and outside the envelope, including λ times its pressure norm. Clause (iii) gives size λ^(−5/4) for the unswitched leading velocity and pressure. The formal fields in (i) are smooth twisted profiles on [0,T]; the weighted estimate uses only their restriction to [t₀,T]. The raw leading fields in (iii) are measured directly by fieldNorm. At the source level its spine arguments are 3.1, 5.1, D.1, D.2, D.3. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

The statement's active estimates still quantify over fields represented as smooth twisted profiles on the full slab; no general extension adapter for arbitrary active-slab data is supplied by this spine node.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3.summary: Seed comparison and estimates for normalized transverse solutions

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3_of_ode.text: This supplies the local Leaves instance from Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2 and the assumed weighted ODE derivative estimate, then invokes lemma_5_3_of_leaves. The separate theorem odeWordBound_of_D3 is what derives that ODE estimate from the cited D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3_of_ode.summary: Pass the supplied estimates to the transverse argument

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_5.text:
This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_5. After the common a₀,a,C,K(n) choices, every transverse profile V with zero phase average has ‖C[V]‖_[n],γ≤K(n)D^C λ⁻¹‖V‖_[n+1],γ. If V_t+MV+κ∂s q=f on the activation interval, f has zero phase mean and q is normalized there, the same frequency gain controls (∂t+M)C[V]+𝐝q by the V and f norms of order n+1. A second clause asserts smooth twisted representatives of A₁ and its pressure on the full slab, equal to the raw leading fields on [t₀,T] over the centered cell; these obey the equation with f=0 and the corresponding bound. Average V=0 and average f=0 are imposed on the whole slab, while transversality and the equation are only required on [t₀,T]. At the source level its spine arguments are 5.1, D.1. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

The full-slab zero-mean restrictions on both velocity and forcing remain in the proved statement. Alongside the broader parent and normalization interface, they prevent treating the complete statement as an unqualified same-or-stronger transcription of arbitrary active-slab data.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_5.summary: One frequency gain from the divergence correction

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_7.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_7. For any real normed target space and any smooth twisted profile g₀ that is phase independent outside the envelope, let F(t,x)=g₀(t,X(t,·)⁻¹(x),k_*·X(t,·)⁻¹(x)). This is graphRead with Y(t)=X t 0. For every order m, the proposition gives a weighted estimate on [t₀,T] and an unweighted one on [0,T]. Each controls the order-m coordinate derivative sum and the full C^(m,1/2) norm, at costs (D^Cλ^(3/2))^m and (D^Cλ^(3/2))^(m+1). If g₀ is phase independent everywhere, replace that scale by D^C. Lean sums ordered coordinate words for the physical derivative bound; this bounds the paper’s multi-index sum with fixed order-dependent multiplicities. At the source level its spine arguments are 5.1, D.1. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_7.summary: Convert profile bounds to physical derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_8.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8. After a is fixed, choose b₀, a depth-dependent floor Γ₀ and constants K(m,P). The claim holds for every b≥b₀ and every Γ≥Γ₀, every admissible expansion of depth P≥2, and Γ(P)D^bλ^(−1/12)≤1. The physical velocity V=U+W^♮ is jointly smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free; Π=pU+𝖯^♮ is jointly smooth and periodic. Its exact residual is the graph evaluation of R_P+S+C[S]. The oscillatory velocity has uniform size λ^(−5/4); all Hölder orders are controlled separately for oscillatory and mean parts. The residual’s C^(1,1/2) bound contains the depth tail and χ.derivativeSize γ, the supremum of the weighted activation derivative. This lemma quantifies over already supplied expansions rather than selecting one. At the source level its spine arguments are 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_8.summary: Approximate Euler solution with controlled physical residual

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_9.text:
This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_9. Under the common expansion and step-smallness assumptions, the Hessian of the pressure correction 𝖯^♮ is at most Γ(P)D^bλ^(−1/4) times the identity as a quadratic form at every point and time. This is an upper quadratic-form estimate, not a bound on the absolute Hessian or its operator norm. On [t₀,T], the central velocity gradient differs from ∇U+χ̃ center⊗κ by at most λ^(−1/3) in operator norm. InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℝ center κ sends v to (κ·v)center; reversing the arguments would describe a different matrix. The error E_c is encoded as the displayed difference, so no separate error field is chosen. At the source level its spine arguments are 3.1, 4.2, 5.1, 5.3, 5.6, 5.7, B.1, D.1, 5.4. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

These bounds concern the finite approximate expansion; Fourier truncation adds errors that are handled separately in Proposition 5.11.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_9.summary: Pressure Hessian upper bound and central gradient return

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1. For 0 < ρ ≤ 1, λ ≥ 1 and T > 0 with T‖Bρ‖ ≤ 1/8, this asserts that a FirstWaveOrigin exists and that every such wave has the conclusions of Lemma 6.1. The existence conjunct prevents a universal claim about an empty wave type. FirstWaveOrigin includes the initial covector λe₁, an amplitude in the positive e₂ direction, the ODEs, transversality, and attainment of the normalization max|a| = λ^{−3/4}. The conclusion is at the origin; it does not by itself build the full spatial hierarchy. At the source level its spine arguments are 2.2. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1.summary: The first wave exists and satisfies the seed bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_A_2.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2. One nonnegative real C and natural p serve two cases: H=ℝ³ with the spatial Leray projection, and H=L²((0,1];ℝ³) with the commuting spatial and zero-time-mean projections. In each case B is a HalfHolder operator field, μ>0, Lip≥0, B is Lipschitz with that constant, and its quadratic form is at least μ‖w‖². The second coercivity assertion is only for paths with endpointIntegral 1 w=0. The conclusion is FreezingConclusion, including a genuine continuous linear isomorphism and the higher-order regularity equivalence. Replacing C^{1,1/2} by a Lipschitz bound strengthens the printed base statement; when higher regularity is requested the separate C^{k,1/2} hypothesis is retained. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_A_2.summary: The two Hölder inverses and their higher regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1. For each smooth even cutoff ψ, this chooses one operator constant and two sequences of nonnegative order constants before quantifying over Λ>0, value spaces and fields. It packages the multiplier identity; derivative commutation; parity, divergence and frequency preservation; uniform and C^{0,1/2} bounds; the Hölder tail estimate; and Bernstein’s estimate. Complex Banach-valued fields form the first block, real velocity fields the second; Bernstein allows any real normed target and detects frequency support through scalar linear measurements. The real time-derivative clause uses a nondegenerate closed slab and HasDerivWithinAt. Sorted coordinate words represent multi-indices. This generalizes the paper’s radial ψ and Λ≥1 assumptions to even ψ and Λ>0; the norm convention is the spatial Fréchet-jet norm. It is the proposition proved by the spine lemma. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1.summary: The frequency cutoff preserves structure and controls derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1. For every positive radius ℓ, positive phase width h, positive time weight γ and order n, this packages four estimates: label/phase differentiation, bilinear products, phase averaging and the zero-mean primitive, and the unweighted half-Hölder product rule for phase-independent fields. Finiteness is required on the inputs and asserted on the outputs. The product is any continuous bilinear map, with its norm included in the explicit constant. The phase-integral block additionally assumes a complete target and period one in s; zero mean is required only for the primitive. Constants are three for the summed label derivative, two for the primitive, and an explicit word-count factor for products. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1.summary: Derivative product and phase estimates for finite norms

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2. The three conjuncts close CoefficientPower under bilinear products of norm at most one, under inverse in a complete real normed algebra, and under summation with a small positive label radius. Output constant sequences are chosen before the time type, D, the fields and, in the product block, the bilinear map. The product exponent is 2 max(a,b); the inverse exponent is 3 max(a,e), where ‖c⁻¹‖≤D^e. The last block assumes 0<ℓ≤(D^a)⁻¹ and retains one factor ℓ when at least one derivative hits c. Natural exponents encode the paper’s absolute real powers after upward rounding; the resulting small-scale hypothesis can be stricter than the literal real-exponent one. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2.summary: Uniform product inverse and weighted coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_3.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3. Fix a finite ordered set of derivative directions, a target order n and numerical bounds C_m; then choose C_n before all vector spaces, operators, coefficients and solutions. The statement assumes commutation of L₀ with derivatives, the Leibniz relation for each coefficient action, commutation of forcing and coefficient derivatives, nonnegative operator bounds bν, a uniform zero-order estimate for every admissible u, and (D.7) only for 1≤m≤n. It concludes the finite-derivative-norm estimate for any v,f satisfying Lv=f. The unknown derivatives DE need no separate commutation hypothesis in the written Lean statement; it uses canonical ordered words. Quotient forcing spaces can encode equations modulo gradients, while the space E encodes preserved constraints. This is an abstract seminorm theorem, not a claim of existence of a solution. At the source level its spine arguments are none. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_3.summary: A zero order inverse estimate lifts to higher derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformation.text:
For an arbitrary supplied two-time flow X, this is fderiv ℝ (X 0 t) a, the continuous linear map D_aX(t,a). It differentiates labels while holding both times fixed. The definition alone has no hypothesis saying X is a flow or is differentiable. In the endpoint statements, MeanParentFlow supplies the geometric setting in which this derivative is invertible and is the deformation used in K and Ω.

Default-value audit (b4): At a nondifferentiable spatial map, fderiv returns 0, so the bare definition can be zero for a degenerate reason. A differentiable but constant map also gives a genuine zero deformation, hence differentiability alone does not imply invertibility. MeanParentFlow supplies a smooth periodic parent and its two-time flow; flow regularity and the inverse-flow identities rule out both failures on [0,T]. Outside that interval the definition has no such guarantee. No integral, supremum, ENNReal conversion, division, or square root occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformation.summary: The derivative of the particle position with respect to labels

TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformationInv.text:
This is the label derivative of X t 0 at the current position X 0 t a. It represents (D_aX(t,a))⁻¹ by differentiating the inverse flow, rather than calling a total inverse operation on a linear map. For MeanParentFlow and t∈[0,T], the flow composition identities identify it with the two-sided inverse of meanDeformation. The definition is otherwise available for any X and does not assert the inverse identity itself.

Default-value audit (b4): The encoding avoids the default value of a singular linear-map inverse, but fderiv of the back-to-label map still returns 0 if that map is not differentiable. MeanParentFlow’s flow regularity and inverse composition identities are the guards in Theorem 4.2. A bound on meanDeformationInv by itself would not establish invertibility for an arbitrary X. No variable division, integral, supremum, ENNReal conversion, or square root is evaluated here.

TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradient.text:
The operator $M(t,a)=D_xU(t,X(0,t,a))$ is the Eulerian velocity gradient evaluated at the particle position. Its derivative convention is the usual Fréchet derivative, so applying it to a vector gives directional differentiation of the velocity. The label is held fixed when this field is differentiated in time. This explicit definition does not assume the parent solves Euler or satisfies a Hessian upper bound.

Default-value audit (b4): fderiv gives 0 at a nondifferentiable spatial slice, which can make M falsely appear small when read without hypotheses. In the endpoint statements joint smoothness in MeanParentFlow ensures true differentiability of every U t on [0,T]. The evaluation point X 0 t a imposes no further division or integral. There is no supremum, ENNReal.toReal, or square root.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradient.summary: The parent gradient along a particle path

TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradientRate.text:
The derivative $M_t(t,a)$ of the parent gradient along the particle with fixed label $a$. Lean differentiates the curve $r\mapsto M(r,a)$ within the closed interval $[0,T]$, which includes the one-sided endpoint convention. This definition names the derivative used in $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)$. The derivative’s existence and continuity follow from the smooth parent-flow hypotheses in the lemmas that use it.

Default-value audit (b4): derivWithin is 0 when differentiability or uniqueness of the within derivative fails. If T < 0 the time set is empty; if T = 0 it is a singleton. Neither case is ruled out by this definition. MeanParentFlow supplies T > 0, smooth parent slices and smooth flow dependence on the slab, giving actual one-sided derivatives with unique directions at both endpoints. All uses of M_t in Theorems 4.1/4.2 are inside that slab. No integral, supremum, ENNReal conversion, reciprocal, or square root occurs directly.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradientRate.summary: Time derivative of the gradient at fixed label

TorusEuler.Paper.meanHsharp.text:
Define H^# = −(M_t + M∘M) using the parent gradient along the particle flow and its within-[0,T] time derivative. endpointHessian is the library formula −(Mt + M.comp M). H^# need not be self-adjoint for an arbitrary parent; the endpoint theorem assumes only the quadratic-form upper bound ⟨H^#w,w⟩ ≤ ‖w‖². It becomes the pressure Hessian along trajectories only when the appropriate Euler/residual identity is also available.

Default-value audit (b4): This inherits the default-zero possibilities of meanGradient and meanGradientRate. Without parent regularity, the inequality H^# ≤ Id could therefore be satisfied by an artifact of those selected derivatives. MeanParentFlow on a positive interval is an explicit hypothesis wherever the bound is used in Lemma 4.1 or Theorem 4.2. Under that hypothesis the matrices have their intended derivatives. The formula adds no integration, supremum, division, ENNReal conversion, or square root.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanHsharp.summary: Effective endpoint Hessian of the parent flow

TorusEuler.Paper.meanKinetic.text:
The label coefficient $K=F^*F$ with $F=D_aX(0,t,a)$. On real Euclidean space the adjoint is the transpose, so this is the paper’s $(D_aX)^TD_aX$. The definition gives a symmetric nonnegative operator without a quantitative lower bound. An inverse-deformation bound $\|F^{-1}\|\le D_-$ supplies ellipticity $K\ge D_-^{-2}I$, which is proved by a separate inequality used in Theorem 4.2.

Default-value audit (b4): If the deformation is the default fderiv value 0, then K is exactly 0; a genuine singular F likewise produces only semidefinite K. Theorem 4.2 assumes MeanParentFlow and an upper bound D ≥ 1 for the genuine inverse deformation, giving a positive ellipticity constant. The bare K formula is not itself an ellipticity certificate. No integral, real supremum, ENNReal.toReal, division, or square root appears.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanKinetic.summary: The metric induced by the particle deformation

TorusEuler.Paper.meanVorticity.text:
The label coefficient $\Omega=F^*(M^*-M)F$, where $F$ and $M$ are derived from the actual parent flow. It is the skew part of the Eulerian gradient transported to the label coordinates. The formula requires no Euler equation and does not identify a pressure. Together with $F_t=MF$, it yields $K_t-\Omega=2F^*F_t$, the coefficient identity used when the integrated momentum equation is differentiated.

Default-value audit (b4): The formula has no inverse or denominator, but it inherits fderiv default values through F and M. In the MeanParentFlow setting their differentiability is justified; outside it Ω = 0 need not mean that the actual parent flow has zero vorticity. Adjoint and composition of continuous linear maps have no analytic domain failure. No integral, supremum, ENNReal conversion, or square root occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanVorticity.summary: The antisymmetric gradient pulled back to labels

TorusEuler.Paper.modelEntries.text:
The matrix whose only potentially nonzero entries are $B_{12}=\nu$ and $B_{32}=\eta$. Lean indexes rows and columns from zero, so these appear at $(0,1)$ and $(2,1)$. These are entries in the moving frame rather than a fixed spatial basis. The model-case predicate separately says that the physical older gradient has these entries throughout the normalized interval.

Default-value audit (b4): This is a finite array built by insertion of ν, η, and zero. It has no divisions, derivatives, integrals, suprema, ENNReal conversions, or square roots. Allowing ν or η to vanish in the bare definition is deliberate; the physical setting excludes that case when the matrix is used as the model background.
TorusEuler.Paper.modelEntries.summary: Model matrix with two prescribed coupling entries

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_2_8.text:
This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_2_8. After one absolute threshold for C₀, assume the growing wave hypotheses, 0 < ε₊ ≤ ε/32, and T ≥ H = 2/√(εε₊). The proposition chooses τ_m, characterized as the zero of every reference solution on [0,∞), with τ_m ≥ 2/ε; it asserts at least one ratio crossing η₊/ν₊ = ε₊ in [τ_m,H]. It chooses a real peak that is an actual greatest value of ‖a‖ over [0,T]. Every crossing in that interval then has normalized strength σ₊/(λ peak) between exp(−1)/(4√(εε₊)) and 18 exp(3)/√(εε₊). Finally all amplitudes at τ∈[0,1] are at most exp(3−1/√ε) peak. The universal reference-solution characterization is used with Lemma 2.5’s existence and uniqueness. At the source level its spine arguments are 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

A least crossing is selected separately when the construction needs one; this proposition does not assert uniqueness of a crossing.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_2_8.summary: Successor crossing with strength bounds and early gain

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_1.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5_1. First choose one natural exponent C and coefficient constants K(m). For every proposed sequence C′(m), choose composition constants Kf(m); only then quantify over every parent and launch. This order makes C and K independent of the parent and allows Kf to depend on the derivative constants of f. The six coefficient families are D_aX, its inverse, M, κ/λ, λ²/‖κ‖² and P_κ. Their m-th Fréchet derivatives have bound K(m)D^(C(m+1)); smooth normed-space-valued f with amplitude Af≥0 has the composition bound Kf(m)Af D^(Cm). For 0<ℓ≤D^(−C), the final clause gives the finite weighted sums in (5.8). The real sequences K,Kf are not separately declared positive. Operator norms of Fréchet derivatives replace the paper’s sums of coordinate derivative suprema; the absolute constants absorb the dimension factors. At the source level its spine arguments are B.1, D.2. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_1.summary: Parent coefficients and composition at every order

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_11.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5_11. For each admissible smooth cutoff symbol ψ, choose all absolute and order constants before the parent. Under the common expansion and step-smallness hypotheses, every Λ≥1 has a pair u,p satisfying IsTruncation; every such pair has the claimed velocity and residual parity, incompressibility and Fourier support at 2Λ and 4Λ. The tail parameter is ε=Λ^(2−P)(1+‖V‖_(C_t C^(P,1/2)))². Lean uses an integer exponent 2−P, so it can be negative. The residual-plus-pressure estimate is quantified over two independent times t,t′, correctly bounding the sum of the two time suprema rather than only a simultaneous-time sum. The final Hessian bound is one sided. This proposition states existence and estimates for every truncation, not an explicit ∃! pair. At the source level its spine arguments are 5.8, 5.9, B.1, Text eq_5_59. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_11.summary: Truncated next parent and its normalized pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_2.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5_2.
