After choosing a sufficiently large absolute envelope exponent a, this chooses C and K(n) uniformly over all positive slabs, admissible parents and ParentGeometry data. Every proposed MeanSolution(f,B,q) satisfies ‖B‖_[n]≤K(n)D^C‖f‖_[n+1] for every natural n. There is no Launch or Origin hypothesis: the mean inverse needs the parent and its geometry, not a particular growing seed. The norms are unweighted on all [0,T], consistent with the mean’s nonzero initial velocity selected by its terminal displacement. The only derivative loss stated here is one label/phase order in the source norm. At the source level its spine arguments are 5.1, D.1, Text eq_D_2, Text eq_5_14. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_2.summary: Mean correction bounded with one extra source derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_4.text:
This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5_4. For every admissible parent, launch, central seed and time cutoff, this first asserts existence of a seed satisfying IsSeed. For every such seed and every P≥2 it asserts existence of R,S,u satisfying IsExpansion. It then gives uniqueness of R,S, the V,B,𝗉,q̄ slots from 1 through P and the C slots from 1 through P+1. Unused slots of the infinite indexed family u are not declared unique. Finally every such family has the sum identity, total divergence zero, the residual identity (5.29), the formula and envelope support of W_osc, pre-activation vanishing, the top-level conventions and phase independence of R_P outside the envelope. Smoothness is encoded in the profile types. The seed existence clause makes explicit an object fixed earlier in the text. At the source level its spine arguments are 4.2. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

The support is in label coordinates; an Eulerian support bound additionally transports that set by the parent flow.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_4.summary: The finite expansion and its exact remainder

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1.text:
This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8_1. For every construction c and C,T satisfying Theorem71Conclusions, there are velocity and pressure fields u,p with Proposition81Conclusions. This asserts existence on [0,T), convergence in every spatial Hölder order on each shorter closed slab, and agreement with every maximal solution from the limiting data. The statement is universal in the admissible construction, not tied to one particular choice function. It is the proposition of Proposition 8.1, proved in the spine. At the source level its spine arguments are 1.3, Text eq_5_59. The result still assumes the setting of 7.1 through its statement; absence from the explicit proof-argument list is not absence of hypotheses. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

The comparison with other maximal solutions ranges over finite real lifespans and is conditional. Maximality of this limit at the accumulation time is proved by Corollary 8.3, not asserted by Proposition 8.1 alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1.summary: The approximate velocities converge to a smooth Euler flow

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_2.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8_2. For every construction satisfying Theorem71Conclusions and every u,p satisfying Proposition81Conclusions, this asserts Proposition82Conclusions. Besides bounded velocity and central curl blow-up it exports the quantitative curl lower bound from the proof, already passed to the limit. The pressure is an input only through the Euler-solution conclusions. The lower bound is available to the Lean proof of Corollary 8.3 without assuming a formalized Beale–Kato–Majda criterion. At the source level its spine arguments are 1.3, 2.2, 2.4, B.1. The result still assumes the setting of 7.1, 8.1 through its statement; absence from the explicit proof-argument list is not absence of hypotheses. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_2.summary: Velocity stays bounded while central vorticity diverges

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_4.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8_4. For every Section 7 construction and every Euler limit furnished by Proposition 8.1, the velocity and its fixed-spatial-point time derivative have limits in C^m(K) for every finite m and compact K avoiding the torus origin. In the lifted representation K avoids every integer lattice point. HasOffOriginLimits permits the local limiting extension to depend on K and m. Joint smooth extension across T is a stronger, separate auxiliary conclusion. At the source level its spine arguments are 1.3. The result still assumes the setting of 7.1, 8.1 through its statement; absence from the explicit proof-argument list is not absence of hypotheses. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_4.summary: Velocity and its time derivative converge off the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAmplitude.text:
For any real function Y and any real τ, define a_ref(τ) = exp(∫₀^τ Y(s) ds). The interval integral is oriented, so the same formula also assigns a value for negative τ, although the reference-solution results only use τ ≥ 0. The exponential guarantees a strictly positive value. To read this as the amplitude whose logarithmic derivative is Y, use ReferenceSlope or another hypothesis giving local integrability and the fundamental theorem of calculus.

Default-value audit (b4): This bare definition is not a certificate of integrability. A non-integrable Y on the interval gives the default integral 0 and therefore a_ref = 1. All uses in Lemmas 2.5, 2.6 and Proposition 2.8 pair it with ReferenceSlope on τ ≥ 0; its derivative witnesses imply continuity on every compact subinterval, hence integrability. Positivity of exp holds even in the default case, so positivity alone would not discharge this audit. There is no ENNReal.toReal, supremum, variable division, or square root in this definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAmplitude.summary: Amplitude recovered by integrating the growth rate

TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAngle.text:
Define φ(ε,τ) = arctan(ετ²/2). This chooses the branch of the angle in (2.4) rather than making φ an independently quantified function. For ε ≥ 0 it lies in [0,π/2), as proved by referenceAngle_mem, and tan φ = ετ²/2 for every real ε and τ. The definition is available outside the physical range ε > 0, but its nonnegative-angle interpretation then needs the displayed sign hypothesis.

This is a reference angle, not generally the exact angle of the perturbed physical wave vector.

Default-value audit (b4): The only explicit denominator is 2, which is nonzero. Real.arctan is defined for every real input and always lies strictly between −π/2 and π/2. Consequently later tan(referenceAngle ε τ) never encounters a tangent pole, even if ε < 0. The sign restriction ε ≥ 0 is needed for φ ≥ 0, not for existence of the angle. No derivatives, integrals, square roots, suprema, or ENNReal conversions are used.

TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAngle_mem.text: For $\varepsilon\ge0$, the reference angle lies in $[0,\pi/2)$ at every real time $\tau$. The argument of the arctangent is nonnegative because it contains $\tau^2$. The strict upper endpoint matters: the cosine is positive for every finite time, so the later trigonometric denominators describe ordinary finite quantities.
TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAngle_mem.summary: Reference angle is nonnegative and below a right angle

TorusEuler.Paper.referenceSystemMatrix.text:
The matrix acting on $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ has first row $(-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi,-\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi))$ and second row $(-1,0)$, with $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. The leading minus sign applies to the whole displayed matrix. At zero its growing direction is $(-1,1)$. The older library uses $(U,V)=(-\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$, so the matrices differ by changing the sign of the first coordinate. This definition supplies coefficients; convergence from finite shear is proved separately.

Default-value audit (b4): All trigonometric expressions are evaluated at referenceAngle, so cos φ > 0 and the tangent quotient is not singular. No variable denominator, integral, derivative, supremum, ENNReal conversion, or square root is introduced. A zero coefficient at a particular time is a legitimate matrix entry, not a default value.
TorusEuler.Paper.referenceSystemMatrix.summary: The coefficient matrix of the reference system

TorusEuler.Paper.remark_1_2.text: This spine theorem proves the existential main Remark 1.2: a singular Euler flow with the headline witness and maximal-solution uniqueness also has one smooth periodic extension through terminal time away from the origin. It imposes no Euler equation after that time. Under ledger decision D28 the proof uses `auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness`, which selects its own cutoff, threshold and scheduled construction. It does not prove the generalized reference propositions `Aux.Statement.theorem_1_1`, `Aux.Statement.lemma_1_2` or `Aux.Statement.lemma_1_3`. The supplied VerifySpine checker exempts this library row from frontier, bypass and setting checks. This return inspects that documented source route and does not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.remark_1_2.summary: The singular flow can extend smoothly off the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.scaledNormSq.text:
For a supplied scale S and vector ζ, return ζ₁² + ζ₂²/S² + ζ₃². The paper uses this number as m in ‖k‖² = λ²m after the coordinate expansion. No wave, frame, or λ is an argument of this definition, so the identity with ‖k‖ is context supplied by zeta and the physical hypotheses. In particular this is not the ordinary Euclidean squared norm of ζ unless S = 1.

Default-value audit (b4): If S = 0, Lean assigns ζ₂²/S² the value 0; the expression then loses its second component. If ζ = 0, m = 0. The numbered model statement gets S > 0 from PhysicalAmplification. Where strongShearMatrix is used, ζ₃ ≠ 0 already implies m > 0 because all three terms are nonnegative. Lemma 2.4 strengthens that guard to ζ₃ ≥ 1/2. There are no integrals, derivatives, suprema, ENNReal conversions, or square roots in the formula itself.

TorusEuler.Paper.statementsS34ASolenoida.text:
This local instance makes the existing NormedAddCommGroup structure on the solenoidal HalfHolder subspace available to elaboration. It introduces no new norm formula and no additional regularity assertion about a field. The paper uses the inherited C^{0,1/2} norm on divergence-free fields without spelling out this type-class step. It is implementation support for the endpoint statements, not a separately numbered mathematical claim.

Default-value audit (b4): No analytic operation is defined here: inferInstance reuses the bundled normed additive-group structure. Finiteness of the HalfHolder norm is part of the ambient bundled space, rather than a fresh real supremum over an arbitrary unbounded function. This instance does not by itself prove coefficient continuity, integrability, or differentiability.
TorusEuler.Paper.statementsS34ASolenoida.summary: The inherited norm on divergence free fields

TorusEuler.Paper.statementsS34ASolenoida.text:
This local instance supplies the inherited real NormedSpace structure on the solenoidal HalfHolder subspace. It lets the endpoint statements use continuous linear maps, scalar multiplication and derivatives in that subspace. No solution is constructed and no coefficient estimate is proved. It is the explicit elaboration support for the paper’s use of a normed linear space of divergence-free fields.

Default-value audit (b4): The declaration only reuses an existing type-class instance. It introduces no derivative, integral, division, supremum, ENNReal conversion or square root. The presence of a NormedSpace instance is not a substitute for any field’s regularity hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.statementsS34ASolenoida.summary: Scalar multiplication on divergence free Hölder fields

TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix.text:
The four entries give the linear system for (α₁,α₂) after Π is expanded and α₃ is eliminated by ζ·α = 0. Both rows contain contributions divided by m; the second also contains S² and ζ₃ denominators. The formula is arranged so that strongShearMatrix_mulVec recovers exactly the displayed two equations of Lemma 2.3. Being a Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ, it records entries; it does not itself assert differentiability or solve the system.

Default-value audit (b4): Three possible singular quantities are S, m = scaledNormSq S ζ, and ζ₃ (Lean ζ 2). All are totalized in the raw formula. Lemma 2.3 assumes ζ₃ ≠ 0 in the amplitude equation and gets S > 0 from w; then m > 0. Its uniform-limit clause explicitly asserts ζ₃ ≠ 0 once S is large. The unconditional multiplication identity remains valid when a denominator vanishes because it is an identity in these totalized expressions; it must not be mistaken for a justified elimination of α₃ in that case. No integral or derivative is evaluated here.
TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix.summary: Finite shear coefficients of the amplitude system

TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix_mulVe.text: This algebraic identity expands each row of the finite-shear matrix against $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ into the corresponding right-hand side displayed in Lemma 2.3, including the pressure term and the third-coordinate elimination. It bridges the coefficient definition and the written amplitude equations. The identity is valid for all real inputs under Lean's total division; the differential theorem separately supplies the model assumptions and the nonzero third coordinate required for its physical interpretation.
TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix_mulVe.summary: The matrix recovers both amplitude equations

TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearPressure.text:
The scalar $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/m$ in the finite-shear model equations. It is linear in the two amplitude coordinates. Lemma 2.3 identifies it with $\lambda Sp_{\rm w}/r$ after eliminating the third coordinate by perpendicularity. The definition uses total division; the theorem supplies the geometric conditions that make the denominator meaningful.

Default-value audit (b4): This definition is total: if m = 0, Π is 0 even if its numerator is nonzero. The definition alone supplies no positivity assumption on S or m. In Lemma 2.3 the amplitude clause requires ζ₃ ≠ 0, making m > 0, and PhysicalAmplification gives S > 0. The later finite comparison gives ζ₃ ≥ 1/2. No derivative, integral, supremum, ENNReal conversion, or square root is evaluated directly.

TorusEuler.Paper.tan_referenceAngle.text: The tangent of the defined reference angle is $\varepsilon\tau^2/2$ for all real parameters. This is the arctangent identity used to move between the paper's angle notation and the library coordinate $x$. It does not assert a sign for the angle; that requires the separate nonnegative-$\varepsilon$ hypothesis.
TorusEuler.Paper.tan_referenceAngle.summary: The tangent equals the quadratic reference coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_1_1.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_1_1. It asks for smooth odd divergence-free periodic initial data, a finite positive maximal time, a smooth Euler velocity with normalized pressure, bounded velocity, divergent gradient and vorticity integrals, diverging central vorticity, and off-origin limits of velocity and its time derivative. The extra universal conjunct states uniqueness of the maximal velocity and its lifespan for those initial data. Compared with TorusEuler.Theorem11, this includes the uniqueness clause. At the source level its spine arguments are 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, Text section8_setting. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_1_1.summary: A smooth Euler flow with finite time singularity

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_4_2.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_4_2. One pair C≥0,p∈ℕ works for every smooth periodic MeanParentFlow with H^#≤Id and every set of caps D≥1, L, K₀,K₁,Ω₀,Ω₁ bounding the inverse deformation, M, and the coefficients and first label derivatives. K and Ω are HalfHolder curves whose lifts equal the geometric formulas on the slab. With A=C(D+L+K₀+K₁+Ω₀+Ω₁)^p, every continuous source has an EndpointSystemSolution, the velocity estimate, and uniqueness of z,v,c,G on the interval. For every smooth periodic force and corresponding source primitive, every such solution yields smooth displacement, b(0)=c, and a smooth periodic zero-mean label pressure solving (4.11); the pushed-forward fields solve (4.12). Finally, at each time it gives a true linear equivalence for the compressed kinetic operator and bounds its inverse followed by Leray projection. The Lean L is a gradient cap; the paper’s source L is called src. At the source level its spine arguments are 4.1, A.1, A.2. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_4_2.summary: The endpoint problem selects a unique mean correction

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6. For a sufficiently large fixed envelope exponent, choose one exponent C, level constants K(n,p) and sum constants KP(m,P), all before the parent and depth. Under D^C λ^(−1/12)≤1, every expansion of depth P≥2 has the level estimates (5.34)–(5.36), including the separately written p=1 cases. K(n,p) does not depend on P. The same expansion has the bounds for W_osc and the summed means/sources in (5.37). Its remainder satisfies KP(m,P)λ^(−5/4)λ^(−2P/3), with no residual factor D^C on that right-hand side. The exponent C is independent of derivative order, level and depth. All orders are quantified, not just a depth-dependent finite range. At the source level its spine arguments are 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, D.1, B.1. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6.summary: All order frequency decay through every finite expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1.text:
This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1. Read the quantifiers in this order: choose any admissible radial cutoff ψ and any desired floor a₀; then choose b ≥ 1, an envelope exponent a ≥ a₀ and a majorant F; for every threshold B satisfying AdmissibleThreshold b F B there is N₁; for every N ≥ N₁ there are parameters P, a construction c and a time T. P is identified with b, B and λ₀=N, and its strength constant is exactly 18 exp 3. Both Theorem71Conclusions and Theorem71Steps are required. Thus B is chosen after the universal constants and before N. The quantifier ∀a₀,∃a≥a₀ allows arbitrarily large choices of a; it does not say every sufficiently large a works. The step record identifies actual velocities, pressure, oscillations and central amplitudes, but leaves the covector/first-wave identifications described in its annotation unstated. At the source level its spine arguments are 1.3, 2.2, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, 5.4, 5.8, 5.9, 5.10, 5.11, 6.1, B.1. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.

The increment conditions state estimates at each time without a separate time-norm continuity conjunct. Theorem71Steps also represents the oscillation through jointly smooth twisted profiles, so this observation concerns the explicit field list and does not deny the time regularity carried by those types.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1.summary: One approximate sequence for every derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_A_1.text: This spine theorem proves the proposition TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1. The constants C≥0 and p∈ℕ are chosen before all coefficient data. On [0,1], K is pointwise self-adjoint, Ω is skew-adjoint, both satisfy EndpointCoefficientC1Bound, K≥κId with κ>0, and the zero-mean L² path energy is bounded below by μ‖v‖² with μ>0. For every continuous HalfHolder source L, the proposition supplies an EndpointSystemSolution, uniqueness of z,v,c,G on [0,1], and ‖v‖₀≤CQ^p‖L‖₀ with Q=2+κ⁻¹+μ⁻¹+K₀+K₁+Ω₀+Ω₁. If the lifts of K,Ω,L are jointly smooth on the closed slab, it also asserts smoothness of z,c,G. The coefficient hypothesis asks for time continuity in C^{0,1/2} and bounded first spatial derivatives; it does not require time continuity in C^{1,1/2}. At the source level its spine arguments are A.2. This review inspected the source and supplied dependency inventory; it did not execute VerifySpine or a kernel check.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_A_1.summary: The endpoint inverse with uniqueness and a polynomial estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.zeta.text:
At normalized time τ, evaluate k and the preceding frame at the physical time t = t₀ + τ/r. The three returned Euclidean coordinates are ⟨E₁,k⟩/λ, S⟨E₂,k⟩/λ, and ⟨E₃,k⟩/λ. Thus k = λ(ζ₁E₁ + (ζ₂/S)E₂ + ζ₃E₃) wherever the frame is orthonormal and λ ≠ 0. WithLp.toLp 2 equips the coordinate triple with its Euclidean norm; the indices 0, 1, 2 mean ζ₁, ζ₂, ζ₃. This definition does not itself assert the reconstruction formula or ζ(0) = (0,0,1).

Default-value audit (b4): Unrestricted λ is a genuine hazard: at λ = 0 all three coordinates are 0, independently of k. NewWaveVector supplies λ > 0 whenever the coordinate is used in the numbered comparison statements. The inherited rate r = √(2σν) is positive because w has nonzero preceding vectors and ν > 0; S = σ/r is also positive. Frame normalization is justified on I, not at arbitrary t outside I. The hypotheses MapsTo w.clock [0,T] I and τ ∈ [0,T] place all theorem evaluations in that domain. No derivative or integral is taken here.
TorusEuler.Paper.zeta.summary: Scaled coordinates of the new wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.zetaRef.text:
The reference vector $\zeta_0=(\tan\varphi,-\varepsilon\tau,1)$ at normalized time $\tau$. Its third coordinate is exactly one, which later makes the amplitude elimination denominator safe when the actual vector stays close. This declaration defines the vector; convergence of model waves to it as $S\to\infty$ is a separate conclusion of Lemma 2.3.

Default-value audit (b4): Although Real.tan uses a totalized quotient, the arctangent branch keeps cos φ strictly positive, so there is no pole. The third coordinate 1 ensures ζ₀ is nonzero for every real ε and τ. The physical interpretation assumes ε > 0, but the vector formula itself is meaningful without it. No derivative, integral, real supremum, ENNReal.toReal, or square root is evaluated.

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.WaveOn.text: The Craik–Criminale equations for a wave vector $k$ and amplitude $\mathbf a$ over a prescribed gradient $D$ on `J`. The two conjuncts require their time derivatives within `J`, so endpoints use one-sided derivatives. The amplitude equation uses `affineWaveAmplitudeOperator`, which includes the pressure coefficient. Perpendicularity and nonvanishing are separate hypotheses; this definition does not include them.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.WaveOn.summary: Wave-vector and amplitude equations on an interval

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.additiveCompariso.text: The physical wave vector stays polynomially close to its reference, and all transverse amplitudes obey one common perturbed reference system. Absolute `N`, `p`, `C` are chosen before the physical data; `C₀ ≥ N` and the two smallness inequalities control the error. The theorem assumes the clock stays in `I`, positive initial frequency and the wave-vector equation. The existential continuous operator `R` precedes `∀ a`, so it is independent of the amplitude. Both supremum and pointwise bounds are included. The amplitude coordinates are $(U,V)=(-\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.additiveCompariso.summary: One additive error for every transverse amplitude

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.exactWave.text: The affine wave solves Euler and preserves nonzero transverse initial data on the same interval. `hJ` makes `J` an interval; `hDiff` permits unique time derivatives there. The hypotheses `hD`, `hS`, `htr` and `hWave` give the background derivative, symmetry, zero trace and wave equations. Only differentiability of $F$ and $P'=F$ are required. Oddness, periodicity and $F'(0)=1$ are unnecessary for this result. Persistence holds at every time in `J`, before or after the initial time.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.exactWave.summary: Exact Euler wave and persistence of transverse data

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.finiteComparison.text: The bundle `w : PhysicalAmplification I t₀` supplies a compact physical set, continuous base and error strains, trace-free base strain, and a nonzero transverse parent wave with positive initial couplings. One universal `N` is chosen before `w`; `N ≤ C₀`, `2 ≤ T`, the two smallness inequalities, clock inclusion, positive wave scale, growing initial data, and the new `WaveOn` equations are explicit inputs. The reference initial value problem is supplied by `referenceModel`. The conclusion gives logarithmic amplitude and coupling control, plus an invertible transverse propagator with coefficient $252eS$. Physical paths are evaluated at `w.clock τ`.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.finiteComparison.summary: Amplitude and coupling comparison on the prescribed interval

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.finiteReturn.text: Under the finite-window assumptions, `0 < next`, `next ≤ w.ratio / 32`, and `crossingHorizon w.ratio next ≤ T`, the growing wave has a crossing strictly between $\tau_m$ and $2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}$. `peak` is the actual maximum of its norm on the full interval $[0,T]$. Every crossing in the closed bracket satisfies the two strength bounds with $C=18e^3$. The final clause gives the early-gain estimate for every $0\le\tau\le1$. No uniqueness of the crossing is asserted.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.finiteReturn.summary: Crossing, strength, and gain of the growing wave

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.finiteWindowNorma.text: For a valid amplification window, positive carrier, sufficiently large C₀, both smallness conditions, prescribed growing-wave initial data, wave equations and Riccati hypotheses, this theorem adds transverse transport to normalizedComparison. For $u\in[0,T]$ and $v\in[u,T]$, it produces a continuous linear equivalence between the corresponding perpendicular planes, with norm at most $252eS\|A(v)\|/\|A(u)\|$. The action agrees with every transverse amplitude solution. It also retains the logarithmic and coupling bounds.

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.movingFrameDeriva.text: The preceding wave determines an orthonormal frame whose three derivatives satisfy the equations of Lemma 2.2, and whose strength satisfies $(\log\sigma)'=B_{33}$. `htr` gives zero trace, `hWave` gives the two wave equations, and `hData` gives nonzero transverse vectors throughout `J`. No smoothness assumption on $B$ or symmetry of $B'+B^2$ occurs. `HasDerivWithinAt` includes the appropriate derivatives at interval endpoints.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.movingFrameDeriva.summary: Moving frame equations and logarithmic strength

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.referenceModel.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, the Riccati initial value problem has a global forward solution, a deviation $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$, and exactly one zero $\tau_m$. The hypotheses are `hε : 0 < ε` and `hε₁ : ε ≤ 1`. The conclusion includes $|Y|\le1$, $2\le\varepsilon\tau_m\le3$, both strict sign conditions, and the gain integral. `Ici 0` means the forward ray; its endpoint derivative is taken from within that ray.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.referenceModel.summary: Global reference solution, turning time, and gain

TorusEuler.PaperFirstWaveConclusion.text: The conclusion of Lemma 6.1 for a given normalized first wave `w`. Its fields require weighted propagation for every transverse amplitude solution and every $D\ge2$, a lower bound $D^{-1}$ for the first coupling, and initial strength between $\lambda^{1/4}/2$ and $\lambda^{1/4}$. This proposition defines the claims; `paperLemma61_firstWave` supplies a proof under the lemma’s hypotheses.
TorusEuler.PaperFirstWaveConclusion.summary: The two origin bounds and initial strength

TorusEuler.PaperLimitAgreement.text: The smooth Euler limit of a compatible stage sequence, with initial convergence in every $C^{m,1/2}$ norm and uniform convergence on each preterminal interval. The structure also records continuous velocity up to $T$ and uniform convergence on the closed slab. Its `maximal_agreement` field compares every maximal solution with a finite real lifespan and the same initial velocity. That conditional comparison is a conclusion to be supplied, not existence of a general maximal continuation on an entire possibly infinite lifespan.
TorusEuler.PaperLimitAgreement.summary: Smooth Euler limit and agreement with maximal solutions

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.text:
A continuous curve of solenoidal spatial half-Hölder velocities, a time-independent solenoidal constant, a zero terminal primitive, and the projected momentum equation. The fields `continuous`, `terminal`, and `projected` are requirements of this structure. The displacement is obtained by integrating `velocity`, so its initial value is zero. Constructing an inhabitant requires an inverse theorem; the structure itself neither supplies that inhabitant nor constructs the pressure gradient.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a solution predicate with endpoint, smoothness and projected-equation obligations. Naming a value of this type does not bypass constructing those proofs.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.summary: Integrated endpoint velocity and solenoidal constant

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.c.text: When the kinetic coefficient starts at the identity and the source starts at zero, the solenoidal constant equals the initial label velocity. These hypotheses are the binders `hK` and `hsrc`; `hT` ensures that zero belongs to the closed interval. Evaluating the integrated equation at zero removes both time primitives. The Leray projection then fixes the already solenoidal velocity. Identifying it with physical $b(0)$ also uses the flow’s initial identity.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.c.summary: The solenoidal constant is the initial correction

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.e.text: A solenoidal displacement satisfying the original pressure equation gives a solution of the projected endpoint problem. The binders `hz`, `h0` and `hEnd` require $z_t=v$ and the two zero traces. The binder `hφ` gives a periodic potential with the represented gradient, and `hEq` is the unprojected momentum identity. The conclusion preserves the supplied velocity and constant and identifies the primitive with $z$, so uniqueness for the projected problem applies to this original formulation.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.e.summary: A pressure solution gives an integrated solution

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.e.text: An integrated projected solution has a periodic scalar potential whose gradient is continuous in the spatial half-Hölder norm. The assumptions `hK`, `hΩ`, and `hsrc` give time continuity of the coefficient and forcing curves. The potential is chosen with zero spatial mean, and its gradient completes the unprojected momentum equation. The statement asserts continuity of the gradient curve, not a separately normalized time regularity theorem for the scalar potential.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.e.summary: Recovering a continuous periodic pressure gradient

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.o.text: Packages a continuous solenoidal velocity and constant as an integrated solution when the terminal primitive vanishes and the original equation holds with a periodic continuously differentiable potential. The represented gradient `Gφ` is annihilated by the spatial projection. Thus the original pressure formulation supplies the exact projected field required by the inverse’s uniqueness theorem.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.o.summary: A periodic pressure solution satisfies the projected equation

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.p.text: Two integrated pressure equations have the same gradient once their velocities and solenoidal constants agree. The binders `hv` and `hc` supply those equalities, and `hφ`, `hψ` supply the two momentum identities. Equality of velocities on the closed slab also gives equality of their vorticity primitives. Subtracting the two momentum identities then gives `EqOn Gφ Gψ`. This theorem completes gradient uniqueness; it does not by itself prove uniqueness of the velocity.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.p.summary: Uniqueness of the integrated pressure gradient

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.text:
The smooth deformation $F$, its inverse $G$, the parent gradient $M$ and its time derivative $M_t$, with the assumptions used by the endpoint inverse. The fields `deformation_ode` and `gradient_derivative` encode $F_t=MF$ and the fixed-label derivative of $M$. The fields `inverse_bound`, `gradient_bound` and `hessian_upper` impose the controls $D$, $L$ and $H^\#\le I$. These are assumptions in this structure; `exists_paperMeanParent_of_flow` constructs them from a supplied parent flow and its bounds.

Default-value audit (b5): The record ties deformation, inverse deformation and strain to a genuine parent flow and includes analytic bounds. Its existence must be built from the parent hypotheses.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.summary: Physical assumptions for the endpoint inverse

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.exists_coeffi.text: For a physical parent with $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$, and $L\ge0$, constructs the Hölder and path-space representations of its kinetic and vorticity coefficients. The parent provides inverse deformation, derivative identities, and the Hessian upper bound. Spatial ellipticity comes from the inverse-deformation bound; mixed coercivity comes from the displacement energy with both endpoint traces.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.exists_coeffi.summary: Build both coefficient representations from the parent

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.exists_integr.text: A smooth periodic force in label coordinates has an integrated source represented by a smooth curve in the spatial half-Hölder space. The binders `hf` and `hp` impose joint smoothness and spatial periodicity. The conclusion identifies the lifted source exactly with the negative primitive of $F^*\mathrm{force}$. This supplies the regularity and the source identity used when a smooth physical mean solution is compared with the integrated endpoint inverse.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.exists_integr.summary: A smooth force defines a smooth Hölder source

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.kinetic.text:
The kinetic coefficient in physical label coordinates.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.kinetic.summary: The kinetic coefficient of the physical parent

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.vorticity.text:
The vorticity coefficient in physical label coordinates.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.vorticity.summary: The vorticity coefficient of the physical parent

TorusEuler.PaperMeanPhysicalCoefficients.text: Packages Hölder time curves for the kinetic and vorticity coefficients, their mixed path operators, and exact evaluation and almost-everywhere action identities. It also records spatial and zero-time-mean coercivity with the physical constants determined by `D` and `L`. These fields are obligations on the record: the structure is not itself an existence theorem, and all regularity claims are restricted to the closed slab.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanPhysicalCoefficients.summary: Represent the kinetic and vorticity coefficients

TorusEuler.PaperPhysicalStepBudget.text: Packages the inequalities needed to use the same step coefficient `Γ` and exponent in the oscillation, residual, central-gradient, pressure and flow estimates. It requires `Γ ≥ 1` and several explicit bounds built from the supplied costs and depth. This is a proposition of numerical compatibility, not a choice of `Γ`; the later existence theorem proves such a budget from its parameter hypotheses.
TorusEuler.PaperPhysicalStepBudget.summary: One numerical budget for all physical estimates

TorusEuler.PaperPhysicalStepBudget.hiera.text: The small-step inequality also supplies the smallness needed by the hierarchy recurrence. Given `h : PaperPhysicalStepBudget ...`, `hD : 1 ≤ D`, `hf : 1 ≤ freq` and `hs`, Lean proves $(\mathsf D^r)^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. The fields `hierarchyPower` and `gamma_ge_one` ensure that the common step constant dominates the recurrence loss; no additional frequency choice is made here.
TorusEuler.PaperPhysicalStepBudget.hiera.summary: Step smallness implies the hierarchy smallness

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.text:
The smooth fields $v,z,B,q$ for the forced mean equation in label coordinates. The fields `initial` and `terminal` impose $z(0)=z(T)=0$, `displacement_derivative` gives $z_t=v$, and `mean_eq` gives $B=Fv$. The stored `momentum` equation is $B_t+MB+G^*\nabla_aq=\mathrm{force}$, with $G=F^{-1}$. Divergence is recorded for $v$; the physical divergence of $B$ uses the volume-preserving flow and Piola identity. These conditions define a solution; the smooth-force inverse supplies existence.

The physical trajectory displacement is $\xi=Fz$, whereas the stored displacement is the label field $z$.

Default-value audit (b5): The record includes joint smoothness, endpoints, periodicity and momentum. It is a solution specification; the existence theorem supplies a value and pressure normalization is tracked separately.
TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.summary: Smooth forced mean correction with zero endpoint displacement

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.euler.text: The pullbacks $b=B\circ X^{-1}$ and $q=\mathsf q\circ X^{-1}$ are smooth periodic fields satisfying the linearized momentum equation and $\operatorname{div}b=0$. The binders `hF` and `hM` identify the abstract parent coefficients with the actual flow derivative and Eulerian gradient. The binder `hdiv` supplies volume preservation through the divergence-free parent. Lean writes the material derivative as the joint derivative in direction `(1, U t x)`. The right side is the label force evaluated at the inverse flow.

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.exist.text: A smooth mean solution gives a solution of the same integrated half-Hölder problem, with the same label velocity. The binder `k` supplies the physical coefficient representations; `src`, `hsrc` and `hSource` identify the smooth integrated force. The proof differentiates the integrated momentum, projects away the pressure gradient, and shows that the projected quantity is constant in time. The displacement traces supply the zero total velocity integral, so the resulting velocity belongs to the endpoint problem.
TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.exist.summary: A smooth mean solves the integrated endpoint problem

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.mean_.text: Two smooth mean solutions for the same parent and force have the same mean field on the entire closed slab. The binders `hT`, `hT₁`, `hD` and `hL` require $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$ and a nonnegative gradient bound. The force is smooth and periodic by `hforce` and `hper`. Both solutions already carry the two zero displacement traces. They are converted to integrated solutions and compared by uniqueness of the endpoint inverse; the initial correction is therefore determined as well.
TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.mean_.summary: The endpoint conditions determine the mean velocity

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.stron.text: Every smooth mean solution satisfies $Kv_t+\nabla_aq=F^*\mathrm{force}-2F^*MFv$. The binder `s : PaperSmoothMeanSolution p force` contains the smooth solution and its momentum equation; `hT` and `ht` give a positive slab and the evaluation time. The expression $2F^*MF$ is the paper’s $\mathcal D$, since $F_t=MF$. The derivative of $v$ is taken within the closed slab, including its endpoints.
TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.stron.summary: The strong momentum equation in label coordinates

TorusEuler.PaperTerminalOffOrigin.text: The velocity and its time derivative both have terminal spatial limits on every compact subset away from the singular point. The definition pairs `HasOffOriginLimits T u` with the same condition for `timeDerivative T u`. The latter is a derivative within $[0,T)$, so it includes the right derivative at zero. This records Proposition 8.4 and does not assert a smooth time extension through $T$.
TorusEuler.PaperTerminalOffOrigin.summary: Both spatial traces converge away from the origin

TorusEuler.PaperTerminalTime.text: The terminal-time conclusion combines maximality of the Euler velocity with divergence of the curl and gradient integrals. Both integrals are nonnegative extended integrals on $[0,T)$, and `⊤` denotes infinity. This is a definition of the desired conclusion, not a continuation theorem. In the common Section 8 theorem, the same $T$ is also identified as the limit of the activation times.
TorusEuler.PaperTerminalTime.summary: Maximal lifespan and the two divergent integrals

TorusEuler.PaperTerminalVelocityCurl.text: The pair of terminal properties in Proposition 8.2: a uniform finite bound for the velocity and a full limit of the central curl norm to infinity. The filter `𝓝[Ico 0 T] T` means approach to $T$ through $[0,T)$. This definition records the claimed properties; their proof is supplied by the common Section 8 theorem. It does not merely ask for an unbounded subsequence of times.
TorusEuler.PaperTerminalVelocityCurl.summary: Bounded velocity and terminal central vorticity blow-up

TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions.text: The proposition containing the conclusions of Theorem 7.1 for a construction `c` and time `T`. Its fields state regularity, frequency and size bounds, pressure control, the central splitting, crossing values, lifetime, and oscillation and correction estimates. This structure defines the proposition rather than proving existence. The theorem `paperTheorem71` constructs a value satisfying it. The paper’s positive wave index is `j + 1` in several fields. Its increment fields state uniform spatial bounds; continuity in time is separate.
TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions.summary: The quantitative conclusions for the common sequence

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.text:
A time cutoff on the closed interval $[0,T]$, with values between zero and one and vanishing at times strictly before `t₀`. Its named fields `smooth`, `range`, and `zero_before` record these requirements for the function `value`. Smoothness is imposed on the closed slab, not on the entire real line. The type admits arbitrary such cutoffs, including the constant-one first-wave cutoff when activation is zero.

Default-value audit (b5): This record contains the smooth cutoff and its support/plateau conditions. It is not an arbitrary function masquerading as a cutoff; a concrete construction supplies the record in the paper proof.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.summary: Smooth bounded cutoff before wave activation

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.abs_le_one.text: At every time in the slab, the absolute value of a `PaperWaveCutoff` is at most one. Its bundled range already gives both nonnegativity and an upper bound by one, so this theorem is a convenient consequence. It does not prove that the cutoff ever reaches one or has a nonzero derivative.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.abs_le_one.summary: The cutoff has absolute value at most one

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative.text: Defines the cutoff derivative using `derivWithin` on $[0,T]$. This is the time domain on which the cutoff has bundled smoothness. It therefore includes a consistent endpoint derivative when $T>0$, rather than requiring any arbitrary continuation outside the slab to be differentiable.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative.summary: The activation derivative on the closed slab

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivativeSiz.text: The supremum of $|\widetilde\chi'(t)|\gamma(t)$ over the closed activation interval $[t_0,T]$. The cutoff is `χ : PaperWaveCutoff t₀ T`, and the weight `γ` is supplied separately. The subtype `t : Icc t₀ T` restricts the supremum to that interval. Continuity and nonnegativity assumptions are added in `derivativeSize_bounds`, which proves that this quantity dominates each pointwise value.

For $T>0$ and $0\le t_0\le T$, a continuous nonnegative weight `γ` makes `derivativeSize γ` nonnegative and bounds every $|\chi^{\prime}(t)|\gamma(t)$ on the active interval. Compactness supplies boundedness and the interval is nonempty. These conditions make the real supremum a genuine maximum-type bound instead of relying on a default value.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivativeSiz.summary: The activation supremum bounds every weighted derivative

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative_fi.text: The within-time derivative of the first-wave cutoff is identically zero for every real `T` and evaluation time. That cutoff is the constant function one, so the total derivative convention gives zero even for a degenerate slab. This is the scalar reason that the first wave has no activation residual.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative_fi.summary: The first wave has no activation derivative

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative_sm.text: For $T>0$, the cutoff’s within-time derivative is infinitely smooth on $[0,T]$. Smoothness of the cutoff is bundled, and the nondegenerate interval supplies unique differentiation. The conclusion is restricted to the closed slab; it does not assert that the chosen total derivative function is smooth across its exterior endpoints.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative_sm.summary: Smoothness of the within-time cutoff derivative

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative_ze.text: For a nondegenerate slab and a time strictly earlier than `t₀`, the cutoff’s selected within derivative is zero. The proof combines local vanishing of the cutoff with uniqueness of derivatives on $[0,T]$. It does not assert that the derivative vanishes during the activation transition or at arbitrary exterior times.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative_ze.summary: The cutoff derivative vanishes before activation

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.first.text: The first-wave cutoff is the constant function one, packaged as a `PaperWaveCutoff 0 T`. The parameter `T` is unrestricted in the definition. The condition of vanishing before activation is vacuous on $[0,T]$, since activation occurs at zero. Consequently its time derivative contributes no switching source. This is distinct from later cutoffs that are flat at a positive activation time.

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.hasDerivWithi.text: At a time belonging to the slab, the cutoff has within derivative equal to its defined `derivative`. Smoothness provides differentiability, and the total derivative operator selects a valid derivative. This statement does not require a separate positive-duration binder because it asserts derivative existence, not uniqueness or an ambient extension.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.hasDerivWithi.summary: The cutoff derivative is its actual within derivative

TorusEuler.ParentLabelJetBound.text:
A bound on every label derivative with one fixed slope in the exponent: $|D_a^mf|\le C_m\mathsf D^{pm+c}$. The time interval, scale, coefficient function, order constants and exponents are all arguments of the predicate. Lean measures the operator norm of the iterated Fréchet derivative. Coordinate derivative sums differ only by order-dependent constants, which the paper allows in $C_m$.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a predicate on the supplied objects. It makes the recorded equalities or bounds assumptions; it does not construct objects satisfying them. The relevant existence and regularity hypotheses are carried by its callers.

TorusEuler.ParentLabelJetBound.weighted_.text: If $|D_a^jf|\le C_j\mathsf D^{pj+c}$ and $\ell_*\mathsf D^p\le1$, summing the radius-weighted suprema leaves only $\mathsf D^c$. The binders `hf` and `hscale` are these two assumptions; `hC`, `hD` and `hℓ` give nonnegativity and $\mathsf D\ge1$. The remaining finite sum of order constants is absorbed into the paper's $C_n$.
TorusEuler.ParentLabelJetBound.weighted_.summary: Weighting removes the derivative dependent power

TorusEuler.PeriodicComplexL2.text: This is the $L^2$ space of complex Euclidean three-vectors with respect to normalized torus Haar measure. Elements are almost-everywhere equivalence classes. The Euclidean coefficient norm is used so that orthogonal Fourier-mode projections produce a contractive Hilbert-space Leray operator.
TorusEuler.PeriodicComplexL2.summary: Square integrable complex vector fields on the torus

TorusEuler.PeriodicVelocityJetSpace.text: The space is the closure of the range of actual smooth periodic jet tuples inside the finite product of bounded continuous functions. Taking the closure yields a Banach space while preserving approximation by compatible tuples. It is a restricted subspace, not the full space of arbitrary bounded derivatives.
TorusEuler.PeriodicVelocityJetSpace.summary: Compatible periodic jets form a complete space

TorusEuler.PhaseJetBound.text:
A uniform bound for all Fréchet derivative norms up to the indicated order.

Default-value audit (b5): This predicate bounds iteratedFDeriv but does not include ContDiff. Even with the zeroth bound, higher derivatives may take default values outside their classical domain; every use as a smooth jet estimate must also establish regularity.
TorusEuler.PhaseJetBound.summary: Uniform bounds through a finite Fréchet derivative order

TorusEuler.PhaseJetBound.mono_order.text: A uniform `PhaseJetBound` through order `n` immediately supplies the same constant through any order `m≤n`. This is restriction of a family of derivative bounds; it introduces no new regularity or scaling estimate. It is used when successive directional differentiations consume the available derivative order.
TorusEuler.PhaseJetBound.mono_order.summary: A derivative bound remains valid at lower order

TorusEuler.PhysicalWaveApproximationBoun.text: Records full-depth velocity size, residual decay at the next frequency, oscillation size, mean bounds through the scheduled order, and an upper quadratic-form bound for the pressure-Hessian increment. The last field compares the approximate pressure to the parent pressure; it is not a two-sided Hessian norm estimate. These are hypotheses used to close the numerical induction after truncation.
TorusEuler.PhysicalWaveApproximationBoun.summary: Eulerian estimates required before the Fourier cutoff

TorusEuler.PhysicalWaveApproximationBoun.text: Packages separately supplied full-depth velocity, residual, oscillation, mean, and pressure-Hessian estimates into `PhysicalWaveApproximationBounds`. Frequency recurrence identifies the indexed induction scales, and the slice-potential identity transfers the pressure estimate to the cutoff representation. The theorem does not derive these five analytic bounds; it ensures they describe the same actual approximation.
TorusEuler.PhysicalWaveApproximationBoun.summary: Collect the measured estimates for the actual approximation

TorusEuler.Pressure.text:
A pressure field is a total real function of time and spatial position. It has the type ℝ → Vec3 → ℝ. This is the scalar potential p in the Euler equation; its gradient, not its value, enters momentum. The mean-zero gauge and spatial periodicity are requirements of IsEulerSolution, not of this abbreviation.

Default-value audit (b4): No derivative or integral occurs in the abbreviation. An arbitrary pressure function need not be differentiable or integrable. The later solution structure supplies the regularity that makes its gradient and mean meaningful.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a completely unrestricted scalar function type. Smoothness, periodicity, the PDE and mean-zero normalization are separate obligations.

TorusEuler.RealNormedTorusFourierBand.text:
Fourier support of a real normed-space-valued field, measured by its continuous dual. This definition also applies when the target space is incomplete.

Default-value audit (b5): The input is already a continuous torus field. Testing all continuous real linear functionals gives the band condition without assuming a complete target space; it is a support predicate, not an estimate.
TorusEuler.RealNormedTorusFourierBand.summary: A Fourier band defined through the continuous dual

TorusEuler.RealNormedTorusFourierBand.co.text: A continuous function into any real normed space has an infinitely smooth Euclidean lift when `RealNormedTorusFourierBand R g` holds. The proof uses its finite expansion in scalar Fourier functions with fixed vector coefficients. Smoothness is obtained from band limitation, without imposing a Banach-space completion or additional derivative assumptions.

TorusEuler.RealTorusFourierBand.text:
A continuous torus field whose Fourier coefficients vanish beyond a prescribed radius. The parameter `D` is the radius, and the condition quantifies over every integer frequency `k` with $D<|k|$. Lean first complexifies the real vector field. The strict inequality retains coefficients on the boundary of the band, as the paper does.

Default-value audit (b5): The input is a continuous torus field. The radius is arbitrary in the raw predicate, and a negative radius can force all Fourier coefficients to vanish; uses impose a positive spectral scale.

TorusEuler.RealTorusFourierBand.add.text: Two continuous real vector fields supported in the same Euclidean frequency band have their sum in that band. Complexification and Fourier coefficients both preserve addition. The radius `r` is unrestricted; the conclusion follows from the supplied support predicates even when the band would be degenerate.

TorusEuler.RealTorusFourierBand.endpoint.text: Applying the concrete spatial Leray projection to a half Hölder field does not enlarge its Fourier band. The hypothesis `hf` bounds the support of the continuous representative. At every excluded frequency the projection acts by a linear multiplier on a zero coefficient, so the output coefficient remains zero.
TorusEuler.RealTorusFourierBand.endpoint.summary: Projection preserves the parent Fourier band

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.exists_pos.text: For a positive continuous amplitude on a nonempty compact interval $[0,T]$ and a prescribed positive height `Ustar`, there exist a maximizing time and a positive scalar that makes its maximum exactly that height. The scalar is `Ustar / A a`, whose denominator is positive. The conclusion is existence, without uniqueness or a selected peak time.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.exists_pos.summary: Scaling a positive amplitude to a prescribed maximum

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.exists_pos.text: Assume the norm of a vector-valued path has an attained greatest value `peak>0` on `J`, and the target `Ustar` is positive. The theorem supplies a positive scalar $c$ with $c\,\mathrm{peak}=U_*$ and proves that the scaled path attains exactly that maximum. It does not assume compactness or continuity; attainment is already in `hpeak`.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.exists_pos.summary: A positive constant sets the prescribed amplitude peak

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.exp_integr.text: The polynomial smallness budget bounds the arbitrary-start exponential amplification factor uniformly on the normalized slab.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.exp_integr.summary: The normalized growth error has a uniform exponential bound

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.growingFac.text: If a continuous rate is nonnegative before $p$ and nonpositive after $p$ in $[0,T]$, its exponential integral attains a maximum at $p$. The hypotheses constrain only the open intervals on either side, and `hp` places the candidate in the closed interval. The conclusion does not assert that the maximizer or the zero of the rate is unique.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.growingFac.summary: A sign change of the rate gives an amplitude maximum

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.growing_am.text: Assuming the global reference Riccati solution, nonvanishing continuous physical amplitude, its logarithmic comparison, late wave-coordinate bounds and continuous ratio comparison, the theorem supplies the reference turning time, an attained physical peak, and a crossing after that turn. Every crossing in the specified bracket has normalized strength $\|a(\tau)\|\,\|k(\tau)\|/(\mathrm{scale}\cdot\mathrm{peak})$ between explicit multiples $e^{-1}/4$ and $18e^3$ of $(\varepsilon\,\mathrm{next})^{-1/2}$. It also gives the early gain bound. The assumptions include $2\varepsilon\le1$ and $0<\mathrm{next}\le\varepsilon/32$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.growing_am.summary: A late crossing has controlled strength and early gain

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.growing_bu.text: A sufficiently large fixed coefficient and exponent in the finite-smallness hypothesis absorb both the normalized matrix-error contribution and the geometric norm correction. The result gives their explicit sum at most epsilon.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.growing_bu.summary: The logarithmic amplitude budget fits finite smallness

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.hasDerivWi.text: Under the Riccati equation, the kernel satisfies $K'=-(2Y+damping)K$ within $[0,T]$. Differentiating its clock factor and diagonal decay makes the coefficients combine in this form. Initial-value and positivity assumptions are unnecessary for this identity; they are introduced later to obtain the kernel's uniform bounds.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.hasDerivWi.summary: The differential equation for the selected kernel

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.hasDerivWi.text: For a Riccati path on $[0,T]$, the within-interval derivative of the selected kernel integral is the kernel itself. Continuity of the kernel comes from its differential equation, allowing the fundamental theorem of calculus. The statement includes both interval endpoints and does not yet assert bounds for the integral.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.hasDerivWi.summary: The accumulated kernel differentiates back to the kernel

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.hasDerivWi.text: If $g,h$ are positive on a set $J$, $F$ is nonnegative there, and $\phi\ge0$, then the logarithmic derivative of the packaged amplitude is $g'/g+h'/h+\phi F'/[2(1+\phi F)]$. The supplied derivative hypotheses are within $J$ at `t`, and `ht` puts that point in the positivity domain. No wave or Riccati equation is assumed.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.hasDerivWi.summary: Separating the three contributions to the logarithmic rate

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.hasDerivWi.text: With positive $\varepsilon$, $Y(0)=1$, and the Riccati equation, the logarithm of the selected second amplitude has derivative $Y-K/(1-I)$. Here $K$ is the kernel and $I$ its integral. The denominator is at least one half under these assumptions. This correction distinguishes the alternate seed's rate from the paper's canonical reference rate $Y$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.hasDerivWi.summary: The logarithmic rate of the alternate seed

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.integrated.text: For $0\le a\le t\le T$, $T\ge2$, $0\le\varepsilon\le1$, nonnegative uniform raw error `η`, and continuous $|Y|\le1$, the weighted perturbation integral lies between zero and $4T^3\eta$. Its integrand is nonnegative, so removing the initial interval $[0,a]$ cannot increase the budget already proved from time zero.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.integrated.summary: The same error budget bounds every forward subinterval

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.integrated.text: The comparison integral satisfies $0\le D\le4T^3\eta$ for a constant nonnegative raw error bound `η`. The hypotheses `hε`, `hε₁`, `hT`, `ht`, and `hη` restrict the parameter, window, observation time, and error size. `hYc` gives continuity and `hYb` gives $|Y|\le1$. The proof bounds $(1+|Y|)^2/s$ by $4T^2$ and integrates over at most $T$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.integrated.summary: The integrated amplitude error has polynomial size

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernel.text: This kernel is $s(t)$ times the decaying diagonal coefficient of the normalized triangular system based at zero. It builds the solution with raw initial amplitudes $(U,V)=(0,1)$ when $Y(0)=1$. That seed differs from the paper's growing data $(1,1)$. The definition alone imposes no differential equation on $Y$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernel.summary: The decaying kernel for the transverse initial seed

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernelInte.text: This is the triangular transfer coefficient from zero to $t$, integrating the kernel that contributes to the selected transverse seed. The factor $1-kernelIntegral$ will determine its normalized second amplitude. The definition accepts every real function $Y$ and time; the bound between zero and one half is a later theorem with Riccati hypotheses.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernelInte.summary: Accumulated transfer for the transverse initial seed

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernelInte.text: The selected kernel integral vanishes at zero because the integration interval has zero length. This holds with no assumptions on $Y$ or $\varepsilon$. It makes the selected second amplitude equal to one initially, and contributes to the cancellation giving the selected first amplitude zero when $Y(0)=1$.

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernel_bou.text: For $\varepsilon>0$ and a Riccati path with $Y(0)=1$, the kernel lies in $(0,1]$ and its integral in $[0,1/2]$ throughout $[0,T]$. The deviation is nonnegative, so the normalized diagonal coefficient decays and its transfer consumes at most half the loss. These bounds provide the positive margin in the alternate seed.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernel_bou.summary: Bounds for the kernel and its accumulated transfer

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernel_eq_.text: Given the Riccati equation on $[0,T]$, the selected kernel equals $\exp(-\int_0^t(2Y+damping))$. The proof shows that both expressions solve the same scalar linear equation and equal one initially, then invokes uniqueness. This equality does not use $Y(0)=1$ or positive $\varepsilon$; those hypotheses are needed for subsequent comparison bounds.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernel_eq_.summary: An exponential formula for the selected kernel

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.kernel_zer.text: At time zero the clock factor and the diagonal propagator coefficient are both one, so the selected kernel equals one. This algebraic identity holds for any function $Y$ and any real $\varepsilon$. It is part of fixing the alternate seed and does not require an existence theorem for the reference rate.

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.log_amplit.text: Assume $h\ge m>0$, $h_0\ge1/2$, closeness of $h$ to $h_0$ and of the supplied numbers $h'$ to $h_0'$, and a nonnegative geometric correction. Then the rate discrepancy is bounded by $(\delta'+2|h_0'|\delta)/m+\phi|F'|/2$. This is an algebraic inequality between numbers; derivatives are identified separately in applications.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.log_amplit.summary: Controlling the error of the logarithmic rate

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.log_amplit.text: For $g>0$, $h,h_0\ge m>0$, and a nonnegative correction $\phi F$, the logarithmic ratio of $gh\sqrt{1+\phi F}$ to $gh_0$ is bounded by $\delta/m+\phi F/2$ when $|h-h_0|\le\delta$. The common growing factor cancels. This is a pointwise scalar inequality; the physical application must supply the component and geometric bounds.

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.log_growin.text: The logarithmic amplitude error is bounded by $2\delta+20T^4S^{-2}$. The hypotheses provide an orthonormal frame, transverse data, positive shear, the coordinate bounds `hX`, `hQ`, `hZ`, and `hY`, and normalized proximity `hclose` with `hδ : δ ≤ 1 / 2`. The two terms come respectively from the error in $h$ and the positive geometric correction in the physical norm.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.log_growin.summary: Normalized proximity controls the physical logarithmic error

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.log_growin.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$ and $T\ge2$, the growing seed $U(0)=V(0)=1$, Riccati equation on $[0,T]$, and supplied bound `hYb` of $|Y|\le1$ give the logarithmic amplitude estimate when the continuous raw-matrix error is at most $CT^p\delta$. The explicit nonnegative budget is $64CT^{p+3}\delta+40T^4\delta\le\varepsilon$. The geometry requires nonzero `scale`, $S\ge1$, $S^{-1}\le2\delta$, orthonormality and transversality at `t`, $|X|\le T^2$, $|Q|\le T$, and $Z\ge1/2$. The conclusion compares the physical norm with the growing reference factor.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.log_growin.summary: A controlled matrix error bounds the physical amplitude

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normCorrec.text:
The nonnegative correction from the first and third moving-frame components.

Default-value audit (b5): The ratios U/V and (X(U/V)−Q)/Z are totalized at zero denominators. The comparison arguments supply bounds excluding V=0 and Z=0 before interpreting this as the physical norm correction.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normCorrec.summary: The norm correction from the other frame components

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normCorrec.text: The correction $w^2+((Xw-Q)/Z)^2$ is at most $40T^4$ when $T\ge1$, $|X|\le T^2$, $|Q|\le T$, $Z\ge1/2$, and $|w|\le2$. These are the explicit hypotheses `hT`, `hX`, `hQ`, `hZ`, and `hw`, with $w=U/V$. Multiplication by the squared inverse shear $S^{-2}$ gives the manuscript's bound on $\rho$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normCorrec.summary: The geometric norm correction grows polynomially

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normCorrec.text: The correction to the principal amplitude component is nonnegative for all real coordinate values. The result is algebraic and does not require a solution of the amplitude equation.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normCorrec.summary: The additional squared-length term is nonnegative

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normalized.text: The selected pair has normalized coordinates $(1-I,-B)$, where $I$ is its kernel integral and $B$ the decaying diagonal coefficient. This is an algebraic identity for arbitrary $Y$, $\varepsilon$, and time because the growth factor and $s$ never vanish. At zero the state is $(1,-1)$, rather than the growing reference state $(1,0)$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normalized.summary: The alternate seed in normalized coordinates

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normalized.text: For $U(0)=V(0)=1$, the actual normalized state lies within $4e^{2D}D$ of $(1,0)$, where $D=\int_0^t(1+|Y|)^2\eta/s$. The reference Riccati path, raw perturbed equations, and continuous error majorant are assumed. With $U=-\alpha_1$, these are exactly the paper's growing initial data. Polynomial smallness of the final error is supplied later.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normalized.summary: Comparing the growing seed with the constant normalized state

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normalized.text: For raw initial data $U(0)=0$, $V(0)=1$, this bounds normalized distance from the selected seed by $4e^{2D}D$, with $D=\int_0^t(1+|Y|)^2\eta/s$. The assumptions include the reference Riccati path, both perturbed raw equations, and a continuous pointwise matrix-error bound. The initial difference vanishes because both paths use the alternate seed.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normalized.summary: Comparing the perturbed transverse seed with its reference

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normalized.text: Under the perturbed raw equations, the first normalized coordinate has derivative $d=sl+(R_1z)_1$, where $R_1$ is the normalized matrix error. Closeness to the selected state gives $|d+K|\le\delta+\|R_1\|\|z\|$. The term $-K$ is the alternate seed's transverse derivative, rather than the zero derivative of the growing reference state.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.normalized.summary: Comparing the transverse derivative with the alternate seed

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.orthonorma.text: In an orthonormal frame with the stated three components, $|\mathbf a|=V\sqrt{1+S^{-2}\{(U/V)^2+((XU/V-Q)/Z)^2\}}$. The arguments `B` and `a` specify the frame and vector. `hV`, `hZ`, and `hS` allow the divisions, while `h₀`, `h₁`, and `h₂` give its coordinates. The result is a Euclidean norm identity and does not assume an amplitude differential equation.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.orthonorma.summary: The physical amplitude norm includes a transverse correction

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.peak_log_g.text: If a positive amplitude stays within logarithmic error $\delta$ of `selectedV`, its maximum logarithmic gain differs from the maximum of the growing factor by a value in $[-(\log2+\delta),\delta]$. Both maximizing points are assumed. The loss $\log2$ comes from the selected seed lying between half and all of the growing factor, and is not the current paper's growing-seed comparison.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.peak_log_g.summary: Comparing peak gains for the alternate seed

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.peak_mem_w.text: For a differentiable scalar path, assume early values are below one comparison value, the derivative is positive on $(c,p)$ and negative on $(q,T)$, and $0\le c\le p\le q\le T$. Every supplied maximizer on $[0,T]$ then lies in $[p,q]$. The theorem neither constructs a maximizer nor asserts a unique peak.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.peak_mem_w.summary: Locating every maximum from derivative signs

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.peak_relat.text: For a positive scale $c$ satisfying $c\,\mathrm{peak}=U_*$, the inequality for the scaled vector against `gain*Ustar` is equivalent to the original inequality against `gain*peak`. Multiplication by $c$ preserves order. The gain and peaks need not be positive in this general algebraic equivalence.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.peak_relat.summary: Peak normalization preserves the early gain inequality

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.peak_relat.text: If $c>0$ and $c\,\mathrm{peak}=U_*$, rescaling the amplitude by $c$ preserves its strength divided by frequency scale times peak. The proof cancels the common positive factor. No nonzero hypothesis on the frequency or peaks appears in this algebraic statement; at zero denominators both sides use Lean’s total division.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.peak_relat.summary: Peak normalization preserves relative wave strength

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.physicalAm.text: This defines $g(t)h(t)\sqrt{1+\phi F(t)}$ for arbitrary scalar functions and a constant weight. In the wave application $g$ is the reference growth, $h$ the normalized transverse component, $F$ the norm correction, and $\phi=S^{-2}$. The binder `φ` is this weight, not the paper's wave-vector angle. Positivity and differential equations are not included.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.physicalAm.summary: A scalar formula for the physical amplitude

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.physical_n.text: For $V>0$, $S>0$, and $Z\ne0$, the Euclidean norm of $(-U/S,V,(XU-QV)/(SZ))$ factors as $V\sqrt{1+S^{-2}F}$, where $F$ is `normCorrection`. This is a scalar identity after eliminating the third component by transversality. A separate theorem inserts an actual orthonormal frame; this one does not assume any wave equation.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.physical_n.summary: Factoring the norm of the three amplitude components

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.raw_compon.text: Closeness within $\delta$ to the selected normalized state bounds the error of $V/g$ by $\delta$ and the sum of both raw component errors by $(1+|Y|+s)\delta$. This is an algebraic change-of-coordinates estimate at one time, requiring neither an ODE nor initial data. The comparison target is the alternate $(0,1)$ seed, not the growing reference pair.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.raw_compon.summary: Recovering raw component errors from normalized closeness

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.raw_ratio_.text: If the normalized state is within `δ ≤ 1 / 2` of $(1,0)$, then $V>0$ and $|U/V-Y|\le2\delta$. The only inputs are the size assumption `hδ` and the pointwise proximity bound `hclose`; no differential equation is needed for this algebraic step. Positivity of $v_g$ and the lower bound $h\ge1/2$ permit division by $V$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.raw_ratio_.summary: A small normalized error controls the amplitude ratio

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.raw_ratio_.text: The identity $U/V=Y+sl/h$ expresses the raw ratio through the normalized coordinates. Its sole hypothesis is `hV : V t ≠ 0`; the definitions already make $v_g$ and $s$ positive. This separates the reference rate $Y$ from the error term $sl/h$, which is small once $h$ stays away from zero and $l$ is small.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.raw_ratio_.summary: The raw amplitude ratio in normalized coordinates

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.reference_.text: A positive amplitude satisfying $|\log(A/v_g)|\le\varepsilon$ lies between $e^{-\varepsilon}v_g$ and $e^{\varepsilon}v_g$. The inputs `hA` and `hlog` are pointwise positivity and logarithmic proximity. No differential equation is used in this conversion. The declaration writes the reference amplitude as `referenceV`, which is the same exponential integral as `growingFactor`.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.reference_.summary: Logarithmic comparison gives two exponential amplitude bounds

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedU.text: The selected first amplitude is $g\bigl(Y(1-I)-K\bigr)$, with $g$ the growing factor, $I$ the kernel integral, and $K$ the kernel. Its value at zero is $Y(0)-1$, hence zero under the reference initial condition. The selected pair solves the same linear reference equations, but begins in a different direction from the paper's growing pair.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedU.summary: The first amplitude of the transverse initial seed

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedU_.text: When `hY₀ : Y 0 = 1`, the selected first component vanishes at zero. The formula subtracts the initial kernel value one from $Y(0)$, while the growing factor is one. This explicitly identifies the seed as $(0,1)$ in $(U,V)$ coordinates, distinct from the growing seed $(1,1)$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedU_.summary: The transverse seed has first component zero

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedV.text: The selected second amplitude is the growing factor multiplied by $1-kernelIntegral$. It starts at one for every $Y$ and, under the Riccati hypotheses, remains between half the growing factor and the growing factor. Its initial first component is zero when $Y(0)=1$, so it must not be identified with the arXiv canonical growing reference solution.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedV.summary: The second amplitude of the transverse initial seed

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedV_.text: The selected second amplitude is strictly positive at every time in $[0,T]$ if $\varepsilon>0$, $Y(0)=1$, and $Y$ satisfies the Riccati equation there. Its growing factor is positive, while the kernel bound gives $1-kernelIntegral\ge1/2$. The result applies to the alternate seed, rather than asserting positivity of every reference solution.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedV_.summary: The transverse component of the alternate seed stays positive

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedV_.text: The selected second component equals one at zero for arbitrary $Y$ and $\varepsilon$. The growing factor is one and the kernel integral is zero there. This fixes one component of the alternate seed only; the companion initial identity for the first component additionally assumes the reference initial value $Y(0)=1$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selectedV_.summary: The transverse seed has second component one

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selected_l.text: Given uniform normalized closeness $0\le\delta<1/2$ to the selected seed, this supplies a logarithmic value bound, a logarithmic derivative formula, and a rate-error estimate for the packaged physical amplitude. The margin is $m=1/2-\delta$, and `herr'` supplies the normalized derivative error separately. Its positive reference is `selectedV`, which differs from the paper's canonical reference amplitude.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selected_l.summary: Value and rate comparison with the alternate seed

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selected_s.text: The selected pair solves $U'=-damping\,U+driving\,V$ and $V'=U$ within $[0,T]$ whenever $Y$ satisfies the Riccati equation there. The proof differentiates the explicit growth and kernel formulas. No initial-value hypothesis appears in this theorem itself; the separate zero-time lemmas identify $(U,V)=(0,1)$ when $Y(0)=1$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.selected_s.summary: The alternate seed solves the reference amplitude equations

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.transverse.text: Assume the Riccati initial-value hypotheses and that the actual normalized state lies within $\delta<1/2$ of the selected state at the given time. Then $V/g\ge1/2-\delta$ and $V>0$. The positive margin comes from the selected seed's bound; no raw amplitude ODE is required beyond the supplied closeness assumption.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.transverse.summary: A small error preserves the transverse component

TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.wave_norm_.text: At normalized time $t\ge2/\varepsilon$, with $0<\varepsilon\le1$, positive frequency scale, $S\ge1$, and an orthonormal frame, separate coordinate errors at most $1/2$ imply $x/2\le\|k(t)\|/\lambda\le3x$. Here $x=\varepsilon t^2/2=\tan\varphi$. This turns the comparison geometry into an explicit late-time wave-number estimate.
TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.wave_norm_.summary: The late wave number follows the reference angle

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.continuou.text: If the reference rate and the raw operator error are continuous on the interval, the normalized matrix error is continuous there too. This is a regularity input for the perturbed triangular ODE.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.continuou.summary: The conjugated amplitude error is continuous

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.continuou.text: If the scale and deviation are continuous on a set $I$, then their triangular generator is continuous there as a continuous-linear-map-valued function. The formula uses only scalar multiplication and addition of fixed coordinate maps. No positivity, interval structure, or solution of the reference equation is required.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.continuou.summary: Continuous coefficients give a continuous normalized matrix

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.exists_no.text: From any $a\in[0,T]$, this theorem constructs operator paths $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ for the triangular system plus a continuous perturbation.
