It gives $\Phi(a)=\mathrm{Id}$, the differential equation for $\Phi$, two-sided inverse identities, and $\|\Phi(t)\|\le2\exp(2\int_a^t\rho)$. The conclusion does not expose a differential equation or norm bound for $\Psi$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.exists_no.summary: The normalized system has an invertible bounded propagator

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.hasDerivW.text: The raw amplitude equation with error operator $\mathcal E$ becomes the triangular equation plus $R\mathcal ER^{-1}$ in normalized coordinates. The inputs `hY`, `hU`, and `hV` supply the Riccati equation and the two perturbed amplitude derivatives, and `ht` specifies the point of $[0,T]$. Lean names the raw error operator `R`; `normalizedMatrixError` performs the coordinate conjugation, so that binder is not the manuscript's coordinate matrix.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.hasDerivW.summary: The amplitude error transforms by matrix conjugation

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.norm_movi.text: The physical amplitude and normalized state $z=(h,l)$ satisfy $|\mathbf b|\le9v_g\|z\|$ and $\|z\|\le7S|\mathbf b|/v_g$. The hypotheses supply orthonormality, transversality, $S\ge1$, and the listed bounds on $X,Q,Z,Y$ and $X-x$. `hscale` excludes zero wave-number scale. The physical norm is Euclidean, while `‖z‖` is the maximum norm; these explicit inequalities connect them.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.norm_movi.summary: Physical and normalized amplitudes control each other

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.norm_movi.text: For a transverse amplitude `b` satisfying the full raw equations, the norm at any $t\in[a,T]$ is at most $126S e^{2D}(a_{\rm ref}(t)/a_{\rm ref}(a))\|b(a)\|$. The geometry is assumed on $[a,t]$, while the raw equations hold on $[0,T]$. The integrated error `D` remains in the result, so a uniform constant requires a further smallness estimate.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.norm_movi.summary: Every transverse amplitude has a reference-relative growth bound

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.norm_norm.text: For an orthonormal basis and a vector with the displayed normalized components, the Euclidean norm is at most $9\|(h,l)\|$, while the pair’s maximum norm is at most $7S\|v\|$. The hypotheses include $S\ge1$, $|X|,|Q|\le S$, $1/2\le Z\le3/2$, $|Y|\le1$ and $|X-x|\le1/2$. The second inequality accounts for the shear cost in recovering coordinates.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.norm_norm.summary: Physical and normalized amplitude coordinates have controlled norms

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.norm_norm.text: The conjugated error has norm at most $((1+|Y|)^2/s)\,\|\mathcal E\|$. The arguments `ε`, `Y`, `R`, and `t` are arbitrary; no evolution equation is required. Here `R` is the raw error, and the pair-space operator norm comes from the maximum norm on `ℝ × ℝ`. Using $|Y|\le1$ and $s^{-1}\le T^2$ gives the polynomial loss used in the comparison.

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.normalize.text:
The raw matrix error after the time-dependent change of amplitude coordinates.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression uses explicit forward and inverse coordinate matrices. Their inverse relationship and the positivity of the reference factors are proved separately, rather than assumed from the word Inv in the identifier.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.normalize.summary: The error after changing amplitude coordinates

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.normalize.text:
The pair $(h,l)$ for raw library coordinates $(U,V)$, with $h=V/a_{\rm ref}$ and $l=(U-YV)/(s a_{\rm ref})$. The manuscript uses $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=(-U,V)$, which gives the same pair. Its Lean type is a product of two reals equipped with the maximum norm. No differential equation is included; on the reference solution the pair equals $(1,0)$.

Default-value audit (b5): The normalization divides by the positive exponential reference factor and the strictly positive reference clock. Those denominators are nonzero; differentiating the state additionally needs regularity of the input trajectories.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.normalize.summary: The pair of normalized amplitude coordinates

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.normalize.text: For raw amplitudes satisfying the perturbed two-row equations on $[0,T]$, their normalized state satisfies $\|z(t)\|\le2\|z(a)\|e^{2D}$ for $a\le t$. The budget integrates $((1+|Y|)^2/s)\eta$ from `a` to `t`, where `η` bounds the raw matrix error. Its continuity assumptions are needed only on $[a,T]$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.normalize.summary: Raw amplitudes obey an arbitrary-start normalized bound

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.raw_matri.text: This compares a perturbed raw system with a supplied unperturbed one after the time-dependent normalization. The integrated error is $D=\int_0^t(1+|Y|)^2\eta/s$, using the raw bound `hRη`. Both normalized growth and their difference are bounded with factors $2e^{2D}$ and $4e^{2D}D$. Initial data may differ, and the conclusion retains that initial error explicitly.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.raw_matri.summary: Comparing raw amplitude solutions through normalized coordinates

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.riccati_p.text: Given a Riccati path on $[0,T]$ with $\varepsilon>0$ and $Y(0)=1$, the normalized triangular flow has perturbation bounds with constant two. The error exponent is $2D$, where $D=\int_0^t\rho$ bounds the integrated matrix error. The rate need not satisfy $\varepsilon\le1$ here, and no smallness of $D$ is assumed. Norms are the maximum norms on the pair and its operators.

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.triangula.text:
Generator of the transverse model in the $(h,l)$ coordinates.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.triangula.summary: The triangular equation in normalized amplitude coordinates

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.triangula.text: The generator maps (h,l) to (scale·l, −2·scale·(1+e)·l). This identifies the damped second coordinate and the upper triangular coupling used by the comparison estimate.
Growth and comparison bounds for a matrix perturbation of the normalized triangular model. The matrix and pair norms here use the maximum norm on `ℝ × ℝ`.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.triangula.summary: Perturbation bounds for the normalized triangular system

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.unscaledC.text: This map sends $(U,V)$ to $(V,(U-YV)/s)$ before division by the reference amplitude. Its matrix has lower-left entry $+1/s$. The manuscript instead starts from $(\beta_1,\beta_2)=(-U,V)$ and therefore displays a lower-left entry $-1/\cos\varphi$. Composing with that first-coordinate sign change gives the same normalized pair. No differential equation is assumed by this definition.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.unscaledC.summary: Change of the library amplitude coordinates

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.unscaledC.text: This map sends $(h,l)$ to $(Yh+sl,h)$ before restoring the common reference amplitude. Its output coordinates are $(U,V)$, not the manuscript's $(\beta_1,\beta_2)=(-U,V)$. Negating the first output gives the displayed inverse matrix in the paper. The definition requires no regularity or evolution assumption on $Y$; positivity of $s$ allows the inverse identities.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.unscaledC.summary: Inverse change to the library amplitude coordinates

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.unscaledC.text: The inverse coordinate map sends a pair $(h,l)$ to $(Yh+sl,h)$. These are the raw variables $(U,V)$ before multiplication by the common growing amplitude. With $U=-\alpha_1$, the first paper component is therefore $-(Yh+sl)$, matching the signs in the paper's inverse matrix.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.unscaledC.summary: Recovering raw components before amplitude multiplication

TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.unscaledC.text: The coordinate map sends $(U,V)$ to $(V,(U-YV)/s)$. Division by the positive growing amplitude is performed separately when forming the normalized state. The paper uses $U=-\alpha_1$ and $V=\alpha_2$, so the apparent sign difference from its displayed matrix is explained by this change of raw variables, not by a different normalization.
TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison.unscaledC.summary: Reading the normalized coordinate matrix before amplitude division

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.decay.text: The coefficient $\exp(-\int_a^t2s(1+e))$ multiplying the second normalized coordinate in the triangular system. The definition accepts arbitrary real coefficient functions and ordered or unordered endpoints. Positivity follows from the exponential. To conclude decay forward in time, the later coefficient-bound theorem assumes nonnegative coefficients and an ordered interval.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.decay.summary: The decay coefficient of the triangular system

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.decay_pos.text: The diagonal coefficient is strictly positive because it is an exponential of a real integral. This holds for arbitrary real-valued scale and deviation functions and for either time order. Positivity alone does not imply decay or an upper bound of one; those require the forward-time and nonnegativity assumptions in triangular_coefficient_bounds.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.decay_pos.summary: The diagonal propagator coefficient is always positive

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.decay_sel.text: The diagonal coefficient of the triangular propagator equals one when its two time arguments agree. The exponent is the integral over an interval of zero length. No regularity or sign assumptions on the coefficient functions are needed for this initial normalization identity.

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.growingFa.text:
The growing reference factor $v_g$ normalized at time zero.

Default-value audit (b5): The totalized integral always gives a real number, so its exponential is positive. Continuity or interval integrability of Y is needed to identify its derivative with Y times the factor.

The growing factor is strictly positive for every real-valued input rate and time, because it is defined as an exponential. Differentiating it requires the separate continuity or integrability assumptions.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.growingFa.summary: The reference growth factor never vanishes

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.growingFa.text: The exponential growth factor equals one at time zero for every real-valued function $Y$. The integral from zero to itself vanishes without a continuity hypothesis. This identity fixes the normalization of the reference amplitude; differential identities and estimates for later times require additional regularity of $Y$.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.growingFa.summary: The growing reference amplitude starts at one

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.hasDerivW.text: For a continuous reference rate on the closed interval, the growth factor has within-interval derivative Y(t) times itself. The conclusion includes both endpoints of that interval.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.hasDerivW.summary: The reference factor solves its scalar growth equation

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.hasDerivW.text: The normalized coordinates satisfy $h'=sl$ and $l'=-2s(1+e)l$. Here `hY` supplies the Riccati equation, `hU` and `hV` the two unperturbed amplitude derivatives, and `ht` places the point in $[0,T]$. The function $e$ is `deviation ε Y`. All derivatives are taken within the interval, so the statement includes its endpoints.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.hasDerivW.summary: The reference amplitude equations become triangular

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.normalize.text:
The coordinate $h=V/a_{\rm ref}$ measures the second amplitude component relative to the reference amplitude. In the current manuscript $V=\alpha_2$, so this is exactly $h=\alpha_2/a_{\rm ref}$. The definition accepts arbitrary functions and imposes no evolution assumptions. Its denominator is positive. On the growing reference solution it equals one at every time.

Default-value audit (b5): The denominator is an exponential and is strictly positive for every input Y. Differentiation and growth estimates still require the hypotheses of the scalar ODE lemmas.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.normalize.summary: Amplitude divided by the reference growth factor

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.normalize.text:
The coordinate $l=(U-YV)/(s a_{\rm ref})$ is the library form of $-(\alpha_1+Y\alpha_2)/(a_{\rm ref}\cos\varphi)$. The identities are $U=-\alpha_1$, $V=\alpha_2$, and $s=\cos\varphi$. The definition assumes no differential equation, and both denominator factors are positive. On the reference pair its numerator vanishes, giving the normalized reference state $(1,0)$.

Default-value audit (b5): Both the reference clock and the exponential growth factor are strictly positive. The raw normalization therefore has no zero denominator; its time derivative needs the stated regularity.

The normalized reference path satisfies $|(h,l)(b)|\le2|(h,l)(a)|$ for any $0\le a\le b\le T$. The assumptions `hε`, `hY₀`, `hY`, `hU`, and `hV` supply the positive parameter, Riccati initial data, and amplitude equations; `ha`, `hb`, and `hab` specify the times. The square-root expression in the conclusion is the Euclidean norm, unlike the maximum norm used in some later comparison lemmas.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.normalize.summary: Uniform Euclidean bound for the reference propagator

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.transfer.text: The transfer coefficient is the integral of the scale times the decaying diagonal coefficient from the starting time $a$ to $t$. It appears in $h(t)=h(a)+transfer(a,t)l(a)$. The definition allows arbitrary functions and either time order; continuity and nonnegative coefficients are required later for its derivative and forward bounds.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.transfer.summary: Transfer from the decaying coordinate to the amplitude

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.transfer_.text: The off-diagonal transfer coefficient vanishes when its starting and ending times coincide. This follows from the zero-length integral even if the input functions are irregular. Along with the diagonal value one, it makes the explicit triangular propagation formula reproduce the initial data.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.transfer_.summary: No transfer over an interval of zero length

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.triangula.text: The diagonal propagator coefficient lies in $(0,1]$, and the off-diagonal transfer lies between zero and half the diagonal loss. The assumptions `hab`, `hs`, `he`, `hs₀`, and `he₀` order the times, give continuous coefficients, and require both coefficients to be nonnegative. Together with the explicit triangular solution, this controls the change in $h$ by the decrease in $|l|$.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.triangula.summary: Decay controls transfer between the normalized coordinates

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.triangula.text: The quantity $|h|+|l|$ is nonincreasing along the triangular system between ordered times. The hypotheses `hs`, `he`, `hs₀`, and `he₀` require continuous nonnegative coefficients; `hh` and `hl` are the two evolution equations, and `hab` orders the endpoints. The estimate follows from the explicit propagator and the bound on its transfer coefficient, without using a particular Riccati solution.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.triangula.summary: The sum of normalized absolute values does not increase

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.triangula.text: Every solution of the triangular equations with continuous nonnegative scale and deviation satisfies $\sqrt{h(b)^2+l(b)^2}\le2\sqrt{h(a)^2+l(a)^2}$ when $a\le b$. The proof first contracts $|h|+|l|$ and then compares norms. This conclusion explicitly uses the Euclidean norm, unlike the maximum norm on the product type used in ReferenceComparison.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.triangula.summary: A uniform bound for the normalized Euclidean norm

TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.triangula.text: The triangular system has the solution $l(t)=d(a,t)l(a)$ and $h(t)=h(a)+q(a,t)l(a)$, where `decay` is an exponential integral and `transfer` is its weighted integral. The inputs `hs`, `he`, `hh`, and `hl` give continuous coefficients and the two differential equations on $[a,b]$; `ht` selects the observation time. Nonnegativity is only needed by subsequent estimates.
TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator.triangula.summary: Explicit solution of the triangular reference system

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.actual_coupl.text: This converts supplied polynomial errors for two normalized coupling functions into the lower bound $\nu\ge\varepsilon/2$ and the two late relative-error bounds. The assumptions include $T\ge2$, $\delta\ge0$, $C_0\ge16$, $p+2\le C_0$, $8C\le C_0$, and both finite-smallness inequalities. The bounds `hνerr` and `hηerr` are inputs; this theorem does not derive them from a physical wave.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.actual_coupl.summary: Turning polynomial coupling errors into the stated inequalities

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.actual_coupl.text: If both actual normalized couplings are within $\varepsilon/(8T^2)$ of the reference values, then the first is at least $\varepsilon/2$ throughout the interval, and the two late-time relative bounds follow. The hypotheses `hνerr` and `hηerr` supply those errors; `hform` and `he` supply the bounded reference deviation. The parameter condition is `hε₁ : ε ≤ 1 / 16`, and `hT` requires $T\ge2$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.actual_coupl.summary: Reference error bounds give the actual coupling conclusions

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.amplitude_in.text: The early amplitude obeys $A(\tau)\le e^{3-\varepsilon^{-1/2}}A(\tau_m)$ for $0\le\tau\le1$. The inputs include `hε : 2 * ε ≤ 1`, continuity and the cap $Y\le1$, the reference gain integral, interval membership, and the two exponential comparison bounds `hcompare`. The right side uses the amplitude at the reference turning time itself. Replacing it by the full-interval maximum gives the initial-window conclusion used in Proposition 2.8.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.amplitude_in.summary: Early amplitude is small compared with the turning-time amplitude

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.amplitude_la.text: The peak-normalized product of amplitude and wave number is comparable to $\sqrt{x/\varepsilon}$. The inputs include the reference representation, a full-interval amplitude comparison, `hmax` identifying the actual maximum, and `hklo` and `hkhi` bounding the normalized wave number by multiples of $x$. The conclusion keeps all constants explicit as `kmin`, `kmax`, `c`, and `C`. The crossing bounds then replace $x$ by a multiple of $1/\varepsilon_+$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.amplitude_la.summary: Late strength follows the square-root clock law

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.amplitude_ra.text: If $cv_g\le A\le Cv_g$ and $v_g$ is maximal at $\tau_m$, then $A(\tau)/M$ is between $(c/C)v_g(\tau)/v_g(\tau_m)$ and $(C/c)v_g(\tau)/v_g(\tau_m)$. The hypothesis `hmax : IsGreatest (A '' Icc 0 T) M` makes $M$ the actual full-interval maximum. The inputs `hc`, `hC`, `hm`, `hτ`, `hpeak`, and `hcompare` provide positivity, interval membership, and both comparisons.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.amplitude_ra.summary: Comparison to the actual maximum on the full interval

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.couplingRati.text: The bounds $1/(4x)\le\rho\le3/(2x)$ follow from `hx : 1 ≤ x ε t` and `hratio : |ρ / s ε t - 1| ≤ 1 / 2`. These are pointwise assumptions; no continuity or crossing is required. The proof combines $s/2\le\rho\le3s/2$ with $1/(2x)\le s\le1/x$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.couplingRati.summary: The coupling ratio is comparable to the inverse clock

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.coupling_err.text: The inequality $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$ implies $CT^p\delta\le\varepsilon/(8T^2)$ when `hp : p + 2 ≤ C₀` and `hC₀ : 8 * C ≤ C₀`. The remaining assumptions are `hT : 2 ≤ T` and `hδ : 0 ≤ δ`. This makes explicit how the universal threshold absorbs both the coefficient and the extra two powers needed by the coupling comparison.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.coupling_err.summary: The finite-window smallness absorbs the coupling error

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.damping.text:
The damping coefficient is 2ετ x s², with x = ετ²/2 and s = (1+x²)⁻¹ᐟ². The angle formulation in Section 2 rewrites this same coefficient trigonometrically.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.damping.summary: The damping coefficient of the reference equation

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.damping_le_t.text: For $0\le\varepsilon\le1$ and nonnegative time, the damping is at most two. The proof treats $\tau\le2$ using $xs^2\le1/2$ and later times using $x^2s^2\le1$. Together with the nonnegative deviation contribution, this gives the reference-rate lower bound $Y\ge-1/2$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.damping_le_t.summary: A global bound on the damping coefficient

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.damping_nonn.text: For $\varepsilon\ge0$ and $\tau\ge0$, the damping coefficient $2\varepsilon\tau x s^2$ is nonnegative. The sign follows from the factors, with $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$. This is the sign needed when comparing the Riccati equation with $Y\le1$; it is not a statement about the sign of $Y$ itself.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.damping_nonn.summary: The damping is nonnegative at future times

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.damping_zero.text: The damping coefficient is zero at $\tau=0$ for every real $\varepsilon$. This follows directly from its factor $\tau$ in $2\varepsilon\tau x s^2$. No positivity or solution assumption is involved; the identity is used to turn zero initial deviation into the prescribed initial Riccati value $Y(0)=1$.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviation.text:
The deviation is (Y + damping/4)/s − 1. Since s is positive, this is the inverse change of variables to the reference-rate formula; boundedness of the deviation comes from the Riccati estimates.

Default-value audit (b5): The clock factor s is strictly positive for every real ε and time. This change of variables is algebraically well-defined without a Riccati hypothesis; the bound on its value needs that hypothesis.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviation.summary: The relative deviation from the reference clock

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviationRhs.text: This is the right-hand side $s(-2e-e^2+\varepsilon x s^2/2)$ of the deviation equation. Here $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2=\tan\varphi$ and $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}=\cos\varphi$. It is a scalar function of three unrestricted real inputs. The initial condition, differential equation, and invariant bound $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$ must be supplied or proved separately.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviation_bo.text: Assume $\varepsilon>0$, $e(0)=0$, and the deviation differential equation within $[0,T]$. Then $0\le e(\tau)\le\varepsilon/8$ for every $\tau$ in that interval. No upper bound $\varepsilon\le1$ is required here. The lower barrier uses a small negative comparison level, while the upper boundary has a strictly inward derivative.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviation_bo.summary: The deviation stays in its invariant interval

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviation_ex.text: For `hε : 0 < ε` and `hε₁ : ε ≤ 1`, there is a deviation path on the whole forward ray, starting at zero, solving the deviation equation, and taking values in $[0,\varepsilon/8]$. The three clauses concern the same path `e`. The construction invokes a scalar existence theorem with an invariant interval and a local Lipschitz bound, rather than assuming a global Riccati solution.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviation_ex.summary: A bounded deviation exists for every nonnegative time

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviation_re.text: Constructing $Y=s(1+e)-damping/4$ from any function $e$ and then applying the inverse deviation formula returns $e$ identically. Equality is equality of functions on all real times. The proof cancels $s$, which is always strictly positive; no ODE, initial value, or invariant-strip hypothesis is needed.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviation_re.summary: Recovering the deviation from the reference rate

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.deviation_ze.text: The substituted deviation satisfies $e(0)=0$ when `h₀ : Y 0 = 1`. At zero, the clock factor is one and the damping coefficient is zero, so the result follows directly from the definition of `deviation`. It supplies the initial condition needed for the invariant-interval argument; no differential equation is assumed by this identity itself.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.driving.text:
The driving coefficient is s²(1−εx). Together with the damping coefficient it gives the scalar Riccati equation used for the growing reference solution.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.driving.summary: The driving coefficient of the reference equation

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.forcing_boun.text: For nonnegative $\varepsilon$, the forcing term $\varepsilon x s^2/2$ lies between zero and $\varepsilon/4$ at every real time. The estimate uses $0\le x$ and $xs^2\le1/2$, which express the elementary bound on $\sin\varphi\cos\varphi$. This controls the signs of the deviation equation at the two ends of its invariant strip.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.forcing_boun.summary: The forcing in the deviation equation is bounded

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.hasDerivAt_s.text: The clock factor satisfies $s'=-\varepsilon\tau xs^3$, equivalently $s'/s=-\varepsilon\tau xs^2$. Lean writes the derivative as `-(damping ε τ / 2 * s ε τ)`. The identity is valid for every real `ε` and `τ`, since $1+x^2$ is always positive. Positivity of $s$ permits the logarithmic-derivative reading used in the manuscript.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.hasDerivAt_x.text: The polynomial coordinate x has derivative ετ at every real time. This identity is used when differentiating the angle and the Riccati change of variables.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.hasDerivAt_x.summary: The reference coordinate has derivative ετ

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.hasDerivWith.text: The Riccati equation implies the differential equation for $e=(Y+\frac12\varepsilon\tau xs^2)/s-1$. The hypothesis `hY` supplies the derivative of `Y` within an arbitrary set `D` at the chosen point. The conclusion differentiates `deviation ε Y` in that same set. Together with the reverse substitution theorem and $s>0$, this makes the two equations equivalent.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.hasDerivWith.summary: The Riccati equation implies the deviation equation

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.hasDerivWith.text: For a continuous rate $Y$ on the forward ray, the exponential reference amplitude has derivative $Ya_{\rm ref}$ within that ray, including zero. The library names this derivative its first component $U$. In the manuscript's coordinates $\alpha_1=-U$ and $\alpha_2=a_{\rm ref}$, so the same statement reads $\alpha_2'=-\alpha_1$. No Riccati equation is required for this differentiation.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.hasDerivWith.summary: The reference amplitude differentiates to its first library component

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.hasDerivWith.text: A solution of $e'=s(-2e-e^2+\frac12\varepsilon xs^2)$ gives a Riccati solution after the substitution $Y=s(1+e)-\frac12\varepsilon\tau xs^2$. The only input `he` is the deviation derivative at the current point within a set `D`. This is one direction of the substitution; `hasDerivWithinAt_deviation` proves the reverse direction. No sign or size restriction on $\varepsilon$ is needed for the algebraic identity.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.hasDerivWith.summary: The deviation equation implies the Riccati equation

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.inv_sq_windo.text: The clock factor obeys $s\ge T^{-2}$ for $0\le\tau\le T$, assuming `hε : 0 ≤ ε`, `hε₁ : ε ≤ 1`, and `hT : 2 ≤ T`. The membership hypothesis is `hτ`. Equivalently, $s^{-1}\le T^2$. This bounds the cost of the time-dependent coordinate change without introducing exponential growth in the window length.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.inv_sq_windo.summary: The clock factor is bounded below on a finite interval

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.inv_two_mul_.text: The bound $1/(2x)\le s$ holds whenever `hx : 1 ≤ x ε t`. This is an algebraic estimate on $(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$ and does not assume the reference differential equation. Together with $s\le1/x$, it converts the late relative coupling comparison into two bounds proportional to $1/x$, which locate the crossing.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceEta.text:
The value $[-1+\varepsilon x+2(1+x^2)Y^2+2\varepsilon\tau xY]s$ of the second reference coupling divided by the preceding coupling $\nu$. The apparent large terms in its numerator cancel when $Y$ has the bounded-deviation form. This definition alone does not assume that form or assert the cancellation. The factor $s=\cos\varphi$ is already included, unlike the numerator-only algebraic lemma.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceNu.text:
The value $(x+\varepsilon+2\varepsilon\tau Y)s$ of the first reference coupling divided by the preceding coupling $\nu$. With $x=\tan\varphi$ and $s=\cos\varphi$, this is the unsimplified trigonometric expression in the coupling proof. The definition imposes no Riccati equation or parameter bounds. Positivity and late-time closeness to one are separate estimates.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceNu_.text: The first normalized reference coupling is at least $\varepsilon$ on $0\le\tau\le\sqrt2/\varepsilon$. The inputs `hε`, `hε₁`, `hτ₀`, and `hτ` restrict the parameter and time, while `hform` and `he` give the deviation representation and $e(\tau)\ge0$. Positivity of $Y$ in this range yields $N_\nu\ge x+\varepsilon$, and an algebraic estimate gives the stated lower bound.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceNu_.summary: The early reference coupling is bounded below by epsilon

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceU.text: The library defines $U(\tau)=Y(\tau)a_{\rm ref}(\tau)$. In the current manuscript the first amplitude coordinate is $\alpha_1=-U$, while $\alpha_2=a_{\rm ref}$. The supplied function $Y$ need not initially satisfy any equation. A separate theorem proves the reference amplitude equations from the Riccati equation, and $Y(0)=1$ supplies the initial coordinate $\alpha_1(0)=-1$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceU.summary: The negative of the first reference amplitude component

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceU_z.text: The library first component satisfies $U(0)=1$ if $Y(0)=1$. The paper's first coordinate is $\alpha_1=-U$, so its initial value is minus one, while $\alpha_2=V$ starts at one. The identity follows from $U=Ya_{\rm ref}$ and $a_{\rm ref}(0)=1$. No differential equation is required for this initial-value calculation.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV.text:
The reference amplitude $a_{\rm ref}(\tau)=\exp(\int_0^\tau Y)$, formerly denoted $v_g$. The definition accepts an arbitrary real function $Y$ and does not assume an evolution equation. The exponential makes it positive and equal to one at zero. Its derivative requires continuity of $Y$. In the current reference pair this is the second coordinate $\alpha_2$.

The library's first component `referenceU` is $Y a_{\rm ref}$, while the paper's first amplitude coordinate is its negative.

Default-value audit (b5): The exponential is always positive, even when the raw interval integral is totalized. Solving the growth ODE requires continuity or the stated integral hypotheses.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV.summary: Positive reference amplitude from the integrated rate

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_i.text: If $Y\le1$ on the nonnegative ray and the supplied gain inequality holds at `τm`, then for $0\le\tau\le1$ the exponential amplitude is at most $\exp(2-1/\sqrt\varepsilon)$ times its value at `τm`. This theorem assumes the gain rather than proving it. It imposes neither a Riccati equation nor positivity of $\varepsilon$ independently of those input inequalities.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_i.summary: The initial amplitude is small relative to the gained amplitude

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_l.text: Assume $0<\varepsilon\le1$, the reference ansatz with continuous $Y$, and the global deviation strip. If `τm` lies in $[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$ and $\tau\ge\tau_m$, the amplitude ratio lies between $1/\sqrt{\varepsilon x(\tau)}$ and $3e^2/\sqrt{\varepsilon x(\tau)}$. The hypotheses locate the comparison time but do not require it to be a zero or maximum.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_l.summary: Explicit bounds for the reference amplitude after the peak window

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_l.text: Under the same ansatz, deviation, and time-window hypotheses as the late amplitude estimate, multiplying the amplitude ratio by $x(\tau)$ gives bounds between $\sqrt{x(\tau)/\varepsilon}$ and $3e^2\sqrt{x(\tau)/\varepsilon}$. The multiplier is the algebraic clock, not an actual wave-vector norm. Further comparison lemmas connect this quantity to physical strength at a crossing.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_l.summary: Multiplying the late reference amplitude by the clock

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_l.text: The reference amplitude is maximal at a time $a\ge0$ when its continuous rate `Y` is nonnegative before $a$ and nonpositive afterwards. These assumptions are `ha`, `hY`, `hbefore`, and `hafter`. The conclusion holds for every nonnegative time, not only a fixed finite interval. The proof compares exponential integrals on either side of $a$. Applied with $a=\tau_m$, the sign clauses of the reference lemma provide the hypotheses.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_l.summary: The turning time maximizes the reference amplitude

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_p.text: The reference amplitude is an exponential of the integrated rate and is strictly positive for every real-valued rate and time. Its evolution and quantitative growth estimates need their own hypotheses.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_p.summary: The integrated reference amplitude is positive

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_r.text: For ordered nonnegative times, the reference-amplitude ratio is $\sqrt{s(b)/s(a)}\exp(\int_a^b s(1+e))$. The hypotheses are the bounded-deviation form of $Y$ and continuity of $Y$; this identity itself does not require a bound on $e$. With $s=\cos\varphi$, it is exactly the square-root ratio displayed in the revised crossing proof.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_r.summary: The reference amplitude ratio splits into two factors

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_r.text: For a continuous rate $Y$ on the nonnegative ray and $0\le a\le b$, the ratio of its exponential amplitudes is $referenceV(Y,b)/referenceV(Y,a)=\exp(\int_a^bY)$. This uses addition of adjacent interval integrals and positivity of the exponential denominator. No Riccati equation or turning-time hypothesis is required.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_r.summary: The amplitude ratio integrates the reference rate

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceV_z.text: The reference amplitude satisfies $v_g(0)=1$ for every real function `Y`. The interval integral from zero to zero vanishes, so the result follows by evaluating the exponential. This statement supplies the second initial condition of the growing reference path without assuming continuity, the Riccati equation, or any bound on $\varepsilon$.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY.text:
The expression $Y=s(1+e)-\frac12\varepsilon\tau xs^2$ used to construct the Riccati solution. The definition is written as `s ε τ * (1 + e τ) - damping ε τ / 4`; `damping` equals $2\varepsilon\tau xs^2$. No differential equation or bound on the supplied function `e` is included here. Separate lemmas prove that its invariant interval yields a global reference solution.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula contains an inverse or quotient. Its nondegenerate mathematical use requires the denominator conditions in the argument or the calling lemma; totalized inversion alone does not provide them.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY.summary: Reference rate expressed through its bounded deviation

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY_d.text: Substituting the deviation associated to Y into the reference-rate formula gives Y back as a function. This is an exact algebraic inverse, independent of whether Y solves the Riccati equation.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY_d.summary: Reconstructing the rate from its deviation

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY_n.text: At a time satisfying `h₃ : ε * τ = 3`, the substituted reference rate is negative if `hε : 0 < ε`, `hε₁ : ε ≤ 1`, and `he : e τ ≤ ε / 8`. These are pointwise conditions on the deviation, not a differential equation. Combined with positivity through $\varepsilon\tau=2$ and continuity, the result brackets a zero of the reference solution.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY_n.summary: The reference rate is negative at the later endpoint

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY_p.text: The substituted reference rate is positive whenever `hε : 0 ≤ ε`, `h₂ : ε * τ ≤ 2`, and `he : 0 ≤ e τ`. These pointwise assumptions suffice; the lemma does not require that `e` solve its differential equation. The identity $Y=s(1+e-\frac12\varepsilon\tau xs)$ and the strict bound $xs<1$ give positivity.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY_p.summary: The reference rate is positive before the turning range

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY_z.text: If the supplied deviation satisfies `h₀ : e 0 = 0`, then its reconstructed reference rate equals one at time zero. The definition of $s$ gives $s(0)=1$, and the damping vanishes there. The statement does not require $e$ to solve its differential equation or assume a sign for $\varepsilon$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.referenceY_z.summary: Zero deviation gives the initial reference rate

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.reference_am.text: A solution of the Riccati differential equation on the forward ray yields both amplitude equations for $U=Ya_{\rm ref}$ and $V=a_{\rm ref}$. The proof differentiates their product and the exponential integral. The manuscript uses $\alpha_1=-U$ and $\alpha_2=V$, giving its pair $(-Ya_{\rm ref},a_{\rm ref})$. This theorem does not impose $Y(0)=1$; that separate initial condition selects the growing reference solution.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.reference_am.summary: A Riccati solution reconstructs the reference amplitude pair

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.reference_co.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1/16$ and $\tau\ge\sqrt2/\varepsilon$, the first reference coupling is at least $\varepsilon$ and the ratio of reference couplings differs from $s$ by relative error at most $4\varepsilon$. The ansatz and the deviation bound at the single time are explicit hypotheses. This statement concerns reference couplings, not yet the couplings of the actual wave.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.reference_co.summary: The late reference coupling ratio follows the cosine factor

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.reference_co.text: For $\tau\ge\sqrt2/\varepsilon$, the normalized reference couplings satisfy $|\nu_{\rm ref}-1|\le7\varepsilon^2$ and $|\eta_{\rm ref}/s-1|\le2\varepsilon$. The hypotheses `hε`, `hε₁`, `hτ`, `hform`, and `he` give $0<\varepsilon\le1$, the time range, and the deviation formula with $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$. The quantities named `referenceNu` and `referenceEta` already include the factor $s$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.reference_co.summary: Late reference couplings are close to their limiting values

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.reference_ta.text: The integral of $s(1+e)$ from any $a\ge2/\varepsilon$ to any later $b$ lies in $[0,2]$. The hypotheses `hε`, `hε₁`, `ha`, `hab`, `hform`, `hY`, and `he` give the positive parameter, ordered late times, continuous reference rate, and bounded deviation. The estimate uses the integrable majorant $4/(\varepsilon\tau^2)$, so it is uniform in the upper time.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.reference_ta.summary: The post-peak envelope integral stays bounded

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.rhs.text:
The scalar expression $s^2(1-\varepsilon x)-2\varepsilon\tau xs^2Y-Y^2$ in the reference Riccati equation. `driving` and `damping` name the first two coefficients, with $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$ and $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$. This is a definition for all real arguments. The existence theorem adds `hε : 0 < ε`, `hε₁ : ε ≤ 1`, and the initial condition $Y(0)=1$.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.rhs.summary: Right-hand side of the reference Riccati equation

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_abs_.text: Every forward Riccati solution with $Y(0)=1$ satisfies $|Y|\le1$ when $0<\varepsilon\le1$. The assumptions are `hε`, `hε₁`, `h₀`, and the pointwise differential equation `hY`. The upper bound uses a scalar barrier at one, while the lower bound uses the deviation representation and the damping bound. The declared conclusion is $|Y|\le1$; it does not separately state the sharper lower estimate appearing in the manuscript's proof.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_abs_.summary: The reference rate has absolute value at most one

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_devi.text: A supplied Riccati solution with $Y(0)=1$ determines a deviation in $[0,\varepsilon/8]$ throughout $[0,T]$, provided $\varepsilon>0$. The proof transforms the derivative and initial value, then applies the deviation barrier. This is a conditional estimate for an existing solution; global construction and uniqueness are separate declarations.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_devi.summary: The Riccati solution determines a bounded deviation

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_devi.text: For ε > 0, any solution of the specified Riccati initial value problem on the forward ray has deviation in [0,ε/8]. The hypotheses include Y(0)=1 and the derivative equation at every nonnegative time.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_devi.summary: The Riccati deviation stays between zero and ε/8

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_exis.text: The reference Riccati initial value problem has a solution on the entire forward ray with the prescribed bounded-deviation decomposition. The source uses the frozen manuscript's equation number; the arXiv proof map identifies it with the current reference equation.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_exis.summary: Global existence of the growing reference solution

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_gain.text: The integral of the reference rate up to a time $\tau_m\ge2/\varepsilon$ is at least $\varepsilon^{-1/2}-1$. Besides `hε` and `hε₁`, the theorem assumes the deviation representation `hform`, its invariant-interval bound `he`, continuity `hYc`, and nonnegativity `hnonneg` before $\tau_m$. It estimates a shorter interval ending at $\sqrt{2/\varepsilon}$, then uses nonnegativity to reach the selected endpoint.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_gain.summary: Integrated reference growth before the peak

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_refe.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, this assembles a global Riccati solution, its deviation in $[0,\varepsilon/8]$, and a turning time in $[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$. The rate is bounded by one in absolute value, positive before the zero and negative afterwards, and its integral to the zero is at least $1/\sqrt\varepsilon-1$. The integral is the logarithm of the separately defined reference amplitude.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_refe.summary: Global reference growth and its unique turning time

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_turn.text: The global Riccati solution has a zero in $[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$, is positive before it, and is negative afterwards. The inputs `hY`, `hform`, and `he` supply the differential equation, the deviation representation, and its bound, with `hε` and `hε₁` restricting the parameter. The strict signs imply uniqueness of the zero. The paper-facing wrapper states that uniqueness as an explicit equivalence.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_turn.summary: The reference solution has one change of sign

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_uniq.text: Two solutions of the reference Riccati initial value problem agree on the nonnegative ray. This is uniqueness on the domain in the statement; it does not assert uniqueness of arbitrary extensions to negative time.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_uniq.summary: Uniqueness of the forward Riccati solution

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s.text:
The scalar $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$ used in the reference amplitude coefficients. Lean writes it as the reciprocal of `Real.sqrt (1 + x ε τ ^ 2)`. The quantity under the square root is positive for every real $\varepsilon,\tau$, so no sign assumption is needed for this definition. Later identities use $s^2(1+x^2)=1$.

Default-value audit (b5): The quantity under the square root is 1+x²>0, so the inverse is always of a positive number. No exceptional square-root or zero-inverse value enters this definition.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_le_inv_x.text: The clock factor satisfies $s\le1/x$ whenever `hx : 0 < x ε t`. It follows directly from $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$ and $\sqrt{1+x^2}\ge x$. No evolution equation or upper bound on $\varepsilon$ is required. In the late-time argument this supplies an integrable $\tau^{-2}$ bound because $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_le_inv_x.summary: The clock factor is at most the inverse clock

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_le_one.text: The algebraic clock factor $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$ is at most one for every real parameter and time. The proof uses $s^2(1+x^2)=1$ together with $s>0$. No choice of angle or sign of $\varepsilon$ is assumed, so this lemma also covers inputs outside the physical parameter range.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_pos.text: The reciprocal square root s of 1+x² is positive for all real parameters and times. This justifies division by s in the normalized reference coordinates.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_pos.summary: The reference clock factor is strictly positive

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_sq_mul.text: The identity s²(1+x²)=1 is valid for all real parameters and times. It converts estimates involving the reciprocal square root into algebraic expressions.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_sq_mul.summary: The reference clock normalizes the squared length

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_zero.text: At τ = 0 the reference coordinate x vanishes, so the clock factor s equals one. This is the initial normalization of the reference system.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x.text:
The reference coordinate $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$ for the triangular wave-vector system. It is a polynomial in normalized time and is defined for all real parameters. Along with $Q=-\varepsilon\tau$ and $Z=1$, it describes the reference trajectory from $(0,0,1)$. Its derivative is $\varepsilon\tau$, as recorded separately in `hasDerivAt_x`.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula contains an inverse or quotient. Its nondegenerate mathematical use requires the denominator conditions in the argument or the calling lemma; totalized inversion alone does not provide them.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_bounds_of_.text: A time $a\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$ has $2/\varepsilon\le x(a)\le9/(2\varepsilon)$. The only assumptions are `hε : 0 < ε` and `ha`, membership in the turning-time interval. The proof substitutes $x=\varepsilon a^2/2$. It does not require that $a$ actually be a zero of the Riccati solution.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_bounds_of_.summary: The clock size at a bracketed turning time

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_mul_s_lt_o.text: The product $xs=x/\sqrt{1+x^2}$ is strictly less than one for every real `ε` and `τ`. There are no positivity or evolution hypotheses in this algebraic lemma. The strict inequality is used with $e\ge0$ to show that the substituted reference rate remains positive through $\varepsilon\tau=2$, so the turning time must occur later.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_mul_s_lt_o.summary: The product of clock factors stays below one

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_mul_s_sq_l.text: The factor $xs^2=x/(1+x^2)$ is at most $1/2$. The statement allows arbitrary real `ε` and `τ`; it does not require the positive-parameter hypotheses of the model lemma. Its proof uses $s^2(1+x^2)=1$ and a nonnegative square. In the deviation equation this controls the positive forcing by $\varepsilon/4$ when $\varepsilon\ge0$.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_nonneg.text: For ε ≥ 0, the polynomial coordinate x = ετ²/2 is nonnegative for every real τ. No forward-time assumption is needed for this elementary bound.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_nonneg.summary: The reference first coordinate is nonnegative

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.add.text: Two smooth coefficient families with the same residual exponent `p` can be added, with the derivative constants replaced by $C+B$. The proof applies additivity of iterated derivatives and the triangle inequality at every order up to `n`. No new parent-power exponent or width condition is introduced.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.add.summary: Adding coefficient profiles adds their allowances

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.bilinear.text: For two jet packages with residual exponents `p` and `q`, a bilinear map of norm at most one produces exponent $p+q$ and constant $2^nCB$. The hypothesis $D\ge1$ is retained. The finite Leibniz estimate distributes derivatives across the factors without changing the common slope sixteen.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.bilinear.summary: A bilinear product adds the residual parent exponents

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.coefficients.text: If $\ell\ge0$, $D\ge1$, and $\ell D^{16}\le1$, a label-jet allowance $CD^{16j+p}$ yields a mixed-word coefficient bound $KD^p$ whenever $C\le K$. Every coefficient is phase independent. The proof absorbs $\ell^jD^{16j}$, leaving a residual power independent of the derivative order.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.coefficients.summary: The envelope width removes derivative-dependent growth

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.const_smul.text: Multiplying a jet-controlled family by a real constant `s` preserves its residual parent exponent and multiplies its allowance by $|s|$. The proof packages scalar multiplication as a fixed continuous linear map and controls every iterated derivative. At `s = 0` the result correctly has zero allowance.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.const_smul.summary: A scalar multiplies the jet allowance by its absolute value

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.map.text: If `hf` gives label jets for `f` and a fixed linear map `L` has norm at most one, the same allowance bounds `L ∘ f`. Smoothness follows by composition and each derivative is mapped linearly. Neither the residual parent exponent `p` nor the constant `C` is increased.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.map.summary: A contractive linear map preserves the jet allowance

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.mono_power.text: For $D\ge1$ and `hpq : p ≤ q`, a jet bound with residual exponent `p` also holds with exponent `q` and the same constant. Only monotonicity of powers is used. This permits several coefficient expressions with different algebraic degrees to share one final exponent.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.mono_power.summary: Enlarging a parent exponent preserves the derivative bound

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.sub.text: The difference of two coefficient families with the same residual parent exponent is bounded using the sum of their nonnegative constants. Iterated differentiation respects subtraction, followed by the norm triangle inequality. This handles the subtraction in the time derivative of the potential without relying on cancellation for its size estimate.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.sub.summary: Subtracting coefficient profiles adds their allowances

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerBase.text: Stores a first-wave selection, its scheduled physical stage, the dyadic cutoff identity and an initial pair of inductive stages. Equality fields identify the base velocity, pressure, stationary parent and oscillation with those of the selected approximation. This richer record lets later terminal estimates recover the actual construction behind the abstract base.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerBase.summary: The initial hierarchy and cutoff retain their exact field identities

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.text: Stores lifetime bounds, one radius exponent, one envelope constant, a scheduled base and a successor for every admissible inductive prefix. The successor is dependent on its actual tip and prefix. This record supports a single infinite construction while retaining the selected finite hierarchy and dyadic cutoff at every stage.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.summary: One schedule retains every selected physical step

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Ap.text: For the selected approximation at step `n`, this predicate requires all time jets `i ≤ q` to satisfy velocity half-Hölder bounds through the hierarchy depth and a first-order residual bound. The child-frequency exponents are `2*(m+1)+e` for velocity and `e` times the next-frequency factor `(-4)` for residual. It records the uniform pointwise-in-time inequalities, not their proof.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Ap.summary: The uncut velocity and residual bounds before truncation

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Me.text: At fixed time order `q` and spatial order `m`, the selected mean correction must belong to `SpatialHolderHalf m` at every slab time and have norm at most half the inverse child frequency. This predicate singles out the mean contribution. The other half of the increment budget is supplied later by the cutoff tail.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Me.summary: The mean contributes half the permitted mixed increment

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po.text: For the actual selected step at index `n`, requires all time jets through `q` of the approximate velocity to satisfy the stated Hölder bounds at every spatial order up to the cutoff depth. The residual is measured at spatial order one. Both carry a common factor $\mu^B$, with explicit child-frequency powers and a next-frequency factor $\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ in the residual. This is a predicate on a fixed construction, not a proved estimate.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po.summary: Approximation time bounds before absorbing the parent power

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po.text: This predicate on one scheduled construction records that the fixed $(q,m)$ time jet of the selected mean correction is spatially half-Hölder on the full closed stage slab and has norm at most $\mu^B\lambda^{-5/2}$. It is an input property, not a proof of the bound. The exponent $B$ is the old-parent polynomial loss. The absorption theorem quantifies over such bounds before sending the stage index to infinity. The regularity conjunct prevents a finite default value of the real-valued norm from serving as regularity evidence; positive scheduled frequencies protect the real-power interpretation.

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc.text: The structure records the factorial time-norm bounds for the selected oscillation, mean, remainder and activation correction. The oscillation and activation use amplitude-weighted norms with factor $\lambda^{-5/4}$, while the mean uses an unweighted norm with factor $\lambda^{-5/2}$. The remainder carries the depth-dependent oscillatory exponent. Spatial orders are restricted by the stated derivative reserve. These are requirements on one selected expansion; a separate theorem supplies them from the coefficient and solver estimates.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc.summary: Auxiliary bounds for the finite expansion

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc.text: This structure records mixed derivative bounds for the selected parent’s flow derivative, inverse flow derivative, pulled-back velocity gradient, normalized covector and reciprocal squared covector. Those fields use time order $q+1$. The pulled-back residual uses order $q$ and retains its small child-frequency factor. The coefficient scale is the ninth power of the parent frequency. The structure lists required estimates; the separate existence theorem constructs them from the actual parent time bounds.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc.summary: Auxiliary bounds for the selected parent coefficients

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Se.text: At reserve `depth+q+1`, this predicate asks for bounds on the actual selected mean, oscillation, remainder, and combined switch profiles. The mean and remainder use unweighted time norms; oscillation and switch use the central amplitude weight. All four share $\mu^E$, while their displayed child-frequency powers remain distinct. The predicate is an input interface, not an existence statement.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Se.summary: Four mixed profile bounds for the selected graph

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Te.text: This record asks for two conditional eventual statements on one scheduled construction. Parent stage bounds through `q` must imply uncut approximation bounds through `q+1` with some exponent `e`, and for each fixed `m` they must imply the half-size mean bound. The exponent is chosen before the eventual stage index; the mean threshold may depend on `q,m,A`.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Te.summary: Two eventual graph estimates close the time induction

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.co.text: Projects a scheduled construction to the abstract `InductiveEulerConstruction` by keeping its lifetime bounds, certified base and each stored successor's step. It does not choose new stages. The auxiliary selected hierarchy data remain available in the original record and are reconnected to this abstract construction by the subsequent equality theorems.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.co.summary: Forgetting retained profiles gives the inductive construction

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: For fixed time order `q` and input exponent `B`, choose a natural exponent `E` before the scale `D` is supplied. For every `D ≥ 2`, the actual recursive flow-coefficient amplitude at input `D^B` is at most `D^E`. The additional inequality `(B+2)*q ≤ E` reserves enough power to cover the pulled-back residual amplitude as well.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: The flow coefficient amplitude has a uniform polynomial power

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: Choose a function `L`, with `L N ≥ 1`, before the parameters and scheduled construction are supplied. If the radius exponent is at least seven, every selected stage satisfies scaled inverse-coframe derivative bounds through order `N`, with amplitude $\lambda_{n+1}^9$. The same function works for all stage indices, while its value may grow with the finite derivative reserve.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: One coframe cost works for every selected stage

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: The selected mean solver gains one time order from its phase-independent forcing. Its factorial seminorm at order $q+1$ and spatial order $m$ is bounded by a parent-scale power times the forcing seminorm at order $q$ and spatial order $m+1$. The theorem assumes the selected coefficient bounds, a sufficiently large fixed radius exponent and the scheduled frequency conditions. Its constants depend on fixed orders, while the radius threshold is uniform in time order.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Auxiliary mean estimate gains one time derivative

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: Time bounds for the selected parent give mixed bounds for the flow derivative, inverse flow derivative, pulled-back velocity gradient, normalized covector, its reciprocal square, and the pulled-back residual. `q` and `A` determine an exponent `E` and constants `C` before the construction and stage. The hypotheses are a parent frequency at least two and `StageTimeBounds q A`. The coefficient structure keeps one extra velocity time order and retains the residual’s small frequency factor; derived products supply the remaining coefficients.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Fixed parent powers control the coefficient time derivatives

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: An estimate `StageTimeBounds q A` on the selected parent supplies mixed derivative bounds through order $q+1$ for its velocity and through order $q$ for its residual on the child slab. The only additional numerical input is a parent frequency at least two. The theorem chooses the velocity exponent `B` and spatial-order constants `K` before the construction and stage. The residual factor remains the child frequency to the power $-5/2$. Replacing Lean’s `q` by the paper’s $q-1$ displays the one-order difference.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Parent velocity gains one time derivative

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: All retained profiles and activation corrections admit one mixed-norm estimate on each actual selected hierarchy. From `hStrength : 2 ≤ strength`, the theorem chooses lower bounds for the radius exponent and initial frequency. For each fixed radius and time-order data it then chooses a loss exponent `e` and monotone order constants `K` before the construction, stage and reserve `H`. The stage still must satisfy `StageTimeBounds` and the explicit smallness inequality with frequency exponent $-1/12$. The loss exponent is independent of `H`.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: One parent power controls the mixed hierarchy

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: For fixed natural `e` and `q`, choose `E` uniformly for all `D ≥ 2` and nonnegative amplitudes `A ≤ D^e`. Then the reciprocal amplitude with initial value `D^4` is at most `D^E`. Induction follows its polynomial recurrence; the successor exponent can be taken as `e+2*E+1`. This theorem controls a scalar amplitude rather than a reciprocal field.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: The reciprocal amplitude has a fixed parent-scale power

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: The selected transverse solver bounds an oscillatory level by its oscillatory source in the factorial time norms. The hypotheses include coefficient time bounds and a sufficiently large radius exponent. The conclusion applies to levels from two through the retained depth, with a coefficient depending on fixed orders and a parent-frequency power. It does not itself state the transverse differential equation or isolate a separate pressure estimate; those enter the surrounding solver construction.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Auxiliary bound for the transverse oscillatory levels

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: For fixed `q`, `E`, and nonnegative `C`, choose one cost array before the construction and stage. A radius exponent at least sixteen and the scheduled parent coefficient record give raw mixed bounds for the amplitude operator and pressure row, plus four coefficient time-seminorm bounds. They all use time order `q+1`, spatial slope sixteen, and common amplitude $D^{4E}$.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Bound the actual transverse and normalized pressure coefficients

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: Fix `q`, `E`, and a nonnegative cost array before choosing the construction or stage. If its radius exponent is at least sixteen and its actual parent coefficient bounds hold, the exact relay coefficients satisfy time budgets through `q+1` with amplitude $D^{\max(6E,a+2E)}$. The cost array is chosen independently of the stage; the exponent records the inner coefficient degree and inverse label radius separately.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: The selected relay coefficients share one parent exponent

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: For each selected step, there is a `TruncatedChildStage` using precisely the dyadic multiplier and cutoff scale `P.frequency (n+2)^5`, whose velocity and residual equal those of that step. The proof transports the existing cutoff along the schedule’s frequency identity and the stored symbol equality. It does not construct a second approximation or alter the cutoff.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Recover the dyadic cutoff used by the selected stage

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: There exists a cutoff-cost table, chosen before the schedule and construction, such that `TerminalCostBounds` for this table together with `TerminalGraphStep` yields the actual stages’ `TerminalTimeStep`. The Boolean row separates the stress-product cost from the ordinary cutoff tail. The proof uses the selected dyadic cutoff, absorbs fixed constants at sufficiently large stages, and combines the mean and tail halves of the mixed increment.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Choose fixed cutoff costs and finish the stage induction

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.le.text: For `m ≤ N` and a nonnegative array `C`, the common parent cost through `N` is at least `C m`. The proof extracts the `m`th summand and then includes the added one. This lets every parent derivative required by the finite graph reserve use the same scalar coefficient.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.le.summary: The parent reserve cost dominates every included order

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.le.text: With nonnegative row costs and `m ≤ H`, the cost of row `m` is bounded by the finite majorant through `H`. The proof isolates that summand and includes the initial one. This turns the separate source, mean, transverse, seed, and relay estimates into a common coefficient `K H`.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.le.summary: Every included hierarchy row fits the majorant

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po.text: The mixed profile estimates give polynomial bounds for the physical approximate velocity, residual and mean. The inputs include the derivative reserves `hReserve` and `hActivationReserve`, a bound for the fixed graph cost, parent mixed jets, coframe bounds and the small activation weight `hEnvelope`. The conclusion supplies both `PolynomialApproximationTimeBounds` and each admissible `PolynomialMeanTimeBound`. The powers depend on the fixed time and spatial orders; the frequency separation is used later to turn them into the final small estimates.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po.summary: Mixed profile bounds give the physical time estimates

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po.text: From the actual parent jets, coframe bounds, four profile estimates, switch-envelope smallness, and one full cost bounded by the parent frequency, obtain polynomial bounds for the uncut velocity, residual, and mean. The old-wave condition absorbs spatial oscillatory costs into child-frequency powers. The velocity/residual exponent is `terminalGraphReadoutPower q B E`; the mean exponent additionally contains `9*(a+1)*(m+1+q)` and may depend on fixed spatial order.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po.summary: Convert the selected profile bounds to Eulerian estimates

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.text: For the actual selected hierarchy, this theorem combines supplied coefficient rows, lower-time-order parent residual and mean estimates, leading-wave and switch bounds, transverse bounds, completion bounds, and relay bounds. It requires `K,L ≥ 1` and `L^6 * freq^(-1/12) ≤ 1`. The output is `ScheduledMixedProfileBounds` at the same `q` and reserve `H`; no new profiles or stage sequence are selected.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.summary: Assemble the mixed estimates on one selected hierarchy

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.text: This is the selected parent’s transported label wave vector divided by `P.frequency (n+2)`. The carrier comes from the exact selected child step, while the flow belongs to its parent. The index distinction matters: the parent scale is at `n+1`, but the carrier is normalized by the new child frequency. No new wave vector is chosen here.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.summary: The transported covector normalized at the child frequency

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.text: The actual selected step supplies bounds for scaled coframe rows, the scaled phase coefficient and the transported parent residual. Coefficients use one more time order than the residual. Under the parent coefficient bounds and the radius restriction, the residual keeps its child-frequency factor $\lambda^{-5/2}$; the fast coefficient retains its $\lambda^{3/2}$ factor. Fixed-order constants and powers of the parent scale remain explicit for later absorption by the schedule.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.summary: Auxiliary coefficient and residual source bounds

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: Given `ScheduledMixedProfileBounds` with recurrence loss $(\mu^9)^e$, this theorem produces the four graph-input estimates with common factor $\mu^{54e}$. The reserve assumptions include `depth+q+1+3*depth ≤ H` and the switch’s extra derivative. The mean uses the sixth loss power exactly; oscillation and activation use only the second, and the tail needs no additional loss.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: Put all four profile bounds under one parent power

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: Applies the stored successor function to the tip and certified prefix found in the actual construction trace at index `n`. The result retains the selected hierarchy for the next later stage, whose sequence index is `n + 2`. This avoids retrieving an unrelated successor that merely satisfies the same abstract estimates.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: The construction trace recovers its selected later hierarchy

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: For each actual selected step, subtracting the parent velocity and the oscillation from the child velocity gives exactly the uncut mean plus the cutoff error. The only input is `c : ScheduledEulerConstruction P` and the stage index `n`. Lean’s child is `n + 2`, its parent `n + 1`. This identity ties the estimates to the same fields that generated the common sequence, so the mean and tail bounds apply to the correction appearing in Auxiliary Lemma 1.2.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: The correction equals the mean plus the cutoff error

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: For the oscillation of actual stage `n+2`, every fixed Eulerian time jet is continuous on that stage’s closed slab in the spatial half-Hölder norm of order `m`. The proof rewrites the stage oscillation as the selected approximation’s oscillation, then uses its smoothness and periodicity. It claims no uniform-in-stage bound or terminal limiting behavior by itself.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: The selected oscillation has continuous mixed spatial norms

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: The residual of stage `n+2` equals the residual of the exact selected cutoff. This equality retains the pressure choice entering the momentum residual, through the scheduled construction’s stored identities. It prevents applying the auxiliary residual estimate to an unrelated truncated field with the same scale.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: The stage residual is the chosen cutoff residual

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: Every time derivative of a selected cutoff velocity and residual is continuous in the spatial supremum norm. The corresponding correction is continuous in each spatial half-Hölder norm. The input `c : ScheduledEulerConstruction P` supplies the actual smooth periodic fields, and `n q m` select the stage and orders. Lean numbers this child stage `n + 2`. This theorem supplies the continuity component in Auxiliary Lemmas 1.2 and 1.3; it does not state their quantitative bounds.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: Continuity of the auxiliary time derivatives

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: For the fixed scheduled construction, the velocity at stage `n+2` is exactly the cutoff velocity attached to `selectedStep n`. This is a function equality, not merely a common estimate or agreement on the slab. It ensures later time-derivative bounds apply to the same stage sequence used in the terminal limit.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: The stage velocity is the chosen cutoff velocity

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.text: At a later index `n + 2`, the oscillation stored in the abstract stage sequence is exactly the oscillation of the selected approximation. This equality is inherited from the scheduled step record. It allows support and derivative estimates for the concrete oscillation to pass to the common-sequence and terminal arguments.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.summary: The sequence keeps the selected oscillatory increment

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.text: Identifies the residual of sequence stage `n + 2` with the selected cutoff residual by rewriting both its velocity and pressure. The equality uses the actual momentum-residual definition. It ensures that later residual estimates concern the stage appearing in the convergence argument, rather than a separate field with a matching bound.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.summary: The sequence residual is the selected cutoff residual

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.text: At sequence index `n + 2`, the constructed stage velocity equals the cutoff velocity of the selected later hierarchy. This is a projection of the successor's stored equality field. It is used when estimates proved for the explicit finite hierarchy must be applied to the abstract stage sequence.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.summary: The sequence velocity is the selected cutoff velocity

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: The active-slab factorial time norm applies the amplitude seminorm after differentiating each selected profile. The data `c : ScheduledEulerConstruction P` and the stage index `j` fix the label scale, phase width and actual central weight. Positivity and continuity of that weight come from the selected step. Thus derivatives act on the profile while division by the central amplitude occurs inside the subsequent spatial seminorm; the amplitude weight is not differentiated.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The oscillatory time norm divides by the amplitude afterwards

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: The parent cost is one plus the sum of `C j` through order `N`. With a nonnegative input array it is at least one and dominates every included derivative cost. This converts the parent’s order-dependent Bernstein estimates into one coefficient for a graph readout at a fixed finite reserve.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: A common parent derivative cost through the reserve

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: If every entry of `C` is nonnegative, `terminalGraphParentCost C N` is at least one for every reserve `N`. The result follows by adding a nonnegative finite sum to one. It is used to keep the scalar graph-conversion factors nonnegative and to compare powers of those factors.

This scalar multiplies the number of retained levels `1,…,d` by the depth-`d` hierarchy level constant. It is the common fixed factor in the mean and oscillatory profile sums before their frequency powers are attached. The definition does not assert that any particular hierarchy satisfies those estimates.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The finite sum cost for retained profiles

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: Assuming eventual polynomial bounds for both the selected approximation and its mean, this theorem absorbs each fixed old-parent power into the next frequency. In the mean branch it first obtains $\mu^B\le\tfrac12\lambda^{3/2}$ and then combines this with $\lambda^{-5/2}$ to get $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. Both derivative orders are fixed before the stage tends to infinity. The input bounds are implications from the previous stage’s time estimates; the result does not establish those premises or cover every construction satisfying only the generic paper statement. Scheduled frequencies are positive and at least one, as required for the real-power identities.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: Frequency separation absorbs the old parent powers

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: The order majorant is one plus the sum of `rowCost m` through the finite reserve `H`. When the rows are nonnegative it is at least one, monotone in `H`, and dominates every included row. It collects the fixed analytic constants before the schedule compares them with the old frequency.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: One majorant covers all finite derivative costs

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: If all row costs are nonnegative, their finite majorant is at least one at every reserve `H`. The proof only uses nonnegativity of the finite sum. This supplies the lower bound needed for hierarchy constants and powers of the common analytic cost; it gives no size bound relative to a frequency.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The hierarchy order majorant starts above one

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: For a nonnegative row-cost array, `terminalHierarchyOrderMajorant rowCost` is monotone in the reserve. Enlarging `H` adds only nonnegative terms to the finite sum. This permits one schedule threshold to cover nested sets of derivative orders without revising constants already included at a lower reserve.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: Increasing the derivative reserve increases the cost majorant

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: This definition measures the actual selected hierarchy with different time orders for profiles and mean forcing. Retained means use the unweighted norm at order $q$, while mean forcing uses order $q-1$. Oscillatory profiles and sources use the amplitude-weighted norm at order $q$. The underlying profiles, completion switch and parent residual all come from the same selected step. This is the choice of measurement used by the auxiliary recurrence, not an estimate.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: Auxiliary means use one fewer forcing derivative
