TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: The graph-conversion cost is evaluated at reserve `d+q+1`, using the parent Bernstein majorant, finite profile-sum constants, the remainder factor, and the switch factor `2*K^2`. This assembles the full scalar product that the enlarged threshold must dominate. It leaves the remaining parent-frequency exponent separate, so increasing depth changes the cost row rather than that exponent.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: One threshold cost for the entire graph conversion

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: Using the hierarchy level constant `C`, this factor is `2*K*(C+1)^2` times one plus the relevant counts of omitted interaction pairs. It is the scalar coefficient in the unweighted remainder estimate at the next hierarchy level. Its parameters are depth and the fixed analytic cost; the child-frequency decay remains outside the definition.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The fixed scalar multiplying the finite-depth remainder

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: The full-slab factorial time norm uses the unweighted spatial seminorm at the selected label and phase scales. The inputs `c`, `j`, `q` and `m` fix the common construction, stage, time order and spatial order. Its definition passes `unweightedSeminorm False` to `timeJetSeminorm`, so the mean is not divided by the central amplitude. The argument `False` selects the supremum version of the finite spatial norm, without a Hölder quotient.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The mean time norm has no amplitude weight

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: Assume eventual conditional estimates for each selected cutoff: parent time bounds through `q` imply child velocity/residual bounds through `q+1`, and the uncut mean plus cutoff tail satisfies the corresponding mixed increment bound. The theorem rewrites these estimates using the exact stage identities and shifts the index once. The result is a `TerminalTimeStep` for the fixed physical sequence.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: Transfer selected cutoff estimates to the common stage induction

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerStep.text: Stores the selected later input over a given tip, its scheduled physical stage and a certified inductive successor. The cutoff symbol is dyadic. Equality fields connect the successor's velocity, pressure and wave oscillation to those of the stored hierarchy, so changing to the abstract recurrence does not lose their mathematical identity.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerStep.summary: A later hierarchy is attached to its exact preceding tip

TorusEuler.ScheduledLaterPhysicalWindowB.text: This proposition bundles a normalized window of length at least two, its exact clock endpoint and interval mapping, the two finite-comparison smallness inequalities, and a positive smaller target ratio. It also places the crossing search horizon within the first physical half and the full normalized interval. These are conditions for applying the crossing theorem.
TorusEuler.ScheduledLaterPhysicalWindowB.summary: The scheduled window carries all comparison and crossing conditions

TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalStage.text: For a fixed parent and the same physical approximation with its qualitative properties, this structure stores one Fourier symbol and truncation together with its cutoff bounds, physical wave bounds, pullback jets, and central derivative estimate. Its numerical fields relate these constants, radius, carrier, and exponent to the common schedule. It supplies evidence needed by stage closure; the record does not manufacture that evidence.
TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalStage.summary: One approximation and cutoff share every closing estimate

TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalStage.of_act.text: This constructor assembles the scheduled physical stage from its actual approximation, numerical budget and Fourier-truncated child. The cutoff radius in the child type is $(\lambda_i^{K(q_{i+1})})^5=\lambda_{i+1}^5$, using the parameter recurrence. The other inputs certify the residual, velocity, mean, pressure and central-gradient bounds. The schedule tie selects only this explicit cutoff scale; it does not treat the constructor as a separate existence theorem for all its inputs.
TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalStage.of_act.summary: The scheduled child uses the prescribed fifth-power cutoff

TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalVelocityBoun.text: A proposition bundling the cutoff-depth velocity size, oscillation supremum bound, low-order mean Hölder bounds and central derivative-error bound for one physical approximation. The center estimate is restricted to the active slab; the other estimates hold on the full slab. The two scalar parameters are the already chosen step and mean costs.
TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalVelocityBoun.summary: The actual velocity carries four scheduled estimates

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.text: Records the central wave, carrier pullback, positive normalized weight, envelope inactivity, relay identities and leading-profile bounds for one actual physical approximation. Its active interval is $[t_0,T]$ with $0\le t_0<T$, sharing the parent's right endpoint and possibly starting at zero. These are the common inputs used to estimate first and later waves through the same measured levels.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.summary: The same central wave measures every selected profile

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.exi.text: Constructs a `ScheduledPhysicalStage` with the dyadic symbol from one selected seed and its measured hierarchy levels. The hypotheses include coefficient bounds, a numerical budget, parent Bernstein estimates, a cutoff witness, the residual bound and a one-sided pressure increment bound. The proof derives velocity and flow estimates from those same levels and installs the same cutoff, preserving the identity of the physical fields.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.exi.summary: Measured profiles and their estimates produce one scheduled stage

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.gam.text: Abbreviates the time weight $\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ of the central vector stored in a selected physical seed. The abbreviation preserves that exact function when passed to measured levels. Its positivity, continuity and upper bound belong to the seed record on the active slab, not to the abbreviation by itself.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.gam.summary: The selected seed uses its normalized central amplitude

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.lab.text: Shows that the label covector at activation has norm equal to the child frequency. The proof identifies the transported label covector with the seed's central covector using its pullback identity and wave equation, then applies the normalization stored in the seed. The equality concerns activation, not every point or time.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.lab.summary: The transported carrier has the prescribed activation length

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.mea.text: Forms the measured hierarchy levels from the approximation's operators, profiles, completion switch and parent residual, using the seed's own radius, phase width and time weight. The argument `hf` supplies nonnegative frequency. This abbreviation ensures recurrence estimates and physical readouts quantify over the same levels rather than independently chosen bounds.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.mea.summary: The measured levels use the actual hierarchy fields

TorusEuler.SpatialHolderHalf.text:
Require C-to-order-m differentiability and bounded uniform and half-Holder increment ranges for every iterated derivative through order m. This is the lifted C-to-order-m-and-one-half regularity predicate, not an existence theorem for derivatives or inverse operators.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate explicitly requires genuine differentiability and bounded supremum and increment ranges through the stated order. At order zero it is continuity plus bounded half-Holder behavior; it does not assert periodicity.
TorusEuler.SpatialHolderHalf.summary: The lifted spatial Holder regularity class

TorusEuler.SpatialJetTuple.text: This is the finite dependent tuple of bounded spatial jets of orders zero through `m`, indexed by `Fin (m + 1)`. It supplies a normed input space for bilinear momentum maps. The components are stored separately, so an arbitrary tuple need not satisfy the differential relations of one underlying function.
TorusEuler.SpatialJetTuple.summary: All spatial derivative orders through a fixed level

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.text:
Period-one functions on the Euclidean lift of the three-dimensional torus. The condition is $f(x+n)=f(x)$ for every integer vector $n$ and every point $x$. The value type `α` is arbitrary, so the same definition applies to velocities, pressures and derivatives. `latticeVector` converts the three integer coordinates to `Vec3`. Periodicity is a hypothesis or a property to prove; this definition alone places no regularity condition on the function.

Default-value audit (b4): The predicate uses equality under every integer translation. It has no analytic default value. It is true for constants, including zero, and does not imply continuity, differentiability or boundedness; those must be supplied at each later use.

Default-value audit (b5): This only asserts invariance under integer translations. Constant functions, including zero, satisfy it; continuity and smoothness do not follow from periodicity.

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.existsUniqu.text: Every function on Euclidean labels that satisfies `SpatiallyPeriodic` factors uniquely through the quotient map to the unit three-torus. The codomain is an arbitrary type, so the statement asserts no continuity or integrability. Periodicity guarantees that choosing different representatives of a torus point produces the same value.
TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.existsUniqu.summary: A periodic lift descends uniquely to the torus

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.exists_cont.text: A continuous spatially periodic lift descends to a continuous torus field.
TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.exists_cont.summary: A periodic continuous lift descends to the torus

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.fderiv.text: If a field is spatially periodic and differentiable everywhere, its Fréchet derivative is periodic under the same lattice translations. The differentiability hypothesis `hf` ensures that `fderiv` is the genuine derivative throughout. This is used to extend convergence of periodic derivative fields from one centered cell to the entire lift.
TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.fderiv.summary: A differentiable periodic field has periodic spatial derivative

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.gradient.text: For a spatially periodic scalar pressure, global differentiability makes the gradient spatially periodic as well. The proof converts the periodic Fréchet derivative to a gradient through the real inner-product duality. This supplies the period condition needed to pass from uniform gradient convergence on the centered cell to the whole space.
TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.gradient.summary: A differentiable periodic pressure has periodic gradient

TorusEuler.TerminalCostBounds.text: This predicate requires every listed cost to be at most `P.frequency i` in absolute value when its time order and depth are at most $S=7K(P.\mathrm{order}(i+2))$ and its spatial order is at most $S+\mathrm{reserve}(q,d)$. It quantifies over all stage indices and rows. The cost function and reserve are supplied arguments; this definition records their required estimates and does not construct a schedule satisfying them.
TorusEuler.TerminalCostBounds.summary: Fixed order costs bounded by the previous frequency

TorusEuler.TerminalGraphCostBounds.text: Requires graph costs with time order `q`, parent exponent `A`, and depth `d` to lie below the previous frequency when both `q` and `A` and the depth fit $S=7K(P.\mathrm{order}(i+2))$. The spatial order may additionally use `reserve (max q A) d`. This extends `TerminalCostBounds` by tracking the parent velocity exponent separately; it remains a proposition whose estimates must be supplied.
TorusEuler.TerminalGraphCostBounds.summary: Graph costs fit the common scheduled threshold

TorusEuler.TerminalGraphCostBounds.event.text: From `TerminalGraphCostBounds`, proves an eventual estimate uniformly over all rows and all spatial orders up to $\max(m_0,\mathrm{stepDepth}(i)+q+2)$. The time order `q`, parent exponent `A`, and baseline spatial order `m₀` are fixed before the stage index tends to infinity. The scheduled slow-order reserve ensures their depth and order demands eventually lie in the common threshold range.
TorusEuler.TerminalGraphCostBounds.event.summary: Every fixed graph order eventually fits the selected depth

TorusEuler.TerminalMeanParentInverseData.text: Packages fixed-time solenoidal inverses and the mixed recovery inverse for one supplied `rec`. The fields identify the operators being inverted, bound their inverse norms, record kinetic Lipschitz and supremum caps, and bound the combined recovery budget by $D^p$. The fixed-time inverse also has the direct bound $D^p$. This is data with obligations, not an existence theorem.
TorusEuler.TerminalMeanParentInverseData.summary: Two actual mean inverses with a common parent bound

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.text: Requires $\|D_x^n\partial_t^i f(t,x)\|\le C(n)A D^{pn}$ for every $i\le q$, every spatial order $n$, and all points on the closed time slab. The time derivative is `slabTimeJet`, so the spatial point is held fixed. The amplitude `A` and slope `p` are independent of `n`; `C n` may vary with spatial order. This proposition contains bounds only, with no smoothness or sign assumptions built in.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.summary: Mixed derivatives with a fixed spatial growth rate

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.add.text: Adds the mixed bounds for jointly smooth `f` and `g` on `a < b`. The inputs share time order, slope, scale, and amplitude, while their constants may differ. The sum has constant `C n + C' n`. Smoothness justifies the time and spatial derivative sum identities, after which the triangle inequality gives the estimate.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.add.summary: Add mixed bounds with a common amplitude and rate

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.apply_c.text: Applies a fixed continuous linear map `L` to a jointly smooth field with a mixed bound on `a < b`. The new bound keeps the same amplitude and spatial slope and replaces each constant by $\|L\|C(n)$. Time differentiation commutes with `L`, and its operator norm controls every spatial derivative of the output.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.apply_c.summary: A bounded linear readout preserves the mixed growth rate

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.bilinea.text: For jointly smooth `f` and `g` on `a < b`, combines their mixed bounds through time order `q` under the stated nonnegativity hypotheses. Applying the fixed bilinear map `B` multiplies amplitudes to $AA'$ and preserves the slope `p`; the constant becomes `terminalMixedProductCost`. Spatial derivative orders split across the factors, so their powers recombine as $D^{pn}$. The docstring says amplitudes are added, but the theorem's conclusion correctly multiplies them.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.bilinea.summary: Multiply amplitudes while retaining the spatial growth slope

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.congr.text: Transfers a mixed bound from `f` to `g` when `hEq` identifies their values for every time in the closed slab and every spatial point. Within-time derivatives agree on that slab, and the resulting spatial functions are equal. No equality outside the time interval and no separate regularity hypothesis are required for this congruence statement.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.congr.summary: Transfer mixed bounds across equality on the slab

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.const_s.text: Given a mixed jet bound and joint smoothness on a nondegenerate slab, multiplying the field by `r` replaces amplitude `A` by $\|r\|A$. The assumptions include nonnegative `D,A` and cost sequence. The proof passes through the continuous linear scalar map and bounds its norm, preserving the same derivative-order cost array and spatial slope.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.const_s.summary: A fixed scalar changes only the mixed-bound amplitude

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.materia.text: Given mixed bounds for `f` through `q+1` and `U` through `q`, bounds $\partial_t f+U\cdot\nabla f$ through `q`. Joint smoothness on `a < b` and all listed nonnegativity assumptions are required. The spatial slope remains `p`, while the amplitude becomes $A(1+D^pA_0)$. The new constant combines the pure time derivative with the spatially shifted bilinear advection term.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.materia.summary: One material derivative spends one time order

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_am.text: Given an existing mixed bound, replaces its amplitude `A` by `A'` when `A ≤ A'`. The hypotheses `hD` and `hC` make the scale powers and order constants nonnegative, so multiplying preserves this comparison. No sign assumption on the old amplitude is stated separately. The spatial slope and the range of time derivatives remain unchanged.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_am.summary: Enlarge the amplitude in every mixed derivative bound

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_co.text: Replaces `C n` by the pointwise larger `C' n` in a mixed bound. The hypotheses `hD : 0 ≤ D` and `hA : 0 ≤ A` ensure that the shared multiplier is nonnegative. All time orders through `q` and the same spatial slope remain available. This theorem compares supplied bounds rather than estimating any new derivative.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_co.summary: Enlarge the constants for each spatial order

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_or.text: Restricts an existing mixed bound from time order `q` to `q'` under `hq : q' ≤ q`. The spatial slope, amplitude, constants, and closed slab stay fixed. It uses only the inclusion of the permitted time indices, so no positivity or smoothness assumption is added to those already present in the input predicate.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_or.summary: Retain fewer time derivatives from a mixed bound

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_sl.text: For `D ≥ 1`, a mixed bound with slope `p` also holds with any `p' ≥ p`. Nonnegativity of the amplitude and order constants permits comparison of $D^{pn}$ and $D^{p'n}$ at every spatial order. This is a deliberately coarser estimate, used to place different coefficient families under one common slope.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_sl.summary: Increase the spatial growth slope of a mixed bound

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.of_pare.text: If each spatial derivative of a fixed time jet costs at most `C n * A * μ^(5*n)`, then for `μ ≥ 1` it also satisfies a mixed bound with scale `μ^9` and spatial slope one. Nonnegative amplitude and costs permit enlarging the power. This is a comparison of supplied bounds, not a new regularity theorem.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.of_pare.summary: Fit parent Bernstein bounds into the coefficient calculus

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.of_zero.text: Builds a mixed bound at time order zero from bounds on all spatial derivatives of `g` on the slab. The hypothesis named `h` supplies exactly these spatial inequalities. Since the only allowed time index is zero, `slabTimeJet_zero` reduces the conclusion to those inequalities. This is not a theorem asserting that the field itself vanishes.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.of_zero.summary: Spatial estimates supply the zeroth time order

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.restric.text: A mixed coefficient bound on `[a,b]` transfers to `[c,d]` when both intervals have positive length, the latter is contained in the former, and the underlying field is jointly smooth on the larger slab. The time jets defined with either closed interval agree on the smaller one, including its endpoints. The amplitude, spatial slope, and cost array remain unchanged.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.restric.summary: Restrict mixed jets to a smaller nondegenerate time slab

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.scaledA.text: Assume a smooth field has `TerminalMixedJetBound` with amplitude $D^e$ and spatial slope $p$. If `D ≥ 1`, $\ell\ge0$, and $\ell D^p\le1$, scaling labels by $\ell$ removes the spatial factor from active time derivatives. For $i\le q$, `PhaseJetBound` through $n$ is controlled by $(\sum_{m\le n}C(m))D^e$. Both the full and active intervals have positive length.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.scaledA.summary: The label radius absorbs the fixed derivative slope

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.slabTim.text: For a fixed continuous linear map `L` and a jointly smooth field `g` on `a < b`, taking any closed-slab time jet commutes with applying `L`. The conclusion is pointwise at `t ∈ Icc a b` and any spatial point. The map is independent of time, so this statement has no Leibniz terms involving derivatives of `L`.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.slabTim.summary: Time derivatives commute with a fixed bounded linear map

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.spaceDe.text: For a jointly smooth field on a nondegenerate slab `a < b`, a mixed bound for `f` gives one for its spatial Fréchet derivative. The spatial slope stays `p`, the amplitude becomes $AD^p$, and the constant at order `n` becomes `C (n+1)`. The proof commutes time and space derivatives; the regularity assumptions give those derivatives their classical meaning at the slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.spaceDe.summary: One spatial derivative multiplies the amplitude by its rate

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.timeDer.text: An input bound through time order `q+1` gives a bound through `q` for the within-time derivative of the same field. The amplitude, spatial slope, and spatial constants do not change. The proof is the iteration identity for `slabTimeJet`; no extra smoothness is needed for this formal identity, although later applications use jointly smooth fields.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.timeDer.summary: Spend one time order without changing the spatial rate

TorusEuler.Theorem11.text:
The existence part of Theorem 1.1. Its four witnesses are initial velocity $u_0$, a real terminal time $T$, velocity $u$ and pressure $p$, with requirements collected in the singularity-witness predicate. The real type excludes an infinite lifespan, and positivity comes from the Euler-solution predicate. This proposition does not quantify over other maximal solutions; that uniqueness clause belongs to the current Paper statement. Fields are periodic functions on the Euclidean lift.

Default-value audit (b4): Existential quantification is over actual smooth data and a positive finite time through EulerSingularityWitness, not over arbitrary total derivatives alone. No new partial analytic operation is introduced by this wrapper. The guards and limitations are exactly those of the witness; absence of the uniqueness conjunct is a scope difference, not a junk-value effect.

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.text:
The data of one frequency-truncated child: the actual cutoff velocity, its smooth mean-zero Poisson pressure and the exact residual identities. The fields `cutoff`, `mean_zero_pressure` and `poisson` identify these objects, while `smooth_velocity`, `odd_velocity`, `divergence_free` and `velocity_band` record their properties. These fields are requirements on an instance, not proofs that an instance exists. `nonempty_truncatedChildStage` constructs one from a smooth periodic approximate solution.

Default-value audit (b5): This records a truncated velocity and a pressure together with smoothness, normalization, Poisson and residual equations. It is not an unchecked choice of pressure; existence and estimates are proved separately.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.summary: The truncated velocity and its normalized Poisson pressure

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.CutoffBou.text: Bundles all spatial tail estimates through depth `P`, the order-two tail estimate, the order-one true residual estimate, and the order-zero pressure-Hessian difference estimate. All are pointwise in time on the child slab. A common pair of constants controls the residual and pressure; the error uses the spatial norm of that time slice.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.CutoffBou.summary: The cutoff tail residual and pressure estimates together

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.PulledBac.text: Records joint smoothness of the parent-coframe pullback after adding the actual cutoff tail. The oscillatory part has a scaled jet bound through order two of size $B \cdot  D^p \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{-5/4}$; the phase mean has a bound through order one of size $B \cdot  D^p \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. These measured hypotheses feed the child-flow estimate.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.PulledBac.summary: Measured jets of the corrected pulled back profile

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.PulledBac.text: Builds corrected pulled-back jet bounds from the uncut profile and the actual cutoff estimate. The phase oscillation is unchanged because the tail is phase independent. Its contribution to the mean costs $\max\{D,D^2+D_1\}\,\varepsilon$; `hBudget` explicitly absorbs this together with the uncut mean bound. Smoothness and first coframe-derivative control are supplied as hypotheses.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.PulledBac.summary: The cutoff tail changes only the pulled back mean

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.cutoffTai.text: Combines certified cutoff bounds with smooth solenoidal approximate velocity to show that the actual tail is jointly smooth, periodic and solenoidal on the slab. Its order-two half-Hölder norm is at most the current frequency to power minus five-halves, provided the next-frequency error budget and frequency ordering hold. The smallness is an assumption-backed estimate on the actual difference field.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.cutoffTai.summary: The cutoff tail satisfies the child flow assumptions

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.divergenc.text: For a positive slab and a time in it, shows that the actual child residual has zero divergence at every spatial point. The child record supplies the Poisson equation, smoothness and velocity solenoidality needed by the general cancellation theorem. This is a derived property of the constructed pressure and velocity.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.divergenc.summary: The constructed pressure cancels residual divergence

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_ch.text: Produces a flow for the actual cutoff velocity with deformation bounded by $\Gamma \cdot  D^b \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{1/4}$. Its hypotheses include the physical profile identity, incompressible parent and profile, cutoff-tail control, corrected profile jet bounds, and the scale smallness condition $\Gamma \cdot  D^b \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{-1/12} \le  1$. The proof applies the scaled-flow theorem to the same cutoff tail, then rewrites the velocity identity.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_ch.summary: The actual cutoff velocity has controlled deformation

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_cu.text: For a fixed smooth normalized cutoff symbol, chooses a nonnegative constant `C` before choosing the depth. For each `P ≥ 2` it then chooses a nonnegative `K`, uniformly over all positive slabs, scales at least one and admissible approximate stages. The actual approximate momentum equation and solenoidality supply the pressure estimate. These quantifiers prevent the residual constant from secretly depending on expansion depth.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_cu.summary: One residual constant works across all expansion depths

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_de.text: Chooses one threshold independent of the child. Above it, a child cut off at the fifth power of its frequency, with the prescribed velocity and residual bounds on a positive slab, has spatial derivative norm at most frequency to the ninth power and within-slab time derivative of that spatial derivative at most frequency to the eighteenth power.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_de.summary: Large cutoff parents satisfy the two low derivative estimates

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.odd_resid.text: On a positive slab with nonnegative cutoff radius, derives oddness of the true child residual at every slab time. The proof first obtains the matching finite-band projected data and then applies the parity theorem. Thus the residual symmetry follows from the same child velocity and pressure that define its momentum equation.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.odd_resid.summary: The actual truncated child has an odd residual

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.periodic_.text: For a time belonging to the child slab, proves spatial periodicity of its actual momentum residual. The within-slab time derivative respects the velocity periodicity throughout the interval, while spatial derivatives use smooth periodic slices. Pressure periodicity is taken from the same stage record at that time.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.periodic_.summary: The child residual is periodic on its slab

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.periodic_.text: Proves spatial periodicity of the physical child velocity for every real time, including times outside the certified slab. This follows from the quotient map and the stored torus field. The unconditional periodicity statement should not be extended to smoothness or the momentum equation outside the slab.

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.phaseJetB.text: Add two first-order bounds for differentiable profiles.

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.pressureH.text: An operator-norm bound for $D^2(p-q)$ gives an upper quadratic-form bound for $D^2p$ relative to $D^2q$. The assumptions `hp`, `hq` give smooth pressures, `hpper`, `hqper` give periodicity and `hB` bounds the half-Hölder norm of the Hessian difference. The proof evaluates that norm bound at a point and uses Cauchy–Schwarz. This is the final passage from the pressure-error estimate to the one-sided bound needed by the next parent.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.pressureH.summary: A pressure difference norm gives an upper Hessian bound

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual.text: The residual $R_u$ computed from the truncated velocity and its selected pressure. For `s : TruncatedChildStage T Λ ψ V RV`, the definition is `momentumResidual (Icc 0 T) s.velocity s.pressure`. Thus it uses the physical time derivative on the closed interval and the actual pressure. The later projected and Fourier identities concern this same residual; they do not define a replacement forcing.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual.summary: The momentum residual of the truncated velocity

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual_.text: For a positive slab and nonnegative cutoff radius, constructs torus representatives of the child residual and its advection at a slab time. It records residual Fourier support within $4\Lambda$, exact physical representation, and the projected within-slab derivative equation. These same representatives feed the later Bernstein and low-derivative estimates.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual_.summary: The child exposes its actual finite-band evolution data

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.scheduled.text: Under the listed schedule inequalities, exact child-flow deformation, parent and oscillation bounds, correction and cutoff budgets, and approximate-pressure comparison, proves the child velocity and flow bounds, the next-frequency residual bound, and the cumulative one-sided pressure-Hessian bound. The pressure conclusion controls quadratic forms from above; it is not a two-sided operator-norm estimate.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.scheduled.summary: The actual child inherits velocity residual and pressure bounds

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.scheduled.text: Assumes an exact split of the approximate velocity into parent, oscillation and mean, together with scheduled mean bounds and the cutoff error budget. Through each order `m ≤ q`, bounds the child minus parent minus oscillation by the inverse child frequency. The depth must cover `q`, and frequency and constant inequalities are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.scheduled.summary: The remaining child increment fits the inverse frequency budget

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: An approximate-velocity bound with exponent $2+\psi$ gives a pointwise cutoff-velocity bound with exponent $3+\psi$. The stage uses scale `freq ^ 5`. The hypotheses require smooth periodic velocity, `hf : 2 ≤ freq`, a time in the closed slab, `hSize` for the uncut time derivative, and `hCost` controlling the cutoff constant. This is the step that supplies the new velocity exponent in Auxiliary Lemma 1.3; the exponent is independent of the spatial point.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The cutoff velocity has a fixed time-derivative power

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: For a truncated child with positive `T,Λ`, assume the slab identity `hSplit : V = U + O + M`, smooth `V,M`, and periodic `V`. At a slab time, `m ≤ depth` and `hMjet` give the child's omitted increment spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ regularity and a norm bound by the mean jet norm plus the order-`depth` Fourier tail bound for `V`. The exact within-time jet is used at the endpoints. Separate smoothness of `U,O` is unnecessary because the combined difference is rewritten first.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: Split the omitted increment into mean and cutoff tail

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: The correction after cutoff has norm at most $\lambda^{-1}$ when its mean part and cutoff tail satisfy the required bounds. `hSplit` identifies the uncut velocity as parent plus oscillation plus mean. The remaining hypotheses supply smoothness, periodicity, the cutoff scale $\lambda^5$, the derivative reserve `hD`, the cutoff cost and the bounds `hVrate` and `hMrate`. The theorem adds two contributions bounded by $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$, retaining spatial half-Hölder regularity.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The two half-bounds give the full correction bound

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: Every time derivative of the selected cutoff residual equals the Leray projection of the cutoff input residual plus a differentiated quadratic cutoff stress. The stress is expanded as a finite binomial sum of time derivatives of the approximate velocity. The hypotheses identify continuous torus representatives and give smoothness on the positive closed slab. At time order zero, expanding the stress yields the residual formula used in the auxiliary paper.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: Time derivatives of the cutoff residual identity

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: The Eulerian time derivative of a cutoff velocity equals the same fixed spatial cutoff applied to the corresponding time derivative of the uncut velocity. The data `g` and `hg` identify continuous torus representatives of all time derivatives, while `hV` gives joint smoothness and `hT` a positive slab. The scale and symbol are fixed in time. This is the commutation needed for the auxiliary truncation difference; it does not itself estimate the resulting tail.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: Time derivatives commute with the selected frequency cutoff

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: The order-$q$ time derivative of the cutoff error has spatial half-Hölder norm bounded by the higher spatial norm of the same time derivative. The decay factor is $\Lambda^{m-P}$ and the constant is `terminalCutoffTailCost depth`. The hypotheses give smooth periodic uncut velocity, positive time and cutoff scale, `hm : m ≤ depth`, and a time inside the slab. This is a tail estimate for the actual `TruncatedChildStage`, rather than an estimate for an independently chosen field.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The frequency tail after Eulerian time differentiation

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.smooth_re.text: On a positive closed slab, the child record supplies joint smoothness of velocity and pressure, and the actual momentum formula then gives joint smoothness of its residual. Positivity permits differentiation within the time interval at endpoints. This statement certifies the true residual rather than an independently chosen smooth proxy.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.smooth_re.summary: The true child residual is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.truncatio.text:
The slice form of the truncation error in (5.56).

Default-value audit (b5): Negative integer powers of Λ are totalized at zero. The actual truncation estimates use positive Λ, finite spatial norms and the required order P.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.truncatio.summary: The velocity error caused by Fourier truncation

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.truncatio.text: At cutoff radius equal to the fifth power of the child frequency, uses depth six times the following exponent to bound the weighted truncation error by the next frequency to power minus five. It requires base scale at least two, positive exponent parameter, `K ≤ μ`, certified high regularity and the explicit full-depth size bound.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.truncatio.summary: Full expansion depth absorbs the cutoff constants

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.velocity.text: Defines the child velocity on Euclidean space by lifting its stored continuous torus velocity. This is the physical function on which gradients, material acceleration and the true momentum residual are evaluated. The definition exists at all real times, while the stage record certifies its analytic properties only on the closed slab.

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.velocity_.text: Identifies the Euclidean child velocity with the real Fourier cutoff of its own stored approximate torus velocity. This equality holds at every real time because the cutoff identity is a field of the stage record. Agreement of the approximate torus field with the original physical velocity is separately restricted to the slab.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.velocity_.summary: The physical child is the cutoff of its input

TorusEuler.UniformPhysicalEstimates.text: States that for every strength constant at least two, nonnegative envelope constant and requested radius floor, one can choose exponents, costs and an initial-frequency floor. Those choices then produce scheduled dyadic-cutoff stages for every admissible first or later input satisfying its numerical budget. This quantifier order is essential: the costs are uniform before the parameter schedule and stage are supplied.
TorusEuler.UniformPhysicalEstimates.summary: Uniform stage estimates are chosen before the schedule

TorusEuler.Vec3.text:
The paper’s real vector space ℝ³ is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3). A vector has coordinates indexed by 0, 1 and 2, while the paper numbers coordinates 1, 2 and 3. The Euclidean norm and inner product are built into this type; a space vector, a velocity value and a wave vector use the same type. This abbreviation does not impose periodicity or encode a quotient torus.

Default-value audit (b4): No partial analytic operation occurs. The three dimensional type is inhabited and has its usual nondegenerate Euclidean norm; there is no empty index set or variable dimension.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a concrete Euclidean space abbreviation. It contains zero vectors as well as nonzero ones; nonvanishing is always a separate wave hypothesis.

TorusEuler.Velocity.text:
A velocity field is a total function ℝ → Vec3 → Vec3. The first argument is time and the second is position, so u t x means u(t,x). Values outside the physical time interval exist in the type but are unconstrained by this abbreviation. Periodicity, smoothness and the Euler equation are supplied separately by IsEulerSolution.

Default-value audit (b4): The function type is unrestricted. It admits discontinuous, nonperiodic and zero fields. No derivative or norm is evaluated here; interpreting an arbitrary inhabitant as a classical Euler solution would require hypotheses not present in the abbreviation.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a completely unrestricted function type. It alone provides no regularity, periodicity, incompressibility or solution property.
TorusEuler.Velocity.summary: Velocity as a function of time and position

TorusEuler.abs_fixedOrderCost_le_thresho.text: Each cost is bounded in absolute value by the chosen threshold whenever its differentiation order and expansion depth are at most $7K(s)$. The hypotheses `hm` and `hp` are these two index bounds; `k : ι` chooses one member of the finite family. The proof bounds that summand by the total nonnegative sum in `fixedOrderThreshold`. It includes order and depth zero, as well as the positive orders used in the paper.
TorusEuler.abs_fixedOrderCost_le_thresho.summary: The threshold bounds every retained order and depth

TorusEuler.abs_oscillatoryPressureSlope_.text: For nonzero $\kappa$, the pressure-slope magnitude is bounded by $(\|f\|+2\|M\|\|V\|)/\|\kappa\|$. Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the two inner products in its numerator, cancelling one factor of the wave-vector norm. This is a pointwise algebraic estimate; integrating the slope and imposing phase normalization require additional hypotheses.
TorusEuler.abs_oscillatoryPressureSlope_.summary: The phase pressure slope loses one wave-vector factor

TorusEuler.abs_terminalGraphCost_le_enve.text: Bounds the absolute value of any graph cost at `(q,A,m,d)` by the envelope indexed by `max q A`. Both order indices lie in the corresponding finite ranges, and every other summand is nonnegative. This comparison is independent of any construction, frequency, or regularity assertion.
TorusEuler.abs_terminalGraphCost_le_enve.summary: A graph cost fits the envelope at its largest order

TorusEuler.absolutelyContinuousOnInterva.text: On a nonnegative-length interval, the anchored primitive of an interval-integrable velocity is absolutely continuous. This is stronger than ordinary continuity and permits integration by parts with other absolutely continuous paths. No pointwise continuity of the velocity is assumed, which is necessary for the weak endpoint formulation.
TorusEuler.absolutelyContinuousOnInterva.summary: An integrable velocity produces an absolutely continuous displacement

TorusEuler.activationGrowthRate_bounds.text: Bounds $c\mu^{1/4}\le\sigma\le C\mu^{1/4}L^2$ and $\pi\le\nu\le4\pi$ imply two explicit bounds for $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}$ at scale $\mu^{1/8}$. Lean assumes `hμ`, `hc`, and `hC` are positive and `hL : 0 ≤ L`. The constants are $\sqrt{2c\pi}$ and $\sqrt{8C\pi}$. Squaring reduces both conclusions to the assumed strength and coupling inequalities.
TorusEuler.activationGrowthRate_bounds.summary: The physical growth rate has the required scale

TorusEuler.activationLifetime_tail.text: If a nonnegative lifetime sequence satisfies $4\tau_{j+1}\le\tau_j$, each shifted sequence is summable and its sum is at most $4\tau_j/3$. Strict positivity is unnecessary, so the conclusion includes zero lifetimes. The theorem bounds tails of the supplied sequence; it neither constructs activation times nor proves that individual increments equal these lifetimes.
TorusEuler.activationLifetime_tail.summary: Geometric lifetime decay controls every remaining lifetime

TorusEuler.activationTimes_converge.text: Nondecreasing activation times with increments bounded by positive quarter-decaying half lengths converge to a positive finite `T`. The hypotheses include `ht0`, the step bounds, and `hlater`, which requires a strict increase somewhere after every index. The conclusion gives $0<T-t_j\le(4/3)\tau_j$ and $T<t_j+2\tau_j$, allowing the two initial activation times to coincide.
TorusEuler.activationTimes_converge.summary: Activation times converge below every endpoint

TorusEuler.activation_interval_weight_lo.text: For positive `L`, `C`, and rate `r`, the bounds $2L^2\le r(stop-start)$ and $r\le C\mu^{1/8}L$ imply `start < stop` and $(2/C)L\le\mu^{1/8}(stop-start)$. Positivity of `μ` is not an explicit hypothesis; the conclusion follows from the stated positive constants and compatible inequalities.
TorusEuler.activation_interval_weight_lo.summary: The clock and rate bounds force positive weighted duration

TorusEuler.activeTimeJet.text: For a field $f(t,x)$ with a general parameter space `X`, this abbreviates the iterated within-time derivative on $[a,b]$ while $x$ stays fixed. In the leading-wave application, $x$ is a scaled label or a label-phase pair. The definition has no smoothness hypothesis and does not differentiate a moving spatial point or a time-dependent weight.
TorusEuler.activeTimeJet.summary: Time derivatives with label and phase held fixed

TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_bilinear_phaseJ.text: Let `B` be a continuous bilinear map with norm at most one. For two jointly smooth fields, assume their time derivatives through $i$ at the selected time have parameter-derivative bounds $A,C$ through order $n$. With `a < b` and nonnegative caps, the order-$i$ time derivative of their product has `PhaseJetBound` $2^i2^nAC$. The constants may depend on the selected time.
TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_bilinear_phaseJ.summary: Time and parameter product derivatives have binomial bounds

TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_homogeneous_pha.text: Assume `hODE` gives actual derivatives $f_t=A(t,x)f$ on a nondegenerate interval, with $A,f$ jointly smooth. If generator time derivatives through $q$ have parameter bound $B$ and $f(t)$ has bound $C$ through parameter order $n$, then order $i\le q$ is bounded by $C(1+2^q2^nB)^i$. This differentiates the equation at a fixed time; it does not estimate the initial-to-final growth of a new solution.
TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_homogeneous_pha.summary: A homogeneous equation bounds all chosen time derivatives

TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_zero.text: The order-zero active time derivative is exactly the original field, as an equality of functions. No structure on the parameter space or interval is needed beyond the displayed function types. This algebraic identity starts the regularity and homogeneous-equation inductions for the leading wave; it is not a claim about any positive derivative order.
TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_zero.summary: Zero active time derivatives give the original field

TorusEuler.actualJetValues_add_le.text: Summing two smooth fields adds the supremum bounds of the same derivative word.
TorusEuler.actualJetValues_add_le.summary: Derivative suprema obey the triangle inequality

TorusEuler.actualJetValues_smul.text: For smooth directions and smooth time slices, multiplying the field by a real scalar sends its entire measurement set to the scalar norm times the original set. This includes the zero sample, pointwise jet norms, and optional half-Hölder quotients. The equality also handles the zero scalar.
TorusEuler.actualJetValues_smul.summary: Scaling a field scales every measured derivative value

TorusEuler.add_gradient_truncatedParentS.text: For a finite-band torus field with smooth Euclidean lift, identifies the lift plus the constructed pressure gradient with its actual periodic Leray projection. The proof shows the sum is solenoidal and uses that the projection fixes solenoidal fields and kills periodic gradients. This is an exact field identity, not merely equality of Fourier support.
TorusEuler.add_gradient_truncatedParentS.summary: Adding the pressure gradient gives the Leray projection

TorusEuler.add_hierarchyLatticeShift.text: Adding the lattice-shift vector preserves time, translates the label by an integer vector and translates phase by its pairing with k. This is the coordinate formula for twisted periodicity.

TorusEuler.add_hierarchyLatticeShift_mem.text: Adding the carrier-dependent lattice shift preserves membership in the profile slab, because its time component is zero. Both label and phase coordinates may change. The equivalence is used to transfer twisted periodicity across zero-extension representatives and to keep derivative evaluations in the same closed domain.
TorusEuler.add_hierarchyLatticeShift_mem.summary: A twisted translation preserves the time-slab condition

TorusEuler.add_hierarchyPhasePeriod.text: Adding `hierarchyPhasePeriod` to a joint point leaves time and label unchanged and adds one to the phase. This coordinate identity converts periodicity of the whole representative into unit periodicity of a phase slice. It is an algebraic statement independent of the slab or any profile.
TorusEuler.add_hierarchyPhasePeriod.summary: A period changes only the phase coordinate

TorusEuler.add_hierarchyPhasePeriod_mem_.text: A point belongs to `hierarchyProfileSlab T` exactly when the point translated by one phase period does. The slab restricts time alone, so phase translation cannot change membership. This equivalence allows periodicity proofs to use the same zero-extension branch at both points.
TorusEuler.add_hierarchyPhasePeriod_mem_.summary: A phase period preserves the time-slab condition

TorusEuler.adjoint_vorticityForm.text: The adjoint of the pulled-back vorticity coefficient is its negative. This algebraic fact holds for arbitrary deformation and gradient operators.
TorusEuler.adjoint_vorticityForm.summary: Skew symmetry of the vorticity coefficient

TorusEuler.ae_endpointMixedCoefficient_s.text: When joint, mixed and fixed-time coefficient descriptions agree almost everywhere and satisfy the stated measurability and bound hypotheses, a spatial slice of the embedded mixed product equals the weak spatial coefficient applied to the slice. The theorem preserves equality only almost everywhere in time, which is the correct input to continuous representative recovery.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointMixedCoefficient_s.summary: Coefficient multiplication survives the change of slices

TorusEuler.ae_endpointMixedCoefficient_s.text: Assuming the mixed coefficient acts as the specified continuous strong coefficient on each temporal path almost everywhere, its product with a mixed field has the expected weak-coefficient action on almost every spatial slice.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointMixedCoefficient_s.summary: Coefficient action agrees on almost every spatial slice

TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_coeff.text: Assume the jointly measurable bounded coefficient `Ωjoint` agrees almost everywhere with the evaluated strong coefficient family `Ω`, and `g` represents the spatial slices of `v`. Then the embedding of the strong product agrees almost everywhere in time with the slice of the joint product multiplier. The explicit representative compatibility is necessary to connect the two constructions.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_coeff.summary: The recovered coefficient product matches the joint weak product

TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_l2Mul.text: For a jointly measurable, essentially bounded coefficient `K`, slicing its product with `v` agrees almost everywhere in time with multiplying the spatial slice of `v`. The conclusion supplies the slice measurability and bound witnesses `hKt` and `bKt`. It compares $L^2$ classes and does not choose values at exceptional times.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_l2Mul.summary: Spatial slicing respects a bounded coefficient multiplier

TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_solen.text: A weakly solenoidal joint field has solenoidal spatial slices on a single full-measure time set for all potential tests. The proof reduces the family of open failure sets to a countable subcover using second countability of spatial L2.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_solen.summary: One full measure set of solenoidal slices

TorusEuler.ae_endpointTimeSlice_congr.text: If two fields agree almost everywhere for the product of time measure and label measure, then for almost every label they agree for almost every time along that label's path. The quantified outer variable is the label `a`. This is the precise Fubini statement needed to integrate chosen $L^2$ representatives in time.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointTimeSlice_congr.summary: Product equality descends to almost every label path

TorusEuler.ae_endpointTimeSlice_of_conti.text: For nonnegative `T`, suppose `f` is continuous in the spatial half-Hölder norm and its $L^2$ embeddings agree with the spatial slices of `v` almost everywhere in time. Then, for almost every label, evaluating `f` gives the same time path as the joint representative. This is a Fubini compatibility statement, not equality at every exceptional space-time point.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointTimeSlice_of_conti.summary: Recover the time path representative from continuous spatial slices

TorusEuler.ae_hasDerivAt_endpointPrimiti.text: For an interval-integrable velocity with values in a complete normed space, its primitive has ordinary derivative equal to that velocity almost everywhere in the restricted time measure. This is the almost-everywhere fundamental theorem of calculus. It does not assert a derivative at every time or at either endpoint.
TorusEuler.ae_hasDerivAt_endpointPrimiti.summary: The primitive differentiates to velocity almost everywhere

TorusEuler.ae_memLp_endpointTimeSlice.text: A square-integrable field on the time-label product has a square-integrable time slice at almost every label. The label measure is assumed s-finite by the surrounding section. This justifies using the one-dimensional time integration estimates on product-space representatives, while keeping the exceptional set explicitly almost everywhere in labels.

TorusEuler.ae_real_inner_angularTimeLera.text: Apply the angular/time-mean projection to a time L² path; its values are orthogonal to the frequency vector almost everywhere in time. The proof uses its representative formula and the finite-dimensional angular identity. This statement imposes transversality only; the separate time-integral theorem supplies the zero-mean condition.
TorusEuler.ae_real_inner_angularTimeLera.summary: The combined time path projection is transverse almost everywhere

TorusEuler.ae_sub_angularTimeLeray_eq.text: The complement of the combined symbol is the constant time mean plus the frequency-parallel part of the mean-free path. The formula is almost everywhere and valid with Lean’s total division. If `ξ = 0`, the longitudinal term vanishes, matching the zero-frequency identity convention; positive `T` is required when interpreting the first term as an average.
TorusEuler.ae_sub_angularTimeLeray_eq.summary: The discarded part is a mean plus a longitudinal path

TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator.text:
The linear operator $\mathbf a\mapsto-D\mathbf a+2(k\cdot D\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$. For a fixed wave vector this is the coefficient of the homogeneous amplitude equation. `InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℝ k k` sends a vector $v$ to $(k\cdot v)k$. Linearity is recorded by the type `E →L[ℝ] E`; continuity as the time-dependent wave vector varies needs separate nonvanishing hypotheses.

Default-value audit (b5): At k = 0 the reciprocal squared norm is zero and the rank-one term vanishes, leaving minus D. This total extension is not a normalized transverse-wave operator at a zero wave vector; continuity and propagation are used only with k nonzero.
TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator.summary: Linear amplitude operator for a fixed wave vector

TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator_a.text: The projected affine-wave operator and the projected forcing sum to $f-MV-(\partial_s\mathsf p)\kappa$, with the pressure slope defined by the preceding formula. This is a pointwise algebraic identity in `M`, `κ`, `f`, and `V`; it is not an existence statement for an ODE. It identifies the right side of the projected equation with the right side of the transverse momentum equation, so either form can be used in a derivative hypothesis.
TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator_a.summary: The projected ODE equals the pressure equation

TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator_a.text: The affine amplitude operator applied to `a` expands as $-Da+2\langle k,Da\rangle k/\|k\|^2$. The theorem is an algebraic identity for a continuous linear map `D` on a real inner product space and arbitrary vectors `k` and `a`. It does not itself solve the evolution equation or assert transversality. The formula is the right-hand side of the seed equation after setting `D = M` and `k = κ`.

TorusEuler.affineWavePressure.text: The pressure $-x\cdot Sx/2-pP(k\cdot x)$ at one fixed time. In the Euler application, $S=D'+D^2$ and $p=p_{\rm w}$. This is a definition for arbitrary `P`, `S`, `p` and `k`; symmetry of `S` and the derivative identity $P'=F$ are hypotheses of the gradient theorem. No mean-zero normalization of the primitive is needed to define this pressure.
TorusEuler.affineWavePressure.summary: Quadratic background pressure with the wave primitive

TorusEuler.affineWavePressureCoeff.text:
The scalar $p_{\rm w}=2k\cdot D\mathbf a/|k|^2$ in the amplitude equation. Its role is to cancel the derivative of $k\cdot\mathbf a$, so a transverse initial amplitude remains transverse. This definition makes sense in Lean even at $k=0$ because division is total. The propagation result supplies the nonzero wave vector needed for its usual mathematical interpretation.

Default-value audit (b5): At wave vector zero, total division makes the pressure coefficient zero. Cancellation and propagation arguments assume nonzero wave vectors when using its physical pressure interpretation.

TorusEuler.affineWaveVelocity.text: Defines the full velocity $D x+F(k\cdot x)\mathbf a$. The profile is scalar, while the amplitude and wave vector are three-dimensional vectors; the matrix is a continuous linear map. The definition alone does not impose perpendicularity or the Euler equations. The exact-wave theorem supplies those conclusions when the background and wave coefficients satisfy their stated differential identities.

TorusEuler.affineWave_exists_Icc.text: For a continuous operator path $D$ on $[l,r]$, constructs both affine-wave paths from nonzero perpendicular data at any $t_0$ in that interval. It solves for $k$ first, proves $k$ never vanishes, then solves the linear amplitude equation. The returned paths stay nonzero and perpendicular. Only within-interval derivatives are asserted, including endpoints; neither trace freeness nor an Euler background is assumed.
TorusEuler.affineWave_exists_Icc.summary: Affine waves exist throughout the closed interval

TorusEuler.affineWave_materialAccelerati.text: The material acceleration of the affine wave is $(D'+D^2)x+F(k\cdot x)(\mathbf a'+D\mathbf a)$. The assumptions `hk` and `hperp` cancel phase transport and self-advection, while `hD`, `ha` and `hF` supply the derivatives used in the calculation. `hs` gives unique time derivatives within the time set. The amplitude equation and pressure cancellation are not yet imposed in this identity.
TorusEuler.affineWave_materialAccelerati.summary: Material acceleration after the phase cancellation

TorusEuler.affineWave_propagation.text: On an order-connected time set, a continuous background and solutions of the two wave ODEs preserve nonzero wave and amplitude vectors and their perpendicularity from one initial time. This holds throughout the interval, including earlier times and endpoints, and requires neither trace zero nor symmetry of the background acceleration.
TorusEuler.affineWave_propagation.summary: Propagation of nonzero perpendicular wave data

TorusEuler.affineWave_solvesEulerOn.text: On a time set with unique derivatives, a trace-free background with self-adjoint acceleration matrix and perpendicular wave data satisfying the two ODEs gives the exact Euler momentum and divergence identities. The primitive need only have derivative equal to the profile; oddness, periodicity, and unit central slope are not required for this local identity.
TorusEuler.affineWave_solvesEulerOn.summary: The affine wave solves the Euler equations

TorusEuler.angularLeray.text: The projection symbol $I-\widehat\xi\otimes\widehat\xi$ for the spatial Leray operator. Lean writes the rank-one operator using `InnerProductSpace.rankOne` and normalizes `ξ`. At a nonzero frequency this removes the component parallel to $\xi$. The normalization at zero is zero, giving the identity there. This definition is spatial; the mixed time-path symbol adds the separate zero time-mean projection.
TorusEuler.angularLeray.summary: The spatial Leray symbol at every frequency

TorusEuler.angularLeray_apply.text: For any real frequency vector, the angular Leray symbol sends $v$ to $v-(\langle\xi,v\rangle/\|\xi\|^2)\xi$. The identity includes zero frequency because real division is totalized there. This formula identifies the normalized rank-one definition with the familiar orthogonal projection onto the perpendicular plane.
TorusEuler.angularLeray_apply.summary: The real Leray symbol removes the frequency component

TorusEuler.angularLeray_isSymmetricProje.text: The angular Leray map is both symmetric and idempotent for every real frequency. Nonzero frequencies use projection away from the normalized frequency direction; zero frequency uses the identity. The result supplies the exact projection hypothesis required by the frozen-symbol coercivity and inverse theorems.
TorusEuler.angularLeray_isSymmetricProje.summary: Every real frequency gives a symmetric projection

TorusEuler.angularLeray_neg.text: The angular Leray operator is unchanged by replacing its frequency by its negative. The longitudinal numerator and vector both change sign, leaving the rank-one correction unchanged. This holds also at zero and supplies the parity needed to relate real symbols to complex Fourier multipliers.
TorusEuler.angularLeray_neg.summary: The real Leray symbol is even in frequency

TorusEuler.angularLeray_pos_smul.text: If `hc : 0 < c`, replacing the frequency by $c\xi$ leaves the angular Leray operator unchanged. The frequency itself may be zero. This degree-zero homogeneity is the starting point for the scaling law of higher derivatives on the punctured frequency space.
TorusEuler.angularLeray_pos_smul.summary: Positive frequency rescaling leaves the Leray symbol unchanged

TorusEuler.angularLeray_zero.text: The spatial Leray symbol at frequency zero is the identity. There is no nonzero-frequency hypothesis and no coefficient input: this follows directly from the definition using the normalized frequency vector, which is zero at the origin. It records why the spatial mean survives Leray projection. The combined time-path projection can still remove a temporal mean; that is a different operation.

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray.text: This path operator first subtracts the time average, then applies the spatial angular Leray symbol at each time. It represents the combined projection used for endpoint velocities. Its projection and zero-integral properties require a positive interval in the subsequent theorems; the definition itself accepts arbitrary real duration.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray.summary: Projecting paths onto transverse zero mean velocities

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_apply_ae.text: The projected path agrees almost everywhere with the angular Leray operator applied to the mean-subtracted path value. The order of the two operations is fixed in this definition, though they commute. The theorem gives representative-level meaning without asserting equality at every chosen time.

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_eq_self_iff.text: For `hT : 0 < T`, a path is fixed by the combined symbol exactly when its time integral is zero and it is almost everywhere perpendicular to `ξ`. The forward direction reads the two projection properties; the reverse uses the mean-subtraction formula and the angular projection formula. Zero frequency leaves only the time-mean condition.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_eq_self_iff.summary: Fixed paths have zero mean and no longitudinal component

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_isSymmetricP.text: On a positive interval, the combined angular-time operator is a symmetric projection. Its factors are the lifted spatial orthogonal projection and time mean subtraction, and the previous commutation theorem allows their product to remain orthogonal. This supplies the projection input for frozen operators on whole time paths.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_isSymmetricP.summary: The two commuting path projections form a symmetric projection

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_pos_smul.text: For a positive real scale, rescaling the spatial frequency leaves the angular-time projection unchanged. The duration is arbitrary in this algebraic statement. Only the spatial angular symbol depends on frequency, so its degree-zero homogeneity passes directly to the mixed path operator.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_pos_smul.summary: The mixed symbol is homogeneous in spatial frequency

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_zero.text: At zero spatial frequency, the combined operator is exactly `endpointSubtractMean T`. The spatial Leray factor becomes the identity, but the terminal-displacement constraint still removes the time average. This prevents confusing the zero mode of the mixed symbol with the identity on all time paths.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_zero.summary: At zero spatial frequency only the time projection remains

TorusEuler.annularLocalize.text: Multiply the operator symbol by the scalar difference $\psi(\xi)-\psi(2\xi)$. With a unit cutoff near zero and compact outer support, this confines the product to an annulus. The definition itself accepts arbitrary functions; vanishing, compact support, and smoothness are proved under separate cutoff and symbol hypotheses.
TorusEuler.annularLocalize.summary: Remove low frequencies before inverting the Fourier transform

TorusEuler.annularLocalize_compact.text: The outer cutoff condition alone ensures that the localized symbol has compact support within the closed ball of radius two. The original operator symbol may be arbitrary. This is a support statement; global smoothness still needs a smooth cutoff, local cancellation near zero, and smoothness of the symbol away from zero.

TorusEuler.annularLocalize_smooth.text: A smooth cutoff equal to one near zero turns a symbol smooth on the punctured space into a globally smooth annular product. Away from zero, multiplication preserves smoothness; near zero the product is identically zero. The theorem does not require the original symbol to have a limit at zero.
TorusEuler.annularLocalize_smooth.summary: Localization removes the origin from the symbol regularity problem

TorusEuler.annularLocalize_zero_of_large.text: If the cutoff is zero at norms at least two, its annular localization of any operator symbol is also zero there. Both cutoff evaluations vanish because doubling the frequency stays outside the same radius. No smoothness or boundedness of the original symbol is required for this support statement.
TorusEuler.annularLocalize_zero_of_large.summary: The localized symbol vanishes beyond the outer radius

TorusEuler.annularLocalize_zero_of_small.text: If the cutoff equals one on the closed unit ball, its difference at `ξ` and `2ξ` vanishes whenever $\|\xi\|\le1/2$. Therefore the localized symbol is zero throughout that inner region, regardless of the original symbol. This removes any singular or discontinuous behavior at the origin before Fourier inversion.
TorusEuler.annularLocalize_zero_of_small.summary: The localized symbol vanishes on the inner half ball

TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientCoordinate.text: Defines the exact-order coordinate quantity by summing over all ordered coordinate words of length `m`. Each term is the real supremum of the corresponding derivative norm over the index and space, with zero inserted. This is not yet a guaranteed analytic norm: the separate coefficient predicate includes boundedness of every supremum set.
TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientCoordinate.summary: The sum of coordinate derivative supremums

TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientMultiIndex.text: The exact-order coefficient norm sums one derivative supremum for each nondecreasing coordinate word of length $m$. These words represent the ordinary spatial multi-indices used in $|c|_m$. The supremum is uniform in the arbitrary time index and the label point. The definition uses unscaled label directions; powers of the envelope radius are attached later in the weighted coefficient estimates.
TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientMultiIndex.summary: Exact-order sums of coefficient derivative supremums

TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientOrderWords.text:
Each nondecreasing coordinate word of length `m` represents one spatial multi-index of order `m`.

Default-value audit (b5): Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.

TorusEuler.appendixCutoffKernel.text: Defines the torus kernel by summing $\psi(k/\Lambda)e_k(x)e_{-k}(z)$ over the finite band of radius $2\Lambda$. It is defined for every real scale and arbitrary real symbol. Identifying this expression with the intended smooth frequency cutoff, and obtaining a uniform kernel norm, require the support and positivity hypotheses of subsequent theorems.

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord.text:
Apply coordinate derivative maps in word order, with the outermost derivative first. The maps can already include coordinate weights.

Default-value audit (b5): The derivative maps are supplied linear maps. Their identification with actual coordinate derivatives and their commutation must be established in each application.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord.summary: Coordinate derivatives applied in ordered words

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_coeffi.text: For a bilinear coefficient action `B` satisfying the stated first-order product rule, differentiating along a word gives the unchanged coefficient acting on the differentiated unknown plus a finite sum of correction terms. Those terms use `endpointMixedCorrectionPairs`, with at least one derivative on the coefficient. This is the algebraic source of the triangular derivative recursion.

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_cons.text: Adding a letter at the front of a derivative word applies that coordinate derivative to the previously evaluated word. This is the recursive convention for order in the finite derivative calculus.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_cons.summary: The first letter is the outermost derivative

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_equati.text: Applying a derivative word to the linear equation produces the same operator on the differentiated unknown, plus correction terms in which a nonempty derivative word falls on a coefficient. The inputs `hComm`, `hProduct`, and `hEq` give commutation, the product rule, and the original equation. The list `endpointMixedCorrectionPairs w` records the Leibniz splittings with their multiplicities, replacing the displayed binomial coefficients in the paper.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_equati.summary: Differentiating the equation separates coefficient derivatives

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_nil.text: Applying `appendixDerivativeWord` to the empty list returns the original vector. This is the zero-order convention in the abstract derivative calculus. It supplies the base case for permutation and Leibniz arguments and ensures that finite derivative norms include the undifferentiated field.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_nil.summary: An empty derivative word leaves the field unchanged

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_perm.text: If every pair of linear derivative maps commutes on every vector, permutation-equivalent words have identical action. The proof uses the generators of list permutation. The commutation hypothesis is necessary here: a word is not treated as a multi-index for an arbitrary collection of noncommuting operators.

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_scaled.text: Multiplying each coordinate derivative by its weight multiplies the whole derivative by the product of its letter weights.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_scaled.summary: Each coordinate weight contributes one factor

TorusEuler.appendixExactOrderDerivativeN.text:
The coefficient size at one order sums its distinct coordinate derivatives of that order. The derivative maps carry the scale factors.

Default-value audit (b5): Only finitely many words of the specified exact order are included. The derivative maps and base seminorm are parameters, so the definition alone is algebraic.
TorusEuler.appendixExactOrderDerivativeN.summary: The coefficient norm at one exact derivative order

TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm.text:
The exact finite norm consists of one word for each mixed multi-index. The zeroth-order seminorm can be the weighted sup norm or the Hölder norm.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a finite sum of a supplied zeroth seminorm applied to supplied derivative maps. Its analytic interpretation depends on those maps being the actual derivatives; it does not infer differentiability.
TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm.summary: The exact finite norm over mixed multi-indices

TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm_.text: Scaling each coordinate derivative by a nonnegative weight multiplies the contribution of a word by the product of its letter weights. The data are a seminorm `p`, linear derivative maps `D`, weights `r`, and `hr : ∀ i, 0 ≤ r i`. The identity explains the factors $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j$ when label and phase derivatives are combined in a finite norm. It is algebraic and does not require a differential equation.
TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm_.summary: Derivative weights multiply along each coordinate word

TorusEuler.appendixSlowCoefficient_word_.text: A slow-coefficient bound for the sum of all derivatives of one order controls the corresponding bound for each individual word. The coefficient derivatives commute by `hComm`; `hb` makes the operator weights nonnegative and `hLow` does the same for the inverse constant. The hypothesis `hSlow` is the exact-order bound. This is the passage from the paper’s multi-index sums to the word-by-word hypothesis used in derivative lifting.
TorusEuler.appendixSlowCoefficient_word_.summary: Exact-order coefficient bounds control each derivative word

TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma12.text: For a chosen schedule, every fixed pair of spatial and Eulerian time orders eventually has correction norm at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$. The proposition combines `HasTerminalMixedIncrementBounds` with continuity on the child slab in `spatialHolderHalfNorm m`, so the paper’s $C([0,S_j];C^{m,1/2})$ norm has both ingredients. The order `∀ q m, ∀ᶠ n in atTop` allows the starting index to depend on both orders. This standalone existential statement is extracted from Auxiliary Theorem 1.1; that combined theorem records coexistence with the other auxiliary estimate.

TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma13.text: Auxiliary Lemma 1.3 gives one selected schedule on which every fixed time order eventually has both velocity and residual bounds. The conclusion combines `StageTimeBounds q ψ n` with time continuity in the spatial supremum norm. The exponent is a natural number in Lean; the paper only asks for an exponent. `∀ q, ∃ ψ, ∀ᶠ n` keeps the exponent independent of the stage and the starting index dependent on the requested time order. The combined auxiliary theorem records coexistence with the mixed increment estimate.
TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma13.summary: Auxiliary Lemma 1.3: velocity and residual time bounds

TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness.text: The library theorem chooses an exponent, threshold and initial-frequency floor before supplying one scheduled construction for each sufficiently large frequency. Its conclusion includes both eventual time-estimate families and an Euler singularity witness with a periodic extension smooth for all real times away from the origin. It imposes no Euler equation after the terminal time. It does not prove the generalized Paper reference statement for arbitrary cutoffs and constructions, nor explicitly record stage convergence or maximal-solution uniqueness in its conclusion.
TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness.summary: Specialized auxiliary construction with smooth terminal extension

TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness_o.text: Assumes `graph` turns the common graph cost bounds into `TerminalGraphStep` for every qualifying scheduled construction. It combines graph costs, using the finite envelope in time order and parent exponent, with the cutoff costs obtained from `exists_terminalCutoffCosts`. The local-time-step assembly then produces `AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness`. The schedule is selected before the initial frequency; actual graph estimates are still the theorem's explicit hypothesis.
TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness_o.summary: Graph estimates and cutoff costs share one schedule

TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness_o.text: Assuming `steps` converts the specified finite cost bounds into `TerminalTimeStep` for every qualifying scheduled construction, this theorem produces `AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness`. It augments the threshold before the initial frequency, obtains a construction and the main Euler witness from its stages, then applies the time-order induction, mixed-increment convergence, and extension theorem. The proof passes the actual convergence witness `hConverge` to the smoothness argument. The local time estimates remain the explicit hypothesis; this is a conditional assembly theorem.
TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness_o.summary: Local time estimates give the auxiliary terminal conclusion

TorusEuler.bddAbove_endpointLabelWord_of.text: Every spatial derivative word of a smooth periodic field on a nondegenerate closed slab has bounded jet-value sets in both the supremum and half-Hölder measurements. The assumptions include nonnegative label scale `ℓ`. Bounds on one additional derivative control the Hölder differences, making subsequent uses of the conditionally complete supremum mathematically justified.
TorusEuler.bddAbove_endpointLabelWord_of.summary: Smooth periodic words have finite uniform bounds

TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_coordinate_sum.text: Sum the supremum norms of order-`j` derivatives over all lists `β : Fin j → Fin 3`. For a field supported below $4\Lambda$, the result is bounded by an explicit kernel-dependent constant times $\Lambda^j\|g\|_\infty$. The list indexing counts ordered coordinate directions, which can include repeated representations of the same multi-index derivative.
TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_coordinate_sum.summary: Summing coordinate derivatives gives a Bernstein constant

TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_finiteFourierS.text: If a finite synthesis is supported in the band of radius $4\Lambda$, with `Λ > 0`, its order-`j` directional derivative is bounded by $(4\Lambda)^j$ times the corresponding undilated kernel derivative L¹ norm and the supplied supremum bound `M`. The cutoff must be smooth, supported in radius two, and equal one on the unit ball.
TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_finiteFourierS.summary: Band limited Fourier polynomials satisfy the directional Bernstein bound

TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_of_band.text: A continuous torus field whose coefficients vanish beyond $4\Lambda$ satisfies the same directional derivative bound as a Fourier polynomial. The positive-scale and cutoff hypotheses are explicit. Finite synthesis first proves that the field’s lift is smooth; the derivative estimate then uses the supremum norm of the original continuous field.
TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_of_band.summary: Continuous band limited fields satisfy directional Bernstein estimates

TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_of_real_band.text: For a smooth cutoff symbol supported in the radius-two ball and equal to one on the unit ball, bounds the $j$th derivative of a real band-limited lift in any specified directions `v`.
