TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection_pathC.text: The Leibniz correction for the path coefficient K minus J Omega equals the K correction minus the time primitive of the Omega correction. This follows term by term from linearity of the finite sum and the primitive.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection_pathC.summary: Splitting the mixed spatial correction into two parts

TorusEuler.endpointMixedIntegration.text:
Define the mixed integration operator by applying the bounded temporal L2 primitive to each label value. It preserves the spatial half-Holder class by bounded linear functoriality.

Default-value audit (b5): The nonnegative duration is part of the input. The operator integrates L2 classes at each label and is zero on a zero-length interval; no continuity in time is asserted by the definition.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient.text:
The labelwise operator $B=K-J\Omega$ acting on temporal $L^2$ paths. Here `Kmix` and `Ωmix` are spatial half-Hölder fields of bounded path operators, and `hT : 0 ≤ T` permits the bounded primitive operator `endpointPrimitiveLp hT`. Composition with the primitive acts after $\Omega$. This definition identifies the coefficient in the compressed equation; it does not by itself assert that a velocity solves that equation.

Default-value audit (b5): The supplied nonnegative duration makes the temporal primitive bounded. At T zero the temporal path space is trivial. Kmix and Omega mix need not arise from time curves until compatibility hypotheses are supplied.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient.summary: The coefficient acting on whole time paths

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.text: Pointwise multiplication by the labelwise path coefficient K minus J Omega is exactly the mixed product operator. This identifies two representations of the same compressed equation.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.summary: The mixed path coefficient gives the integrated operator

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.text: The mixed path coefficient has lower bound $[2D^2(1+L)^2]^{-1}\|v\|^2$ on every zero-time-mean path. Besides the coefficient action identities, the theorem assumes $0<T\le1$, deformation evolution, the inverse bound and the quadratic Hessian upper bound. No nonzero spatial-frequency restriction appears, so the estimate also applies to the spatial constant mode.

Evaluating the mixed coefficient at a fixed label gives the temporal operator $K(a)-J\circ\Omega(a)$. Here `J` is the bounded primitive on $L^2((0,T])$, not a scalar coefficient. The identity holds for every label and nonnegative duration, and exposes the operator to which spatial freezing will be applied.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.summary: The path coefficient is multiplication minus integration

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.text: For a temporal path with zero integral, pairing $K-J\Omega$ against that path equals the endpoint energy. The hypotheses `hK` and `hΩ` require the mixed operators to act as the physical kinetic and vorticity coefficients almost everywhere. The primitive adjoint identity changes the minus sign into the plus sign in the label energy.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.summary: The path pairing recovers the positive label form

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.text: The quadratic form of $B=K-J\Omega$ equals the integral $\int(Kv\cdot v+\Omega v\cdot Jv)$ for a mean-zero $L^2$ path. The hypothesis `hv` removes its time mean. The hypotheses `hK` and `hΩ` identify the supplied path operators with multiplication by the time-slice coefficients almost everywhere. This theorem establishes the identity; the lower bound by $\mu\|v\|^2$ is the separate energy assumption.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.summary: The mixed operator has the Sobolev energy

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_apply_.text: Assume `hw` says the mixed half-Hölder field of time paths represents the joint field labelwise almost everywhere. At each specified time in the closed slab, evaluating the mixed primitive and embedding spatially agrees almost everywhere in labels with the primitive of the joint representative. Integration removes the input time-representative ambiguity.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_apply_.summary: Mixed and joint time primitives agree at each time

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_contin.text: A representative obtained by applying a bounded operator to primitive evaluation is continuous on the closed interval and has the stated square-root-duration norm bound. This proves continuity of the Volterra term before the velocity is known to be continuous.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_contin.summary: Continuity and size of the mixed primitive

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_end.text: A continuous half-Holder curve agreeing with a mixed field almost everywhere has exactly the same Banach-valued primitive at every closed-interval time. This identifies recovered displacements independently of representative choices.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_end.summary: The mixed and continuous primitives coincide

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_of_.text: A mixed time-path field and its continuous half-Hölder spatial representative have identical primitives at every time in the closed interval. The input comparison is only almost everywhere after embedding into spatial $L^2$. Integration and continuity upgrade that comparison to an equality of half-Hölder fields, including at the two time endpoints.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_of_.summary: Both representatives give the same primitive at every time

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_spa.text: Under `hw`, the embedded mixed primitive at almost every time equals the spatial slice of the joint $L^2$ primitive. The theorem supplies a proof that each such time lies in the closed slab. This distinction matters: the mixed primitive is evaluated at a genuine time, while the joint slice is initially only almost-everywhere data.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_spa.summary: Mixed integration agrees with joint spatial slices

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_termin.text: With nonnegative `T` and the representation hypothesis `hw`, evaluating the mixed primitive at terminal time and embedding into spatial $L^2$ gives `endpointTorusTimeIntegral hT v`. This is the compatibility needed to recover the terminal displacement condition from zero time mean. The conclusion is equality of spatial equivalence classes.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_termin.summary: The terminal primitive equals the weak time integral

TorusEuler.endpointMixedProductOperator.text:
Define the operator K applied pointwise minus the time primitive of Omega applied pointwise on the mixed Holder space. This is the ambient operator before compression by the combined projection.

Default-value audit (b5): The nonnegative duration supplies the bounded primitive. The formula is valid for any mixed coefficients and is zero on the trivial duration-zero path space; coercivity and invertibility are not part of the definition.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjectedPrimiti.text: For almost every slab time, the weak projection of the joint primitive equals the embedded strong projection of the mixed primitive evaluation. The theorem supplies membership of that time in the closed interval.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjectedPrimiti.summary: The projected primitive agrees in both representations

TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjectedSolve_t.text: If `v` is fixed by `P` and `hr` says the projected residual $Bv+L$ vanishes, compatibility of both `P` and `B` with joint $L^2$ yields a constrained weak solution. The right side is $-L$, as retained in the conclusion. The theorem transports an existing solution; it does not assert a new inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjectedSolve_t.summary: A projected Hölder solution satisfies the joint weak equation

TorusEuler.endpointMixedResidual_project.text: Averaging the joint L2 residual in time and applying the weak projection gives the embedding of its strong half-Holder projected mean. The identity also holds at duration zero by totalized normalization.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedResidual_project.summary: The mean residual agrees in strong and weak spaces

TorusEuler.endpointMixedSource_hasSpatia.text: Compatible mixed source fields inherit the spatial derivative relation of their time-slice curves, provided the derivative curve has a uniform half-Hölder bound. The representation hypotheses hold at every label and almost everywhere in time. The proof bounds the temporal $L^2$ remainder by $\sqrt T$ times the pointwise bound, then identifies the derivative from its vanishing error.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedSource_hasSpatia.summary: Pointwise source jets become mixed path jets

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint.text:
Construct a norm-nonincreasing linear embedding from half-Holder label fields of temporal L2 paths into joint time-label L2. Its slice identities ensure that the embedding does not depend on a pointwise choice of L2 representative.

Default-value audit (b5): The joint field is built through measurable L2 representatives, but the resulting L2 class and its labelwise almost-everywhere slice identities are fixed by the input. At nonpositive duration the time measure and target path spaces are trivial.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint.summary: Embedding mixed Holder fields into joint integral space

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_apply_ae.text: For almost every label, the joint embedding's time path agrees almost everywhere with the mixed field evaluated at that label.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_apply_ae.summary: The joint embedding has the expected time slices

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_coeffici.text: With the additional joint measurability hypothesis `hKjoint`, embedding the mixed coefficient product equals applying the joint L² multiplier to the embedded input. Slice representations identify both outputs almost everywhere. The theorem applies equally to the kinetic and vorticity coefficients, provided each meets the explicit uniform bounds.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_coeffici.summary: Coefficient multiplication commutes with the mixed embedding

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_eq_proje.text: Suppose mixed fields `w` and `u` have real Fourier moments related by the combined symbol at every frequency and phase. For positive `T`, embedding `u` equals the joint orthogonal projection of embedded `w`. Fourier separation proves equality, so compatibility can be checked entirely through mode formulas rather than arbitrary representatives.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_eq_proje.summary: The mixed symbol formula identifies the weak projection

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_injectiv.text: Equal joint L2 images imply equal mixed fields. Almost-everywhere equality of labelwise L2 paths becomes everywhere equality because those paths depend continuously on the torus label.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_injectiv.summary: The mixed to joint embedding is injective

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_integrat.text: For nonnegative duration, embedding the mixed primitive into joint L2 yields the joint primitive at fixed labels. The proof uses slice agreement and invariance of the integral under almost-everywhere equality.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_mul_of_a.text: The assumption `hCm` identifies the action of the mixed coefficient `Cmix` on time paths with the jointly measurable bounded coefficient `C` at almost every label. Under this compatibility, embedding `Cmix v` into joint $L^2$ equals the product multiplier applied after embedding. The explicit action hypothesis prevents identifying unrelated coefficient encodings.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_mul_of_a.summary: Coefficient multiplication agrees in both mixed representations

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_norm_sq.text: For the bundled mixed-to-joint embedding, the squared joint norm is exactly the Haar integral of the squared norms of the labelwise time paths. This is an energy identity rather than equality with the full half-Hölder norm. Spatial Hölder variation is additional information not measured by the joint L² norm.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_norm_sq.summary: The mixed embedding preserves integrated path energy

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_productO.text: For nonnegative `T`, bounded measurable coefficients `K` and `Ω`, and compatible mixed coefficient actions `hKm` and `hΩm`, the mixed operator $K-JΩ$ intertwines with the joint product operator. The proof combines multiplication compatibility with the primitive comparison. This establishes that the two endpoint equations describe the same integrated residual.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_productO.summary: The integrated operator agrees with its weak product form

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_productO.text: If `Kmix` and `Ωmix` act as the physical coefficient multipliers on almost every label slice, their mixed product operator embeds into the joint $L^2$ flow operator. The equality is an equality of $L^2$ elements, established through almost-everywhere representatives. It connects the Hölder-in-label construction with the weak space-time equation used for uniqueness.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_terminal.text: At terminal time, spatially embedding the primitive of a mixed path field equals taking the joint field’s weak time integral. The theorem assumes `T ≥ 0` so terminal evaluation lies in the closed slab. This compatibility converts zero time mean of the weak velocity into the desired final-displacement condition.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_terminal.summary: The terminal mixed primitive is the joint time integral

TorusEuler.endpointParityPart.text: Defines half the sum of a field and its reflected field multiplied by `sign`. At sign minus one this is the odd component; at sign one it is the even component. The function is defined for any real sign, so the docstring’s word projection should be understood only for the two parity choices.
TorusEuler.endpointParityPart.summary: The odd or even component under spatial reflection

TorusEuler.endpointParityPart_const_smul.text: Shows that multiplying a field by a real constant before reflection averaging gives the same result as multiplying the averaged field afterward. The statement holds for every real sign and needs no regularity. It is used when moving time-dependent normalization constants through estimates one fixed time slice at a time.
TorusEuler.endpointParityPart_const_smul.summary: Reflection averaging commutes with constant rescaling

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalCoefficientWo.text: For a derivative word $q$, this scalar cost is twice the closed-time norm of $K_q$ plus twice $T$ times that of $\Omega_q$. The vorticity factor carries the duration because it enters through a primitive. These are the coefficient factors multiplying the shorter velocity words in the physical derivative recurrence.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalCoefficientWo.summary: Combine kinetic and integrated vorticity coefficient costs

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalCoefficientWo.text: For $0\le T\le1$, a weighted bound on the sum of the kinetic and vorticity coefficient time norms, together with $A_{\rm inv}D^9\sqrt\ell\le1$, implies the combined recurrence cost is at most $2H$. Nonnegative radius, inverse cap and coefficient constant are explicit. The factor $T$ can be discarded because the slab is at most unit length.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalCoefficientWo.summary: Weighted coefficient bounds pay for the inverse cap

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalForcePrimitiv.text:
The negative time primitive $L=-\int_0^tF^*\mathrm{force}$ at fixed label. The argument `force` is already expressed in label coordinates; for an Eulerian force it is $f\circ X$. The deformation is evaluated on the unit torus, while the label field is represented by its periodic Euclidean lift. The value at time zero vanishes by the zero-length integral. This definition alone asserts no smoothness or equation for the recovered mean.

Default-value audit (b5): The Bochner interval integral is total and takes its default value for nonintegrable inputs. At time zero it is zero. Smoothness and the force-source interpretation are established only with the continuity and flow hypotheses supplied later.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalForcePrimitiv.summary: The integrated force in label coordinates

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalIntegratedRes.text: This defines the continuous periodic field $Kg-\int_0^t\Omega g+L-c$ after forgetting the half-Hölder norm. For a solution of the projected equation its solenoidal projection vanishes, which later yields a pressure potential. The definition itself imposes no equation, continuity in time, or differentiability on the supplied curves.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalIntegratedRes.summary: The integrated equation leaves a gradient residual

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.text:
Define the explicit recovery bound combining the instantaneous inverse, mixed inverse, projection norms, and kinetic and vorticity operator norms. Its time factors reflect the cancellation of the apparent inverse-duration cost in the recovered time average.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression is total for arbitrary real inverse caps, including negative caps. Its interpretation as an upper bound requires nonnegative valid inverse bounds and coefficient compatibility; the definition contains no inverse-time division.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.summary: The common bound from both Holder inverses

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.text: Control the explicit recovery bound by the closed-time half-Holder norms of K and Omega and the supplied inverse and projection bounds. Almost-everywhere mixed-coefficient compatibility is sufficient.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.summary: Bounding the inverse expression by time slice norms

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.text: The recovery budget is nonnegative when the slab duration and the two inverse caps `As` and `Am` are nonnegative. Every remaining factor is an operator norm or a nonnegative constant. This algebraic lemma permits multiplying the budget by upper bounds in the later physical derivative estimates.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.summary: Nonnegative inverse caps give a nonnegative budget

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalJetNormRecurr.text: Through order $N$, assume continuous coefficient, source and velocity words, compatible mixed representatives, projected differentiated equations, and the base spatial and mixed inverse bounds. Then each velocity time norm satisfies one recurrence using the same inverse budget and shorter velocity words. This theorem derives the recurrence from the physical equations; the subsequent lifting lemma performs the induction in derivative order.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalJetNormRecurr.summary: Every physical derivative uses the same base inverse

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalLabelVelocity.text:
Evaluate the recovered solenoidal Holder curve on the torus covering map to obtain its physical label-space velocity lift. Time regularity and pointwise divergence statements are proved under additional hypotheses.

Default-value audit (b5): The torus covering map makes the lift periodic for every time. The solenoidal subspace is a weak divergence constraint; classical divergence and time smoothness require additional regularity, and no values are specially chosen outside the time interval.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalLabelVelocity.summary: The periodic lift of the recovered label velocity

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMeanWordConst.text: Defines the scalar factor collecting the number of admissible spatial words, product-rule powers of two, coefficient bounds `C`, and the finite sum of derivative costs `H`. It depends on the requested order `N` and those two scalar families. Dependence on the parent deformation scale is kept outside this constant in the subsequent estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMeanWordConst.summary: The finite order constant in the mean estimate

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMeanWordConst.text: Assuming every entry of `C` and `H` is nonnegative, the finite order constant for the physical mean is nonnegative at each natural order `N`. The proof checks the finite sum and all scalar factors. This sign fact is needed when multiplying norm inequalities and absorbing deformation powers in the quantitative estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMeanWordConst.summary: Nonnegative budgets give a nonnegative mean constant

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMean_reflecti.text: For even deformation, inverse coframe and material coefficients and odd forcing, replaces a smooth periodic mean solution by odd label velocity, displacement and physical velocity, with even pressure. The same forced equation, divergence condition, zero-mean pressure and both displacement endpoint conditions remain valid. The positive slab and all original field equations are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMean_reflecti.summary: Select an odd mean while preserving its endpoint equation

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMixedSolution.text: A mixed solution fixed by the strong projection, with exact projected equation and coefficient actions representing the kinetic and vorticity forms, embeds into the constrained torus $L^2$ space. It satisfies the physical weak equation against every constrained test vector, with source equal to the negative embedded mixed forcing. No continuous time representative or pressure is constructed here.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMixedSolution.summary: The projected mixed solve gives the physical weak equation

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMomentumResid.text: The field is $dK\,g+K\,dg-\Omega g+dL$, expressed as a continuous periodic vector field. It is the product-rule derivative of the integrated residual when the supplied derivative values are correct. The later pressure theorem makes its negative a gradient; the algebraic definition does not certify those derivative or projection conditions.

TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient.text:
Descend the smooth periodic Euclidean gradient to a continuous torus field. Existence is selected noncomputably, but uniqueness of descent makes the resulting gradient independent of the choice.

Default-value audit (b5): The noncomputable choice is from a unique torus descent of the smooth periodic gradient. Periodicity guarantees well-definedness, and there is no undefined or arbitrary gradient on a bad input because the structure requires smoothness.
TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient.summary: The gradient of a periodic potential on the torus

TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient_fou.text: The torus gradient of the real Fourier test equals the real scalar `L` applied to $2\pi i$ times the character, multiplied by the integer wave vector. This exact formula shows that these weak tests inspect longitudinal Fourier components. It holds for arbitrary real-linear `L`, including real and imaginary parts.
TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient_fou.summary: The gradient of a real Fourier test is longitudinal

TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient_toU.text: Evaluation of the torus potential gradient at the image of a Euclidean point is exactly the ordinary gradient of the periodic lift there.
TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient_toU.summary: The descended gradient agrees with the lift

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive.text:
The displacement $Jv(t)=\int_0^t v(s)\,ds$, defined for a function into a real normed vector space. It is a Bochner interval integral; reversing the endpoints reverses its sign. No continuity or integrability assumption occurs in the definition. Results that identify its derivative or terminal value state the relevant assumptions separately, so the definition alone should not be read as an existence or regularity theorem.

Default-value audit (b5): The interval integral is total, gives zero on a zero-length interval, and changes sign when endpoints reverse. Without integrability it has the Bochner integral's default value; derivative and endpoint statements require the hypotheses of the later lemmas.

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation.text:
For a time in the closed interval, integration up to that time is a continuous linear map from temporal L2 to the target space, with norm at most the square root of that time.

Default-value audit (b5): The time is a subtype element of the closed interval, excluding out-of-window evaluation. At time zero the functional is zero. Integration makes it independent of the temporal L2 representative.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation.summary: Evaluating a primitive at a prescribed time

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation_a.text: Applying the bundled primitive-evaluation operator at a time belonging to the slab gives exactly `endpointPrimitive v t`. This is an equality in the target normed space, rather than an almost-everywhere equality of functions. Integration makes this value independent of null-set changes in the input $L^2$ representative.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation_a.summary: The evaluation operator returns the anchored time integral

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation_l.text: For an essentially bounded measurable coefficient field `Ω`, primitive evaluation of the bundled multiplier applied to an $L^2$ path equals the ordinary integral of $\Omega(r)v(r)$ from zero to the selected time. This removes the quotient-space packaging while preserving null-set independence. The coefficient's measurability and essential bound are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation_l.summary: Evaluating the primitive of a coefficient product gives its integral

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp.text:
Define the temporal L2 integration operator with operator norm bounded by the nonnegative duration. The resulting object is an L2 class, while pointwise representatives are treated by separate lemmas.

Default-value audit (b5): The interval duration is nonnegative. At zero duration the L2 space is trivial and the primitive operator is zero. A pointwise primitive of a chosen representative agrees only almost everywhere with the operator output.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp.summary: The bounded primitive on square integrable time paths

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_apply_ae.text: The temporal L2 primitive operator agrees almost everywhere on the interval with the ordinary interval primitive of an L2 representative.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_apply_ae.summary: The bounded primitive agrees almost everywhere

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_inner_add.text: For any two $L^2$ time paths on a nonnegative interval, the sum $\langle Ju,v\rangle+\langle u,Jv\rangle$ equals the inner product of their total time integrals. The proof uses absolutely continuous primitives and their almost-everywhere derivatives. If either terminal integral vanishes, the boundary term disappears, producing the skew-pairing identity used in endpoint coercivity.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_inner_add.summary: Integration by parts leaves the terminal integral pairing

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_inner_eq_.text: The primitive satisfies $\langle Ju,v\rangle=-\langle u,Jv\rangle$ when the test path $v$ has zero time mean. The assumptions are `hT : 0 ≤ T` and `hv : endpointIntegral T v = 0`, with both paths in $L^2$. Integration by parts leaves an endpoint product, which vanishes by `hv`. This is an inner-product identity, not a separate pointwise definition of the adjoint function.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_inner_eq_.summary: Adjoint identity against a mean zero path

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_toLp_appl.text: If an explicit velocity function has $L^2$ membership proof `hv`, then the continuous primitive operator applied to its quotient class agrees almost everywhere with the function's anchored primitive. The result combines the operator's representative formula with invariance under the `toLp` representative choice. The conclusion is not an everywhere equality of representatives.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_toLp_appl.summary: Bundling a velocity preserves its primitive formula

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_congr_ae.text: If velocities agree almost everywhere on the full positive-oriented interval, their primitives agree at every time in its closed subinterval. No choice of L2 representative affects the displacement there.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_congr_ae.summary: Almost everywhere equal velocities have equal primitives

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_eq_neg_term.text: A primitive with zero total velocity integral equals the negative integral from the current time to the terminal time. The hypotheses `hv` and `hmean` give integrability on the full interval and the zero integral; `ht` places the current time in that interval. Taking $v=z_t$ rewrites $z(t)$ in the form used before Cauchy–Schwarz. No continuous derivative is required by this identity.

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_sub_eq_inte.text: For an interval-integrable velocity and two times `a,b` in the slab, the difference of primitive values equals the oriented integral from `a` to `b`. The theorem does not require `a≤b`; interval integration handles either orientation. This identifies the increment used in continuity and half-Hölder estimates.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_sub_eq_inte.summary: Displacement increments are integrals over the intervening times

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_sub_velocit.text: For two interval-integrable velocities on the whole slab, the primitive of their difference equals the difference of their primitives at every allowed time. The membership `ht` restricts integration to a subinterval where both integrability hypotheses still apply. This linearity is used to transfer $L^2$ stability estimates to displacement paths.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_sub_velocit.summary: Primitives respect subtraction of integrable velocities

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal.text: If the integral of a velocity from zero to `T` vanishes, its anchored primitive is zero at `T`. The result simply unfolds the primitive definition and does not assume integrability or positivity of `T`. In analytic applications, those properties are supplied before this equality is used as an endpoint condition.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal.summary: Zero total time integral gives zero terminal displacement

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal_po.text: The same mean-zero $L^2$ velocity gives $\int_0^T|z|^2\le(T^2/2)\int_0^T|v|^2$. The hypotheses `hT`, `hv` and `hmean` are nonnegative duration, square integrability and zero total integral. The proof integrates the pointwise terminal estimate; the factor $T^2/2$ comes from integrating $T-t$. This is a Sobolev-level statement through the primitive representation, not only an estimate for continuously differentiable paths.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal_po.summary: Integrated Poincaré bound for a zero trace displacement

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal_po.text: The primitive of a mean-zero $L^2$ velocity satisfies $|z(t)|^2\le(T-t)\int_0^T|v|^2$. The binder `hv : MemLp v 2 ...` supplies the square integrability, `hmean` supplies the zero terminal trace, and `ht` gives $0\le t\le T$. The initial trace is zero by the definition of the primitive. The theorem is stated for complete real normed spaces, so it includes the paper’s three-dimensional displacement.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal_po.summary: Pointwise Poincaré bound for a zero trace displacement

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_zero.text: The time primitive at zero is zero for any integrand, because the integration interval has zero length. No regularity assumption is needed.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_zero.summary: The displacement primitive starts at zero

TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator.text: Build $B=K-J\Omega$ on the joint $L^2$ space, first multiplying by each coefficient and then integrating the vorticity term in time. `hK`, `hΩ`, `bK`, and `bΩ` supply measurable, essentially bounded coefficients. The definition itself imposes neither ellipticity nor the endpoint constraint; these enter the inverse theorem.
TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator.summary: Multiplication minus integrated vorticity in the joint space

TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator_apply.text: Under the measurable bounded coefficient hypotheses, the operator representative equals $K(t,a)v(t,a)-\int_0^t\Omega(s,a)v(s,a)\,ds$ almost everywhere. The proof uses slice congruence to replace the representative of the intermediate multiplier inside the integral. It establishes the formula for arbitrary joint $L^2$ input, before projection.
TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator_apply.summary: The joint operator has the integrated equation formula

TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator_coerc.text: The hypothesis `hslice` supplies a lower bound for the explicit $K v-J(\Omega v)$ expression on almost every label slice. The theorem transfers it to the inner product of the bundled joint operator with `v`. Measurability and coefficient bounds remain explicit; no zero-mean or divergence condition is inferred automatically.
TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator_coerc.summary: Slice bounds give coercivity of the joint operator

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive.text:
Define the bounded joint L2 time primitive, integrating at fixed label, with operator norm bounded by the nonnegative duration.

Default-value audit (b5): The construction takes a nonnegative duration and yields a bounded operator on joint L2 classes. It is zero for duration zero and does not choose classical time derivatives.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive.summary: The time primitive in the joint integral space

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveRep.text: At a pair `q`, integrate the chosen representative of `v` from zero to `q.1`, with label `q.2` fixed. The integration measure is already restricted to $(0,T]$. This representative is defined everywhere; later results identify it with the ordinary primitive only inside the time slab.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveRep.summary: Integrate time while keeping the label fixed

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveRep_e.text: For `hq : q.1 ∈ Icc 0 T`, the extra restriction to $(0,T]$ does not change integration from zero to `q.1`. The chosen product representative therefore equals `endpointPrimitive` on that label slice. This equality is pointwise for the indicated representative, without asserting pointwise integrability of every slice.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveRep_e.summary: The restricted integral is the usual primitive

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive_ae_t.text: For almost every label, the input has an $L^2$ time slice and the joint primitive agrees almost everywhere in time with `endpointPrimitiveLp` applied to that slice. The existential `hv` records the needed MemLp proof. The statement separates a label null set from the time null sets of representatives.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive_ae_t.summary: Joint integration agrees with the one label operator

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive_appl.text: The chosen representative of the bundled joint primitive agrees almost everywhere with the ordinary time primitive of the input slice. The conclusion is a product-measure equality, not an identity for every representative and every label. Nonnegative `T` and almost-everywhere membership in the restricted interval justify the identification.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive_appl.summary: The joint operator integrates each label path

TorusEuler.endpointProduct_inner_lower_b.text: Assume `h` bounds the time-integrated inner product of `w` and `v` below by `c` times the time-slice energy for almost every label. Fubini yields $c\|v\|_2^2\le\langle w,v\rangle$ in the joint Hilbert space. This transfer does not require `c` to be positive; positivity is needed when inverting.
TorusEuler.endpointProduct_inner_lower_b.summary: Integrating slice coercivity preserves the constant

TorusEuler.endpointProjectedHilbertOpera.text: The compression of a bounded operator to a closed Hilbert subspace is injective when its quadratic form is bounded below by $\kappa\|v\|^2$ there. The inputs are `hV`, positive `hκ`, and `hK`. The result is used for the difference of the weak and recovered solutions at almost every time. It is an abstract Hilbert-space statement; the application identifies the subspace with spatially solenoidal fields.
TorusEuler.endpointProjectedHilbertOpera.summary: Ellipticity gives uniqueness of the weak spatial solution

TorusEuler.endpointProjectedMixedResidua.text: Rewrite a differentiated compressed equation with its forcing and Leibniz correction as a vanishing projected mixed residual. This is the form required by the time-recovery helper.
TorusEuler.endpointProjectedMixedResidua.summary: The differentiated equation has zero projected residual

TorusEuler.endpointProjectedWeak_eq_mean.text: If subtraction of the temporal mean sends an $L^2$ path to zero, that path equals its average almost everywhere. The input is `h : endpointSubtractMean T w = 0`; the recovered value is $T^{-1}\int_0^T w$. This identifies the constant component of the weak projected momentum equation. It does not by itself supply spatial regularity or a pointwise-in-time representative of that equation.
TorusEuler.endpointProjectedWeak_eq_mean.summary: Recovering the constant removed by time projection

TorusEuler.endpointProjection_eq_zero_of.text: For positive `T` and `t ∈ [0,T]`, assume a continuous-field-valued path `G` has derivative `dG` within the slab and its weak spatial projection vanishes throughout. Then the projection of `dG` vanishes too. The bounded projection commutes with differentiation, and positive interval length supplies uniqueness of the derivative within the closed slab.
TorusEuler.endpointProjection_eq_zero_of.summary: Differentiation preserves a vanishing spatial projection

TorusEuler.endpointProjection_residual_e.text: If the weak projection of `F` equals the embedding of a solenoidal half-Hölder field `c`, subtracting `c` from `F` leaves a field with zero weak projection. This is the algebraic step preparing pressure reconstruction after the time-independent component has been recovered. The solenoidal membership of `c` is carried by its subtype.
TorusEuler.endpointProjection_residual_e.summary: Subtract the recovered solenoidal constant from the residual

TorusEuler.endpointRealFourierCharacter.text: For lattice frequency `k` and complex amplitude `c`, define the real continuous character $a\mapsto\operatorname{Re}(c e_k(a))$. Varying `c` includes cosine and sine tests. These real characters let the proof describe time-valued Fourier moments without first complexifying the entire joint time-space Hilbert space.
TorusEuler.endpointRealFourierCharacter.summary: Real Fourier characters include cosine and sine phases

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredPrimitive_ha.text: The primitive of the recovered continuous velocity has zero values at both ends and has that velocity as its derivative within the interval. The assumptions are a nonnegative length, an injective continuous linear embedding `hEmb`, continuity `hv`, almost-everywhere agreement `hRep`, and the weak zero-mean condition `hMean`. The initial trace follows from the integral definition. Injectivity transfers the terminal trace from the weak space to the strong space.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredPrimitive_ha.summary: The recovered displacement retains both zero endpoint values

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredPrimitive_of.text: A continuous half-Hölder solenoidal representative of a velocity in the endpoint subspace has primitive zero at both $0$ and `T`. Its primitive has within-interval derivative equal to the representative throughout the closed slab. The terminal zero comes from the weak zero-time-mean constraint and injectivity of the embedding into spatial $L^2$.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredPrimitive_of.summary: The recovered primitive vanishes at both endpoints

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredSpatialHiera.text: A finite hierarchy of mixed spatial derivatives with continuous time representatives retains each spatial derivative relation at every time. Almost-everywhere representative agreement and continuity promote the identities to the closed slab.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredSpatialHiera.summary: Recovered spatial derivative hierarchies agree at every time

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredTimeSlice_di.text: For a mixed field and its spatial derivative with continuous time representatives, every nonzero spatial difference quotient of the recovered field equals the segment average of the recovered derivative. This holds at every time in $[0,T]$, including endpoints. The proof first compares primitives, then differentiates within the closed interval using `hT : 0 < T`.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredTimeSlice_di.summary: Recovered difference quotients equal derivative averages

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredTimeSlice_ha.text: Continuous time representatives of a mixed field and its torus directional derivative retain that derivative relation at every time in the closed slab. Both almost-everywhere slice comparisons and both continuity assumptions are needed. The argument passes through exact segment-average identities, avoiding any unsupported differentiation of chosen $L^2$ representatives.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredTimeSlice_ha.summary: Spatial derivatives persist through time recovery

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveryBudget_scalar.text: If the two inverse caps cost at most $C_sQ^{145}$ and $C_mQ^{145}$, projection norms have fixed bounds, and the remaining coefficient cost is at most $6Q$, the recovery expression is bounded by a fixed prefactor times $Q^{291}$. The hypotheses control signs needed for multiplication. This explicit degree is a sufficient bound, with no claim of sharpness.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveryBudget_scalar.summary: Two inverse caps yield one fixed polynomial power

TorusEuler.endpointSkew.text: Defines the operator $F^*(M^*-M)F$ on a complete real Hilbert space. In the flow application, `F` is the deformation and `M` the velocity gradient along trajectories, so this is the pulled-back vorticity coefficient. The definition itself requires neither a flow equation nor invertibility of `F`; those conditions enter later coercivity theorems.

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord.text: Defines a derivative word by recursively applying the within-slab Fréchet derivative in each prescribed constant space-time direction. The first letter is the outermost derivative, and the empty word is the original field. This definition accommodates both temporal and spatial directions; genuine derivative properties are proved later under smoothness and positive-duration assumptions.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord.summary: Successive directional derivatives within the closed slab

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_c.text: On a positive-duration closed slab, applying any finite word of constant space-time directional derivatives to a smooth field produces another smooth field there. Positive duration gives uniqueness of within-slab derivatives, including temporal endpoints. The statement is independent of periodicity and imposes no linear-independence condition on the chosen directions.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_c.summary: Every derivative word stays smooth on the slab

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_e.text: For smooth data and a time inside a positive-duration slab, derivative words whose directions have zero time component agree with the existing `phaseOperatorWord` applied to the spatial slice. The proof identifies the within-slab derivative with the ordinary derivative of that slice. The result reconciles two encodings of the same spatial derivatives.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_e.summary: Pure spatial slab words agree with spatial operator words

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_h.text: For a smooth field on a positive-duration slab, prefixing a purely spatial direction to a word gives the ordinary derivative of that word along the corresponding spatial line. The time is fixed anywhere in $[0,T]$, including endpoints. Spatial differentiation remains two-sided because the spatial domain is unrestricted.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_h.summary: A spatial letter gives a two-sided line derivative

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_h.text: For a smooth field on a positive-duration slab, prefixing the direction $(1,0)$ yields the time derivative of a word at any fixed spatial point. The derivative is explicitly within $[0,T]$, so both endpoints are included. This does not claim smooth extension or an ordinary two-sided time derivative outside the slab.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_h.summary: A time letter gives the closed-interval derivative

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_p.text: If every time slice of a field is periodic on the slab, every constant space-time directional word remains periodic there, even when directions have time components. The proof uses translation invariance of the domain and congruence of the total within-derivative operator. This invariance statement alone does not assert differentiability; it carries no smoothness or positive-duration hypothesis.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_p.summary: Within-slab derivative words preserve spatial periodicity

TorusEuler.endpointSlabLiftDirections.text: Encodes one time direction $(1,0)$ and a family of purely spatial directions $(0,u_i)$ using `Sum Unit I`. This allows time and spatial letters to appear in the same derivative word without confusing their meaning. The spatial family is arbitrary and need not be a basis or contain nonzero vectors.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabLiftDirections.summary: Separating the time direction from spatial directions

TorusEuler.endpointSlabSpatialWord.text: Takes a list of spatial direction indices, tags every letter as spatial, and evaluates the corresponding within-slab derivative word. The empty list still denotes the original field. This is the common lifted expression represented by both strong half-Hölder coefficient curves and their mixed temporal realizations.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabSpatialWord.summary: Spatial words inside the common space-time encoding

TorusEuler.endpointSlabSpatialWord_eq_sp.text: On a smooth positive time slab, the coordinate words in the geometric jet structure equal the ordinary iterated spatial partial derivatives of each time slice.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabSpatialWord_eq_sp.summary: Spatial words are ordinary derivatives of the lift

TorusEuler.endpointSolenoidalEmbedding.text:
Restrict the Holder-to-L2 embedding to its divergence-free subspace, retaining the proof that the target lies in the weak solenoidal subspace.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a restriction of the same natural embedding to proven solenoidal subspaces. There is no coefficient inversion or exceptional branch.
TorusEuler.endpointSolenoidalEmbedding.summary: Embedding solenoidal Holder fields into the weak space

TorusEuler.endpointSolenoidalEmbedding_i.text: The embedding from solenoidal half-Hölder fields to solenoidal spatial $L^2$ fields is injective. Equality of embedded subtype elements reduces to equality in the full Hilbert space, then to equality of the original continuous representatives. Restricting to the divergence-free subspaces does not lose this uniqueness property.
TorusEuler.endpointSolenoidalEmbedding_i.summary: The constrained Hölder embedding remains injective

TorusEuler.endpointSourceCurve_eq_negPri.text: If a continuous force curve and source curve have lifts related by the negative time integral, then the source curve itself equals the negative Banach-valued force primitive throughout the interval. Evaluation commutes with the integral.
TorusEuler.endpointSourceCurve_eq_negPri.summary: A pointwise source formula determines its Holder primitive

TorusEuler.endpointSourceWords_eq_negPri.text: If a spatial derivative hierarchy has the base source equal to the negative force primitive, compatibility of its spatial derivatives and time regularity propagates that identity to every available word. The proof identifies derivatives and zero initial values on the closed interval.
TorusEuler.endpointSourceWords_eq_negPri.summary: Every source derivative is a negative force primitive

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialAllFiniteMixed.text: For a cutoff `N`, derivative families of the source and coefficient through the required orders yield a family `w` with `w [] = v`. Every word of length at most `N` satisfies the projected equation with its lower-order correction, and shorter words have the next directional derivative. The inverse, positive coercivity, weak bound, and translation compatibility remain explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialAllFiniteMixed.summary: Construct the full finite hierarchy of spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialComplexificati.text: Instantiate the abstract complexification with real and complex Euclidean three-space. Coordinatewise embedding, real part, and imaginary part satisfy reconstruction, multiplication-by-$i$ identities, and squared-norm splitting. The object makes these concrete formulas available uniformly to the abstract extension machinery used by frozen spatial symbols.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialComplexificati.summary: Euclidean velocities have their standard complexification

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative.text: A compatible self-adjoint Hilbert operator supplies the weak bound and pairing for `P`. Together with positive coercivity, the compressed inverse, and actual directional derivatives of the coefficient and source, this gives the directional derivative of `v`. The conclusion records its projection constraint, commutator equation, and inverse norm estimate, rather than merely a formal differentiated identity.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative.summary: The compressed solution inherits one spatial derivative

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_can.text: Given an actual equivalence `S` for the compressed coefficient and a projected source derivative `df`, this theorem constructs a projected candidate `w` solving the linearized coefficient equation. Its norm is bounded using the inverse norm and the coefficient product estimate. No derivative of `v` is asserted here; the limit argument establishes that identification later.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_can.summary: Solve the equation that the spatial derivative must satisfy

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.text: This version identifies the derivative from difference-quotient bounds and limits when the strong projection intertwines with a bounded Hilbert operator `Q`. That compatibility supplies the weak norm bound; the projected pairing and coercivity are still explicit assumptions. The conclusion gives the actual line derivative of `v`, its projected equation, and its inverse-based norm estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.summary: Obtain the derivative using a compatible Hilbert operator

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.text: Assume the compressed inverse, positive coercivity, translation commutation, a weak projection bound, and the specified difference-quotient bounds and supremum limits `hDfSup` and `hProdSup`. The theorem produces a projected `w` with the commutator equation and norm bound, and proves it is the line derivative of the periodic lift of `v`. The limits are hypotheses at this stage.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.summary: Identify the candidate derivative through weak error estimates

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.text: With a compressed inverse, positive coercivity, translation commutation, a projected pairing, and a weak Haar bound, directional derivative identities for `f` and `B` yield a derivative `w` of `v`. Its equation includes the coefficient commutator and its norm is bounded by the inverse norm. The theorem derives the required difference-quotient limits from the supplied actual derivative data.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.summary: Differentiate the compressed equation from actual data derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDifference_equ.text: Assume `hτ` and `hτB` identify the same shift on fields and coefficients, `hComm` says projection commutes with it, and `hEq` gives the original projected equation. The difference quotient then solves the differentiated-form equation with a coefficient difference multiplying the translated unknown. This identity is exact for every `h`, before taking any limit.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDifference_equ.summary: The difference quotient satisfies an exact commutator equation

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDifference_fix.text: If `P` commutes with `τ` and fixes `v`, it also fixes the scaled difference $h^{-1}(τv-v)$. The statement is algebraic and permits every real `h`, including zero under Lean’s total inverse. It ensures that the coercive estimate may be applied to the finite differences before their limit is identified.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDifference_fix.summary: Difference quotients remain in the projected subspace

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDivergenceTest.text: This bounded functional pairs a spatial $L^2$ field with the gradient of a smooth periodic potential. It is the fixed-time counterpart of the joint endpoint divergence test. The velocity need not possess classical derivatives; vanishing of all such functionals is the weak solenoidal condition.

Evaluation of the spatial divergence functional is the torus integral of the real inner product of the potential gradient with the $L^2$ velocity. The proof replaces the continuous gradient’s $L^2$ representative almost everywhere. This formula connects the abstract kernel condition to the standard weak divergence definition.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDivergenceTest.summary: The fixed time test is an integral gradient pairing

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSecondMixedDer.text: This version of the second derivative step uses compatibility with a self-adjoint Hilbert operator `Q` to obtain the weak estimate and pairing. The supplied first commutator equation and directional derivative data determine the new source `dg`. It returns a derivative of `w₁`; it does not independently assert that arbitrary mixed derivative orders commute.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSecondMixedDer.summary: Obtain a second mixed derivative through the weak operator

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSecondMixedDer.text: Given the equation for a first derivative `w₁`, the theorem constructs its derivative in the new direction `u`. The data include derivatives of `B`, `dB₁`, `df₁`, and the original field `v`, represented by `w₂`. The new source contains both product-rule terms, and the conclusion supplies the actual second derivative, projected equation, and norm bound.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSecondMixedDer.summary: Differentiate the first commutator equation once more

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSegmentAverage.text: Defines a continuous linear map that averages a half-Hölder vector field along the segment with lifted displacement $hu$, using the parameter interval $[0,1]$. The construction proves operator norm at most one. It averages the evaluation values themselves, so even a zero-length segment is meaningful and simply returns the value at its starting label.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSegmentAverage.summary: Averaging a spatial field along a torus segment

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSegmentAverage.text: Applying the segment-average continuous linear map to a field yields its explicit integral along the torus segment. This is a definitional equality for all labels, directions and real step lengths. It exposes the integral when proving that the recovered derivative agrees with difference quotients of the recovered field.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSegmentAverage.summary: The segment operator evaluates to its defining integral

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSlice.text:
Take the spatial L2 class of a joint field's slice when that slice is square integrable, and assign zero otherwise. The later almost-everywhere slice theorem proves the ordinary interpretation at almost every time; the definition alone gives no pointwise time representative.

Default-value audit (b5): The definition explicitly returns zero at a time whose chosen joint representative has a non-L2 slice. Fubini proves that branch is confined to a null set in the intended setting; this value cannot be used to claim pointwise time regularity before recovery.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSlice.summary: Spatial slices with an exceptional time convention

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSlice_apply_ae.text: For almost every time, the slice is square integrable and its L2 representative agrees almost everywhere in labels with the joint field. Fubini excludes the exceptional branch on a full-measure set.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSlice_apply_ae.summary: Spatial slices agree almost everywhere with the joint field

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSolenoidal.text: This submodule is the intersection of the kernels of spatial divergence tests over all smooth periodic potentials. It encodes distributional divergence freedom in the spatial $L^2$ space. It imposes no zero spatial mean: constant vector fields belong to the intended solenoidal space.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSolenoidal.summary: The Hilbert subspace of weakly divergence free fields

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialWeakErrorEstim.text: For a field fixed by the projection, pointwise coercivity and the projection pairing identity bound its Haar $L^2$ norm by the projected residual norm. The proof tests the residual against the field and then uses Cauchy–Schwarz. It normalizes the coercivity constant to $\min(1,\mu)$, so the displayed estimate in Appendix A with coefficient $\mu$ is not its literal intermediate inequality. The hypotheses require $\mu>0$; hence the reciprocal of $\min(1,\mu)$ is protected. The field and coefficient live in bundled Hölder spaces, which supply boundedness and integrability for the Haar embedding.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialWeakErrorEstim.summary: Projected residual controls the weak spatial error

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialWordCoefficien.text: At a fixed time, this operator multiplies a solenoidal half-Hölder field by the half-Hölder coefficient $K(t)$. Its target is the full half-Hölder space, since multiplication need not preserve divergence. The definition composes ordinary coefficient multiplication with the subspace inclusion; projection is supplied elsewhere when solving the mean equation.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialWordCoefficien.summary: Restrict coefficient multiplication to solenoidal fields

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray.text:
Define the path-valued Fourier multiplier imposing both spatial solenoidality and zero time mean. Its time-path Hilbert space is built over the specified interval; agreement with the joint L2 orthogonal projection is a later theorem.

Default-value audit (b5): For nonpositive T the restricted time measure on (0,T] is zero and the path space is degenerate. The concrete mixed projection remains defined, but the theorems identifying the endpoint constraint and proving idempotence in the intended setting assume T positive.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray.summary: The combined spatial and time mean projection

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_agre.text: For positive duration, embedding the strong mixed projection into joint L2 equals the orthogonal projection onto the joint endpoint constraint space.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_agre.summary: The mixed projection agrees with its Hilbert version

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_allS.text: The same finite spatial derivative hierarchy is constructed for fields valued in temporal $L^2$ paths on a positive interval. The hypotheses `hv`, `heq`, `S`, `hS`, `hμ`, `hcoercive`, `hB`, and `hf` supply a solved compressed equation, its base inverse, coercivity, and actual jets. Every returned derivative remains in the mixed fixed subspace. The exact commutator and norm estimate involve only lower solution words and differentiated coefficients.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_allS.summary: Differentiated equations for the time path inverse

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_comp.text: With `X` the complexification of the $L^2$ time-path space, the Fourier coefficient of the strong mixed projection is obtained by extending `angularTimeLeray` complex-linearly. The coefficient statement applies for the supplied `T`. It identifies the combined constraint operator with the symbol used in the path-valued freezing construction.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_comp.summary: Complex Fourier modes carry the combined projection

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_haar.text: For positive duration, the Haar L2 norm of the mixed field cannot increase under the combined projection. This weak norm control is used when passing difference quotients through the projection.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_haar.summary: The mixed projection contracts the spatial integral norm

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_idem.text: For positive duration, the strong mixed projection is idempotent, by injectivity of the mixed-to-joint embedding and idempotence of the Hilbert-space projection.

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_mem_.text: For positive duration, the joint L2 image of a strongly projected mixed field lies in the weak solenoidal zero-time-mean space.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_mem_.summary: The mixed projection satisfies the weak constraints

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_pair.text: For positive `T` and a path-valued field `v` fixed by the mixed projection, projecting `w` does not change its Haar pairing with `v`. The proof uses the joint weak orthogonal projection and the equality of mixed inner products. This supplies the projected coercivity pairing for the time-dependent endpoint inverse.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_pair.summary: The mixed projection disappears against constrained fields

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_real.text: Every real-character moment of a path-valued half-Hölder field is transformed by `angularTimeLeray` when the strong mixed projection is applied. The time-path space uses the restricted measure on $(0,T]$. The symbol combines spatial projection with removal of the time mean; no positivity assumption on `T` is needed for this algebraic coefficient identity.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_real.summary: The mixed projection acts by the time path symbol

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_seco.text: For a positive time interval, a first mixed-projection derivative equation and the required directional derivative data yield its next spatial derivative. The explicit source `dg` contains both product-rule terms. The result remains fixed by the mixed projector and obeys the stated inverse norm estimate; time differentiability is addressed by separate recovery arguments.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_seco.summary: Take a second spatial derivative of the mixed solution

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_spat.text: For positive `T`, the concrete mixed Leray projection supplies the abstract translation and weak estimates on time-path-valued half-Hölder fields. With coefficient and source derivative data, positive coercivity, and the compressed inverse, the theorem produces a spatial derivative of the mixed solution. It preserves both the spatial projection and zero-time-mean constraint encoded by the fixed space.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_spat.summary: Differentiate the path valued projected endpoint equation

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_time.text: For positive `T`, the time integral of the projected path is zero at every torus label. The pointwise-in-label conclusion is stronger than an almost-everywhere representative statement because the result lies in a continuous half-Hölder space. The hypothesis `hT` makes the time-mean normalization legitimate.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_time.summary: The mixed projection has zero time mean at every label

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_toru.text: The combined spatial and time-mean projection commutes with translations on the label torus. Its Fourier-symbol action makes this true for every interval parameter.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_toru.summary: The mixed projection commutes with label translations

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray.text:
Define the concrete spatial Leray projection as a real homogeneous Fourier multiplier on half-Holder vector fields. Its fixed-space characterization and idempotence are separate theorems.

Default-value audit (b5): The Fourier multiplier is defined on all half-Holder fields. Its Leray symbol includes the zero spatial mode; mean vector fields are retained rather than silently removed. Fixed-space and projection properties are proved separately.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray.summary: The spatial Leray projection on Holder fields

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_ag.text: Embedding the strong spatial Leray projection of a real half-Hölder field in $L^2$ gives the real Hilbert-space Leray projection of the embedded field. This is an equality of operators on the shared inputs. It transfers orthogonality and the weak divergence constraint to the strong projection used in the freezing inverse.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_ag.summary: The Hölder and Hilbert Leray projections agree

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_al.text: All derivative words through order `N` of the spatial solution exist and satisfy the differentiated compressed equation and a lower-order norm estimate. Inputs include `hv`, `heq`, an already supplied equivalence `S` with identification `hS`, coercivity `hcoercive`, and genuine coefficient and source jets `hB`, `hf`. The term `endpointMixedCorrection B w t` is the Leibniz commutator. This theorem propagates regularity of a solved equation; it does not construct the initial inverse.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_al.summary: Differentiated equations for the spatial compressed inverse

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_co.text: The complexified Fourier coefficient of the strong spatial projection equals the complex-linear extension of `angularLeray` acting on the original coefficient. This is the complex form of the already established real-character law. It is used when composing with the frozen inverse multipliers and when proving commutation with translations.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_co.summary: Spatial Leray has the complexified transverse symbol

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_fi.text: Identify the fixed space of the concrete strong Leray operator with the weakly divergence-free half-Holder subspace. This allows the freezing isomorphism to be used in the endpoint solver's space.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_fi.summary: The Leray fixed space is the solenoidal space

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_fi.text: A half-Holder field is fixed by the concrete Leray operator exactly when its L2 image is weakly divergence free. Agreement with the L2 orthogonal projection proves both directions.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_fi.summary: Leray fixed fields are exactly divergence free

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_ha.text: The Haar $L^2$ norm of a half-Hölder field cannot increase under the strong spatial Leray projection. Agreement with the orthogonal real $L^2$ Leray projector supplies the contraction. This gives the weak bound with constant one in the concrete spatial derivative argument; it is not a contraction claim for the Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_ha.summary: Spatial Leray contracts the embedded Hilbert norm

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_id.text: The strong spatial Leray projection is idempotent. The proof places its image in the solenoidal fixed space rather than relying on an unproved formal projection label.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_id.summary: Applying the spatial Leray projection twice

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pa.text: For a field `v` fixed by the strong spatial Leray projection, the Haar pairing of `v` with the projection of `w` equals its pairing with `w`. The proof transfers the orthogonality of the $L^2$ projector through the embedding. This gives the exact energy pairing required by the abstract freezing theorem.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pa.summary: Spatial Leray disappears against a projected field

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pr.text: The actual periodic Leray projection commutes with each spatial direction.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pr.summary: Spatial derivatives commute with the Leray projection

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pr.text: If two half-Hölder fields form a torus directional derivative pair, applying the strong spatial Leray operator to both preserves that derivative relation at every label and line parameter. The proof uses translation invariance and agreement with the real $L^2$ projection. It supplies the hypothesis needed by the abstract first-order lift estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pr.summary: The actual Leray projection preserves line derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_re.text: At each integer Fourier mode, every real-character moment of the strong spatial projection is obtained by applying `angularLeray` to the original moment. The statement allows every complex character parameter `c`, encoding both real components of the coefficient. It includes the mean mode through the symbol value at zero.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_re.summary: Spatial Leray acts by the transverse real symbol

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_se.text: Starting from a projected first-derivative equation, the concrete spatial Leray theorem constructs its derivative in a further direction. The source includes the derivatives of both the coefficient and the existing product correction. It requires the listed derivative data and coercive inverse, and returns the second derivative with its equation and norm estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_se.summary: Take a second derivative of the fixed time solution

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_sp.text: For the actual spatial Leray projection, positive coercivity, a supplied compressed equivalence, and directional derivatives `df` and `dB` yield a projected derivative `w` of `v`. The theorem records the commutator equation and inverse norm estimate. Translation commutation, the weak contraction, and the pairing identity are supplied by the concrete projector lemmas.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_sp.summary: Differentiate the concrete fixed time projected equation

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_to.text: The concrete strong spatial Leray projection commutes with every torus translation on real half-Hölder vector fields. Its previously established complex Fourier coefficient law supplies the proof. This verifies one of the abstract hypotheses needed to differentiate the compressed fixed-time equation, rather than assuming translation commutation as additional data.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_to.summary: The spatial Leray projection commutes with translations

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialProjecti.text:
Restrict the codomain of the strong Leray operator to the divergence-free half-Holder subspace. The underlying projected field is unchanged.

Default-value audit (b5): The codomain restriction uses the proved idempotence of the same concrete Leray map. It changes only the subspace type; zero fields and constant fields are handled by the ordinary projection, with no fallback branch.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialProjecti.summary: Leray projection with a solenoidal target

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialProjecti.text: Embedding the strong spatial projection into L2 gives the same field as applying the weak L2 projection after embedding. This bridges the instantaneous equation between the two regularity spaces.

TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean.text: The bounded linear operator sending an $L^2$ time path to itself minus the constant path with its average value. For interval length $T$, that average is $T^{-1}\int_0^T v(t)\,dt$; the paper normalizes $T=1$. The definition uses `Lp.constL` and `endpointIntegral`, so equality is equality of $L^2$ classes. Idempotence and the identification of its range require separate positive-length lemmas.

TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_apply.text: The mean-subtraction operator sends $v$ to $v$ minus the constant $L^2$ path with value $T^{-1}\int_0^T v$. This evaluation identity has no sign hypothesis on $T$. Its interpretation as a projection onto zero-integral paths is supplied separately under positive interval length.

TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_apply_ae.text: The path representative after mean subtraction equals $w(t)-T^{-1}\int_0^T w$ almost everywhere. The theorem is stated for every real `T`; positive time is needed for the intended average interpretation in application. At zero or negative `T`, the restricted time measure is empty, so the almost-everywhere assertion is vacuous.
TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_apply_ae.summary: Mean subtraction has its normalized time integral formula

TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_isSymmet.text: For `hT : 0 < T`, the mean-subtraction map is symmetric and idempotent on the real vector-valued $L^2$ path space. Positive duration justifies the average factor $T^{-1}$. This strengthens the earlier norm-two estimate by identifying the map as an orthogonal projection, whose norm is at most one.
TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_isSymmet.summary: Time mean subtraction is an orthogonal projection

TorusEuler.endpointTemporalSpatialCorrec.text:
Sum the ordered product-rule terms in which at least one spatial derivative hits the coefficient. Only lower-order velocity words occur, which makes induction on word length possible.

Default-value audit (b5): The finite sum is zero for the empty derivative word. Every nonempty term has a positive coefficient order and lower velocity order; arbitrary input families remain allowed without any derivative compatibility until the later theorem assumes it.
TorusEuler.endpointTemporalSpatialCorrec.summary: The spatial product correction at a fixed time

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral.text: Bundle the previously constructed linear partial time integral as a continuous linear map using the bound $\sqrt T$. The domain is joint time-label $L^2$ and the codomain is spatial $L^2$ for the s-finite measure `ν`. This operator defines the zero-time-integral constraint used in the endpoint subspace.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral.summary: Time integration as a bounded operator into spatial L²

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_apply_ae.text: For a joint $L^2$ class, the output of the continuous time-integral operator agrees almost everywhere in labels with integrating the selected representative over $(0,T]$. This formula connects the abstract operator to the time-mean constraint. Equality is intentionally limited to the measure-theoretic representative level.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_apply_ae.summary: The bounded operator has the expected fiber integral

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_eq_zero_.text: The partial time-integral operator sends a joint $L^2$ class to zero exactly when its representative has zero time integral at almost every label. This identifies an algebraic kernel with the intended endpoint constraint. The conclusion remains almost everywhere in labels and does not impose a separate normalization by the interval length.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_eq_zero_.summary: The operator kernel is the zero-integral path constraint

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_toLp_app.text: If a joint field has an $L^2$ membership proof, applying the time-integral operator to its `toLp` class gives the same label function almost everywhere as integrating the original field. The result uses Fubini to handle the representative change on time fibers. It does not strengthen product almost-everywhere equality to pointwise equality.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_toLp_app.summary: Bundling explicit data preserves its time integral

TorusEuler.endpointTimeMultiplier.text:
Define multiplication by an operator curve continuous on the closed interval as a bounded operator on temporal L2. Compactness supplies its essential bound, and only values in the restricted time measure are relevant.

Default-value audit (b5): The chosen essential bound exists by continuity on a compact interval. It only constructs the same multiplication operator, not an arbitrary action. At nonpositive duration the restricted L2 space is trivial.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeMultiplier.summary: A continuous time coefficient on square integrable paths

TorusEuler.endpointTimeMultiplier_apply_.text: The bounded time multiplication operator agrees almost everywhere with application of the given coefficient to the L2 path representative.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeMultiplier_apply_.summary: The time multiplier acts pointwise almost everywhere

TorusEuler.endpointTimeParityPart.text: Applies the spatial reflection average independently to each time slice of a field. Time is neither reversed nor shifted. This makes it possible to select odd endpoint velocities and displacements and even pressure while retaining the same initial and terminal times in the forced mean equation.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeParityPart.summary: Select a spatial parity component at each time

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTest.text: This continuous linear functional pairs a joint path with a bounded time test times the gradient of a smooth periodic scalar potential. Requiring every such pairing to vanish encodes weak spatial divergence freedom. No pointwise derivative of the $L^2$ velocity is needed or claimed in this definition.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTest.summary: Testing spatial divergence with separated time factors

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTest_a.text: Evaluating the divergence test gives the joint integral of the bounded time factor times the inner product of the spatial potential gradient with the velocity. This is the standard weak divergence pairing. The time dependence of the testing factor remains arbitrary within bounded measurable functions.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTest_a.summary: The divergence test integrates a gradient pairing

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.text: For one fixed smooth potential `p`, all bounded time tests vanish exactly when its spatial gradient pairing with the velocity vanishes for almost every time. The potential is fixed outside the almost-everywhere assertion. A common full-measure set for every potential requires the later compatibility argument.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.summary: A fixed potential has zero pairing at almost every time

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.text: Assume that at almost every time a joint L² velocity has a spatial representative with a C¹ divergence-free Euclidean lift. Then all its weak time-weighted gradient tests vanish. The slice representative may vary with time and need only agree almost everywhere in labels; no jointly smooth lift is required by the theorem.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.summary: Classically solenoidal slices satisfy all weak tests

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.text: Given a square-integrable joint function `g`, suppose almost every time slice has a C¹ divergence-free lift. The quotient element `hg.toLp g` then passes every weak spatial gradient test. The proof tracks almost-everywhere agreement of the chosen L² representative with `g`, so quotient construction does not lose the solenoidal condition.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.summary: A square integrable classical field enters the weak space

TorusEuler.endpointTorusFlowOperator.text: Builds the bounded operator $v\mapsto Kv-J(\Omega v)$ on joint time-label $L^2$, with $K=F^*F$ and $\Omega=F^*(M^*-M)F$.
