The duration is nonnegative and both coefficient fields are continuous on the slab. This ambient operator does not itself enforce solenoidality or zero time mean; those restrictions enter through the endpoint subspace.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusFlowOperator.summary: The endpoint operator on space-time velocities

TorusEuler.endpointTorusFlowOperator_app.text: For any joint $L^2$ velocity, the bounded endpoint operator agrees almost everywhere with the kinetic multiplier minus the time primitive of the pulled-back vorticity multiplier at each label. The equality is for representatives, not for every space-time point. Nonnegative duration and continuity of `F` and `M` are precisely the data used to build the operator.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusFlowOperator_app.summary: The weak operator has the expected pointwise formula

TorusEuler.endpointTorusGradientPairing_.text: Let `g` on the torus be represented by a C¹ Euclidean lift `v` through `hrep`. If `hdiv` makes its divergence vanish everywhere, its Haar pairing with every smooth potential gradient is zero. Periodicity of the lift is derived from the torus representation, then periodic integration by parts proves the weak condition.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusGradientPairing_.summary: A classical solenoidal lift annihilates torus gradients

TorusEuler.endpointTorusGradientPairing_.text: For a smooth periodic lift, vanishing pairing with every smooth periodic potential gradient is equivalent to pointwise zero divergence. The reverse implication uses integration by parts; the forward implication tests against the divergence and uses continuity after an L2 identity.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusGradientPairing_.summary: Weak gradient annihilation equals zero classical divergence

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text:
Specify a Holder field as the directional derivative of another by requiring the derivative identity along every translated torus line at every real line parameter. This is a predicate about an actual supplied derivative field.

Default-value audit (b5): The supplied derivative field must satisfy HasDerivAt along every line. In zero direction that identity forces the derivative field to be zero; no arbitrary derivative default is used.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: A spatial directional derivative on torus lines

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If two half-Hölder fields have directional derivatives along the same fixed torus direction, their sum has the sum of those derivatives. The proof evaluates the fields along each translated torus line and uses the ordinary derivative sum rule. It supports the finite linear combinations arising from the differentiated mean forcing.

For a finite family of half-Hölder fields, if each indexed field has the stated derivative in one common torus direction, then their finite sum has the corresponding summed derivative. The empty finite set gives the usual derivative of zero. This rule keeps all terms when the mean forcing is assembled from finitely many product contributions.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Finite sums retain their torus derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: Multiplication of a half-Hölder field by a natural number preserves its torus directional derivative, with the same natural multiple of the derivative field. The statement uses repeated addition, matching the integer multiplicities in the product rule. It does not itself state a rule for arbitrary real or time-dependent scalar multiplication.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Natural multiplicities pass through torus derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: For two half-Hölder fields with derivatives in the same torus direction, the derivative of their difference is the difference of the derivatives. This follows pointwise along each torus line from the usual subtraction rule. It is needed for the signed coefficient corrections in the time-differentiated mean equation.

For time-smooth curves forming a spatial directional derivative pair on a positive closed interval, every available within-time derivative remains a spatial derivative pair. The endpoint derivative is taken within the interval.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Time derivatives preserve spatial derivative relations

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If `df` is the torus directional derivative of `f`, every nonzero-step difference quotient differs from `df` at the starting label by at most $\|df\|\sqrt{|h|\|u\|}$. The estimate holds in any complete real normed target. It upgrades a known derivative relation to a uniform quantitative remainder bound.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: A half-Hölder derivative controls the spatial slope error

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If two half-Hölder-valued curves form a spatial derivative pair throughout $[0,T]$ and both have within-interval derivatives at `t`, their time derivatives form the same spatial derivative pair. Positive duration provides uniqueness of derivatives within the closed interval. The result includes endpoint times and requires no extension of the curves beyond the slab.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Time differentiation preserves the spatial derivative relation

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: For half-Hölder curves in any real normed target, within-slab time differentiation preserves a spatial directional derivative relation when both curves have the required time derivatives. Positive duration ensures a nontrivial punctured within-slab filter at the evaluation time. The proof obtains uniform convergence along every torus line from the stronger half-Hölder norm, including at time endpoints.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Uniform line convergence preserves mixed derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If every nonzero directional difference quotient differs from a candidate derivative by at most $C\sqrt{|h|\|u\|}$ at every label, that candidate is the actual torus line derivative. The error tends to zero with the step. No separate sign condition on `C` is needed, because the assumed nonnegative norm bound already controls the relevant remainder.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: A square-root remainder proves spatial differentiability

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTest.text: This continuous linear functional pairs an endpoint path with a bounded spatial scalar times one coordinate unit vector. Vanishing for all such tests imposes zero time integral componentwise at almost every label. The definition itself is a Hilbert pairing; the almost-everywhere characterization is proved later.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTest.summary: Testing each component of the time integral

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTest_apply.text: Evaluating the coordinate mean test gives the joint integral of the spatial scalar test times that velocity component. This unfolds the Hilbert-space definition into a familiar scalar integral. It is the form used for Fubini and for detecting vanishing time integrals by all bounded spatial tests.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTest_apply.summary: The mean test integrates a weighted velocity component

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTests_iff_ae.text: Vanishing of every coordinate mean test is equivalent to the vector-valued time integral being zero for almost every torus label. Fubini moves the time integral inside the spatial pairing, and bounded-test detection handles each coordinate. Finitely many coordinates can share one full-measure set.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTests_iff_ae.summary: The mean tests detect zero time integral at almost every label

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeasure.text: This measure is Lebesgue measure restricted to $(0,T]$ multiplied by normalized Haar measure on the unit three-torus. It provides the joint space-time $L^2$ environment for the endpoint problem. The half-open time interval differs from the closed interval only at a null endpoint when duration is positive.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeasure.summary: Product measure for time paths on the spatial torus

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeasure_finite.text: For every real `T`, the endpoint product measure is finite. The time factor is a bounded restricted interval and the spatial factor is a probability measure. This instance justifies the later inclusion of square-integrable paths into integrable paths and the bounded-test constructions.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeasure_finite.summary: The joint time and torus measure is finite

TorusEuler.endpointTorusSpace.text:
Define the joint endpoint-velocity space as the intersection of the kernels of all time-mean tests and all spatial divergence tests. Both constraints are weak and representative independent.

Default-value audit (b5): The constraint space is defined by intersections of kernels of continuous tests, including zero time mean and weak divergence. No pointwise representative or smoothness is chosen; at a zero time measure the space is trivial.

TorusEuler.endpointTorusSpace_eq_timeKer.text: For a nonnegative slab, the endpoint subspace is the intersection of the kernel of time integration and the joint weakly solenoidal submodule. This separates the final-displacement constraint from incompressibility. The equality is between submodules of the same joint $L^2$ space; it does not equate a time derivative with a classical function at every point.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusSpace_eq_timeKer.summary: Both endpoint constraints as an intersection

TorusEuler.endpointTorusSpace_starProjec.text: For hT : 0 < T, the orthogonal projection onto the endpoint space equals spatial solenoidal projection composed with time-mean removal. Multiplication of continuous linear maps denotes composition, so the rightmost operation acts first. The proof uses the intersection description, commutation, and the characterization of an orthogonal projection by membership and orthogonality. It concerns the joint Hilbert space, without asserting Hölder boundedness.

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral.text:
Define the bounded time integral of a joint time-label L2 field, with values in spatial L2. Nonnegative duration supplies the finite-interval construction.

Default-value audit (b5): The definition takes T nonnegative; T zero gives a zero-measure time interval and the zero integration map. It acts on L2 classes, so pointwise exceptional slices are not prescribed.

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_adj.text: For hT : 0 ≤ T, the adjoint of time integration sends a spatial field v to its constant-in-time lift, almost everywhere on $(0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$. The proof tests against an arbitrary joint $L^2$ field and uses Fubini and the adjoint identity. This identifies the operator needed to subtract the temporal mean; it does not assert pointwise regularity of an $L^2$ representative.

Integrating the constant lift of a spatial field v gives $T v$ as an equality in spatial $L^2$. The binder hT : 0 ≤ T identifies the measure of $(0,T]$ with $T$. The adjoint supplies the constant lift, and almost-everywhere representative identities justify integrating it. The formula remains valid when $T=0$.

The constant-in-time adjoint lift of a solenoidal spatial field is jointly solenoidal. The proof identifies its almost-everywhere time slices with the original field and tests against gradients. The hypotheses are hT : 0 ≤ T and hw, the weak divergence constraint on the spatial input; no spatial regularity beyond $L^2$ is claimed.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_adj.summary: A constant lift preserves zero divergence

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_app.text: For nonnegative duration, the torus partial-integral operator agrees almost everywhere in the torus variable with the ordinary interval integral from zero to `T`. This changes the restricted-set integral notation to the interval notation used in the paper. It preserves the quotient-space, almost-everywhere meaning of the output.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_app.summary: On the torus the operator equals the oriented time integral

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_end.text: For hT : 0 < T, the time integral of $Qu$ is zero. The proof expands $Q$, uses $JJ^*v=Tv$, and cancels the nonzero scalar $T$. This is an equality in spatial $L^2$, hence encodes zero time mean at almost every label. It does not by itself select a continuous representative.

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_eq_.text: For nonnegative duration, the joint time integral vanishes exactly when the time primitive at the terminal time vanishes for almost every label. This is the time-mean endpoint constraint in slice form.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_eq_.summary: Zero time integral in joint and labelwise form

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_mem.text: With hT : 0 ≤ T, a joint weakly solenoidal field has a solenoidal time integral in spatial $L^2$. The proof uses the constant time test and rewrites the resulting joint pairing through the adjoint of integration. The input constraint hu is essential; integrating an arbitrary joint field does not supply divergence freedom.

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient.text:
Turn a spatial half-Holder operator field into a bounded multiplication operator on spatial L2. Its essential measurability and bound follow from the Holder field; compatibility with strong multiplication is proved elsewhere.

Default-value audit (b5): The input is already a half-Holder coefficient, so boundedness and measurability are available. The operator acts on L2 equivalence classes; representative values on null sets have no mathematical role, and no ellipticity is asserted.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient.summary: The spatial coefficient acting in square integral norm

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficientEquiv.text: Positive `κ` and the pointwise lower bound `hK` produce a continuous linear equivalence on the weak solenoidal spatial subspace. Its forward map is multiplication by `K` followed by orthogonal projection. This is weak Hilbert-space invertibility; the definition does not itself provide a half-Hölder inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficientEquiv.summary: The projected weak kinetic coefficient is invertible

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficientEquiv_.text: Applying the weak coefficient equivalence to a solenoidal vector gives the projected Hilbert operator associated with `endpointWeakCoefficient K`. This identifies the forward action of the abstract inverse construction. The same positive ellipticity hypotheses remain explicit, so the equivalence is tied to the intended projected equation.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficientEquiv_.summary: The equivalence acts as projected coefficient multiplication

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient_apply.text: For spatial $L^2$ input `v`, the representative of `endpointWeakCoefficient K v` equals $K(a)v(a)$ almost everywhere on the torus. The coefficient is half-Hölder and therefore measurable and bounded. The assertion identifies representatives of a quotient-space operator and does not claim equality on every exceptional point.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient_apply.summary: Weak multiplication agrees with the pointwise coefficient action

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient_coerc.text: If `hK` bounds $\langle K(a)z,z\rangle$ below by $\kappa\|z\|^2$ at every label and vector, multiplication by `K` has the same lower bound in spatial $L^2$. Integration preserves the constant. Positivity of `κ` is not required for this inequality, but is required to construct an inverse.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient_coerc.summary: Pointwise ellipticity gives the same weak quadratic bound

TorusEuler.endpointWeakInstant_of_subtra.text: The projected weak equation yields $P(Kv)=c+P(J\Omega)-P(L)$ almost everywhere in time, where $c$ is the average of the projected momentum. The hypotheses `h` and `hw` say that its temporal mean subtraction is zero and identify its almost-everywhere representative. The maps `K` and `P` act between the stated normed spaces. The minus sign in $Bv=Kv-J(\Omega v)$ becomes a plus sign on the right.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakInstant_of_subtra.summary: The instantaneous equation after recovering the time mean

TorusEuler.endpointWeakInstantaneous_of_.text: Assume positive `T`, measurable bounded coefficients `K` and `Ω`, and the joint weak identity `hweak` with source $-L$. The theorem extracts the spatially projected time average `c` and obtains the instantaneous projected equation for almost every time. This precedes the separate argument selecting a continuous representative; the assertion is not yet pointwise for every time.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakInstantaneous_of_.summary: Recover the instantaneous weak endpoint equation

TorusEuler.endpointWeakResidualProjected.text: If a joint residual is orthogonal to every solenoidal zero-time-mean test, its weak spatial projection equals the projection of its time average for almost every time. A countable reduction makes the equality simultaneous for all spatial test vectors.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakResidualProjected.summary: A weak residual equals its projected time average

TorusEuler.endpointWeakSpatialProjection.text:
Define the L2 orthogonal projection onto the closed weak solenoidal space, with its codomain restricted to that space. It is the Hilbert-space counterpart of the strong Holder projection.

Default-value audit (b5): The projection uses completeness of the closed weak solenoidal subspace. It is a globally defined orthogonal projection on spatial L2 and has no noninvertible-coefficient fallback.

TorusEuler.endpointWeightedPhysicalMeanE.text: Given the physical word recurrence, a common weighted source bound and inverse-weighted positive coefficient bounds, every derivative word satisfies $\ell^{|q|}\|g_q\|_{C_t}\le A_{\rm inv}M_f(1+2^NC)^{|q|}$. All scalar bounds and the duration are nonnegative. The theorem applies the abstract derivative induction to closed-time norms; it assumes the recurrence rather than constructing the physical solution.
TorusEuler.endpointWeightedPhysicalMeanE.summary: Lift the physical recurrence without repeated inverse losses

TorusEuler.endpointWeightedPhysicalMeanE.text: The physical lifting estimate needs forcing, coefficient and recurrence bounds only for sorted words through order $N$. Every correction pair remains a sublist of the original word, so the induction stays within that family. The proof extends the scalar data by zero on unsorted words internally; the conclusion is asserted only for sorted words, where the supplied data remain unchanged.
TorusEuler.endpointWeightedPhysicalMeanE.summary: Sorted multi-indices suffice for derivative lifting

TorusEuler.envelopeCutoff.text: The scalar cutoff is $1-\mathrm{smoothTransition}(s-1)$. It equals one for $s\le1$ and zero for $s\ge2$, providing the radial envelope used after substituting $s=\|a\|/\ell$. This declaration defines the scalar function only; positivity of the spatial scale belongs to the radial-envelope lemmas.
TorusEuler.envelopeCutoff.summary: A smooth cutoff between radii one and two

TorusEuler.eqOn_iteratedFDeriv_gradient_.text: On an open target set separated from the far source, the lifted multiplier pressure and kernel pressure have equal gradient jets at every order. The representative hypothesis matches the cutoff tensor on the fundamental cell. Equality on an open neighborhood gives equality of derivatives even before any regularity is separately invoked.
TorusEuler.eqOn_iteratedFDeriv_gradient_.summary: Local pressure equality identifies all gradient jets

TorusEuler.eqOn_lift_farPressureTensorMu.text: A half Hölder torus tensor whose lift matches the far cutoff tensor on the fundamental cell has pressure equal to the corresponding separated kernel integral on `U`. The support lemma removes all cell points outside the far source set. Equality of representatives is required only on that cell; periodic separation is required for every target point.
TorusEuler.eqOn_lift_farPressureTensorMu.summary: The actual multiplier agrees with the far kernel on separated targets

TorusEuler.eq_L2_of_mFourierCoeff_eq.text: Two spatial L² fields in a complete complex normed target are equal if their Fourier coefficients agree at every lattice frequency. Apply the zero-coefficient theorem to their difference, with integrability justifying coefficient subtraction. The conclusion is equality of L² classes, not equality of arbitrary representatives at every label.
TorusEuler.eq_L2_of_mFourierCoeff_eq.summary: Fourier coefficients determine Banach valued L² fields

TorusEuler.eq_endpointPrimitive_of_close.text: On a positive closed interval, a smooth periodic solenoidal velocity whose projected residual is `R` equals its initial value plus the time primitive of residual minus projected tensor divergence. The proof first identifies the actual within derivative and then applies the fundamental theorem of calculus. No separate continuity hypothesis for `R` is needed.
TorusEuler.eq_endpointPrimitive_of_close.summary: The stage equation integrates from the initial slice

TorusEuler.eq_halfHolder_of_mFourierCoef.text: Two half-Hölder fields are equal if the Fourier coefficients of their underlying continuous fields agree at every frequency. Continuous Fourier uniqueness identifies their values, and extensionality identifies the bundled objects. The theorem does not require a Fourier series to converge in the half-Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.eq_halfHolder_of_mFourierCoef.summary: Fourier coefficients determine a half Hölder field

TorusEuler.eq_of_mFourierCoeff_eq.text: Two continuous fields valued in a complete complex normed space are equal when every Fourier coefficient agrees. If values differed at one point, Hahn–Banach would supply a scalar functional detecting the difference, contradicting scalar Fourier uniqueness. This separates functions without requiring a basis or finite-dimensional target.
TorusEuler.eq_of_mFourierCoeff_eq.summary: Continuous Banach valued fields are determined by Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.eq_zero_of_integral_norm_sq_c.text: A continuous periodic vector field with zero cell integral of its squared norm vanishes at every point. The proof descends the field to the torus, obtains almost-everywhere vanishing from the nonnegative integral, and uses continuity to strengthen it to pointwise vanishing. This is the last step of the velocity uniqueness energy argument.
TorusEuler.eq_zero_of_integral_norm_sq_c.summary: Zero energy determines the zero periodic field

TorusEuler.eulerMomentum_of_prefix_dynam.text: Assuming the derivative on every closed prefix equals minus advection and the gradient of the same pressure, this proves the zero-residual momentum equation on the half-open solution interval. The result only assembles that identity; regularity, pressure normalization, periodicity and zero divergence remain separate requirements of `IsEulerSolution`.
TorusEuler.eulerMomentum_of_prefix_dynam.summary: The prefix identities give the Euler momentum equation

TorusEuler.eulerianMomentum_of_strongLab.text: The strong label momentum equation yields $B_t+MB+\nabla q=f$ for $B=Fv$. The binder `hFG` gives a right inverse of $F$, while `hF` and `hv` give the two time derivatives. The hypothesis `hEq` is the pulled-back strong momentum identity. Applying the adjoint inverse cancels the deformation adjoint. This lemma concerns the momentum equation at one label; spatial pullback and the divergence equation require the separate flow and Piola results.
TorusEuler.eulerianMomentum_of_strongLab.summary: Recovering momentum for the physical mean

TorusEuler.eval_halfHolderTorusDifferenc.text: Evaluation of the torus difference quotient at `a` equals $h^{-1}$ times the difference between the values at `a + toUnitTorus (h • u)` and `a`. The identity holds even at zero step because both sides use the same totalized inverse. Derivative statements later exclude the zero step when dividing increments.
TorusEuler.eval_halfHolderTorusDifferenc.summary: Evaluate the directional quotient as a difference of values

TorusEuler.eval_homogeneousHalfHolderMul.text: For a symbol smooth away from zero with `A 0 = 0`, a torus half Hölder input supported in a compact set separated from `x` has multiplier value equal to the corresponding periodic kernel integral. The support condition is imposed on the fundamental cell. The proof passes finite dyadic convolution identities to the limit with absolute integral bounds.
TorusEuler.eval_homogeneousHalfHolderMul.summary: The bounded multiplier agrees with its separated kernel integral

TorusEuler.eval_lift_recoveredSpatialWor.text: A smooth base field and a family of torus representatives are assumed to agree at the empty word and to satisfy the spatial derivative relation at every lower order. Induction then identifies each recovered representative with the corresponding ordinary spatial derivative word. Uniqueness of line derivatives makes this an identity for the same base field, not merely an existence assertion.
TorusEuler.eval_lift_recoveredSpatialWor.summary: Recovered derivative fields equal the actual lift derivatives

TorusEuler.eval_pressureTensorMultiplier.text: For a half Hölder tensor supported in a compact cell source set separated from the observation point, the real Fourier pressure multiplier equals `periodicFarPressure`. The proof uses the complex multiplier agreement and proves integrability before moving real part through the integral. The support assumption is precisely the condition that all omitted cell sources vanish.
TorusEuler.eval_pressureTensorMultiplier.summary: The Fourier pressure multiplier equals the far integral on separated data

TorusEuler.eval_realifyHalfHolderMultipl.text: At any spatial point $a$, evaluation of the realified operator on $f$ equals the real part of the value of $L$ applied to the pointwise complex embedding of $f$. The formula unfolds the two Hölder mapping operations and makes subsequent estimates or identities possible at the level of actual point values.

TorusEuler.eval_sub_homogeneousHalfHolde.text: For two spatial labels, the difference of full multiplier outputs equals the difference of the dyadic outputs alone. The mean contribution is a constant field, so it cancels exactly. This identity allows off-support increment estimates to ignore the separately handled zero mode without dropping its contribution to the overall supremum norm.
TorusEuler.eval_sub_homogeneousHalfHolde.summary: The zero mode disappears from spatial increments

TorusEuler.eval_torusHalfHolderDirection.text: Evaluating the bundled directional field at a label equals applying the original operator field there to the chosen direction. This is a definitional identity. It makes the connection between derivative columns and arbitrary directional derivatives explicit when proving that a spatial operator preserves first-order regularity.
TorusEuler.eval_torusHalfHolderDirection.summary: The directional field has the expected pointwise value

TorusEuler.eval_torusHalfHolderProjected.text: At any label, applying the reconstructed projected operator field to `v` equals evaluating `P` applied to the original field in direction `v`. Linearity and the coordinate-basis expansion of `v` prove the identity. It ensures that projecting coordinate columns is consistent with projecting arbitrary directional values.
TorusEuler.eval_torusHalfHolderProjected.summary: Projected columns recover every projected directional derivative

TorusEuler.even_endpointParityPart.text: Proves invariance under spatial inversion for the reflection average with sign one. The result applies to arbitrary real vector-space-valued functions, although the main use is scalar pressure. Evenness follows algebraically from double negation and commutativity, before imposing any pressure normalization or differential equation.
TorusEuler.even_endpointParityPart.summary: The positive-sign average is an even field

TorusEuler.even_fderiv_of_odd.text: The Fréchet derivative of an odd map is an even function of its argument. The only functional hypothesis is `hf : Function.Odd f`; the statement is valid between real normed spaces. Applied to the odd parent flow it gives the parity of $D_aX$, and applied to the velocity it gives the parity needed for the material gradient.

TorusEuler.even_firstWaveSmoothSeed.text: The first-wave smooth seed is unchanged under label reflection for arbitrary time, scale and shear parameter. Its entire label dependence factors through the even accumulated shear. This verifies the seed parity needed for the vector potential and ultimately the odd Eulerian velocity.
TorusEuler.even_firstWaveSmoothSeed.summary: The explicit first seed is even in the label

TorusEuler.even_firstWaveSweep.text: At every fixed time, the accumulated stationary shear is unchanged by negating the label. This follows from the evenness of cosine in the second coordinate. The identity does not require a small time interval or any restriction on the size of the shear parameter.
TorusEuler.even_firstWaveSweep.summary: The accumulated shear is even in the label

TorusEuler.even_firstWaveTransportedCove.text: The explicit first-wave covector is an even function of the label at each fixed time. Its two-component expression depends on the label only through the even accumulated shear. The identity holds for arbitrary real frequency, including the zero covector case, and supports the potential parity calculation.
TorusEuler.even_firstWaveTransportedCove.summary: The first transported covector is even in the label

TorusEuler.even_localizedTransportedProf.text: An even phase profile and an even vector coefficient, multiplied by a radial envelope and transported by an odd inverse label map, produce an even localized field. The support condition is $2r\le1/2$, sufficient for vanishing on the walls. This parity theorem needs no smoothness assumption and prepares the oddness proof for the curl velocity.
TorusEuler.even_localizedTransportedProf.summary: An even potential stays even after odd transport

TorusEuler.even_pressure_of_odd_momentum.text: On a selected time slice, assumes odd velocity throughout the time set, odd actual momentum residual and differentiable pressure. It first obtains an odd pressure gradient. The difference between pressure at opposite points has zero derivative and vanishes at the origin, hence is identically zero. No separate zero-mean pressure condition is needed.
TorusEuler.even_pressure_of_odd_momentum.summary: Odd velocity and residual force an even pressure

TorusEuler.even_pressure_on_closedSlab_o.text: Applies the single-slice pressure-parity result at every time of a closed slab. Joint pressure smoothness supplies differentiability of each spatial slice, while odd velocity and residual are assumed throughout that slab. The theorem preserves those exact fields and does not construct a new pressure normalization.
TorusEuler.even_pressure_on_closedSlab_o.summary: Every pressure slice has the compatible even symmetry

TorusEuler.even_transportedProfile.text: When the inverse-label map is odd and the profile is invariant under simultaneous label and phase negation, the evaluated physical field is even. The theorem is stated for any target type, though pressure is its intended application. It requires the actual reflection hypotheses and does not derive them from periodicity.
TorusEuler.even_transportedProfile.summary: An even profile gives an even physical pressure

TorusEuler.even_wavePressurePrimitive.text: For profile width between zero and one, the zero-mean periodic primitive of the odd wave profile is even. This supplies the parity of the leading pressure.
TorusEuler.even_wavePressurePrimitive.summary: The pressure primitive of the odd profile is even

TorusEuler.eventually_half_curl_power_lo.text: For positive `c` and a frequency sequence tending to infinity, the quantity $c\mu_j^{1/8}-B\mu_j^{1/32}-B$ eventually exceeds $(c/2)\mu_j^{1/8}$. The scalar `B` is arbitrary; nonnegativity is not required. The result compares a positive leading power with a smaller power and a constant, and supplies no explicit threshold.
TorusEuler.eventually_half_curl_power_lo.summary: The leading curl power eventually absorbs both errors

TorusEuler.eventually_inductive_projecti.text: If frequencies tend to infinity and satisfy the three-step logarithmic gain bound, the eighth power of the later gain is eventually at most the preceding frequency to power one eighth. Positivity of the gain is included. The proof compares $(\log\mu)^{16}$ with $\mu^{1/8}$, keeping the shifted indices explicit.
TorusEuler.eventually_inductive_projecti.summary: Logarithmic window losses are absorbed by a frequency power

TorusEuler.exists_affineWave_transverse_.text: For a continuous background and a nonvanishing wave vector solving its transport equation on a closed slab, amplitude transport is a continuous linear equivalence between the perpendicular planes at two selected times. Every initial transverse vector has a transported amplitude path that stays perpendicular. No differentiability or self-adjoint acceleration condition on the background is assumed. This is why the result applies to the perturbed background in Lemma 2.6.
TorusEuler.exists_affineWave_transverse_.summary: Amplitude evolution is an equivalence of transverse planes

TorusEuler.exists_angularLeray_frozen_in.text: For each order $n$, one $D\ge1$ bounds the inverse-symbol derivatives for spatial vector coefficients and for time-path coefficients. Both cases require positive coercivity; the path case also requires positive duration and coercivity only on zero-integral paths. The bound is explicit in $\|\xi\|^{-1}$, $\|B\|+1$, and reciprocal coercivity.
TorusEuler.exists_angularLeray_frozen_in.summary: One angular constant controls both frozen inverse families

TorusEuler.exists_angularLeray_jet_bound.text: For each finite order $n$, there is $D\ge1$ such that every derivative of order $i\le n$ is bounded by $(D/\|\xi\|)^i$ for nonzero frequency. Order zero uses the contraction bound. A single constant can therefore be passed to the general frozen-inverse differentiation theorem.
TorusEuler.exists_angularLeray_jet_bound.summary: One constant controls all angular orders up to n

TorusEuler.exists_angularProjection_annu.text: Chooses one $D\ge1$ bounding derivatives through order five of the spatial angular Leray projection by $D^i$ whenever $\|\xi\|\ge1/2$. The same $D$ also controls the time-dependent angular projection for every $T>0$. Its existential quantifier precedes $T$, giving interval-independent control; the statement actually covers the entire exterior region, not only a bounded annulus.
TorusEuler.exists_angularProjection_annu.summary: One derivative constant controls spatial and mixed projections

TorusEuler.exists_annularLocalize_mass_l.text: For fixed cutoff and value spaces, there is a nonnegative constant controlling the localized symbol’s derivative mass by a common bound `M` on derivatives of orders zero through five on $1/2\le\|\xi\|\le2$. Smoothness off zero is explicit. The later universal theorem strengthens the quantifier order to make the constant independent of the value spaces.
TorusEuler.exists_annularLocalize_mass_l.summary: Five annular derivative bounds control the localized mass

TorusEuler.exists_annularLocalize_mass_u.text: For a fixed smooth normalized cutoff, choose a nonnegative constant before quantifying over the input and output complex normed spaces. It bounds localized derivative mass from a common bound on annular derivatives through order five. This quantifier order prevents the constant from depending on the dimension or identity of the time-path value spaces.
TorusEuler.exists_annularLocalize_mass_u.summary: One localization constant works for all complex value spaces

TorusEuler.exists_bandBernsteinJetBounds.text: There are nonnegative constants $K_m$ such that a continuous torus field with norm at most $A$ and Fourier coefficients zero beyond radius $4D$ lifts to a smooth Euclidean field with derivatives bounded by $K_m A D^m$. The hypotheses require $D>0$ and $A\ge0$. The constants are uniform over the fields and scales.
TorusEuler.exists_bandBernsteinJetBounds.summary: Fourier support bounds every spatial derivative

TorusEuler.exists_bound_spatial_jet_of_c.text: Each spatial jet of a jointly smooth periodic field is uniformly bounded on the closed slab.
TorusEuler.exists_bound_spatial_jet_of_c.summary: Periodic spatial derivatives are bounded on the slab

TorusEuler.exists_bounded_separated_offO.text: A compact subset of `offOrigin` lies in a bounded open neighborhood whose points have a common positive distance from every lattice singularity. The theorem supplies both a radius bound `R` and separation `ρ`. These two bounds are exactly the hypotheses needed to dominate all translated dyadic kernel derivatives.
TorusEuler.exists_bounded_separated_offO.summary: Every compact punctured region has uniform lattice separation

TorusEuler.exists_close_lifts.text: For any two torus labels, choose Euclidean representatives whose distance is at most twice the torus distance. The proof puts their displacement in the centered cell and bounds its three coordinates. The factor two safely controls the Euclidean norm from the product-torus metric; it is not asserted to be the best constant.
TorusEuler.exists_close_lifts.summary: Torus points admit lifts within twice their distance

TorusEuler.exists_closedSlab_jointContDi.text: Suppose each time slice of a jointly smooth field has a periodic potential with zero mean. The theorem chooses those potentials and proves that the resulting pressure is jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$. The positivity assumption on `T` supports endpoint differentiation. No regularity or pressure identity is promised outside the closed slab.
TorusEuler.exists_closedSlab_jointContDi.summary: Smooth slice gradients select a smooth periodic pressure

TorusEuler.exists_closedSlab_momentumRes.text: At a chosen time in a positive slab, assumes nonnegative cutoff radius, a jointly smooth solenoidal torus velocity in band $2\Lambda$, jointly smooth pressure periodic at that slice, and equality of the true residual with projected momentum. It constructs matching torus representatives of residual and advection, proves residual support in band $4\Lambda$, and certifies the actual within-slab time derivative equation.
TorusEuler.exists_closedSlab_momentumRes.summary: The true residual has finite-band projected evolution data

TorusEuler.exists_concrete_freezingCompr.text: For a chosen complexification and projection symbol satisfying smoothness, homogeneity, symmetry, and the five-derivative budget, there is a constant independent of the subsequent coefficient `B`. Compatible strong projection data and positive coercivity on both symbol ranges and projected field values yield an inverse bounded by a polynomial of power $145$. The theorem packages the general uniform result for one setting.
TorusEuler.exists_concrete_freezingCompr.summary: Construct the inverse for one fixed projection symbol

TorusEuler.exists_contDiffOn_extension_o.text: On an open subset `D` of a finite-dimensional real space, suppose every point has a smooth local field agreeing with `f` on an arbitrary agreement set `A`. A smooth partition of unity combines them into one smooth field on `D` agreeing on `A ∩ D`. Agreement is preserved by the sum of weights being one; no PDE or divergence condition is preserved by this statement.
TorusEuler.exists_contDiffOn_extension_o.summary: Combining local extensions with a partition of unity

TorusEuler.exists_contDiff_parameterized.text: If the coefficient and forcing are $C^n$ maps into uniform continuous-path spaces and the initial value is $C^n$, there is a $C^n$ solution map into that path space. It has the prescribed initial value and solves the ODE with derivatives within $[0,T]$. The proof uses `Ring.inverse` only after proving the Volterra equation is a unit at every parameter.
TorusEuler.exists_contDiff_parameterized.summary: The forced ODE depends smoothly on its parameters

TorusEuler.exists_continuousOn_uniformLi.text: If every approximant is continuous on `s`, the uniform limit obtained from summable consecutive distance bounds is also continuous there. The same explicit series tail controls its distance from each sufficiently late approximant. Completeness is a property of the target space, and no compactness assumption on `s` is needed.
TorusEuler.exists_continuousOn_uniformLi.summary: The summable increment limit remains continuous

TorusEuler.exists_continuousTorusFunctio.text: A continuous profile supported in a centered label ball of radius $0\le r<1/2$, composed with a continuous lattice-equivariant label map, defines a continuous torus field. The phase vector `k` may be any real vector. The vanishing collar around the cell boundary removes the discontinuity of the centered-label choice.
TorusEuler.exists_continuousTorusFunctio.summary: A localized real phase descends continuously to the torus

TorusEuler.exists_continuousTorusTimeJet.text: Joint smoothness on a positive-length slab and spatial periodicity produce continuous torus representatives `g j t` for all fixed-position time derivatives. The agreement is required only for `t ∈ Icc 0 T`. The proof may choose the zero torus function outside the interval, so the existential family carries no regularity or derivative claims there.

TorusEuler.exists_endpointContinuousRepr.text: A weak solution agreeing with the instantaneous equation has a continuous representative obtained by applying the strong inverse to its continuous right side. The inputs include inverse continuity `hInv`, bounds `hBound`, source continuity and bounds, operator compatibility `hCompat`, weak injectivity `hWeakInjective`, and the weak equation `hWeak`. The result gives the strong equation at every time, agreement almost everywhere, and a uniform norm estimate. These hypotheses record the preceding elliptic and continuity work.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointContinuousRepr.summary: Recovering a continuous representative of the weak velocity

TorusEuler.exists_endpointInstantaneousI.text: Uniform ellipticity, spatial Lipschitz control and a supremum bound for `K` on `I` produce a family of solenoidal coefficient equivalences. If `K` is `ContDiffOn ℝ n` there, the inverse operator curve has the same regularity and the common polynomial norm bound. The constructed family is the identity outside `I`; its coefficient equation and regularity are claimed only on `I`.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointInstantaneousI.summary: Time regularity of the instantaneous inverse

TorusEuler.exists_endpointJointVelocity_.text: Under the same matching-jet, ellipticity and mixed coercivity hypotheses as the preceding theorem, returns a jointly smooth solenoidal label velocity and the time-independent field `c`. The projected integrated equation holds at every closed-slab time, and the velocity primitive vanishes at both endpoints. This wrapper discards the finite-word witnesses while preserving their recovered velocity.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointJointVelocity_.summary: Recover the jointly smooth solenoidal velocity

TorusEuler.exists_endpointJointVelocity_.text: Compatible mixed and strong coefficient jets, positive spatial and mixed coercivity, and the stated Lipschitz bounds produce one solenoidal velocity with zero endpoint primitive. Its lift is jointly smooth on the closed slab. For every `N`, the theorem retains a finite recovered-word family whose empty word is that same velocity; it does not choose unrelated velocities at successive orders.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointJointVelocity_.summary: One smooth velocity realizes every finite derivative family

TorusEuler.exists_endpointLabelL2Solutio.text: Assume $0<T\le1$, $1\le D$, $0\le L$, continuous coefficients, their prescribed derivative equations, a left inverse G, and the inverse, gradient and Hessian bounds. Then the equation tested against zero-mean time paths has a unique solution with norm at most $\|f\|/c$, where $c=[2D^2(1+L)^2]^{-1}$. This is a fixed-label $L^2$ statement; spatial incompressibility and Hölder regularity are not conclusions.

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedCoefficie.text: Realize each coefficient word from the smooth jet structure on the same temporal L2 space, preserving the spatial directional derivative relations and pointwise-in-time action.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedCoefficie.summary: Mixed realizations of coefficient derivative words

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedCoefficie.text: A uniformly bounded continuous half-Holder coefficient curve defines a mixed coefficient of no larger norm, whose operator at each label multiplies temporal paths pointwise almost everywhere.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedCoefficie.summary: A mixed coefficient from a continuous time curve

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedLerayInve.text: Fix `hT : 0 < T`. The theorem provides a nonnegative constant and a continuous linear inverse for each spatially Lipschitz path coefficient coercive on paths with zero time mean. The resulting equivalence has underlying map equal to the actual mixed Leray compression. Its bound depends polynomially on reciprocal coercivity and coefficient size.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedLerayInve.summary: Invert the mixed coefficient on a chosen time interval

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedLerayInve.text: The nonnegative constant `C` is chosen before the positive time length `T`. A spatially Lipschitz path-operator coefficient that is coercive on zero-time-mean paths then has an inverse after mixed Leray compression, with the stated power-$145$ bound. The coercivity hypothesis only concerns paths satisfying the endpoint integral constraint, matching the projected unknown.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedLerayInve.summary: One mixed inverse constant works for every positive time interval

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedPhysicalC.text: Constructs mixed kinetic and vorticity multipliers from continuous physical fields with deformation, gradient and spatial Lipschitz bounds. It records their almost-everywhere action, a supremum and Lipschitz bound for $B=K-J\Omega$, and its coercivity on zero-time-mean paths. The assumptions include deformation evolution, a bounded left inverse and the Hessian upper bound; the result prepares the freezing solve rather than producing the correction itself.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedPhysicalC.summary: Physical coefficients satisfy the mixed inverse hypotheses

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedSolveSpat.text: A mixed solution with an invertible compressed leading operator and positive coercivity admits spatial derivative words through order `N`. The output remains fixed by the mixed projection, solves the differentiated residual equations, and satisfies recursive norm bounds involving lower-order correction pairs. The hypotheses explicitly provide coefficient and source derivative hierarchies; this theorem does not invent their regularity.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedSolveSpat.summary: The mixed inverse supplies every prescribed spatial jet

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedSource.text: A continuous half-Holder source bounded by M on a nonnegative time interval has a mixed representative with norm at most square root duration times M and the correct spatial and temporal slices. A clamped extension is used only to construct the representative; the conclusion concerns the original interval.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedSource.summary: Representing a continuous source in the mixed space

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedSource_je.text: For nonnegative duration, realize all source words as mixed temporal L2 paths, with their stated time slices and spatial derivative relations intact.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedSource_je.summary: Mixed realizations of source derivative words

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedTimeRecov.text: From a fixed mixed solution with vanishing projected residual, uniformly elliptic Lipschitz kinetic coefficients and a compatible continuous source, recovers a continuous solenoidal half-Hölder velocity on $[0,T]$. It agrees with the mixed solution almost everywhere, satisfies the instantaneous projected equation, and has a primitive vanishing at both endpoints. The constant field is the projected normalized time mean of the residual; `hT` ensures its factor $T^{-1}$ is legitimate.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMixedTimeRecov.summary: Recovering a continuous velocity with the two endpoint conditions

TorusEuler.exists_endpointMomentumPressu.text: For a positive time interval, a differentiable continuous residual path with vanishing projection has a periodic zero-mean pressure whose gradient is the negative time derivative of that residual. The theorem also identifies the pointwise derivative of the residual as minus this gradient. The conclusion is at the specified time `t`, with derivatives taken within the slab.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointMomentumPressu.summary: A differentiated projected residual supplies the momentum pressure

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalForced.text: This wrapper exposes the smooth fields from the physical endpoint construction without its auxiliary recovery record. Under $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$, nonnegative strain bound and the stated ODE, inverse and Hessian assumptions, it returns periodic label velocity, displacement, transported mean and zero-mean label pressure. The displacement vanishes at both ends, while the momentum identity still uses label coordinates.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalForced.summary: Smooth mean motion with zero endpoint displacement

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalForced.text: Smooth periodic forcing, the deformation ODE, two inverse identities, uniform inverse and strain bounds, and the Hessian upper bound produce smooth periodic fields `v`, `Z`, `B` and normalized pressure `q`. They satisfy $Z_t=v$, zero endpoint displacement and the pulled-back momentum equation for $B=Fv$. The returned recovery record certifies this same `v`; composition with the inverse flow is a separate step.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalForced.summary: The forced endpoint solve retains the same velocity

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalForced.text: Combines the smooth endpoint existence result with the parent estimate, retaining one common set of fields `v`, `Z`, `B` and `q`. After the parent budget `R` fixes the constants, the hypotheses include $2\le D$, $L\le D$, the actual flow derivatives, periodic smooth forcing and the Hessian upper bound. All finite-order estimates apply to the returned $B$, with zero endpoint displacement preserved.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalForced.summary: The same forced mean satisfies every derivative estimate

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalInvers.text: Fix a polynomial bound $C_0D^a$ on ellipticity reciprocals, coefficient sizes and label Lipschitz constants. For $0<T\le1$, positive spatial and mixed coercivity, and matching time/mixed coefficients, this constructs both inverse equivalences and bounds the full recovery budget by $CD^{291a}$. The outer constant is chosen before the slab duration and data. The spatial family is only identified on the slab.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalInvers.summary: The physical inverse admits duration-independent polynomial caps

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalJetDat.text: For positive duration, jointly smooth periodic fields `F`, `M` and `L` produce a nonempty `EndpointPhysicalJets` package for any chosen spatial directions. Operator algebra supplies smooth kinetic and vorticity coefficients, then the descent and mixed-realization theorems supply their jets. The conclusion is existence of regularity data; no invertibility, Hessian condition or endpoint solution is asserted.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalJetDat.summary: Smooth periodic physical data have compatible jet realizations

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMeanFr.text: Given a jointly smooth recovered solenoidal velocity satisfying the projected integrated equation and the correct force derivative, construct a smooth zero-ended displacement, pulled-forward label velocity, and zero-mean periodic pressure. Differentiation of the projected equation supplies its pressure gradient; the statement does not identify it with a derivative of an earlier potential.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMeanFr.summary: A smooth mean velocity and normalized label pressure

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMixedS.text: For a fixed slab with $0<T\le1$, this returns the same mixed physical solution and polynomial estimate as the duration-uniform theorem. All deformation, inverse, evolution, Lipschitz and Hessian hypotheses remain explicit. Its existential constant appears after fixing $T$, although the proof obtains it from the stronger theorem whose constant is uniform in duration.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMixedS.summary: Specialize the mixed inverse to a fixed slab

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMixedS.text: One nonnegative constant works for all positive durations at most one. Under deformation evolution, an inverse deformation bound, coefficient size and Lipschitz bounds, and the upper Hessian condition, the theorem constructs the mixed projected solution, its zero time integral and physical weak representative. Both projected-source and full-source norms are bounded with an explicit $Q^{145}$ factor.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMixedS.summary: Construct the mixed solution with a uniform prefactor

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMoment.text: This version obtains the needed derivative values from $C^1$ regularity of $K$, $L$ and the solenoidal velocity, while only continuity of $\Omega$ is required. At each specified slab time it gives a periodic mean-zero pressure with the required gradient. It does not by itself assemble those pressures into a jointly smooth time-space function.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMoment.summary: First time derivatives suffice for pressure recovery

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMoment.text: At a fixed time in a positive closed slab, a projected integrated equation and supplied derivatives of its factor curves yield a spatially periodic, mean-zero scalar pressure. Its gradient is the negative momentum residual, and evaluation of the residual curve differentiates to that gradient with the same sign. The projection must match the weak Leray projection through `hP`.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalMoment.summary: The projected residual derivative has a normalized pressure

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalPulled.text: For the exact kinetic and vorticity coefficients and deformation evolution $F_t=MF$, pressure recovery yields $K\,dg+\nabla q=-dL-2F^TMFg$. The assumptions include the projected equation, the supplied slab derivatives and the coefficient identification. This is the label-coordinate momentum identity at a fixed time; conversion to physical coordinates is performed elsewhere.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalPulled.summary: Physical coefficients identify the pulled-back momentum equation

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalPulled.text: For a recovery record and a smooth periodic force, constructs half-Hölder curves representing every spatial derivative word of $F^*f$. Each actual source jet equals minus the time primitive of the corresponding curve throughout the slab. This identifies the source used in the derivative recurrence with the supplied forcing, rather than with an independent family of bounds.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalPulled.summary: Every source derivative is an integrated force derivative

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalRecove.text: Given a nonnegative parent derivative budget `R`, chooses a power `p`, threshold `s₀` and order constants before the parent, forcing and derivative order are supplied. Under the stated flow, smoothness and deformation bounds, every recovery record satisfies the mean estimate at every $s\ge s_0$. The constants are uniform in the slab, but depend on the prescribed family `R`.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalRecove.summary: One parent bound controls every recovered mean order

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalTimeSo.text: For physical coefficients satisfying the mixed-solve hypotheses and $C^n$ half-Hölder time curves, the theorem produces a solenoidal velocity `g` and constant `c` satisfying the projected instantaneous equation at every closed-slab time. The velocity is $C^n$ in time and its primitive has one additional derivative. That primitive vanishes at both endpoints and has within-slab derivative `g`.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPhysicalTimeSo.summary: Recover a smooth time velocity with both endpoint conditions

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPower_absorb_p.text: For any real prefactor $C$ and natural exponent $a$, there is a natural $b$ such that $CD^a\le D^b$ for every $D\ge2$. The proof bounds $\max(1,C)$ by a power of two and then enlarges the exponent. Although the docstring mentions a nonnegative prefactor, the formal statement permits negative $C$ too.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPower_absorb_p.summary: A larger exponent absorbs a fixed prefactor

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPressure_of_pr.text: Given a half-Hölder residual `F` whose weak projection is the embedded solenoidal field `c`, the theorem constructs a periodic zero-mean pressure with gradient equal to `F-c` on the periodic lift. It first cancels the projected component and then applies the continuous potential reconstruction. The pressure is a scalar function, while its gradient retains the supplied residual values.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPressure_of_pr.summary: Recover pressure after removing the solenoidal residual

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPressure_of_pr.text: Every continuous torus vector field whose weak Leray projection is zero is the gradient of a periodic scalar potential with zero centered-cell mean. This theorem chooses suitable smooth cutoffs and proves their uniform approximation before applying the limit argument. The conclusion identifies a genuine gradient at every Euclidean point of the periodic lift.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPressure_of_pr.summary: A continuous field in the Leray kernel has a periodic potential

TorusEuler.exists_endpointPressure_of_un.text: Assume `g` has zero weak Leray projection and `happrox` gives uniform convergence of the real cutoff fields to its periodic lift. The theorem constructs a periodic zero-mean potential with gradient equal to that lift. It uses finite cutoff pressures and the uniform-gradient limit theorem; the approximation property remains an explicit hypothesis.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointPressure_of_un.summary: Uniform cutoff gradients recover the original pressure

TorusEuler.exists_endpointSlabHalfHolder.text: For a jointly smooth periodic lift on a positive closed time slab, construct the entire family of spatial derivative words as time-smooth half-Holder curves. The theorem derives all evaluations and directional derivative relations from the lift.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointSlabHalfHolder.summary: Constructing Holder curves for every spatial derivative word

TorusEuler.exists_endpointSpatialJetTime.text: From projected mixed equations for all words through length `N`, constructs solenoidal half-Hölder time curves with the supplied regularity `n`, almost-everywhere slice agreement and zero endpoint primitives. Uniform ellipticity and Lipschitz control concern the zeroth kinetic coefficient. All available time derivatives retain the spatial derivative relations; words beyond `N` are assigned zero internally and carry no asserted jet properties.

TorusEuler.exists_endpointSpatialLerayIn.text: The Leray compression of a coercive Lipschitz coefficient has a continuous linear inverse on the solenoidal half-Hölder fields. Its hypotheses require $\mu>0$, a spatial Lipschitz bound $L$, and the quadratic lower bound $\langle Kv,v\rangle\ge\mu|v|^2$. The norm of the inverse is at most $C(4+\mu^{-1}+\|K\|_\infty+L)^{145}$. This gives the fixed-time result used with $\mu=D_-^{-2}$; the larger common bound in Theorem 4.2 also includes composition with the Leray projection.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointSpatialLerayIn.summary: The fixed time inverse on solenoidal fields

TorusEuler.exists_endpointSpatialSolenoi.text: For a half-Hölder coefficient `K` with spatial Lipschitz bound `L` and positive quadratic lower bound `μ`, produces an equivalence on solenoidal fields whose forward map is $v\mapsto\mathbb P(Kv)$. Its inverse norm is bounded by $C(4+\mu^{-1}+\|K\|_\infty+L)^{145}$. The universal constant precedes the coefficient quantifiers. This is a fixed-time inverse, with no time regularity asserted.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointSpatialSolenoi.summary: The instantaneous inverse on solenoidal fields

TorusEuler.exists_endpointStrongLabelMom.text: The hypotheses supply the flow derivative `hF`, the velocity derivative `hv`, a differentiable projected residual `G`, continuity of the integrated terms, and the integrated equation `hEq`. For positive `T`, it constructs a periodic zero-mean pressure with the gradient identity at every label and derives the momentum equation at the specified `x` and `t`. The twice-adjoint term and pressure sign $-dG$ are retained.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointStrongLabelMom.summary: Recover the strong label momentum equation with normalized pressure

TorusEuler.exists_endpointStrongMixedSol.text: For a fixed positive time length, coercivity on zero-time-mean paths and a spatial Lipschitz coefficient bound give a half-Hölder path-valued solution. The conclusion retains both the projection constraint on `v` and the equation $P(Bv+f)=0$. Its estimate uses the projected source, so it does not introduce a bound for discarded gradient components.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointStrongMixedSol.summary: Solve the mixed projected equation on a fixed interval

TorusEuler.exists_endpointStrongMixedSol.text: A single nonnegative `C`, chosen before `T`, bounds the mixed projected solution for every positive interval and coefficient satisfying the Lipschitz and zero-mean coercivity conditions. The output `v` is fixed by the mixed projection, its residual vanishes after projection, and its norm is controlled by the projected source. This is the quantitative strong solution before time recovery.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointStrongMixedSol.summary: Solve all positive interval endpoint problems with one constant

TorusEuler.exists_endpointTorusContinuou.text: Uniform ellipticity, compatible strong and weak projections, and a continuous bounded family of fixed-time inverses turn a weak joint solution into a continuous half-Holder velocity. It agrees with the weak solution almost everywhere, has the stated norm bound, and its primitive vanishes at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointTorusContinuou.summary: A continuous representative from the weak instantaneous equation

TorusEuler.exists_endpointTorusFlowL2Sol.text: Under $0<T\le1$, deformation evolution, a bounded left inverse `G`, and the quadratic Hessian upper bound, each ambient source `f` has a unique weak solution in the endpoint subspace. The norm bound is $\|v\|\le\|f\|/c$, with $c=[2D^2(1+L)^2]^{-1}$. This proves an $L^2$ variational equation; continuity, Hölder estimates and pressure recovery are separate results.

TorusEuler.exists_endpointTorusL2Solutio.text: Assuming positive `c`, measurable bounded coefficients, and `hcoercive` for every zero-mean $L^2$ path at almost every label, construct a unique velocity in `endpointTorusSpace T` satisfying the variational equation. Its norm is at most $\|f\|/c$. This theorem supplies weak existence and uniqueness only; spatial Hölder regularity and continuous time representatives require later arguments.
TorusEuler.exists_endpointTorusL2Solutio.summary: A unique weak endpoint velocity in the joint space

TorusEuler.exists_envelopeExponent_for_l.text: An envelope radius chosen as a sufficiently negative power of the parent parameter absorbs a fixed polynomial label Lipschitz bound.
TorusEuler.exists_envelopeExponent_for_l.summary: A small envelope absorbs the label variation

TorusEuler.exists_firstWaveHierarchyLead.text: The actual twisted first-wave velocity and pressure satisfy the sum estimate $\|v\|+\lambda\|p\|\le C\lambda^{-5/4}$ in amplitude seminorms. The assumptions include $0<T\le1$, $|s|\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, positive radius, and $2r<1/2$. The collar ensures the wrapped and raw profiles agree throughout the closed cell, allowing the preceding jet bounds to pass to the exact seminorms.
TorusEuler.exists_firstWaveHierarchyLead.summary: The wrapped first wave satisfies the leading finite norm

TorusEuler.exists_firstWaveLeadingProfil.text: For each `n`, one constant controls scaled jets of the first leading velocity and frequency-multiplied pressure by $\gamma C\lambda^{-5/4}$. Here $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}\|w.amplitude\ t\|$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $|s|\le1$, $T\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, and $0<r\le1$. This is the explicit first-wave version of the leading-profile estimate, before conversion to mixed-word seminorms.
TorusEuler.exists_firstWaveLeadingProfil.summary: The first velocity and pressure obey the leading budget

TorusEuler.exists_firstWaveOrigin_spatia.text: Uniform constants bound the spatial seed derivatives by the actual central amplitude of any `FirstWaveOrigin`. The assumptions are $|s|\le1$, $T\le1$, nonzero frequency, and time in $[0,T]$. Combining the initial-scale bound with the central-amplitude comparison gives the weight needed for the hierarchy without differentiating that weight.
TorusEuler.exists_firstWaveOrigin_spatia.summary: Spatial seed derivatives follow the central amplitude

TorusEuler.exists_firstWavePressureCoeff.text: For nonzero frequency and time in $[0,1]$, all spatial derivatives of the first-wave pressure coefficient are bounded by `B m * (|c| / |freq|)`. The constants are independent of the shear ratio as well as amplitude and frequency. The exact factorization reduces the estimate to the normalized smooth periodic coefficient.
TorusEuler.exists_firstWavePressureCoeff.summary: Pressure derivatives gain one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.exists_firstWavePrimaryPressu.text: Selects an absolute constant giving the one-sided bound $D^2p\le K r^{-2}\lambda^{-1/4}\mathrm{Id}$ for the actual first pressure on the entire periodic lift. The hypotheses include normalized first-wave data, a slab of duration at most one, small tilt, frequency at least one and `2*r ≤ 1/4`. The proof transports the estimate from a centered label cell using periodicity of the Hessian.
TorusEuler.exists_firstWavePrimaryPressu.summary: The first periodic pressure has a uniform upper Hessian

TorusEuler.exists_firstWaveSmoothSeedJet.text: There are nonnegative constants `B m` such that every spatial derivative of order `m` is at most `B m * |c|`, uniformly for $|s|\le1$, $0\le t\le1$, and every label. The amplitude scale may vanish. The proof combines compact periodic derivative bounds with the exact linear dependence on `c`.
TorusEuler.exists_firstWaveSmoothSeedJet.summary: Seed derivatives are controlled by the initial scale

TorusEuler.exists_forward_flowJetBounds.text: The parent flow satisfies $|D_a^nX|\le C_n\mathsf D^{5n-4}$ for every $n\ge1$. The velocity derivative sequence `R` is fixed before the parent. A smooth periodic flow, its forward and inverse deformation bounds and the higher velocity derivative estimates are the inputs. The proof combines the actual variational recurrence with a strong induction in the derivative order.
TorusEuler.exists_forward_flowJetBounds.summary: All forward flow derivatives satisfy the polynomial bound

TorusEuler.exists_freezingCompressionEqu.text: This abstract assembly theorem assumes idempotence, the projected pairing, positive coercivity, and uniform frozen operators `F` and `G` along the affine path. The hypotheses `hfreeze`, `hoff`, and `hsmall` supply the splitting, distant estimate, and absorbable nearby error. It returns a continuous linear equivalence equal to the compressed coefficient operator, with an explicit inverse norm bound.
TorusEuler.exists_freezingCompressionEqu.summary: Local frozen estimates yield the projected inverse

TorusEuler.exists_freezingContinuationEq.text: If $(1-s)I+sS$ satisfies the same lower norm estimate for every $s$ in $[0,1]$, there is a continuous linear equivalence whose underlying operator is exactly `S`. Its inverse norm is at most `M`. This is the existence conclusion used after the frozen-coefficient estimate has supplied the uniform bound.
TorusEuler.exists_freezingContinuationEq.summary: The a priori path estimate gives a bounded isomorphism

TorusEuler.exists_freezingHalfHolderMult.text: Fix a smooth projection family, its complexification, and a common five-derivative bound $D\ge1$ on the annulus. Chooses nonnegative constants $C,K$ before varying $B$ and $\mu>0$. For coercivity on every projected range, both frozen operators have norm at most $CQ^{11}$, where $Q=2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|$; the projected operator also satisfies a local Lipschitz bound $KQ^{11}\|f\|_\infty/r$. Global projection and coercivity hypotheses cover frequency zero as well.
TorusEuler.exists_freezingHalfHolderMult.summary: Polynomial bounds for both frozen real multipliers

TorusEuler.exists_freezing_near_source.text: With `hr : 0 < r`, `hr₁ : r ≤ 1`, and Lipschitz coefficient bound `hBlip`, the cutoff-localized error $(B(a)-B(x))v(x)$ is a half-Hölder field with norm at most $8L\sqrt r\|v\|$. This is the quantitative small term later absorbed by choosing the localization radius sufficiently small.
TorusEuler.exists_freezing_near_source.summary: The nearby coefficient error is small in Hölder norm

TorusEuler.exists_freezing_split_sources.text: The coefficient error $(B(a)-B(x))v(x)$ splits into two spatial half-Hölder sources. With `hr : 0 < r`, `hr₁ : r ≤ 1`, and a nonnegative Lipschitz bound `hL`, the near source has norm at most $8L\sqrt r\|v\|$. The far source vanishes on the radius-$r$ ball and has a supremum bound. The theorem constructs sources and estimates them; the frozen multiplier identity is a separate result.
TorusEuler.exists_freezing_split_sources.summary: Splitting the coefficient error into near and far sources

TorusEuler.exists_frequencySchedule_late.text: For fixed comparison order and positive lower and upper strength constants, one initial frequency threshold makes every later scheduled window satisfy the full comparison and crossing conditions. The premises include the actual error estimate, coupling range, strength bounds, and older-gradient scales. The conclusion places the entire crossing search in the first physical half interval.
TorusEuler.exists_frequencySchedule_late.summary: A large scheduled frequency validates the comparison window

TorusEuler.exists_frequencySchedule_sati.text: Given $b\ge1$, $N\ge B(1)$, positive thresholds and the logarithmic floor $\log B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$, there exist the paper’s order and frequency sequences. They satisfy the recurrence and exact constrained maxima, both tend to infinity, adjacent orders differ by zero or one, and $4\log\lambda_{i+3}\le(\log\lambda_i)^2$. No monotonicity or fixed-order-constant domination of $B$ is assumed in this numerical theorem.
TorusEuler.exists_frequencySchedule_sati.summary: A single schedule has unbounded orders and controlled logarithmic gain

TorusEuler.exists_frequencySchedule_with.text: Given `1 ≤ b` and a starting frequency above the first threshold, the theorem chooses order and frequency sequences. Orders increase by at most one, both sequences diverge, and the logarithmic spacing inequality holds. Every cost whose two indices fall in the permitted finite range is bounded by the current frequency. Costs are fixed before the schedule is chosen.
TorusEuler.exists_frequencySchedule_with.summary: Choose a growing schedule that absorbs every listed cost

TorusEuler.exists_halfHolderWords_norm_l.text: A field whose lift is $C^{n,1/2}$ has a family of actual coordinate derivatives through order $n$, each with half-Hölder norm at most $\sqrt2$ times its lifted norm. The input is `hf : SpatialHolderHalf n` of the lift. The family `w` has `w [] = f` and the prescribed derivative relations. These identities prevent the later derivative bounds from being applied to arbitrary, unrelated arrays.
TorusEuler.exists_halfHolderWords_norm_l.summary: The Hölder norm bounds every coordinate derivative

TorusEuler.exists_halfHolder_of_spatialH.text: A periodic order-zero half-Hölder Euclidean field descends to a bundled torus field with the same values on every lift. The bundled norm is at most $\sqrt2$ times the lift norm. The proof uses controlled representatives of pairs of torus points; periodicity is essential to making their values independent of the chosen lifts.
TorusEuler.exists_halfHolder_of_spatialH.summary: A periodic Hölder lift descends with a controlled norm

TorusEuler.exists_halfHolder_timeCurves_.text: A sequence of jointly smooth periodic fields with successive pointwise time-derivative relations yields corresponding smooth curves in the torus half-Hölder space. Every curve agrees with the original lift on the closed interval and has an order-dependent uniform bound. The construction sets values outside the interval to zero; no regularity or representation outside the slab is asserted.
TorusEuler.exists_halfHolder_timeCurves_.summary: Periodic time jets descend to smooth Hölder-space curves

TorusEuler.exists_hierarchyRelayPotentia.text: For any nonnegative derivative-constant sequence `C`, there is a nonnegative sequence `K` that controls four normalized potential and pressure coefficients by $K_nD^{15}$. The exponent fifteen is independent of `n` and the time index. Smoothness, nonvanishing of `κ`, inverse-norm jets, and $\ell D^{16}\le1$ remain explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.exists_hierarchyRelayPotentia.summary: One parent exponent controls the four potential coefficients

TorusEuler.exists_induction_amplificatio.text: For fixed comparison exponent `C₀` and nonnegative window and error constants, one base threshold ensures the two required smallness inequalities. The assumptions constrain the gains between $\log\mu$ and $(\log\mu)^2$, the nonnegative time window by the fourth power of the next gain, and the nonnegative error by three decaying frequency terms. The result is uniform above that threshold.
TorusEuler.exists_induction_amplificatio.summary: Large frequency makes both comparison smallness conditions hold

TorusEuler.exists_induction_amplificatio.text: Above one threshold, the frequency recurrence, older-gradient estimates, positive scaling lower bound, gain constraints, residual control, and physical-frame error estimate imply a normalized interval of length at least two and both comparison smallness inequalities. The theorem assembles previously proved scalar bounds. Its final error inequality is an input, so it does not independently estimate the actual moving-frame error.
TorusEuler.exists_induction_amplificatio.summary: The inductive physical estimates supply a valid comparison interval

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveCutoffBudget.text: Selects a nonnegative absolute residual-pressure constant and nonnegative depth-dependent tail constants for the fixed dyadic cutoff. For every physical approximation of depth at least two and cutoff frequency at least one, it provides a truncated child and its cutoff bounds. Internally the tail constant is defined as zero below depth two, but that branch is excluded from every asserted cutoff estimate.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveCutoffBudget.summary: One dyadic cutoff supplies all stage tail constants

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerBase_of_.text: Constructs the base using the actual first-wave hierarchy and its cutoff. The stationary parent, prescribed tilt, localized first-wave split, support, and remainder derivative estimate are supplied alongside the quantitative cutoff and flow budgets. It derives admissible phase scale from the frequency schedule and concludes exact agreement of the base’s parent, child fields, and oscillation with the specified construction.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerBase_of_.summary: Close the first induction stage from actual hierarchy fields

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerChild_of.text: Specializes the profile-jet stage closure to `PhysicalApproximationData`. The qualitative properties automatically supply smoothness, divergence, periodicity, graph identities, and the mean-oscillation split. Quantitative Eulerian bounds, cutoff bounds, scalar scale budgets, and corrected pulled-back jet bounds are still hypotheses. The resulting stage preserves the exact cutoff velocity and Poisson pressure.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerChild_of.summary: Close the child built from the retained hierarchy

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerChild_of.text: Given cutoff bounds, the quantitative approximation bundle, a compatible slab, scalar budgets, and a deformation certificate for the cutoff velocity, constructs the next inductive stage. It proves exact agreement with the cutoff velocity and pressure and obtains the required small oscillation and smooth-correction bounds. The flow estimate remains an explicit input at this level.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerChild_of.summary: The physical cutoff satisfies the next stage bounds

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerChild_of.text: Adds the scaled profile hypotheses needed to derive the deformation estimate, then constructs the next stage from the actual cutoff. The corrected pulled-back jets are supplied as `hJets`, while parent flow regularity comes from the existing stage. The scalar bound $\Gamma \cdot  D^bFlow \le  childFrequency^{1/32}$ implies the smallness needed by the flow argument.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerChild_of.summary: Derive the child flow and close the physical stage

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerStages_o.text: Given lifetime bounds, an inhabited base and existence of successors for every compatible finite prefix, constructs an infinite stage family with exactly the prescribed frequency and order sequences. It also supplies matching central waves. Classical choice selects the base and local extension function once; recursion then preserves all earlier choices.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerStages_o.summary: Local compatible extensions produce a common infinite family

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerStep_of_.text: Constructs a full later step from the retained hierarchy and the preceding selected comparison. In addition to the quantitative stage inputs, it requires the oscillation’s support and early-time vanishing, and the central rank-one decomposition with scale $-1/3$ error. The conclusion identifies the child velocity, child pressure, and step oscillation with the actual constructed fields.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerStep_of_.summary: Close a later induction step from actual hierarchy fields

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_late.text: For a fixed strength constant `C ≥ 2`, chooses a comparison constant at least 240 and a base-frequency threshold. Any certified tip above that threshold, with `P.LifetimeBounds` and parameter constants equal to the selected ones, admits a later window and wave selection. No compatible-prefix argument is required. The conclusion supplies comparison data before constructing the truncated child.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_late.summary: Uniform constants select the next amplified wave

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_olde.text: Produces a uniform frequency threshold which, together with `P.LifetimeBounds`, ensures ninth-power and eighteenth-power bounds for a certified tip’s older central gradient and its within-slab time derivative on the next comparison interval.
