It also provides the derivative witness. The proof uses the actual projected momentum equation and Fourier support of the stored velocity.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_olde.summary: The older gradient and its time derivative are controlled

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_sche.text: Above one threshold depending on the strength constant, the derivative of the actual later-wave switch times its normalized center amplitude is bounded by the parent frequency times the next frequency to power $-4$. The statement holds for every real time: the early-amplitude estimate handles the switching interval, and support of the switch derivative handles its complement.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_sche.summary: The actual switch costs four inverse frequency powers

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_swit.text: For fixed strength constant at least two and nonnegative switch constant, one initial-frequency threshold controls every compatible tip, physical window, and selected later wave. It gives positivity of the next frequency, absorbs the physical growth rate into the parent frequency, and bounds the child’s normalized early amplitude by the logarithmic gain at the next frequency. All conclusions concern the same selection.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_swit.summary: One threshold controls both rate and early amplitude

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveFirstWaveSele.text: Produces a single threshold $N\ge4$ such that every parameter schedule above it, with `LifetimeBounds`, admits a first-wave selection for every exponent `a ≥ 6`. The proof combines the geometry threshold, gain and shear inequalities, and an origin-wave existence result. The quantifier order makes the threshold independent of the chosen envelope exponent.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveFirstWaveSele.summary: One frequency threshold supplies the first wave

TorusEuler.exists_inductive_periodicEule.text: Given the complete stage hypotheses, including growing frequencies, increasing derivative order, activation convergence, increment bounds, and small actual projected residuals, this theorem constructs a continuous closed slab velocity. It is jointly smooth, periodic, odd, solenoidal, and satisfies projected Euler before `T`. Every spatial jet converges on strict positive prefixes. The terminal time itself is only covered by continuity.
TorusEuler.exists_inductive_periodicEule.summary: The inductive tower yields an unforced projected velocity limit

TorusEuler.exists_inductive_periodicEule.text: All the stage increment, activation, smoothness, parity, frequency, and projected residual hypotheses produce an actual Euler velocity and normalized pressure before `T`. The velocity extends continuously to the closed slab; its spatial jets and Hölder norms converge on strict positive prefixes. The theorem is conditional on the supplied tower and does not itself prove terminal blow-up or maximality.
TorusEuler.exists_inductive_periodicEule.summary: The tower produces an actual Euler solution before accumulation

TorusEuler.exists_inductive_velocity_lim.text: Quadratically growing frequencies, derivative orders tending to infinity, and the supplied oscillatory and correction bounds produce a continuous velocity limit on the common closed slab. On any open spatial region and time set where late oscillations vanish, all actual spatial jets converge uniformly, remain continuous, and have tail bound $2/\mathrm{freq}(n+1)$. No Euler equation is concluded here.
TorusEuler.exists_inductive_velocity_lim.summary: Stage increments converge wherever late oscillations vanish

TorusEuler.exists_isEulerSolution_of_per.text: A positive-time, jointly smooth periodic solenoidal velocity satisfying the actual projected momentum equation admits a pressure making it `IsEulerSolution T u p`. The pressure is periodic and mean zero, and its gradient equals minus time derivative minus self advection. Joint pressure smoothness is proved from the smooth gradient and normalization, not assumed.
TorusEuler.exists_isEulerSolution_of_per.summary: Projected dynamics recovers a smooth normalized Euler pressure

TorusEuler.exists_isEulerSolution_of_pre.text: Assume a jointly smooth limit velocity, uniform prefix convergence of velocities, spatial derivatives and periodic pressure gradients, approximation symmetries and divergence, and the limiting dynamics. The theorem constructs a jointly smooth mean-zero pressure and an Euler solution with odd velocity. It first recovers spatial pressure slices, then uses momentum to prove joint gradient smoothness and normalization to control the time-dependent gauge.
TorusEuler.exists_isEulerSolution_of_pre.summary: Recover a smooth normalized pressure for the limiting velocity

TorusEuler.exists_iteratedDeriv_waveProf.text: For each derivative order `j` with the named hypothesis `hj : 2 ≤ j`, there is a positive constant bounding $|\partial_s^jF_h(s)|$ by $C h^{1-j}$. That constant is chosen before the scale and phase quantifiers, so it is uniform for every $0<h\le1$ and every real `s`. The theorem supplies exactly the higher-derivative part of Lemma 3.1 and permits the constant to depend on the derivative order.
TorusEuler.exists_iteratedDeriv_waveProf.summary: Higher profile derivatives have uniform scale bounds

TorusEuler.exists_jet_majorant_dyadicPer.text: For any derivative order, bounded points uniformly separated from the lattice admit a summable majorant for the corresponding derivative of every translated dyadic kernel. The sequence is indexed by scale and lattice point together. This is the quantitative convergence input for smoothness of the full periodic kernel.
TorusEuler.exists_jet_majorant_dyadicPer.summary: Separated regions have one summable bound for all kernel terms

TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.text: For finite-dimensional parameters and state, smooth periodic zero-mean forcing and a smooth transported wave vector nonzero initially produce a jointly smooth zero-start velocity and its normalized pressure. Both profiles remain periodic with zero phase mean. The velocity is transverse, and the pressure's phase derivative gives the exact momentum equation at every label, phase and closed-slab time.
TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.summary: Construct the smooth periodic transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.text: Smooth coefficients and a smooth source with zero phase mean admit a jointly smooth velocity and normalized pressure. The hypotheses `hκ₀` and `hκt` give a nonzero initial covector and its adjoint evolution; `hfper`, `hfmean`, and `hfTwist` impose the phase and lattice conventions. The conclusion fixes `V 0 = 0` and proves both equations, the two mean normalizations, transversality, and conditional reflection and support properties. It asserts existence, not a comparison with every other solution.
TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.summary: Smooth transverse solutions preserve support and symmetry

TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.text: In finite-dimensional parameter and inner-product state spaces, smooth strain, wave vector and forcing, with nonzero initial wave vector and its adjoint transport equation, produce a jointly smooth zero-start velocity on the closed slab. The velocity stays transverse and satisfies both the projected ODE and the equation using the pressure slope. Phase periodicity and averaging are not included here.
TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.summary: Construct a jointly smooth transverse velocity from zero data

TorusEuler.exists_jointly_continuous_par.text: For continuous-in-time coefficients and forcing with uniform size and parameter Lipschitz bounds, construct solutions for all parameters in one complete normed space. The initial family `x₀` is bounded and Lipschitz. The output satisfies the ODE within the closed interval, has an explicit Grönwall size bound, and is jointly continuous with a uniform parameter Lipschitz constant.
TorusEuler.exists_jointly_continuous_par.summary: A jointly continuous family of linear ODE solutions

TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc.text: Joint continuity `hU`, a uniform velocity bound `hbound`, and a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound `hLip` give a two-time label flow on the closed interval. The produced function is defined for all real arguments, but its initial and trajectory laws are constrained only when the start and evaluation times lie in the interval.
TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc.summary: Bounded Lipschitz velocities admit flows on the whole closed interval

TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc_of_co.text: For the nondegenerate interval `hlr : l < r`, a jointly $C^1$ periodic velocity yields both a uniform spatial Lipschitz constant and a two-time label flow. The regularity is within the closed slab, including its endpoints. The theorem supplies pointwise trajectories; higher label smoothness is proved in later modules.
TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc_of_co.summary: A periodic C1 velocity gives the closed slab flow

TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc_of_pe.text: Given joint continuity, spatial periodicity, and a uniform Lipschitz bound on the closed time interval, there exists a label flow throughout that interval. Compactness of the centered cell supplies a velocity bound, which periodicity extends to every label. The result asserts the flow laws only on the prescribed slab.
TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc_of_pe.summary: Spatial periodicity supplies the boundedness needed for a full flow

TorusEuler.exists_lattice_dist_le_of_mem.text: The closed support of the periodic radial envelope lies in the union of the closed radius-`2 * ℓ` balls around the lattice.
TorusEuler.exists_lattice_dist_le_of_mem.summary: The envelope support lies near lattice points

TorusEuler.exists_lattice_separation_of_.text: A compact subset of `offOrigin` has a common positive lower bound on its distance to every lattice vector. Here the punctured Euclidean lift excludes all integer translates of the torus origin. The proof uses an open thickening of the compact set; excluding only the single Euclidean point zero would be insufficient.
TorusEuler.exists_lattice_separation_of_.summary: A compact punctured set has a uniform lattice gap

TorusEuler.exists_leading_scaledJetBound.text: At each order, chooses a constant before the frequency and slow-amplitude budgets. With frequency at least one, phase scale $\mathrm{freq}^{-1/2}$, and weight $\gamma = \mathrm{freq}^{3/4}\cdot g$, supplied smooth scaled amplitude and pressure-coefficient jets imply leading velocity and frequency-weighted pressure bounds proportional to $\gamma\cdot \mathrm{freq}^{-5/4}$. The amplitude hypothesis already includes the fixed-time switch, so no separate switch bound is assumed.
TorusEuler.exists_leading_scaledJetBound.summary: Slow seed jets produce the leading frequency decay

TorusEuler.exists_leading_scaledJetBound.text: For fixed order and slow-jet prefactors at least one, chooses $C \ge  1$ independently of frequency, deformation, and the time-slice switch. With frequency and `D` at least one, switch magnitude at most one, and amplitude and coefficient costs $D^{13}$ and $D^7$, both the switched leading velocity and frequency-weighted pressure have scaled jet bound $\gamma\cdot C\cdot D^{20}\cdot \mathrm{freq}^{-5/4}$.
TorusEuler.exists_leading_scaledJetBound.summary: Leading velocity and pressure cost twenty parent powers

TorusEuler.exists_lipschitzWith_of_contD.text: A jointly (C^1) periodic velocity on a nondegenerate closed slab has a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound, including at the temporal endpoints.
TorusEuler.exists_lipschitzWith_of_contD.summary: A smooth periodic velocity is uniformly Lipschitz in space

TorusEuler.exists_nearestTorusLift.text: Given Euclidean representatives $x,a$, constructs another representative $x'$ of the same torus point as $x$ whose distance to $a$ equals the auxiliary torus Euclidean distance. Coordinatewise integer translations realize the minimum. The result gives existence of a shortest lifted segment, which is enough for the local estimate, without requiring a unique lift.

TorusEuler.exists_norm_endpointStrongMix.text: There is one nonnegative constant bounding the operator norm of the mixed half-Hölder Leray projection for every positive duration `T`. The proof uses five angular derivatives of the multiplier and treats the zero mode separately. The conclusion is a spatial half-Hölder operator bound independent of the changing temporal $L^2$ target, not an assertion that this norm is one.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_endpointStrongMix.summary: The mixed Leray bound is uniform in duration

TorusEuler.exists_norm_homogeneousHalfHo.text: For a fixed cutoff and fixed complex value spaces, a nonnegative constant bounds the constructed multiplier norm by the derivative mass of its annular localization plus $\|A(0)\|$. The proof combines kernel half-moment and block-summation estimates. It does not require homogeneity for this bound on the constructed operator.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_homogeneousHalfHo.summary: Derivative mass and the mean bound control the operator norm

TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_pe.text: The difference of far pressure gradients is bounded in every spatial derivative by the integral of the difference of their tensor sources. Compact observation and source sets are separated modulo the lattice by `hsep`; both source tensors are integrable on the source cell. The theorem supplies an open neighborhood and a derivative-order constant. It concerns the explicit far-pressure operator; identifying that operator with the localized Leray term requires the adjoining Fourier representation results.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_pe.summary: Separated pressure gradients obey a local integral bound

TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_pe.text: For compact periodically separated target and source sets, one open target neighborhood supports a nonnegative constant at every derivative order bounding pressure-jet differences by the integral tensor difference norm. Both densities must be integrable on the source portion of the fundamental cell. The constants are independent of those densities.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_pe.summary: Each far pressure derivative is controlled by the source integral error

TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_ra.text: At each derivative order `m`, there is a positive constant independent of the positive radius and label such that the envelope derivative norm is at most $C(\ell^{-1})^m$. Compactness controls derivatives of the unit envelope, while support gives zero outside a fixed ball. The constant is allowed to depend on the derivative order.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_ra.summary: Envelope derivatives cost inverse powers of the radius

TorusEuler.exists_norm_realHomogeneousHa.text: For a fixed complexification `X`, chooses $C\ge0$ that works for every symbol smooth away from zero. The real multiplier norm is bounded by $C$ times the derivative mass of its fixed annular localization, plus $\|A(0)\|$ for the mean mode. This separates the nonzero-frequency kernel estimate from the independently specified zero mode; no homogeneity assumption is used for the norm bound.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_realHomogeneousHa.summary: Bound the real multiplier by localized symbol mass

TorusEuler.exists_norm_universal_homogen.text: A single cutoff-dependent nonnegative constant bounds the constructed multiplier by its localized derivative mass plus its zero-mode norm for all complete complex value spaces. The existential constant precedes the space parameters. This is the uniform estimate needed when the value space varies with the time interval in the mixed endpoint problem.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_universal_homogen.summary: The multiplier norm constant is uniform across Banach spaces

TorusEuler.exists_offOrigin_compact_neig.text: Every compact set contained in `offOrigin` has a positive radius whose closed thickening remains compact and avoids the integer lattice. The theorem also gives strict separation from every lattice point. Here `offOrigin` is the punctured periodic lift, so excluding only the Euclidean point zero would be insufficient.
TorusEuler.exists_offOrigin_compact_neig.summary: A compact region stays away from the singular lattice

TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.text: For sufficiently large older frequency, a smooth torus parent with the supplied Fourier band, amplitude bound, small residual, and actual projected momentum equation satisfies the small central gradient powers required by amplification. The schedule relation converts the raw powers of `old` to powers of `μ`. The advection representative `A` is explicitly identified in the hypotheses.
TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.summary: Fourier and momentum estimates control the older central strain

TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.text: The raw central bounds derived from the projected residual become the amplification bounds $\mu^{1/32}$ and $\mu^{1/16}$ after imposing the scheduled relation between `old` and `μ`. The conclusion includes the actual within derivative on the comparison interval. Smoothness, band limitation, divergence freedom, and residual smallness remain explicit assumptions.
TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.summary: The actual parent supplies the amplification gradient powers

TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.text: The parent projected momentum identity, frequency band, divergence condition, and small pointwise residual imply the actual central gradient bounds with exponents nine and eighteen on any contained later interval. The theorem constructs the required torus representatives internally through the preceding result. A uniform initial frequency threshold is quantified before the parent data.
TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.summary: The actual residual identity yields raw central derivative bounds

TorusEuler.exists_open_farPressureSource.text: If a compact target is periodically separated from the support of $1-\chi$, it has an open neighborhood separated from the compact far source set. The proof first obtains a positive uniform separation radius, then uses a thickening of the target. The conclusion excludes equality modulo every lattice vector for all target-source pairs.
TorusEuler.exists_open_farPressureSource.summary: Compact separation persists on an open target neighborhood

TorusEuler.exists_oscillatoryPhaseSolve_.text: For a continuous forcing of periodic mean-zero phase profiles, there is a zero-initial solution with periodic mean-zero velocity and pressure, pointwise transversality, and the forced amplitude equation. The hypotheses `hM`, `hκ`, and `hκ₀` give continuous coefficients, the covector evolution, and initial nonvanishing. The forcing assumptions are `hf`, `hfper`, and `hfmean`; `hlr` permits even a degenerate closed interval. This is a fixed-label analytic solve, with continuity in the bounded-continuous phase-profile norm.
TorusEuler.exists_oscillatoryPhaseSolve_.summary: Zero initial transverse solve for a periodic forcing

TorusEuler.exists_oscillatoryTransverse_.text: A transverse amplitude exists for any transverse initial vector `V₀` at a time selected by `ht₀`. The coefficients satisfy continuity `hM`, the covector equation `hκ`, initial nonvanishing `hκ₀`, and continuous forcing `hf`. The conclusion supplies initial agreement, persistent transversality, nonvanishing covector, and the momentum equation with its exact pressure slope. Setting the forcing to zero gives the seed equation separately at each label; joint smooth dependence on labels is not asserted by this theorem.
TorusEuler.exists_oscillatoryTransverse_.summary: Transverse amplitude with prescribed initial data

TorusEuler.exists_paperA1_smoothSolution.text: Smooth coefficient lifts and forcing yield an integrated solution whose physical label velocity is jointly smooth on the closed slab. The assumptions `hK`, `hΩ`, `hPos`, and `hEnergy` are the coefficient, ellipticity, and energy hypotheses of Theorem A.1, while `hsK`, `hsΩ`, and `hsL` give joint smoothness. This helper concludes smoothness of the velocity. Smoothness of the displacement, constant, and pressure gradient is supplied in the full Theorem A.1 wrapper.
TorusEuler.exists_paperA1_smoothSolution.summary: Smooth velocity from smooth endpoint data

TorusEuler.exists_paperMeanParent_of_flo.text: The deformation, inverse deformation and velocity gradient of a smooth periodic parent give the coefficient object used by the mean inverse. The binder `hX : IsLabelFlowOn U X J(T)` supplies the actual flow; `hD`, `hL` and `hsharp` supply the inverse bound, gradient bound and quadratic upper bound on $H^\#$. The conclusion identifies all four coefficient fields, including the derivative at fixed label. No Euler equation for $U$ is assumed, and this coefficient construction itself does not require divergence freedom.
TorusEuler.exists_paperMeanParent_of_flo.summary: Coefficients constructed from the actual parent flow

TorusEuler.exists_paperPhysicalStepBudge.text: One coefficient $\Gamma_P$ controls the residual, pressure, central error and flow estimates for every parent scale $\mathsf D\ge1$. The hypotheses `hC`, `hL`, `hK`, `hLevel`, `hTail`, `hPrimary`, `hLead` and `hParent` require nonnegative fixed constants. The quantifier $\exists\Gamma\,\forall D$ makes the independence from the parent scale explicit. `PaperPhysicalStepBudget` records each inequality absorbed by $\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$.
TorusEuler.exists_paperPhysicalStepBudge.summary: One step constant controls all physical estimates

TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers.text: Smooth transverse profiles defined only on $[t_0,T]$ satisfy the launch-data estimate with a fixed power $\mathsf D^{20}$. In addition to the standing parent and central-wave bounds, the explicit profile hypotheses require phase periodicity and lattice twisting of the launch slice and source, their common support, transversality, and the projected ODE. The conclusion uses `paperHierarchyActiveVelocityNorm` and `paperHierarchyLaunchValueNorm`. No smooth extension of the profiles to times before $t_0$ is assumed.
TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers.summary: Forward estimates for profiles defined on the active interval

TorusEuler.exists_parameter_differentiab.text: For uniformly bounded, parameter-Lipschitz coefficients and forcing with the stated parameter derivatives, constructs a jointly continuous solution whose spatial parameter slices are differentiable. The initial family `x₀` is assumed differentiable. Adjoining a constant scalar coordinate turns the forced system into a homogeneous one; the conclusion does not include higher parameter derivatives.
TorusEuler.exists_parameter_differentiab.summary: A forced solution varies differentiably with its parameter

TorusEuler.exists_parameter_differentiab.text: Under uniform coefficient bounds, parameter Lipschitz bounds and a coefficient derivative continuous in time, constructs a jointly continuous fundamental solution. At every parameter it has a Fréchet derivative satisfying the forced variational equation and vanishing initially. The time interval may have zero length; infinite smoothness in the parameter is not asserted here.
TorusEuler.exists_parameter_differentiab.summary: The fundamental solution varies differentiably with its parameter

TorusEuler.exists_parentDerivedLowBounds.text: After one uniform lower threshold on the current frequency, the spatial gradient is bounded by $\lambda^9$ and its time derivative by $\lambda^{18}$ on the closed slab. The assumptions give joint smoothness, velocity size and Fourier band, residual size at the next frequency, and the projected momentum equation with the actual self-advection. Lean uses `derivWithin` so the assertion includes both slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.exists_parentDerivedLowBounds.summary: The gradient and time gradient obey the induction powers

TorusEuler.exists_parentGradient_halfHol.text: One nonnegative universal constant controls every torus field with bandwidth at most `4 * D`, `D ≥ 1`, and physical first-gradient norm at most `D`. Its lifted gradient has half-Hölder norm at most $CD^2$. The bandwidth hypothesis supplies the additional spatial variation control; a first-gradient supremum bound alone would not imply this estimate.
TorusEuler.exists_parentGradient_halfHol.summary: Bandwidth controls the parent gradient Hölder norm

TorusEuler.exists_parentMeanCoefficientJ.text: For a smooth periodic parent with controlled flow, inverse flow, and velocity jets on a slab of length at most one, this constructs uniform constants for the deformation, its adjoint, $K$, and $\Omega$. It proves their spatial smoothness and derivative bounds with powers $5n+1$, $5n+1$, $5n+2$, and $6n+3$ of $D$, respectively.
TorusEuler.exists_parentMeanCoefficientJ.summary: The actual mean coefficients have uniform jet bounds

TorusEuler.exists_parentMeanWeightedCoef.text: The weighted derivatives of $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$ satisfy a common bound $H_m\mathsf D^9\sqrt{\ell_*}$ at every positive order. The assumptions provide smooth parent flow, its velocity derivatives, both deformation bounds and $\ell_*\mathsf D^6\le1$. The derivative directions already contain the factor $\ell_*$. The theorem also bounds the coframe and its adjoint in the finite half-Hölder norms.
TorusEuler.exists_parentMeanWeightedCoef.summary: Weighted Hölder bounds for the mean coefficients

TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualLabelJet.text: Given nonnegative velocity-jet constants, this produces constants controlling a band-limited residual composed with the actual parent flow. A positive slab of length at most one, smooth periodic velocity, forward and inverse deformation bounds, and higher velocity jets are assumed. A residual of amplitude $A$ supported below $4D$ gains the bound $C_m A D^{6m}$ in label derivatives.
TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualLabelJet.summary: Pulling back the residual costs powers of the parent scale

TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualWeighted.text: A residual in the $4\mathsf D$ band with size $\lambda^{-5/2}$ retains that size in every weighted label norm after composition with the parent flow. The hypotheses include the flow derivative bounds and $\ell_*\mathsf D^6\le1$. The conclusion also provides boundedness of the derivative suprema used in the norm. Lean writes the frequency power as `hierarchyMeanExponent 2`, which is $-5/2$.
TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualWeighted.summary: The pulled back residual retains its small amplitude

TorusEuler.exists_parentVelocityJetBound.text: A continuous torus field in the $4\mathsf D$ band with gradient bounded by $\mathsf D$ satisfies $|\nabla^kU|\le V_n\mathsf D^k$ for $1\le k\le n$. The sequence `V` is chosen before the field and scale. Bernstein estimates are applied to gradient columns. The paper's $2\mathsf D$ velocity band is a special case, so the all-order parent derivative input is supplied by a separate result.
TorusEuler.exists_parentVelocityJetBound.summary: Fourier support controls all parent velocity derivatives

TorusEuler.exists_parent_coefficientJetB.text: The actual parent coefficients have separate powers before a common bound is chosen: $5n+1$ for the deformation, $7n+1$ for its inverse, $6n+1$ for the strain, $7n+2$ for $\kappa/\lambda$, $16n+4$ for the reciprocal squared length and $16n+8$ for the projection. The fixed sequence `R` supplies velocity derivatives, and the remaining hypotheses give smooth flow, deformation bounds and frequency normalization.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_coefficientJetB.summary: Individual derivative powers for the parent coefficients

TorusEuler.exists_parent_coefficient_lab.text: A nonnegative derivative family `R` fixes a common constant before the smooth periodic parent and frequency are chosen. Under the stated flow, inverse bounds and positive reference frequency, label differences of forward deformation, inverse deformation and material gradient are bounded with powers $D^6,D^8,D^7$. The transported covector has relative loss $D^{11}$, and its transverse projection has absolute loss $D^{24}$.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_coefficient_lab.summary: Parent derivative budgets control all localization coefficients

TorusEuler.exists_parent_genericLeading_.text: The leading pressure has upper Hessian bound $C\mathsf D^{2a+74}\lambda^{-1/4}$ for every admissible smooth cutoff. Constants are chosen from the parent velocity table `W` before the parent and frequency. The inputs include deformation bounds, velocity derivatives, carrier normalization, the central amplitude cap and `CenterWaveOn`. The quantifier `∀ χ : PaperWaveCutoff t₀ T` preserves the paper’s cutoff freedom. The conclusion bounds the quadratic form, not the absolute Hessian norm.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_genericLeading_.summary: The leading pressure has a uniform one-sided Hessian bound

TorusEuler.exists_parent_leading_pressur.text: Chooses $A\ge30$ and $C\ge0$ before the parent, carrier and exponent $a$. Given the parent jet table `W`, $A\le a$, $0<T\le1$, $D\ge2$, frequency at least one, normalized launch covector, $\|k\|\le D\,\mathrm{freq}$, deformation bounds, a central wave and regular seed with $\ell^{-1}=D^a$, proves $D_x^2p_1\le C D^{2a+74}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ as quadratic forms. The central amplitude cap is a hypothesis. This bounds the leading pressure from above, not its absolute Hessian norm.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_leading_pressur.summary: Uniform upper bound for the leading pressure

TorusEuler.exists_parent_projectedMoment.text: From the smooth solenoidal parent, its Fourier band, and its actual closed-slab projected residual, this theorem constructs torus representatives of advection and residual. It proves the residual band and smoothness, the gradient bounds $\mathrm{old}^9$ and $\mathrm{old}^{18}$, and a residual gradient bound $K\mathrm{old}^5\mu^{-3}$. The representatives agree with the original physical fields on the slab.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_projectedMoment.summary: Actual projected residuals determine all needed parent bounds

TorusEuler.exists_parent_scaledPhasePote.text: For a fixed nonnegative parent jet-control sequence, chooses an order-dependent nonnegative constant before any parent flow, carrier, or frequency. Smooth periodic parents with bounded deformation and the stated normalized center covector then yield smooth scaled potential coefficients and order-`n` jet bound $C(n)D^6/\mathrm{freq}$. Radius smallness $\ell\cdot D^{16} \le  1$ is required on the entire closed time slab.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_scaledPhasePote.summary: Actual parent potential coefficients have uniform finite jet budgets

TorusEuler.exists_periodicFarMultiplierJ.text: For compact periodically separated target and source sets, a common open target neighborhood supports measurable kernel jets, a uniform norm bound at every order, and the actual next-order derivative relations. The source measure is arbitrary. Compactness of the difference region and smoothness off the lattice supply all the analytic hypotheses needed by the far-integral theorem.
TorusEuler.exists_periodicFarMultiplierJ.summary: The actual periodic kernel satisfies the separated integral hypotheses

TorusEuler.exists_periodicPressure_of_le.text: A periodic half Hölder field `f` has a periodic mean-zero potential whose gradient is $\mathbb P f-f$. The normalization is the integral over `centeredCell`. This theorem recovers a pressure for the negative complement, with the sign matching the Euler equation. It assumes the genuine Hölder domain rather than trusting the raw projection formula.
TorusEuler.exists_periodicPressure_of_le.summary: The Leray complement is a normalized pressure gradient

TorusEuler.exists_periodic_meanZero_pres.text: Uniform gradient convergence on `I × centeredCell`, periodicity of the approximants and limit, and spatial differentiability give a pressure family whose slices have zero mean and gradient `g t`. The conclusion is for each `t ∈ I`. It asserts no joint time continuity or time differentiability of the selected family; those require later arguments.
TorusEuler.exists_periodic_meanZero_pres.summary: Recover a normalized pressure separately at every time

TorusEuler.exists_periodic_meanZero_pres.text: For differentiable periodic pressures whose gradients converge uniformly to `g`, the theorem constructs a periodic pressure with zero cell mean and gradient exactly `g`. It does not assume convergence of the original pressure values: constants are first normalized at one point, then the final mean is removed. Smoothness is a separate conclusion requiring regularity of `g`.
TorusEuler.exists_periodic_meanZero_pres.summary: A uniform gradient limit has a normalized periodic potential

TorusEuler.exists_periodic_offOrigin_cut.text: A compact set away from the periodic origin admits a smooth periodic cutoff equal to one near the set and zero near every lattice point. The hypotheses are `hK : IsCompact K` and `hKo : K ⊆ offOrigin`. The conclusion also places the cutoff in $[0,1]$ and supplies separation between $K$ and the support of $1-\chi$. That separation allows the far pressure kernel to be differentiated without its singularity.
TorusEuler.exists_periodic_offOrigin_cut.summary: A periodic cutoff separates the compact set and origin

TorusEuler.exists_periodically_separated.text: If every difference between points of compact target and source sets avoids the integer lattice, their periodic separation remains uniformly positive on a closed thickening of the target. The proof applies compact off origin separation to the difference set. This provides a common open region on which derivatives of the far kernel are bounded.
TorusEuler.exists_periodically_separated.summary: Source separation persists near the compact observation region

TorusEuler.exists_perturbedLabelFlows.text: Jointly $C^1$ periodic fields `U` and `b` have a family of flows for $U+\varepsilon b$ on the same closed interval, for every real parameter. The output is a choice of pointwise flows. The theorem does not yet assert continuity or differentiability of that family with respect to the perturbation parameter.
TorusEuler.exists_perturbedLabelFlows.summary: Flows for every scalar velocity perturbation

TorusEuler.exists_phaseJetBound_scaledRa.text: A fixed number of radius-normalized envelope derivatives has a bound that depends on the derivative order alone.
TorusEuler.exists_phaseJetBound_scaledRa.summary: Envelope derivatives are bounded after radius normalization

TorusEuler.exists_projectedHilbertSoluti.text: For a closed Hilbert subspace and an ambient bounded operator coercive there with positive constant `c`, every ambient forcing `f` has a unique subspace solution tested against all vectors in that subspace. Its norm is at most $\|f\|/c$. This supplies Hilbert existence and uniqueness; spatial Hölder regularity and identification with the Euler correction are separate steps.
TorusEuler.exists_projectedHilbertSoluti.summary: A unique weak solution with a coercivity bound

TorusEuler.exists_radial_scaledPhaseSlow.text: For $0<r\le1$, multiplying a smooth slow factor by the radial envelope and evaluating at the rescaled label preserves finite derivative bounds up to a constant depending only on `n`. The envelope becomes the unit envelope under this rescaling. The input bound `A` must be nonnegative, and the conclusion also records smoothness.
TorusEuler.exists_radial_scaledPhaseSlow.summary: Localization preserves the rescaled slow derivative budget

TorusEuler.exists_realFourierCutoffPoiss.text: On a positive closed slab, starts with a smooth periodic solenoidal approximate velocity satisfying its momentum equation and matching torus representatives for velocity and residual. For an even cutoff symbol it constructs a jointly smooth, periodic, mean-zero pressure for the truncated field. Its Poisson equation and equality of the true residual with the cutoff projected residual are certified together.
TorusEuler.exists_realFourierCutoffPoiss.summary: The cutoff receives its actual normalized Euler pressure

TorusEuler.exists_realTruncatedParentPro.text: On a nondegenerate closed slab, assume smooth periodic `V,RV`, divergence-free `V`, and the momentum identity `hMom` with the supplied smooth periodic pressure. For an even smooth cutoff, supported in the radius-two ball and one on the unit ball, constructs representatives and identifies actual projected momentum. For $P\ge2$ and $\Lambda\ge1$, put $\varepsilon=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\sup_t\|V(t)\|_{C^{P,1/2}})^2$. The order-two tail is at most $C_t\varepsilon$; the order-one momentum norm is at most $C_r\sup_t\|RV(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}+C_t\varepsilon$. The prefactor $C_r$ precedes $P$, and $C_t$ precedes $\Lambda$.
TorusEuler.exists_realTruncatedParentPro.summary: Bound the actual truncated parent momentum

TorusEuler.exists_scaledFlow_on_Icc.text: For a complete normed space, a jointly continuous field with uniform size and spatial Lipschitz bounds has a two-time family satisfying the initial and trajectory equations throughout the closed interval. The theorem makes no claim about times outside that interval. If the interval is empty, the restricted conditions are vacuous.
TorusEuler.exists_scaledFlow_on_Icc.summary: Bounded Lipschitz fields have flows on the whole slab

TorusEuler.exists_scaledFlow_with_deform.text: A bounded smooth finite-dimensional field with derivative bound `K` and projected derivative bound `M` has a two-time flow when `hSmall` holds. The output includes restart, differentiability, derivative norm at most two, and projected-displacement derivative at most $2M|t-s|$. These are properties of an actual constructed flow rather than estimates for a hypothetical variational matrix.
TorusEuler.exists_scaledFlow_with_deform.summary: A scaled flow with quantitative derivative control

TorusEuler.exists_scaled_wavePhaseJetBou.text: At every finite order, a constant at least one bounds the mixed jets of both $F_h(hs)$ and its normalized primitive $P_h(hs)$ by `C * h`, uniformly for $0<h\le1$. The profiles are independent of the label variable. The same chosen constant covers both functions, which allows the velocity and pressure estimates to share one phase budget.
TorusEuler.exists_scaled_wavePhaseJetBou.summary: Both normalized phase profiles have uniformly small jets

TorusEuler.exists_scheduledEulerConstruc.text: Given uniform physical estimates and a schedule-selection hypothesis, constructs scheduled Euler data for every sufficiently large initial frequency. The schedule may impose an additional property depending on the radius exponent. The conclusion fixes one exponent parameter and one monotone threshold function before that frequency is varied, and it retains the requested radius floor and additional property.
TorusEuler.exists_scheduledEulerConstruc.summary: A compatible numerical schedule gives one physical construction

TorusEuler.exists_scheduledEulerConstruc.text: For a finite index type and uniform physical estimates, uses the general numerical schedule theorem to construct a scheduled Euler sequence above any prescribed initial-frequency floor. It fixes the exponent parameter and monotone threshold function uniformly for all sufficiently large initial frequencies. The strength constant is the explicit value $18e^3$.
TorusEuler.exists_scheduledEulerConstruc.summary: The basic schedule satisfies all selected physical budgets

TorusEuler.exists_slabTimeJet_torusFouri.text: For a smooth periodic velocity field on `a < b`, suppose `g t` represents every time slice on the torus and has the fixed Fourier band `R`. Then every order-$q$ within-time derivative has a continuous torus representative with the same band at all times in the slab. Outside the interval the chosen representative is unconstrained; the proof differentiates vanishing Fourier coefficients on the interval.
TorusEuler.exists_slabTimeJet_torusFouri.summary: Time differentiation preserves a fixed Fourier band

TorusEuler.exists_smoothExtensionOfClose.text: Smooth extension in both time directions, retaining agreement at the left endpoint of the original closed slab.
TorusEuler.exists_smoothExtensionOfClose.summary: Extending a smooth field beyond the closed time slab

TorusEuler.exists_smooth_meanZero_L2_app.text: Given `hT : 0 < T`, `hε : 0 < ε`, an $L^2$ path `hv`, and the zero interval integral `hv0`, there is a globally smooth path with the same zero integral and $L^2$ error below $\varepsilon$. The conclusion does not require the approximant to retain compact support after subtracting its mean.
TorusEuler.exists_smooth_meanZero_L2_app.summary: Approximating zero mean paths by smooth ones

TorusEuler.exists_spatialHolderHalfNorm_.text: Smooth spatially periodic fields on a nondegenerate compact time slab have a uniform spatial half-Hölder norm at every finite order.
TorusEuler.exists_spatialHolderHalfNorm_.summary: Smooth periodic fields have uniform finite Hölder norms

TorusEuler.exists_spatialHolderHalfNorm_.text: A common bound $K$ for all actual coordinate derivatives through order $n$ controls the lifted $C^{n,1/2}$ norm by $C_nK$. The theorem requires nonnegative $K$, the directional derivative identities for `w`, and the bound on every list of length at most $n$. Its constant is chosen before `w` and $K$. Together with the converse estimate, this translates the derivative-word argument back to the norm used in the paper.
TorusEuler.exists_spatialHolderHalfNorm_.summary: Coordinate derivative bounds control the lifted Hölder norm

TorusEuler.exists_spatiallyPeriodic_cont.text: Given a smooth field `g` on `J × offOrigin` agreeing with a spatially periodic field `f` on `A × offOrigin`, constructs a smooth extension with the same agreement and spatial periodicity at every time. The time set `J` is open. A normalized locally finite sum of lattice translates preserves agreement; the statement supplies neither an Euler equation nor divergence preservation.
TorusEuler.exists_spatiallyPeriodic_cont.summary: Making the smooth extension spatially periodic

TorusEuler.exists_sub_latticeVector_mem_.text: Every point of the lift has a representative in the centered cell.
TorusEuler.exists_sub_latticeVector_mem_.summary: Every spatial point has a centered representative

TorusEuler.exists_summable_bound_dyadic_.text: For dyadic kernels with numerator scale $2^{j(3+m)}$ and decay order `m+4`, bounded observation points separated from every lattice singularity admit a summable majorant over both scale and translation. One surplus decay power produces geometric decay in `j`; the spatial exponent exceeds dimension three. Positive separation is essential.
TorusEuler.exists_summable_bound_dyadic_.summary: Separation makes the scale and lattice sum converge together

TorusEuler.exists_summable_bound_lattice.text: A kernel with decay order above three has a summable lattice majorant uniform for observation points with norm at most `R`. The assumptions require nonnegative amplitude and radius and scale at least one. The triangle inequality compares translated distances with lattice size, giving a bound independent of the observation point.
TorusEuler.exists_summable_bound_lattice.summary: Polynomial decay uniformly controls all translates on bounded sets

TorusEuler.exists_switchRate_threshold.text: Given nonnegative constants `C` and `K`, one threshold works for every parent frequency above it and every $0\le L\le(\log\mu)^2$. If $r\le K\mu^{1/8}L$, then $Cr e^3\le\mu$. The proof absorbs the logarithmic factor into $\mu^{7/8}$; it does not require a separate positivity hypothesis on `r`.
TorusEuler.exists_switchRate_threshold.summary: A logarithmic growth rate fits below the parent frequency

TorusEuler.exists_switchedLeadingProfile.text: For each order, chooses one constant controlling the rescaled leading velocity and frequency-weighted pressure. The hypotheses explicitly assume smoothness and jet budgets for the slow envelope-amplitude factor and the pressure coefficient; those budgets are not derived here from a parent flow. Multiplication by the scaled phase profiles supplies the remaining frequency factor, giving bounds proportional to $\gamma\lambda^{-5/4}$.
TorusEuler.exists_switchedLeadingProfile.summary: Slow factor bounds produce the full leading jet estimates

TorusEuler.exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_cut.text: For a compact target, a continuous cutoff between zero and one, and periodic separation from the complementary support, uniform convergence of continuous velocities on the closed cell yields convergence of every far pressure gradient jet on one open target neighborhood. No convergence of source derivatives is required. The proof combines an integrable tensor difference with the smooth separated kernel bound.
TorusEuler.exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_cut.summary: Uniform velocity limits suffice for every separated pressure derivative

TorusEuler.exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_pre.text: Smooth periodic velocities converging uniformly on the closed cell and in every jet on compact off-origin sets have pressure gradients converging in every jet on an open neighborhood of each compact target contained in `offOrigin`. The limit velocity is continuous globally, smooth off the lattice and periodic. A smooth local limiting pressure is constructed by adding the near multiplier pressure to the far kernel pressure.
TorusEuler.exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_pre.summary: Global values and local jets determine the terminal pressure gradient

TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.text: For each pair of degrees `n,k`, chooses a nonnegative constant independent of the positive scale and evaluation time. The `k`th derivative norm is at most $A\varepsilon^n(\varepsilon^{-1})^k$. Compact support bounds the fixed atom’s derivatives, and the linear rescaling supplies the scale factors; no ordering of `n,k` is needed.

When `k ≤ n`, the atom derivative estimate can be written as $A\varepsilon^{n-k}$ for every positive scale and time. The natural-number subtraction is justified by the order hypothesis. For `k=n` there is no smallness factor; strictly lower derivative orders are the ones that become small as the support shrinks.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.summary: Lower derivative bounds gain a positive scale power

TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.text: Given nonnegative weights `W k` and a positive tolerance `δ`, chooses one radius $0<\varepsilon\le1$ so that all weighted derivatives of orders `k<n` of the degree-`n` atom are bounded by `δ` everywhere. The finite range of lower orders permits a common radius. When `n=0`, that family of requirements is empty.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.summary: One radius makes all lower derivatives small

TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelExtension.text: For a sequence `a n` of smooth, individually compactly supported spatial functions into a complete real normed space, constructs a jointly smooth field whose `n`th time derivative at zero is `a n`. The proof chooses data-dependent shrinking radii, proves summable bounds for every joint derivative order, and differentiates the series. It asserts existence, not a continuous linear extension operator.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelExtension.summary: A smooth field with arbitrary compactly supported boundary jets

TorusEuler.exists_terminalBoundaryLocali.text: In finite-dimensional space, a smooth field on a nondegenerate closed slab yields a neighborhood `V` of any chosen point in the open spatial set and smooth compactly supported extensions of every terminal time jet. All orders agree with the original jets on the same `V`. A single spatial bump supplies this common neighborhood before the Borel series is formed.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalBoundaryLocali.summary: Localizing all boundary jets near one spatial point

TorusEuler.exists_terminalCutoffStress_h.text: Fix a smooth unit cutoff multiplier and `depth ≥ 2`. A nonnegative constant is chosen before the radius and the two input fields. For positive `Λ` and spatially $C^{\mathrm{depth},1/2}$ inputs, the stress divergence has $C^{1,1/2}$ norm at most $A\Lambda^{2-\mathrm{depth}}$ times their depth norms. The two-derivative loss accounts for divergence and the final Hölder order.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalCutoffStress_h.summary: Bound the divergence of a bilinear cutoff stress

TorusEuler.exists_terminalFlowLinearJetB.text: Chooses nonnegative spatial constants from `R`, `W`, and `q` before the individual flow and frequencies. For a smooth periodic label flow with `0 < T ≤ 1`, `D,A ≥ 1`, deformation bounds, spatial velocity estimates, and the supplied mixed velocity bound, it bounds forward deformation, inverse deformation, material gradient, and the normalized covector through order `q`. All four use slope $16$, amplitude `terminalFlowTimeAmplitude`, and one constant function. The positive carrier is normalized at a specified launch time.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalFlowLinearJetB.summary: The flow coefficients share one spatial growth slope

TorusEuler.exists_terminalMaterialIterat.text: For fixed material order $j$ and remaining time order $q$, this chooses constants before the interval, fields, and scales. Given smoothness and mixed bounds through time order $q+j$ for $U,f$, the $j$fold material derivative of $f$ satisfies a bound with amplitude $A(1+D^pA_U)^j$ and the same spatial slope $p$. Nonnegative scales and `a < b` are required.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalMaterialIterat.summary: Material iteration preserves a fixed spatial derivative slope

TorusEuler.exists_terminalMaterialPullba.text: For fixed $q$, this chooses a nonnegative constant family independent of the later fields and scales. Assume a smooth periodic parent with label flow, mixed bounds of spatial slope one for $U,f$, and flow derivatives bounded by $C_X(j)D^{5j}$. With `0 < T` and `D ≥ 1`, the pullback $f(t,X(0,t,x))$ has time order $q$, spatial slope six, and amplitude $A(1+DA_U)^q$.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalMaterialPullba.summary: Pullback time derivatives have spatial slope six

TorusEuler.exists_terminalMeanCoefficien.text: For fixed $q$ and nonnegative input constants, this selects three constant families for the algebraic mean coefficients. Smooth matrix fields $F,M$ with common mixed bound of amplitude $A$ and spatial slope $p$ yield amplitude $A^2$ for $F^*F$ and $A^3$ for the vorticity form and $2F^*MF$. It assumes neither that $F$ is a flow derivative nor that $F_t=MF$; applications supply that interpretation.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalMeanCoefficien.summary: Mean coefficients inherit the supplied mixed derivative bounds

TorusEuler.exists_terminalMeanParentInve.text: From a nonnegative parent derivative constant family, this chooses $p,s_0,H$ before the flow and scale. For a smooth periodic label flow with `0 < T ≤ 1`, `D ≥ 2`, `0 ≤ L ≤ D`, deformation bounds, and coefficient identifications, every supplied recovery has `TerminalMeanParentInverseData rec p`. For $s\ge s_0$, positive coefficient words at radius $\ell=D^{-s}$ also have the bound $H(|w|)D^9\sqrt\ell$.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalMeanParentInve.summary: The parent flow supplies both inverse caps

TorusEuler.exists_terminalSmoothExtensio.text: A jointly smooth field on a closed time slab over an open spatial set extends smoothly past the right endpoint. The hypotheses are `ha : a < T`, `hO : IsOpen O` and `hf : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (Icc a T ×ˢ O)`. The codomain is a complete real normed space and the spatial domain is finite dimensional. The conclusion gives smoothness on $(a,\infty)\times O$ and agreement on the original closed slab. The source constructs boundary jets and glues local extensions.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalSmoothExtensio.summary: Smooth extension through a terminal time boundary

TorusEuler.exists_terminalTimeCutoffResi.text: This chooses a nonnegative constant `Cr` and costs `Ct q depth` before the stage, radius, or fields. For a smooth periodic approximate velocity and residual, positive `T,Λ`, `i ≤ q`, and `depth ≥ 2`, a common depth-norm bound `M` on velocity jets through order `i` gives a $C^{1,1/2}$ residual bound $C_r\|\partial_t^iR_V\|+C_t\Lambda^{2-\mathrm{depth}}M^2$ at every slab time. The input residual norm has order one. Only `Ct` may depend on the time order and depth.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalTimeCutoffResi.summary: Choose uniform constants for the differentiated cutoff residual

TorusEuler.exists_terminalWaveRelayGeome.text: Fix a nonnegative cost array and time order. A single output array is chosen before the positive slab and scales `D,A ≥ 1`. Mixed bounds for smooth inverse coframe and strain yield all three geometric row bounds with common amplitude $\|\ell^{-1}\|A^2$ and spatial slope sixteen. The statement permits `ell = 0`, when both the rows and the displayed amplitude vanish algebraically.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalWaveRelayGeome.summary: One mixed bound controls all geometric relay rows

TorusEuler.exists_terminalWaveRelayPoten.text: From a nonnegative input cost array and fixed time order, this chooses one nonnegative output array before the slab or coefficient fields. On a positive time slab, assume smooth nonvanishing covectors, smooth strain, scales `D,A ≥ 1`, and mixed bounds for strain, covector, and reciprocal squared norm. The four actual relay coefficients are smooth and satisfy mixed bounds with common amplitude $A^6$ and spatial slope sixteen.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalWaveRelayPoten.summary: All normalized potential and pressure coefficients share a bound

TorusEuler.exists_theorem11Witness_of_in.text: Chooses a universal base-frequency threshold. Above it, any compatible stage family `s` and matching central waves yield a positive common terminal time, an Euler velocity and pressure, and an `EulerSingularityWitness`, together with closed-slab uniform convergence of the original stages. The family and matching waves remain hypotheses. This theorem does not independently construct the local successor steps.
TorusEuler.exists_theorem11Witness_of_in.summary: Compatible stages produce one Euler singularity witness

TorusEuler.exists_truncatedParentPoisson.text: A smooth divergence-free velocity in the $2\Lambda$ Fourier band has a smooth periodic pressure of zero spatial mean satisfying $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla U)^2)$. The hypotheses `hU`, `hband` and `hdiv` concern the actual velocity. The conclusion also identifies its momentum residual with projected momentum. No equation forcing that residual to vanish is assumed.
TorusEuler.exists_truncatedParentPoisson.summary: Zero mean pressure for the truncated parent

TorusEuler.exists_truncatedParent_T1.text: From a smooth periodic odd divergence-free velocity on a nondegenerate closed slab, chooses continuous torus representatives and proves the cutoff has joint smoothness, oddness, incompressibility and the retained frequency band. The symbol is assumed even, but its scale is arbitrary here. The chosen representatives are zero outside the slab; every representation and regularity claim is restricted to the slab.
TorusEuler.exists_truncatedParent_T1.summary: Truncation supplies the smooth odd incompressible parent

TorusEuler.exists_uniformJetBounds_of_co.text: For a globally smooth family `f`, periodic in its spatial argument, compactness of the parameter set `K` gives nonnegative constants `B m` controlling both joint and spatial derivatives of every order. Periodicity reduces arbitrary labels to the centered cell. The constants depend on the family and `K`, not on the chosen parameter or label.
TorusEuler.exists_uniformJetBounds_of_co.summary: Uniform derivative bounds for a periodic family

TorusEuler.exists_uniformLimit_of_summab.text: In a complete metric target, a summable sequence bounding consecutive distances from grade `N` gives a uniform limit on `s` and an explicit tail bound. Outside `s`, the constructed function is assigned the value `F 0`. The proof requires no global continuity and asserts convergence only on the specified set.
TorusEuler.exists_uniformLimit_of_summab.summary: Summable increments produce a uniform limit and tail bound

TorusEuler.exists_uniformLimit_of_vanish.text: When each consecutive increment splits as `B n + O n`, and the oscillatory part `O n` vanishes on `s` from grade `N`, summable bounds on `B n` give uniform convergence and the corresponding tail estimate. The hypotheses are pointwise on the stated set. No smallness of oscillations outside that set is used.
TorusEuler.exists_uniformLimit_of_vanish.summary: Vanishing oscillations leave a summable correction series

TorusEuler.exists_uniform_concrete_freez.text: For a fixed angular derivative budget `J ≥ 1`, one nonnegative constant works across the quantified real Hilbert spaces and their complexifications. The symbol must be a smooth homogeneous symmetric projection with five controlled derivatives; the strong projector must have its Fourier law and pairing. Positive coercivity and spatial Lipschitz bounds then give the compressed inverse estimate with power $145$.
TorusEuler.exists_uniform_concrete_freez.summary: One inverse constant works for all permitted coefficient spaces

TorusEuler.exists_uniform_freezingHalfHo.text: The frozen inverse and its projected version have spatial half-Hölder operator norms bounded by $C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|)^{11}$. The uniform constants are chosen after `hD` and before the Hilbert space, coefficient, and coercivity constant. Inputs include the complexification, smooth symmetric projection symbol, and its five annular jet bounds. The theorem also gives a difference estimate for sources vanishing on a radius-$r$ ball, at pairs separated by at most $r/4$.
TorusEuler.exists_uniform_freezingHalfHo.summary: Uniform Hölder bounds for frozen multipliers

TorusEuler.exists_uniform_log_gain_budge.text: For finitely many nonnegative constants, natural gain powers, and positive frequency exponents, one threshold works for the entire family. Above it, every $0\le L\le(\log\mu)^2$ satisfies $C_kL^{p_k}\le\mu^{a_k}$. Finiteness of the index type is essential to choosing a common threshold; the bound does not cover an arbitrary infinite family.
TorusEuler.exists_uniform_log_gain_budge.summary: A finite family of logarithmic losses shares one threshold

TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_iteratedDer.text: There is one nonnegative array `C q` such that, for every positive rate `r`, activation time `t₀`, and time `t`, the absolute switch derivative of order `q` is at most `C q * r^q`. The constants are chosen before all clock parameters. Compactness of `[0,1]` bounds positive derivatives of the transition, while order zero uses its bound by one.
TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_iteratedDer.summary: Choose switch derivative constants independently of the physical clock

TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_scheduled_w.text: A uniform switch constant gives $|\widetilde\chi'\gamma|\le\mu\lambda_{\rm next}^{-4}$ at every real time. The assumptions are positive rate and next frequency, the early bound $|\gamma|\le e^{3-4\log\lambda_{\rm next}}$, and absorption of $Cre^3$ by `μ`. The theorem converts the logarithmic gain to an exact inverse power before applying the weighted derivative bound.
TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_scheduled_w.summary: Switching loses only a fourth inverse frequency power

TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_weighted_it.text: Choose nonnegative constants uniformly in the clock and weight. For positive `q` and `r`, if `|γ| ≤ G` only on the closed switching interval and `G ≥ 0`, then the switch derivative times `|γ t|` is bounded everywhere by `C q * r^q * G`. No continuity or bound on `γ` outside that interval is required because the derivative vanishes there.
TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_weighted_it.summary: A small weight is needed only during switching

TorusEuler.exists_weighted_iteratedFDeri.text: For each derivative order, chooses a positive constant bounding $\ell^m$ times the order-`m` derivative norm of every positive-radius envelope at every label. Multiplication cancels the inverse-radius factor from the raw derivative estimate. Uniformity concerns radius and position; the theorem does not give one common constant across all derivative orders.
TorusEuler.exists_weighted_iteratedFDeri.summary: Radius-weighted envelope derivatives have a uniform spatial bound

TorusEuler.farKernelIntegral.text: The expression integrates the action of an operator-valued kernel `K x y` on a density `P y` over the supplied measure. The definition itself accepts arbitrary inputs. Its later estimates establish integrability, measurability, and uniform kernel bounds so that the expression represents the intended far pressure contribution.
TorusEuler.farKernelIntegral.summary: A separated kernel acts on an integrable source density

TorusEuler.farPressureCutoffTensor.text: The far tensor field is $(1-\chi)v\otimes v$ in complex coordinates. It is the density integrated against the pressure kernel on the separated source portion of the fundamental cell. Bounds $0\le\chi\le1$ later make its difference no larger than the uncut quadratic tensor difference.
TorusEuler.farPressureCutoffTensor.summary: Keep the quadratic tensor outside the near cutoff

TorusEuler.farPressureCutoffTensor_eq_ze.text: At a point of the kernel cell outside the far source set, the far tensor is zero. Since that point already lies in the cell closure, it must lie outside the topological support of $1-\chi$, forcing the scalar factor to vanish. This support certificate allows the multiplier integral to be restricted to the source set.
TorusEuler.farPressureCutoffTensor_eq_ze.summary: The far density vanishes outside its source enclosure

TorusEuler.farPressureSourceSet.text: The far source set is the intersection of the closure of the half-open kernel cell with the topological support of $1-\chi$. Including the closure makes this set compact. Actual far integration still uses its intersection with the half-open cell, avoiding duplicate lattice boundary representatives.
TorusEuler.farPressureSourceSet.summary: The far source occupies a compact portion of one cell

TorusEuler.fderivWithin_hierarchyProfile.text: For positive slab length, a profile with reflection multiplier `sign` has a derivative obeying the reflected chain rule. At the reflected point, the derivative applied to the reflected direction equals `sign` times the original derivative. The statement allows arbitrary real `sign`, with its compatibility supplied by `hf`.

If a direction `d` is sent to `-d` by reflection, differentiating a profile of reflection multiplier `sign` in that fixed direction gives multiplier `-sign`. This follows from the reflected derivative identity and linearity in the direction. Spatial label and phase directions are the intended applications.
TorusEuler.fderivWithin_hierarchyProfile.summary: A reversed direction reverses the derivative’s parity

TorusEuler.fderiv_fourierMode.text: The derivative of a Fourier mode in the real direction `v` equals $2\pi i(k\cdot v)$ times that mode. The direction need not be a coordinate vector. This is the basic differential-symbol formula used to identify divergence, gradient, and Laplacian on finite Fourier sums.
TorusEuler.fderiv_fourierMode.summary: A directional derivative multiplies by the frequency pairing

TorusEuler.fderiv_fourierMode_single.text: The Fréchet derivative of the mode along the coordinate unit vector is the mode multiplied by `fourierDerivativeSymbol k i`. This is the coordinate specialization of the directional formula. It fixes the derivative convention subsequently used to compute the divergence and gradient of synthesized polynomials.
TorusEuler.fderiv_fourierMode_single.summary: Coordinate differentiation applies the Fourier derivative symbol

TorusEuler.fderiv_frozenSymbol_inverse_a.text: The derivative of the inverse frozen operator in a variation `H` of the projection is $-A^{-1}(DA)A^{-1}$. The assumptions `hr`, `hμ`, and `hB` ensure invertibility, with the coefficient $B$ fixed. `frozenSymbolDerivative r B H` is the derivative of $A=rBr+I-r$ with respect to `r`. Angular differentiation uses this formula after composing with the frequency-dependent projection.
TorusEuler.fderiv_frozenSymbol_inverse_a.summary: Derivative formula for the frozen inverse

TorusEuler.fderiv_gradient_add_three_pre.text: The graph pressure Hessian is the sum of the three physical Hessians.
TorusEuler.fderiv_gradient_add_three_pre.summary: The pressure Hessian splits into three contributions

TorusEuler.fderiv_gradient_single_coord.text: For a real $C^2$ field, component `j` of the derivative of its gradient in direction `i` equals the derivative in direction `i` of its `j`th coordinate derivative. This identifies the operator-valued Hessian with the scalar mixed derivatives used in the Fourier calculation. It is not an appeal to symmetry of mixed derivatives.
TorusEuler.fderiv_gradient_single_coord.summary: Identify a Hessian entry with a mixed derivative

TorusEuler.fderiv_halfHolderProjectionLi.text: For periodic `f` in `SpatialHolderHalf 1`, the Fréchet derivative of its projected lift equals the lift of its derivative projected directionwise. `hP` supplies commutation with actual line derivatives. The proof reconstructs a Fréchet derivative from continuous directional derivatives, so the equality is backed by differentiability rather than by a default zero value of `fderiv`.
TorusEuler.fderiv_halfHolderProjectionLi.summary: Differentiation commutes with the lifted projection

TorusEuler.fderiv_liftConvolution_eq_lif.text: For an integrable scalar kernel and a C¹ function with globally bounded value and derivative, the Fréchet derivative of the lift convolution equals convolution with the derivative. Bounds `hM` and `hM'` provide domination for differentiation under the integral. The result is an operator-valued derivative equality, not merely a directional estimate.
TorusEuler.fderiv_liftConvolution_eq_lif.summary: One bounded derivative passes through convolution

TorusEuler.fderiv_lift_finiteFourierSum_.text: The coordinate derivative of a finite Fourier synthesis is the synthesis of its coefficients multiplied by the corresponding derivative symbols. The same finite frequency set is used on both sides. This makes differentiation compatible with the algebraic mode calculations without any interchange of infinite sums.
TorusEuler.fderiv_lift_finiteFourierSum_.summary: Differentiating a polynomial multiplies each coefficient

TorusEuler.fderiv_lift_realVectorFourier.text: A coordinate derivative of the real vector cutoff equals the cutoff of that coordinate derivative. The periodic lift is $C^1$ by `hg`, and `hd` identifies the torus field `d` with its derivative in direction `i`. The symbol and scale are arbitrary in this finite-sum identity. The statement concerns one spatial coordinate at a time; it is the concrete real-velocity commutation used to preserve divergence.
TorusEuler.fderiv_lift_realVectorFourier.summary: Coordinate differentiation commutes with the real cutoff

TorusEuler.fderiv_periodicLerayHolderLif.text: For a periodic vector field with first-order half-Hölder regularity, the derivative of its Leray lift is obtained by projecting its derivative field directionwise. The concrete spatial Leray operator supplies the general commutation hypothesis internally. This is the derivative formula used when a projected coefficient or residual is estimated at higher orders.
TorusEuler.fderiv_periodicLerayHolderLif.summary: Differentiate the Leray lift column by column

TorusEuler.fderiv_phaseMean_eq_phaseMean.text: For a globally smooth label-and-phase profile, the label Fréchet derivative of its phase mean equals the phase mean of its label derivative. The label space is proper and the target complete, supporting differentiation under the compact phase integral. This identity is used to show that the slow curl preserves zero phase mean.
TorusEuler.fderiv_phaseMean_eq_phaseMean.summary: Label differentiation commutes with phase averaging

TorusEuler.finiteCoefficientPower_iff_co.text: For $D\ge1$, the operator-norm coefficient-power predicate is equivalent to its bounded ordered-coordinate version. The forward direction bounds coordinate evaluations by the operator norm; the reverse expands multilinear maps in coordinates. Order-dependent constants may change, but the exponent `a` does not. Both sides retain spatial smoothness and uniformity over the time index.

TorusEuler.finiteCoefficientPower_iff_mu.text: The coefficient power condition expressed using full derivative operator norms is equivalent to the condition using sums over spatial multi-indices. The sole extra parameter assumption is `hD : 1 ≤ D`. Changing between these norms changes the order-dependent constants but preserves the absolute slope `a` in $D^{a(m+1)}$. The equivalence explains why the internal derivative representation does not lose the paper’s coefficient exponent.
TorusEuler.finiteCoefficientPower_iff_mu.summary: Operator and multi-index coefficient bounds are equivalent

TorusEuler.finiteFourierSum.text:
Synthesis of a trigonometric polynomial from its finite list of coefficients.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a finite sum, including the zero sum for an empty frequency set. Convergence questions do not enter the definition; Fourier approximation estimates require additional assumptions on the original field.
TorusEuler.finiteFourierSum.summary: A finite trigonometric sum from Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.finiteFourierSum_mFourierCoef.text: If the Fourier coefficients of a continuous field vanish outside radius `R`, summing its coefficients over `frequencyBand R` reconstructs the field. The proof compares all coefficients and uses Fourier uniqueness. No positivity of `R` is assumed: an empty band and the support hypothesis then force the field to be zero.
TorusEuler.finiteFourierSum_mFourierCoef.summary: A continuous band limited field equals its finite synthesis

TorusEuler.finiteFourierSum_neg_arg.text: Assume `ha` states that replacing $k$ by $-k$ multiplies each coefficient by a fixed real scalar `c`. The synthesis over a frequency ball then satisfies the same relation under spatial negation. Choosing $c=1$ or $c=-1$ gives the usual even or odd cases.
TorusEuler.finiteFourierSum_neg_arg.summary: Frequency symmetry transfers coefficient parity to the field

TorusEuler.firstCoupling_cumulative_log_.text: Positive couplings and nonnegative ratios with geometric decay satisfy $|\log(\nu_n/\nu_0)|\le4\varepsilon_0$, provided `hlocal` bounds each successive logarithmic change by $2\varepsilon_i$. The theorem assumes `hratio : ε (i + 1) ≤ ε i / 32`. It telescopes the logarithms and dominates their sum by the decaying ratio budget.
TorusEuler.firstCoupling_cumulative_log_.summary: Local coupling errors sum to a uniform bound

TorusEuler.firstCoupling_pi_bounds.text: The first coupling stays in $[\pi,4\pi]$ when it starts at $2\pi$, satisfies the local logarithmic error bound, and the prescribed ratios decay by a factor of at least thirty-two. The explicit smallness assumption is `hsmall : 4 * ε 0 ≤ Real.log 2`. The cumulative logarithm bound then places the multiplicative ratio in $[1/2,2]$.
TorusEuler.firstCoupling_pi_bounds.summary: All crossing couplings remain between pi and four pi

TorusEuler.firstCoupling_prefix_bounds.text: For a positive coupling sequence through index `n`, geometrically decreasing nonnegative ratios and local logarithmic increment bounds imply a uniform accumulated logarithmic bound. If the initial coupling is $2\pi$ and $4\varepsilon_0\le\log2$, every retained coupling lies between $\pi$ and $4\pi$. Later stages need no hypotheses: the proof temporarily extends the finite data by constants and zeros.
TorusEuler.firstCoupling_prefix_bounds.summary: Every constructed finite prefix keeps the coupling bounded

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector.text: The first-wave transported covector is embedded as a phase-independent profile in the twisted space with carrier firstWaveLaunchCovector freq. Its coefficients depend on time and label through the inverse deformation. This packages the exact wave vector for use in the concrete fast-gradient and phase-advection operators.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector.summary: The transported covector as a hierarchy coefficient

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector_ev.text: At a point satisfying the slab membership hypothesis, this embedded coefficient equals the first-wave transported covector at the point’s time and label. The phase coordinate does not enter the expression. The equality removes the nested profile wrappers and the off-slab zero branch, enabling direct use of the original coefficient formulas.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector_ev.summary: Read the transported covector from its profile

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector_ne.text: For `hf : freq ≠ 0`, the embedded transported covector is nonzero at every slab point. Evaluation reduces the claim to the explicit first-wave covector theorem. The on-slab condition is essential because the representative is zero outside; the result is not a global nonvanishing statement about that representative.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector_ne.summary: The actual transported covector never vanishes on the slab

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector_ph.text: The embedded transported-covector coefficient is independent of the phase variable at every point of the time slab. It comes from a global time-label field, so changing phase leaves its value unchanged. This explicit compatibility fact is needed when the concrete hierarchy interprets mean fields and averages phase advection.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector_ph.summary: The transported covector ignores the profile phase

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector_re.text: The embedded transported-covector coefficient has reflection multiplier one under simultaneous label and phase negation, with time fixed. Its original label field is even and the embedding is phase independent. This provides one of the coefficient symmetries used to propagate odd velocity profiles through the finite hierarchy.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyCovector_re.summary: The transported covector is even under joint reflection

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyInverseDefo.text: The explicit inverse shear deformation is embedded as a phase-independent twisted operator profile. Its joint smoothness and label periodicity are supplied by earlier theorems. The carrier k is unrestricted because the coefficient has no phase dependence. On the slab it is the actual backward-flow derivative in material coordinates.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyInverseDefo.summary: The inverse deformation as a hierarchy coefficient

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyInverseDefo.text: At a point satisfying the slab membership hypothesis, this embedded coefficient equals the explicit inverse shear deformation at the point’s time and label. The phase coordinate does not enter the expression. The equality removes the nested profile wrappers and the off-slab zero branch, enabling direct use of the original coefficient formulas.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyInverseDefo.summary: Read the inverse deformation from its profile

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyInverseDefo.text: The embedded inverse-deformation coefficient is independent of the phase variable at every point of the time slab. It comes from a global time-label field, so changing phase leaves its value unchanged. This explicit compatibility fact is needed when the concrete hierarchy interprets mean fields and averages phase advection.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyInverseDefo.summary: The inverse deformation ignores the profile phase

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyInverseDefo.text: The embedded inverse-deformation coefficient has reflection multiplier one under simultaneous label and phase negation, with time fixed. Its original label field is even and the embedding is phase independent. This provides one of the coefficient symmetries used to propagate odd velocity profiles through the finite hierarchy.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyInverseDefo.summary: The inverse deformation is even under joint reflection

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingOutp.text: This record packages the wrapped first-wave velocity and pressure as a `HierarchyTransverseOutput` for the concrete stationary-parent operators. Its velocity has zero phase mean, and its transversality makes advection in the phase direction vanish. The separate momentum theorem provides the leading equation needed by the finite recursion.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingOutp.summary: Supply the actual first wave to the abstract recursion

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingOutp.text: The first-wave output record satisfies `A.material L.V + A.phaseGrad L.p = 0` for the actual stationary-parent hierarchy operators. This directly reuses the wrapped momentum identity. It provides the leading equation required by `construct_momentum`, with no leading switching source because the first-wave switch is constant.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingOutp.summary: The packaged leading output solves its linear equation

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingPres.text: This constructs the radial, carrier-compatible pressure profile paired with the first leading velocity. It uses the same radius, phase scale, and centered phase shift. In addition to the support and wave-profile hypotheses, `hf : freq ≠ 0` guarantees smoothness of the inverse squared covector norm in its coefficient.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingPres.summary: The leading pressure uses the same carrier wrapping

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingPres.text: At a slab point, the hierarchy’s pressure equals the carrier-twisted periodization of the localized leading pressure profile. The same carrier phase correction appears as in the velocity. Its hypotheses include nonzero frequency and the smooth radial-support and phase-scale conditions used when constructing the pressure.

The wrapped leading pressure has reflection multiplier one. Its seed, transported covector, and material coefficient are even in labels, while the pressure primitive is even in phase. Nonzero frequency and the smooth localization hypotheses justify its construction, after which the wrapping preserves this combined parity.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingPres.summary: The first leading pressure is even under joint reflection

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingVelo.text: The first leading velocity is the primary oscillation multiplied by the radial envelope and wrapped with the launch covector. Positive radius, a strict gap before the cell boundary, and `0 < h ≤ 1` provide a smooth twisted profile. Its activation switch is identically one rather than a later-wave cutoff.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingVelo.summary: The fully active first velocity in the periodic hierarchy

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingVelo.text: At a slab point, the hierarchy’s leading velocity equals the carrier-twisted periodization of `firstWaveLeadingProfile`. The radial envelope is already included in that profile. This identity exposes the exact function used by the physical graph evaluation and avoids treating the wrapped profile as an unshifted label formula.

Evaluate the wrapped profile at the inverse shear-flow label and at the launch carrier paired with that label. The result is exactly the centered-periodized, localized transported leading velocity at the physical point. This establishes the connection between the function-space hierarchy representation and its Eulerian graph readout.
TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingVelo.summary: The hierarchy profile gives the actual physical leading wave

TorusEuler.firstWaveHierarchyLeadingVelo.text: The wrapped leading velocity changes sign when label and phase are both negated.
