The linear terms control curl and pressure rows, while the quadratic term allows the strain–coframe commutator. It is an explicit finite-order allowance rather than a universal numerical constant.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayGeometricRowBud.summary: A common allowance for the three geometric row types

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayLabelJet.text:
Compose the Fréchet derivative of a label–phase function with the inclusion of label directions. The resulting continuous linear map differentiates only the three label coordinates at fixed phase.

Default-value audit (b5): The Fréchet derivative is a total function and becomes zero at nondifferentiability points. The relay estimates supply differentiability or smoothness before using this as a classical label derivative.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayLabelJet.summary: The label component of a profile derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayMaterialRow.text:
This row is M composed with the curl row minus the curl row formed with GM. It records the commutator contribution to the material derivative of the divergence correction.

Default-value audit (b5): This combines the two curl rows algebraically and inherits their inverse-radius convention. Radius positivity is part of the analytic use, not of this raw row definition.

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.text:
The coefficient of the potential after normalizing the covector by the central frequency.

Default-value audit (b5): The raw inverse squared norm is total and gives zero at k=0. The wave-potential interpretation in the construction requires k≠0.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.summary: The vector-potential coefficient after normalizing frequency

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.text: Scaling a covector by a positive frequency multiplies its potential coefficient by the reciprocal frequency. The squared norm contributes two inverse factors, while the cross-product operator contributes one positive factor. The equality is valid even for the zero covector because the total coefficient definition is used; positivity is required only for the scaling parameter.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.summary: Potential coefficients gain one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureAmplitu.text:
The scalar row sends v to −2⟨k,Mv⟩/‖k‖². It is the amplitude contribution to the transverse pressure slope, before taking the mean-zero phase primitive.

Default-value audit (b5): At k=0 totalized inversion makes this scalar row zero. Pressure recovery uses a nonzero transported covector and the solution equation.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureAmplitu.summary: The amplitude contribution to the pressure slope

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureRow.text:
This scalar-to-vector map is multiplication by the coframe-transformed coordinate vector, with a factor ℓ⁻¹. It restores the unweighted slow derivative from the radius-weighted derivative norm.

Default-value audit (b5): The inverse label radius is total at zero. Applications use ℓ>0; the raw definition alone is not an invertible rescaling.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureRow.summary: The pressure-gradient row with inverse radius

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureSourceC.text:
The scalar row sends f to ⟨k,f⟩/‖k‖². The complementary amplitude row supplies the other term in the transverse pressure slope.

Default-value audit (b5): At k=0 this row is zero under the totalized formula. The transverse pressure construction requires nonzero covectors before interpreting the row as division by squared length.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureSourceC.summary: The forcing contribution to the pressure slope

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayTimeAmplitudeCo.text:
This continuous linear operator collects the terms involving M, the covector and the amplitude in the time derivative of the normalized vector potential. Its inverse powers of the covector norm require nonvanishing when it is used analytically.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula contains inverse powers of ‖k‖². Nonzero covectors are supplied by the parent geometry in the relay estimates; the raw expression at k=0 is not a time derivative of a physical wave potential.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayTimeAmplitudeCo.summary: The amplitude coefficient in the potential time derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_label.text: A smooth operator-valued coefficient bounded through order `n`, applied to one weighted label derivative of a profile bounded through order `n + 1`, has budget $2^nAC$. The label index is `Fin 3`; the phase coordinate is excluded. Reciprocal label scale is accounted for in the supplied coefficient rather than differentiated separately.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_label.summary: A coefficient times a label derivative loses one order

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_linea.text: Smooth phase-independent operator coefficients acting on smooth periodic zero-mean velocity and forcing profiles produce a smooth normalized primitive with an explicit word bound. The constant combines the two coefficient budgets and the factor from phase integration. Time is only an arbitrary index, so no time regularity of coefficients or forcing is assumed.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_linea.summary: A linear combination of profiles has a bounded phase primitive

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_fi.text: If every sampled derivative set is bounded above, the finite mixed norm bounds each word of order at most n. Boundedness is explicit because the norm is a finite sum of real suprema.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_fi.summary: The finite norm bounds all normalized words

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_ph.text: A normalized label-jet bound gives the same mixed-word bound for the phase-independent lift of the coefficient.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_ph.summary: Label bounds also control phase-independent mixed words

TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledCoframeRow.text: This definition composes one coordinate projection with the operator field `A` and multiplies it by $\ell^{-1}$. Applied to an advector, it is the chosen component of $Az$ divided by the label radius. It pairs with a radius-weighted coordinate derivative in the slow-advection estimate.
TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledCoframeRow.summary: A coframe row carries the reciprocal label radius

TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledPhaseCoefficie.text: The coefficient is the linear form $z\mapsto h^{-1}\langle\kappa,z\rangle$. Factoring this reciprocal width out of the weighted phase derivative recovers the physical fast-advection term. The definition permits arbitrary real `h`; the later identity cancelling the width assumes `hh : h ≠ 0`.
TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledPhaseCoefficie.summary: The phase coefficient carries the reciprocal width

TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_remainder_l.text: The exact algebraic remainder is bounded in an arbitrary seminorm from separate estimates for its linear, slow-product, completion-phase, and mean-phase terms. The assumptions include $\lambda\ge1$, nonnegative constants, and `loss * freq^(-1/12) ≤ 1`. The conclusion counts the retained tail pairs explicitly; the analytic product estimates are hypotheses here.
TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_remainder_l.summary: Component estimates control the exact finite remainder

TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_velocity_su.text: Given all measured level bounds through depth `P ≥ 1`, this theorem bounds the total oscillation at $\lambda^{-5/4}$, its part beyond the first velocity at $\lambda^{-23/12}$, and the total mean at $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Constants retain the number of levels and explicit powers of `loss`. The norms are arbitrary seminorm families satisfying the supplied nonnegativity conditions.
TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_velocity_su.summary: Summing levels separates the leading oscillation from corrections

TorusEuler.hierarchySlowAdvectionCompone.text: With nonzero label radius, this bounds the component $(Az)_i\partial_{a_i}g$ using the scaled coframe-row norm, the advector norm, and one extra order of the advected field. Smoothness and bounded jet sets are required for each input. The coefficient bound `hAN` is assumed; this statement does not establish the deformation estimates itself.
TorusEuler.hierarchySlowAdvectionCompone.summary: Slow advection uses one coframe row and derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchySmoothProfileSubmodu.text:
A smooth slab profile is represented by its zero extension. Values of this representative outside the slab do not enter any derivative or equation.

Default-value audit (b5): The representative is deliberately zero outside the slab. Smoothness is required within the slab, and no smooth zero extension across the time endpoints is claimed. If the slab is empty the stored function must be zero everywhere.
TorusEuler.hierarchySmoothProfileSubmodu.summary: Smooth slab profiles stored by zero extension

TorusEuler.hierarchyStepCap.text:
The order-dependent constants grow with depth through finitely many terms, independently of the frequency and parent loss.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

TorusEuler.hierarchyTailPairs.text:
The interaction pairs remaining after cancellation through depth $P$. The parameter `shift` is zero for label advection and one for phase advection. Filtering by `P + shift < i + j` gives $i+j\ge P+1$ in the first case and $i+j\ge P+2$ in the second. The underlying pair set also enforces positive indices and the depth cutoff, omitting the identically zero initial phase factors.

Default-value audit (b5): Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTailPairs.summary: The index pairs beyond the retained depth

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord.text: This recursively defines linear differentiation by a word in four coordinate directions. The first three directions carry the label scale and the last carries the phase scale; the empty word leaves the profile unchanged. Each step differentiates the previously obtained profile while preserving smoothness and both periodicity conditions.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord.summary: Apply a sequence of scaled label and phase derivatives

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_app.text: At any fixed time in the slab, the recursively packaged mixed derivative has exactly the value of `phaseOperatorWord` on the ordinary label-phase slice. Induction on the word uses the slice derivative identity. This confirms that the norm infrastructure measures actual derivatives, rather than independent stored jet data.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_app.summary: The profile operator equals the actual derivative word

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_bdd.text: A bounded time-only multiplier preserves the boundedness of all samples used for the finite norm, over any subset of the closed time slab.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_bdd.summary: Bounded time weights preserve bounded spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_exi.text: Every fixed mixed word has a common bound for its values and half-Hölder differences over the slab. The proof bounds a difference both by twice the uniform value bound and by a derivative bound times distance, then takes their geometric mean. The result supplies bounded measurement sets for the optional Hölder seminorm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_exi.summary: Interpolate bounded values and derivatives to a half-Hölder bound

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_exi.text: For positive slab length, each mixed label-phase derivative word of a twisted profile is uniformly bounded on the slab. The derivative word is itself represented by a smooth twisted profile, so compact-cell boundedness applies. The theorem gives existence of a constant for that word, without a quantitative frequency estimate.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_exi.summary: Every fixed derivative word has a uniform bound

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfileSubmod.text:
The actual phase-periodic profiles compatible with the label lattice.

Default-value audit (b5): This imposes a simultaneous lattice-and-phase identity on already phase-periodic smooth slab profiles. For k=0 it reduces to ordinary spatial periodicity; physical launch conditions decide whether that special case is relevant.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfileSubmod.summary: Phase profiles compatible with the label lattice

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfile_exist.text: Every smooth twisted profile has a nonnegative uniform bound over the full closed time slab and all labels and phases. Lattice and phase periodicity move each point into a compact centered cell times one phase period. Continuity on that compact set supplies the bound without requiring an a priori norm estimate.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfile_exist.summary: A twisted profile is bounded on the closed slab

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfile_exist.text: For positive slab length, one nonnegative Lipschitz constant controls every label-phase slice of a twisted profile on the slab. The derivative profile is uniformly bounded by compactness, and the global spatial mean-value estimate gives the Lipschitz property. The bound may depend on the whole profile and time interval.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfile_exist.summary: All time slices share a finite Lipschitz bound

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedSliceDerivati.text: For positive slab length, this linear profile operator takes the full derivative within the slab and restricts its directions to label and phase. The output is again a smooth twisted profile, now valued in bounded linear maps on the label-phase space. Time differentiation is excluded by construction.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedSliceDerivati.summary: Differentiate the profile with time held fixed

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedSliceDerivati.text: At an on-slab time, the value of `hierarchyTwistedSliceDerivative` equals the ordinary Fréchet derivative of the fixed-time label-phase slice. The equality connects the profile-space operation with the genuine derivative on the unrestricted spatial domain. Positive slab length is retained for constructing the profile-valued derivative.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedSliceDerivati.summary: Read the ordinary derivative of a time slice

TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_mean_parent_.text: For frequency at least one and nonnegative `loss`, the smallness condition $\mathrm{loss}\,\mathrm{freq}^{-1/12}\le1$ absorbs the parent factor in the mean estimate. The mean exponent differs from the inductive mean exponent by exactly $1/12$. The conclusion is a scalar power inequality at any natural level, not a mean-solver theorem.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_mean_parent_.summary: The mean loses its parent factor before reuse

TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_parent_loss.text: A nonnegative loss factor can be absorbed whenever `hsmall : loss * freq ^ (-1 / 12 : ℝ) ≤ 1`. With `hfreq : 1 ≤ freq` and spare exponent at least $1/12$, the conclusion bounds $\mathrm{loss}\,\lambda^{e-\mathrm{spare}}$ by $\lambda^e$. The paper applies this with a fixed power of $\mathsf D$ as the loss. This algebraic lemma explains why that parent power does not accumulate with the hierarchy depth.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_parent_loss.summary: One twelfth of frequency decay absorbs the parent factor

TorusEuler.hierarchy_advection_filtratio.text: The complete finite quadratic sum splits into interactions at levels $2$ through $P$ and interactions in the tail. The parameter `shift` distinguishes label from phase advection, so the same theorem handles both diagonal thresholds. This is a finite-sum identity for any additive commutative monoid. In the momentum calculation, the level sums cancel against the solved equations, leaving only the high-level interactions and the final linear correction.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_advection_filtratio.summary: The quadratic sum separates retained levels from the tail

TorusEuler.hierarchy_collar_of_support_b.text: If the oscillatory part vanishes whenever $\|a\|>2\ell$, with $\ell\ge0$ and $2\ell<1/2$, then a positive collar near every centered-cell face has `f = mean`. The proof chooses width $1/2-2\ell$. No topology or normed structure on the target is required because the conclusion is equality of values.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_collar_of_support_b.summary: Small radial support provides a collar near cell faces

TorusEuler.hierarchy_completion_previous.text: The frequency exponent of the preceding divergence correction equals the current oscillatory exponent minus an additional third. The named hypothesis `hp : 1 ≤ p` ensures the natural subtraction `p - 1` matches ordinary subtraction after conversion to real numbers. At `p=3`, it places the correction of the second oscillation within level three with a spare factor $\lambda^{-1/3}$. This is the exponent bookkeeping identity, not an analytic estimate for the actual field.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_completion_previous.summary: Previous completion exponent and current oscillatory exponent

TorusEuler.hierarchy_correction_level_bo.text: This specializes the correction-level estimate to the recurrence’s default residual loss. The coefficient `K` is automatically at most `K * L^5` when `K,L ≥ 1`. The analytic recurrence, previous-level bounds, smallness condition, and three-order derivative reserve remain hypotheses of the resulting bound.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_correction_level_bo.summary: Close a correction step with the standard residual budget

TorusEuler.hierarchy_correction_level_bo.text: Given the analytic norm recurrence and bounds at all earlier positive levels through order `N`, this obtains the full measured bound at a retained correction level and order `n`. It requires `n+3 ≤ N ≤ H`, a controlled optional residual loss, and the sixth-power parent smallness condition. The conclusion uses the explicit finite constant `hierarchyStepCap`.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_correction_level_bo.summary: Close one correction level with three derivative orders reserved

TorusEuler.hierarchy_depth_tail_of_measu.text: Per-level bounds at order `n + 1`, terminal-level comparisons, and measured product and linear estimates yield the exact remainder bound at exponent `hierarchyOscExponent (P + 1)`. The smallness condition is $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. The coefficient records the tail-pair count and $2K(C+1)^2$; the theorem does not derive its analytic operator estimates.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_depth_tail_of_measu.summary: Measured products give the remainder rate at every depth

TorusEuler.hierarchy_fastAdvection_timeF.text: If each phase-and-label slice of `g` is differentiable, scalar factors depending only on time can be pulled out of the fast advection term. The two scalars combine as `r t * q t`. No time regularity is required: the derivative in this equality is taken only in the phase direction.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_fastAdvection_timeF.summary: Time factors leave phase differentiation unchanged

TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_completion_exp.text: The phase cost $\lambda^{3/2}$, a preceding completion, and an oscillatory block combine to the current oscillatory exponent minus $1/12$. The assumptions `hi : 1 ≤ i` and `hij : i + j = p + 1` identify the relevant interaction. This is the smallest spare frequency power in the induction. It is therefore the exponent that determines the smallness condition used to absorb the parent factors.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_completion_exp.summary: Fast completion advection leaves one twelfth of spare decay

TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_mean_exponent.text: A mean measured with the induction exponent, acting through a phase derivative on an oscillation, has exponent equal to the target oscillatory exponent minus $1/4$. The assumption `hij : i + j = p + 1` fixes the interaction level. It includes the case where the current mean acts on the leading oscillation. This is why that source can be estimated after the mean solve without requiring the new transverse velocity.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_mean_exponent.summary: Mean phase advection leaves one quarter of spare decay

TorusEuler.hierarchy_label_inputs_previo.text: If two positive indices satisfy $i+j=p$, each is strictly smaller than $p$. The hypotheses `hi` and `hj` exclude a zeroth-level input. This elementary fact makes the label-advection part of the hierarchy recursive in already constructed levels, without making any estimate on the associated fields.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_label_inputs_previo.summary: Label advection uses strictly earlier levels

TorusEuler.hierarchy_label_product_expon.text: The sum of two oscillatory exponents equals the mean exponent at their combined level, and also equals the oscillatory exponent there minus $7/12$. The variables `i` and `j` are the two levels; no analytic hypothesis is needed. This identity supplies the frequency arithmetic for $(Z_i\cdot\mathbf d)Z_j$ after the product and derivative estimates have bounded its norm.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_label_product_expon.summary: Label products have seven twelfths of spare decay

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_analysis_cost.text: If the requested order `m` and depth `P` lie in the threshold range, the analytic cost at order `m + 3 * P` is bounded by a threshold built from the shifted cost table. The shift is part of the table before taking the finite maximum. No uniform bound over all orders is asserted.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_analysis_cost.summary: Include the derivative reserve in the cost table

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds.text: A hierarchy norm recurrence gives `HierarchyLevelBound` at every retained level with enough derivative reserve. The hypotheses are `recurrence : HierarchyNormRecurrence s freq L K P H`, `hf`, `hL`, and `hK`, placing frequency and constants at least one, and `hsmall : L ^ 6 * freq ^ (-1 / 12 : ℝ) ≤ 1`. The conclusion requires $n+3(p-1)+1\le H$. In particular, its oscillatory source and induction mean bounds have no remaining parent factor.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds.summary: The measured recurrence implies the induction bounds

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds_throug.text: A single finite order budget controls every requested order through the retained depth. The internal derivative reserve is included in the order argument of the analytic cost table.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds_throug.summary: One finite derivative reserve controls the retained hierarchy

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds_withRe.text: The norm recurrence yields bounds at every retained level $1\le p\le P$ whenever `n + 3*(p-1) + 1 ≤ H`. Three extra orders are spent per correction level and one on the leading completion. The common constant depends on depth, the derivative-order constant bound, and level; parent-loss control and frequency smallness remain explicit assumptions.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds_withRe.summary: Iterate the measured bounds through every retained level

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_budget_of_ste.text: For `D`, `freq` and `Γ` at least one, assume `6 * p ≤ b` and the step inequality $\Gamma D^b\le\mathrm{freq}^{1/32}$. Then $(D^p)^6\mathrm{freq}^{-1/12}\le1$. This is the smallness condition used by the level recurrence, derived from the stronger budget already imposed for the step.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_budget_of_ste.summary: The step inequality absorbs the hierarchy parent loss

TorusEuler.hierarchy_mean_inductive_shif.text: The induction exponent for the mean equals its sharper theorem exponent plus $1/12$. The identity holds for every natural-number level `p` and follows by unfolding the two affine expressions in that level. It explains the paper's replacement of a parent factor by $\lambda^{1/12}$ in the induction hypothesis. No estimate for the actual mean is part of this algebraic identity.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_mean_inductive_shif.summary: The two mean exponents differ by one twelfth

TorusEuler.hierarchy_mean_product_expone.text: Adding the two induction exponents for means gives the theorem's mean exponent at the combined level minus one. Thus a product of two means has an extra factor $\lambda^{-1}$ relative to the leading averaged oscillatory products, once the label-advection estimate is supplied. The theorem is only the exponent identity for natural-number indices `i` and `j`; it does not take profile fields as inputs.

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_apply_eq_.text: A continuous linear map applied pointwise to a continuous profile with zero phase mean still has zero phase mean. The ambient normed spaces are complete so the phase integral commutes with the map. This is the averaging step used for phase-independent coefficients in the hierarchy source cancellation.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_apply_eq_.summary: Linear maps preserve a vanishing phase mean

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_completio.text: The hypotheses give periodic differentiable phase profiles and the identity $\partial_s\langle\kappa,C\rangle=-\mathrm{divV}$. Integration by parts over one period then identifies the mean of $\langle\kappa,C\rangle Y_s$ with the mean of $\mathrm{divV}\,Y$. Continuity assumptions justify the integrals; this identity removes the costly phase derivative in the mean source.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_completio.summary: Averaging exchanges the fast derivative for divergence

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_labelDeri.text: For a jointly smooth function of label and phase, assume its phase average vanishes at every label. The average of the label derivative in any direction `v` then vanishes as well. The proof differentiates the parameter-dependent integral over a fixed period, rather than assuming cancellation only at the selected label.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_labelDeri.summary: Label differentiation preserves a vanishing phase mean

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_supplemen.text: The phase average of $(\kappa\cdot B)\,Y_s$ vanishes when `κ` and `B` are fixed vectors and `Y` is periodic. The named hypotheses `hYper`, `hY`, and `hYs` require period one, a specified derivative `Ys`, and continuity of that derivative. This proves why the mean correction's transport of the leading fast phase enters only the oscillatory equation. It gives no size estimate for that forcing.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_supplemen.summary: Mean advection of a fast derivative has zero average

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phase_inputs_previo.text: For $i\ge2$, $j\ge1$, and $i+j=p+1$, the completion level $i-1$ and the advected level $j$ are below $p$, while $i\le p$. Equality $i=p$ occurs exactly when $j=1$. Thus the same-level mean contribution is confined to its interaction with the leading wave.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phase_inputs_previo.summary: Only the leading wave reaches the current mean

TorusEuler.hierarchy_slowAdvection_timeF.text: The coefficient operator is linear in the advecting vector, and the derivative of `g` is taken in a label-coordinate direction. Consequently time-only factors on the two profiles factor out as their product. Slice differentiability of `g` is assumed; this identity does not differentiate either time factor or the coefficient field.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_slowAdvection_timeF.summary: Time factors leave label differentiation unchanged

TorusEuler.hierarchy_sum_fast_previous.text: Assuming `p ≤ P`, summing a function at $(i-1,j)$ over the fast pairs gives the corresponding sum over slow pairs. The statement holds in any additive commutative monoid, so it uses no analytic estimate. It supplies the precise reindexing after phase integration by parts replaces $C_i$ by the divergence of $V_{i-1}$.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_sum_fast_previous.summary: Shift the completion index in the finite sum

TorusEuler.hierarchy_weighted_coefficien.text: If a derivative of positive order $m$ costs at most $C D^{k(m+1)}$ and $\ell D^k\le1$, then its weighted size is at most $C D^{2k}\ell$. The assumptions include $D\ge1$ and nonnegative radius and constant. Keeping one factor of $\ell D^k$ produces the gain used in coefficient thresholds.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_weighted_coefficien.summary: A positive coefficient derivative retains a radius factor

TorusEuler.higherPressureGradientBudget_.text: The sum of higher pressure-gradient budgets is controlled by the decay at level two, $\lambda^{-23/12}$. The assumptions `hF`, `hV` and `hQ` are the source, velocity and pressure bounds for levels $2\le p\le P$; `hg` expresses the gradient budget in those quantities. The relation `hslow : cQ ≤ cSlow * freq` absorbs the slow pressure derivative. The theorem is scalar bookkeeping after the transverse pressure-gradient identity.
TorusEuler.higherPressureGradientBudget_.summary: The higher pressure gradients have the second-level decay

TorusEuler.higherPressureGraphCost_le.text: With `freq ≥ 1`, positive label length and phase width $h=\mathrm{freq}^{-1/2}$, assume inverse length and carrier size bounds. The explicit graph differentiation cost is then bounded by a constant times $\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. This numerical step is applied only once after reconstructing the pressure gradient from the transverse equation.
TorusEuler.higherPressureGraphCost_le.summary: One physical derivative costs three half frequency powers

TorusEuler.higherPressure_prefactor_le_p.text: The hypotheses bound the jet, carrier, inverse-length and loss factors by specified powers of a parent parameter `D ≥ 1`. The conclusion bounds their combined Hessian prefactor by an explicit power of `D`; dependence on retained depth appears through the cardinality of levels two through `P`. No frequency estimate is established by this algebra alone.
TorusEuler.higherPressure_prefactor_le_p.summary: Keep the higher-pressure parent exponent independent of depth

TorusEuler.holderBridge_exists_close_lif.text: Any two torus labels admit Euclidean representatives whose separation is at most twice their torus distance. The proof chooses a centered representative of their difference and estimates its Euclidean norm from its coordinate bounds. This is a controlled choice of lifts, not a claim that arbitrary representatives are close or that the metrics are isometric.
TorusEuler.holderBridge_exists_close_lif.summary: Nearby torus points have controlled Euclidean representatives

TorusEuler.homogeneousDyadicBlocks.text: Construct certified dyadic blocks from a symbol smooth away from zero by applying the fixed annular localization. The cutoff gives compact support, cancellation at zero, and the required frequency band. No degree-zero homogeneity hypothesis is needed to form these blocks; that hypothesis enters the theorem identifying their sum with the intended symbol.
TorusEuler.homogeneousDyadicBlocks.summary: Annular localization supplies the nonzero frequency blocks

TorusEuler.homogeneousHalfHolderMultipli.text: Define a bounded operator by summing the annular dyadic blocks and adding the constant field obtained from `A 0` applied to the input mean. Only smoothness away from zero is required to construct it. The separate `hhom` hypothesis in the Fourier-action theorem is essential before identifying this operator with the symbol `A` at nonzero frequencies.
TorusEuler.homogeneousHalfHolderMultipli.summary: Sum annular blocks and add the prescribed mean action

TorusEuler.homogeneousHalfHolderMultipli.text: Assume positive-scale homogeneity of `A` and `hB`, which gives the same coefficient formula for a supplied bounded L² operator `B`. Then embedding the constructed half-Hölder output equals applying `B` to the embedded input. Fourier uniqueness proves the equality; the theorem does not construct or estimate the separate L² operator.
TorusEuler.homogeneousHalfHolderMultipli.summary: Matching symbols identify the Hölder and weak operators

TorusEuler.homogeneousOffOriginMultiplie.text: This definition annularly localizes an operator symbol using the fixed dyadic cutoff, packages the compact smooth localization as a Schwartz map, and forms its full periodic kernel. Only smoothness away from zero is a formal input here. Homogeneity and the zero mode are separately relevant when identifying the resulting multiplier with a desired Fourier symbol.
TorusEuler.homogeneousOffOriginMultiplie.summary: The fixed annular partition selects an off diagonal kernel

TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3.text: Lift the coordinatewise imaginary-part map to vector-valued L² for a general measure. This gives a real continuous linear projection from complex paths to real paths. Together with the real-part map and embedding, it enables componentwise extension of operators that act on entire time paths.
TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3.summary: Take imaginary parts of vector valued L² paths

TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_I_smul.text: The imaginary part of $i v$ equals the real part of `v` in the L² quotient. This is the complementary component identity to the negative-real-part formula. Together they control multiplication by $i$ in the concrete path complexification without making pointwise choices of representatives.
TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_I_smul.summary: Multiplication by i turns real paths into imaginary parts

TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_apply_ae.text: The representative of `imagPartL2Vec3 μ v` equals the coordinatewise imaginary part of `v` almost everywhere. The statement records representative compatibility for a bounded map acting on an L² quotient. It is used alongside real-part compatibility to prove reconstruction and the squared-norm splitting of complex paths.
TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_apply_ae.summary: Path imaginary parts agree with pointwise imaginary projection

TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_complexify.text: The imaginary part of a complexified real L² path is the zero L² path. The proof compares the induced representatives and uses the vanishing imaginary part of each embedded real coordinate. This is a structural identity for arbitrary measure, independent of any PDE or endpoint constraint.
TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_complexify.summary: Embedded real paths have no imaginary component

TorusEuler.inductionCrossingStrengthCons.text: The numerical constant $18e^3$ is at least two, and its reciprocal is no greater than $e^{-1}/4$. These inequalities allow first-wave and later crossing strength bounds to share one induction convention. The theorem is a numerical comparison only; it contains no wave or schedule hypotheses.
TorusEuler.inductionCrossingStrengthCons.summary: One strength constant works for the whole induction

TorusEuler.inductionHalfLength.text: Defines the half length for wave `i+1` as $\mathrm{freq}_i^{-1/8}(4\log\mathrm{freq}_{i+3})^3$. The index shift accounts for the future logarithmic gain in the paper’s formula. This definition accepts any real-valued frequency sequence; positivity and geometric decay of the resulting lengths require the separate schedule and largeness theorem.

TorusEuler.inductionHalfLength_zero_le_q.text: If the base frequency is at least $4^{16}$ and the first half-length is bounded by its negative one-sixteenth power, that half-length is at most one quarter. The negative power reverses the frequency comparison. This elementary numerical step leaves room for the first child endpoint within the stationary time interval.
TorusEuler.inductionHalfLength_zero_le_q.summary: The first endpoint fits inside the stationary slab

TorusEuler.inductionPressure_endpointHes.text: The pressure budget and residual-gradient estimate imply that the effective endpoint Hessian is bounded above by the identity. Frequencies start at least at four and double at each step; this bounds the sum of their reciprocals by one half. The residual gradient contributes at most the other half. The theorem uses the actual residual identity along a parent trajectory, so it supplies the quantitative hypothesis needed by the next mean inverse.
TorusEuler.inductionPressure_endpointHes.summary: Pressure and residual budgets preserve the next coercivity bound

TorusEuler.inductionPressure_eulerianCoe.text: Assumes a base frequency at least four, at least doubling frequency growth, the accumulated one-sided pressure-Hessian bound, and residual-gradient norm at most one half. It proves the quadratic-form upper bound for pressure Hessian minus residual gradient by the identity matrix. The pressure budget and residual budget each contribute at most one half.
TorusEuler.inductionPressure_eulerianCoe.summary: The pressure and residual budgets give endpoint coercivity

TorusEuler.inductionPressure_sum_le.text: The sum of reciprocal frequencies through any finite stage is at most $2/\lambda_0$. The assumptions `h0 : 0 < freq 0` and `hgrow : ∀ n, 2 * freq n ≤ freq (n + 1)` are sufficient. The proof compares reciprocal frequencies with a geometric progression; no information about the actual pressure is used in this scalar estimate.
TorusEuler.inductionPressure_sum_le.summary: The total pressure budget is bounded by two over N

TorusEuler.induction_approximate_child_c.text: Suppose the approximate velocity splits into parent, primary wave, oscillatory remainder, and mean. Differentiability hypotheses and the exact primary gradient identify the remaining central error as the sum of the last two derivatives. The bound `hBound`, with `Cstep ≤ freq^(1/32)`, makes that error at most `freq^(-1/3)`.
TorusEuler.induction_approximate_child_c.summary: Separate the leading rank-one gradient from corrections

TorusEuler.induction_child_center_error_.text: The sum $\lambda^{-1/3}+\lambda_{\rm next}^{-5}$ is at most $\lambda^{-1/4}$ when `hfreq : 2^12 ≤ freq` and `hnext : freq ≤ next`. This is a scalar inequality for the two error estimates. It explains why adding the gradient of the Fourier tail does not exhaust the allowed central error at the next stage.
TorusEuler.induction_child_center_error_.summary: The central truncation error fits the induction

TorusEuler.induction_child_center_split.text: At a time in the given interval, suppose `child = V + tail`, both summands are differentiable at the origin, and the approximate field has the supplied rank-one splitting. Combining an error of size `freq^(-1/3)` with a cutoff gradient bounded by `next^(-5)` gives central error at most `freq^(-1/4)` under the stated frequency bounds.
TorusEuler.induction_child_center_split.summary: Add the cutoff gradient to the central error

TorusEuler.induction_child_cutoffTail_bu.text: A full-depth tail estimate with cutoff `freq^5`, together with the smallness budget `hEpsilon`, implies `tail ≤ freq^(5*m) * next^(-5)`. The theorem uses integer powers for the potentially negative order difference and nonnegative size parameters. It works at orders zero and one as well as higher orders.
TorusEuler.induction_child_cutoffTail_bu.summary: Reduce the full-depth cutoff estimate to low orders

TorusEuler.induction_child_flow_tail_bud.text: If `1 ≤ freq ≤ next`, then the fifth inverse power of the next frequency is bounded by the child frequency to power $-5/2$. Monotonicity in the positive base and the negative exponent gives the estimate. It is the scalar comparison used to supply the cutoff perturbation’s smallness.
TorusEuler.induction_child_flow_tail_bud.summary: The next cutoff tail fits the flow estimate

TorusEuler.induction_child_increment_bud.text: For `freq ≥ 4` and `next ≥ freq`, the sum $\mathrm{freq}^{-3/2}+\mathrm{next}^{-4}$ is at most `freq⁻¹`. The proof bounds both terms by half of the target through the square-root lower bound. This combines the two nonoscillatory contributions to the tower increment.
TorusEuler.induction_child_increment_bud.summary: The mean and cutoff tail fit one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_a.text: If `freq ≥ 1` and `Cstep ≤ freq^(1/32)`, the oscillatory bound becomes at most `freq⁻¹`, while the deformation bound becomes at most `freq`. The statement is an inequality for real powers. It does not construct either an oscillation or a flow; later lemmas insert those quantities.
TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_a.summary: Absorb the step constant into the child frequency

TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_l.text: For an odd periodic parent flow with deformation bound `D`, assume `μ ≥ 2`, `μ ≤ D`, and `ell ≤ D⁻³`. A localized transported profile nonzero at `x` must lie within `μ⁻¹` of some lattice vector. The label-support hypothesis is explicit, and the flow assumptions establish that the center remains fixed.
TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_l.summary: The transported support lies near a lattice origin

TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_z.text: If the switching rate is nonnegative and the higher profile `C` vanishes at every time up to `t₀`, then the localized transported sum of the primary wave and `C` is zero there. The result includes the activation time itself. It uses the cutoff’s zero branch and periodization of the zero function.
TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_z.summary: The transported oscillation vanishes through activation

TorusEuler.induction_child_velocity_boun.text: The child velocity is bounded by its frequency if the parent is bounded by `μ`, the oscillation by $\lambda^{-1}$, and the remaining increment by the same amount in $C^{0,1/2}$. Lean assumes `hμ : 2 ≤ μ` and `hfreq : 2 * μ ≤ freq`. The pointwise triangle inequality then absorbs both small increments into the new frequency.
TorusEuler.induction_child_velocity_boun.summary: The new velocity stays below its frequency

TorusEuler.induction_comparison_error_bu.text: The physical error bound reduces to the three decay powers used in the induction. Hypotheses `hB`, `hBt`, and `hE` give the older-gradient and correction bounds, while `hr` gives the lower growth rate. With $\nu\ge1$ and positive gain `L`, the conclusion uses the explicit constant $A(5+c^{-1})$. The displayed $L^2$ is $\varepsilon^{-1}$.
TorusEuler.induction_comparison_error_bu.summary: The comparison error has three decaying terms

TorusEuler.induction_normalized_comparis.text: Upper and lower bounds on the physical scaling rate `r` yield corresponding bounds on the normalized window $2r\mu^{-1/8}L_{next}^3$. Positive frequency cancels the reciprocal powers. The upper estimate uses $L\le L_{next}$ and nonnegative `LNext`; the lower coefficient `c` is not assumed positive in this algebraic lemma.
TorusEuler.induction_normalized_comparis.summary: The normalized window lies between cubic and quartic gain bounds

TorusEuler.induction_older_gradient_scal.text: If the older scale is at least one and $\mu=\text{old}^{K(q)}$, then older bounds $B\le\text{old}^9$ and $B_t\le\text{old}^{18}$ become $B\le\mu^{1/32}$ and $B_t\le\mu^{1/16}$. The binder `hb : 1 ≤ b` ensures the exponent $K(q)=320b(q+1)$ is large enough. The statement concerns scalar bounds, with the actual gradients supplied by its application.
TorusEuler.induction_older_gradient_scal.summary: Older gradient bounds become small powers of the parent scale

TorusEuler.inductiveEuler_terminal_trace.text: Starting with the specified uniform limit `u` on a positive common closed slab, proves continuity and periodicity of its terminal slice, global uniform velocity convergence, and convergence of every spatial derivative on compact sets away from the lattice. It uses summable correction derivatives and shrinking oscillation supports. Uniqueness of uniform limits identifies this chosen `u` with the abstractly constructed limit.
TorusEuler.inductiveEuler_terminal_trace.summary: The chosen limit has a smooth terminal trace away

TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu.text: Oscillations supported in shrinking neighborhoods of the integer lattice eventually vanish on an open neighborhood of any fixed compact set away from that lattice. The assumptions `hK` and `hKo` locate the compact set; `hradius` sends the support radii to zero, and `hsupport` gives their geometric containment. The conclusion is uniform over the closed time interval, which is needed to pass spatial derivatives to the terminal trace.
TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu.summary: Late oscillations vanish near every punctured compact set

TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu.text: On every fixed interval $[0,S]$ with $S<T$, all sufficiently late oscillations vanish. The assumptions are convergence of the activation times in `hactivation`, the strict inequality `hST`, and vanishing up to activation in `hO`. The conclusion uses `O (n + 1)` because the finite construction indexes the increment after stage $n$. It supplies the point where only the small correction remains in a preterminal increment.
TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu.summary: Late oscillations vanish before the terminal time

TorusEuler.initialLocalizedCompletedWave.text: For positive $r$ with $2r<1/2$, width $0<h\le1$, nonzero wave vector `hk`, and transverse amplitude `hb`, the periodized localized potential has a smooth periodic divergence-free curl. On the inner ball it equals the plane wave exactly. At the origin its derivative is the rank-one map $v\mapsto(k\cdot v)b$.
TorusEuler.initialLocalizedCompletedWave.summary: The initial curl completion preserves the central plane wave gradient

TorusEuler.inner_cross3_left.text: The cross product $k\times a$ has zero inner product with $k$ for arbitrary vectors in three-dimensional Euclidean space. No nonzero or transverse assumption is needed. This algebraic orthogonality supports both the moving frame and the terminal projection that removes the newest wave from the vorticity.
TorusEuler.inner_cross3_left.summary: A curl is perpendicular to its wave vector

TorusEuler.inner_endpointL2Operator_self.text: For a path v whose time integral vanishes, pairing $Bv$ with v equals endpointL2Energy. The hypothesis hv removes the boundary term in the adjoint identity for the time primitive. No positivity of the energy is proved here. The result identifies the operator's quadratic form so the separate coercivity theorem can be applied.

TorusEuler.inner_firstWaveTransportedCov.text: The pairing of the explicit first-wave covector with `v` is $\lambda v_1-\lambda z v_2$. Only the first two components contribute. This exact formula is used to verify perpendicularity of the smooth seed and to simplify the numerator of the affine pressure and amplitude coefficients.
TorusEuler.inner_firstWaveTransportedCov.summary: Pairing the transported covector with a vector

TorusEuler.inner_firstWaveTransportedCov.text: The explicit first-wave seed is perpendicular to its transported covector at every time and label. Substituting their first two components makes the pairing cancel exactly. The identity also holds for zero frequency or zero scale, although separate nonvanishing hypotheses are required when the pair is used to form a frame.
TorusEuler.inner_firstWaveTransportedCov.summary: The explicit seed stays perpendicular to the covector

TorusEuler.inner_fixedTransverse_lift_eq.text: The identities $RJ=I$ and $JR=P_k$ force every lifted coordinate vector `J z` to equal its transverse projection. For a nonzero covector `k`, its inner product with `J z` therefore vanishes. This proves that the solution constructed in a fixed coordinate space represents a physical seed in the moving transverse plane.
TorusEuler.inner_fixedTransverse_lift_eq.summary: Lifted coordinates lie in the transverse plane

TorusEuler.inner_frozenSymbol_eq.text: For a symmetric projection `hr`, the quadratic form of the frozen operator equals $\langle B(rv),rv\rangle+\|v-rv\|^2$. The formula separates the coefficient acting on the range from the identity acting on the orthogonal complement. It does not require `B` to be symmetric or positive.

TorusEuler.inner_kineticForm_self.text: For any bounded operator `F`, pairing $F^*Fv$ with $v$ gives $\|Fv\|^2$. No invertibility assumption is needed for this identity. With `F` the deformation of the parent flow, it identifies the kinetic coefficient with a nonnegative form; a positive lower bound requires the additional inverse-deformation estimate.
TorusEuler.inner_kineticForm_self.summary: The kinetic quadratic form is a squared deformation norm

TorusEuler.inner_lerayModeProjection_lef.text: The inner product of the projected first coefficient with a second coefficient equals the inner product with projection applied to the second. This self-adjointness holds at every frequency. It permits projection to be moved onto a transverse test field in the coercivity calculation.

TorusEuler.inner_normalize_cross3_ge_of_.text: Converts a lower bound for the scaled new wave vector along `frameAxis`, and an upper bound for its scaled norm, into a signed projection bound for the preceding curl. It needs `hk'`, positive `carrier`, nonnegative `strength` and `component`, and the exact frame identity `hframe`. Positivity of the denominator follows from the nonzero scaled wave vector and its length bound.
TorusEuler.inner_normalize_cross3_ge_of_.summary: The preceding curl has a positive projected component

TorusEuler.inner_normalize_cross3_left.text: The vector $k\times a$ has zero inner product with the normalized vector $k$. The theorem has no nonzero assumption on `k`; Lean defines the normalization of zero as zero, so the identity still holds. Applied to the newest wave, this removes its leading curl from the projection used to retain the preceding wave. It is an algebraic cancellation, independent of the activation coefficient.
TorusEuler.inner_normalize_cross3_left.summary: The newest curl has zero longitudinal component

TorusEuler.inner_normalize_twoLayerCurl.text: Expands the projection of a background curl plus two wave curls along the normalized newest wave vector. The newest term vanishes for every real `cutoff`, so the identity is independent of its activation level. This remains an algebraic identity when the newest wave vector is zero; positivity and unit length are needed only in later norm bounds.
TorusEuler.inner_normalize_twoLayerCurl.summary: The newest wave drops out of the projection

TorusEuler.inner_oscillatoryTransversePr.text: For κ ≠ 0, the transverse projection of any forcing vector has zero inner product with κ. The nonvanishing hypothesis is essential to the usual projection interpretation.
TorusEuler.inner_oscillatoryTransversePr.summary: The projected forcing is perpendicular to the covector

TorusEuler.inner_periodicComplexLeray_le.text: The complex spatial $L^2$ pairing is unchanged when the Leray projection is moved from its first argument to its second. This self-adjointness is inherited from orthogonal projection. It is the all-field version of the finite-frequency identity used when testing a projected equation against a solenoidal solution.
TorusEuler.inner_periodicComplexLeray_le.summary: The full Leray projection is self adjoint

TorusEuler.inner_projectedHilbertOperato.text: For test and trial vectors in `H`, pairing the compressed operator with the test vector equals pairing the ambient operator value with that same vector. Orthogonal projection changes only a component orthogonal to `H`. This identity converts coercivity and weak equations in the ambient Hilbert space into statements about the compressed operator.
TorusEuler.inner_projectedHilbertOperato.summary: Testing inside the subspace removes the projection

TorusEuler.instAddCommGroupHierarchyTwis.text: The twisted profile submodule inherits an additive commutative group from its periodic and smooth ambient spaces. Addition and subtraction are pointwise on representatives and preserve the stored periodicity constraints. The instance supplies algebraic operations for the finite hierarchy; it introduces no new functions or analytic hypotheses.
TorusEuler.instAddCommGroupHierarchyTwis.summary: Add and subtract profiles with the same twist

TorusEuler.instModuleHierarchyTwistedPro.text: The twisted submodule is a real vector space, with scalar multiplication inherited from periodic profiles. Multiplying a representative by a real scalar preserves both the unit phase period and its carrier-dependent lattice translation law. This instance enables linear and bilinear hierarchy operators on the same profile space.
TorusEuler.instModuleHierarchyTwistedPro.summary: Scale profiles without changing their carrier twist

TorusEuler.integrable_liftConvolution.text: An integrable scalar kernel times a translated continuous field with a uniform norm bound is integrable at every output point. The assumptions `hK`, `hf`, and `hM` provide the kernel integrability, measurability through continuity, and dominating bound. This makes the defined convolution an ordinary Bochner integral.
TorusEuler.integrable_liftConvolution.summary: An integrable kernel acts on bounded continuous fields

TorusEuler.integrable_operatorLiftConvol.text: An integrable operator-valued kernel applied to translates of a continuous uniformly bounded field gives an integrable function of the integration variable. The operator norm times the input bound supplies domination. This theorem establishes that the defined operator convolution is a genuine Bochner integral at every output point.
TorusEuler.integrable_operatorLiftConvol.summary: Integrable operator kernels act on bounded continuous fields

TorusEuler.integrable_scaledLiftKernel.text: If a kernel is integrable and the dilation parameter `Λ` is positive, its dimensionally normalized dilation remains integrable. The factor $\Lambda^3$ compensates for three-dimensional volume scaling. Strict positivity excludes the collapsed zero-scale map and fixes the sign used in the change-of-variables formula.

TorusEuler.integrable_scaledMultiplierKe.text: For a positive scaling parameter, the normalized dilation of an integrable Banach-valued kernel is integrable. The theorem explicitly assumes `hK`, so it supplies the convergence guard for later convolution identities. The zero-scale case is excluded even though the defining kernel expression remains total there.
TorusEuler.integrable_scaledMultiplierKe.summary: Integrable multiplier kernels remain integrable after dilation

TorusEuler.integrable_sqrtNorm_mul_norm_.text: Every positive dilation of a Schwartz kernel has integrable norm times the square root of distance. The theorem combines the original kernel's weighted integrability with the scale change. It validates the moment appearing in the quantitative half-Hölder convolution bound for each frequency-localized kernel.
TorusEuler.integrable_sqrtNorm_mul_norm_.summary: The dilated Schwartz kernel retains a finite half-order moment

TorusEuler.integral_divergence_centeredC.text: A continuously differentiable, spatially periodic vector field has zero divergence integral over the centered fundamental cell. After transferring to coordinate functions, the divergence theorem gives opposite-face terms that cancel by periodicity. This is a classical statement on the Euclidean lift, without requiring the field itself to have zero divergence.
TorusEuler.integral_divergence_centeredC.summary: Periodic divergence integrates to zero over one cell

TorusEuler.integral_endpointEvenPart_cen.text: For a continuous scalar field, proves that its even part has the same integral over the centered torus cell. Continuity yields integrability on the compact cell, permitting linearity of the integral. Consequently an already normalized zero-mean pressure remains normalized after the symmetry selection.
TorusEuler.integral_endpointEvenPart_cen.summary: The even pressure retains its spatial mean

TorusEuler.integral_endpointFiniteFourie.text: Every finite pressure constructed from the pressure-correction modes has integral zero over the centered cell. The nonzero characters have zero average, and the pressure correction assigns zero to the constant mode. This fixes the additive constant without requiring any gradient compatibility for the supplied vector coefficients.

TorusEuler.integral_endpointLabelEnergy_.text: The label energy integral equals $\int_0^T(|\xi_t|^2-\langle H^\#\xi,\xi\rangle)$. The binders `hF`, `hM` and `hz` impose the three time derivative equations, and `hz0`, `hzT` impose the two zero traces. This named identity additionally requires continuous `Mt` and `v` through `hMt` and `hv`. Its proof integrates the derivative of $\langle\xi,M\xi\rangle$. The full Sobolev Hardy inequalities are stated separately after a density argument.

TorusEuler.integral_endpointLabelVelocit.text: The squared label-velocity norm is bounded by $D^2(1+L)^2$ times the squared physical-displacement derivative norm. The binders `hGF`, `hG` and `hM` give the inverse deformation and the two operator bounds, and `hzT` gives the terminal zero trace. This declaration also requires `hv : ContinuousOn v (Icc 0 T)` and a pointwise derivative relation `hz`. It therefore states the continuously differentiable case of the paper’s Sobolev estimate.
TorusEuler.integral_endpointLabelVelocit.summary: Comparing label and physical displacement derivatives

TorusEuler.integral_endpointVelocity_nor.text: Assume $0\le T\le1$, terminal vanishing of `ξ`, continuous derivative and velocity, and `hvelocity : v = G(dξ − Mξ)` on the slab. Bounds `hG` and `hM` give $\int\|v\|^2\le D^2(1+L)^2\int\|dξ\|^2$. The theorem needs no assertion that `G` is an inverse; the displayed velocity relation carries the required algebra.
TorusEuler.integral_endpointVelocity_nor.summary: Displacement energy controls the label velocity

TorusEuler.integral_fourier_pair.text: The integral of the mode at $-k$ times the mode at $j$ is one when $k=j$ and zero otherwise. The product Haar measure has total mass one. This orthogonality fixes the normalization used to recover coefficients exactly from a finite Fourier synthesis.

TorusEuler.integral_gradient_pair_center.text: For continuously differentiable periodic `p` and `v`, the cell integral of $\langle\nabla p,v\rangle$ equals minus the integral of $p\,\mathrm{div}\,v$. The proof applies zero integral of divergence to the product field. Both periodicity assumptions matter because they make opposite boundary faces cancel.
TorusEuler.integral_gradient_pair_center.summary: Periodic integration by parts removes the boundary

TorusEuler.integral_innerProduct_moment_.text: If the Fourier transform of a Schwartz kernel is constant in a neighborhood of zero, every directional signed moment of positive degree vanishes. The hypothesis `hj : 0 < j` excludes the mass term. The proof differentiates the locally constant transform and cancels the explicitly nonzero factor $(-2\pi i)^j$.
TorusEuler.integral_innerProduct_moment_.summary: A flat Fourier symbol forces every positive moment to vanish

TorusEuler.integral_inner_advection_cent.text: For periodic $C^1$ fields `w` and `v`, assume only the advecting field `v` is divergence free. Then the cell integral of $\langle w,Dw\,v\rangle$ vanishes. The proof differentiates $|w|^2$ and uses periodic integration by parts, providing the advection cancellation in the classical uniqueness argument for Proposition 8.1.

TorusEuler.integral_inner_endpointSpatia.text: For nonnegative duration, integrating the inner product of a joint field's spatial slice with a fixed spatial L2 field equals pairing that field with the joint time integral. The identity is independent of pointwise slice conventions on exceptional times.
TorusEuler.integral_inner_endpointSpatia.summary: Pairing commutes with time integration of spatial slices

TorusEuler.integral_inner_finiteFourierS.text: The spatial integral pairing of two Fourier polynomials over the same finite frequency set equals the sum of their coefficient inner products. The coefficients may lie in any complex Hilbert space. Finiteness justifies distributing both sums through the integral, and distinct frequencies contribute zero.
TorusEuler.integral_inner_finiteFourierS.summary: Finite Parseval preserves coefficient inner products

TorusEuler.integral_inner_gradient_cente.text: A periodic gradient has zero integral pairing with a periodic divergence-free vector field over the centered fundamental cell. Both fields are $C^1$. Applying this identity to the Eulerian displacement and pressure variation removes the pressure term after the volume-preserving change of variables. The theorem supplies that cancellation, not the complete forced Jacobi energy identity. Periodicity accounts for the disappearance of boundary terms on opposite faces.
TorusEuler.integral_inner_gradient_cente.summary: Pressure gradients pair to zero with solenoidal fields

TorusEuler.integral_inner_leray_finiteFo.text: If `hb` places every test coefficient in the transverse mode space, projecting the first Fourier polynomial leaves its integral inner product with the test polynomial unchanged. The proof moves projection across the coefficient inner product and fixes the transverse test coefficient. This is the finite version of the projected coercivity pairing.
TorusEuler.integral_inner_leray_finiteFo.summary: Transverse test fields do not see the Leray projection

TorusEuler.integral_lift_finiteFourierSu.text: The centered-cell integral of a finite Fourier synthesis is its zero-frequency coefficient when that frequency is present, and zero otherwise. The target complex normed space is complete. This is coefficient recovery at frequency zero, with the cell volume normalized to one.
TorusEuler.integral_lift_finiteFourierSu.summary: The spatial mean is the zero Fourier coefficient

TorusEuler.integral_lift_inverseLaplacia.text: The centered-cell integral of any finite synthesis weighted by the inverse Laplacian symbol is zero. This follows because its zero-frequency coefficient vanishes by definition. The theorem fixes the additive pressure constant and does not require the original source itself to have zero spatial mean.
TorusEuler.integral_lift_inverseLaplacia.summary: The finite Poisson solution has zero mean

TorusEuler.integral_lift_lerayMode.text: The centered-cell integral of the finite projected field equals that of the original Fourier polynomial. The proof reduces both integrals to their zero coefficients and uses the identity action of the zero-frequency Leray symbol. This preservation matters for the time-independent solenoidal field in the endpoint problem.
TorusEuler.integral_lift_lerayMode.summary: The Leray projection preserves the spatial mean

TorusEuler.integral_lift_pressureCorrect.text: The finite pressure correction synthesized from arbitrary vector coefficients has zero centered-cell integral. Its coefficients use the zero-mode-free inverse Laplacian, so the pressure constant is fixed. This normalization is compatible with subtracting its gradient in the finite Leray decomposition.
TorusEuler.integral_lift_pressureCorrect.summary: The Leray pressure correction has zero spatial mean

TorusEuler.integral_norm_iteratedFDeriv_.text: The integral of the absolute $j$th derivative of the dilated kernel is $\Lambda^j$ times the corresponding undilated integral. The input `K` is a Schwartz function, the scale satisfies `hΛ : 0 < Λ`, and `v` is an arbitrary list of derivative directions. The factor $\Lambda^3$ in the kernel definition cancels the volume change. Coordinate direction lists give the multi-index identity used in Bernstein’s estimate.
TorusEuler.integral_norm_iteratedFDeriv_.summary: Kernel derivative integrals scale by the derivative order

TorusEuler.integral_norm_pow_iteratedFDe.text: For positive `Λ`, the `N`th weighted absolute moment of an `m`th directional derivative of the scaled kernel equals $\Lambda^m\Lambda^{-N}$ times the original moment. The derivative directions remain fixed on both sides. This records precisely how derivative loss and positive distance from support trade against the cutoff scale.
TorusEuler.integral_norm_pow_iteratedFDe.summary: Weighted kernel derivatives have the expected scaling

TorusEuler.integral_norm_pow_scaledLiftK.text: The absolute moment of degree $j$ of the dilated kernel is $\Lambda^{-j}$ times its original absolute moment. The only scale assumption is `hΛ : 0 < Λ`, and `j` is a natural number. The theorem is a change-of-variables identity for the total integral; in Appendix B the Schwartz property ensures these absolute moments are finite. It supplies the power $\Lambda^{s-M}$ after setting $j=M-s$.
TorusEuler.integral_norm_pow_scaledLiftK.summary: Absolute kernel moments scale by inverse powers

TorusEuler.integral_norm_scaledLiftKerne.text: For positive frequency scale, the normalized dilation of a complex kernel has the same integral of its norm as the original kernel. The equality gives scale-independent convolution bounds once the kernel is integrable. The theorem states equality of the integral expressions without asserting their integrability separately.
TorusEuler.integral_norm_scaledLiftKerne.summary: Kernel dilation preserves its integral norm

TorusEuler.integral_norm_scaledMultiplie.text: At every positive scale, the integral of the norm of the normalized multiplier kernel equals that of the original kernel. This makes the basic convolution bound independent of the chosen dyadic frequency. Integrability is a separate property, supplied by the adjacent theorem when a classical kernel estimate is needed.
TorusEuler.integral_norm_scaledMultiplie.summary: Multiplier dilation leaves the integral norm unchanged

TorusEuler.integral_norm_sq_finiteFourie.text: The integral of the squared norm of a finite Fourier polynomial equals the sum of the squared coefficient norms. The measure is normalized product Haar measure on the torus. The result is derived from the inner-product Parseval identity and applies to arbitrary complex Hilbert-space coefficients.
TorusEuler.integral_norm_sq_finiteFourie.summary: Finite Parseval identifies spatial energy with coefficient energy

TorusEuler.integral_norm_sq_leray_finite.text: Projecting every coefficient of a finite vector Fourier polynomial by the Leray symbol cannot increase its spatial squared $L^2$ norm. Parseval reduces the claim to the contraction of each Euclidean coefficient projection. This is the finite-polynomial precursor of boundedness on the completed $L^2$ space.
TorusEuler.integral_norm_sq_leray_finite.summary: Finite Leray projection decreases spatial energy

TorusEuler.integral_scaledCompactMultipl.text: For a smooth compactly supported symbol and positive dilation, the integral of the dilated kernel is exactly `symbol 0`. Thus it is zero when the symbol vanishes at the origin. The docstring highlights that application, but the declaration itself proves the more general identity and does not assume zero mean.
TorusEuler.integral_scaledCompactMultipl.summary: The kernel integral equals the symbol at zero

TorusEuler.integral_scaledCutoffSchwartz.text: The integral of the scaled inverse Fourier kernel equals $\psi(0)$ for a smooth symbol supported in the ball of radius two and a positive scale. The theorem itself does not assume that the symbol equals one near zero. In Appendix B that separate symbol condition gives $\psi(0)=1$. The identity follows by evaluating the Fourier transform at zero and applying the scaling change of variables.

Every positive-degree coordinate monomial has zero signed integral against the dilated cutoff kernel. The symbol is smooth, supported, and equal to one on the unit ball by `hψ`, `hs`, and `hunit`. The scale is positive and `hj : 0 < j` excludes the zeroth moment. The coordinate list `ι` permits repetitions, so the statement covers all multi-indices needed to cancel the Taylor polynomial.
TorusEuler.integral_scaledCutoffSchwartz.summary: Every positive coordinate moment of the cutoff kernel vanishes

TorusEuler.integral_scaledCutoffSchwartz.text: For a smooth cutoff equal to one on the unit ball and zero outside radius two, every positive directional moment of its dilated inverse-Fourier kernel vanishes. `hΛ : 0 < Λ` ensures the scaled symbol is one near zero. This applies the general moment theorem to the actual kernel used in the cutoff.
TorusEuler.integral_scaledCutoffSchwartz.summary: The actual dilated cutoff kernel has vanishing positive moments

TorusEuler.integral_scaledCutoffSchwartz.text: For positive degree `j`, the dilated cutoff kernel integrates to zero against any continuous real multilinear diagonal term valued in a complete complex normed space. Coordinate expansion reduces the assertion to vanishing coordinate moments. Smoothness and unit-neighborhood assumptions belong to the cutoff; the multilinear map itself is arbitrary.
TorusEuler.integral_scaledCutoffSchwartz.summary: The cutoff kernel cancels positive homogeneous Taylor terms

TorusEuler.integral_sqrtNorm_scaledMulti.text: Positive dilation multiplies the integral of kernel norm times $\sqrt{\|y\|}$ by $\sqrt{\Lambda^{-1}}$. This scaling is responsible for the half-order gain in each dyadic block. The theorem is an equality of total integrals; the subsequent Schwartz lemmas supply finiteness of the weighted moment.
TorusEuler.integral_sqrtNorm_scaledMulti.summary: The half-order kernel moment gains an inverse square root

TorusEuler.integral_truncatedParentSlice.text: Proves that the integral of the slice pressure over the centered fundamental cell is zero. This fixes the additive constant in the pressure without imposing any condition on the average of the input vector field. The finite smooth potential is integrable on that bounded cell; the equality is not a fallback for a nonintegrable function.

TorusEuler.integratedLimit_of_uniformCon.text: Assume uniform convergence of approximate states and drift terms, uniform decay of residuals, continuous drift and residual curves, and their exact integrated relation. The limit satisfies $u(t)=u(0)-\int_0^t d(s)\,ds$ and has within-interval derivative $-d(t)$. The result works for $T\ge0$ in a Banach space; it does not establish smoothness or Euler structure by itself.
TorusEuler.integratedLimit_of_uniformCon.summary: A vanishing residual leaves the limiting evolution equation

TorusEuler.integrated_spatialJets_of_zer.text: Assume two compatible spatial jet towers `J` and `U`, with `U` continuous in time. An integrated identity for their zeroth entries then differentiates to the same identity at every finite order. The proof uses uniqueness of spatial derivatives at each induction step. The interval may have length zero; no evolution is inferred beyond the given identity.
TorusEuler.integrated_spatialJets_of_zer.summary: One integrated identity determines every spatial jet identity

TorusEuler.intervalIntegrable_sq_velocit.text: If a velocity is in $L^2$ for the restricted measure on an ordered interval, its squared norm is interval-integrable there. This is the integrability condition needed for Cauchy–Schwarz and energy bounds. The theorem concerns a representative together with `hv`, not an arbitrary function with a formal squared-integral expression.
TorusEuler.intervalIntegrable_sq_velocit.summary: The squared velocity norm is time-integrable

TorusEuler.intervalIntegrable_velocity_o.text: On an ordered finite interval, an $L^2$ representative is interval-integrable. The proof uses the finiteness of the restricted time measure to pass from exponent two to exponent one. The order hypothesis `hab` identifies the oriented interval integral with the intended restriction to $(a,b]$.

TorusEuler.intervalIntegral_endpointSpat.text: A spatial $L^2$-valued path continuous on $[0,T]$ and equal almost everywhere to the spatial slices of a joint field has the same total time integral as that field. Nonnegative duration aligns the interval and restricted-measure integrals. Testing against arbitrary spatial $L^2$ vectors reduces the identity to scalar Fubini compatibility.
TorusEuler.intervalIntegral_endpointSpat.summary: The recovered spatial path has the original time integral

TorusEuler.inv_sq_norm_inv_smul.text: The reciprocal squared norm of the normalized vector is the coefficient of Proposition 5.1.
TorusEuler.inv_sq_norm_inv_smul.summary: The reciprocal covector norm after frequency normalization

TorusEuler.inverseAdjoint_activationWave.text: The vector $k_*=\lambda F^{\mathsf T}E_3$ becomes $\lambda E_3$ after applying $F^{-\mathsf T}$. The binder `F : Vec3 ≃L[ℝ] Vec3` is a continuous linear equivalence and `carrier` is any real scalar. The statement is an exact operator identity, supplying the algebra needed to prescribe the Eulerian wave vector at activation.
TorusEuler.inverseAdjoint_activationWave.summary: Pulling back the prescribed activation covector

TorusEuler.inverseLabel_materialDerivati.text: Assume `hInv` identifies the composed inverse label along a trajectory locally within the time interval. Together with the derivatives `hA`, `hX`, membership `ht`, and unique differentiation `hI`, it implies $A_t+A_xu=0$. The local identity is enough; a globally specified inverse flow is unnecessary.
TorusEuler.inverseLabel_materialDerivati.summary: Differentiating the inverse label identity gives transport

TorusEuler.inverseLabel_spatialDerivativ.text: At corresponding label and spatial points, assume derivatives `hA` and `hX` and a local inverse identity `hInv`. The flow derivative is already a continuous linear equivalence `F`, so the inverse label derivative equals `F.symm`. This uses genuine invertibility data, avoiding a totalized inverse of a possibly singular matrix.
TorusEuler.inverseLabel_spatialDerivativ.summary: The inverse label derivative is the inverse deformation

TorusEuler.inverseLaplacianMode.text: This scalar is the reciprocal of the Laplacian symbol. At nonzero frequency it inverts $-(2\pi)^2|k|^2$; at zero frequency Lean assigns zero to the reciprocal of zero. Thus the definition selects a zero-mean pressure rather than attempting to solve for an arbitrary constant source.
TorusEuler.inverseLaplacianMode.summary: The pressure inverse sets the constant mode to zero

TorusEuler.inverseLaplacianMode_zero.text: The inverse Laplacian symbol at zero frequency is zero. This theorem records the normalization chosen through totalized scalar inversion. It does not state that the Laplacian is invertible on all periodic fields; the constant mode must be removed from the source.
TorusEuler.inverseLaplacianMode_zero.summary: The pressure inverse has zero constant coefficient

TorusEuler.inverseMultiplierKernel_decay.text: A Banach-valued Schwartz symbol has an inverse-transform kernel whose value and first derivative decay with weight $(1+\|y\|)^5$. The quantitative bound is thirty-two times the preceding derivative-mass constant. This supplies sufficient decay in three dimensions for the kernel's integral norm and its half-order moment.
TorusEuler.inverseMultiplierKernel_decay.summary: The kernel and its gradient decay to fifth order

TorusEuler.inverseMultiplierKernel_decay.text: For a Schwartz symbol, $(1+\|y\|)^p$ times the order `d` inverse Fourier kernel derivative norm is bounded by `multiplierJetDecayConstant d p`. The proof treats points inside and outside the unit ball separately, using moment orders zero and `p`. Both the derivative order and decay order are arbitrary naturals.
TorusEuler.inverseMultiplierKernel_decay.summary: Every kernel derivative has arbitrary polynomial decay

TorusEuler.inverse_secondCoupling_le.text: Assuming the first coupling is at least $\pi$, the reciprocal of $\nu\,\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon=1/L^2$ is at most $L^2/\pi$. The theorem permits arbitrary real `L`; at zero gain the totalized inverses make the inequality degenerate to zero. Applications to the induction use a positive prescribed gain.
TorusEuler.inverse_secondCoupling_le.summary: The first coupling bounds the reciprocal second coupling

TorusEuler.isClosed_endpointHalfHolderSo.text: The half-Hölder solenoidal submodule is closed as the inverse image of the closed Hilbert solenoidal subspace under the continuous embedding. This transfers the weak divergence constraint without differentiating Hölder fields. It ensures the fixed-time inverse is formulated on a complete constrained function space.

TorusEuler.isClosed_endpointJointSpatial.text: The weakly solenoidal submodule is closed for every real T. Each defining divergence test is a continuous linear functional, so its kernel is closed, and the intersection over the time tests and scalar potentials remains closed. This supplies the completeness needed to form the spatial orthogonal projection in the joint Hilbert space.

TorusEuler.isClosed_endpointSpatialSolen.text: The spatial weak divergence-free submodule is closed because every testing functional is continuous and has a closed kernel. An arbitrary intersection preserves closedness. This supplies the Hilbert-space foundation needed for orthogonal projection and coercive inverse constructions on the fixed-time solenoidal space.
TorusEuler.isClosed_endpointSpatialSolen.summary: The weak solenoidal Hilbert subspace is closed

TorusEuler.isClosed_endpointTorusSpace.text: The intersection defining the joint endpoint constraint space is closed because every test functional is continuous and has a closed kernel. This permits the orthogonal projection used by the mixed solve.
TorusEuler.isClosed_endpointTorusSpace.summary: The joint endpoint constraint space is closed

TorusEuler.isClosed_freezingFixedSpace.text: For any continuous linear operator `P`, the set of vectors satisfying $Pv=v$ is closed. Idempotence of `P` is unnecessary for this topological fact. In the freezing argument it makes the projected space complete, allowing bounded inverse and continuation results to be applied on that subspace.

TorusEuler.isClosed_range_latticeVector.text: The set of embedded integer lattice vectors is closed in three-dimensional Euclidean space. It is the intersection of the inverse images of the closed integer subset under coordinate evaluation. This supplies the topology of the lifted torus origin, which consists of every lattice translate of zero.
TorusEuler.isClosed_range_latticeVector.summary: The integer lattice is closed in Euclidean labels

TorusEuler.isCompact_centeredCell.text: The centered fundamental cube is compact in three-dimensional Euclidean space. This makes spatial suprema and periodic boundedness arguments available on a fixed compact representative set.

TorusEuler.isCompact_closure_multiplierK.text: The closure of the half open fundamental cell is compact because it is a closed subset of the basis parallelepiped. This allows all differences between a fixed observation region and cell source points to be bounded uniformly. The theorem carefully concerns the closure, not compactness of the half open cell itself.
TorusEuler.isCompact_closure_multiplierK.summary: The periodization cell has compact closure

TorusEuler.isCompact_farPressureSourceSe.text: The far source set is compact because it is a closed support intersected with the compact closure of the kernel fundamental cell. No continuity of the cutoff is required: topological support is closed by definition. This compactness provides finite source measure and allows uniform kernel bounds after separation is proved.
TorusEuler.isCompact_farPressureSourceSe.summary: The support enclosure is compact for any cutoff

TorusEuler.isEulerSolution_of_prefix_lim.text: Joint smoothness of the candidate velocity and normalized periodic pressure is supplied, along with approximation symmetries, zero divergence, uniform velocity and derivative convergence on each prefix, and the limiting dynamics. The theorem then constructs `IsEulerSolution T u p` and oddness of the velocity. It does not independently prove the assumed smoothness or convergence.
TorusEuler.isEulerSolution_of_prefix_lim.summary: Assemble an Euler solution from the prefix limits

TorusEuler.isEulerSolution_stationaryShe.text: The time-independent shear and zero pressure solve the unforced Euler equation on any positive lifespan `hT : 0 < T`.
