The metric comparison doubles the Lipschitz constant and explains the quarter-radius restriction; the assumed dyadic convergence remains part of the hypotheses.
TorusEuler.norm_sub_dyadicLimit_torus_pr.summary: Off-support estimate in the product torus metric

TorusEuler.norm_sub_liftConvolution_scal.text: Applies the positive-order cutoff error estimate to the translated difference $f(\cdot+v)-f$. A bound $D$ on the corresponding highest-derivative increment gives a cutoff-error increment bounded by $\Lambda^{-(n+1)}D$ times the kernel absolute moment. The input is bounded and $C^{n+1}$, with a smooth supported symbol equal to one near zero. Choosing $D$ from a half-Hölder seminorm yields the increment part of the tail estimate.
TorusEuler.norm_sub_liftConvolution_scal.summary: The Taylor estimate also controls spatial increments

TorusEuler.norm_sub_liftConvolution_scal.text: For a bounded $C^{n+1}$ field with its highest derivative bounded by $M$, the cutoff error is bounded by $\Lambda^{-(n+1)}M$ times the kernel absolute moment of order $n+1$. The symbol is smooth, supported and equal to one near zero, and the scale is positive. The proof cancels the Taylor polynomial with the kernel moments. This is a pointwise estimate; the full Hölder norm also needs derivative and increment estimates.
TorusEuler.norm_sub_liftConvolution_scal.summary: The Taylor remainder bounds the cutoff error

TorusEuler.norm_sub_operatorLiftConvolut.text: Under the integrability, differentiability and dyadic derivative bounds on $K_j$, assumes explicitly that the finite convolution sums converge at every point to $u$. The common Lipschitz estimate then passes to $u$ on the concentric half-ball where the source vanishes nearby. The theorem transfers a uniform bound; it does not establish the convergence asserted by `hLimit`.
TorusEuler.norm_sub_operatorLiftConvolut.summary: Pass the off-support bound to a pointwise limit

TorusEuler.norm_sub_operatorLiftConvolut.text: Assume every kernel $K_j$ is integrable and differentiable, with weighted derivative bound $(1+2^j|w|)^5\|DK_j(w)\|\le C2^{4j}$. For a continuous bounded source vanishing on a radius-$r$ ball, all finite convolution sums satisfy the same Lipschitz estimate on its half-ball. The constant is $16\cdot18C$ times the tail mass divided by $r$, independently of the truncation length.
TorusEuler.norm_sub_operatorLiftConvolut.summary: Uniform off-support bound for dyadic partial sums

TorusEuler.norm_sub_operatorLiftConvolut.text: For an integrable differentiable kernel with derivative bounded by $C|w|^{-4}$, a continuous source bounded by $M$ and zero on the radius-$r$ ball produces a convolution difference bounded by $16C\,\mathrm{tail}\,M\|x-y\|/r$ inside the concentric half-ball. The source vanishing removes the singular region, and the scaled tail integral handles the remainder.
TorusEuler.norm_sub_operatorLiftConvolut.summary: Convolution is Lipschitz away from source support

TorusEuler.norm_sub_weightedLabelWord_le.text: For a nonempty derivative word, adjacent Fréchet-jet bounds and $\ell D^p\le1$ give a half-Hölder increment constant $\sqrt{2C_mC_{m+1}}D^{p+q}\sqrt\ell$. Smoothness, $D\ge1$, and nonnegative radius and constants are explicit. The positive order provides a radius factor in the value bound before interpolation with the next derivative.
TorusEuler.norm_sub_weightedLabelWord_le.summary: Positive weighted derivatives gain the square-root radius

TorusEuler.norm_switchedLeadingProfile_d.text: With frequency at least one, positive envelope radius and a switch in $[0,1]$, assume the seed is at most twice its nonzero center value inside the envelope ball. The switched scalar profile times the seed then has norm, divided by $\lambda^{3/4}\|a_0\|$, at most $\lambda^{-5/4}$ at every label and phase. Outside the ball the envelope makes the profile zero.
TorusEuler.norm_switchedLeadingProfile_d.summary: The localized leading profile has the target weighted size

TorusEuler.norm_toUnitTorus_sub_le.text: The norm of the difference of two torus labels obtained from `x` and `y` is at most the Euclidean norm of `x-y`. The proof compares the component circle distances and the vector norm. This bound controls the Hölder increment caused by a small Euclidean translation.
TorusEuler.norm_toUnitTorus_sub_le.summary: The torus quotient cannot increase distance

TorusEuler.norm_torusHalfHolderDerivativ.text: The operator norm of the directionwise extension is at most $\|P\|$. Although the definition reconstructs a derivative from three coordinate evaluations, this estimate introduces no factor of three. The bound is for the bundled half-Hölder norm and needs no derivative-commutation hypothesis; later induction combines it with that separate hypothesis.
TorusEuler.norm_torusHalfHolderDerivativ.summary: Directionwise projection keeps the same norm bound

TorusEuler.norm_torusHalfHolderProjected.text: The bundled half-Hölder norm of the projected operator field is at most $\|P\|\|H\|$. The proof estimates action on arbitrary directions, including both value and increment bounds, rather than summing three separate column norms. This avoids an unnecessary dimension factor in the first-order projection estimate.
TorusEuler.norm_torusHalfHolderProjected.summary: Projecting derivative columns costs only the operator norm

TorusEuler.norm_twoLayerCurl_ge_of_proje.text: From `hb : ‖b‖ ≤ backgroundBound` and a signed lower bound on the preceding wave projection, obtains a lower bound `signedLower - backgroundBound` for the full two-layer curl norm. The newest cutoff remains arbitrary. The nonvanishing hypothesis `hk'` makes its normalized direction a unit vector, so Cauchy–Schwarz controls both the background projection and the full projection.
TorusEuler.norm_twoLayerCurl_ge_of_proje.summary: Projected curl gives a lower bound for its norm

TorusEuler.norm_vorticityForm_le.text: From $\|F\|\le F_0$ and $\|M\|\le M_0$, bounds $\|F^*(M^*-M)F\|$ by $2F_0^2M_0$. The two factors of deformation come from the pullback, while the factor two bounds the skew part. This is a pointwise coefficient estimate, not a bound on the Euler vorticity solution over time.
TorusEuler.norm_vorticityForm_le.summary: The pulled-back vorticity has a cubic bound

TorusEuler.norm_vorticityForm_sub_le.text: With common size bounds for two deformations and two gradient matrices, controls the difference of their pulled-back skew coefficients by $(4F_0F_1M_0+2F_0^2M_1)d$. The hypotheses bound both deformation and gradient differences by their respective constants times `d`. The product expansion separates changes in the two deformation factors from changes in the skew gradient.
TorusEuler.norm_vorticityForm_sub_le.summary: Spatial differences of the pulled-back vorticity

TorusEuler.norm_wavePotentialTimeSource_.text: At a nonzero covector, the explicit time-source integrand is bounded by $(4\|M\|\|v\|+\|f\|)/\|\kappa\|$. No derivative of the strain or forcing appears. The estimate follows from cross-product bounds and operator norms, and it does not assume that the input vectors are transverse.
TorusEuler.norm_wavePotentialTimeSource_.summary: The potential time source retains the inverse-frequency gain

TorusEuler.norm_wavePotential_le.text: The potential satisfies $\|Q[V](s)\|\le2B/\|\kappa\|$ uniformly in phase. The hypothesis `hn` excludes zero covectors, `hc`, `hp`, and `hm` make the input continuous, one-periodic, and mean zero, and `hB` bounds it by $B$ on one period. The estimate does not require transversality. It supplies the inverse-covector factor in the paper; the separate cost of a slow curl comes from differentiating in labels.
TorusEuler.norm_wavePotential_le.summary: Vector potential gains one inverse wave frequency

TorusEuler.norm_wavePrimaryPressure_cent.text: Under the same $C^2$ and zero-central-phase assumptions, the operator norm difference between the primary Hessian and its negative rank-one term is at most $h\|D^2c(0)\|$. The estimate uses the uniform bound on the zero-mean primitive. It does not conclude that the complete central Hessian is nonpositive.
TorusEuler.norm_wavePrimaryPressure_cent.summary: The remaining central term costs the profile width

TorusEuler.norm_wavePrimaryPressure_geom.text: The geometric terms of the leading pressure Hessian cost at most $\lambda^{3/2}$ times the profile budget. The assumptions `hκ` and `hφ` control the transported covector and its derivative, while `hgc`, `hF` and `hP` bound the slow coefficient terms. The conclusion gives the explicit bound $(3D^2+D)N\sqrt N\,B$ with `N` representing frequency. The signed rank-one phase term is excluded from this operator-norm estimate.
TorusEuler.norm_wavePrimaryPressure_geom.summary: The remaining Hessian terms use one fast derivative

TorusEuler.norm_wavePrimaryPressure_geom.text: Substitutes the hierarchy pressure budget $B\le KN^{-9/4}$ into the geometric Hessian estimate. With $N\ge1$ and the stated nonnegative scale bounds, the derivative cost $N\sqrt N$ leaves decay $N^{-3/4}$ and factor $(3D^2+D)K$. This is an operator norm estimate for the remainder, separate from the signed leading tensor.
TorusEuler.norm_wavePrimaryPressure_geom.summary: The geometric remainder decays by three quarters

TorusEuler.norm_waveProfile_le.text: The profile satisfies $|F_h(s)|\le h/2$ for every phase, assuming `hh : 0 < h` and `hle : h ≤ 1`. The proof reduces to a single period and integrates derivative bounds in both directions from the zero endpoint values. This is the amplitude estimate used for the narrow shear profile. The exported theorem states a bound in terms of $h$, not the intermediate bump-mass bound $2c_h$ appearing in the paper's proof.
TorusEuler.norm_waveProfile_le.summary: Profile amplitude is bounded by half its scale

TorusEuler.norm_word_le_hierarchyFiniteW.text: Each actual pointwise mixed jet is controlled by the finite norm.
TorusEuler.norm_word_le_hierarchyFiniteW.summary: The finite norm controls each derivative word

TorusEuler.normalizedPressureAmplitudeCo.text: For positive frequency, applying the normalized scalar pressure row to c·a equals frequency times the negative leading-wave pressure coefficient. This is the normalization and sign conversion used to identify the leading pressure.
TorusEuler.normalizedPressureAmplitudeCo.summary: Leading pressure coefficients agree after frequency normalization

TorusEuler.normalizedWaveNorm_ne_zero_an.text: The lower covector bound implies the reciprocal bound used in Proposition 5.1.
TorusEuler.normalizedWaveNorm_ne_zero_an.summary: A lower covector bound controls inverse squared length

TorusEuler.odd_closedSlab_momentumResidu.text: For a positive slab, assumes a finite-band velocity slice, oddness of the velocity throughout the slab, a half-Hölder representative of its advection, and the actual projected time-derivative identity. The time derivative and projected advection are both odd, hence so is the true momentum residual. No pressure-parity hypothesis is needed in this argument.
TorusEuler.odd_closedSlab_momentumResidu.summary: Projected evolution transfers oddness to the actual residual

TorusEuler.odd_curl_of_even.text: A differentiable even vector potential has an odd curl. Differentiating the reflection identity shows that its spatial derivative changes sign, and the linear curl map preserves that sign change. The differentiability hypothesis is essential to identify the derivative, rather than relying on the default value of `fderiv`.

TorusEuler.odd_endpointParityPart.text: Proves that the reflection average with sign minus one changes sign under spatial inversion. This holds for an arbitrary vector-valued function, with no smoothness or periodicity assumptions. Later results separately show that selecting this odd component preserves the endpoint equation and its quantitative bounds.
TorusEuler.odd_endpointParityPart.summary: The negative-sign average is an odd field

TorusEuler.odd_firstWaveLocalizedVelocit.text: For nonzero frequency and the valid collar and profile parameters, the first-wave velocity is odd in space at each time. The inverse shear is odd, the envelope, seed and covector are even, and the phase primitive is even. Their localized potential is therefore even, and spatial curl makes the velocity odd.

TorusEuler.odd_lift_realVectorFourierCut.text: If the original real torus field has an odd Euclidean lift and the scalar symbol is even, the real cutoff lift is odd too. The theorem permits any real cutoff scale. Its proof descends oddness to torus reflection, applies the parity identity for complex Fourier synthesis, and then takes real parts.
TorusEuler.odd_lift_realVectorFourierCut.summary: An even cutoff preserves odd real velocities

TorusEuler.odd_stationaryShear.text: Negating the spatial point negates the stationary shear velocity. The result follows from oddness of sine, while the fixed shear direction remains unchanged. This holds for every real parameter and supplies the parity condition carried by the parent flow and subsequent wave construction.
TorusEuler.odd_stationaryShear.summary: The stationary shear is odd about the origin

TorusEuler.odd_stationaryShearFlow.text: For every real duration and shear parameter, negating the initial label negates the evolved label. Both the identity part and the stationary velocity increment are odd. This parity property is required when transporting the even envelope and seed to obtain odd localized Euler velocities.
TorusEuler.odd_stationaryShearFlow.summary: The explicit shear flow is odd in its label

TorusEuler.odd_transportedProfile.text: The graph of a jointly odd label-phase profile is an odd spatial field. The named hypothesis `hA` makes the inverse-label map odd, and `hf` states $f(t,-a,-s)=-f(t,a,s)$. The result holds for any real initial wave vector `k` and requires no differentiability. It is the last parity step in passing from the odd completed profile to its Eulerian evaluation; support and periodic extension are addressed separately.
TorusEuler.odd_transportedProfile.summary: Joint profile parity gives Eulerian oddness

TorusEuler.odd_waveProfile.text: The constructed velocity profile is odd at every admissible scale. The hypotheses `hh` and `hle` require $0<h\le1$. The proof rewrites the integral under $s\mapsto-s$, uses evenness of the normalized slope, and reverses the integration limits. This is the parity step in the proof of Lemma 3.1; it does not by itself prove period one or existence of a normalized pressure primitive.
TorusEuler.odd_waveProfile.summary: Integrated even slope gives an odd profile

TorusEuler.ofReal_norm_curl_zero_le_toru.text: For a spatially continuously differentiable vector field, the extended nonnegative norm of its curl at the origin is at most the cellwise essential supremum of the curl. Continuous differentiability provides continuity of the curl, allowing the preceding neighborhood argument. The theorem imposes no periodicity or Euler-equation hypothesis.
TorusEuler.ofReal_norm_curl_zero_le_toru.summary: The central curl is bounded by the torus essential supremum

TorusEuler.ofReal_norm_zero_le_torusLInf.text: For a continuous map from space into any normed additive group, the extended nonnegative norm of its value at the origin is at most its cellwise essential supremum. A strictly larger central value would persist on a positive-volume neighborhood, contradicting that supremum. Spatial periodicity is not a hypothesis of this local argument.
TorusEuler.ofReal_norm_zero_le_torusLInf.summary: Continuity makes the central value visible to the essential supremum

TorusEuler.offOrigin.text:
The complement of the integer lattice in $\mathbb R^3$. Removing every lattice point is the lift of removing the single origin from $\mathbb T^3$, since all integer vectors represent the same torus point. The compact sets in `HasOffOriginLimits` must lie in this open set. Removing only the Euclidean point zero would leave other representatives of the singular torus point in the domain.

Default-value audit (b4): This is a set complement, not an analytic operation. The removed set is every integer lattice vector. A compact set in this complement may be empty, making its own convergence clause trivial; HasOffOriginLimits quantifies over all such compact sets, including nonempty ones.
TorusEuler.offOrigin.summary: The Euclidean lift with lattice points removed

TorusEuler.older_central_gradient_bounds.text: The older gradient and time-gradient bounds become $\mu^{1/32}$ and $\mu^{1/16}$ when the scheduled frequency relation `μ = old ^ frequencyExponent b q` holds with `b ≥ 1` and `old ≥ 1`. The actual derivative is inherited from the original smooth slab. This is an exponent comparison after restriction, not an additional PDE estimate.
TorusEuler.older_central_gradient_bounds.summary: Frequency separation converts older bounds to small powers

TorusEuler.older_central_gradient_raw_bo.text: Given the global closed-slab bounds $\|B\|\le\mathrm{old}^9$ and $\|B_t\|\le\mathrm{old}^{18}$, the actual central gradient and its time derivative satisfy them on any contained later interval. The time derivative is defined on the original slab and then restricted. Joint $C^2$ regularity proves it is a genuine within derivative on the smaller interval.
TorusEuler.older_central_gradient_raw_bo.summary: Older gradient estimates restrict to a later slab

TorusEuler.older_gradient_scale_le_of_fr.text: For nonnegative older frequency, the gap $\mathrm{older}^{288}\le\mu$ implies $\mathrm{older}^9\le\mu^{1/32}$. The proof raises the gap to a nonnegative real power and uses $288/32=9$. This converts the older gradient’s growth scale into a lower power than the main projected curl contribution.
TorusEuler.older_gradient_scale_le_of_fr.summary: A large frequency gap suppresses the older gradient scale

TorusEuler.one_le_freezingLowerOrder.text: The maximum defining the lower-order localization constant always includes $1$, so this lower bound requires no assumptions on `r` or `D`. It is used to choose a legitimate interpolation parameter. This unconditional algebraic bound should not be confused with the analytic estimates that require a positive localization radius.

TorusEuler.one_le_profileFlowJetConstant.text: Nonnegative coefficient costs and a nonnegative level constant imply the common pullback-jet coefficient is at least one, for every depth. The proof separates the nonnegative oscillatory and mean contributions and retains the explicit $1+C(1)$ tail allowance. No lower bound on depth or strict positivity of the level constant is required.
TorusEuler.one_le_profileFlowJetConstant.summary: The common jet coefficient always includes a positive allowance

TorusEuler.operatorLiftConvolution.text: At each output point, integrate the operator-valued kernel applied to the field at the translated point $x-y$. This allows Fourier symbols to act on vectors or whole time paths rather than only by scalar multiplication. The definition has no integrability premise; subsequent lemmas establish convergence for bounded continuous inputs.
TorusEuler.operatorLiftConvolution.summary: Convolving a periodic lift with an operator kernel

TorusEuler.operatorLiftConvolution_compa.text: For a smooth compactly supported operator-valued symbol and positive frequency scale, convolution with its dilated inverse-transform kernel acts on each coefficient of a finite torus Fourier sum by that symbol at the rescaled lattice frequency. The result identifies the exact multiplier on polynomials; norm completion and density are later steps.
TorusEuler.operatorLiftConvolution_compa.summary: A localized operator symbol is realized by convolution

TorusEuler.operatorLiftConvolution_eq_in.text: For an integrable continuous operator kernel and bounded continuous periodic input, a summable bound on lattice translates over the cell gives equality between Euclidean convolution and cell integration against the periodized kernel. The proof decomposes space into lattice cells and justifies exchanging sum and integral by integrability of the norm series.
TorusEuler.operatorLiftConvolution_eq_in.summary: Euclidean convolution equals the periodized cell integral

TorusEuler.operatorLiftConvolution_fouri.text: For an integrable operator kernel, convolving a Fourier mode with coefficient `a` gives the same mode multiplied by the Fourier-transform operator evaluated at the lattice frequency and applied to `a`. Completeness of the target justifies moving fixed linear evaluations through the integral. This identifies the mode action before summing polynomials.
TorusEuler.operatorLiftConvolution_fouri.summary: Operator convolution acts diagonally on each Fourier mode

TorusEuler.operatorTorusConvolution.text: Given an integrable operator-valued kernel, integrate its action on the continuously translated torus input field. The complete target and a dominating function $\|K(y)\|\|f\|_\infty$ yield a continuous output. This definition supports kernels between different complex normed spaces, including operators acting on whole time paths.
TorusEuler.operatorTorusConvolution.summary: Convolve a torus field with an operator valued Euclidean kernel

TorusEuler.operatorTorusConvolution_toUn.text: At the torus image of a Euclidean point, operator-valued torus convolution equals `operatorLiftConvolution` of the periodic lift. Quotient compatibility with subtraction makes the integrands identical. This is the bridge allowing Euclidean kernel bounds to control the continuous torus output.
TorusEuler.operatorTorusConvolution_toUn.summary: Operator convolution agrees with convolution of the lifted field

TorusEuler.orthonormal_movingFrame.text: The wave vector and the transverse amplitude determine the oriented orthonormal frame of the affine-wave comparison.
TorusEuler.orthonormal_movingFrame.summary: A perpendicular wave defines an oriented orthonormal frame

TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure.text:
The phase pressure is the primitive on the unit period normalized to zero mean.

Default-value audit (b5): The phase primitive is defined for arbitrary functions via a totalized integral. Its smooth periodic mean-zero pressure interpretation requires the regularity, periodicity and zero-mean slope established in the solve.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure.summary: The pressure primitive with zero phase mean

TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_freq.text: The mean-zero pressure from the transverse equation has the same inverse-frequency factor.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_freq.summary: Transverse pressure gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_prim.text: The selected mean-zero phase pressure for the leading wave equals $-c_{\mathbf a}P_h$. The theorem allows arbitrary scalar `cutoff`, covector `κ`, amplitude `a` and linear map `M`. The proof writes the pressure slope as a scalar multiple of $F_h$ and uses linearity of the zero-mean phase primitive. Thus the primitive and its normalization are those used by the transverse solve, rather than a separate pressure choice.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_prim.summary: The leading pressure is a normalized phase primitive

TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_spec.text: For continuous periodic zero-mean forcing and velocity profiles, the normalized phase pressure is periodic, has zero mean and differentiates to the algebraic pressure slope. The theorem holds even for a zero wave vector, where the slope degenerates to zero. It does not establish the time momentum equation or the nonvanishing wave vector used in the physical solve.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_spec.summary: The normalized pressure has the required phase derivative

TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_weig.text: The normalized pressure multiplied by the carrier frequency obeys weighted mixed-derivative bounds in terms of the velocity and source. The hypotheses `haN` and `hbN` control the normalized strain and covector coefficients, while `hVN` and `hfN` bound the amplitude-weighted velocity and forcing. Smoothness, phase periodicity, and zero phase means are explicit. The conclusion is a word-derivative bound; summing the admissible words and inserting the parent coefficient bounds yields the seminorm estimate used in the proof.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_weig.summary: Every pressure derivative retains the inverse frequency factor

TorusEuler.oscillatoryPressureSlope.text:
The phase derivative of the oscillatory pressure in (5.16).

Default-value audit (b5): The slope formula contains totalized division by the squared covector norm. Nonzero covectors and the transverse evolution equation are needed before interpreting it as a pressure derivative.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryPressureSlope.summary: The derivative of the oscillatory phase pressure

TorusEuler.oscillatoryPressureSlope_eq_c.text: The oscillatory pressure slope is the sum of the scalar amplitude row and the scalar forcing row. The identity is algebraic; regularity and the mean-zero primitive are handled elsewhere.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryPressureSlope_eq_c.summary: The pressure slope separates amplitude and forcing

TorusEuler.oscillatorySolve_preserves_co.text: Starting with a zero-initial solution and its periodic zero-mean phase pressure, proves preservation of the lattice-phase twist. It additionally gives reflection and inactive-region implications when the corresponding coefficient and forcing hypotheses hold. Velocity equality follows from fixed-label ODE uniqueness; pressure equality uses its derivative and zero mean to remove the additive constant.
TorusEuler.oscillatorySolve_preserves_co.summary: The actual transverse solution preserves twist, parity and inactivity

TorusEuler.oscillatoryTransverseProjecti.text:
The operator $I-\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$, used to project the central activation vector onto the plane perpendicular to the local wave vector. Lean represents the rank-one term by `InnerProductSpace.rankOne`. Orthogonality and the norm bound require the separate hypothesis $\kappa\ne0$; the definition alone makes no nonvanishing assertion about a projected vector.

Default-value audit (b5): For κ=0 the totalized formula gives the identity. It is the projection onto κ⊥ for all κ, but κ⊥ is a two-dimensional plane only when κ≠0.
The projection formula is f − ⟨κ,f⟩κ/‖κ‖². It is an algebraic equality even at κ = 0 under Lean's totalized division; perpendicularity requires the separate nonzero-covector hypothesis.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryTransverseProjecti.summary: The transverse projection subtracts the longitudinal component

TorusEuler.oscillatoryVelocity_weightedW.text: The zero-start transverse estimate removes the initial-data term from the fixed-plane lifting argument. It retains the actual physical equation, transversality, coframe identities, common closed support, positive time weight, and coefficient bounds. The final word constant includes time length, homogeneous stability, coframe factors, and forcing size, so the theorem alone does not select uniform parent-independent constants.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryVelocity_weightedW.summary: Bound a transverse correction with zero initial value

TorusEuler.oscillatoryVelocity_weightedW.text: For a transverse physical velocity satisfying the forced equation, uses smooth lift and readout coframes with $RJ=\mathrm{Id}$ and $JR$ equal to transverse projection. Weighted stability and coefficient bounds for the fixed-plane operator $-2RMJ$ give a physical finite-word bound. The displayed constant includes both coframe costs, the initial-data budget, the forcing budget, and the order recurrence.
TorusEuler.oscillatoryVelocity_weightedW.summary: Lift fixed-plane estimates back to the transverse velocity

TorusEuler.oscillatory_transverse_of_ini.text: A solution of the projected forced amplitude equation remains orthogonal to its covector. The named hypotheses `hκ` and `hV` give the covector and amplitude equations, `hκ₀` excludes a zero covector throughout the interval, and `hV₀` imposes initial orthogonality at `t₀`. The set is order-connected by `hJ` and contains the initial time by `ht₀`. The result includes zero amplitudes and arbitrary projected forcing, so the paper applies it with zero forcing.
TorusEuler.oscillatory_transverse_of_ini.summary: Initial transversality persists along each trajectory

TorusEuler.paperA1_displacement_eq_primi.text: A solenoidal displacement with zero initial value equals the time primitive of its velocity on $[0,1]$. The inputs are `hz₀ : z 0 = 0`, continuity `hv` of the velocity, and `hz`, the derivative identity within the interval at every time. The proof applies the fundamental theorem of calculus. This also covers the endpoints through one-sided, within-set derivatives; no continuation beyond the interval is asserted.
TorusEuler.paperA1_displacement_eq_primi.summary: Recovering displacement from its continuous velocity

TorusEuler.paperA1_solution_of_unproject.text: Any displacement and velocity satisfying the unprojected pressure equation produce a `PaperMeanIntegratedSolution` with the same velocity and constant. The assumptions include `hz₀`, `hz₁`, continuity `hv`, derivative identity `hz`, periodicity `hper`, gradient identity `hgrad`, and equation `heq`. The primitive identity supplies the terminal condition, and Leray projection removes the periodic gradient. This bridge lets the uniqueness statement in Theorem A.1 apply to solutions originally expressed with a displacement and pressure.

TorusEuler.paperA2_wordNorm_le.text: A triangular Leibniz recurrence bounds every solution word of length at most $N$ by a constant times the forcing bound $F$. The inputs `ha`, `hp`, `hb`, `hF` give nonnegative bounds; `hCoef`, `hForce`, and `hRec` provide the coefficient, forcing, and recurrence inequalities. The explicit constant depends on $N,a,p,b$, but is linear in $F$. This is numerical induction on word length, before the conversion to a lifted Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.paperA2_wordNorm_le.summary: Uniform bounds for the triangular derivative recurrence

TorusEuler.paperAppendixD_holderComparis.text: The supremum finite norm is bounded by the half-Hölder finite norm, which is at most $4\ell^{-1/2}$ times the supremum norm one order higher. The scale assumptions are `hℓ : 0 < ℓ` and `hℓ₁ : ℓ ≤ 1`. The field is spatially smooth, and `hb` and `hbh` supply bounded derivative-value sets so the real supremums behave as finite norms. The constant four is explicit and independent of the derivative order.
TorusEuler.paperAppendixD_holderComparis.summary: One extra derivative gives the half-Hölder finite norm

TorusEuler.paperFiniteNorm_directionalDe.text: For constant directions weighted by `r`, differentiating in the unweighted direction `i` costs at most `(r i)⁻¹` and one extra order in the finite word norm. The assumptions include `0 < r i`, smooth slices and bounded derivative-value sets through order `n+1`. It is an individual-direction estimate, so summing label directions is a further step.

TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveVelocityN.text: The spatial and phase norm on $[t_0,T]$ with the amplitude weight applied after differentiation. The definition takes `γ : ℝ → ℝ` and measures the functions $(\gamma(t))^{-1}f(t,a,s)$ using the scaled label and phase directions determined by `ℓ` and `h`. The time variable indexes the supremum and is not one of those derivative directions. Consequently this definition takes no time derivatives of $\gamma$.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveVelocityN.summary: The amplitude-weighted active spatial and phase norm

TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveWord_bddA.text: For a smooth twisted-periodic profile on $[t_0,T]$ with `htT : t₀ < T`, every fixed mixed derivative word has bounded samples after multiplication by any time weight bounded on a subset of that interval. The subset may be the launch singleton. The proof shifts the interval to start at zero and uses a zero continuation only outside the slab; it claims smoothness on the slab, not across that continuation's boundary.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveWord_bddA.summary: All active mixed derivative samples are bounded

TorusEuler.paperHierarchyLaunchValueNorm.text: Defines the finite mixed spatial and phase derivative norm on the singleton time slice $\{t_0\}$. The direction fields already carry the label scale and phase width, and the norm uses no Hölder difference quotients or amplitude weight. It measures the launch datum retained in the active inverse estimate, rather than replacing that datum by zero.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchyLaunchValueNorm.summary: The launch trace has its own unweighted norm

TorusEuler.paperHierarchySumCost.text: Defines twice the number of retained indices in `Finset.Icc 1 P` times a common coefficient `C`. This turns a uniform per-level estimate into the summed hierarchy estimate. The depth and coefficient are explicit parameters; the definition itself asserts neither nonnegativity nor the validity of the individual level bounds.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchySumCost.summary: Counting the cost of summing retained levels

TorusEuler.paperHierarchyTailCost.text: Defines the explicit tail prefactor using `K`, the square of `C+1`, and the cardinalities of the two omitted-interaction pair sets. The extra constant term accounts for the remaining linear contribution. It is a bookkeeping coefficient for a finite-depth remainder bound, not a statement that the remainder has the required size.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchyTailCost.summary: Counting the interactions in the hierarchy tail

TorusEuler.paperLemma13_slowOrders.text: The schedule has $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, the orders tend to infinity, and $L_{j+1}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$. The hypotheses explicitly include `hFrequency`, `hMaximum`, `hPositive` and `hFloor`, as well as the initial order and threshold conditions. The Lean statement does not require the threshold to be nondecreasing or to dominate the analytic cost table. Index `i` is $j-1$, so `freq (i+3)` is the frequency entering $L_{j+1}$.
TorusEuler.paperLemma13_slowOrders.summary: Orders increase slowly and the gain stays controlled

TorusEuler.paperLemma31_waveProfile.text: There exist profile families $F_h,P_h$ and a single positive constant $C$ with all of Lemma 3.1's properties for every $0<h\le1$. The quantified order matters: `F`, `P`, and `C` precede `h`, and each `Cj` is chosen after `j` but before `h` and `s`. Smoothness, oddness, period one, normalized primitive, unit central slope, two-sided slope bounds, amplitude control, and all higher derivative estimates are explicit. Pointwise bounds give the displayed supremum bounds over a period.
TorusEuler.paperLemma31_waveProfile.summary: Uniform odd profiles with controlled negative slope

TorusEuler.paperLemma57_periodicGraphFro.text: A smooth profile on the label cell gives a smooth periodic Eulerian graph when it agrees with its periodic mean near the cell faces. The hypothesis `hcollar` states this agreement on a collar of width `δ`; `hLeft`, `hRight` and `hAper` describe the inverse labels. With `hprofile` and `hcoeff`, the theorem also preserves the derivative and half-Hölder bounds across the gluing. The collar expresses the paper’s compactly supported oscillation inside the cell.
TorusEuler.paperLemma57_periodicGraphFro.summary: Smooth periodic extension of the cell graph

TorusEuler.paperLemma61_exists_firstWave.text: A normalized first wave satisfying every conclusion of Lemma 6.1 exists. Besides `hs : 0 < s`, `hs₁ : s ≤ 1`, and `hf : 0 < freq`, Lean assumes `hT : 0 ≤ T` and the small-slab condition `hSmall`. The existential produces the wave and its estimates together, so the annotations do not leave construction of the input wave as an unproved hypothesis.

TorusEuler.paperLemma61_firstWave.text: The normalized first wave satisfies the two origin conditions and the initial strength bounds of Lemma 6.1. Its hypotheses are `hs : 0 < s`, `hs₁ : s ≤ 1`, `hf : 0 < freq`, and `hSmall : T * ‖stationaryShearGradient s‖ ≤ 1 / 8`. The input `w : FirstWaveOrigin s T freq` already records the equations, transversality, and exact peak normalization.

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed.text: The time-path clause of Lemma A.2, restricted to time-mean-zero fields by the same mixed projection as Appendix A.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed.summary: A polynomial bound for the time-path inverse

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_higher.text: This is the path-valued version of the higher spatial inverse on the normalized interval. `hCoercive` is required only on paths with `endpointIntegral 1 w = 0`. Both datum and solution lie in the fixed space of the mixed projection, which imposes spatial solenoidality and zero time mean. The derivative words through order `n` concern spatial labels, not time differentiability.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_higher.summary: The mixed inverse preserves derivative words

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder.text: The compressed operator on spatial half-Hölder fields of $L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ paths is a continuous linear equivalence, with polynomial inverse estimate of exponent $145$. The hypothesis `SpatialHolderHalf 1` concerns the label variable. Coercivity is required only for paths with `endpointIntegral 1 w = 0`, exactly the temporal constraint. The fixed space also includes spatial Leray projection. This is the time-path case of Lemma A.2.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder.summary: Time path Hölder inverse with a polynomial bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_bou.text: The mixed compression of multiplication by a path-operator coefficient is bounded on each lifted $C^{n,1/2}$ class. The coefficient condition `hB` is entirely spatial; time remains an $L^2$ variable. Commutation of the projection with spatial derivatives and the product estimate give the result. No lower energy bound appears here, and this theorem alone does not provide an inverse.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_bou.summary: Bounded time path compression in higher Hölder norm

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_bou.text: The mixed inverse preserves the lifted $C^{n+1,1/2}$ class and is bounded in that norm, with a constant independent of the datum. The input coefficient acts on temporal $L^2$ paths, and `hCoercive` applies only when their mean is zero. The hypothesis `hB` supplies spatial regularity. The equivalence `e` remains a base-space equivalence; the conclusion separately records its higher-class restriction and norm bound.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_bou.summary: Bounded time path inverse in higher Hölder norm

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_hig.text: This gives the analogous unique solution on the fixed space of the mixed spatial and time-mean projection. The coefficient’s coercivity is required only on zero-time-mean paths, and the higher regularity is with respect to spatial labels. It does not produce time derivatives or a continuous-in-time representative; those are later parts of the endpoint recovery.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_hig.summary: The mixed inverse preserves the ordinary Hölder class

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_res.text: The mixed spatial and time-mean compression preserves $C^{n+1,1/2}$ in the label variable and has a unique preimage in that class for each datum there. The coefficient hypothesis is `hB : SpatialHolderHalf (n + 1)`, with positive `μ`. The coercivity hypothesis `hCoercive` tests only mean-zero temporal paths. This is the setwise higher-regularity restriction; separate norm estimates make the restricted map and its inverse bounded.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_res.summary: Time path inverse preserves each higher Hölder class

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial.text: The spatial clause of Lemma A.2, with a fixed polynomial in the coercivity, sup-norm and Lipschitz constants.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial.summary: A polynomial bound for the spatial inverse

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_higher.text: Under positive coercivity and a nonnegative Lipschitz bound for `B`, the spatial compressed equation has a unique solution carrying actual coordinate derivative words through order `n` whenever coefficient and datum carry those words. `hB` and `hf` are `HasSpatialHolderWords` witnesses. The result is qualitative and uses the same order-zero inverse; conversion to the usual lifted Hölder norm is proved later.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_higher.summary: The spatial inverse preserves derivative words

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder.text: For a $C^{1,1/2}$ operator coefficient coercive with constant $\mu>0$, the compressed spatial Leray operator is a continuous linear equivalence on its fixed subspace in $C^{0,1/2}$. The coefficient regularity is `SpatialHolderHalf 1` of the periodic lift; the coercivity hypothesis quantifies over every label and vector. The inverse estimate uses the coefficient supremum and first derivative supremum, with exponent $145$. This declaration covers the spatial-vector case of Lemma A.2.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder.summary: Spatial Hölder inverse with a polynomial bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_b.text: Multiplication by a coefficient followed by spatial Leray projection maps $C^{n,1/2}$ into itself with a bounded norm. The sole coefficient regularity input is `hB : SpatialHolderHalf n` for its lift. No coercivity is needed for this forward estimate. The result supplies one constant valid for every input in the fixed subspace; it does not assert invertibility or control the inverse.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_b.summary: Bounded spatial compression in higher Hölder norm

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_b.text: The inverse of the compressed spatial map is bounded in the lifted $C^{n+1,1/2}$ norm. Given positive `μ`, coefficient coercivity `hCoercive`, and regularity `hB`, the theorem supplies a base-space equivalence `e` and a nonnegative constant independent of the datum. Its inverse preserves the higher class and satisfies the stated linear estimate. The constant may depend on the coefficient and order; this is not a uniform polynomial estimate in all higher-order coefficient norms.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_b.summary: Bounded spatial inverse in higher Hölder norm

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_h.text: For positive coercivity and a Lipschitz coefficient, the spatial compressed equation has a unique solution in the lifted order-`n` half-Hölder class whenever coefficient and datum belong to that class. The proof converts their ordinary regularity to derivative words and back. This statement is qualitative; boundedness in the higher norm is established in a later module.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_h.summary: The spatial inverse preserves the ordinary Hölder class

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_r.text: The compressed spatial map preserves $C^{n+1,1/2}$ and every datum in that class has a unique preimage there. The assumptions are `hμ : 0 < μ`, pointwise coercivity `hCoercive`, and `hB : SpatialHolderHalf (n + 1)` for the coefficient lift. Existence and uniqueness are taken in the base fixed subspace, with higher regularity as a conclusion. Boundedness in the higher norm is established by separate forward and inverse estimates.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_r.summary: Spatial inverse preserves each higher Hölder class

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein.text: A field with Fourier support in radius $4\Lambda$ has the sum of all ordered coordinate derivatives of order $m$ bounded by $C_m\Lambda^m\|g\|_\infty$. The symbol is smooth, supported, and equal to one on the unit ball; the target is a complete complex normed space and $\Lambda\ge1$. Ordered words count repeated mixed derivatives separately. The real multi-index theorem gives the paper’s exact indexing and its general real normed-space scope.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein.summary: Bernstein bounds for all ordered coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real.text: Chooses a nonnegative constant for each derivative order and cutoff symbol, uniformly over all real normed value spaces and $\Lambda\ge1$. The sum over all ordered coordinate words of length $m$ is at most $C\Lambda^m\|g\|$ for a $4\Lambda$-band-limited function. Ordered words include repetitions of mixed multi-indices, so this directly controls the paper’s smaller multi-index sum.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real.summary: Bernstein estimate for real normed values

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real_m.text: The sum over spatial multi-indices of order $m$ is bounded by $C_m\Lambda^m\|g\|_\infty$ for every real normed-space-valued torus field with the prescribed Fourier band. No completeness assumption is imposed on the target. The constant is chosen before that target and before $\Lambda$. Nondecreasing maps `β : Fin m → Fin 3` represent each multi-index once, matching the paper’s derivative sum.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real_m.summary: Bernstein bounds in arbitrary real normed spaces

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_LInfinity.text: The cutoff has an $L^\infty$ operator bound given by the fixed integral of the absolute Schwartz kernel. The assumptions are a smooth symbol supported in the radius-two ball, positive scale, and `hg : MemLp g ∞ unitTorusMeasure`. The target is a complex normed space in this realization. Both sides use `eLpNormEssSup`, so this is an estimate on essentially bounded measurable fields, not only on continuous inputs.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_LInfinity.summary: The complex cutoff is bounded on essential supremum

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_aeBound.text: An integrable torus field bounded almost everywhere by $M\ge0$ has cutoff bounded at every point by $\|\check\psi\|_1M$. The assumptions `hsupp`, `hsmooth`, and `hΛ` give a smooth supported symbol and positive scale; `hg`, `hM`, and `hbound` supply the input bounds. The conclusion is pointwise although the input bound is only almost everywhere. This is the estimate underlying the essential-supremum operator bound.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_aeBound.summary: An almost-everywhere bound controls the cutoff pointwise

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_commutes_.text: Every continuous spatial derivative through order $m$ commutes with the convolution cutoff. The assumptions include a smooth symbol supported in the radius-two ball, positive scale `hΛ`, and `hg : ContDiff ℝ m` for the periodic lift of `g`. The target is a complete complex normed space. The right side is convolution with the derivative tensor; the declaration does not address time differentiation.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_commutes_.summary: Spatial differentiation commutes with the cutoff

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_congr_ae.text: If two torus functions agree almost everywhere for `unitTorusMeasure`, their Fourier cutoffs agree as functions at every output point. Each Fourier coefficient is unchanged by almost-everywhere replacement, so the finite reconstruction is identical. No integrability binder appears here, because the library integral is defined for all functions.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_congr_ae.summary: The cutoff respects almost everywhere equality

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_derivativ.text: The $m$th spatial derivative of the cutoff is convolution of the same kernel with the $m$th derivative of the field. Here `hg : SpatialHolderHalf m` supplies spatial differentiability and uniform derivative bounds. The symbol is smooth and supported in the radius-two ball, and `hΛ` makes the scale positive. This is the Hölder-input version of spatial commutation; the separate continuous-derivative theorem needs no final Hölder seminorm.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_derivativ.summary: Hölder spatial derivatives commute with the cutoff

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_holder.text: The cutoff preserves $C^{0,1/2}$ regularity and has operator norm bounded by the same kernel mass as in the supremum estimate. The input assumption is `hg : SpatialHolderHalf 0`; the symbol is smooth and supported, and `hΛ` is positive. The theorem returns both regularity of the output and its full half-Hölder norm bound. The proof applies convolution to field values and to spatial increments.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_holder.summary: The cutoff is bounded in the half-Hölder norm

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_sup.text: The supremum norm of the cutoff is at most the integral of the absolute Schwartz kernel times the continuous torus norm of `g`. The symbol is smooth and supported in the radius-two ball, and `hΛ : 0 < Λ`. The target is a complete complex normed space. The kernel integral does not depend on $\Lambda$, which gives the scale-independent constant asserted in Lemma B.1.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_sup.summary: Continuous fields have a uniform cutoff bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_support_p.text: The cutoff has Fourier support inside radius $2\Lambda$ and preserves the relation $g(-x)=c\,g(x)$ for any real scalar $c$. The parity part requires `heven : Function.Even ψ`; support follows from finite Fourier synthesis. The input is a continuous torus field with values in a complete complex normed space. Taking $c=1$ or $c=-1$ gives evenness or oddness, respectively.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_support_p.summary: Cutoff support and parity in the complex realization

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_tail.text: The cutoff error is bounded in $C^{s,1/2}$ by $C_M\Lambda^{s-M}$ times the input $C^{M,1/2}$ norm for every $s\le M$. The symbol is smooth, supported, and equal to one near zero; the input is a continuous torus field with `SpatialHolderHalf M`. The constant is chosen uniformly in $s$, the input, and all $\Lambda\ge1$. The conclusion includes the equal-order case $s=M$.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_tail.summary: The cutoff tail gains the difference of derivative orders

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realBanachCutoff.text: The essential-supremum cutoff bound holds for values in any real Banach space. The ambient assumptions include `[CompleteSpace V]`; the explicit assumptions give a smooth supported symbol, positive scale, and `hg : MemLp g ∞`. The operator is defined using the real part of the spectral kernel. Its norm is bounded by the same absolute Schwartz-kernel integral, uniformly in $\Lambda$.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realBanachCutoff.summary: Real Banach-valued cutoffs are bounded on essential supremum

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realBanachCutoff.text: For a smooth supported symbol and positive scale, an almost-everywhere bound $\|g\|\le M$ with $M\ge0$ gives the pointwise output bound $\|K\|_1M$. Unlike the vector predecessor, this theorem has no `Integrable g` binder and omits completeness. It bounds the total Bochner integral; `MemLp` is supplied when using the result as the paper’s $L^\infty$ operator estimate.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realBanachCutoff.summary: The real kernel gives a uniform pointwise bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_LInfi.text: The cutoff of an essentially bounded real torus velocity is essentially bounded by the kernel mass times its input norm. The assumptions are `hsupp`, `hsmooth`, `hΛ`, and `hg : MemLp g ∞`. The input need not be continuous. The operator `realVectorFourierCutoffOfFunction` is the measurable-input version, and `ENNReal.ofReal` converts the finite real kernel constant to the extended nonnegative range used by $L^\infty$ norms.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_LInfi.summary: Real velocities have an essential-supremum cutoff bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_admis.text: The real cutoff preserves oddness and divergence freeness and has no Fourier coefficients outside radius $2\Lambda$. The input’s periodic lift is smooth by `hg`, and `heven` gives an even symbol. The oddness and divergence-free assumptions appear as implications inside the conclusion, so the theorem also applies to inputs lacking one of them. Frequency support is expressed after complexifying the real vector field.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_admis.summary: The real cutoff preserves admissibility and frequency support

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_aeBou.text: For an integrable real velocity representative bounded almost everywhere by $M\ge0$, its cutoff is bounded at every point by $\|K\|_1M$. The symbol is smooth with radius-two support and the scale is positive. The conclusion is stronger than merely an almost-everywhere output bound, while integrability remains an explicit hypothesis.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_aeBou.summary: A pointwise bound from an essential velocity bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_parit.text: The real vector cutoff preserves $g(-x)=c\,g(x)$ whenever the symbol is even. The assumptions are `heven` and the input symmetry `hg`; there is no positivity requirement on the scale in this finite-sum statement. The parameter `c` is any real number, with $c=1$ and $c=-1$ giving the usual parity cases. The proof transfers the corresponding complex Fourier symmetry to its real part.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_parit.summary: The real cutoff preserves evenness and oddness

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_sup.text: The real vector cutoff satisfies the same scale-independent supremum bound as the complex realization. The symbol assumptions `hsupp` and `hsmooth` and the positive scale `hΛ` determine the Schwartz kernel. The input `g` is a continuous torus velocity. The proof uses the derivative estimate at order zero and the norm-decreasing real-part map, so the kernel constant is unchanged.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_sup.summary: Real velocities have the same uniform cutoff bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_derivatives.text: One label derivative costs $\ell^{-1}$ and one phase derivative costs $h^{-1}$ in the finite weighted coordinate norm. The sum over the three label directions costs $3\ell^{-1}$. The assumptions `hell`, `hh`, `hf`, and `hb` give positive scales, smooth fields, and bounded jets through order $n+1$. The theorem is written for an input `f` already normalized by any time-only amplitude; that normalization does not affect spatial or phase differentiation.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_derivatives.summary: Label and phase derivatives cost their inverse scales

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phaseAverage.text: Phase averaging has finite-norm bound one, and subtracting the phase average has bound two. The field is smooth by `hf`, period one in phase by `hper`, and has bounded jets by `hb`. The directions `d` are constant and may already contain the label and phase weights. For the paper’s amplitude-weighted statement, apply the theorem to $f/\gamma(t)$; integration and the coordinate derivatives commute with that time-only normalization.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phaseAverage.summary: Phase averaging and mean removal are bounded

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phasePrimitive.text: The periodic primitive of a phase-mean-zero field has finite norm at most twice the original norm. The hypotheses are spatial-phase smoothness `hf`, period one `hper`, zero phase average `hzero`, and bounded derivative-value sets `hb`. The directions are constant, including any coordinate weights. As with averaging, the amplitude-weighted version is obtained by using the normalized field $f/\gamma(t)$ as the input.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phasePrimitive.summary: The zero-mean periodic primitive has norm bound two

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product.text: A continuous bilinear product obeys a finite derivative estimate with one factor divided by the time-only amplitude $\gamma$. The inputs include the bilinear map `B`, smooth derivative fields `hD`, smooth functions `hf` and `hg`, and bounded jet sets `hfb` and `hgb`. The parameter `holder` selects supremum or half-Hölder norms. The explicit constant counts admissible words and Leibniz terms, and contains the norm of the bilinear map.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product.summary: Products obey a finite weighted derivative estimate

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse.text: A pointwise invertible coefficient with derivative slope $a$ and inverse bound $D^a$ has inverse derivative slope $3a$. The hypotheses are `hc`, `hUnit`, `hInv`, and `hD : 1 ≤ D`. The target is a complete real normed algebra. `Ring.inverse` denotes the inverse on units. The zero-order inverse bound is essential; invertibility alone is not asserted to control the higher derivatives uniformly.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse.summary: Inverting a coefficient triples the absolute power slope

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse_coordina.text: In a complete normed algebra, a family with coefficient exponent `a` has inverse exponent `3*a` if $D\ge1$, every coefficient is a unit, and its inverse norm is bounded by $D^a$. The `IsUnit` hypothesis rules out the total inverse’s fallback at nonunits. The proof transfers the operator-norm inverse theorem through the coordinate equivalence.

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse_multiInd.text: The inverse coefficient satisfies the multi-index power condition with slope $3a$. The target is a complete real normed algebra, and the hypotheses `hc`, `hUnit`, `hInv`, and `hD` give the original coefficient bounds, pointwise invertibility, a uniform inverse bound, and $D\ge1$. The equivalence with derivative operator norms preserves the exponent slope when passing to and from the internal inverse theorem.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse_multiInd.summary: Coefficient inverses obey the ordinary multi-index bounds

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul.text: The product of two coefficients with power slope $a$ has power slope $2a$. The assumptions `hc` and `hd` supply the all-order bounds and smoothness, while `hD : 1 ≤ D` permits enlarging powers of the parent parameter. The target is a real normed algebra. Leibniz’s rule supplies order-dependent constants; only the fixed slope is doubled, so the growth remains linear in the derivative order.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul.summary: Coefficient products retain an absolute power slope

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul_coordinate.text: For $D\ge1$, two coefficient families with coordinate exponent `a` have a product family with exponent `2*a`. The theorem converts to operator-norm bounds, applies the product estimate, and converts back. Constants are allowed to depend on derivative order; the conclusion is a fresh coefficient-power predicate rather than a fixed numerical table.

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul_multiIndex.text: The product coefficient satisfies the paper’s exact multi-index power condition with slope $2a$. The hypotheses `hc` and `hd` are already stated using `FiniteCoefficientMultiIndexPower`, and `hD : 1 ≤ D`. The theorem transfers to derivative operator norms, applies the product estimate, and returns by the norm equivalence. Thus the public statement uses one term per spatial multi-index, without retaining multiplicities from ordered words.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul_multiIndex.summary: Coefficient products obey the ordinary multi-index bounds

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted.text: If $\ell D^a\le1$, the weighted coefficient derivatives are bounded by $C_mD^a$, and every positive-order derivative retains the extra factor $D^{2a}\ell$. The assumptions are `hD`, `hℓ`, `hscale`, and the coefficient power bound `hc`. The conclusion also bounds the full finite word norm. The permitted scale includes $\ell=0$; the paper uses a positive envelope radius.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted.summary: Small label radius leaves a positive-order factor

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_coordin.text: Assumes $D\ge1$, $\ell\ge0$, $\ell D^a\le1$ and the coordinate coefficient-power predicate. It gives an order table controlling both the full weighted derivative sum by a multiple of $D^a$ and each positive-order term by $C_mD^{2a}\ell$. The second bound retains one radius factor for the derivative-lifting argument.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_coordin.summary: Retaining a radius in differentiated coefficients

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_multiIn.text: The weighted sum through order $n$ is bounded by an order-dependent constant times $D^a$, and the exact-order term at every $m\ge1$ is bounded by $C_mD^{2a}\ell$. The inputs `hscale : ℓ * D ^ a ≤ 1` and `hc` are the scale and multi-index coefficient assumptions. The theorem uses $D\ge1$ and allows every nonnegative radius, so the paper’s positive-radius case is included.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_multiIn.summary: Weighted multi-index bounds retain one label-radius factor

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting.text: A linear equation with slowly varying coefficients inherits finite derivative bounds with only one factor of the zero-order inverse bound. The hypotheses `hComm` and `hProduct` encode differentiation of the equation, `hForcingCommutes` permits sorted derivatives, and `hInverse` is the zero-order estimate. `hCoefficient` supplies coefficient bounds through the chosen order. The spaces and seminorms are abstract, so constraints and prescribed data must already be represented in those spaces.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting.summary: Higher derivative estimates retain one inverse-bound factor

TorusEuler.paperMeanBaseScale.text: Defines the sum of the inverse-deformation bound `D`, velocity-gradient bound `L`, and the size and Lipschitz bounds for the kinetic and vorticity coefficients. This is the scale used to express a common polynomial cap for the endpoint and fixed-time inverses. Positivity and lower bounds are hypotheses of the comparison lemmas, not properties imposed by the definition.
TorusEuler.paperMeanBaseScale.summary: Combine the physical coefficient size controls

TorusEuler.paperMeanIntegratedInverse_of.text: For $0<T\le1$, continuous Hölder coefficients with positive spatial and mixed coercivity yield a unique integrated velocity and a fixed-time inverse. Exact mixed coefficient actions and nonnegative size and Lipschitz bounds are explicit inputs. A single absolute prefactor gives the common cap with exponent $291$, chosen independently of duration and source. Uniqueness is on the closed slab; this declaration does not yet recover the scalar pressure potential.
TorusEuler.paperMeanIntegratedInverse_of.summary: Construct and bound the integrated endpoint inverse

TorusEuler.paperMeanIntegratedMomentum.text:
The spatial half-Hölder field $K(t)v(t)-J(\Omega v)(t)+L(t)$, with `src` representing $L$. The velocity is already valued in the solenoidal subspace. Coefficient application is written `coefficientMul`, and the time integral is `endpointPrimitive`. This definition records the left side of the unprojected equation. It imposes no differential equation or endpoint condition; those belong to the solution structure and the existence theorem.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression contains time primitives and coefficient action. For arbitrary functions those integrals are totalized; the integrated-solution record supplies the regularity and equations used later.
TorusEuler.paperMeanIntegratedMomentum.summary: Integrated momentum before the Leray projection

TorusEuler.paperMean_contDiff_one_of_has.text: If `q` has the specified half-Hölder gradient at every Euclidean point, then `q` is continuously differentiable. The hypothesis uses `HasGradientAt`, which includes actual differentiability. The proof identifies the Fréchet derivative through the inner-product duality map and obtains its continuity from the torus field’s continuous lift.
TorusEuler.paperMean_contDiff_one_of_has.summary: A represented Hölder gradient gives a continuous derivative

TorusEuler.paperMean_inverse_scale.text: The ellipticity and coercivity parameters are bounded by a fourth power of the sum of the physical coefficient controls. The binders `hD`, `hL`, `hCK`, `hCΩ`, `hLK` and `hLΩ` impose $D\ge1$ and nonnegativity of the remaining bounds. The conclusion is the explicit estimate $4+D^2+2D^2(1+L)^2+C_K+C_\Omega+L_K+L_\Omega\le16Q^4$. It is the algebraic step converting the abstract inverse estimate into a polynomial in the manuscript’s parent bounds.
TorusEuler.paperMean_inverse_scale.summary: Polynomial control of the inverse parameters

TorusEuler.paperMean_normalized_potentia.text: Two potentials with the same represented half-Hölder gradient and zero integral over the centered cell are equal everywhere. Actual gradient witnesses make both potentials continuously differentiable, so their difference is constant and their cell integrals are genuine integrals. The cell has volume one, forcing the constant to vanish. Periodicity of the potentials is not required by this theorem.
TorusEuler.paperMean_normalized_potentia.summary: Equal gradients determine the normalized pressure

TorusEuler.paperMean_projection_C1_gradi.text: The spatial Leray projection of $g=\nabla q$ is zero when the potential is periodic and $C^1$. These hypotheses are `hq₁ : ContDiff ℝ 1 q`, `hqper : SpatiallyPeriodic q`, and the pointwise lift identity `hq`. The gradient is represented by a spatial half-Hölder field. The theorem does not remove gradients of arbitrary nonperiodic potentials; periodicity is the condition that makes the torus pressure term orthogonal to solenoidal fields.
TorusEuler.paperMean_projection_C1_gradi.summary: Leray projection removes a periodic pressure gradient

TorusEuler.paperMean_projection_gradient.text: A half-Hölder field whose lift is the gradient of a smooth periodic potential has zero solenoidal projection. This supplies the pressure cancellation needed to pass between projected and unprojected mean equations.
TorusEuler.paperMean_projection_gradient.summary: The spatial Leray projection kills pressure gradients

TorusEuler.paperPhysicalStepExponent.text: The common exponent $b$ used to absorb the parent powers in the physical estimates. For the label exponent `a`, hierarchy loss exponent `r` and mean exponent `aMean`, the definition chooses $6r+5a+2a_{\rm mean}+160$. This is one sufficient choice, independent of the expansion depth and derivative-order constants. The accompanying budget theorem supplies the coefficient $\Gamma_P$.
TorusEuler.paperPhysicalStepExponent.summary: A common exponent for the physical estimates

TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC.text: A smooth even cutoff produces the velocity, normalized Poisson pressure and residual of Proposition 5.11. The symbol hypotheses `hEven`, `hSupport`, `hSmooth` and `hUnit` specify the cutoff. Constants are chosen before the interval, approximation and cutoff scale. The inputs are smooth periodic $V,R_V$, odd solenoidal $V$, its momentum equation and the upper Hessian bound relative to $p_U$. The conclusion gives a `TruncatedChildStage`, the residual Fourier band, the two time-uniform error bounds and the inherited one-sided pressure bound.
TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC.summary: Frequency truncation with normalized pressure and residual bounds

TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentCoef.text: The six coefficient families of Proposition 5.1 have label derivative bounds with the common power $\mathsf D^{16m+16}$. The input `R` bounds the velocity derivatives; it is fixed before the parent and supplied from Fourier support by `exists_parentVelocityJetBounds`. The remaining assumptions give the smooth periodic flow, both deformation bounds and the central frequency normalization. The exponent has fixed slope and intercept, both 16; after radius weighting, the remaining power is independent of derivative order.
TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentCoef.summary: Uniform powers for the parent coefficients

TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentComp.text: Composition with the parent flow sends Bernstein-scale derivatives of a field to bounds $|D_a^m(f\circ X)|\le C_m A_f\mathsf D^{6m}$. The sequences `R` and `C'` are fixed first, and the conclusion then quantifies over the parent and field. The hypothesis the field’s derivative hypothesis is the field's original derivative estimate. Smoothness, periodic parent velocity and two deformation bounds supply the chain-rule argument.
TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentComp.summary: Derivative bounds after composition with the parent flow

TorusEuler.paperProposition51_weightedCo.text: The weighted derivative sum is at most $(\sum_{j\le n}C_j)A_f$ when the already composed field satisfies the slope-six estimate. The assumptions `hf` and `hscale : ℓ * D ^ 6 ≤ 1` are the relevant inputs. There is no remaining power of $\mathsf D$ and the field amplitude stays outside the sum. This declaration performs the final weighting step, not the flow composition itself.
TorusEuler.paperProposition51_weightedCo.summary: The weighted composition bound retains the field amplitude

TorusEuler.paperTheorem71.text: One exponent parameter and one monotone threshold produce the common sequence for every sufficiently large $N$. The theorem returns a scheduled construction, its lifetime and the fixed strength constant $18e^3$. This is the older library existence theorem. The current paper statement quantifies over every admissible threshold above a majorant and adds identities with the Section 5 expansion. The increment fields here state bounds at each time, without a separate assertion of time continuity.
TorusEuler.paperTheorem71.summary: A common sequence for one selected threshold

TorusEuler.paperTheorem71_of_constructio.text: Given an inductive construction, a large initial-frequency bound and the required stationary-start identity, produces a finite terminal time and the full `PaperTheorem71Conclusions` record. The proof transfers regularity, Fourier support, inverse deformation, pressure, central splitting, crossings and increment estimates from the actual stages. This is the retained frozen correspondence, not the current conditional spine theorem.
TorusEuler.paperTheorem71_of_constructio.summary: One physical construction supplies all common-sequence conclusions

TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1.text: The endpoint problem on $[0,1]$ has a solution, a periodic normalized potential, and a continuous pressure gradient. The inputs are positive `κ`, `μ`, coefficient bounds, pointwise ellipticity, `EndpointSobolevEnergyBound`, and `ContinuousOn src I`. The conclusion gives the velocity estimate with exponent $291$, both displacement traces, uniqueness of velocity, displacement, constant and gradient, and smooth conclusions for smooth data. Symmetry of $K$ and skew-symmetry of $\Omega$ are not separately required. The field `s.terminal` carries the second trace.
TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1.summary: Existence and uniqueness for the endpoint problem

TorusEuler.paper_mean_columns.text: Every smooth endpoint mean satisfies $\|B\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^{b+2+2s}\|\bar f\|_{[n+1]}$ with $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-s}$. The threshold `s₀`, exponent `b` and order constants are chosen before the parent. The solution `sol` is arbitrary, and `s₀ ≤ s` fixes an admissible radius exponent. Once $s$ is fixed, the power of $\mathsf D$ is independent of the measured derivative order $n$.
TorusEuler.paper_mean_columns.summary: Every smooth endpoint mean satisfies the derivative estimate

TorusEuler.paper_mean_hardy.text: If $H^\#\le I$ and $0<T\le1$, the Hessian term is at most half the physical-displacement kinetic energy, and the label energy is at least that half. The binders `hF`, `hM`, `hMt` and `hUpper` give the coefficient equations, continuity and quadratic upper bound. A zero-trace Sobolev displacement is represented by `v : Lp E 2 ...` with `hv : endpointIntegral T v = 0`, then $z=\int_0^t v$. The result holds in any complete real inner product space.

TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse.text: For each admissible parent, the integrated endpoint problem has a solution for every continuous spatial half-Hölder source. Its velocity and constant are unique on the slab. One polynomial bound controls both this velocity and the fixed-time inverse composed with the Leray projection. The binders after `p : PaperMeanParent T D L` bound the coefficients and their first spatial derivatives by $K_0,K_1,\Omega_0,\Omega_1$. The exponent is explicitly $4\cdot291=1164$. The potential has zero spatial mean and a continuous represented gradient.
TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse.summary: The endpoint inverse and its common polynomial bound

TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse_smooth_for.text: A smooth periodic label force admits a smooth mean solution with both displacement traces zero and a zero-mean label pressure. The parent is `p : PaperMeanParent T D L`; `hT`, `hT₁`, `hD` and `hL` give $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$ and $L\ge0$. The source hypotheses are `hforce` and `hper`. The result supplies `PaperSmoothMeanSolution`, including the mean relation, divergence condition and momentum equation. Recovering Eulerian fields additionally requires identifying the coefficients with an actual flow.
TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse_smooth_for.summary: Smooth mean recovery with normalized label pressure

TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse_smooth_for.text: A smooth periodic Eulerian force admits smooth periodic corrections $b,q$ satisfying the divergence condition and the linearized Euler equation over the actual parent flow. The hypotheses `hX`, `hU`, `hper`, `hdiv`, `hD`, `hL` and `hsharp` describe that flow, its regularity, and the coefficient controls. The force is pulled back as `force t a := f t (X 0 t a)`. The theorem constructs the parent coefficients and the smooth label solution before recovering the Eulerian fields.
TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse_smooth_for.summary: The smooth mean inverse for an Eulerian parent

TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE.text: One common limit has all four conclusions of Section 8: preterminal agreement, bounded velocity and central vorticity blow-up, maximal lifespan and divergent integrals, and both off-origin limits. The theorem first chooses a threshold $N_0$, then quantifies over compatible stages `s` and central waves `_w` with `N₀ ≤ s.frequency 0`. Those structures contain the induction estimates. The terminal time is the limit of the same activation sequence throughout.
TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE.summary: One Euler limit with all terminal properties

TorusEuler.parentResidualFourierBand_of_.text: A smooth torus velocity supported in the band $2D$ has projected momentum residual supported in $4D$. Lean assumes `hU` for the velocity band, `hA` identifying the Hölder field with self-advection, and `hEq` for the projected momentum equation, together with positive slab length and nonnegative `D`. Multiplication doubles the Fourier band, while the Leray projection preserves it.
TorusEuler.parentResidualFourierBand_of_.summary: The residual has twice the velocity frequency band

TorusEuler.parentResidual_invCube_le_par.text: For frequency $\Lambda\ge1$, the bound $\Lambda^{-3}\le\Lambda^{-5/2}$ holds, since the exponent $-3$ is smaller. Lean writes the latter exponent as `hierarchyMeanExponent 2`. This scalar comparison lets the preceding stage's stronger residual estimate supply the next stage's parent-smallness hypothesis.
TorusEuler.parentResidual_invCube_le_par.summary: Cubic decay supplies the required parent smallness

TorusEuler.periodicComplexLeray.text: This is the orthogonal projection onto the Fourier-defined solenoidal subspace of complex spatial $L^2$. Unlike the earlier finite-mode formulas, it acts on every Hilbert-space field. The later mode and coefficient identities establish that this all-field operator has the intended Fourier symbol.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexLeray.summary: Orthogonal Leray projection on all complex L2 fields

TorusEuler.periodicComplexLeray_mode.text: Applying the full $L^2$ Leray projection to one inserted Fourier mode gives the same mode with its coefficient projected by `lerayModeProjection`. The proof checks the projected candidate and its longitudinal error using orthogonality. This certifies the intended Fourier symbol rather than assuming it.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexLeray_mode.summary: The Hilbert projection has the prescribed Leray mode action

TorusEuler.periodicComplexSolenoidal.text: This submodule consists of spatial complex $L^2$ fields orthogonal to the longitudinal Fourier span. It is the Fourier definition of the solenoidal space. Later lemmas characterize membership by transverse coefficients and connect real weakly divergence-free fields with this complex Hilbert formulation.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexSolenoidal.summary: The Hilbert space orthogonal to longitudinal modes

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2.text: This bounded real-linear map applies coordinatewise complexification to a real spatial $L^2$ field. It retains the underlying real velocity while placing it in the complex Hilbert space suited to Fourier analysis. Its following evaluation theorem states the representative relation almost everywhere.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2.summary: Embedding real spatial fields into complex L2

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_apply_ae.text: The image of a real spatial $L^2$ field under complexification agrees almost everywhere with coordinatewise complexification of its representative. This is the standard representative formula for the bounded map on $L^2$. It supports the comparison of real weak tests with complex Fourier mode inner products.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_apply_ae.summary: Complexified Hilbert fields agree pointwise almost everywhere

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_injectiv.text: The embedding of real spatial L² fields into complex spatial L² is injective. Its left inverse is the real-part map proved in the previous identity. Thus any equality obtained after complexification can be pulled back to real fields; the statement concerns L² equivalence classes, not arbitrary pointwise representatives.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_injectiv.summary: Complexification distinguishes real square integrable fields

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_mem_sole.text: A real spatial L² field belongs to the weak gradient kernel exactly when its complexification belongs to the complex Fourier solenoidal subspace. One direction uses weak tests to constrain coefficients; the other uses projection and real parts. The equivalence connects two definitions without assuming a classical derivative for the field.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_mem_sole.summary: Weak real solenoidality is Fourier transversality after embedding

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_mem_sole.text: If a real spatial $L^2$ field is weakly divergence free as stated by `hv`, its complexification belongs to the Fourier solenoidal subspace. Each longitudinal mode pairing reduces to a vanishing coefficient supplied by the preceding Fourier-test lemma. The theorem proves this direction of compatibility, not an equivalence by itself.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_mem_sole.summary: Weak real divergence freedom implies Fourier solenoidality

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_realLera.text: Complexifying the real weak Leray projection of `v` gives the complex Fourier Leray projection of the complexified `v`. The proof first compares real parts and then shows the imaginary part vanishes. This establishes the Fourier realization of the real projection on arbitrary spatial L² fields.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_realLera.summary: Complexification commutes with the real Leray projection

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyVector.text:
Coordinatewise complexification of the real Euclidean spatial vector.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyVector.summary: Embedding real vectors into complex Euclidean space

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyVector_appl.text: The complex Euclidean embedding of a real vector has coordinate `i` equal to the complex cast of its original real coordinate.
