The proof writes the derivative as the divergence of a coordinate-directed vector field and applies periodic cancellation. The regularity hypothesis ensures the derivative is actual and integrable on the compact cell.
_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.summary: A periodic coordinate derivative has zero integral

_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.text: The Fourier coefficient of a chosen matrix entry of a continuous operator field equals that entry of the operator-valued Fourier coefficient. Compactness of the torus supplies integrability, and the continuous complex-linear coordinate map commutes with the integral. This justifies proving the operator equality entry by entry.
_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.summary: Extracting an entry commutes with Fourier integration

_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.text: For real source data, each entry of the constructed complex multiplier has the Fourier coefficient prescribed by two coordinate derivative factors and the inverse Laplacian symbol. The proof combines entrywise integration with the exact multiplier symbol. This establishes the formula for all integer frequencies before any candidate potential is introduced.
_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.summary: Each constructed Hessian entry has the correct coefficient

_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.text: The Fourier coefficient of the bundled complexification of a real half-Hölder field equals the coefficient obtained by complexifying its values directly. This follows by pointwise evaluation of `HalfHolder.map`. It aligns two encodings of the same scalar source before comparing the constructed multiplier with the actual pressure.
_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.summary: Identify the Fourier coefficients of complexified source data

_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.text: The norm of the bundled product is at most $2\|U\|\|V\|$. This combines its supremum and half-Hölder increment estimates in the norm characterization of `HalfHolder`. It is a bound for arbitrary operator-valued fields, so its later application to velocity gradients uses separate field representations.
_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.summary: The operator product has a uniform Hölder bound

_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.text: The trace functional has operator norm at most three in the Euclidean operator norm. Each diagonal entry is bounded by the operator norm, and summing over the three coordinate vectors gives the estimate. This dimension-dependent factor combines with the Hölder product bound in the quantitative pressure error.
_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.summary: The trace costs at most a factor of three

_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.text: Complexifying a real coordinate unit vector produces the corresponding complex coordinate unit vector. This elementary identity aligns the basis vectors used by the real and complex operator formulations. It is needed when comparing individual matrix entries of the pressure multiplier, with no analytic assumptions on a field.
_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.summary: Complexification preserves each coordinate unit vector

_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.text: A differentiable periodic complex field has a periodic derivative in any fixed coordinate direction. The theorem applies periodicity of the Fréchet derivative and then evaluates the chosen coordinate vector. Unlike the unconditional periodicity lemmas for total derivatives elsewhere, this signature includes an explicit differentiability hypothesis.

At an integer frequency `k`, the entry obtained by applying the angular operator to coordinate vector `j` and reading coordinate `i` is $k_jk_i/|k|^2$. `frequencyNormSq` is the squared lattice norm. The formula includes the zero frequency through total division, giving zero there.
_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.summary: Read a matrix entry of the lattice pressure symbol

_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.text: Defines the trace of a real spatial operator by summing its three diagonal coordinate entries. Bundling this as a continuous linear map permits it to act on half-Hölder fields while preserving the function-space structure. The following lemmas identify it with the algebraic trace and bound its norm by three.

Identifies the bundled coordinate-sum map with `LinearMap.trace` of the underlying linear map. The proof uses the standard Euclidean basis. This allows the Hölder-space construction of the source to be compared with the matrix trace in the pressure Poisson equation without changing the trace convention.

Defines a bounded real-linear functional that applies an operator to coordinate direction `i` and reads output component `j`. Keeping that order explicit avoids a transpose ambiguity when comparing a Hessian with mixed scalar derivatives. The input is an arbitrary spatial operator and need not already be known to be symmetric.

Extracts direction `i`, component `j` from a real operator-valued half-Hölder torus field and packages it as a continuous scalar function. Continuity follows from the input field and the bounded coordinate functional. This prepares the field for entrywise Fourier comparison; no assertion that it is an actual Hessian is part of the definition.
_private.TorusEuler.PressureHessianMulti.summary: View a represented Hessian entry as a continuous function

_private.TorusEuler.ProjectedHilbertInve.text: Pair the projected operator applied to its first argument with its second argument in the closed Hilbert subspace. The result is a bounded bilinear form on `H`. It is the form passed to Lax–Milgram after a positive coercivity estimate is supplied; symmetry is not imposed by this definition.
_private.TorusEuler.ProjectedHilbertInve.summary: The bilinear form of the compressed operator

_private.TorusEuler.ProjectedHilbertInve.text: If the ambient operator satisfies $c\|u\|^2\le\langle Au,u\rangle$ on the closed subspace with `hc : 0 < c`, then the associated compressed bilinear form is coercive. The inner-product identity removes the orthogonal projection. No self-adjointness or symmetry assumption is required by this coercivity conclusion.
_private.TorusEuler.ProjectedHilbertInve.summary: Ambient coercivity passes to the compressed form

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.text: The absolute value of the first coordinate of a real pair is at most its norm. The norm here is the standard product norm, namely the maximum of the two coordinate absolute values. This helper extracts a component estimate from a normalized-state comparison; it does not use a Euclidean inner-product norm.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.summary: The first component is bounded by the pair norm

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.text: If $a,b\ge m>0$ and $|a-b|\le\delta$, then $|\log(a/b)|\le\delta/m$. The proof applies $\log x\le x-1$ in both directions. The positive lower bound prevents totalized division or the value of the logarithm at zero from entering the argument; nonnegativity of $\delta$ follows from the assumed error bound.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.summary: Positive lower bounds control logarithmic changes

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.text: The absolute value of the second coordinate is bounded by the standard norm on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$. This is the maximum norm, so the proof is simply the second entry being no larger than their maximum. It extracts the deviation-coordinate estimate from bounds on normalized states.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.summary: The second component is bounded by the pair norm

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.text: If $Y$ satisfies the Riccati equation within $[0,T]$, its reconstructed deviation is continuous on that interval. The proof first obtains its derivative from the change of variables and then extracts continuity. No initial-value condition or positivity of $\varepsilon$ is needed for this regularity conclusion; those enter the invariant-strip estimate separately.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.summary: A supplied Riccati solution has continuous deviation

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.text: The algebraic factor $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$ is continuous on the entire real line for every fixed $\varepsilon$. The proof uses its previously established derivative at every time. This supplies the coefficient continuity needed by the kernel and triangular propagator calculations without imposing the physical positive-parameter range.

For a supplied Riccati path, the diagonal factor used in the kernel has within-interval derivative $-2s(1+e)$ times itself. The deviation here is reconstructed from $Y$. The theorem requires the differential equation on $[0,T]$ and a time in that interval, but neither an initial value for $Y$ nor a sign restriction on $\varepsilon$.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.summary: The decay equation for the selected kernel factor

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceAmplitude.0.text: For a continuous scalar function on $[0,T]$, its integral from zero has derivative equal to the integrand within that closed interval. Membership `ht` provides both the nonnegative time and the upper bound. This private calculus helper is used to differentiate the growth factor and the selected-seed kernel.

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison..text: Any trajectory of the triangular generator satisfies $\|z(t)\|\le2\|z(r)\|$ for ordered times in the interval, assuming continuous nonnegative scale and deviation. Despite its name, this is a bound on solutions, not on the generator matrix itself. The product norm is $\max(|h|,|l|)$; the proof passes through the contracting sum $|h|+|l|$.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison..summary: A uniform bound on normalized trajectories in the maximum norm

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison..text: A continuous scalar integrand on $[a,b]$ has a primitive based at $a$ whose within-interval derivative is the integrand. The endpoint membership `ht` ensures the integral runs through points where continuity is known. This private version supports the integrating-factor proof of the Volterra inequality used in the matrix perturbation argument.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceComparison..summary: Differentiating the accumulated forcing from the initial time

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..text: If continuous $Y$ equals the reference expression built from $e$, then $s(1+e)$ is continuous on the nonnegative ray. The proof rewrites that product as $Y+damping/4$. No continuity assumption on $e$ is supplied separately, and the theorem does not itself assert that this envelope is positive.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..summary: Continuity of the positive term in the reference ansatz

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..text: One quarter of the damping is a continuous function of time for every fixed real $\varepsilon$. Its algebraic expression contains only smooth clock functions and polynomial operations. This fact permits integration of the correction term when the Riccati ansatz is split into a positive envelope and a logarithmic derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..summary: Continuity of the correction to the reference rate

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..text: At a nonzero time $t$, the derivative of $-(4/\varepsilon)/t$ is $4/(\varepsilon t^2)$. The only explicit nonzero assumption is `ht`; no assumption $\varepsilon\ne0$ appears. At $\varepsilon=0$, Lean's total real division makes both expressions zero. The tail estimate applies this helper only with $\varepsilon>0$ and strictly positive time.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..summary: Integrating the inverse square bound for the tail

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..text: The derivative of $-\tfrac12\log s$ is one quarter of the damping. The function $s$ is strictly positive for every real parameter and time, so the logarithm is differentiated on its ordinary positive domain. The declaration differentiates the logarithm of $s$, despite the abbreviated Lean name mentioning damping.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..summary: An antiderivative for one quarter of the damping

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..text: A function continuous on $[0,\infty)$ is interval-integrable between any two ordered nonnegative endpoints. The proof restricts continuity to the compact interval between them. This small helper justifies the integral addition and comparison identities used to estimate the reference amplitude after its turning time.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..summary: Integrating a continuous function between future times

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $a\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$, and $b\ge a$, the ratio $s(b)/s(a)$ lies between $1/(\varepsilon x(b))$ and $9/(\varepsilon x(b))$. This is a bound on the clock functions alone. It does not assume that $a$ is actually a zero of $Y$ or involve an amplitude solution.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..summary: Comparing cosine factors after the turning-time window

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..text: The square root of $s(b)/s(a)$ equals the exponential of half the difference of their logarithms. Since $s$ is positive for all real inputs, both the ratio and logarithms are nondegenerate without extra hypotheses. This identity combines the integrated damping correction with the reference amplitude's exponential formula.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceLateBounds..summary: Writing the cosine prefactor as an exponential

_private.TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator..text: For continuous scale and deviation on $[a,b]$, the diagonal coefficient has derivative $-2\,scale(t)(1+e(t))\,decay(a,t)$ within that interval. The statement includes endpoint derivatives and assumes only continuity, not nonnegativity. It verifies the diagonal entry of the explicit solution to the second normalized equation.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator..summary: The differential equation for the diagonal coefficient

_private.TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator..text: If $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and both $c$ and $t$ lie there, then the integral from $c$ to the variable upper endpoint has derivative $f(t)$ within $[a,b]$. The base point need not be the left endpoint. This includes one-sided endpoint derivatives used for the triangular propagator coefficients.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator..summary: Differentiating an integral on the closed interval

_private.TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator..text: For continuous scale and deviation on $[a,b]$, the transfer coefficient has derivative $scale(t)\,decay(a,t)$ within the same closed interval. This is the fundamental theorem of calculus after proving continuity of the diagonal coefficient. It supplies the first component of the explicit triangular propagation formula.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferencePropagator..summary: The differential equation for the transfer coefficient

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRatio.0.Tor.text: For positive $\varepsilon$ and $\tau\ge\sqrt2/\varepsilon$, the time is positive, $x(\tau)\ge1/\varepsilon$, and $\varepsilon\tau\ge1$. The proof squares the threshold using its positivity and the clock definition. No upper bound on $\varepsilon$ is required; this lemma isolates the consequences of being in the late coupling range.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRatio.0.Tor.summary: Clock inequalities in the late coupling range

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRatio.0.Tor.text: If $u>0$ and $u,v$ differ from one by at most $d_U,d_V$, then $|v/u-1|\le(d_V+d_U)/u$. The proof rewrites the quotient error as the difference of the two input errors over the positive denominator. It does not assume that $u$ is close enough to one to have a fixed positive lower bound.

If $Y$ has the reference ansatz, the two normalized couplings simplify to expressions in $x,s,e$. In particular, dividing the second by $s$ gives $1+4e+2e^2+\varepsilon xs^2$, making the large-term cancellation visible. This is an algebraic identity with no sign, time-domain, or ODE assumptions on the supplied deviation.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRatio.0.Tor.summary: Cancellation in the two reference couplings

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRatio.0.Tor.text: If $0<\varepsilon\le1/16$, then $7\varepsilon^2\le7\varepsilon/16$. This elementary inequality turns the explicit quadratic error of the first reference coupling into a linear error. It has no time variable and contains no coupling or reference-solution hypothesis itself.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRatio.0.Tor.summary: Absorbing a quadratic error in the small parameter

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.text: The deviation right-hand side is jointly continuous in time and state for each fixed real $\varepsilon$. The assertion concerns the uncurried map $(\tau,e)\mapsto deviationRhs\,\varepsilon\,\tau\,e$. Its inverse square root has a strictly positive denominator everywhere, so continuity holds without restricting to the invariant strip or the physical parameter range.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.summary: Joint continuity of the deviation equation

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.text: If $\varepsilon\le1$, then at every time the deviation right-hand side is Lipschitz with constant three on $[0,\varepsilon/8]$. The difference factors as $-s(2+y+z)(y-z)$, and $s\le1$. No lower bound on $\varepsilon$ appears in this lemma; for negative $\varepsilon$ the state interval is empty, while the existence theorem separately assumes positivity.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.summary: A uniform Lipschitz bound inside the deviation interval

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.text: With $\varepsilon\ge0$, the driving coefficient $s^2(1-\varepsilon x)$ is at most one at every real time. The second factor may be negative; the proof needs only its upper bound and $0<s\le1$. This inequality controls the Riccati derivative where the rate is at or above one.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.summary: The reference driving coefficient is at most one

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.text: The derivative of one quarter of the damping is $\tfrac32\varepsilon x s^2-2\varepsilon x^3s^4$. This holds for arbitrary real parameter and time and follows by differentiating $\varepsilon\tau x s^2/2$. Together with the derivative of $s$, it verifies that the change from deviation $e$ to reference rate $Y$ respects the differential equations.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.summary: Differentiating the correction to the reference rate

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.text: The derivative of $s$ is $-\varepsilon\tau x s^3$ for all real $\varepsilon$ and $\tau$. The expression $1+x^2$ is strictly positive, so differentiating its inverse square root needs no additional nonvanishing hypothesis. This expanded derivative is used in the Riccati substitution before it is rewritten in terms of the damping coefficient.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.summary: Differentiating the cosine factor in algebraic coordinates

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.text: For $t\in[a,b)$, a derivative within $[a,b]$ is also a derivative within $[t,\infty)$ at $t$. The strict inequality $t<b$ is what permits the change of neighborhood filter. This private lemma lets the invariant-strip proof use a right-sided boundary comparison at every time before the interval endpoint.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.summary: Passing to a right-sided scalar derivative

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.text: The reference rate can be written as $s(1+e-\varepsilon\tau xs/2)$. This identity is valid for every supplied deviation function and every real parameter and time. Since $s>0$, subsequent lemmas can determine the sign of $Y$ from the bracket, which is the form used to locate the turning time.

For $\varepsilon>0$, $0\le\tau\le\sqrt{2/\varepsilon}$, and nonnegative deviation at that time, the reference rate is at least $1/\sqrt2-\varepsilon\tau/4$. The argument bounds $x$ by one and estimates the damping correction directly. This additive lower bound is integrated to obtain the logarithmic gain, without requiring the deviation ODE in this lemma.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.summary: A lower bound for the initial growth rate

_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.text: Whenever $2\le\varepsilon\tau$, the Riccati right-hand side at $Y=0$ is strictly negative. The identity $\varepsilon x=(\varepsilon\tau)^2/2$ makes the driving factor negative, and $s^2$ is positive. No separate sign hypothesis on $\varepsilon$ or $\tau$ is needed for this pointwise algebraic implication.
_private.TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.0.T.summary: The reference rate crosses zero with negative derivative

_private.TorusEuler.ScalarBarriers.0.Tor.text: An interval derivative at $t$ gives the right-sided derivative at the same point when $a\le t<b$. The strict upper-endpoint hypothesis `htb` ensures that the interval contains a right neighborhood of $t$. This is a change of differentiation domain, with no differential equation or sign conclusion.

_private.TorusEuler.ScheduleExistence.0..text: This private function returns `order + 1` if its threshold $B(\mathrm{order}+1)$ does not exceed the current frequency, and otherwise keeps the current order. It is an explicit two-case implementation of the schedule’s constrained maximum once the current order is known to be positive and admissible.
_private.TorusEuler.ScheduleExistence.0..summary: Advance the derivative order only when its threshold is met

_private.TorusEuler.ScheduleExistence.0..text: If the current order is at least one and already satisfies its frequency threshold, `nextOrder` is the greatest positive order at most one higher whose threshold is met. No monotonicity of $B$ is required: either the highest allowed order qualifies, or every other allowed natural order is at most the admissible current one.
_private.TorusEuler.ScheduleExistence.0..summary: The two-case choice realizes the admissible maximum

_private.TorusEuler.ScheduleExistence.0..text: The recursive state at index $i$ stores $(q_{i+1},\lambda_i)$. It starts at $(1,N)$, chooses the next order from the old order and old frequency, and raises that frequency to $320b(q_{i+1}+1)$ using the old order. This indexing preserves the paper’s lag between the threshold test and the next frequency.
_private.TorusEuler.ScheduleExistence.0..summary: Construct derivative orders and frequencies together

_private.TorusEuler.ScheduleExistence.0..text: For $b\ge1$, $N\ge1$ and $B(1)\le N$, each recursively constructed state has order at least one, frequency at least one and its order threshold below its frequency. The induction uses the greatest-element property and the fact that a base at least one cannot decrease under a positive integer exponent. Strict frequency growth is not asserted here.
_private.TorusEuler.ScheduleExistence.0..summary: Every recursive state keeps a positive admissible order

_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.text: A smooth inverse coframe whose adjoint sends the carrier to a nonzero vector at every label gives a smooth longitudinal projection, through the stated differentiability order. The projection is a rank-one operator divided by the squared covector norm. The nonvanishing assumption controls that denominator and excludes the algebraic zero-covector branch from this regularity argument.
_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.summary: The longitudinal projection is smooth away from zero covectors

_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.text: For operator-valued functions smooth through order `n`, assumes derivative bounds with a shared slope `p` in the exponent of nonnegative `D`, and offsets `q` and `r`. Every derivative through `n` of their composition is bounded by $2^n\cdot \mathrm{C1}\cdot \mathrm{C2}\cdot D^{p\cdot i+q+r}$. The finite Leibniz factor is uniform over the lower orders, not over `n`.
_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.summary: Composition combines two polynomial operator-jet budgets

_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.text: If two natural derivative orders are equal, evaluating the first iterated derivative after transporting its finite index set gives the evaluation of the second derivative. Substitution of the equality proves the statement. This bookkeeping lemma aligns the finite tuple indexing used by word estimates with the indexing of a continuous multilinear derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.summary: Equal derivative orders give equal multilinear evaluations

_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.text: For a continuous multilinear map and a nonnegative candidate bound, a bound on every tuple of vectors of norm at most one implies the same bound on the operator norm. The proof handles zero arguments separately and normalizes the remaining vectors. This converts estimates for individual derivative words into bounds on full iterated Fréchet derivatives, including order zero.
_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.summary: Unit-vector control bounds a multilinear operator

_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.text: Specializes the bilinear product estimate to evaluation of a continuously varying linear map on a vector field. If both inputs are smooth and their jets through order `N` are bounded by nonnegative `A` and `B`, the resulting vector field has bound $2^N\cdot A\cdot B$. The evaluation operator has norm at most one, so no additional constant is needed.
_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.summary: Applying a varying linear map preserves finite jet control

_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.text: If a smooth function has a phase-jet bound through order `N`, precomposing it with a continuous linear map of norm at most one preserves that bound. The proof bounds the multilinear derivative after inserting the linear map in every argument. This embeds label-only coefficients in label-and-phase space without an extra derivative cost.
_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.summary: A linear contraction cannot increase a jet budget

_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.text: Multiplying a smooth function by a real constant `c` multiplies any finite phase-jet budget by $\lVert c\rVert$. The scalar may be zero or negative; the norm absorbs its sign. This helper applies time switches at a fixed time without introducing time derivatives, since the jet variable consists only of labels and phase.
_private.TorusEuler.SeedDerivativeBudget.summary: A fixed scalar multiplies the jet budget by its norm

_private.TorusEuler.StationaryShear.0.To.text: Under `hs : |s| ≤ 1`, the norm of the seed direction is at most two. The proof uses the triangle inequality on its first and third coordinate components. This deliberately simple estimate feeds the later uniform velocity and gradient bounds for the stationary parent.
_private.TorusEuler.StationaryShear.0.To.summary: A bounded shear parameter bounds its direction

_private.TorusEuler.StationaryShear.0.To.text: This bounded real-linear functional pairs a vector with the second coordinate unit vector. It is the covector controlling the sinusoidal phase of the stationary shear. The neighboring evaluation lemma identifies it with the second coordinate, enabling both derivative calculations and the nilpotence argument.

Evaluating the seed covector at a vector returns its second coordinate. This identifies the inner-product definition with the coordinate notation used in the sinusoidal shear. It allows the affine-wave differentiation formula to be applied with a phase depending on exactly one coordinate.
_private.TorusEuler.StationaryShear.0.To.summary: The shear covector is the second coordinate

_private.TorusEuler.StationaryShear.0.To.text: This vector is the first coordinate unit vector plus `s` times the third. Its second component vanishes, so a velocity in this direction does not move the coordinate on which the shear depends. That elementary geometry makes the stationary shear have zero self-advection.
_private.TorusEuler.StationaryShear.0.To.summary: The direction of the stationary shear velocity

_private.TorusEuler.StationaryShear.0.To.text: The second coordinate of the seed direction vanishes for every real `s`. The direction only involves the first and third unit vectors. This ensures that the stationary shear leaves its phase coordinate fixed and that its rank-one velocity gradient squares to zero.
_private.TorusEuler.StationaryShear.0.To.summary: The shear direction has zero second component

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBorelCutoff..text: The normalized monomial times the fixed bump is infinitely smooth for every natural degree. The proof uses smoothness of polynomial powers, division by a constant and multiplication by the bump. This establishes the regularity needed for global derivative bounds of each later rescaled atom.

Multiplies $t^n/n!$ by the fixed bump. Near zero it agrees with the normalized monomial, while away from zero its support is compact. The degree `n` is any natural number, including zero. Its normalization makes the derivative of order `n` at zero equal to one.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBorelCutoff..summary: A normalized time monomial with compact support

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBorelCutoff..text: Chooses the scalar smooth bump with center zero, inner radius one and outer radius two. It equals one near the endpoint and vanishes outside its support radius. This fixed bump is the building block for normalized time monomials; the shrinking radii used in the Borel series are chosen later.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBorelCutoff..summary: A fixed smooth cutoff near the time origin

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBorelSeries..text: If a continuous linear map `g` has norm at most one and `f` is smooth, the norm of each derivative of `f ∘ g` is at most that of the corresponding derivative of `f` at `g x`. The proof bounds the product of operator norms. It supports the time and space projections in the joint Borel series.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBorelSeries..summary: A contraction cannot enlarge derivative norms by composition

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: Applies the within-set Fréchet derivative of `f` to the fixed direction `d`. The set and evaluation point remain explicit. This notation lets the gluing proof discuss time and space directions uniformly, but the definition alone neither asserts differentiability nor gives uniqueness of the within-set derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: A directional derivative within a specified set

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: For a smooth function on a uniquely differentiable set contained in the closure of its interior, the two within-set directional derivatives commute at points of the set. The dense-interior hypothesis allows interior symmetry to reach the boundary. The theorem is not a commutation rule for arbitrary thin subsets.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: Directional derivatives commute up to the boundary

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: At a point of a uniquely differentiable set, the directional derivative of `along s f d` in direction `w` is the derivative of the derivative-valued map evaluated first in `w` and then in `d`. Smoothness ensures these within derivatives exist. This bookkeeping identity prepares the symmetry argument for mixed derivatives.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: Evaluating an iterated derivative in two directions

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: If `f` is infinitely smooth on `s` and `s` has unique differentiation, its within-set derivative evaluated in a fixed direction is again smooth on `s`. The uniqueness hypothesis controls the chosen derivative operator. This permits the gluing induction to differentiate its matching-jet hypotheses repeatedly.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: A fixed directional derivative remains smooth on the set

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: Assumes both fields are smooth on their respective closed half-slabs, the spatial domain is open, and all pure time jets agree at every spatial boundary point. It proves that all normal jets of the full derivative-valued maps agree there too. Tangential differentiation of the boundary identities and commutation of mixed derivatives supply the spatial components.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: Matching normal jets also matches derivative-valued jets

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: Abbreviates $[a,\infty)\times O$, the domain on which the left field and right extension are combined. The finite-order gluing induction first works on this closed lower slab. The public smoothness theorem then restricts to $(a,\infty)\times O$, avoiding a claim of an open extension through the lower endpoint.

A within derivative on a time-space product restricts to the spatial slice at a time belonging to `I` by composition with the spatial inclusion. The result is a `HasFDerivWithinAt` statement on `O`. It separates the spatial component of the full derivative without assuming the product domain is open.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: Restricting a derivative to a spatial slice

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: A within derivative on `I × O` restricts to the time slice at a fixed spatial point in `O` by composition with the time inclusion. The theorem states a `HasFDerivWithinAt` property and does not select a derivative using `fderivWithin`. No uniqueness or interval geometry is needed for this elementary chain rule.

Abbreviates the time-space domain $[a,0]\times O$ used for the original field in the gluing argument. It records both the terminal boundary and the lower time endpoint. Geometry is supplied separately: smooth gluing assumes `a < 0` and an open spatial set so that boundary derivatives have the required uniqueness.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: The closed slab to the left of the boundary

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: If `a < 0` and `O` is open, every point of the closed left slab lies in the closure of its interior. This includes the time-zero boundary and the lower endpoint. The fact is needed to extend symmetry of second derivatives from interior points to the boundary in the jet-gluing argument.

Evaluates the iterated within-set Fréchet derivative on the same direction in every argument. At order zero this is the field value. For positive order it represents a repeated normal jet only under the smoothness and domain hypotheses used later; the definition is meaningful as a total Lean expression for arbitrary functions and sets.

Under smoothness, unique differentiation and dense interior of `s`, taking `n` repeated derivatives in direction `d` commutes with one derivative in direction `w`, as functions restricted to `s`. Iterating the two-direction symmetry proves the identity. This is what lets equality of boundary time jets also control their spatial derivatives.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: Tangential differentiation commutes with repeated normal jets

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: For a smooth function on a set with unique differentiation, each repeated directional jet is smooth on that same set. The direction and derivative order are fixed. The result does not extend the function beyond the set; it provides regularity of the boundary data used by the later extension construction.

On a set with unique differentiation, a smooth function’s repeated jet of order `n+1` equals the within-set directional derivative of its repeated jet of order `n`. The evaluation point must belong to the set. This recursive identity turns matching normal derivatives into an induction on smoothness order.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: One more repeated jet is a directional derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: The repeated-jet expression at order zero equals the original function value, for arbitrary set, function, direction and point. No regularity assumption is needed. Thus matching all time jets across a boundary includes matching the functions themselves, which is the continuity condition at the first stage of smooth gluing.

Abbreviates $[0,\infty)\times O$, the domain of the candidate right-hand extension in the gluing proof. The common time-zero boundary is included. Later smoothness and dense-interior arguments use openness of `O`; the abbreviation itself places no assumptions on the spatial set.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: The closed slab to the right of the boundary

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: For an open spatial set, the right half-slab is contained in the closure of its interior. The time-zero boundary is approached from positive times. This geometric fact supplies the dense-interior hypothesis needed for commuting derivatives of the smooth right-hand extension at the gluing surface.

Defines the piecewise field to equal `f` when time is nonpositive and `g` when time is positive. In particular its value at zero comes from `f`. Continuity or differentiability across that boundary is not built into the expression; matching values and derivatives must be proved before using the smooth gluing result.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: Choosing the left field at the time boundary

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: Under `a < 0`, an open spatial domain, smoothness on both closed half-slabs and matching time jets of every order, proves the piecewise field is $C^k$ on the combined slab. The proof inducts on `k`, upgrading the matching data to derivative-valued jets. The hypotheses are all-order even when the requested conclusion is one finite order.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: Smooth gluing at each finite derivative order

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.text: Given smooth fields on the two half-slabs with equal values and full within derivatives on their common boundary, the piecewise field has the piecewise derivative on the combined slab. This is a derivative-existence statement, not yet all-order smoothness. It handles the boundary by combining the one-sided derivative estimates and handles interior points by local equality.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalBoundaryJetG.summary: Matching first derivatives differentiates the glued field

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalCoefficientT.text: Extracts joint smoothness in time and label for `f` from a smooth bundled profile whose values equal `f t a` on the whole slab. The proof restricts the profile to phase zero and uses the equality `hVal`. This private helper supplies regularity for later derivative conversions; it does not establish bounds on the field.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalCoefficientT.summary: Smooth profile values give a smooth label field

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalCurlIntegral.text: For positive `c`, `C`, and gain `l`, a nonnegative interval length `δ`, a normalized delay bound $2l^2\le r\delta$, and a rate bound $r\le Csl$ imply $(2c/C)l\le cs\delta$. This is the scalar cancellation behind the direct integral proof. Positivity of `r` and `s` is not separately assumed.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalCurlIntegral.summary: The normalized clock converts amplification into curl mass

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalCurlIntegral.text: The open Euclidean ball of radius one half about the origin lies inside the closed centered unit cell. Each coordinate is bounded by the vector norm. The inclusion supplies a positive-volume neighborhood on which continuity can compare a central value with the essential supremum over the cell.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalCurlIntegral.summary: A neighborhood of the origin lies inside the cell

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHalfHolderTi.text: For a smooth time curve valued in `HalfHolder` and `T > 0`, evaluates its closed-slab time jet at a torus label by first evaluating the curve and then differentiating. Point evaluation is a bounded linear map on the Hölder space, which supplies the commutation. The statement includes `t = 0` and `t = T` through the within-time derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHalfHolderTi.summary: Point evaluation commutes with Hölder valued time derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: If the fixed bilinear map `B` has operator norm at most one, its time-product cost is bounded by the common quadratic constant at order `n`. Both constants count the same admissible derivative words. This comparison removes map-specific constants for scalar multiplication and row evaluation in the auxiliary advection estimates.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: Unit norm bilinear maps share the quadratic constant

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: Proves nonnegativity of the finite-word product constant for four label and phase directions at every spatial order. It unfolds the cardinality and positive numerical factors. This private sign lemma permits later inequalities to be multiplied by the common quadratic constant without changing their direction.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: The common quadratic product constant is nonnegative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: Bounds the bilinear operator that evaluates a continuous linear functional on a vector by one in operator norm. The statement is purely about `Vec3` and its continuous linear dual. It supplies the map norm hypothesis used to give row evaluation the common quadratic product constant.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: Applying a row has bilinear norm at most one

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: Identifies the earlier `scaledLabelDerivativeProfile` with the corresponding `scaledProfileDerivative` direction. The statement assumes only a positive slab length and fixed real scales. The proof evaluates both definitions on the slab. This compatibility allows the earlier slow-divergence identity to reuse the new time-commuting directional operator.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: Two label derivative constructions agree as profiles

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: For a coordinate `i : Fin 3`, evaluating the corresponding scaled profile derivative gives `ℓ` times the spatial label derivative in that coordinate direction. The phase and time are held fixed, and the time lies on a nondegenerate slab. This exact identity exposes the factor that cancels the reciprocal radius in a scaled coframe row.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: The label derivative carries its radius scale

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: Expresses any vector in `Vec3` as the sum of its three coordinates times the corresponding coordinate direction. This finite-dimensional identity has no time, scale, or regularity assumptions. It is used to expand the coframe-transformed advector into the three slow label derivatives in the auxiliary source calculation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: Recover a vector from its three coordinate directions

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: Packages value evaluation at a fixed profile point `x` as a linear map from vector profiles to `Vec3`. Addition and scalar multiplication are pointwise, so their preservation is definitional. This private map lets the source proof move evaluation through finite sums when reconstructing advection from its three coordinate terms.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: Evaluate a vector profile as a linear map

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: For positive continuous `γ` on the active interval, places its reciprocal measurement weight on the advector `z`, while the differentiated target `g` uses the full-slab unweighted norm. With nonzero radius and row cap `L`, the slow-advection bound is $3Q_n^2L$ times these norms at orders `n` and `n+1`. No assumption `γ ≤ 1` is needed for this split alone.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: Put the amplitude weight on the slow advector

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: For positive continuous `γ`, places the active reciprocal-amplitude weight on the differentiated field `g`; the advector `z` uses the unweighted full-slab norm. It assumes nonzero radius and the scaled coframe row cap. The factor is $3Q_n^2L$, and the extra spatial order is spent on the weighted target. This complements the version with the weight on the advector.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: Put the amplitude weight on the differentiated slow field

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: With a continuous positive amplitude on the active interval, increasing spatial order from `m` to `n ≥ m` can only increase the amplitude-weighted factorial time seminorm. The same `q` time derivatives and the same active interval are used on both sides. The proof is the monotonicity of the underlying spatial seminorm.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: The amplitude time norm grows with spatial order

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: Bounds row-profile evaluation in the factorial time norm by the common quadratic constant times the unweighted row norm and weighted vector norm. The time weight is bounded on a subset of the positive-length slab. All time jets through `q` and spatial words through `n` are included; the row's own time derivatives are part of its measured norm.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: A coefficient row acts with one quadratic product cost

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: The factorial time seminorm measured on any subset `A` of the slab with constant weight one is at most the full-slab unweighted seminorm. The time jets themselves are still defined on the original positive-length slab. This statement restricts the measurement set; it does not replace the within-derivative domain by `A`.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: Restricting measured times can only decrease the unweighted norm

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: For a coefficient row `R`, advector `z`, and target `y`, estimates the product of `R z` with one scaled derivative of `y`. The output weight is the product of the two input weights. The bound has the square of the quadratic constant, the unweighted row norm at order `n`, the advector at `n`, and the target at `n+1`. The time order remains `q`.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: One advection term costs two products and one derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: For a scalar and vector profile, assumes three bounded weights satisfy `τP = τZ * τY` on the measured time set. Their pointwise scalar multiple has time norm at most the common quadratic constant times the two corresponding weighted norms. The identity between weights is pointwise; no derivative of a weight is taken or required.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: Product weights split between the two differentiated factors

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.text: For `m ≤ n`, the unweighted factorial time seminorm through spatial order `m` is at most the one through `n`. The time order `q`, slab, scales, and profile are unchanged. This follows from inclusion of the admissible spatial derivative words, applied to every time jet.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyNon.summary: The unweighted time norm grows with spatial order

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyPha.text: Shows that integrating a smooth twisted profile in the phase variable and subtracting the primitive's phase mean preserves joint smoothness in time, label, and phase on the slab. The only additional parameter is `hT : 0 < T`. This helper concerns smoothness, while periodicity and lattice-twist compatibility are proved separately for the bundled primitive.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyPha.summary: The phase primitive remains jointly smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyPha.text: For a continuous one-periodic function `f` with zero phase mean, translating its argument by `b` commutes with taking the normalized phase primitive. The zero-mean assumption makes the primitive periodic and fixes the otherwise possible additive constant. This identity is used to preserve the lattice twist when a primitive is bundled as a profile.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyPha.summary: The normalized primitive respects phase translation

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyPha.text: Fixes a label `a` in a smooth twisted profile and obtains joint continuity in time and independent phase on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$. This follows by composing the bundled smooth function with the coordinate inclusion. It supplies the continuity hypothesis for differentiating a phase integral; no derivative interchange is asserted yet.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyPha.summary: A fixed label leaves a continuous time and phase slice

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyPha.text: For `T > 0`, identifies the derivative of the time slice at a fixed label and phase with the evaluated bundled `timeDerivative`. The time lies in the closed slab, so the conclusion is `HasDerivWithinAt`, including its endpoints. Smoothness comes from the profile bundle and gives an actual derivative witness, not only a totalized derivative expression.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyPha.summary: A fixed label and phase give the genuine time derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.text: Unfolds the completion profile at a slab time as the carrier inverse times three curl rows applied to scaled label derivatives of the normalized relay potential. The input is centered, and the canonical coefficient equalities replace the bundled rows and potential. This intermediate identity does not need nonzero carrier or radius; those assumptions enter the following comparison with the physical completion.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.summary: Evaluate the completion through its canonical potential

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.text: For two continuous functions in a complete normed space, the normalized phase primitive of their sum is the sum of their normalized primitives. The statement does not assume either function has zero phase mean. It proves the additive identity through derivative recovery and vanishing of the normalization constants, and is used to separate the relay's pressure and potential terms.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.summary: The normalized phase primitive is additive

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.text: Defines the corresponding two-product constant for a vector-to-scalar pressure coefficient followed by a scalar-to-vector gradient row. The inner operation is measured at order `n+1`, and the outer at `n`; the factor two again accounts for the normalized phase primitive. Its target spaces distinguish it from the vector primitive cost.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.summary: The order constant for pressure primitive terms

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.text: Packages evaluation at a point as a linear map for a profile with any normed real target space. It preserves finite sums and scalar multiples by their pointwise definitions. The private helper is used to unfold completion and relay formulas under evaluation, allowing the coordinate sums to be compared with their physical expressions.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.summary: Evaluate a profile before comparing coordinate formulas

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.text: Restricts a smooth profile to any time on its slab and obtains an unrestricted smooth function of label and phase. The proof composes with the fixed-time coordinate inclusion. This private helper provides the Fréchet differentiability needed to expand the potential and pressure sums in the exact relay identification.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.summary: A profile is smooth in label and phase at fixed time

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.text: Specializes the relay primitive estimate when the inner coefficient at order `n+1` and the outer row at order `n` are both bounded by `K ≥ 0`. Their product becomes $K^2$. The input remains centered, the inner coefficient phase-independent, and the output retains the input's bounded time weight. The spatial order on the input is still `n+1`.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.summary: Two coefficient bounds give a square of their common cap

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.text: For any seminorm `N` and three profiles whose seminorms are each at most `C`, bounds the seminorm of their sum by `3 * C`. It uses the seminorm triangle inequality and the cardinality of `Fin 3`. No smoothness or frequency hypothesis is added to the profile type.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.summary: Three bounded coordinate terms have at most triple the bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.text: Defines twice the product of the vector-operator evaluation constants at spatial orders `n` and `n+1`. The factor two comes from the normalized phase primitive; the order shift records its following label derivative. This constant depends only on spatial order and the fixed finite-dimensional evaluation map, not on frequency or time order.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyRel.summary: The order constant for vector primitive terms

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchySou.text: For a vector profile and `n ≤ m`, compares the full-slab unweighted factorial time seminorm at spatial order `n` with that at `m`. The time order remains `q`. This local order-inclusion lemma is used in source assembly to give all measured factors the spatial order required by the hierarchy recurrence.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchySou.summary: Use a higher spatial order in a source estimate

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchySou.text: Given nonnegative `c`, `x`, and `y`, together with upper bounds `c ≤ d`, `x ≤ a`, and `y ≤ b`, concludes $cxy\le d(ab)$. The hypotheses also ensure the necessary upper factors are nonnegative. This private real-inequality helper collects coefficient and profile estimates into the standard source-bound format.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchySou.summary: Compare three nonnegative factors in a source bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyTim.text: For an arbitrary seminorm and a finite family in the real module `E`, bounds the seminorm of the finite sum by the sum of the seminorms. The proof temporarily reads the seminorm as the norm of a seminormed group. This helper supplies the finite-expansion summation step; it has no frequency or time-order content.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyTim.summary: A finite expansion is bounded by the sum of its norms

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: For a positive switching rate $r$, the derivative of the wave switch is zero outside $[t_0,t_0+1/r]$. Before the ramp the switch is locally zero, and after the ramp it is locally one, so both cases use derivatives of constant functions. This statement excludes the endpoints from its hypothesis rather than relying on an endpoint convention.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: The switch derivative vanishes outside its closed ramp

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: The scaled enveloped amplitude has a genuine within-time derivative given by the original affine-wave generator at the scaled label acting on that amplitude. The evaluation time belongs to the seed’s active interval. The proof multiplies the seed’s derivative witness by a time-independent envelope and uses linearity; no extra derivative of the envelope appears.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: The fixed envelope preserves the amplitude equation

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: For a seed with `HierarchyRegularity`, its radius-scaled envelope amplitude is jointly smooth on the active slab. The proof composes the smooth amplitude with $(t,x)\mapsto(t,\ell x)$ and multiplies by the smooth envelope. The bundled regularity includes a positive radius and positive active interval length; no new time or spatial bounds are claimed.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: The scaled envelope amplitude is jointly smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: When both $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ have positive length and the latter lies inside the former, a field smooth on the larger slab has identical active time derivatives computed on either interval at points of $[c,d]$. The proof restricts actual derivative witnesses. This includes the smaller interval’s endpoints and supports transfer from the full stage to its active portion.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: Restricting the active interval preserves its time derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: For a smooth amplitude $f(t,a)$ and a smooth time-independent scalar factor $\phi(a,s)$, the order-$i$ time derivative of $\phi f$ is bounded in parameter derivatives by $2^nCA$ when the two factors have bounds $C,A$ through order $n$. Only the selected derivative of $f$ is required. The phase factor is not differentiated in time.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: A time-independent phase factor costs no time derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: At a time in the nondegenerate interval, the order-$i$ active time derivative of a jointly smooth field is smooth as a function of its remaining parameter. The proof takes a spatial slice of the preceding joint-smoothness result. This justifies ordinary Fréchet derivative estimates in scaled labels and phase after the time differentiation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: Active time derivatives are smooth in the remaining variables

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: For `a < b`, every active time derivative of a jointly smooth field remains jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times X$. The proof extracts the joint derivative in direction $(1,0)$ and iterates. Strict interval length ensures unique within-set derivatives at the endpoints; the parameter space can include both label and phase variables.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: Active time derivatives preserve joint smoothness

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: Joint smoothness of $f$ on $[a,b]\times X$ implies within-interval smoothness of $t\mapsto f(t,x)$ at each fixed parameter $x$. The proof composes with the constant-parameter inclusion. This provides the regularity required by time Leibniz identities without moving the label or the independent phase during differentiation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: A fixed parameter gives a smooth time curve

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: The bilinear map $(A,x)\mapsto A(x)$ has operator norm at most one for the given normed spaces. The proof applies the defining operator-norm inequality twice. This is the precise bound required to instantiate the generic product estimate with the amplitude generator acting on the amplitude field.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: Applying an operator has bilinear norm at most one

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: If $\|c\|\le A$, the constant field with value $c$ has `PhaseJetBound n A` for every finite order $n$. The zeroth derivative uses the given norm bound; all positive parameter derivatives vanish. This turns the scalar time derivatives of a switching function into spatially constant factors in the leading-wave product estimate.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: A constant field satisfies every parameter derivative bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialCoef.text: For a nonnegative sequence $C$ and `j ≤ n`, the value $C(j)$ is at most one plus the sum of $C(r)$ for $r\le n$. The proof isolates the corresponding term of a nonnegative sum. This lets the composition estimate replace several lower-order constants by one common cap without requiring the original sequence to increase.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialCoef.summary: The finite order cap dominates each earlier constant

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialCoef.text: The number one plus the finite sum of nonnegative constants through order $n$ is at least one. This scalar observation creates a usable common bound for flow-composition estimates. It imposes no monotonicity on the original constant sequence; the finite sum supplies a positive dominating quantity at the selected order.

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialGrap.text: When `1 ≤ L`, the explicit material graph factor is monotone in its natural-number order. Both the base and the exponent can be increased because every relevant base is at least one. This permits a graph derivative estimate at order $m\le N$ to use the same prefactor chosen for order $N$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialGrap.summary: The graph factor increases with spatial order

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanHolderJe.text: For smooth spatial fields with bounded scaled label words through $N+1$, a torus half Hölder field representing a word of length at most $N$ satisfies $\ell^{|w|}\|u\|\le4R/\sqrt\ell$, where $R$ is that finite label norm. The hypotheses require $0<\ell\le1$ and the exact lift identity `hLift`. The proof combines value and gradient bounds on close torus lifts.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanHolderJe.summary: One extra label order bounds each half Hölder word

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanParentIn.text: If a coefficient field is jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, then at any time in the interval its spatial slice is smooth everywhere. This is composition with the map $x\mapsto(t,x)$. The helper supplies ordinary spatial differentiability when constructing Hölder and Lipschitz caps for the actual mean coefficients.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanParentIn.summary: A smooth coefficient has smooth fixed-time spatial slices

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.text: Defines a linear isometry between the fixed space of the actual spatial Leray projection and the half-Hölder solenoidal subspace. It is obtained from the proved equality of these subspaces, so the underlying vector field and its norm are unchanged. This lets the abstract compression estimate be applied to the concrete fixed-time mean inverse.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.summary: The Leray fixed space is the solenoidal space

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.text: The inverse isometry from the solenoidal subspace to the Leray fixed space leaves the underlying half-Hölder field unchanged. The proof combines the forward value identity with the inverse law of an isometry equivalence. It supplies the reverse rewriting needed when conjugating the supplied fixed-time inverse into the abstract fixed space.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.summary: The inverse subspace identification also preserves the field

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.text: The forward isometry from the Leray fixed space to the solenoidal subspace has exactly the same underlying half-Hölder field. This follows from its construction by equality of subspaces. The identity is needed to compare the abstract compressed coefficient multiplication with the concrete projected kinetic operator on actual fields.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.summary: Changing the subspace type preserves the field

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.text: If two half-Hölder fields both represent the directional derivative of the same field along a fixed torus direction, they are equal. The proof evaluates each derivative on the same line at parameter zero and uses ordinary derivative uniqueness, then field extensionality. It allows the spatial bootstrap's derivative family to be identified with the actual supplied derivatives.

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.text: Evaluating a `HalfHolder` field along the torus segment $a+[(sh)u]$ gives a continuous function of the real parameter $s$. This holds for every displacement $h$ and direction $u$, with no differentiability assumption on the field. Continuity follows from its bundled Hölder regularity and the continuous quotient map to the torus.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.summary: Half Hölder fields vary continuously along label segments

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.text: The difference between the segment average of $z$ and its value at $a$ is at most $\|z\|\sqrt{|h|\|u\|}$. This estimate uses only the bundled half Hölder norm and is valid for zero or negative $h$. The bound tends to zero with the displacement, providing the remainder estimate used to recover a spatial derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.summary: Segment averages approach the starting value

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.text: Constructs a continuous linear map sending a half Hölder field to its integral along $s\mapsto a+[(sh)u]$ for $0\le s\le1$. The map has norm at most one, proved from the pointwise evaluation bound. It replaces spatial difference quotients by integrals when commuting strong spatial differentiation with time differentiation.

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTime.0.T.text: For a smooth curve of half Hölder matrix coefficients on a positive-length interval, the $i$th time derivative of its multiplication operator is multiplication by the $i$th derivative of the coefficient. Evaluation is at `t ∈ Icc 0 T`. The reason is that `coefficientMulL` is a fixed continuous linear map between the corresponding Banach spaces.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTime.0.T.summary: Coefficient multiplication commutes with time derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: The sum of $\binom{n+1}{i+1}$ over $0\le i\le n$ is at most $2^{n+1}$. This omits the zeroth-index term from the full binomial sum. It bounds the kinetic-coefficient derivatives on the right side of the higher mean equation, where the highest velocity derivative has already been moved to the left.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: Positive-index binomial terms fit the same total bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: The sum of the real casts of $\binom ni$ for $0\le i\le n$ is exactly $2^n$. Lean obtains this from the natural-number binomial identity. The equality bounds the number and weights of terms produced when differentiating a product in time, keeping that combinatorial cost dependent only on the chosen time order.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: All binomial coefficients sum to a power of two

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: If every summand has scaled norm $a\|f_i\|\le B$ with $a\ge0$, then the scaled norm of the finite natural-weighted sum is at most $B$ times the sum of its weights. No positivity assumption on $B$ is separately needed. This converts time Leibniz sums into scalar binomial totals in the mean bounds.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: Bound a natural-weighted sum in half Hölder norm

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: Given three strong derivative relations in the same direction, the derivative relation for $a+b-c$ has value $a\prime+b\prime-c\prime$. This follows from linearity in the half Hölder space. The auxiliary mean recurrence uses it to combine the differentiated vorticity product, the forcing term, and the kinetic commutator terms.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: Strong spatial derivatives preserve addition and subtraction

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: If each pair of half Hölder fields satisfies the strong spatial derivative relation in direction $u$, the same relation holds for their finite sums weighted by natural numbers `k i`. The proof combines linearity with repeated addition. These weights represent the binomial coefficients appearing after time differentiation of the mean equation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: Strong spatial derivatives pass through weighted finite sums

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedDerivat.text: At a time belonging to the slab, fixing the spatial point gives a `HasDerivWithinAt` statement whose derivative is the joint within-slab derivative applied to $(1,0)$. The assumption is joint differentiability on the slab. No uniqueness claim is made for a degenerate time interval; later equalities with the selected derivative use `a < b`.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedDerivat.summary: A time slice inherits its joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedDerivat.text: For a function differentiable on the closed slab, fixing a time in the interval gives an ordinary spatial Fréchet derivative. It is the joint within-slab derivative composed with the inclusion $v\mapsto(0,v)$. This helper does not require `a < b`, because its conclusion stays entirely in the unrestricted spatial directions at a fixed allowed time.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedDerivat.summary: A spatial slice inherits its joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: At `t ∈ Icc 0 T`, with `0 < T`, a supplied genuine joint within-slab derivative identifies the within-time derivative of $r\mapsto f(r,x)$ with `timePartial T f (t,x)`. The proof composes with the time line and uses uniqueness on the interval. The hypothesis supplies a derivative witness; a totalized derivative value alone is insufficient.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Identify the derivative of a fixed spatial time slice

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: A supplied joint derivative at $(t,x)$, with $t$ in the time interval, identifies the ordinary spatial derivative of $y\mapsto f(t,y)$ with `spatialPartial T f (t,x)`. The spatial slice stays in the slab for every $y$. This statement does not need `0 < T`, since the asserted derivative is in space only.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Identify the derivative of a fixed time spatial slice

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Assume `0 < T`, joint smoothness, and a nonnegative constant $C$ bounding every mixed derivative of total order $n$ at the chosen point. Then the order-$n$ joint within-slab derivative has norm at most $2^nC$. The finite induction splits each derivative into time and space; it requires bounds for every decomposition $q+m=n$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: A common mixed derivative bound controls the joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: For a smooth function on a positive-length slab, the norm of its joint derivative of order $n+1$ is at most the sum of the order-$n$ joint derivative norms of its time and spatial partials. The proof decomposes a product-space direction into $(t,0)$ and $(0,x)$ and applies the triangle inequality. Evaluation stays on the slab.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Split the next joint derivative into time and space

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Takes the joint within-slab derivative of $f$ and restricts it to the spatial directions. The result is a function valued in continuous linear maps from $E$ to the target. This operation defines notation for the mixed derivative proof; it does not, by itself, show that a spatial slice is differentiable.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Extract the spatial partial from the joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: The spatial component of the joint within-slab derivative is jointly smooth when `0 < T` and the original function is smooth. Restriction to spatial directions is a fixed continuous linear operation, so it preserves the smoothness of the derivative map. This permits the induction to switch between spatial and temporal differentiation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The extracted spatial partial is jointly smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: For a smooth function on $[0,T]\times E$ with `0 < T`, extracting a time partial after a spatial partial equals extracting them in the reverse order at each slab point. The proof uses the symmetry of the second derivative within a set that is the closure of its interior. It therefore covers the time endpoints.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The extracted time and spatial partials commute

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Defines a continuous linear map that sends a joint derivative $L$ to $v\mapsto L(0,v)$. This separates the spatial component without changing the target space. The operation itself is purely linear algebra; later theorems identify its value on an actual joint derivative with the ordinary Fréchet derivative of the fixed-time spatial slice.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Restrict a joint derivative to spatial directions

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Defines the continuous linear map that evaluates a joint derivative on $(1,0)$. Its input is a linear map from time and space to the target, and its output is the corresponding time-direction vector. It performs no differentiation itself; it is used to extract time partials from the joint within-slab derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Read the time component of a joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Defines the order-$q$ time derivative of $r\mapsto f(r,p.2)$ within $[0,T]$, evaluated at `p.1`. The pair $p$ retains the fixed spatial coordinate during differentiation. This private operator belongs to the mixed-to-joint proof; it is distinct from the same-named profile operator, which acts on bundled twisted profiles.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Time derivatives at a fixed point in product coordinates

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: On a positive-length slab, the private fixed-spatial-point `timeJet` of a jointly smooth function agrees with repeated application of `timePartial`. The conclusion is equality only on the slab. Induction uses congruence of within-interval derivatives and the time-slice identification, allowing the norm proof to work with linear coordinate extraction.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Slice time derivatives equal iterated extracted partials

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: For a jointly smooth function with `0 < T`, the order-$q$ fixed-point time derivative of its extracted spatial partial equals the spatial derivative of its order-$q$ time derivative. The equality is between spatial functions at a time in the interval. The proof combines commutation of extracted partials with their identification as actual slice derivatives.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Slice time derivatives commute with the extracted spatial partial

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: At an allowed time on a positive-length slab, taking $q$ slice time derivatives of `timePartial T f` is the same as taking $q+1$ slice time derivatives of $f$. Joint smoothness is assumed. The proof identifies both sides with function iterates of the same extracted time-partial operator and uses the iteration law.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: One extracted time partial raises the slice time order

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Takes the joint within-slab derivative of $f$ on $[0,T]\times E$ and evaluates it on $(1,0)$. This is an encoding of the time partial on the closed slab. The definition makes sense for arbitrary $T$ and $f$; identification with the derivative of a time slice requires the later smoothness and positive-length hypotheses.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Extract the time partial from the joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: If two functions agree throughout the closed slab, their extracted within-slab time partials also agree there. This is a congruence statement for the selected derivative and needs no smoothness or positive-length assumption. It allows local equalities to be substituted under repeated within-slab differentiation without asserting anything outside the domain.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Agreement on the slab preserves the extracted time partial

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: If the original function is jointly smooth on a positive-length closed slab, iterating the extracted time-partial operator any finite number of times preserves that smoothness. The proof is induction using `timePartial_smooth`. This concerns the within-slab operator; its equality with repeated one-variable derivatives is a separate theorem.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Repeated extracted time partials remain smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: For `0 < T` and a jointly smooth function on $[0,T]\times E$, the extracted `timePartial` is jointly smooth there. The proof differentiates within a set with unique derivatives and then applies the fixed linear map `timeEval`. This supplies the regularity needed to repeat time differentiation without assuming it anew.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The extracted time partial is jointly smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: If `0 < T`, the product $[0,T]\times E$ has unique derivatives in the sense required by Mathlib’s within-set calculus. The interval has unique derivatives even at its endpoints, and the spatial factor is unrestricted. This condition makes the selected joint derivative usable throughout the mixed-to-joint derivative comparison.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The closed terminal slab has unique derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalParentTimeBa.text: A jointly smooth field on a closed slab has a smooth ordinary spatial slice at each time belonging to the interval. The proof is composition with the fixed-time inclusion and does not require positive interval length. This local helper is used when treating stage velocity and residual as continuous functions on the spatial torus.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalParentTimeBa.summary: Fixed-time slices preserve the stage field regularity

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.text: Rewrites the argument $(x+k)-j$ as $x-(j-k)$ after embedding the integer vectors. The equivalence `Equiv.subRight k` provides the bijection of lattice indices. This exact identity lets the periodic extension proof show invariance under integer shifts by reindexing its locally finite sum.

The lattice-vector embedding sends addition of two integer triples to addition in `Vec3`. This coordinatewise identity is used when reindexing the translated bumps in periodic extension. It supplies the additive compatibility needed for lattice periodization and carries no analytic estimate or smoothness assumption.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.summary: Integer translations add as spatial vectors

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.text: For any real radius `R`, the integer triples whose embedded Euclidean norm is at most `R` form a finite set. Bounding each coordinate places the set inside a finite box. This discreteness fact is the basis of local finiteness for the lattice-translated bump supports.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.summary: Only finitely many lattice points lie in a bounded ball

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.text: The lattice-vector embedding sends subtraction of integer triples to subtraction of their spatial vectors. This algebraic identity converts between translated spatial arguments and index differences. It is used to show that periodizing a local extension respects every integer translation.

The supports of all lattice translates of a fixed smooth compactly supported bump form a locally finite family.
