For each order $n$, there is a positive constant uniformly bounding the norm of the bump’s $n$th derivative over the real line. Compactness bounds it on a fixed quarter interval; outside that interval the bump is locally zero. The constant depends on order and is not supplied numerically.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: Every fixed derivative of the compact bump is bounded

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: For $0<h\le1$, the $n$th derivative of the periodic bump equals $h^{-n}$ times the corresponding derivative of the original bump at the centered scaled phase. Local translation agreement legitimizes differentiating across seams. The floor value is frozen locally in this calculation rather than differentiated.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: Each phase derivative contributes an inverse width factor

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: For positive derivative order `hn` and admissible width, differentiating the normalized slope gives the corresponding derivative of the periodic bump divided by the same constant denominator. The phase mean disappears because it is constant. The order restriction excludes the value itself, where the subtraction still matters.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: Positive slope derivatives ignore the subtracted mean

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: For $0<h\le1$ and phase in the closed interval $[-1/2,1/2]$, the periodic bump equals the original bump evaluated at $s/h$. The equality includes both boundary points because the bump vanishes there. It allows the phase mean to be estimated directly from the scaled support.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: The periodic bump matches the scaled bump on the closed cell

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: For $0<h\le1$, if phase `s` lies within distance $3/4$ of an integer `z`, the periodic bump equals the bump scaled around that integer. If the nearest integer differs, both candidate bumps vanish. This overlap agreement removes the apparent discontinuity introduced by the floor function.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: A nearby bump copy agrees with the periodic definition

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: Under $0<h\le1$, reversing phase leaves the periodic bump unchanged. The proof compares copies centered at opposite integers and uses evenness of the original bump. The collar where copies vanish handles half-cell boundary choices, where the nearest-integer representative itself is not odd.

Under $0<h\le1$, the periodic bump agrees near any phase with one fixed translated and scaled copy of the original bump. The integer center is chosen from the floor value at that phase. This local identity is stronger than a pointwise formula and allows all derivative orders to transfer.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: Every phase has a smooth local bump formula

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: The periodic bump has value at most one at every scale and phase. This follows from the range of the smooth transition and remains true even outside the intended width range. Together with its support length, the bound controls the mean removed in the phase-profile construction.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: The periodic bump is bounded above by one

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: The periodic bump is nonnegative for every real scale and phase because the underlying smooth transition is nonnegative. This value bound does not rely on admissible scale or smoothness across seams. It enters the lower estimate for the normalized mean-free slope.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: The periodic bump is everywhere nonnegative

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: The normalized slope is one-periodic for every real scale because its phase dependence comes only from the periodic bump. Subtracting a fixed mean and dividing by a fixed scalar do not change the period. This includes degenerate scales, although the intended normalization requires the later positive-width hypotheses.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: Subtracting the mean preserves slope periodicity

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: For $0<h\le1$, the phase mean of the periodic bump is at most $h/4$. The proof shifts integration to the centered cell and restricts it to the support interval of length $h/4$, where the bump is at most one. This supplies a positive lower bound for slope normalization.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: The bump mean is at most one quarter of its width

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: For an admissible width, the normalized slope has zero mean over one period. The numerator subtracts exactly the bump’s own mean, and division by a constant preserves zero mean. This is the condition that makes the integral based at zero a periodic wave profile rather than a function with linear drift.

The chosen bump takes the same value at $s$ and $-s$. Its argument depends only on $s^2$, so the identity is exact for all real inputs. Evenness is preserved through the permitted scaled periodization and later makes the integrated normalized slope into an odd wave profile.

For positive `hh`, the scaled bump at $s/h$ vanishes whenever $|s|\ge h/8$. Positivity is used to translate the support inequality through division. This locates the narrow active region within each unit phase cell and underlies the upper bound on its mean.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: Scaling the bump scales its support radius

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: If `hs` gives $|s|\ge1/8$, the bump vanishes. The chosen quadratic argument is then nonpositive, where the smooth transition is zero. The support is narrower than the paper’s allowed quarter interval, leaving a generous zero collar for the periodic copies to fit together smoothly.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: The bump vanishes outside the inner eighth interval

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: At every phase and for $0<h\le1$, the slope lies between $-h/2$ and one. The lower bound uses the small bump mean and the denominator lower bound; the upper bound uses the bump’s value at most one. These are concrete constants for the inequalities in Lemma 3.1.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: The slope has a small negative part and unit upper bound

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: For $0<h\le1$, one minus the bump’s phase mean is strictly positive. The preceding mean bound gives a value at least $3/4$, though this lemma states only positivity. It is the guard allowing division to normalize the slope and cancellation at phase zero.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: The normalized slope has a positive denominator

_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.text: For $0<h\le1$, the normalized slope is even in phase. The bump is even and its mean and denominator are phase-independent scalars. Integrating this even slope from zero will therefore produce an odd profile, which is the symmetry needed for the localized Euler velocity.

For $0<h\le1$, the slope at phase zero is exactly one. The bump value there is one, so numerator and denominator agree; their common value is nonzero by the positivity lemma. This verifies the normalization that prescribes the central gradient of the localized wave.
_private.TorusEuler.WaveProfile.0.TorusE.summary: The normalized slope equals one at the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_13.text: The comparison uses the paper’s fixed-profile convention and torus lift. S5.Parent admits any smooth periodic pressure meeting the residual and coercivity conditions, whereas §5.1 chooses the zero-mean Poisson pressure. Thus the conditional estimate has a broader parent class; no conclusion has been lost on the paper’s class. The display’s two-step bound is preserved, and finiteness of the coefficient Hölder jet suprema is added. Its A is generalized from the particular inverse constant of (4.10) to every positive A≤D^CA. The crucial quantifier order is ∀CA∃a₀∀a≥a₀∃C∃Cm before the parent and A: the radius floor may depend on the exponent that bounds A, but NOT on D, A or derivative order m. Cm(m) may depend on m; the absolute C does not. Taking A≤0 is explicitly ruled out. Theorem4.2 enters by notation and the separately supplied A bound, not as a hidden theorem application. The link must retain that context; the isolated display does not prove A≤D^CA.

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_14.text: The comparison uses the paper’s fixed-profile convention and torus lift. S5.Parent admits any smooth periodic pressure meeting the residual and coercivity conditions, whereas §5.1 chooses the zero-mean Poisson pressure. Thus the conditional estimate has a broader parent class; no conclusion has been lost on the paper’s class. The order ∃a₀ ∀a≥a₀ ∃C ∃K before the parent makes C independent of the parent, derivative order and expansion depth; C may depend on the one fixed absolute envelope exponent a. The bound has the same derivative order n on v and g, so it does not accidentally incorporate the later one-derivative loss used in Proposition5.2. v is universally quantified subject to smoothness, periodicity and B=D_aX v; invertibility of the actual flow identifies it with the displacement velocity in MeanSolution. g is exactly (D_aX)^T f̄, read at phase 0, and MeanSolution forces the source to be phase independent. HolderFieldNormFinite g is an explicit guard, with HolderFieldNormFinite v in the conclusion. In the intended smooth periodic compact-slab setting that guard follows by bounded derivatives; it is not a new PDE hypothesis, but dropping it from an arbitrary raw real-valued norm formulation would be unsafe. C and Cn remain uniform before the parent and source.

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_59.text: The scalar/vector/tensor product estimate is generalized to every continuous bilinear B:E→L[ℝ]F→L[ℝ]G, with the necessary factor ‖B‖. ∀m∃Cm≥0 precedes E,F,G,B,f,g, so the order constant is uniform over all these choices. Both inputs must belong to SpatialHolderHalf m, and membership of their product is concluded in addition to the bound. Specializing to multiplication or a norm-controlled tensor product gives the cited Hölder algebra inequality. This is stronger generality, not a weakened scalar estimate; omitting ‖B‖ would be false for scaled bilinear maps.

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_D_2.text: Both inequalities in (D.2), including the lower norm comparison, are present at every order with ℓ in (0,1]. Lean chooses the explicit universal C=4 and supplies finiteness of the Hölder quantities it bounds. It admits arbitrary time domains and real normed target spaces. The norm convention is a maximum of supremum and Hölder quotient rather than their sum: for each derivative term Nmax≤Nsum≤2 Nmax, uniformly in the field and derivative order, so the paper's unspecified absolute C is recovered with at most a factor 2. This is a norm-equivalent reading, not exact equality of the two definitions. Smoothness and bounded jets are made explicit through CoefficientNormFinite; these prevent real-supremum junk values. The full first bound and the summed bound are separate conjuncts, so a link to this statement is not limited to one of the two displayed estimates.

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.section8_setting.text: The requested node is an existence statement only: there are P,c,C,T with Theorem71Conclusions c C T. The full opening paragraph at flat 4241–4246 also states the increment estimate ≤2 λ_j^(-1), summability, and uniform convergence on the CLOSED terminal slab [0,T∞]×T3 to a continuous w. Neither w nor a closed-slab limit appears in this Lean proposition, and Theorem71Steps is discarded as well. This is adequate to anchor the clause “On the common interval ... of Theorem 7.1”, but not the whole paragraph. The missing limit is already proved by the authors in Paper.Proofs.S678b.Library.Limit.closedSlab_velocity_limit (its h81 premise serves the additional agreement with u). The new UNCOMPILED ClosedSlabSetting.lean makes the full limit a reader-facing conclusion using that library theorem and Paper.proposition_8_1. This is a wrapper over existing mathematics, not a new proof of BKM and not a change to the original citation frontier.

TorusEuler.Paper.corollary_8_3.text: The construction-specific conclusions are the same: u is maximal at the positive finite time T=T∞; every finite maximal solution from u(0) has that same terminal time; both the gradient and curl lower integrals equal top. The route is different. The Lean input Proposition82Conclusions includes the extra curl_lower estimate, and c carries quantitative crossing data absent from the short statement of Proposition 8.2. It uses these, not the general periodic BKM continuation criterion. In the actual construction, rΔt≥2L² and r≤C μ^(1/8)L imply μ^(1/8)Δt≥(2/C)L; together with the eventual curl lower bound ≳μ^(1/8), crossing intervals have unbounded integral weight. Pointwise blow-up alone would not suffice, as (T−t)^(-1/2) shows. There is consequently no missing divergence conclusion to repair with BKM. This verdict concerns the displayed corollary in its enriched construction setting, and does not certify the general theorem “finite curl integral implies continuation”.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3.text: The conclusions and one-based indexing agree with the paper: q_j≤q_(j+1)≤q_j+1 for j≥1, q tends to infinity, and 4 log λ_(j+2)≤(log λ_(j−1))². The Lean hypotheses explicitly reconstruct (1.13)–(1.14), including positive B, q_1=1, λ_0=N, the frequency recurrence, and an attained IsGreatest rather than a possibly empty maximum. It drops the standing monotonicity of B and its domination of analytic fixed-order constants, and permits every integer b≥1 rather than only the construction's selected b. Those hypotheses are unused by the arithmetic proof in Appendix C (flat 4732–4755). Hence the formal result is an arithmetic generalization; it does not reverse the quantifier order or choose B after q. q_0 and B(0) are unconstrained, as the paper only uses positive indices.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_1.text: The Euler momentum identity, divergence-free identity, pressure formula and persistence of nonzero perpendicular k,a are all present. The Lean theorem genuinely generalizes the setting: its F need only be differentiable and P satisfy P′=F; the paper fixes smooth, odd, periodic F with F′(0)=1 and zero-mean P at lines 795–799. The Euler part does not assume k≠0, whereas the TeX does at line 802. Persistence is for every t∈J, including times before t₀, while the TeX states t≥t₀. D is assumed differentiable along J with D′+D² self-adjoint and trace zero, rather than smooth. Order-connected J and UniqueDiffOn give the interval/derivative setting; both hold on a nondegenerate interval of the paper. The conclusion is the actual pointwise Euler equations and differentiability needed to read them, not IsEulerSolution on the torus; the lemma is explicitly on ℝ³. No paper clause has been identified as lost.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_2.text: All four derivatives in (2.2) have the correct entries and signs after translating the paper’s 1-based indices to Fin 3 indices 0,1,2. In particular the last is (log(‖k‖‖a‖))′=B₃₃. The explicit Orthonormal conclusion formalizes the TeX phrase “this orthonormal frame”. The Lean drops the paper’s smoothness hypothesis on B (line 858): the ODE derivative hypotheses for k,a and pointwise trace zero suffice. It also allows arbitrary J and records HasDerivWithinAt, which specializes to the ordinary interval derivatives in the manuscript. This is a useful generalization, not a missing equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_3.text: Both parts of the model lemma are retained: constant preceding strength; all three ζ derivative equations; both amplitude equations with the conditional ζ₃≠0; and uniform convergence of ζ and every entry of the amplitude coefficient matrix to (2.5). The second conjunct has the correct uniformity order: ∀ε,T,tol>0 ∃S₀, then ∀ model configurations with the same ε and S≥S₀, then ∀τ∈[0,T]. S₀ is independent of time, phase scale λ, activation t₀ and chosen amplitude. The output additionally asserts ζ₃≠0 for these sufficiently large S, making the eliminated system meaningful. T≥2 is a standing hypothesis at paper line 960, not a new restriction. The physical package only assumes continuous B on its ambient compact window, rather than smooth B in line 921, and permits a larger window containing the active slab; both specialize to the paper. The added eventual nonvanishing and widened formulation justify stronger; the mathematical limit and equations themselves match.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_4.text: The two errors of (2.10), their common ≤1/2 ceiling, both bounds on ζ₃, the 3T² vector bound, and one amplitude-independent error operator ℰ all occur. The quantified order ∃C,p,N ∀C₀≥N ∀configuration makes both the prefactor and exponent independent of C₀ and of T, as paper lines 1115–1124 require. The same ℰ is chosen before ∀a, so no amplitude-dependent error has been substituted. Two conclusions strengthen the numbered TeX statement: ContinuousOn ℰ [0,T] and the preceding-wave strength ratio bound |σp/σ−1|≤2Tδ. They are proof exports, not additional assumptions. C₀ and the exponent p are natural numbers; choosing a sufficiently large integer for an absolute large constant is a cofinal normalization of the paper’s choice, and separating the factor C from p does not alter polynomial control for T≥2. A larger ambient compact I makes δ refer to that I; choosing I equal to the paper’s active slab recovers precisely its δ. Continuous B also generalizes the smooth setting.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_5.text: The Lean explicitly supplies a solution of (2.12), uniqueness on [0,∞), and the paper’s assertions for every solution. ReferenceSlope includes the essential initial condition Y(0)=1. The same function e is existentially chosen before both the ansatz and the amplitude integral formula. Its uniform 0≤e≤ε/8 bound is over all τ≥0. Exactly one zero is stated as Yτ=0 iff τ=τm for τ≥0; together with 2≤ετm≤3 and ε>0 this forces τm>0 and actually realizes a zero. Positivity before, negativity after, the global amplitude maximum, and log gain ≥(√ε)⁻¹−1 are retained. “The solution” in the paper is made explicit as existence plus uniqueness; this is faithful disambiguation, not a reduced conditional theorem.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_6.text: Positivity of α₂, the relative slope estimate, the two-sided norm comparison, and the exact ε logarithmic amplitude error are present. The constants C,p precede the sufficiently large C₀ threshold, so neither is selected after the data. Y is universally quantified only in the two clauses that use it; Lemma 2.5 and the smallness-implied 0<ε≤1 supply its existence and uniqueness. The propagator is a continuous linear equivalence between the actual transverse planes, so surjectivity is explicit. It is selected before every other amplitude b and satisfies Φb(τ₁)=b(τ₂). Its bound has the explicit absolute constant 252 exp(1), rather than an unspecified C; the paper allows enlarging its absolute constants. The main generalization is continuous older B and the larger-window formulation, as in 2.4. The fact that each time pair has an existential Φ does not omit a requirement of a jointly regular propagator: the TeX asserts no such regularity.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_7.text: The global ν₊≥εν/2 lower bound and both late-window ratio estimates of (2.19) are present with the correct denominators. The late premise √2/ε≤τ is exactly ε tanφ≥1 because ε>0, tanφ=ετ²/2 and τ≥0. The common ∃N ∀C₀≥N order makes the threshold absolute and independent of the configuration, T and λ. Continuous B and the larger compact ambient window generalize the paper’s smooth active-slab setup; no conclusion from the numbered statement is lost. The late interval may be empty for short T, exactly as in the paper, while the first bound is still asserted over the entire nonempty [0,T].

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_3_1.text: Unfolding ProfileFamily gives exactly the oddness, smoothness, period one, zero-mean periodic primitive, primitive derivative, F′(0)=1, lower and upper slope bounds, size bound and all j≥2 derivative estimates of the TeX. The absolute C is chosen before every h; Cj is chosen after j but before h and phase s. The integer exponent 1−(j:ℤ) faithfully represents h^(1−j); it is not natural subtraction. The difference is a strict witness specialization in the conclusion: the Lean proves ProfileFamily waveProfile wavePressurePrimitive for the explicitly constructed family, whereas the paper’s numbered statement only asserts ∃F,P. The named family implies that existential immediately. No new theorem is needed just to repackage it.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_4_1.text: The two displayed energy inequalities are preserved with the same factor 1/2 and the correct Ω z_t·z sign. MeanParentFlow includes exactly the standing 0<T≤1, smooth periodic divergence-free parent and its label flow; no Euler equation has been added as a hidden premise. Hsharp unfolds to −(M_t+M²), with M the actual gradient evaluated on that flow. A test path is represented by v∈L²(0,T) with zero time integral and z(t)=∫₀ᵗv. This is the usual exact parametrization of H¹₀ paths, not just smooth test functions. ξ_t=Mξ+D_aXv is the weak derivative of ξ; the integral assertions are unaffected by representatives of v on null sets. The labelled coefficients meanKinetic and meanVorticity use the correct matrix order. The periodic lift and intervalIntegral over (0,T] give the same integrals as the TeX torus/[0,T] convention.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_10.text: The comparison uses the paper’s fixed-profile convention and torus lift. S5.Parent admits any smooth periodic pressure meeting the residual and coercivity conditions, whereas §5.1 chooses the zero-mean Poisson pressure. Thus the conditional estimate has a broader parent class; no conclusion has been lost on the paper’s class. S5.Origin.normalized requires only λ^(3/4)|center(t)| ≤ 1, not the attained normalization max|center| = λ^(-3/4) in flat TeX 2321. CenterWaveOn.nonzero still requires center(t) ≠ 0 and κ(t) ≠ 0. This broadens the admitted amplitudes; it does not allow a zero seed. The paper’s C_tC² smallness implies Lean’s separate bound for each Fréchet derivative j≤2. The latter is a broader perturbation class than a sum-norm bound with the same numerical cutoff. Both forward and inverse flow derivative estimates are retained, and Lean explicitly asserts existence of a DeformationOn flow and bounds EVERY label flow of V+v. The inverse derivative is evaluated at arbitrary Eulerian x rather than only x=Y(t,a); the flow is invertible, so these quantify the same bound. b,Γ and the smallness condition are fixed in the same order as 5.8; there is no uncontrolled exponential factor hidden in Cflow.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3.text: The comparison uses the paper’s fixed-profile convention and torus lift. S5.Parent admits any smooth periodic pressure meeting the residual and coercivity conditions, whereas §5.1 chooses the zero-mean Poisson pressure. Thus the conditional estimate has a broader parent class; no conclusion has been lost on the paper’s class. S5.Origin.normalized requires only λ^(3/4)|center(t)| ≤ 1, not the attained normalization max|center| = λ^(-3/4) in flat TeX 2321. CenterWaveOn.nonzero still requires center(t) ≠ 0 and κ(t) ≠ 0. This broadens the admitted amplitudes; it does not allow a zero seed. The order ∃a₀ ∀a≥a₀ ∃C ∃K before the parent makes C independent of the parent, derivative order and expansion depth; C may depend on the one fixed absolute envelope exponent a. The numerical clauses (5.19)–(5.22), including strict κ·M a>0, support/zero-phase-mean restrictions, pressure factor λ and launch norm γ(t₀)⁻¹‖V(t₀)‖, are present. Two interface distinctions prevent a literal equivalence claim: (i) paper quantifies over smooth fields supplied only on [t₀,T], while Lean quantifies over HierarchyTwistedProfile on [0,T]; the docstring appeals to a time extension preserving the lattice twist, but the general extension adapter is not part of Statement.lemma_5_3 and has not been checked here. (ii) paper refers to the solution from V(0)=0; Lean gives a bound conditional on TransverseSolution, not existence in that clause. Authors’ Bridge.transverseSolvable and TransverseSolution.unique close (ii), and the return supplement packages their ∃! conclusion. Mixed scope: weaker field interface, broader parent/normalization class. No claim is made that these are errors in the PDE estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_5.text: The comparison uses the paper’s fixed-profile convention and torus lift. S5.Parent admits any smooth periodic pressure meeting the residual and coercivity conditions, whereas §5.1 chooses the zero-mean Poisson pressure. Thus the conditional estimate has a broader parent class; no conclusion has been lost on the paper’s class. S5.Origin.normalized requires only λ^(3/4)|center(t)| ≤ 1, not the attained normalization max|center| = λ^(-3/4) in flat TeX 2321. CenterWaveOn.nonzero still requires center(t) ≠ 0 and κ(t) ≠ 0. This broadens the admitted amplitudes; it does not allow a zero seed. The order ∃a₀ ∀a≥a₀ ∃C ∃K before the parent makes C independent of the parent, derivative order and expansion depth; C may depend on the one fixed absolute envelope exponent a. Both estimates keep exactly the λ⁻¹ gain and one-derivative loss. The leading A₁ clause is explicit: whole-slab representatives agreeing on the active interval exist, have zero phase mean, satisfy the homogeneous equation, and receive the source-free estimate. The general V/f clauses, however, require A.average V=0 and A.average f=0 as identities on ALL [0,T], while the paper’s weighted norm and leading discussion operate on [t₀,T]. Their transversality, pressure mean and differential equation are required only on the active interval. Hence the formal interface uses stronger global mean hypotheses; projection/extension should remove them, but no checked general adapter is supplied. Combined with the broader normalization/parent hypotheses this is a mixed-scope statement, not a missing λ gain.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_7.text: The comparison uses the paper’s fixed-profile convention and torus lift. TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1.text: After importing its standing data, the result has the same two (5.5) conditions and the same initial-strength interval. FirstWaveOrigin fixes κ(0)=λe1, positive initial amplitude in direction e2, the covector/seed ODEs, nonzero transverse vectors, the upper peak bound and attainment of λ^(-3/4). TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_A_2.text: Both Hilbert-space cases are explicit conjuncts sharing one pair C,p chosen before B,μ,Lip. In the time-path case the coercivity test is restricted by endpointIntegral 1 w=0, exactly Qw=w. FreezingConclusion supplies a continuous linear equivalence of the fixed space of the actual P or PQ, with its forward map equal to the compressed coefficient multiplication; it is not merely an estimate on an unspecified inverse. For every k≥1, the same e preserves C^{k,1/2} in both directions and gives two-sided norm bounds with a Ck uniform in the input field. Together with base surjectivity this is the higher-order isomorphism in the TeX. The base coefficient premise is weakened from B∈C^{1,1/2} to a Holder field with an explicit Lipschitz bound. The base loss uses ‖B‖∞+Lip; for the paper’s C¹ coefficient one can take Lip=2 sup‖∇B‖ on the fixed torus, recovering its C¹ loss up to an absolute prefactor. This is a substantive regularity generalization. The higher-order premise remains SpatialHolderHalf k for the actual coefficient lift.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1.text: The cutoff properties, Bernstein estimate and tail estimate are retained. Constants Cop,Cb,Ct are chosen after ψ and before Λ, target spaces and fields, so no illicit field/frequency dependence is introduced; Cb and Ct are whole sequences in the derivative order. The Lean range is every Λ>0, broader than Λ≥1, and AppendixB.CutoffSymbol requires evenness rather than radiality; the radial assumptions imply it via CutoffSymbol.of_radial. The normed-space Bernstein block is uniform over real normed spaces, while the cutoff is furnished for complex Banach-valued fields and real velocities with explicit Fourier multiplier formulas and norm-finiteness guards. Spatial commutation is given at arbitrary order for the complex cutoff and first order for real velocities; higher real orders follow by iteration on smooth fields. Hölder norms use Fréchet jets; the fixed-order conversion factors can be absorbed in constants depending only on the order. The multipliers are defined on arbitrary functions, but the analytic L∞ inequality is correctly guarded by MemLp and the tail by SpatialHolderHalf.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1.text: All three groups (D.3)–(D.5) and the phase-independent Hölder product estimate are included. Constants are explicit and independent of fields, weights and the arbitrary time type. The label derivative constant is 3; the primitive constant is 2; products are continuous bilinear maps with their operator norm as a factor, extending scalar/matrix products. Phase periodicity is required only for average/primitive estimates, so the derivative and product blocks apply more generally. Positivity of γ is quantified at every time before n and the fields. Every inequality includes the appropriate finite-norm conclusion; the complete-space assumption for Bochner phase integration is automatic for the paper's finite-dimensional fields. The Hölder part uses max rather than sum; its fixed factor equivalence preserves the paper's arbitrary C_n. This classification is in the paper's smooth profile class: FieldNormFinite and HolderFieldNormFinite require C∞ rather than merely finite differentiability through the displayed order.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2.text: Parts (a) and (b) preserve polynomial derivative growth with explicit exponents 2 max(a,b) and 3 max(a,e), with output constant sequences chosen before I,D,ℓ and the coefficient fields; products are generalized to norm≤1 bilinear maps and inverses to complete normed real algebras. The inverse branch explicitly requires IsUnit at every point. The exact literal difference is the exponent domain: CoefficientPower uses a natural a, while (D.6) and part (c) name a real absolute exponent C. Rounding C up is valid for obtaining some polynomial bound and for the construction's freely chosen sufficiently small scale, but it changes part (c)'s threshold and its displayed powers: ℓ≤D^(−ceil C), D^(ceil C), D^(2ceil C) replace ℓ≤D^(−C), D^C, D^(2C). For C=1/2,D=4, the original condition admits ℓ=1/2 whereas the rounded condition requires ℓ≤1/4. This is not a counterexample to the mathematics; it is a reason not to advertise the literal fixed-real-exponent clause as identical. If C is treated only as an existential adjustable absolute exponent, the natural specialization is sufficient for all uses in this construction. No strengthening is needed solely to preserve those uses.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_3.text: The zero-order estimate is required for every u in the admissible solution space, with its own full forcing L0u+ΣT(c)u, rather than only for the particular v; this matches “for every admissible source” and is essential to differentiate. The conclusion retains a single factor Clow. Cn is chosen after the finite derivative index type, n and Cm, but before all spaces, seminorms, operators, coefficients, b, Clow, v and f. Dependence on the fixed 3/4 derivative directions is harmless; Cm is used only for orders 1 through n, a genuine generalization of the paper's all-positive-order premise. The operator/quotient abstraction encodes the preserved constraints and forcing data in E and F. Commutation is imposed on coefficient and forcing derivatives; no commutation of DE is assumed. Specializing to the commuting spatial/phase derivatives and their genuine field seminorms gives the paper's estimate. The statement is an abstract lifting estimate, not an existence or invertibility theorem for an arbitrary PDE.

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_2_8.text: The Lean gives an actual crossing in [τm,2/√(εε₊)], a greatest amplitude peak on the full [0,T], the two strength bounds at every crossing there, and the early-time suppression estimate for every τ∈[0,1]. The crossing ratio is η₊/ν₊, and σ₊ is the new wave’s ‖a‖‖k‖, not the parent’s σp. The peak is chosen before all crossings and early times, so it cannot vary with the evaluation time. τm is the unique zero of every reference solution; Lemma 2.5 makes that specification nonempty. The two explicit constants exp(−1)/4 and 18 exp(3) imply the paper’s common-C form by taking C=18 exp(3). This provides sharper numerical data and the same continuous-B/larger-window generalization as 2.4–2.7. No purported occurrence of “a crossing” has been weakened to a universal statement about crossings that might not exist.

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1.text: The convergence, regularity and lower-lifespan assertions agree with the paper in its classical well-posedness setting, but the full maximal-solution interface is different. Lean supplies an actual Euler solution u on [0,T∞), with its initial smooth odd divergence-free datum and convergence in every fixed C^(m,1/2) norm uniformly on [0,S], S<T∞. It then requires agreement for every finite maximal solution from u(0), without asserting the existence of any maximal solution on its entire, possibly infinite, lifespan. The paper instead says “Let u be the maximal smooth solution ... supplied by Section 1,” importing the general existence-and-uniqueness background at flat 66–72. Thus this is an explicit construction of the preterminal restriction plus a conditional identification, rather than a formalization of that whole background maximal-solution object. It is not a missing Euler existence proof: u on the full [0,T∞) is existentially produced. Nor should 8.1 be strengthened by demanding a finite maximal time as if this were its premise: at this stage the paper permits T*=infinity, and finiteness is established only later. In this construction 8.3 proves that the displayed u itself is maximal at T∞. With the paper's background maximal solution available, the intended comparison follows; the changed verdict records the standalone interface, not a failure of the convergence argument. Empty negative-S intervals are harmless, and norm-equivalence constants are independent of the sequence index.

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_2.text: Bounded velocity on the whole half-open slab and central curl tending to infinity are exactly the two numbered conclusions. The formal Proposition82Conclusions additionally exports a quantitative bound from the proof: fixed c1>0,C1 and all sufficiently large j satisfy |curl u(t,0)|≥c1 λ_(j−1)^(1/8)−C1 λ_(j−1)^(1/32)−C1 for every t in [tj,t_(j+1)). Constants precede the eventual j and the time quantifier. The older-gradient term C λ_(j−2)^9 in display (8.2) is bounded above by the λ_(j−1)^(1/32) term; this is a quantitative export from the proof, not the literal (8.2) formula. It is stronger than the short proposition and is deliberately used by Corollary 8.3. Half-open crossing intervals lose only the right endpoint and are sufficient for the integral argument.

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_4.text: Both requested fields are present: HasOffOriginLimits T u and HasOffOriginLimits T (timeDerivative T u). Each quantifies every compact subset of the punctured periodic lift and every natural derivative order; produces a C^m limit on an open neighborhood of K avoiding the lattice; and gives uniform convergence of all ambient spatial jets through order m as t approaches T from [0,T). timeDerivative is the within-slab temporal derivative of the same solution. The representation of C^m(K) uses jets on the lift, rather than merely values on K; this avoids an under-specified notion of derivatives on an arbitrary compact set. No extension across the origin or Euler equation after T is asserted. Joint smooth extension is the separate Remark 1.2.

TorusEuler.Paper.remark_1_2.text: The Lean existential retains the whole Theorem 1.1 witness and its explicit maximal-velocity uniqueness, and adds a spatially periodic extension g that agrees with u on [0,T)×offOrigin and is jointly C∞ on that set union an open neighborhood O containing {T}×offOrigin. This is smooth space-time extension through the terminal time away from the origin, not an Euler continuation through the singular point. No Euler equation is imposed on g after T, matching the auxiliary note's precise meaning. The existence wording “may be chosen” is retained; the result does not assert that every Theorem 1.1 witness has this extension. The proof route is the separately declared library exception D28, not a proof from the unproved auxiliary statement propositions.

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_1_1.text: The existential witness has every displayed conclusion: smooth periodic odd divergence-free initial data; a genuine smooth Euler solution on a positive finite slab; no smooth continuation; oddness; both lower Lebesgue integrals equal top; bounded velocity; central curl tending to infinity; and both off-origin limits. The extra conjunction explicitly spells out the unique maximal classical velocity meant by “whose maximal classical solution” and the standing uniqueness assertion at flat 66–72: for every finite maximal solution with the same initial datum, T'=T and v=u at every spatial point for every 0≤t<T. It is not uniqueness of arbitrary weak solutions and does not constrain arbitrary values at/after T. Mean-zero pressure fixes the pressure gauge; velocity uniqueness is the stated conclusion. Periodic lifts, operator norms and lower nonnegative integrals preserve this statement; divergent integrals are unchanged by fixed matrix-norm equivalence. HasOffOriginLimits allows the local limit representative to depend on K and m, but its values are forced by uniqueness of the nontrivial one-sided limit; this is the local C^m convergence asserted in the paper. The bare library Theorem11 omits the explicit uniqueness conjunction, but the requested Paper.Statement.theorem_1_1 includes it.

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_4_2.text: All three parts of the theorem survive unfolding. EndpointSystemSolution encodes a C¹ displacement with continuous solenoidal velocity, both endpoints zero, a time-independent solenoidal c, a continuous Holder gradient with an actual periodic potential, and the full integrated equation. Uniqueness compares z,v,c and the gradient G on [0,T], correctly leaving the additive pressure gauge unclaimed. The smooth-forcing part includes smooth z, b(0)=c, a smooth periodic zero-mean label pressure, equation (4.11), smooth physical b,q and the physical equation/divergence in (4.12). The fixed-time clause supplies a continuous linear equivalence on the solenoidal space and bounds its inverse composed with P. One pair C,p is selected before T,U,X, all bounds, sources and t. The quantitative strengthening is that A depends on first-derivative supremum caps K₀+K₁ and Ω₀+Ω₁, not the larger C^{1,1/2} norms in the TeX. For the optimal caps these are bounded by a fixed multiple of the paper’s norms, giving (4.10) after changing the absolute prefactor. The auxiliary curves K,Ω and src are representations of the actual coefficient/source lifts; smooth periodic coefficients supply such curves. Their explicit quantification does not turn the result into a theorem about unrelated matrices.

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6.text: The comparison uses the paper’s fixed-profile convention and torus lift. S5.Parent admits any smooth periodic pressure meeting the residual and coercivity conditions, whereas §5.1 chooses the zero-mean Poisson pressure. Thus the conditional estimate has a broader parent class; no conclusion has been lost on the paper’s class. S5.Origin.normalized requires only λ^(3/4)|center(t)| ≤ 1, not the attained normalization max|center| = λ^(-3/4) in flat TeX 2321. CenterWaveOn.nonzero still requires center(t) ≠ 0 and κ(t) ≠ 0. This broadens the admitted amplitudes; it does not allow a zero seed. The order ∃a₀ ∀a≥a₀ ∃C ∃K before the parent makes C independent of the parent, derivative order and expansion depth; C may depend on the one fixed absolute envelope exponent a. All level exponents in (5.34)–(5.38) match, including p=1 with the forcing terms absent by their zero convention, mean levels starting at p=2, the correction index C_{p+1}, and the remainder bound without an extra D^C factor. Lean quantifies a finite expansion depth P and bounds p≤P; constants K(n,p) are chosen BEFORE P, whereas KP(m,P) may depend on depth. This is the appropriate finite-depth form of the paper’s all-p construction: Proposition 5.4 supplies each depth, and its normalized recursive uniqueness identifies common levels. The smallness hypothesis uses the same existential C as the displayed D^C bounds, and C is independent of n,p,P.

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1.text: The numbered theorem's T1–T4 clauses, positive finite common time, localized oscillations, reciprocal-frequency bounds and vanishing before activation are present. Quantifiers are ψ, then arbitrary a0, then b,a,F with b≥1 and a≥a0, then any admissible B, then a threshold N1, then every N≥N1, then P,c,T. Thus b,a and all fixed-order majorants precede B and N; N1 may depend on B; none is chosen per derivative order after N. The absolute strength constant is fixed to 18 exp 3, and the statement adds step data plus the comparison and window bounds used later, rather than merely T1–T4. But the full contextual objects are not literally identified: Theorem71StepData identifies the physical center seed with c.centralWaves.amplitude, not the transported wave vector from k with c.centralWaves.waveVector; the first central pair's κ1(0)=λ1e1, direction e2 and attained normalization from (6.3) are not exported. Its type retains only the base initial coupling and center-wave equations. Classify the complete contextual statement as different, with the headline estimates retained and provenance weaker in these named clauses; this is not a counterexample to the theorem. Do not infer missing regularity merely from the docstring: the StepData oscillation equality uses jointly smooth HierarchyTwistedProfiles, so much time regularity is available through its type.

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_A_1.text: Symmetry of K, skew symmetry of Ω, pointwise positive ellipticity, positive μ and the full H¹₀ energy inequality are explicit. EndpointSystemSolution retains all endpoint, divergence, regularity and pressure-gradient requirements, and uniqueness includes all z,v,c,G data. The smoothness implication has K,Ω,L jointly smooth on the actual closed slab and returns smooth z, c and G. C,p are chosen before every coefficient and coercivity constant. The genuine generalization is EndpointCoefficientC1Bound: coefficients are continuous in time in C^{0,1/2}, have differentiable spatial lifts and uniformly bounded first derivatives; continuity in time into C^{1,1/2} and Holder continuity of those first derivatives are not assumed. Q uses K₀+K₁+Ω₀+Ω₁ rather than the larger C^{1,1/2} coefficient norms. The original assumptions imply the Lean caps and hence the original bound after one absolute enlargement. The H¹₀ test class is encoded by all mean-zero L² derivatives and is not narrowed to smooth tests.
